title: EJBCA Certificate Enrollment Error (Not Allow Signature Algorithm Different from CA)
body_text:
I have a question about when I use different Signature Algorithm Certificate profile against form CA_x000D_
Such like CA is using SHA512ECDSA and Certificate profile is setting up to SHA256RSA_x000D_
will get the enrollment error below_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
EJBCA Certificate Enrollment Error_x000D_
Username: _x000D_
Request failed. org.bouncycastle.operator.OperatorCreationException: cannot create signer: Supplied key_x000D_
(org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.asymmetric.ec.BCECPrivateKey) is not a RSAPrivateKey instance_x000D_
```
top_3_comments_text: primetomas: Hi, This is as it should be. If the CA has an EC key, it can not sign with an RSA signature algorithm. A CA that has an EC key, i.e. Root CA that has signed itself with ECDSA, can only issue certificates signed using an ECDSA signature algorithm. This is the nature of the cryptography. Set the Certificate Profile setting to SHA256WithECDSA (or SHA384WithECDSA or SHA512WithECDSA)... Cheers, Tomas

title: WARNING: An illegal reflective access operation has occurred
body_text:
Greetings colleagues._x000D_
It turns out that I am implementing the primekey/ejbca-ce image in a virtualized environment. I cloned the virtual server where I have it running and when I lift the container on the new server I get this error in the logs: _x000D_
WARNING: An illegal reflective access operation has occurred..._x000D_
I can access the public web via http but I cannot access the interface via https. _x000D_
I will appreciate any suggestions _x000D_
Thanks_x000D_
![error an illegal reflective access](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49497727/144940470-b7d03132-3d7c-4c3b-9598-59f0d79d9bd4.png)
top_3_comments_text: primetomas: That is a warning from WildFly, not EJBCA. It's nothing to care about. You are using WildFly 22, so my guess is that the https/tls settings are not right. It's nothing to care about. > > You are using WildFly 22, so my guess is that the https/tls settings are not right. The bin (ejbca.ear) file can not configure TLS in WildFly, you can automate it in your container for sure. The message: WARNING: An illegal reflective access operation has occurred has nothing todo with this, this is completely harmless. You need to look elsewhere in the log for the description about TLS. title: Issue with Subject Alternative Names and re-key
body_text:
I have been testing CMP for OpenSSL using the [generic CMP client ](https://github.com/siemens/gencmpclient) and run into some trouble with Key Update Request (KUR) messages where the end entity has a DNS name set as the SAN which matches their CN.  In end-entity profile I have:_x000D_
Subject Alternative Name: DNS Name_x000D_
- [x] Use entity CN field _x000D_
- [ ] Required_x000D_
- [x] Modifiable_x000D_
- [ ] Validation_x000D_
_x000D_
My Initialisation Request seems to work fine but the KUR constantly fails with_x000D_
_x000D_
> ERROR: received PKIStatus: rejection; PKIFailureInfo: badRequest; StatusString: "Wrong number of DNSNAME fields in Subject Alternative Name."_x000D_
_x000D_
I have tried multiple variations of the config above and I can't seem to get it to work.  IR and KUR when I remove the SAN config work fine._x000D_
_x000D_
I have also tried to rekey manually by uploading a CSR to the web portal.  But when I tried to change the status of the end-entity to new I got a similar message, see attached._x000D_
![EJBCA](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23117233/149959197-3dd78407-8e2d-4bd2-bf5e-196341b7baab.PNG)_x000D_
_x000D_
Not sure whether this is a problem with my configuration or a bug so any help would be appreciated._x000D_

title: Publish artifacts to a server using SCP
body_text:
EJBCA Enterprise contains a publisher called "SCP publisher" which can publish CRLs and certificates to another server using SCP._x000D_
_x000D_
It would be nice to have something similar in EJBCA Community. The publisher in EJBCA Enterprise also has certain limitations, e.g. it publishes the certificates as a serialised Java objects which makes it difficult to read them with a non-Java application. It could also be useful to be able to invoke a script after the publisher has completed._x000D_
_x000D_
There is a library here on GitHub called [sshj](https://github.com/hierynomus/sshj) which provides an SCP client for Java._x000D_
_x000D_
The publisher could be written as a plugin by adding a class to the ``org.ejbca.scp.publisher`` package. For example:_x000D_
```_x000D_
public class ScpPublisherv2 extends CustomPublisherContainer implements ICustomPublisher, CustomPublisherUiSupport {_x000D_
    // Implementation goes here_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Here are some features which would be nice to have:_x000D_
_x000D_
- Support publishing of CRLs, certificates and pre-produced OCSP responses_x000D_
- Attempt to create the specified directory if it does not exist_x000D_
- Support the following variables in path:_x000D_
    * ISO_TIMESTAMP, e.g. 2022-01-01T13:37_x000D_
    * ISSUER_DN, e.g. CN=Foo CA,O=Foo AB,C=SE_x000D_
    * ISSUER_CN, e.g. Foo CA_x000D_
    * SERIAL_NUMBER (only for certificates), e.g. 0E34CB12_x000D_
    * CRL_NUMBER (only for CRLs), e.g. 3_x000D_
- Atomic publishing by transferring to a temporary directory and then moving the file to the correct location_x000D_
- Optionally invoke the specified script after publishing_x000D_
- Authenticate with a private key which is either uploaded as a file or pasted in a textbox_x000D_
- The button "Save and test connection" should print the current public key fingerprint of the server_x000D_
- The button "Save" should cache the current public key fingerprint_x000D_
_x000D_
With these features supported, the following information needs to be specified by the CA administrator:_x000D_
_x000D_
- SSH username_x000D_
- IP or hostname_x000D_
- Port number_x000D_
- The name of the directories where the artifacts will be published_x000D_
- A private key_x000D_
- The password of the private key_x000D_
- The name of the script to invoke after publishing

title: EJBCA 7.9.0.x community edition deployment issues
body_text:
This is something that I am not really familiar with, but I banged my head against the wall some days and nights because of this. Of course I might have missed something that is obvious for everyone else._x000D_
_x000D_
Following the deployment instructions "ant deploy-keystore" copies the two files to Wildfly .../keystore as "*.jks" while the instructions to configure Wildfly 24 refer to the same files as "*.p12".  The deployment succeeds but nothing works as for some weird reason Wildfly startup doesn't fail if the configured certificates are missing._x000D_
_x000D_
As the next step, while finally after endless troubleshooting I found this issue, my .p12 files were owned by root. Then at least Wildfly finally failed to start up. So chown wildfly.wildfly .../keystore/*.p12 would also be needed to do a successful setup after the files have been named correctly._x000D_
_x000D_
A smaller issue is that whatever configuration files you put into /opt/ejbca-custom are copied by ant to /opt/ejbca/ instead of /opt/ejbca/conf where they are actually read from during the configuration and installation.
top_3_comments_text: primetomas: For the ejbca-custom question I can answer. Everything under ejbca-custom is copied "as-is", i.e. you should place modified properties files under /opt/ejbca-custom/cont. This enables _any_ files to be modified. title: I can't access superadmin console
body_text:
Hello, I have installed the docker version of ejbca, with the Quick Start: Classic Workflow, with the command line_x000D_
`docker run -it --rm -p 80:8080 -p 443:8443 -h mycahostname keyfactor/ejbca-ce`_x000D_
I am able to access and download the superadmin.p12 certificate and import it into my browser, however it does not allow me to access the ejbca admin console "https://localhost/ejbca/adminweb/" I get the message "Authorization Denied_x000D_
No client certificate was presented". Can you help me please?
top_3_comments_text: pkmarios: Did the browser prompt for a certificate authentication at all? This is probably related to your browser is set to not send a client certificate for 'localhost' per se, or a different certificate is already configured to authenticate with localhost, mostly from a previous run. On a general note, each new run _(per the given command)_ will generate a fresh superadmin from a fresh CA, using `--rm` will make it ephemeral, so the previous runs' superadmin(s) won't work. A few possible tracking approaches: - Try a Private/Incognito Window and select the correct superadmin from the same run, or use a different browser. - Use the machine hostname instead of 'localhost' or the local network IP, so if 'localhost' is currently bound to another imported certificate, this should make the browser to prompt anew. - Start over clean: 1. Stop any ejbca running container 2. Assuming Firefox → Settings → Privacy & Security → View Certificates → Your Certificates → Under EJBCA Container Quickstart → Remove all previous superadmin(s) - if any 3. Same dialog → Authentication Decisions tab → select and delete all lines with Host: localhost 4. Close all tabs and windows 5. Run a new container and a new browser window → enroll the superadmin p12 → import it to the browser → go to https://localhost/ejbca/adminweb/ → Select the superadmin certificate when prompted - P.S. Alternatively, ignore steps 2-3 and create a new Firefox profile. That said, for testing only you could also omit using client SuperAdmin authentication to start with: `docker run -it --rm -p 80:8080 -p 443:8443 -h mycahostname -e TLS_SETUP_ENABLED="simple" keyfactor/ejbca-ce` Then navigate to adminweb and click cancel if/when prompted for a certificate authentication. | jhondari1989: I have solved it, when selecting the algorithm select RSA 2048 and it worked. Thanks. | primetomas: Great. Thanks.

title: NullPointerException while editing End Entity
body_text:
I am using EJBCA 7.9.0.2 Community and am getting NullPointerException after I hit "Save" in End Entity edit page. This End Entity uses subAltNames (DNS Names)._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException_x000D_
	at org.cesecore.util.CertTools.isAllDNSNamesExcluded(CertTools.java:4746)_x000D_
	at org.cesecore.util.CertTools.checkNameConstraints(CertTools.java:4726)_x000D_
	at org.ejbca.core.ejb.ra.EndEntityManagementSessionBean.changeUser(EndEntityManagementSessionBean.java:930)_x000D_
```_x000D_
checkNameConstraints() has an explicit check for variable "excluded" not being null before executing bunch of code, however later it misses such check before invoking isAllDNSNamesExcluded(excluded), which by itself does not expect its parameter to be null._x000D_
_x000D_

title: URLs in [?]-buttons do not work with confluence-based documentation
body_text:
**Summary**:_x000D_
- during the migration to confluence docs, the paths to subpages changed, and this has not been updated in the `[?]` buttons in the web-UI._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment**:_x000D_
- EJBCA-CE 7.9.0.2_x000D_
- WildFly 24.0.1.Final_x000D_
- RHEL 8.6 x86_64_x000D_
_x000D_
**Details**:_x000D_
_x000D_
As a workaround for issue #80, we tried to change `web.docbaseuri` in the `web.properties` file from `internal` to the URL of the online documentation. _x000D_
_x000D_
After a rebuild, the links to documentation in the web UI now point there, but the direct links are still broken: For example, clicking on the `[?]` at adminweb/home -> CA Status links to `https://doc.primekey.com/ejbca790/doc/CA_Operations_Guide.html#CA%20Status`, but this page does not exist in the online documentation (and neither do any other pages that are linked to in the ?-buttons). _x000D_
_x000D_
It should be `https://doc.primekey.com/ejbca790/ejbca-operations/ejbca-operations-guide/ca-operations-guide/ejbca-overview-page#EJBCAOverviewPage-CAStatus`. (I checked this by manually searching through the documentation)_x000D_
_x000D_
All documentation paths should probably be updated to reflect their new URLs.

It's a bit tricky now since the documentation built into the zip release as sf.net does have the URLs and anchors. https://sourceforge.net/projects/ejbca/files/ejbca7/ I created this issue: https://jira.primekey.se/browse/ECA-10907 | uedvt359: With this zip from SF, the documentation paths are better, but still not 100% correct. Using the same example as above: the ? next to `CA Status` on /ejbca/adminweb/ links to `/ejbca/doc/CA_Operations_Guide.html#CA%20Status`. This page exists now (yay), but the documentation for lives at a subpage of the Operations Guide, at `/ejbca/doc/EJBCA_Overview_Page.html`. Also, the anchor is now `#src-108529490_id-.EJBCAOverviewPagev7.5.0-CAStatus`, so even if the URL were correct, it would not jump to the correct position. I guess that is just how the confluence export works; maybe they could be massaged after the export into something stable. Again, thanks: This is already way better, now that we know how to get the local documentation at all. It seems, the paths in the online documentation are just different and incompatible. I would suggest removing the default external URL from the web.properties.sample file, to avoid confusion. | primetomas: Thanks for the suggestion, we'll track it and try to figure out a good way in the future. The anchors where changed when moving to confluence, which allowed the documentation to be much better, but not as good support for anchors...it's something we are aware one but hasn't been trivial to fix, and not highest priority unfortunately.

title: Publish JAR artifacts to OSSRH
body_text:
Hi, would it be possible to have EJBCA artifacts published to [OSSRH](https://central.sonatype.org/publish/publish-guide/), so that they can be included in pom.xml?_x000D_
_x000D_
I'm primarily looking for the ``ejbca-common`` artifact which is needed when developing EJBCA plugins.
top_3_comments_text: Realiserad: To expand on the plugin part. If you want to develop a custom publisher for EJBCA - using let's say Maven - you would need to provide the following jars at compile time: ```xml <dependency> <groupId>org.ejbca</groupId> <artifactId>ejbca-common</artifactId> <version>7.10.0.2</version> <scope>provided</scope> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>org.cesecore</groupId> <artifactId>cesecore-common</artifactId> <version>7.10.0.2</version> <scope>provided</scope> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>org.cesecore</groupId> <artifactId>cesecore-entity</artifactId> <version>7.10.0.2</version> <scope>provided</scope> </dependency> ``` The jars ``ejbca-common`` and ``cesecore-common`` can be found in Maven Central, but they are old, so I ended up building my own jars from source. There is no ant target for ``cesecore-entity`` so you need to rip it out from ``ejbca.ear``. In addition to our mail to support@keyfactor.com:_x000D_
_x000D_
today we edited the CT Logs in our ejbca production installation. We added 7 new entries for 2024. Since the ones from letsencrypt are now split into two (2024h1 and 2024h2), we used the log sharding feature:_x000D_

This happens in the `start.sh` when running the ejbca docker image. The start script tries to read the memory limits to set the proper -xmx args to start the JVM. hablutzel1: I've just stumbled upon this on a Debian 11 Docker host, which uses cgroup v2 by default (see https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/blob/main/docs/cgroup-v2.md). The following patch fixes this: ```patch --- a/start.sh +++ b/start.sh @@ -99,9 +99,16 @@ fi # Calculate memory available to the container -memCgroup=$(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes) +if [ -f /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes ] ; then + memCgroup=$(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes) +elif [ -f /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max ] ; then + memCgroup=$(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max) +else + log "ERROR" "Expected cgroup file not found. Aborting startup." + exit 1 +fi memTotal=$(cat /proc/meminfo | awk '/MemTotal/ {print $2*1024}') -if [ ${memCgroup:-0} != -1 ] && [ ${memCgroup:-0} -lt ${memTotal} ] ; then +if [ $memCgroup != -1 ] && [ $memCgroup != "max" ] && [ $memCgroup -lt ${memTotal} ] ; then memLimit=${memCgroup} log "INFO" "Detected $memLimit bytes available memory assigned to this container." else ```

title: SCP Publisher not working with server using OpenSSL 8.8+
body_text:
Tried setting up the SCP publisher to publish CRLs to a web server running Ubuntu 22.04, which ships with OpenSSH 8.9. OpenSSH 8.8 changed the default security settings to not allow `ssh-rsa` and instead require `rsa-sha2-256` or `rsa-sha2-512`. Ended up getting this error:_x000D_
```_x000D_
2023-02-20 07:38:06,291+0000 INFO  [org.ejbca.scp.publisher.ScpPublisher] (default task-1) Could not connect to CRL destination. Auth fail_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
On the web server, I can see this in `/var/log/auth.log`_x000D_
```_x000D_
Feb 20 07:38:06 hostname sshd[1904715]: userauth_pubkey: key type ssh-rsa not in PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms [preauth]_x000D_
Feb 20 07:38:06 hostname sshd[1904715]: error: Received disconnect from 10.0.0.0 port 49636:3: com.jcraft.jsch.JSchException: Auth fail [preauth]_x000D_
Feb 20 07:38:06 hostname sshd[1904715]: Disconnected from authenticating user username 10.0.0.0 port 49636 [preauth]_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I'd rather not change the security settings on my web server to allow the less secure signature if I can avoid it._x000D_
_x000D_
The JSch library being used in EJBCA does not support the more secure key signature types and hasn't been updated since 2018. There is a fork available that is actively maintained and adds support for newer key signature types, but has `ssh-rsa` support disabled by default, so I don't know what the customer impact of replacing the library here would be. It's otherwise supposed to be a drop in replacement._x000D_
_x000D_
From the OpenSSH changelog:_x000D_
OpenSSH has supported [RFC8332](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8332) RSA/SHA-256/512 signatures since release 7.2 and existing ssh-rsa keys will automatically use the stronger algorithm where possible._x000D_
_x000D_
OpenSSH 7.2 was released in Feb 2016._x000D_
_x000D_
Are there any objections to upgrading this library?_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/mwiede/jsch

title: Error when building version 8.0.0 with Java 11
body_text:
I am trying to upgrade my EJBCA deployment from version 7.11.0 to the newest 8.0.0. As I can see on the [release notes](https://doc.primekey.com/ejbca/ejbca-release-information/ejbca-release-notes/ejbca-8-0-release-notes#EJBCA8.0ReleaseNotes-RunningonJava8notsupported), Java version 8 (which I was using) is now deprecated, so I previously upgraded to Java 11._x000D_
_x000D_
My problem comes when executing ```ant deployear``` to start the new deployment. When it starts to build the ```admin-gui``` module, inside the ```setup``` target, ```ant``` calls a module called ```native2ascii```. As I have been researching online, this was deprecated all the way back in Java 9 [(link)](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8074431)._x000D_
```_x000D_
<native2ascii encoding="UTF-8"_x000D_
    src="${admin-gui.resources.dir}/languages"_x000D_
    dest="${admin-gui.build.dir}/languages"_x000D_
    includes="languagefile.*.properties" _x000D_
    excludes="languagefile.zh.properties"_x000D_
/>_x000D_
<native2ascii encoding="GBK"_x000D_
    src="${admin-gui.resources.dir}/languages"_x000D_
    dest="${admin-gui.build.dir}/languages"_x000D_
    includes="languagefile.zh.properties" _x000D_
/>_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I found two alternatives that helped me:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Manually copying the related files (those called ```languagefile.*.properties``` inside the resources folder to the build folder) and commenting this target._x000D_
2. Modifying this targets to use the ```copy``` module instead:_x000D_
```_x000D_
<copy todir="${admin-gui.build.dir}/languages" >_x000D_
    <fileset dir="${admin-gui.resources.dir}/languages" includes="languagefile.*.properties"/>  _x000D_
</copy>_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Both allow the compilation and deployment to continue and finish successfully._x000D_
_x000D_
My question is if this is the method to be used, or if I am doing something wrong when it comes to deploying the application. Furthermore, I wonder if the ```build.xml``` for the ```admin-gui``` module needs to be modified for future releases._x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks in advance

title: Allow merge DNs not working correctly with SubjectAltNames
body_text:
Hi,_x000D_
Noticed some issues when importing certificates which included SANs. The EE Policy I was using had the 'Allow Merge DNs across all interfaces" activated. I thought this setting only affected the Subject DN, but it turns out it also affects SANs (**Note**: This should be mentioned in the documentation).  _x000D_
_x000D_
The error when importing a certificate was:_x000D_
`ERROR: org.ejbca.core.model.ra.raadmin.EndEntityProfileValidationException: Wrong number of DNSNAME fields in Subject Alternative Name.`_x000D_
_x000D_
There is a DEBUG message that helped to understand the issue:_x000D_
`DEBUG [org.ejbca.core.model.ra.EndEntityInformationFiller] (default task-5) merged dn: DNSNAME=test.org.au,dNSName=test.org.au`_x000D_
Note that 'merged dn' has two entries with the same value, but one is referenced/keyed as "**DNSNAME**" and the other "**dNSName**"._x000D_
_x000D_
The code at EndEntityInformationFiller.mergedDnString()  is adding the SAN's default value from the EE Policy as "DNSNAME", and then adding the SAN's value from the certificate as "dNSName". As these strings are different case, this is preventing the code to merge properly._x000D_
_x000D_
A fix to this issue is to ensure the 'key' string is made UPPERCASE, so the "dNSNAME" becomes "DNSNAME". This is quite easy as there is a 'getBcNameStyle()' method which is easily modified: _x000D_
```_x000D_
    private static String getBcNameStyle(String parameter, String entityType) {_x000D_
        if(entityType.equals(SUBJECT_ALTERNATIVE_NAME)) {_x000D_
            // The SAN's type name needs to be UPPERCASE, so it matches with the EE policy. _x000D_
            return parameter.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);_x000D_
            //return parameter;_x000D_
        }_x000D_
        return BC_STYLE_PARAMETERS.getOrDefault(parameter.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), parameter.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));_x000D_
    }_x000D_
```_x000D_
Now, when I import the same certificate, the debug message looks much better, and the certificate import works:_x000D_
`DEBUG [org.ejbca.core.model.ra.EndEntityInformationFiller] (default task-1) merged dn: DNSNAME=test.org.au`_x000D_
_x000D_
I also had a look at the Unit tests for this 'mergeDnString' method, but there wasn't any. So I prepared a few tests:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
    @Test_x000D_
    public void testMergeAltName() {_x000D_
        //TODO_x000D_
        // Order changed when I did the "fix"_x000D_
        // assertEquals("rfc822Name=foo@bar.com,dnsName=foo.bar.com,dnsName=foo1.bar.com", data.getSubjectAltName());_x000D_
        // ->dnsName=foo1.bar.com,dnsName=foo.bar.com,rfc822Name=foo@bar.com_x000D_
        _x000D_
        // Test the merge operation with SANs_x000D_
        //_x000D_
        _x000D_
        // Add a SAN (dnsName) to the EE Policy_x000D_
        profile.addField(DnComponents.DNSNAME);_x000D_
        // Set default value and make it not modifiable_x000D_
        profile.setValue(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 0, "test.org");_x000D_
        profile.setModifyable(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 0, false);_x000D_
        _x000D_
        try {_x000D_
            // Test the DN type name can have any case._x000D_
            String sMergedAltName = EndEntityInformationFiller.mergeDnString("dnsName=test.org",profile, EndEntityInformationFiller.SUBJECT_ALTERNATIVE_NAME, null);_x000D_
            assertEquals( "Merged DNSNAME should not change.", "DNSNAME=test.org", sMergedAltName);_x000D_
            _x000D_
            // Test the User cannot override the policy if the field is fixed (not-modifiable)._x000D_
            try {_x000D_
                sMergedAltName = EndEntityInformationFiller.mergeDnString("dnsName=test1.org",profile, EndEntityInformationFiller.SUBJECT_ALTERNATIVE_NAME, null);_x000D_
            } catch (EndEntityProfileValidationException e1) {_x000D_
                assertEquals( "Exception thrown with message", "User DN has too many components for DNSNAME", e1.getMessage());_x000D_
            }_x000D_
_x000D_
            // Test the User can override the policy if the field is modifiable._x000D_
            profile.setModifyable(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 0, true);_x000D_
            sMergedAltName = EndEntityInformationFiller.mergeDnString("dnsName=test1.org",profile, EndEntityInformationFiller.SUBJECT_ALTERNATIVE_NAME, null);_x000D_
            assertEquals( "Merged DNSNAME should be the User's value.", "DNSNAME=test1.org", sMergedAltName);_x000D_
_x000D_
            _x000D_
            // Tests with two SANs of the same type, one fixed and the other modifiable_x000D_
            profile.addField(DnComponents.DNSNAME);_x000D_
            profile.setValue(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 1, "changeme.org");_x000D_
            profile.setModifyable(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 1, true);_x000D_
            profile.setModifyable(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 0, false);_x000D_
            sMergedAltName = EndEntityInformationFiller.mergeDnString("dnsName=test1.org",profile, EndEntityInformationFiller.SUBJECT_ALTERNATIVE_NAME, null);_x000D_
            assertEquals( "Merged DNSNAME should have two values.", "DNSNAME=test1.org,DNSNAME=test.org", sMergedAltName);_x000D_
            _x000D_
            // Remove 2nd DNSNAME_x000D_
            profile.removeField(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 1);_x000D_
            _x000D_
            // Test two types of SANs_x000D_
            profile.addField(DnComponents.DIRECTORYNAME);_x000D_
            profile.setValue(DnComponents.DIRECTORYNAME, 0, "CN=Test,O=org");_x000D_
            profile.setModifyable(DnComponents.DIRECTORYNAME, 0, true);_x000D_
            profile.setModifyable(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 0, true);_x000D_
           _x000D_
            sMergedAltName = EndEntityInformationFiller.mergeDnString("dnsName=test1.org,directoryName=cn=Test One,O=Org",profile, EndEntityInformationFiller.SUBJECT_ALTERNATIVE_NAME, null);_x000D_
            assertEquals( "Merged DNSNAME should have two types, both values override defaults.", "DNSNAME=test1.org,DIRECTORYNAME=cn=Test One,O=Org", sMergedAltName);_x000D_
           _x000D_
            sMergedAltName = EndEntityInformationFiller.mergeDnString("dnsName=test1.org",profile, EndEntityInformationFiller.SUBJECT_ALTERNATIVE_NAME, null);_x000D_
            assertEquals( "Merged DNSNAME should have two types, one value overrides default.", "DNSNAME=test1.org,DIRECTORYNAME=CN=Test,O=org", sMergedAltName);_x000D_
_x000D_
            // Remove the DIRECTORYNAME_x000D_
            profile.removeField(DnComponents.DIRECTORYNAME, 0);_x000D_
_x000D_
            _x000D_
        } catch (EndEntityProfileValidationException e) {_x000D_
            fail("Exception not expected: "+e.getMessage());_x000D_
            _x000D_
        }_x000D_
        _x000D_
        // Cleanup_x000D_
        profile.removeField(DnComponents.DNSNAME, 0);_x000D_
_x000D_
    }_x000D_
```_x000D_

title: Unable to restart container when Security parameters are set
body_text:
When the security parameters "PASSWORD_ENCRYPTION_KEY" and "CA_KEYSTOREPASS" are set in a environment variable, it's only possible to stop and remove the container. A restart makes the cryptotokens not readable. _x000D_

`PKCS12 key store mac invalid - wrong password or corrupted file`_x000D_
_x000D_
In the startup script "after-init-app.sh" these variables are copied to the end of "/ejbca/conf/cesecore.properties". In the case of a restart these variables are copied again. This results in a cesecore.properties file like this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```\# Allow override of CESeCore config files from /etc/cesecore/conf/_x000D_
allow.external-dynamic.configuration=true_x000D_
_x000D_
\# Optimization for fresh installations on EJBCA 6+_x000D_
db.keepinternalcakeystores=false_x000D_
_x000D_
\# All security log events are written to all enabled/configured devices._x000D_
\# The following AuditLogDevice implementations are available:_x000D_
\#securityeventsaudit.implementation.X=org.cesecore.audit.impl.log4j.Log4jDevice_x000D_
\#securityeventsaudit.implementation.X=org.cesecore.audit.impl.integrityprotected.IntegrityProtectedDevice_x000D_
_x000D_
securityeventsaudit.implementation.1=null_x000D_
_x000D_
\# Nodeid used for integrity protected audit log. If not set the hostname of local host is used._x000D_
\# Default: not set_x000D_
password.encryption.key=encryptionkey_x000D_
password.encryption.key=encryptionkey_x000D_
password.encryption.key=encryptionkey _x000D_
```_x000D_
My compose file:_x000D_
```_x000D_
version: '3.9'_x000D_
services:_x000D_
    ejbca-ce:_x000D_
        image: keyfactor/ejbca-ce:latest_x000D_
        hostname: localhost_x000D_
        environment:_x000D_
          - DATABASE_PASSWORD=databasepassword_x000D_
          - DATABASE_USER=ejbca_x000D_
          - 'DATABASE_JDBC_URL=jdbc:mysql://ejbca-db:3306/ejbca?characterEncoding=UTF-8'_x000D_
          - TLS_SETUP_ENABLED=simple_x000D_
          - PASSWORD_ENCRYPTION_KEY=encryptionkey                 _x000D_
        ports:_x000D_
          - 8443:8443_x000D_
        restart: unless-stopped_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
After a `docker compose restart` the cryptotokens are not readable. After a `docker compose down` and `docker compose up -d` everything is back to normal._x000D_
_x000D_
I guess that was also the case in #293 but it was not a problem with the imported CA keystore._x000D_

title: Error in SystemTest Build script
body_text:
In ./modules/systemtests/build.xml, the following section includes an OCSP test, but the reference states "scep" rather than "ocsp" (see 2nd "<include name=  >) in code fragment below"._x000D_
_x000D_

	<target name="runweb" depends="build, assert-appserverrunning" description="Run web-realted system tests">_x000D_

				<path refid="systemtests.classpath" />_x000D_

			<jvmarg line="${tests.jvmargs.endorsed}"/>_x000D_
			<formatter type="xml" />_x000D_
			<batchtest fork="yes" todir="${reports.dir}">_x000D_
				<fileset dir="${systemtests.build.test.dir}">_x000D_
					<include name="org/ejbca/core/protocol/scep/ProtocolScepHttpTest.class" />_x000D_

>    The sender field contains the name of the sender of the PKIMessage._x000D_

title: Honor TryCount in PublisherQueue FIFO list
body_text:
Currently entries of the publisher queue are strictly handled by FIFO. This is reflected in the [findDataByPublisherIdAndStatus](https://github.com/Keyfactor/ejbca-ce/blob/main/modules/ejbca-entity/src/org/ejbca/core/ejb/ca/publisher/PublisherQueueData.java#L310) which use the select_x000D_
_x000D_
`SELECT a FROM PublisherQueueData a WHERE a.publisherId=:publisherId AND a.publishStatus=:publishStatus ORDER BY a.timeCreated DESC`_x000D_
_x000D_
to get data. This means that newest entries are returned first._x000D_
_x000D_
Now if you have 10 or more "new" entries in your queue which cannot be published no "older" entry will ever be published using the queue since [shouldBreakPublishingOperation](https://github.com/Keyfactor/ejbca-ce/blob/main/modules/ejbca-ejb-interface/src/org/ejbca/core/ejb/ca/publisher/PublishingResult.java#L63) in PublisherResult will always fail after the first 10 entries._x000D_
_x000D_
My suggestion now is to honor the trycounter in the select and try to publish entries with lower trycounter first. This would lead to a select like_x000D_
_x000D_
`SELECT a FROM PublisherQueueData a WHERE a.publisherId=:publisherId AND a.publishStatus=:publishStatus ORDER BY a.tryCounter, a.timeCreated DESC`_x000D_
_x000D_
This would allow to publish entries with lower trycounter first and do not stall the queue if the newest 10 entries are failing._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

title: [BUG] java.lang.OutOfMemoryError caused by low MaxMetaspaceSize
body_text:
**Describe the Bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
We noticed that since recently, EJBCA runs out of memory when searching certificates through the API (querying /ejbca/ejbca-rest-api/v2/certificate/search), as well as when looking at the audit log. _x000D_
_x000D_
We noticed that the Metaspace Utilisation is already at the limit (`MC` is in kB, 262144/1024=256; configured limit was 256MB):_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
[root@ejbca02 bin]# jstat -gcmetacapacity `pidof java`_x000D_
   MCMN       MCMX        MC       CCSMN      CCSMX       CCSC     YGC   FGC    FGCT     GCT   _x000D_
       0.0  1277952.0   262144.0        0.0  1048576.0    33792.0  2913   491  398.453  921.049_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
A simple service restart did bring it down again below the limit (`MC`=195968.0 immediately after restart), but that's still cutting it extremely close._x000D_
 _x000D_
We have "fixed" this by increasing ` -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize` to `1536m` (from `256m`), half of the `{{HEAP_SIZE}}` of 3gig we set._x000D_
_x000D_
**I'm opening this ticket because the value of 256 MB was taken directly from the [ejbca wildfly setup docs](https://doc.primekey.com/ejbca/ejbca-installation/application-servers/wildfly-26) and we believe this should be increased in the documentation to avoid this pitfall in the future.** _x000D_
_x000D_
This random [Stackoverflow answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/57329582) suggests setting this to half the heap size limit, which also suggests that the documented limit is way too low._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
It'll unlikely be reproducable unless you run into the limit, but just opening  https://ejbca.xxx:8443/ejbca/adminweb/audit/search.xhtml or the snippet below already triggered it for us:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
endentityProfile=..._x000D_
commonName=..._x000D_
curl -Epkcs11: "https://ejbca.xxx/ejbca/ejbca-rest-api/v2/certificate/search" -d '{_x000D_

        {"property": "STATUS", "operation": "EQUAL", "value": "CERT_ACTIVE"},_x000D_
    ],_x000D_
    "sort": {"property": "ISSUED_DATE", "operation": "DESC"},_x000D_
    "pagination": {"page_size": 1, "current_page": 1}_x000D_
}'_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected Behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
not to run out of memory :\^)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Screenshots and Logs**_x000D_
_x000D_
wildfly's `server.log` for api request:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2024-02-20 09:09:56,681 INFO  [org.ejbca.core.model.era.RaMasterApiSessionBean] (default task-2762) formed query: SELECT a.username FROM UserData a WHERE (a.caId IN (:caId)) AND (UPPER(a.subjectDN) LIKE :subjectDN OR a.subjectAltName LIKE :subjectAltName OR UPPER(a.username) LIKE :username)_x000D_

title: Using random hexadecimal strings for passwords can cause the build and install process to fail
body_text:
**Describe the Bug**_x000D_
I'm in the process of writing a build script to install and deploy EJBCA CE (8.2.0.1) under Wildfly (26.1.3) running with Java 11. _x000D_
_x000D_
Following the [documentation](https://doc.primekey.com/ejbca/ejbca-installation/application-servers/wildfly-26) for configuring Wildfly and EJBCA I discovered an issue when generating random secure passwords for the truststore between EJBCA and Wildfly. _x000D_
_x000D_
If the password I generate is all hexadecimal characters and the length is a multiple of 32, the underlying library (cesecore-common/src/org/cesecore/util/StringTools.java) interprets this password as being already encrypted, and throws the following exception from the passwordDecryption function:_x000D_
_x000D_
`Password decryption failed. 'password.encryption.key' might have been modified more than once.`_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
From a fresh server:_x000D_
1. Download and install all dependencies (database of choice, OpenJDK 11)_x000D_

title: allow username and password while generating certificate from ejbca
body_text:
### Description_x000D_
_x000D_
The `ejbca_certificate` module is an essential tool for managing EJBCA certificates using Ansible. However, the current implementation of the module requires the username and password to be hardcoded within the module itself. This restricts the user from providing custom credentials, potentially leading to security vulnerabilities and limitations in flexibility._x000D_
_x000D_
### Proposed Solution_x000D_
I propose that the `ejbca_certificate` module be updated to allow users to pass custom username and password parameters. This can be achieved by modifying the module to accept these parameters as variables, rather than hardcoding them within the module._x000D_

title: [BUG] "Approve actions" list is empty
body_text:
There seems to be an issue about approval request listing_x000D_
_x000D_
**Context**_x000D_
_x000D_
We have an approval profile enabled on a certificate profile for "Add/Edit End Entity"._x000D_
It's a simple partition approval. It can be seen by anybody and one role "validator" can approve._x000D_
When an end entity is set to "new", mail is correctly sent._x000D_
_x000D_
**Behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
- On `/adminweb/approval/approvalactions.xhtml`, no approval request is listed (with either superadmin or validator role)._x000D_
- On `/ra/managerequests.xhtml?tab=to_approve`, no approval request is listed (with either superadmin or validator role)._x000D_
- On `/ra/managerequests.xhtml?tab=pending`, superadmin can see the "Waiting for Approval" request, and validator see nothing._x000D_
- On `/ra/managerequests.xhtml?tab=custom_search`, the "Waiting for Approval" request is listed for superadmin and validator. The validator **can review and approve**._x000D_
_x000D_
**Deployment**_x000D_
_x000D_
Software, EJBCA 8.2.0.1 and 8.3.2 Community_x000D_

The doc page `Managing_Requests_in_the_RA_UI.html` says different things about pending approval: * At the beginning of the page: "_lists currently pending requests you have access to view, including those that you may approve yourself_" * At the end of the page: "_this tab displays the requests that you have made, and that are waiting for approval by another administrator_" The 2nd sentence seems to comply with the code. Realiserad: The memory calculation for the JVM running EJBCA is done in the `start.sh` script by manually inspecting files in `cgroupfs`. It cannot gobble up all resources detected ([the default behaviour](https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2022/04/19/java-17-whats-new-openjdks-container-awareness#recent_changes_in_openjdk_s_container_awareness_code)) as there may be other processes running inside the container. 'data-source add --name=ejbcads --connection-url="jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1/ejbca" --jndi-name="java:/EjbcaDS" --use-ccm=true --driver-name="org.postgresql.Driver.jar" '/subsystem=elytron/server-ssl-context=httpspub:add(key-manager=httpsKM,protocols=["TLSv1.3","TLSv1.2"],use-cipher-suites-order=false,cipher-suite-filter="TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256",cipher-suite-names="TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256")' ./bin/jboss-cli.bat --connect '/subsystem=elytron/server-ssl-context=httpspriv:add(key-manager=httpsKM,protocols=["TLSv1.3","TLSv1.2"],use-cipher-suites-order=false,cipher-suite-filter="TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256",cipher-suite-names="TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256",trust-manager=httpsTM,need-client-auth=true)' --connect '/subsystem=undertow/server=default-server/https-listener=httpspriv:add(socket-binding="httpspriv", ssl-context="httpspriv", max-parameters=2048)' ./bin/jboss-cli.bat --connect ':reload' ### body_text:
**Describe the Bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Hi, I am using 2 tier PKI infrastructure where we have both PKIRootCA and PKISubCA. I am running Network policy server on windows server 2022 for authentication. I have the supplicant machine running on Ubtunu version 24.04.1 LTS. There is a fibrolan switch which acts as an authenticator and connects both supplicant and authentication server which is in our case is Microsoft server 2022._x000D_
I generated 2 certificates for client (ubuntu) and server (windows server 2022). I then installed complete chain of certificate in PK7 format on server and installed specific rootCA certificate in trusted zone and subCA certificate in intermediate certificate authority._x000D_
On those certificate, I just defined CN name for both server and client which I have configured the hostname. Eg. the server NPS server hostname is radius.testbed.local which is also a domain controller (testbed.local) and the client has CN name (dot1x-thinkpad) and thats the CN for the client I have defined in the client certificate._x000D_
_x000D_
I tried my level best to get this sorted but couldn't and finally raised a ticket to Microsoft support and they checked server configuration and found no issue there and ask me to contact EJBCA since there might be an issue with the certificate. primetomas: I start with client certificate. Client certificate is issued by the SubCA. But CDP seem to point to Root CA: X509v3 CRL Distribution Points: Full Name: URI:http://172.17.21.65/ejbca/publicweb/crls/search.cgi?iHash=pmTlWoFwLTY/OG1B3U50KIneqzs CRL Issuer: DirName:CN = My PKI Root CA-G1, O = MTI, C = DK The client certificate is issued by the SubCA, and it's CDP should therefore point to the CRL issued by the SubCA. Also "keyEncipherment" is not an allowed keyUsage for EC keys. Remove that. The CDP does not conform to RFC5280 with usage of both URI and CRLIssuer: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.13 "If the certificate issuer is also the CRL issuer, then conforming CAs MUST omit the cRLIssuer field and MUST include the distributionPoint field." As I assume that the certificate issuer and the CRL issuer are the same here, as this is the only option EJBCA supports (and the only option used in all relevant PKIs you can find).

title: EJBCA Upgrade from 8.2 to 8.3 fail - Certificates disappear from RA web
body_text:
I have a local installation of EJBCA CE in a local VM. It was running version 8.2.0.1 correctly. I tried to upgrade to 8.3.2 and it seemingly performed said upgrade correctly. However, when I went to the RA web, I could not see any certificates, no matter the filters I tried. I then went back to the 8.2.0.1 folder and after deploying it again, the certificates appeared, which means they are not removed in the database._x000D_
_x000D_
I tried to upgrade via the intermediate 8.3.1 version, which showed the same error._x000D_
_x000D_
I copied the configuration files from the previous folder, and no changes to the database were made. Plus, as I said the certificates are stored correctly it seems. No other error was found related to the database, PKCS11 or any other aspect I checked. The VM is running SLES 12._x000D_

title: [BUG] EJBCA instance needs restart before SuperAdmin certificate can be used
body_text: **Describe the Bug** After setting up a fresh EJBCA instance in docker with a superadmin user, it's not possible to access EJBCA WebUI or the REST API using the p12 file of the superadmin. When doing so, EJBCA always responds with an empty response / closes the connection. The EJBCA instance needs to be restarted first and after the restart the instance can be accessed with the superadmin user **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start EJBCA container with version 9.0.0 with TLS setup set to simple 2. Generate the SuperAdmin user 3. Add the Super Admin user to the Super Administrator group 4. Try to access EJBCA with the SuperAdmin.p12. You can either try to access the WebUI which will fail, or try to access the REST API using nodejs: ``` import axios from "axios"; import { Agent } from "https"; import { readFile } from "fs/promises"; console.log( JSON.stringify( ( await axios.get( "https://ca.localtest.me:8443/ejbca/ejbca-rest-api/v1/ca", { httpsAgent: new Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: true, pfx: await readFile("./certs/SuperAdmin.p12"), passphrase: "test", }), } ) ).data ) ); ``` **Expected Behavior** I woulde expect EJBCA to work right after creating the SuperAdmin user instead of needing a restart. **Screenshots and Logs** **Product Deployment** Please complete the following information: - Deployment format: container - Version 9.0.0 **Desktop** Please complete the following information: - OS: OS X - Browser Chrome - Version 131
top_3_comments_text: VonRehberg: FYI: I also tried the clear system cache button, but it didn't help | primetomas: I think that is expected. Using "simple" means that TLS configuration is not done for requiring client certificate and WildFly need to be re-configured. I assume the restart didn't use "simple"? | VonRehberg: Hi primetomas, The restart also used simple :-) But it also happens when using "later" and setting up an own ManagementCA + TLS.
all_comments_text:
VonRehberg: FYI: I also tried the clear system cache button, but it didn't help
primetomas: I think that is expected. Using "simple" means that TLS configuration is not done for requiring client certificate and WildFly need to be re-configured. I assume the restart didn't use "simple"?
VonRehberg: Hi primetomas, The restart also used simple :-) But it also happens when using "later" and setting up an own ManagementCA + TLS.
VonRehberg: Ah and if it was expected I really wonder why it's nowhere mentioned in the documentation 🤔
primetomas: You will find that at https://hub.docker.com/r/keyfactor/ejbca-ce "Quick start - classic workflow" and among the tutorials https://docs.keyfactor.com/ejbca/latest/quick-start-guide-start-ejbca-container-with-clien "simple" is not meant to be a production start step, but an unsecure demo mode. To do a secure installation with client certificate authentication use the classic workflow.
VonRehberg: Good morning! I don't wanna be picky, but the link you sent doesn't mention anything regarding restarting the container after the superadmin was created. I got the idea of the "simple" workflow, which I'm not using in my current use case. I just used it to compile some easy reproduction steps for you to check the issue ;-) Maybe the issue I'm describing is not yet described well enough. But here's the gist: 1. Start a container with TLS setup "simple". 2. Generate the super admin and add it to the role according to the documentation 3. Import the super admin p12 file into the browser 4. Open the web UI 5. The web UI stays empty 6. Restart the container 7. The web UI works Not sure if it's related to the problem: I use a postgres database and am running it on a M1 Mac. The issue is also reproducible on a different Mac. BR
primetomas: What I am telling you is to NOT start the container with TLS setup "simple" if you want to use a client certificate authentication. Follow the tutorial instead and you do not have to restart the container. As you can see in the tutorial the container is started with TLS_SETUP_ENABLED="true.
VonRehberg: I see, but still if I start the container with TLS_SETUP_ENABLED = true it doesn't work. I don't create the superadmin via WebUI, but via bash script, so maybe this could be the issue. Still seems weird to me: ``` ejbca.sh ra addendentity --username=SuperAdmin --caname="Management CA" --token=P12 --type=1 --dn="CN=SuperAdmin" --password=test ejbca.sh ra setclearpwd SuperAdmin test ejbca.sh batch cp p12/SuperAdmin.p12 /etc/import/SuperAdmin.p12 ejbca.sh roles addrolemember --role "Super Administrator Role" --with="CertificateAuthenticationToken:WITH_COMMONNAME" --value="SuperAdmin" --caname="Management CA" ```
primetomas: You might want to check that the roles are probably already pre-populated, not need to change roles that are already set up for you. The end entity is also already there as the console output from the container says. That addendentity command should just result in a failure doesn't it? Sounds like you try to do too many steps yourself, perhaps you are used to a pure software install from before? The container startup already does everything for you except hand you the P12. Read the console output from the container carefully and run through the tutorial first at least once before modifying the process. Using the Admin UI worked fine for me, I just tried. Than if you want to script to get the p12 from the CLI instead of the UI...you should do only that step and nothing else. When following the classic workflow install you should pay attention to the part that says "Delete default public access role after superadmin enrollment", to ensure that you have no more access than you want.
VonRehberg: Thanks again Primetomas, I just tried it with the very basic config and the superadmin is created and I can download the P12 file with a randomly generated password. However I try to automcatically setup an own CA and issue the superadmin from that CA with a predefined p12 passphrase, so that it can be used in our integration tests. I guess this will always require a reboot then!?
primetomas: Yes because in this scenario you have to add certificates to the TLS trust store, which I guess you do file mounts? And since it is a container, which is not supposed to be operated as a VM, i.e. you go in and to configuration inside the container (which is then not active on another started container), bouncing the container with the proper configs/files mounted is the proper way to to do it. A container should be treated as ephemeral and any started container should be completely identical. This enables things like multiple pods for HA, auto-scaling and other kubernetes things. Bouncing a container/pod on configuration changes should be the expected way. For TLS trust anchors an envoy proxy or ingress in the pod is typically used for highly automated scenarios.

title: [BUG] ejbca.sh batch error
body_text:
Calls to `ejbca.sh batch` may have a wrong environment, which may cause errors.

## Environment

- EJBCA CE v8.3.2 on RockyLinux 9.5.
- Java 17.0.14 and WildFly 26.1.3
- Fresh install
- `keys.alg=ECDSA` and `keys.spec=prime256v1` in batchtool.properties

## Renew tomcat cert

```

# $EJBCA ra setendentitystatus --username tomcat -S 10
New status for end entity tomcat is 10
# $EJBCA ra setclearpwd tomcat serverpwd
Setting clear text password for user tomcat
# $EJBCA batch
Use 'batch --help' for additional options.
Generating keys in directory /tmp/hsperfdata_ejbca/p12.
Generating for end entities with status NEW.
Batch generating 1 users.
Loading configuration from defaults.
Generating RSA keys of size 2048 for tomcat.
Created Keystore for 'tomcat'.
New user generated successfully - tomcat.
1 new users generated successfully - :tomcat.
Generating for end entities with status FAILED.
Batch generating 0 users.
# ls /tmp/hsperfdata_ejbca/p12/
tomcat.jks
```

The algo defined is batchtool.properties is not enforced and the destination directory is wrong.

## Change tomcat profiles

1. Create a crypto token and a P-256 key
2. Create a CA with this key
3. Clone SERVER cert profile and require P-256 algo on the previous CA
4. Create an end entity profile and force cert profile and CA to the previous one
5. Edit tomcat end entity and assign it to the new end entity profile

## Renew tomcat cert

```
 $EJBCA ra setendentitystatus --username tomcat -S 10
New status for end entity tomcat is 10
[root@e83 ~]# $EJBCA ra setclearpwd tomcat serverpwd
Setting clear text password for user tomcat
[root@e83 ~]# $EJBCA batch
Use 'batch --help' for additional options.
Generating keys in directory /tmp/hsperfdata_ejbca/p12.
Generating for end entities with status NEW.

Loading configuration from defaults.
Generating RSA keys of size 2048 for tomcat.
BatchMakeP12 failed for 'tomcat'. Illegal key algorithm, not authorized by certificate profile: RSA.
An error happened, setting status to FAILED.
See config file conf/batchtool.properties for settings.

        at org.ejbca.ui.cli.infrastructure.library.CommandLibrary.findAndExecut

This time, generating RSA certificate cannot happen.

```
2025-01-30 17:52:25,991 INFO  [org.cesecore.audit.impl.log4j.Log4jDevice] (default task-3) 2025-01-30 17:52:25+01:00;CA_USERAUTH;SUCCESS;CA;EJBCA;ejbca;2072958;;tomcat;msg=Authenticated user tomcat.

title: [BUG] Incorrect Encoding of Percent-Encoded Characters in URI Fields
body_text:
**Describe the Bug**

When creating a certificate in EJBCA, either through a CSR (Certificate Signing Request) or directly, URI input fields such as Subject Alternative Name (SAN) URI or DNS Name incorrectly handle certain special characters.

For example, if a CSR contains the SAN  ```URI:test:ce fe```, the issued certificate correctly reflects ```URI:test:ce fe```. However, when using a percent-encoded space (```%20```), such as ```URI:test:ce%20fe```, the issued certificate incorrectly replaces ```%``` with ```/```, resulting in ```URI:test:ce/20fe```.

This issue is observed across other URI-based fields as well (e.g., DNS Name).

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Navigate to EJBCA and generate a certificate using a **CSR** or direct input.
2. In the **Subject Alternative Name (SAN)** field, enter ```URI:test:ce%20fe```.
3. Issue the certificate and inspect the generated **Subject Alternative Name**.
4. The expected value ```URI:test:ce%20fe``` is incorrectly replaced with ```URI:test:ce/20fe```.

**Expected Behavior**

The issued certificate should preserve the percent-encoded characters as provided in the input, without altering them. In this case, ```URI:test:ce%20fe``` should appear exactly as entered in the certificate.


**Product Deployment** 

Please complete the following information:
- Version: EJBCA 7.11.0 Community


**Additional Context**

This issue affects multiple URI-based fields, including **Subject Alternative Name (SAN) URI** and **DNS Name**. The incorrect character replacement could lead to interoperability issues with systems that rely on correct percent-encoding for URI fields.

title: [BUG] Upgrade error
body_text:
When I try to upgrade a 6.10 database to 9.0 (either from WebUI or from ant), I get an error.

```
ERROR org.ejbca.ui.cli.UpgradeCommand - Post Upgrade not performed, see server log for details.
```

In server.log, the stack trace begins with:

```
 ERROR [org.ejbca.core.ejb.upgrade.UpgradeSessionBean] (default task-2) Unexpected error from post-upgrade: java.lang.ClassCastException: class org.jboss.logmanager.log4j.JBossLogger cannot be cast to class org.apache.logging.log4j.core.Logger (org.jboss.logmanager.log4j.JBossLogger is in unnamed module of loader 'org.jboss.logmanager.log4j2@1.1.2.Final' @56d4bd5b; org.apache.logging.log4j.core.Logger is in unnamed module of loader 'deployment.ejbca.ear' @71231573): jakarta.ejb.EJBException: java.lang.ClassCastException: class org.jboss.logmanager.log4j.JBossLogger cannot be cast to class org.apache.logging.log4j.core.Logger (org.jboss.logmanager.log4j.JBossLogger is in unnamed module of loader 'org.jboss.logmanager.log4j2@1.1.2.Final' @56d4bd5b; org.apache.logging.log4j.core.Logger is in unnamed module of loader 'deployment.ejbca.ear' @71231573)
```

Searching the web, I found there was some change in logging (l4j) in recent WildFly versions. Following hints, I tried to exclude `org.apache.logging.log4j.api` in `src/deploy/ear/META-INF/jboss-deployment-structure.xml`:

```
<exclusions>
    <module name="org.apache.logging.log4j.api" />
</exclusions>
```

After `ant build deployear` + restart, `ant upgrade` succeed, and the application *seems* to be still OK.

Tech stack:

- EJBCA r9.0 CE
- WildFly 32
- PostgreSQL 16
- Rocky Linux 9.5

title: Potential bug if the CA has been renewed
body_text:
When I download the SubCA used for signing client certificates through EJBCA Admin UI and Web RA, which underwent re-key several years ago, its serial number is completely different from what the EJBCA WS returns.

1. Add an End Entity, the data we send to the WebService is as follows:
`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"><soapenv:Body><ns1:editUser xmlns:ns1="http://ws.protocol.core.ejbca.org/"><arg0><caName>My CA</caName><certificateProfileName>testprofile</certificateProfileName><clearPwd>false</clearPwd><email>ejbca@localhost</email><endEntityProfileName>test</endEntityProfileName><endTime>2025-04-05 00:00:00+00:00</endTime><keyRecoverable>false</keyRecoverable><password>somerandompassword</password><sendNotification>false</sendNotification><startTime>2025-04-04 00:00:00+00:00</startTime><status>10</status><subjectAltName/><subjectDN>DC=0,L=Test,ST=Test,C=EE,OU=Test,O=Test Org,CN=Test cert</subjectDN><tokenType>USERGENERATED</tokenType><username>96D6250CA49F5FBEC0E116BF67AB3E6A6F9E509C3F8B4EEABD8EBC78B5371623</username></arg0></ns1:editUser></soapenv:Body></soapenv:Envelope>`

2. Perform a PKCS10 Enrollment, the input is currently as follows:
`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"><soapenv:Body><ns1:pkcs10Request xmlns:ns1="http://ws.protocol.core.ejbca.org/"><arg0>96D6250CA49F5FBEC0E116BF67AB3E6A6F9E509C3F8B4EEABD8EBC78B5371623</arg0><arg1>somerandompassword</arg1><arg2>-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----<DATA_HERE>-----END CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----</arg2><arg4>CERTIFICATE</arg4></ns1:pkcs10Request></soapenv:Body></soapenv:Envelope>`

3. Finally request the last certificate chain:
`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"><soapenv:Body><ns1:getLastCertChain xmlns:ns1="http://ws.protocol.core.ejbca.org/"><arg0>96D6250CA49F5FBEC0E116BF67AB3E6A6F9E509C3F8B4EEABD8EBC78B5371623</arg0></ns1:getLastCertChain></soapenv:Body></soapenv:Envelope>`

4. In response to the query made in point 3, the CA chain is returned:
`<soap xmlns="[http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">](http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/%22%3E)[soap:Body](javascript:void(0))<ns2 xmlns="[http://ws.protocol.core.ejbca.org/">](http://ws.protocol.core.ejbca.org/%22%3E)<return><type>0</type><certificateData>%%DATA%%</certificateData></return><return><type>0</type><certificateData>%%DATA%%</certificateData></return><return><type>0</type><certificateData>%%DATA%%</certificateData></return><return><type>0</type><certificateData>%%DATA%%</certificateData></return></ns2></soap></soap>`

In the getLastCertChainResponse, the SubCA serial number that underwent re-key is something different (probably the serial used before re-key) than the serial on the same SubCA certificate downloaded through the Ejbca Admin UI.

Relevant code seems to be here.
https://github.com/Keyfactor/ejbca-ce/blob/main/modules/ejbca-ejb/src/org/ejbca/core/model/era/RaMasterApiSessionBean.java#L2789

_Originally posted by @aloeenmae in https://github.com/Keyfactor/ejbca-ce/discussions/850#

sveinnthorarins: Hey guys, I noticed the same issue on my end running EJBCA CE v8.3.2. This is a serious bug in my opinion because the end entity profile does not allow renewal ("Allow renewal before expiration" is unchecked). What happens is the renewal request fails but the end entity status is successfully changed from "Generated" to "New". Which results in the email being sent out with a new enrollment code and, upon attempting enrollment, a successful renewal of the end entity (a new certificate issued). The user I used has only been given the `/endentityprofilesrules/.../create_end_entity/` and `/endentityprofilesrules/.../view_end_entity/` access rules. body_text:
**Describe the Bug**

A clear and concise description of what the bug is.


**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. With a clean PostgreSQL database (I used version 17 on Windows) log in with psql
2. Create tables (e.g. 'ejbcadb=> \i create-tables-ejbca-postgres.sql'). This works fine.
3. Create indexes (e.g. 'ejbcadb=> \i create-index-ejbca.sql')
4. It reports
psql:create-index-ejbca.sql:65: ERROR:  function subjectaltname(integer) does not exist
LINE 1: ...INDEX certificatedata_idx_san ON CertificateData (subjectAlt...
                                                             ^
HINT:  No function matches the given name and argument types. You might need to add explicit type casts.LINE 1: ...INDEX certificatedata_idx_san ON CertificateData (subjectAlt...
                                                             ^
HINT:  No function matches the given name and argument types. You might need to add explicit type casts.


**Expected Behavior**

I would expect the index to be created and the event to be reported with 'CREATE INDEX'


**Product Deployment** 

Please complete the following information:
 - Deployment format: Downloaded zip file from SourceForge, unzipped and used script from ejbca_ce_9_1_1\doc\sql-scripts
 - Version 9.1.1

**Desktop**

Please complete the following information:
 - OS: Windows Server 2022 Standard
 - PostgreSQL 17.5

**Additional Context**

It's an easy workaround (for Postgres). Just change the line in create-index-ejbca.sql
CREATE INDEX certificatedata_idx_san ON CertificateData (subjectAltName(750));
To
CREATE INDEX certificatedata_idx_san ON CertificateData (subjectAltName);

title: Can't remove public access from Super Administrator role
body_text:
I deployed CE v9.1.1 via Helm chart (with ingress enabled, only using our default ingress certificate/enterprise CA instead of generating a certificate as described [here](https://docs.keyfactor.com/container/latest/ejbca/deploy-ca-in-kubernetes#id-(9.3.2-7.3.2)DeployCAinKubernetes-CreatesecretsforIngress)) and everything seems to be working fine, except that when I go to remove public access from the Super Administrator role, I get the following error:
```
Cause: Granted access of the current administrator might be affected by this change.
```
I'm not sure why this is happening since we do have a match for CN in the client certificate, and it accepts that SuperAdmin certificate for authentication through our ingress, so the user's authorization really shouldn't change when that's removed:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/550ef5d9-c7bc-4d95-9064-1659f5b4f156)
It feels like I've misconfigured _something_ but I have no idea what that is, so I appreciate any feedback. Let me know if any more information is needed as well.

I see `Welcome to EJBCA Administration.`, not `Welcome SuperAdmin to EJBCA Administration.` which normally indicates such a problem (according to the docs). The thing is that I know the certificate is being passed at least to ingress, because otherwise I'd get a 400 (since we're verifying auth). I added the SuperAdmin.p12 to my browser and chose it when prompted, and the ingress controller allows configuration snippets (and the same controller works for SignServer, which requires the same configuration, just fine), so I'm not sure why the certificate wouldn't be getting passed to the upstream. Or, if it is, the EJBCA container isn't processing it. | primetomas: Have you looked at other posts here, and the available helm charts, for what environment variables you need to set in nginx/httpd ingress configurations?

title: `RaLoginBean.java` is hardcoded with its Redirect URI to web configuration instead of Using Browser URL
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem or specific use case? Please describe.**  

Yes — the current implementation of `RaLoginBean.getRedirectUri()` builds the OAuth redirect URI using hardcoded configuration values from `WebConfiguration.getHostName()` and `GlobalConfiguration.getBaseUrl(...)`. This causes issues in deployments where EJBCA is accessed via a load balancer, reverse proxy, or alternate hostname — leading to `redirect_uri` mismatches and failed OAuth logins.

Even the [EJBCA Cloud AWS Launch Guide](https://doc.primekey.com/ejbca-cloud/ejbca-cloud-aws/aws-launch-guide/configure-via-ejbca-cloud-configuration-wizard) step 1.2 implies that support for **multiple domains** is expected, especially in cloud and reverse proxy scenarios. But is completely counter intuitive when OAuth is pinned to the one `http.hostname` property.

**Describe the solution you'd like**  

Update the method `RaLoginBean.getRedirectUri()` to use the actual browser-accessed request URL, so the generated `redirect_uri` matches what the user sees. For example:

```java
private String getRedirectUri() {
    HttpServletRequest request = (HttpServletRequest) FacesContext.getCurrentInstance()
        .getExternalContext().getRequest();
    return request.getRequestURL().toString();
}
```

Or give some type of boolean option in `web.properties` to make this effect.

This change would:
- Dynamically align the redirect URI with the browser's current address. E.g. User A hits via hostname, User B hits via FQDN. Both are accepted ReplyURI's in the IDP
- Eliminate issues caused by mismatched domain names 
- Improve compatibility with OAuth providers that strictly validate redirect URIs and support multiple redirect URis to the same application

**Describe alternatives you've considered**  
- Manually editing the XHTML template to hardcode a valid OAuth URL (not maintainable or scalable)
- Reverse proxy rewrite rules (brittle and not always viable). Also seems stupidly overkill to get baseline functionality.
- Pinning everything to one domain, not scalable longer term.

**Product deployment**  
- Deployment format: Azure Marketplace Image  
- Version: 9.3.2  
- Edition: Enterprise  

**Additional context**  
This affects real-world OAuth login flows. If the redirect URI passed to the provider does not match the one configured (or derived from the browser context), the OAuth flow fails. This is particularly problematic in environments with dynamic public hostnames or multi-tenant domain routing.

Would prefer if this became either:
- The default behaviour
- A toggle in global configuration (e.g. “Use dynamic redirect URI”)

title: PKCS#12 export uses ASN.1 encoding with indefinite lengths, causing interop trouble with OpenSSL < 3.5(?) OSSL_STORE_API
body_text:
Password-encrypted PKCS#12 files produced by EJBCA on exporting, e.g., TLS and CMP client credentials
use not only an anachronistic form of encryption: `pbeWithSHA1And3-KeyTripleDES-CBC`
but also a BER (non-DER) ASN.1 encoding with indefinite field lengths,
which causes confusion and interoperability trouble with various tools, such as OpenSSL-based clients.

While the OpenSSL PKCS#12 CLI and library can cope with both:
``` console
$ openssl pkcs12 -info -noout -passin pass:12345 -in test-BER.p12 
MAC: sha1, Iteration 102400
MAC length: 20, salt length: 20
PKCS7 Data
Shrouded Keybag: pbeWithSHA1And3-KeyTripleDES-CBC, Iteration 51200
PKCS7 Encrypted data: pbeWithSHA1And3-KeyTripleDES-CBC, Iteration 51200
Certificate bag
Certificate bag
Certificate bag
```
since OpenSSL 3.0, most other tools (being based on the OSSL_STORE API) cannot handle it, e.g.:
``` console
$ openssl x509 -passin pass:12345 -in test-BER.p12
Could not find certificate from test-BER.p12

```
until a patch developed yesterday is used.
See https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/28010 for details.

I know that, for instance, some golang tools cannot handle the non-DER encoding, neither.

A workaround is to re-encode (and re-encrypt, if applicable) those `.p12` files using tools like `openssl pkcs12`.

Please switch to DER encoding, and for encryption to, e.g., AES-256-CBC.

title: [BUG] Azure AD OAuth2 Key Rotation Causes Authentication Failure (Missing `kid` Handling in Configdump)
body_text:
## Describe the Bug

When integrating EJBCA (Enterprise 9.3.2) with Azure Active Directory as an OAuth provider, the public key and its `kid` (Key ID) are required for configuration via configdump import and are also included in configdump export. Azure AD rotates its signing keys periodically for security purposes, and the frequency is not publicly documented. When a rotation occurs, the new `kid` value used by Azure AD is not recognised by EJBCA until the public key and `kid` are manually re-imported and updated in EJBCA’s configuration. This results in authentication failures for all Azure AD OAuth logins after a key rotation event.

## To Reproduce

1. Configure an OAuth provider in EJBCA using Azure AD, importing the public key and `kid` via configdump.
2. Allow time for Azure AD to rotate its signing key (rotation schedule is not published and may happen at any time).
3. Attempt authentication with Azure AD after the key rotation event.
4. Observe that authentication fails unless the config is manually updated with the new public key and `kid`.

## Expected Behavior

EJBCA should support automatic key rotation by dynamically fetching and caching signing keys from the Azure AD JWKS endpoint, matching the JWT header’s `kid` to the correct key. Manual updating of the public key and `kid` in the configdump should not be required for production environments using Azure AD as an OAuth authority.

## Screenshots and Logs

Below is a log entry from EJBCA (collected via Log Analytics, which is pulling from `standalone/server.log`):

```
TimeGenerated [UTC]: 2025-07-28T05:43:25.1082046Z
EventLevel: INFO
Category: AUTHENTICATION
Outcome: FAILURE
User: none
ResultType: ADMINWEB
Thread: org.cesecore.audit.impl.log4j.Log4jDevice
Message: 2025-07-28 05:42:07+00:00;AUTHENTICATION;FAILURE;ADMINWEB;EJBCA;none;;;;msg=Could not find OAuth2 JWT key by ID
RawData: 2025-07-28 05:42:07,187+0000 INFO [org.cesecore.audit.impl.log4j.Log4jDevice] (default task-6: 49988980) 2025-07-28 05:42:07+00:00;AUTHENTICATION;FAILURE;ADMINWEB;EJBCA;none;;;;msg=Could not find OAuth2 JWT key by ID
```

This error occurred after an Azure AD key rotation, resulting in the `kid` value in the JWT no longer matching any public key configured in EJBCA. Authentication fails until the configuration is manually updated with the new key and `kid`.

## Product Deployment

- Deployment format: EJBCA Cloud Image Azure.
- Version: 9.3.2

## Desktop

- OS: N/A
- Browser: N/A
- Version: N/A

## Additional Context

- The OAuth provider’s public key and `kid` are required for import using configdump and are also included in configdump exports.
- Administrators must keep the `kid` in sync with Azure AD’s current key. If the `kid` changes due to a key rotation, and configuration is not promptly updated, all authentication attempts will fail.
- Azure AD does not provide a public key rotation schedule. Rotations can occur at any time, and there may be multiple active keys during a transition window.
- Requesting support for **automatic key rotation** (JWKS discovery and `kid` matching) in EJBCA, so that cloud identity integrations like Azure AD are reliable and require less manual operational intervention.
- References:
  - [Azure AD signing key rollover – Microsoft Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/develop/active-directory-signing-key-rollover)
  - [Azure AD OpenID Connect JWKS endpoint](https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/discovery/v2.0/keys)

## Impact

Without support for automatic key rotation and dynamic handling of the `kid`, OAuth validation using Azure AD fails unexpectedly whenever a key rotation occurs. This leads to authentication failures and potential outages, requiring manual reconfiguration to restore functionality.

title: [BUG] RA Web Pages accessible without Authentication and No Login Prompt Shown
body_text: **Describe the Bug** When a user is not authenticated via OAuth (Enta Azure AD in this example), the EJBCA RA Web UI presents a misleading and confusing experience. Users can navigate directly to functional application pages, such as "Make Request" and "Search for End Entities," without being redirected to the login page or notified that they are not logged in. The interface appears normal with active menus, forms, and buttons, but the user is not actually authenticated and cannot complete any actions. There is no tooltip, banner, or warning to indicate that authentication is required. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behaviour: 1. Ensure you are logged out or have not authenticated via OAuth to the EJBCA RA Web UI. 2. Go directly to a functional RA page, such as: - `https://host/ejbca/ra/enrollmakenewrequest.xhtml` - `https://host/ejbca/ra/search_ees.xhtml` 3. Observe that the UI loads with all navigation and form elements visible. 4. Attempt to submit a request, search, or interact with the page. Note that actions do not work, and no message or prompt appears to indicate you must log in. **Expected Behavior** When accessing any protected or functional RA Web UI page while not authenticated, the user should be: - **Automatically redirected** to the login/authentication page, or - **Clearly notified** via tooltip, banner, or modal that login is required to use the page, - **Controls that require authentication** should be disabled, hidden, or replaced with a message such as: _"You are not logged in. Please log in to access this page."_ The UI should never present a fully interactive page without enforcing authentication or providing an explicit message to the user. **Screenshots and Logs** _See attached screenshots:_ - "Make Request" page loaded while not authenticated (shows full UI, no login prompt) - "Search for End Entities" page loaded while not authenticated (UI appears normal, no results, no error) **Product Deployment** Please complete the following information: - Deployment format: EJBCA Cloud Azure - Version: 9.3.2 **Desktop** Please complete the following information: - OS: Any OS - Browser: Any browser - Version: Any version of the browser **Additional Context** - The current UI behaviour causes significant user confusion, as users believe they are authenticated and expect the page to function. They believe it's a role mapping issue most times. - The OAuth from the CA Admin Web UI, to the RA Web UI also doesn't use the same token (a good thing). The issue is though, a user which had auth'd to the CA is rightly thinking they are auth'd to the RA Web UI when in fact they are not. Instead they have to manually hit https://host/ejbca/ra/login.xhtml - No visible prompt or guidance is given for resolving the authentication issue. - This leads to unnecessary support queries and is inconsistent with best practices for secure applications. - Recommended: All RA Web UI pages should enforce authentication on page load (If OAuth) and provide immediate feedback or redirection if the user is not logged in.

title: AJP not supported by ingress-nginx
body_text: AJP is [not supported](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/pull/10158) by ingress-nginx as of 1.9. Most of the documentation (at least, for the Helm chart) uses `proxyAJP.enabled: true` so if that's the preferred backend protocol, it's not going to work for a lot of people.

Here's the quick fix that works with modern nginx-ingress: Solution: Use Apache HTTPD as HTTP-to-AJP translator The official Keyfactor documentation (Step 11 of [MicroK8s tutorial](https://docs.keyfactor.com/ejbca/9.0/tutorial-deploy-ejbca-container-in-microk8s)) already provides this solution: ```shell # Deploy Apache HTTPD with AJP proxy apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: httpd-config data: httpd.conf: | LoadModule proxy_ajp_module modules/mod_proxy_ajp.so <VirtualHost *:80> ProxyPass /ejbca/ ajp://ejbca-service:8009/ejbca/ </VirtualHost> --- # Then use HTTP ingress instead of AJP nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol: HTTP # Not AJP backend: service: name: apache-httpd-service port: number: 80 Traffic Flow: text Browser → nginx-ingress (HTTP) → Apache HTTPD → EJBCA (AJP) For Helm Chart users: text # Disable broken AJP ingress proxyAJP: enabled: false ``` ### Deploy Apache HTTPD separately as shown above This approach follows Keyfactor's own documentation. title: Cannot create signer: signature configured for ML-DSA-65
body_text: Hi, I am using the latest docker image of ejbca and was trying to create Hybrid PQC SubCA for which i am following this tutorial video: https://youtu.be/NYp4ZvHvpko?si=uXuqp4JqXl9vsZfX I was able to create Hybrid PQC Root CA. But now while creating Hybrid PQC Sub CA, I am getting this issue: `Error: org.bouncycastle.operator.OperatorCreationException: cannot create signer: signature configured for ML-DSA-65 ` I am attaching the image of the configuration: Thanks, Aditya
top_3_comments_text: primetomas: Do you have a certificate profile configured that is used, where the signature algorithm in the profile is not set to "Inherit from issuing CA"? | AdityaKoranga: These are the all the certificate profiles. `MyRootCAProfile`, `MyFirstSubCAProfile`, `TLS CLient Profile` & `TLS Server Profile` use "inherit from issuing CA" while `MyPQCRootCAProfile` and the `MyPQCSubCAProfile` **do not** use "inherit from issuing CA" | primetomas: Set everything to inherit, it is normally the correct setting. For PQC it's always the correct setting.
all_comments_text: primetomas: Do you have a certificate profile configured that is used, where the signature algorithm in the profile is not set to "Inherit from issuing CA"? AdityaKoranga: These are the all the certificate profiles. `MyRootCAProfile`, `MyFirstSubCAProfile`, `TLS CLient Profile` & `TLS Server Profile` use "inherit from issuing CA" while `MyPQCRootCAProfile` and the `MyPQCSubCAProfile` **do not** use "inherit from issuing CA" primetomas: Set everything to inherit, it is normally the correct setting. For PQC it's always the correct setting. AdityaKoranga: Thanks @primetomas. "inherit from issuing CA" solved the issue. However In the video mentioned above it was not to set to that option- maybe environment or env difference(?) Would you be kind enough to explain in brief how not selecting "inherit from issuing CA" was causing issue? I am new to ejbca :) primetomas: You can put another value than "inherit from issuing CA", but the selected value has to match the issuing CAs signing key. The common mistake is for example to think that the signature algorithm in a SubCA certificate profile has to do with what the sub CA sign, but it is the signature algorithm for certificates issued using the Sub CA profile which means that the profile is used by the Root CA. Therefore the signature algorithm must match the Root CAs signing key and not the Sub CAs. The field was originally put there in order to allow migration from say SHA1WithRSA to SHA256WithRSA. So if the Root CA was signed with SHA1WithRSA it could sign new SubCAs with SHA256WithRSA. In this case both SHA1- and SHA256WithRSA matches the Root CAs RSA key. In the case of ML-DSA if the Root CA has a key with ML-DSA-87 it can not create any other signatures than ML-DSA-87, so if the Sub CA profile is set to ML-DSA-65 it will give you an error. I think the tutorial over-complicated things by not using "inherit". As there is only one option (apart from inherit) to use the only point in setting it is to prevent anyone from creating a Root CA with another algorithm and trying to issue Sub CAs. This is of course a point, preventing someone from doing such a mistake, but creating Root CAs is rare enough that mistakes like that should be rare. AdityaKoranga: Thanks @primetomas for the nice explanation. I understood it really well. (Also, Looking forward to attend your session at OpenSSL Conf. and PKI Conf.) Best Regards, Aditya

- Create a new EE profile name "zz"
- Only change "Maximum number of failed login attempts" => Use, Default=3, NOT unlimited, NOT modifiable
- Create a new EE on profile "zz"
- Fill the fields and press "Add" => OK
- Rename the EE profile "aa"
- Create a new EE, don't touch the profile selector and let it on "aa" profile
- The "Maximum number of failed login attempts" is on "Specified" with an empty text field
