- Switch to "EMPTY" profile and switch back to "aa"
- The "Maximum number of failed login attempts" is on "Specified" with "3" in text field
- Fill the fields and press "Add" => OK

This installation was set up by following the official Keyfactor Community video playlist: [https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLt17f5skfOPGLHMR7IhOUdsr1992PcfGh](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://youtube.com/playlist%3Flist%3DPLt17f5skfOPGLHMR7IhOUdsr1992PcfGh&authuser=1)

## Description:
When issuing a certificate using a Certificate Profile where "Store Certificate Data" is enabled, the resulting row in the CertificateData table has a NULL value for the base64Cert column. Is this a normal behaviour?

## Steps to Reproduce:
- Deploy EJBCA-CE and MariaDB using the standard docker-compose.yml provided below.

- Complete the initial EJBCA setup (create a CA, PKI Hierarchy etc.) as demonstrated in the tutorial playlist.

- Navigate to Admin Web > Certificate Profiles.

- Verify that a profile (e.g., "TLS Client Profile") has the "Store Certificate Data" checkbox enabled.

- Navigate to RA Web and issue a new certificate using that profile.

- Connect to the MariaDB database and observe the database state using the queries in the "Diagnostic Queries" section below.

## Expected Behavior (as per my assumptions):
Newly issued certificates should have their base64 data populated in the base64Cert column.

## Actual Behavior:
The base64Cert column is NULL for all issued certificates, despite the configuration.

## Database Diagnostic Queries & Output:
The following queries confirm that active certificates exist, but none have their base64Cert data stored.

1. Confirm active certificates exist:

```sql

MariaDB [ejbca]> SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM CertificateData GROUP BY status;
+--------+----------+
| status | COUNT(*) |
+--------+----------+
|     20 |       10 |
+--------+----------+
```
Result: Shows 10 certificates with status 20 (active).

2. Confirm none of the active certificates have stored data:

```sql
MariaDB [ejbca]> SELECT base64Cert FROM CertificateData WHERE status=20 AND base64Cert IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1;
Empty set (0.001 sec)
```

Result: Proves that of the 10 active certificates, none have a non-NULL base64Cert value.

    volumes:
      - ./datadbdir:/var/lib/mysql:rw

title: [BUG] · organizationIdentifier (OID 2.5.4.97) attribute missing in End Entity Profile “Subject DN Attributes” for EJBCA-CE
body_text:
**Describe the Bug**

We have identified an issue with the Community Edition of EJBCA (running image keyfactor/ejbca-ce:latest, version EJBCA 9.1.1 Community) in our TEST environment, where we cannot locate the organizationIdentifier attribute (OID 2.5.4.97) in the “Subject DN Attributes” section when creating an End Entity Profile.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
 
1. Go to "RA Funcions"
2. Click on "End Entity Profile"
3. Add/Edit an Entity Profile
4. Search for "Subject DN Attributes"
5. organizationIdentifier (OID 2.5.4.97) it's not avaiable

**Product Deployment** 

- Deployment format: docker, in `keyfactor/ejbca-ce:latest`
- Version: EJBCA 9.1.1 Community (8207be0e6112067a33b82328d8e15870b5492da7)

**Additional Context**

The EJBCA-EE 9.1.1 already shows this item (and many others)

title: Add UI feedback when loading the list of workers
body_text:
When I go to `signserver/adminweb/workers.xhtml` on my test instance of SignServer, the list loads slowly and there is no indication of the fact that the system is busy doing some work. _x000D_
_x000D_
From a usability perspective, the best practice is to show some indication of "hey, I'm still alive!" if it takes more than 250ms to provide the result. It could be a progress bar, or an indeterminate progress bar if there's no reliable way of estimating how long the process will take. Otherwise users think their input was not received, so they click again._x000D_
_x000D_
This is not a big deal, but it would be a nice touch for improving usability a bit._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
- My test environment has 117 workers._x000D_
- SignServer 5.10.0.Final
top_3_comments_text: netmackan: Hi, That is a great suggestion. We have also noticed the slowness of the workers page and have tracked down the issue to be because of the checking of the worker status of each worker when they are listed. Checking the worker status involves a lot of checks including the configuration but also more slow ones like testing that it is possible to sign with the configured crypto token. I believe there is a lot that could be done here to improve that. One thing we have been exploring is to change so that the list of workers is first displayed without the worker status as that should be much faster and then the statuses would be queried in the background and displayed first when they are available. That way the page is usable almost directly but the status info may come later. Combining all of this with also the progress information as you suggest might be even better.

title: The script to download depencecies not yet published to Maven Repositories is absent from the latest release.
body_text:
The `lib/maven-install-files.sh`  script required to download dependencies not yet published to the Maven repositories is absent from the latest release, namely from the zip `signserver-ce-6.0.0.1.Final.zip`._x000D_
While on the zip `signserver-ce-6.0.0.1.Final-bin.zip` it's still there.

That the dependencies are not yet published to the Central repo. While 1. is only meant as a temporarily solution until 2. is fixed we should probably address that as well even if the dependencies are available before the next release. | netmackan: SignServer ticket (for future reference only, as Jira is not yet available publicly): https://jira.primekey.se/browse/DSS-2682 | mlundblad: This should be fixed since 6.2.0.Final, so closing this now.

top_3_comments_text: netmackan: I believe it currently is a known issue that the admin web link assumes the default ports are being used. The port for the link can be changed in /opt/signserver/conf/signserver_deploy.properties changing to: ``` httpserver.external.privhttps=8443 ``` Then when starting the container you can mount in your modified version of signserver_deploy.properties: ``` docker run -it --rm \ -p 8080:8080 -p 8443:8443 -h localhost \ -v /home/user/my-signserver_deploy.properties:/opt/signserver/conf/signserver_deploy.properties \ --name signserver \ keyfactor/signserver-ce:6.3.0 ``` Then the link should use what you have set in the config file (i.e. 8443). Not sure if a container could be made aware of what port mappings are used and if we then could set the right port automagically. Otherwise, maybe we could introduce some ENV variable where the correct port could be specified so that mounting in the conf file would not be necessary. | Vampire: Or maybe just use a relative path like for the other links and if you want to ensure this path is only access via https, ensure this otherwise? | netmackan: Relative paths are not enough as the point with the Administration Web link is to use HTTPS and the port that can accept client-certificate authentication. I think this is something that the one starting the container will need to provide as this depends on the port-mappings provided with your `docker run`. Currently it can be achieved by mounting in your own signserver_deploy.properties but we are considering if not this should be possible through an container environment variable to make it easier.

netmackan: Note that, depending on the configuration and environment, it is not guaranteed that two calls to SignServer would return a signature using the same key and certificate. For instance if a load balancer is used in front of SignServer the request could go to an other SignServer instance potentially using different certificate and even different key. Also the certificate might not exist before the signing request comes in, if the 'one-time key and certificate feature' is used where a key is generated on demand and a new short-lived certificate is issued just for this signing request. Sure this are special cases but just to give an idea. In #108 it is mentioned that Jsign has the option to let the user (?) choose which signature algorithm to use. If that is used, then it could be up to the user to provide the correct algorithm that matches what SignServer would then use. That way the certificate should not be needed before signing (at least not if it is only to get the algorithm) and only one call to SignServer (assuming the right algorithm is chosen). A check after signing (when the certificate is also returned) could be made to give a clear error message to the user about what was the expected algorithm.
ebourg: Load balancing the signature endpoint and serving different keys is a bit surprising, but why not if there is a use case for that. It's nice if SignServer is very flexible but I don't think Jsign has to support every possible configuration. Jsign focuses on code signing and in this scenario SignServer is likely to be used as a proxy for a USB token delivered by a CA with a fixed long-lived key and certificate, and the user will simply configure the signer as Jsign expects. In this case the full certificate chain is probably not stored on the token anyway, so SignServer can't really do better, unless PlainSigner is modified to allow an external chain to be specified in the configuration.
ebourg: > Is it still required in Jsign to get the certificate before signing? Do you know why that is? I got a look, when signing NuGet files there is a required signed attribute derived from the certificate (the RFC 5035 SigningCertificateV2 attribute containing the SHA-256 hash of the certificate, the name of the issuer and its serial number), so the certificate has to be know before signing. NuGet put aside, I'm not sure Bouncy Castle's CMSSignedDataGenerator works if the certificate is known after signing. It holds a SignerInfoGenerator which is built by providing the content signer (referencing the key) and the certificate (it may just need the certificate serial number and the issuer though).
netmackan: Okey, yes for those advanced signatures where the signature covers also the certificate than we can not get away from having the certificate before creating the plain signature. Workaround for now is to to a "dummy" signature call first. Possible improvements could be to introduce a concept of dry-run signature which would be that same call but the actual signing would not be carried out. I guess only benefit with that would be to not perform signature creation twice. Third option would be to introduce a similar separate call that would require the same credentials but not the data to be signed and which would just return the certificate chain but not a signature.
netmackan: I am looking into adding new REST endpoint(s) that hopefully could also address this issue. The draft idea right now is to add the following ones for listing certificates, from any accessible worker or from a specific worker: * GET /workers/certificates * GET /workers/{idOrName}/certificates You would call them using the same credentials as for the signing/process call and internally each worker configured to be visible in this way would have its Authorizer being invoked to check the authorization. There could also be a new endpoint for specifying a specific certificate to use when signing (only needed if there are multiple certificates to choose from): * POST /workers/{idOrName}/certificates/{certId}/process Example of a get response: ``` [ { "base64CertChain": [ "", "" ], "certId": "9c221307cdafa8540c8c3e6ca74d227a295c83246079621619876f6f7a269a81", "links": { "process": "/workers/301/certificates/9c221307cdafa8540c8c3e6ca74d227a295c83246079621619876f6f7a269a81/process", "certificate": "/workers/301/certificates/9c221307cdafa8540c8c3e6ca74d227a295c83246079621619876f6f7a269a81" }, "workerDescription": "First PlainSigner accessible by Admin 4.", "workerIdOrName": "301" } ] ``` Note the certificate chain in base64CertChain and the certId that can be used when posting and also for convenience a link called "process" containing the location to post to. Let me know if you have any feedback on the above.

**Is your feature request related to a problem or specific use case? Please describe.**_x000D_
It would be nice to be able to specify the signature algorithm the PlainSigner uses when being invoked via the REST interface._x000D_
For example when using Jsign, you can specify which signature algorithm should be used._x000D_
But when using server-side hashing, there is no way to specify which signature algorithm should be used._x000D_

It would be nice if you could include in the REST request `metadata` the signature algorithm that should be used, or at least the hash algorithm, so that you for example can request `SHA1withRSA` or `SHA256withRSA` and the signer will use that if it is a workable algorithm. It might also be sufficient being able to specify the hash algorithm, so that you can just request `SHA1` or `SHA256` and the `RSA` part comes from the configuration of the worker or determined from the token capabilities._x000D_

Alternative considered was using client-side hashing, but for example with a Nitrokey HSM 2 we were not able to set this up properly, but got a `Caused by: java.security.NoSuchAlgorithmException: No such algorithm: RSA/ECB/PKCS1Padding` exception when trying to use `NONEwithRSA` for the worker._x000D_

body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We want to share keys between quorum of people and on some servers. Scripts on this servers will automatically unseal vault after restart. But this key parts still can be used to generate root. We need a way to restrict so only people's keys can be used to generate root token._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Add additional command to generate key parts that can only be used to unseal vault.

Thanks! | Djaler: We are using shamir, because we have vault installed on virtual server, without any cloud infrasturcture | maxb: I think it might be impossible to securely implement this request - here's why: A quorum of unseal keys allows Vault to reconstruct the master key so the Vault program itself can read the encrypted secrets on disk. This is something that's actually enforced by the properties of the Shamir's Secret Sharing cryptographic algorithm, not just the Vault program. No matter what you do, there's no getting away from the fact that unseal keys need to allow Vault to decrypt its own data - and so any hypothetical "unseal-only" keys must allow this. And if they allow this, there's no cryptographic protection against a malicious attacker building their own version of the Vault program which pretends that "unseal-only" keys are "root-token-capable" keys. Ultimately, if you possess a quorum of unseal keys, you can decrypt your Vault. I've always assumed that this is why a quorum of unseal keys are allowed to create a root token - because they already possess the cryptographic secrets to allow reading the secrets out of the raw data in the storage backend, so permitting the generation of a root token is not any further compromise of security.

title: Backup with transit seal method and revoked token silently fails
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We use Raft as our storage backend._x000D_
We also do use transit sealing against a secondary Vault instance to provide auto unsealing for our primary Vault installed in Kubernetes. The token we use for that gets created by an init-container and is only valid for a few minutes._x000D_
Until recently, this setup worked fine for us. The pods got unsealed automatically and the backups were present and valid (could be successfully restored)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Probably due to https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/12388, this behaviour changed!**_x000D_
Creating a backup using `vault operator raft snapshot save <snapshot file>` results in an error regarding the `SHA256SUMS.sealed` file. Using the API endpoint, we can successfully download the snapshot without any error._x000D_
**In both cases the snapshot file gets created and looks to contain data:**_x000D_
- the file size makes sense (it's not only a few bytes but matches old backups)_x000D_
- using `file <snapshot file>` the backup is recognized as `gzip compressed data` _x000D_
_x000D_
However, the **backup can not be restored** and Vault complains about `Load error` in the UI. Restoring using the CLI also fails. If I try to unpack the backup using gzip, I get `unexpected end of file` -> it looks like the backup file is corrupted._x000D_
_x000D_
If I extend the lifetime of the unseal token, the backup gets created and can be restored successfully!_x000D_
There is no word in the docs, that the transit token used in the Vault config/env variables must still be valid for a backup to succeed!_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Setup a Vault with transit sealing_x000D_
2. Issue a new token on the Vault providing the Transit engine_x000D_
3. Unseal the new Vault using that token_x000D_
4. Wait for the token to be revoked / revoke it manually_x000D_
5. Create a backup using API or UI_x000D_
6. Try to restore that exact backup_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Either a valid backup file (a file that can be extracted using gzip+tar and restored) should be created; even though there is the warning about `SHA256SUMS.sealed` file._x000D_
OR the creation of the backup should hard fail without any file being created._x000D_
_x000D_
If someone uses the API to create the backup but does not regularly check the restore, there would be no way to see, that the backup file is corrupted._x000D_
_x000D_
Also, the docs about raft snapshotting should mention, that the seal-configuration (including the token) must be valid for the backup to fully work. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.8.3, 1.8.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.8.3, 1.8.4_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
disable_mlock = true_x000D_
log_level = "Info"_x000D_
log_format = "json"_x000D_
_x000D_
api_addr = "http://localhost:8200"_x000D_
cluster_addr = "http://localhost:8201"_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
  cluster_address = "[::]:8201"_x000D_
_x000D_
  tls_disable = 1_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
seal "transit" {_x000D_
  token = "<token>" # this token is the problem_x000D_
  key_name = "vault-transit"_x000D_
  mount_path = "transit/"_x000D_
  address = "https://transit-providing-vault:8200"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
storage "raft" {_x000D_
  path = "/data"_x000D_
_x000D_
  retry_join {_x000D_
    leader_api_addr = "http://localhost:8200"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
There must be a notice in the docs about the token used for transit. The docs and also the howto guides only mention to create a new token and to put it in the config/env variable. **This would also break after the default lifetime of 32d**:_x000D_
- https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/commands/operator/raft#snapshot-save_x000D_
- https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/configuration/seal/transit_x000D_
- https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/autounseal-transit#step-2-configure-auto-unseal-vault-2

title: Browser CLI commands: unable to write to KV v2
body_text:
Hi,_x000D_
_x000D_
I’m trying to use the embedded browser CLI to write to a KV v2 engine.  I simple started a dev server (v1.8.5) , logged in with root token and did the steps below:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ write secret/data/test foo=bar_x000D_
Error writing to: secret/data/test._x000D_
URL: /v1/secret/data/test_x000D_
Code: 400_x000D_
Errors:_x000D_
  no data provided_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
That' odd. I have provided “foo=bar” as data._x000D_
_x000D_
Another attempt:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ write secret/data/test data='{"foo":"bar"}'_x000D_
Error writing to: secret/data/test._x000D_
URL: /v1/secret/data/test_x000D_
Code: 400_x000D_
Errors:_x000D_
  error converting input {"foo":"bar"} for field "data": '' expected a map, got 'string'_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Hmm, so when I declare explicitly the field “data”, it recognizes it, but complains it’s not a map._x000D_
_x000D_
So I decided open the hood and see how the UI was making the API requests, and eventually stumbled on this function:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
write: function(e, t, n) {_x000D_
  return this.ajax("write", r(e), {_x000D_
    data: t,_x000D_
    wrapTTL: n_x000D_
  })_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Debugging I could see that:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
e = "secret/data/test", t = {foo: "bar"}, n = undefined_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
And as this variable “t” is being passed directly to ajax lib, without being enclosed in a object with “data” attribute, I decided to help with a little “hack”:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ write secret/data/test foo=bar_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Breakpoint at function above and run at developer tools’ console:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
t = { data: t }_x000D_
```_x000D_
```_x000D_
Key           Value                         _x000D_
created_time  2021-02-26T18:43:44.445292403Z_x000D_
deletion_time                               _x000D_
destroyed     false                         _x000D_
version       1 _x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
And it worked! So it seems like a bug, that the data is not passed correctly to the ajax lib._x000D_
_x000D_
This problem was already mentioned in a [discuss topic](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/browser-cli-commands-unable-to-write-to-kv-v2/21451), but I thought it might be worse to open a bug report for it. (To get it fixed, eventually.)_x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks,_x000D_
_x000D_

-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
A clear and concise description of what the bug is._x000D_
_x000D_
When enabling (by uncommenting) the configuration for consul storage backend, the following error appears in the logs:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2021-11-17T07:55:57.015Z [WARN]  storage.consul: appending trailing forward slash to path_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This is easily fixed by adding a `/` to the path (e.g. `path = "vault/"`), but **Vault should ship with that slash already included**. _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Uncomment this part from the default `vault.hcl`:_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
storage "consul" {_x000D_
  address = "127.0.0.1:8500"_x000D_
  path    = "vault"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
2. Start vault_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
No warnings. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
Vault v1.8.5 (647eccfe0bd5817bdd8628f3c3171402dfc8a8fc)_x000D_
Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
storage "consul" {_x000D_
  address = "127.0.0.1:8500"_x000D_
  path    = "vault"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_

user with policy:_x000D_

path "app-secrets/data/application_1/*" {_x000D_

}_x000D_
_x000D_

path "app-secrets/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_

only after I add this to a user policy:_x000D_

option in UI appears:_x000D_

create user with the above policy and verify options available in the UI_x000D_

Users should be allowed to delete secrets under the specific paths with this first policy._x000D_
_x000D_

* Vault Server Version 1.8.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version Vault v1.8.4 (925bc650ad1d997e84fbb832f302a6bfe0105bbb)_x000D_

title: PKI certificate issue fails as CA approaches expiration
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We use a pre-generated corporate CA cert in our Vault PKI backend root certificate. This root certificate is going to expire next year and we are discovering that some of our tools that need long lasting certs are failing to generate certificates with the error `cannot satisfy request, as TTL would result in notAfter 2022-... that is beyond the expiration of the CA certificate at 2022-...`. When we make the request to issue the certificate we are not actually requesting a specific end date so it defaults to the one calculated by Vault based on the TTL values for the given role. This seems to ignore the fact that the CA itself expires at a specific date. The problem is the endpoint calculates the expiration of the current cert from the current time + TTL but this is a moving target and is not easy for clients to calculate and explicitly ask for something before the CA expiration, but it would be trivial for Vault to calculate and cap the certificate based of the CA expiration._x000D_
_x000D_
The implication of this bug is that things that services that are working perfectly fine for months and years start to fail to renew certificates if they are unlucky enough to have default TTL longer than the time left on their certificates. Failures start occurring at (CA Cert expiration - TTL) instead of at (CA Cert expiration)._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. generate a pki mount with max TTL of 60 days:_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    vault secrets enable pki_x000D_
    vault secrets tune -max-lease-ttl=1440h pki_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
2. generate a root cert that expires in 29 days_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    vault write pki/root/generate/internal common_name=test ttl=696h_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
3. create a role with ttl 30d_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    vault write pki/roles/example-dot-com allowed_domains=my-website.com allow_subdomains=true ttl=720h max_ttl=720h_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
4. request a cert_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    vault write pki/issue/example-dot-com common_name=www.my-website.com_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
5. See error_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    Error writing data to pki/issue/example-dot-com: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
    URL: PUT http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/pki/issue/example-dot-com_x000D_
    Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
    * cannot satisfy request, as TTL would result in notAfter 2021-12-17T20:53:34.1477146Z that is beyond the expiration of the CA certificate at 2021-12-16T20:46:53Z_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
I did not specify an explicit date so the endpoint automatically calculated one from the TTL which turned out to be invalid. It would be ideal if the logic takes into account the CA end date and automatically truncate the TTL to match. Even if I specify a TTL the expected behavior should still truncate it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): Vault v1.8.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.8.4_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux/Docker_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
NA, I started this within docker so this is easily repeatable inside a container `docker run --rm -d --cap-add=IPC_LOCK vault`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Add any other context about the problem here._x000D_

title: OIDC provider: nonce should be optional in authorization code flow
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I am testing the Vault 1.9.0 OIDC provider tech-preview._x000D_
_x000D_
Using the [dex example-app](https://github.com/dexidp/dex/tree/master/examples/example-app) as a client, I get the following response:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
invalid_request: nonce parameter is required_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
However, according to the [OpenID Core Connect specification](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#AuthRequest) section 3.1.2.1, the nonce is "OPTIONAL" in the Authorization Code Flow._x000D_
_x000D_
(It is required in the Implicit Flow and Hybrid Flow, but that's not what Vault implements)_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Set up Vault OIDC provider as [here](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/secrets/identity/oidc-provider)_x000D_
2. Install [dex example-app](https://github.com/dexidp/dex/tree/master/examples/example-app)_x000D_
3. Run the example app pointing at Vault_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    bin/example-app --client-id XXXXXXXX --client-secret hvo_secret_YYYYYYYY --debug \_x000D_
      --issuer https://vault.example.com:8200/v1/identity/oidc/provider/my-provider --listen http://0.0.0.0:5555 \_x000D_
      --redirect-uri http://127.0.0.1:5555/callback_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
4. Login to example app via web_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should accept Authorization flow without nonce, as compliant applications are not required to provide one._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): `1.9.0`_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): `Vault v1.9.0`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: `Ubuntu 20.04 amd64`_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s): N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The spec also says:_x000D_
_x000D_
> If present in the ID Token, Clients MUST verify that the nonce Claim Value is equal to the value of the nonce parameter sent in the Authentication Request. If present in the Authentication Request, Authorization Servers MUST include a nonce Claim in the ID Token with the Claim Value being the nonce value sent in the Authentication Request. Authorization Servers SHOULD perform no other processing on nonce values used. The nonce value is a case sensitive string._x000D_
_x000D_
Note use of "If present"._x000D_

We're going to make the nonce parameter optional (authorization code flow) to comply with the spec. We do recommend supplying a nonce for security concerns highlighted by the spec though. We're targeting to release this update in Vault 1.9.1.

I suspect there is possibly a race condition occurring allowing for a namedKey to be saved with incomplete data such that the key is seen as needing to be rotated despite the fact that not all of the values needed to perform the rotation are present(not exactly sure exactly which value was missing). _x000D_

title: OIDC Provider (tech preview): suggestions for allowed_client_ids
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I'm evaluating the OIDC Provider in Vault 1.9.0, and I have it working together with apache mod_auth_openidc.  You have made a very impressive piece of work!_x000D_
_x000D_
The issue I'd like to raise is around the binding of client ids, which is highlighted from following your [overview](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/secrets/identity/oidc-provider).  The example commands shown include the following, twice:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
  allowed_client_ids="xxAQWBYzD2WXsB8GiZqwq4jsUwfG0hJV"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
... once for the key ([API ref](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/identity/tokens#create-a-named-key)), and once for the provider ([API ref](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/identity/oidc-provider#create-or-update-a-provider))._x000D_
_x000D_
However, it doesn't say where this value comes from.  It turns out that this is, indeed, the OpenID "client_id" - which you cannot choose, but is only created by Vault when you create the client itself.  You can find it by doing `vault read identity/oidc/client/my-webapp` *after* creating the client - but this step is not shown in the documentation._x000D_
_x000D_
Now, there is a chicken-and-egg problem.  You want to specify the allowed_client_ids when creating the key, but you have to specify the key before you can create a client._x000D_
_x000D_
Moreover, there is a usability problem.  Every time you create a new client, you have to modify the related key and provider(s) to authorize that client.  And since you can't even choose the client_id, it becomes a multi-step process:_x000D_
_x000D_
* Create the client_x000D_
* Read back the client to get the client_id_x000D_
* Modify the provider to add the client_id to allowed_client_ids_x000D_
* Modify the key to add the client_id to allowed_client_ids_x000D_
_x000D_
Note that there is a double relationship: the client points to the key *and* the key has a list of clients.  Maybe there is some technical reason for this, but it's not convenient for the API user._x000D_
_x000D_
Given that this is a technical preview, maybe there is an opportunity to change the API here.  If not, there's at least an opportunity to clarify the documentation._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
If the API is open to change, then the simplest change would be to reverse the bindings, so that the client points to the key and provider, rather than the other way round.  That is:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault write identity/oidc/client/my-webapp \_x000D_
  redirect_uris="http://127.0.0.1:8251/callback,http://127.0.0.1:8500/ui/oidc/callback" \_x000D_
  assignments="my-assignment" \_x000D_
  providers="my-provider" \     <<< NOTE_x000D_
  key="my-key" \_x000D_
  id_token_ttl="30m" \_x000D_
  access_token_ttl="1h"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
(And remove `allowed_client_ids` from both provider and key)_x000D_
_x000D_
This means you can:_x000D_
* Create the key(s) and provider(s) in advance of the clients_x000D_
* Create new clients in a single operation_x000D_
* Remove clients safely without having to remember to update the provider and key_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
*Option 1:* It would be possible to nest clients under the provider:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
/v1/identity/oidc/provider/test-provider_x000D_
/v1/identity/oidc/provider/test-provider/clients/my-webapp_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
However, this would limit you to a 1:N relationship between provider and client.  (I can't think why you might want the same client to appear under multiple providers, but I guess someone might want to do this)._x000D_
_x000D_
You would still need to link to keys - and maybe a single key per provider would be sufficient. (I can't think of any case where multiple clients under the same provider would use different keys, but again, maybe someone wants this)_x000D_
_x000D_
*Option 2:* When a client is created, you could allow the client_id and/or client_secret to be specified, rather than randomly generated.  Hence you could pick the client_id like "xxAQWBYzD2WXsB8GiZqwq4jsUwfG0hJV" in advance._x000D_
_x000D_
This might be useful anyway, e.g. when migrating systems._x000D_
_x000D_
*Option 3:* If the existing design is to stay as-is, then I suggest the following documentation improvements._x000D_
_x000D_
* Change step 1 ("Create a key that will be used to sign/verify ID tokens") to:_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    $ vault write identity/oidc/key/my-key \_x000D_
      allowed_client_ids="*" \_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
* In step 4 ("Create an OIDC client"), after creating the client, show_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    vault read identity/oidc/client/my-webapp_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
    to get the client_id (which will be used in the following step 5 to create the provider)_x000D_
_x000D_
* At the end, optionally show modifying `my-key` to bind to the specific client_id obtained in step 4._x000D_
_x000D_
EDIT: I have since found [this tutorial](https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/oidc-identity-provider?in=vault/new-release) which is much better, as it uses `allowed_client_ids="*"`.  It's the set of steps in the [main documentation](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/secrets/identity/oidc-provider) under secrets/identity/oidc-provider which I'm referring to above._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
The main use case for me is being able to add new clients simply, without having to modify existing providers and keys._x000D_
_x000D_
(EDIT: on reflection, since I'm only likely to create one provider, I can avoid this issue just by setting `allowed_client_ids="*"` for both the key and provider.  Therefore, this isn't actually a major issue for me, but it took me a while to realise this)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
There's one other minor documentation point I'd like to make. [Here](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/concepts/oidc-provider#authorization-endpoint) it says:_x000D_
_x000D_
> The authorization endpoint for each provider **is added to** Vault's default policy using the identity/oidc/provider/+/authorize path *[My emphasis]*_x000D_
_x000D_
My test system was upgraded from 1.6.3 to 1.9.0.  I thought that "is added to" implied that the default policy would be automatically upgraded - but it wasn't.  I had to write the new default policy in manually._x000D_
_x000D_
I think this could be clarified to say "is included in" or "is present in" Vault's default policy from v1.9 onwards.

Not applicable_x000D_

title: Transit: Support algorithms with large nonces
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Currently, `transit` keys need to be rotated after 2³² uses, due to the algorithm employed (AES-GCM with a random nonce)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Use a long, random nonce with an algorithm such as XChaCha20-Poly1305.  For algorithms such as AES-GCM that don’t support this natively, one can use any KDF with a root key and any random number, and include the number in the nonce._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Maintain a stateful counter on each node, together with a consensus algorithm to ensure that each node has a unique node number.  This is not particularly attractive, since it means a consensus problem turns into a cryptographic disaster._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Operations are dramatically simplified: users do not need to worry about key rotation.  The overhead of the KDF should be dwarfed by the overhead of the Vault RPC itself, unless I am missing something._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Most people [do not deal with key rotation](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/13025#issuecomment-961889260), nor should they need to.

title: Feature request: Enable extensible physical layer (plugin)
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
vault physical package only support a limited number of databases drivers, different applications may have different architecture when it comes to persisting the data, _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
extend vault plugin to support physical Backend & HABackend _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
n/a_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
1. assume the site setup consists of three replicated sites where one of the sites is active and the other is in standby mode for ha purposes, _x000D_
each site consists of a vault and database with another bunch of containers. _x000D_
indeed to put the vault on active, standby mode, the vault is required to connect into one single database to acquire the lock which interferes with the system architecture. _x000D_
right now the only solution is to connect all vaults from all sites into the same active database and when the failover takes place, reconfigure the vault followed by a restart.  _x000D_
_x000D_
2. On-premise object storage _x000D_
_x000D_
3. kv database_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Internal Server error "no namespace" on paths /v1/auth/token/lookup-accessor, /v1/auth/token/renew-accessor, /v1/auth/token/revoke-accessor when accessor has random Unicode chars
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Making a `POST` at any of the 4 URLs with `accessor` having the supplied value in the JSON examples, results in `500 - Internal Server Error`_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run curl with the payload supplied in the json files._x000D_
_x000D_
[Tests.zip](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/files/7597582/Tests.zip)_x000D_
_x000D_
Same steps to reproduce for all paths._x000D_
_x000D_
This was discovered while running a fuzzing tool I wrote for OpenAPI specs: https://github.com/Endava/cats. You can replay all the tests using:_x000D_
_x000D_
`./cats.jar replay --tests="Test349.json,Test785.json,Test1163.json"`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
A `400` response._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.9.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.9.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: macOS Monterey 12.0.1 _x000D_
_x000D_
Probably same root cause as: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/13225_x000D_
_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: ryowright: Hi @ludovicianul, so after taking a closer look at the cause of the "no namespace" error, it doesn't seem to be the unicode characters that cause the "no namespace" response, but rather the periods ('.') that are within the unicode strings. According to the source code in the `vault/token_store.go` file, the function that handles these particular requests attempts to parse a namespace ID through specific characters in the string (one of them being '.'). Because there are multiple '.' characters within the unicode strings provided in the .json files, a portion of the string gets parsed as a namespace ID that is invalid because it cannot be found, resulting in the "no namespace" error. I have also tested a portion of the unicode strings without the '.'s and this results in a proper 400 response with the "invalid accessor" error message. If I may ask, is the "invalid accessor" error, the one you were expecting for the proper 400 response? Also, I will attach the json file I used with a unicode string with no periods ('.') as the payload if you would like to test this in case I may have missed something: [payload2.json.zip](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/files/7630560/payload2.json.zip) | ryowright: I believe this may also be the root cause of the "namespace error" for [Issue #13273](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/13273). | ludovicianul: Hi @ryowright. Yes, I would expect a 400 "invalid accessor". I see 500 for things which are not predicable, rather than an expected known error. I initially wondered what might've caused the 500 as not all random Unicodes was causing it. I suspected the right-to-left text marker. Thanks for checking this.

title: Make grace period of lease configurable
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When I using **consul_template** to generate certificate from Vault PKI, I want to know explicit renew period. But in Vault, it is hard code inside [`calcuateGrace`](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/lifetime_watcher.go#L379-L391) function._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Set up grace period by configuration. Ratio or specific grace period(with some jitter internally) in PKI issue API (or globally)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Predict the period or using cron job._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Maybe renewable credentials of Database._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
It might be useless when dealing with short period._x000D_

title: Unable to get just the secret values (data) if the secret itself contains a "data" key

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
The only way (afair) to get list of `key: value` from a secret, but not the metadata, is by executing_x000D_
_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
vault kv get --field data --format yaml mysecret_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The usecase for getting all keys (instead of a particular one) is, for example, generation of an `.env` file._x000D_
_x000D_
Now, if you run `vault kv get` _without_ `--field data`, you will receive lots of metadata (lease id, duration, etc). To filter those out, you want to run it with `--field data`. The problem is that you won't get a list of all keys **if** one of the keys is actually called **data**._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
$ vault kv put dev/foo user=alice pass=123_x000D_
$ vault kv put dev/bar user=alice pass=123 data=err_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
$ vault kv get --field data --format yaml dev/foo_x000D_
pass: "123"_x000D_
user: alice_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
$ vault kv get --field data --format yaml dev/bar_x000D_
err_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
$ vault kv get --field data --format yaml dev/bar_x000D_
pass: "123"_x000D_
user: alice_x000D_
data: err_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:** Vault v1.9.0_x000D_
_x000D_
**Comment:**_x000D_
_x000D_
Possible workaround would be to use a 3rd party tool (eg. [yq](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq)) and filter the results yourself, although.. that's still just a workaround._x000D_
_x000D_
``` _x000D_
vault kv get --format yaml dev/bar | yq -M e .data.data -_x000D_
```

ryowright: According to the source code in the `command/kv_get.go` file, ``` if data, ok := secret.Data["data"]; ok && data != nil { // If they requested a literal "data" see if they meant actual // value or the data block itself if c.flagField == "data" { if dataMap, ok := data.(map[string]interface{}); ok { if _, ok := dataMap["data"]; ok { return PrintRawField(c.UI, dataMap, c.flagField) } } return PrintRawField(c.UI, secret, c.flagField) } return PrintRawField(c.UI, data, c.flagField) } ``` Vault kv handles having both a "data" literal field and the user wanting to only see the data (and not the metadata) by returning the value for the key "data". If there happens to be a "data" key, then it will default to displaying the "data" key's corresponding value. This results because the purpose of the `--field` option is to specify a specific key and have that key's value returned. My proposed solution so that this bug does not reproduce itself with another keyword, would be to create a `--metadata` field that users can set to true or false to display or hide the metadata. However, this would require a significant amount of change to the code, and I am not sure if it is ideal. @hsimon-hashicorp What are your thoughts? I can implement this if you are okay with the code change.

title: ACL Policies wildcard usage at odds with the Idiomatic Unix glob pattern usage
body_text:
**Feature Request:**_x000D_
Comment on the **_ACL Policies path pattern/wildcard design_** _x000D_
It is quite **_counter Intuitive and not aligned_** with the most accepted path regex pattern semantics espoused by the Unix [GLOB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glob_(programming))_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Version: 1.9.0_x000D_
* Operating System/Architecture: Alpine Linux Docker Container on K8s_x000D_
* _x000D_
* I did find [HashiCorp’s glob usage](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/concepts/policies) at odds with what is the accepted and prevalent glob behavior in most implementations( Python,Java and Unix/Linux)_x000D_
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------_x000D_
**Basic Globbing - Globbing cheatsheet**_x000D_
```_x000D_
Character Description_x000D_
* Matches any character zero or more times, except for /_x000D_
** Matches any character zero or more times, including /_x000D_
? Matches any character except for / one time_x000D_
[abc] Matches any characters inside the brackets. For example, [abc] would match the characters a, b or c, and nothing else._x000D_
Notes:_x000D_
_x000D_
* typically does not match dotfiles (file names starting with a .) unless explicitly enabled by the user via options_x000D_
? also typically does not match the leading dot_x000D_
More than two stars in a glob path segment are typically interpreted as a single star (e.g. /***/ is the same as /*/)_x000D_
```_x000D_
https://docs.python.org/3/library/glob.html is aligned to the summary above and so is Java, looking at a build files for subdirectories under path: **/*.java in ant files_x000D_
_x000D_
that begs the question why would HashiCorp not align their path pattern matching to glob accepted semantics?_x000D_
for instance in HashiCorp, _x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
secret/data/test/* would match secret/data/test/one, secret/data/test/one/tester and secret/data/test/two_x000D_
Also,_x000D_
secret/data/test* would match secret/data/testtwo, secret/data/test/two, secret/data/test-one but not secret/data/tes/one_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
And their use of + in path based patterns(which is not a glob token)_x000D_
NonPlussed and Counter Intuitive implementation to say the least._x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks
top_3_comments_text: ncabatoff: Hi @RoopGuron, This is indeed counter-intuitive, unfortunately. However, we didn't want traditional regex or glob semantics for this use case: they weren't the right fit for the functionality we wanted to offer. And we were constrained as to what symbols were available to use: we had to use symbols that couldn't exist already in paths, we wanted them to be ASCII rather than weird unicode symbols, and that really didn't leave many options. Sorry, it's just one of those things you're going to have to get used to when working with Vault.

title: Token roles don't respect 'allowed_entity_aliases' parameter
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When a token role is created using the `allowed_entity_aliases` parameter it is still possible to create a token using the role when no entity alias is passed._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1) Create a dev server with the needed resources:_x000D_
```shell_x000D_
$ vault server -dev &_x000D_
$ export VAULT_ADDR='http://127.0.0.1:8200'_x000D_
$ vault login [root token]_x000D_
_x000D_
# Create a KV with a secret_x000D_
$ vault secrets enable -path=TEST -version=1 kv_x000D_
$ vault write TEST/somesecret password=passw0rd_x000D_
_x000D_
# Create a policy that allows reading the above secret and the role, restricting the aliases allowed to use it_x000D_
$ echo '{ "path": [ { "TEST/*": { "capabilities": ["read", "list"] } } ] }' | vault policy write read_secret -_x000D_
$ vault write auth/token/roles/read_test_role allowed_policies=read_secret allowed_entity_aliases=privileged_alias_x000D_
_x000D_
# Enable userpass, create a user and a policy that allows it to create tokens using the role_x000D_
$ vault auth enable userpass_x000D_
$ echo '{ "path": [ { "auth/token/create/read_test_role": { "capabilities": ["update"] } } ] }' | vault policy write someuser_policy -_x000D_
$ vault write auth/userpass/users/someuser password='12344321' token_policies=someuser_policy_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
2) Check that the user can't read the secret and can't create a token using his alias_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault login -method=userpass username=someuser password=12344321_x000D_
$ vault read TEST/somesecret_x000D_
Error reading TEST/somesecret: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: GET http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/TEST/somesecret_x000D_
Code: 403. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* 1 error occurred:_x000D_
        * permission denied_x000D_
_x000D_
$ export VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault token create -role=read_test_role -entity-alias=someuser -field token)_x000D_
Error creating token: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: POST http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/token/create/read_test_role_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* invalid 'entity_alias' value_x000D_
_x000D_
$ unset VAULT_TOKEN_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
3) But the user is able to get a token and read the secret, without passing the `entity_alias` parameter or with a valid alias:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ export VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault token create -role=read_test_role -field token)_x000D_
$ vault read TEST/somesecret_x000D_
Key                 Value_x000D_
---                 -----_x000D_
refresh_interval    768h_x000D_
password            passw0rd_x000D_
_x000D_
$ unset VAULT_TOKEN_x000D_
$ export VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault token create -role=read_test_role -entity-alias=privileged_alias -field token)_x000D_
$ vault read TEST/somesecret_x000D_
Key                 Value_x000D_
---                 -----_x000D_
refresh_interval    768h_x000D_
password            passw0rd_x000D_
_x000D_
$ unset VAULT_TOKEN_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The [documentation](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/auth/token#allowed_entity_aliases) states that:_x000D_
_x000D_
> allowed_entity_aliases (string: "", or list: []) - String or JSON list of allowed entity aliases. If set, specifies the entity aliases which are allowed to be used during token generation. This field supports globbing. Note that allowed_entity_aliases is not case sensitive._x000D_
_x000D_
If a list of allowed users is set, there's no point in allowing anyone else to generate a token using the role. The API should refuse generating the token when `entity-alias` is not passed/empty. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.9.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.9.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS / amd64_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s): none, dev server_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
None_x000D_

kauedg: @ncabatoff any insights on this issue? If a token role was supposed to be protected from unauthorized token generation, based on an entity alias whitelist, and an unauthorized alias is able to create a token from this role, it is clear to me it's a case of unauthorized access. ncabatoff: I think you are envisioning a different use case than was intended for allowed_entity_aliases. We could add a require_entity_alias bool param to roles for your use case.
kauedg: > I think you are envisioning a different use case than was intended for allowed_entity_aliases. We could add a require_entity_alias bool param to roles for your use case. Which use case would require an allowed entity list but allowing any alias to request tokens, at the same time? I believe that the field's name implies that other aliases shouldn't be allowed to request tokens, so the new field wouldn't even be required. If there's such use case then I think the `require_entity_alias` should be created.
ncabatoff: The field was added in https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/6267, and the fact that they made it optional suggests to me that they weren't thinking about it the same way you are. Either way, we can't change this retroactively without the risk of breaking things for someone, so the new behaviour you're looking for must be opted-in to via a new field.
kauedg: > The field was added in #6267, and the fact that they made it optional suggests to me that they weren't thinking about it the same way you are. Either way, we can't change this retroactively without the risk of breaking things for someone, so the new behaviour you're looking for must be opted-in to via a new field. So, if I understood correctly, `allowed_entity_aliases` is an *additional* list of aliases that are able to create a role token from this role, beyond the entities that already have permissions (by means of a policy) to do so?
ncabatoff: I don't think so. allowed_entity_aliases specifies which entities can be bound to tokens created with that role. It doesn't constrain token creation, it grants permission to extend the privileges of the created token by granting it the permissions associated with the entity tied to be to the specified alias. Another use case is for billing: with Vault Enterprise, you're billed based on how many "clients" you have, so by using tying the token to an entity you can ensure the "client" associated with that token will be that entity. This is less important in recent versions, since we treat all tokens with the same set of policies in a given namespace as a single "client". If you want to restrict access to the token role to specific entities, you should use identity policies to grant access to the role endpoint.
kauedg: Here we go, now I got it. Maybe the field's documentation could use some rephrasing. The endpoint has fields that are related to the endpoint (like `allowed_policies`) while others are related to the created token (like `orphan`). They have different definitions on to which case they apply. Maybe the `allowed_entity_aliases` description could be changed to something more alike to those about the token.

title: Add certificate extensions as metadata
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I'm running a configuration management tool (puppet) on ~1000 nodes in a decentralized manner, and each node needs access to vault, limited to a number of scopes depending on the node properties (role such as webserver/compute node/..., hostname, ...). The number of nodes and the set of possible "roles" changes regularly, and I want rather static vault policies based on identity metadata._x000D_
_x000D_
This is currently partially possible by using the puppet host certificates combined with the cert authentication method: the certificate name, common name and serial number are already available as identity metadata and can be used in policy templates. This means that I can already create a policy that restricts read access to paths in vault containing the hostname (= certificate common name) as a variable. However, I would need more key value metadata retrieved from the certificate to work efficiently._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
All certificate ASN1 extensions should be added as key/value pairs in the metadata._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Creating a single approle role and different secret_id's for each host, with metadata, but I ran into #11798. Creating a role_id per host is too dynamic and would require manually creating policies and assignments, when my set of host "roles" grows. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Any situation where certificates carry embedded metadata as ASN1 extensions, would benifit from the possibility to use it in vault policy templating._x000D_

h4l: @voiprodrigo (or anyone else looking for this) you probably need to enable the [`enable_identity_alias_metadata` option](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/cert#enable_identity_alias_metadata): ```console # vault write auth/cert/config enable_identity_alias_metadata=true ``` Without this enabled, the entity alias created when authenticating does not contain the metadata, so the ACL template can't populate it. Verify the alias is populated correctly by reading its alias data from `identity/entity-alias/id/<id>`: ```console # vault read identity/entity-alias/id/7fb503bd-5039-df91-a5fd-c83ba1b8a1fa Key Value --- ----- canonical_id e25fd73a-51c1-c723-f363-2f92bafef24a creation_time 2023-03-01T14:42:18.073514135Z custom_metadata <nil> id 7fb503bd-5039-df91-a5fd-c83ba1b8a1fa last_update_time 2023-03-01T14:42:18.073514135Z local false merged_from_canonical_ids <nil> metadata map[1-3-6-1-4-1-34380-1-1-8:super-db authority_key_id: cert_name:testbed common_name:db1.superapp.example.local serial_number:119173039740046606856485670279679599198664210762 subject_key_id:] mount_accessor auth_cert_f67089d9 mount_path auth/cert/ mount_type cert name db1.superapp.example.local namespace_id root ``` (You can find the entity-alias ID by `vault token lookup <token>` to find the token's `entity_id`, then read the entity via that id from `identity/entity/id/<id>`, the entity-alias id will be in the entity metadata.) If you can see the metadata there, the policy template can reference it like any normal entity alias metadata, e.g: ```hcl path "secret/data/app/{{identity.entity.aliases.${cert_mount_accessor}.metadata.1-3-6-1-4-1-34380-1-1-8}}" { capabilities=["read","list"] } ```

title: PKI: /sign-verbatim - key_usage and ext_key_usage request params are used as defaults instead of restrictions
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
/sign-verbatim API documentation states that "key_usage" and "ext_key_usage" request params should be used as restrictions for the allowed values of those certificate extensions. From docs:_x000D_
`key_usage (list: ["DigitalSignature", "KeyAgreement", "KeyEncipherment"]) – Specifies the allowed key usage constraint on issued certificates...`_x000D_
`ext_key_usage (list: []) – Specifies the allowed extended key usage constraint on issued certificates...`_x000D_
_x000D_
However if the CSR includes those extentitions the values of the request params are discarded and the certificate is issued with "Key Usage" and "Extended Key Usage" extensions as they are defined in the CSR._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Generate a CSR with "Extended Key Usage"  = "CodeSigning" in it._x000D_
2. Sign the certificate using /sign-verbatim endpoint and add "ext_key_usage: ["ServerAuth"]" param in the request. _x000D_
3. Parse the issued certificate and see that it includes  "Extended Key Usage"  extension has a value equal to "CodeSigning" (as it was defined in the CSR)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
1. If the CSR does not contain "Key Usage" and/or "Extended Key Usage" extensions the ones specified in the request are used for issuing the certificate (that's the current behaviour as well)_x000D_
2. If the CSR contains "Key Usage" and/or "Extended Key Usage" extensions only the values that match the request params will be kept and the others will be discarded._x000D_
3.  If the CSR contains "Key Usage" and/or "Extended Key Usage" extensions but none of them matches the request params the signing of the certificate will be rejected with a proper error.  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The issue seems to be that:_x000D_
`x509.CreateCertificate`_x000D_
method discards any "certTemplate" member values if they are already part of "certTemplate.ExtraExtensions"_x000D_

title: Error with Postgresql Engine `row is too big: size 8480, maximum size 8160`
body_text:
I have had errors in postgresql when lots of roles are created. The error:_x000D_
```_x000D_
row is too big: size 8480, maximum size 8160_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This is because the limitation of granting permissions to a role. The best way to do this is not to gran all permissions to the dynamic role. I better to create a "generic" role and then  grant the "generic" role to created role:_x000D_
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57087519/row-is-too-big-maximum-size-8160-when-running-grant-connect-on-database_x000D_
_x000D_
Steps:_x000D_
_x000D_
Create generic role:_x000D_
```_x000D_
CREATE ROLE "generic-role";_x000D_
ALTER ROLE "generic-role" NOLOGIN;_x000D_
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE database TO "generic-role";_x000D_
```_x000D_
Vault creation statement:_x000D_
```_x000D_
CREATE ROLE \"{{name}}\" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '{{password}}' VALID UNTIL '{{expiration}}' NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOSUPERUSER;_x000D_
GRANT generic-role to \"{{name}}\";_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
With this it will work better.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Given a config like this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "auto_auth": {_x000D_
    "sink": [_x000D_
      {_x000D_
        "config": {_x000D_
          "mode": 256,_x000D_
          "path": "/run/keys/my-token"_x000D_
        },_x000D_
        "type": "file"_x000D_
      }_x000D_
    ]_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
_Note the 256 is to work around #9404.__x000D_
_x000D_
The `/run/keys/my-token` file is deleted and recreated with the owner / group running the Vault agent. This is different from the templating support, which will preserve the owner and group of the existing file._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
I would like to specify the owner and group of the sink file, _or_, have the sink preserve the ownership._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Running `vault login` in a loop to create the file instead._x000D_

When initialising an empty Vault cluster with three nodes from scratch with two shared keys and also a key threshold of two the number of shared keys is displayed wrong after a force restore from a snapshot from a Vault with five shared keys._x000D_
At the leader Vault node the correct number of shared keys is displayed, but the follower will only show, that they are setup with two shared keys._x000D_
When restarting all Vaults and unsealing them again it is displayed everywhere correctly._x000D_
I also found out, that when stepping-down the leader the formerly follower, that showed the wrong number of keys is displaying the right number of keys as a leader._x000D_

3. Unseal Vault with the unseal keys from the restored backup_x000D_

title: Adjust Vault Agent Log Level Until Dependencies Resolved (or Resolution Fails)
body_text:
Debugging and troubleshooting is difficult with current log levels for Vault Agent.  Specifically, If you use a parameterized path for kv secrets, such as the following:_x000D_
```_x000D_
{{- with secret (printf "kv/path_prefix/%s/env" (file "/vault/secrets/dag_id" | trimSpace)) -}}_x000D_
{{ range $k, $v := .Data.data }}_x000D_
{{ $k }}={{ $v }}_x000D_
{{- end -}}_x000D_
{{- end }}_x000D_
```_x000D_
You will get warning such as the following with the default INFO level logging:_x000D_
```_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:16:24.388Z [WARN] (view) vault.read(kv/path_prefix//env): no secret exists at kv/data/path_prefix/env (retry attempt 1 after "250ms")_x000D_
```_x000D_
This suggest that the file /vault/secrets/dag_id has a null content, or content that was nulled by the trimSpace.  This causes customers to _go down the rabbit hole_ and waste time thinking that there is an issue with this file._x000D_
_x000D_
Turning logging level to DEBUG shows the following (only pertinent logs shown):_x000D_
```_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.786Z [DEBUG] (runner) missing dependency: file(/vault/secrets/dag_id)_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.786Z [DEBUG] (runner) missing dependency: vault.read(kv/path_prefix//env)_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.786Z [DEBUG] (runner) add used dependency file(/vault/secrets/dag_id) to missing since isLeader but do not have a watcher_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.786Z [DEBUG] (runner) add used dependency vault.read(kv/path_prefix//env) to missing since isLeader but do not have a watcher_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.786Z [DEBUG] (watcher) adding file(/vault/secrets/dag_id)_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.786Z [DEBUG] (watcher) adding vault.read(kv/path_prefix//env)_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.811Z [WARN] (view) vault.read(kv/path_prefix//env): no secret exists at kv/data/path_prefix/env (retry attempt 1 after "250ms")_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.899Z [DEBUG] (runner) missing dependency: file(/vault/secrets/dag_id)_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.899Z [DEBUG] (runner) missing dependency: vault.read(kv/path_prefix//env)_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.902Z [DEBUG] (runner) missing dependency: vault.read(kv/path_prefix/dag_id_1234/env)_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.902Z [DEBUG] (runner) add used dependency vault.read(kv/path_prefix/dag_id_1234/env) to missing since isLeader but do not have a watcher_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.902Z [DEBUG] (runner) was not watching 1 dependencies_x000D_
2021-12-16T16:30:27.902Z [DEBUG] (watcher) adding vault.read(kv/path_prefix/dag_id_1234/env)_x000D_
more logs..._x000D_
```_x000D_
So it is clear that the contents of the vault/secrets/dag_id file is `dag_id_1234`, which exists before vault agent is run._x000D_
_x000D_
What I'd like to see is that WARN log message turned into a DEBUG, or at most INFO, if there are pending dependencies that have not been resolved yet.  There is no reason to log this as a WARN at this point in the process.  It distracts and wastes time in the troubleshooting process.  Normal processing should not produce WARN log messages.  I can see CRITICAL and ERROR messages if the vault agent process itself fails, due to internal panic or something.  WARN messages perhaps if the end-result of the resolution of dependencies fail and vault agent is ultimately not able to render the file.  But for situations such as these where there is no issue rendering the file, there should be no WARN messages._x000D_
_x000D_
There really are no alternatives to fixing the log levels.  For customers that parse the logs and show service health or even alert on warning messages, this would mean either false positives, or having to create custom parsers, perhaps specific to individual applications, to ignore these log messages._x000D_

title: pki: ca_chain endpoints do not return the chain when populated by root/generate
body_text:
**Background**_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault has 3 endpoints for reading certificates from a PKI secrets engine, one of which has multiple options for the response:_x000D_
1. [pki/ca/pem](https://www.vaultproject.io/api/secret/pki#read-ca-certificate) - returns the single certificate_x000D_
2. [pki/ca_chain](https://www.vaultproject.io/api/secret/pki#read-ca-certificate-chain) - returns the full certificate chain_x000D_
3. [pki/cert/{ca,ca_chain}](https://www.vaultproject.io/api/secret/pki#read-certificate) - returns a JSON response with either the single certificate, or the full certificate chain_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
`pki/ca_chain` and `pki/cert/ca_chain` return an empty response when the value was created with [/pki/root/generate/internal](https://www.vaultproject.io/api/secret/pki#generate-root). They correctly return the full chain if the value was populated using [/pki/intermediate/set-signed](https://www.vaultproject.io/api/secret/pki#submit-ca-information)._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault secrets enable pki_x000D_
$ vault write -field=certificate pki/root/generate/internal common_name="dc1.consul"_x000D_
_x000D_
$ curl -v "${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/pki/ca_chain"_x000D_
# 204 No Content , with empty response body_x000D_
_x000D_
$ curl -v "${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/pki/cert/ca_chain"_x000D_
{"data":{"certificate":"","revocation_time":0}}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
The docs say the following about these endpoints:_x000D_
_x000D_
> This endpoint retrieves the CA certificate chain, **including the CA**_x000D_
_x000D_
And, when a chain is saved using `/pki/intermediate/set-signed` they do properly return the full chain (including the root cert, if it was included in the PEM passed to set-signed)._x000D_
_x000D_
So my expectations are:_x000D_
_x000D_
The first `curl` should have a response body with the certificate PEM, not an empty response. A chain of 1 root cert is still a valid chain._x000D_
_x000D_
The second `curl` should have a non-empty value for `data.certificate`. The value should be the certificate PEM of the root cert.

title: Allow configuration for TLS session reset when reloading certificates
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When reloading certifications for Vault using `SIGHUP`, Vault keeps the certificate sessions and does not allow any configuration for it. The current implementation uses the Go TLS defaults which is [7 days](https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.16.12:src/crypto/tls/common.go;l=743)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
On TLS load (can be done [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/internalshared/listenerutil/listener.go#L75)), enable configuration for session reset. Implementation can use [SetSessionTicketKeys](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls#Config.SetSessionTicketKeys) in order to reset existing saved sessions. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
The only option we have found that resets sessions is restarting Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
- A good example is doing certificate rotation on an extremely short time (sub 15 minutes) and needing to reset existing saved sessions._x000D_
- When certificates become compromised and required to be replaced, Vault keeps the sessions for the compromised ones._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
None._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: cipherboy: \o Hello @orshlom We don't agree with this, for two main reasons: 1. In the case of a compromise of Vault's API certificates, the reasonable scenario here is to seal Vault and investigate the compromise. This more effectively prevents reuse of existing session resumption tickets two ways, one by preventing any sensitive data from being returned over the compromised API, and two, because after compromise you'll likely want to restart Vault completely, clearing the cache. 2. On large scale deployments, if rotating the certificates (via SIGHUP) caused session resumption ticket invalidation, you'd run into a thundering herd problem as all clients were forced to fully re-handshake (potentially with mTLS as well). Except in limited scenarios where certificates are 15 minutes (most short-lived certs are around 30-90 days), sessions tokens live much shorter than cert lifetime and the extension isn't much of a concern. And organic expiration would prevent a thundering herd. I think the best compromise for your deployment would be to lengthen certificate lifecycle and if sessions must be cleared, restart Vault. I'm also not aware of any literature on resetting session caches on traditional certificate rotation (barring compromise of course). Let us know if you disagree or have a reference for truncating session length. In the case of the latter, the best course would probably be to file a bug against Go's TLS library.

body_text: **Describe the bug**_x000D_ Any port is not allowed when using localhost as a redirect URI._x000D_ _x000D_ **To Reproduce**_x000D_ Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_ 1. Waypoint uses a port that is [automatically chosen by the net package in Go](https://github.com/hashicorp/waypoint/blob/main/internal/auth/oidc/cli.go#L33) for starting up an HTTP server for the OIDC callback. Login to Vault via auth method_x000D_ 5. Experience redirect URI mismatch error_x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_ **Expected behavior**_x000D_ The user is authorized without error._x000D_ _x000D_ **Environment:**_x000D_ * Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.9.2_x000D_ * Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.9.2_x000D_ * Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux amd64_x000D_ _x000D_ **Additional context**_x000D_ OAuth 2.0 RFC 8252 documentation: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252#section-7.3_x000D_ Original forum post: https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/oidc-login-error/33562

title: X-Vault-Wrap-TTL gets overwritten by vault agent on calling "sys/wrapping/wrap"
body_text:
While working with one of the services in Kubernetes, we ran into a problem when it is unable to set the wrap TTL for a token, created by the endpoint `sys/wrapping/wrap`. Whatever value was set, the TTL of the token was always 5 minutes. Although, the TTL worked fine with other endpoints. _x000D_
After researching, we found out that it was caused by the vault-agent sidecar, which was running on the same pod with the service. _x000D_
Because the vault agent doesn't have a custom wrapping lookup function, the default one will be used. [The default function](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/release/1.9.x/api/client.go#L1009.) always return the default value of `5m` for `sys/wrapping/wrap`._x000D_
The header of the request, which needs to be forwarded, then [gets copied](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/release/1.9.x/api/client.go#L1012) to a new one._x000D_
Because the `r.WrapTTL` of the request is not empty, it will [overwrite the header](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/release/1.9.x/api/request.go#L133) of the HTTP request, which will be sent out._x000D_
_x000D_
We were looking for a way to set the env variable `VAULT_WRAP_TTL` for the vault agent, but it doesn't seem to support it._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Run a vault instance_x000D_
2. Run a vault agent. It should point to the vault instance._x000D_
3. Create a service that uses the golang API [to write](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/logical.go#L134) to `sys/wrapping/wrap`. The API client should point to the vault agent. Set up a custom wrapping look-up function to return a constant._x000D_
```_x000D_
	client, _ := vaultAPI.NewClient(&vaultAPI.Config{_x000D_
		Address: "<vault-agent-address>",_x000D_
	})_x000D_
	client.SetWrappingLookupFunc(func(operation, path string) string {_x000D_
		return "30m"_x000D_
	})_x000D_
..._x000D_
         client.Logical().Write("sys/wrapping/wrap", data)_x000D_
... _x000D_
```_x000D_
4. Look up the token by `vault token lookup`._x000D_
5. The token TTL is 5m_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Token TTL is set to the value in the header `X-Vault-Wrap-TTL`_x000D_
