title: sys/raw endpoint does not allow writing values that cannot be encoded in json
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The sys/raw/* write endpoint does allow writing values that cannot be encoded in json._x000D_
_x000D_
For example, the mount table optimizes for space by [gzip](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/internals/limits#mount-point-limits) compressing the entry.  In a recovery scenario where we need to modify the mount table, it is not possible to write in the compressed format (since the gzip data likely contains invalid utf-8 byte sequences and cannot be encoded in json).   In that scenario, the mount limits goes from ~7000 to ~1000 before you couldn't use the raw endpoint to modify the mount table without the table entry being too large to fit in storage._x000D_
_x000D_
It is also an issue for fixing issues in the KV mount, since most entries in the KV are protobuf messages, and often cannot be encoded in json._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
Pre-req -- setup vault to use consul_x000D_
1. Run vault with in recovery mode_x000D_
2. Read out the entry for sys/raw/core/mounts_x000D_
3. Write back table mount entry into sys/raw/core/mounts_x000D_
4. Notice the mount table entry in consul is significantly bigger then before_x000D_
5. Then try to use gzip the entry like vault's compress util library; and then notice writing it out can't work because the gziped data cannot be encoded in json (invalid utf-8 sequences)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
sys/raw support writing values that cannot be encoded in json.  i.e.  sys/raw takes an alternative "value_base64" argument that is used if "value" is empty.  "value_base64" is the base64 encoded value of intended entry (allowing data that cannot be encoded in json)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault 1.9

title: SPIFFE/Spire compatible TLS + x509/JWT-SVID termination
body_text:
#### Feature Description

1. Vault terminates tls connections via spiffe/go-sdk, which in turn provisions and atomically cycles cryptographic material on `crypto/tls.Config`.

2. Vault further uses spiffe/go-sdk to validate JWT- or x509-SVIDs against a configurable set of workload identities (SPIFFE-IDs). (JWT-SVID can easilly cross the L7 boundary, while x509-SVID can double up for mTLS)

3. Vault accepts JWT-SVIDs (bearer tokens) directly as ACL tokens (to avoid the bothersome login step).

#### Use Case(s)

Zero trust environments governed by SPIFFE/spire.

/cc @manveru

- https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/11974

I don't (personally) see the value here in _both_ a numeric value and an absolute timestamp (which, would have to go in a second field btw, perhaps `not_before`). Unlike NotAfter (where the Y10K date is a good reason to specify the exact NotAfter value -- because as an offset in seconds, it'd overflow a 64-bit numeric type), I don't really see the value in backdating by that much? title: Request Forward errors during Active Node rotation
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
TL;DR Request forward errors during Active Node rotation of Vault HA configuration._x000D_
_x000D_
We often see these client forward request error logs during our EC2 instance rotation process which sends a sigterm signal to the running docker container hosting the Active Node. This seems to indicate that a request was sent to the Vault cluster, routed to a standby node and failed because there was no Active Node Address to route to. This re-election process is taking less than a second in most cases that we have seen and pending the incoming traffic volume we see 1-3 forward request errors during this process._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
{_x000D_
  @level | error_x000D_
  @message | error during forwarded RPC request_x000D_
  @module | core_x000D_
  @timestamp | 2022-01-11T20:26:34.495207Z_x000D_
  error | rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. send sigterm to Active Node docker container_x000D_
2. See error pending traffic volume during Active Node being rotated_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The expectation here is to avoid client forward request errors during Active Node rotation. We expect to see a zero downtime Active Node rotation process when the sigterm signal is sent to the Active Node container. The current understanding is that the Active Node will graceful shutdown and the cluster will elect a new Active Node. This re-election process will cause a small moment of time in which there is no Active Node address (1-3 seconds). The expectation during this rotation is that the request will be held until there is an active node address to route to. Its our understanding that there is a write concurrency limitation which is why there can only be at most 1 Active Node Address, however we don't expect for requests to fail during this time period._x000D_
_x000D_

title: Documentation consistency for "Kubernetes Auth"
body_text:
Dear Hashicorp Vault Team,_x000D_
_x000D_
Hope you are doing well. Thank you for the amazing support and creating documentation for the same. We really appreciate it. _x000D_
_x000D_
Recently, we want to create a `Certificate Authority` using `Vault` and issue certificates using `cert-manager` cluster-issuer in `Kubernetes` that requires creating a `service account` and `ClusterRoleBinding` for that service account._x000D_
_x000D_
I am afraid to say, it took my approx 3-4 days to do the same with good amount of debugging, googling, reading issues and what I am doing wrong whereas it's probably a 30 mins job ._x000D_
_x000D_
The problem is a bit of miss in the documentation. For instance, for creating the CA and using cert-manager, there's a [Configure Vault as a Certificate Manager in Kubernetes with Helm](https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/kubernetes-cert-manager?in=vault/kubernetes), now if we read this documentation. In the [Configure Kubernetes authentication](https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/kubernetes-cert-manager?in=vault/kubernetes#configure-kubernetes-authentication), there is a _x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/kubernetes/config \_x000D_
    kubernetes_host="https://$KUBERNETES_PORT_443_TCP_ADDR:443" \_x000D_
    token_reviewer_jwt="$(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)" \_x000D_
    kubernetes_ca_cert=@/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt \_x000D_
    issuer="https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"_x000D_
Success! Data written to: auth/kubernetes/config_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Now, it is not exactly provided that which `service account` is `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`. A beginner like me just blindly copied the code and executed (I am not the only one).  Now, later in [section Configure an issuer and generate a certificate](https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/kubernetes-cert-manager?in=vault/kubernetes#configure-an-issuer-and-generate-a-certificate), we create a service account `issuer` that is ideally used for Kubernetes authentication, rather than the one that was mounted on the `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token` in the `vault-0` pod._x000D_
_x000D_
Now, here I was confused whether there are two `service accounts` - `issuer` and the `default` in either the `default` namespace or `cert-manager` namespace.  Further, the above documentation fails to mention the `ClusterRoleBinding` required for the service account for Kubernetes Auth._x000D_
_x000D_
So, the result of following the above documentation kind of results into multiple people facing issues like [Kubernetes Authentication Denied](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/kubernetes-authentication-denied/9324/15) and [Vault ClusterIssuer with Kubernetes authentication not possible?](https://github.com/jetstack/cert-manager/issues/2969#issuecomment-711245377)_x000D_
_x000D_
Documentation [Integrate a Kubernetes Cluster with an External Vault](https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/kubernetes-external-vault?in=vault/kubernetes#configure-kubernetes-authentication) also doesn't mention anything about `ClusterRoleBinding` probably because helm would have installed it automatically (might be wrong)._x000D_
_x000D_
Now, the best and proper documentation on Kubernetes Auth that solved my issue in 5 mins was [Vault Agent with Kubernetes](https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/agent-kubernetes?in=vault/kubernetes). It clearly mentions about process of Kube Auth, `service account`, `TokenReviewAPI` and `ClusterRoleBinding`. I followed this and was able to resolve the issue. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Suggestion**_x000D_
_x000D_
A minor suggestion I have is maybe we can structure the tutorials/documentation in a different way. For instance,_x000D_
_x000D_
- Vault Installation _x000D_
  - Downloading binary and running it_x000D_
  - Via Helm3_x000D_
  - Via Kubernetes Operator_x000D_
- Kubernetes Auth_x000D_
  - Vault Agent (installed using Helm and using injector)_x000D_
  - Creating service account (providing access to TokenReviewAPI/ ClusterRoleBinding)_x000D_
  - Any other method_x000D_
_x000D_
The benefit probably might be _x000D_
- Clear and concise documentation_x000D_
- Less repeatation of documentation. For instance, in most of the tutorials, we install MiniKube, setup Vault using Helm, configure Kubernetes Auth. There are high chances of these subsection being out-of-sync as result of 1) being written by different authors 2) some tutorial being updated/left. _x000D_
- If we follow the above structure, we can just point to one doc and say "Install Minikube" as described here._x000D_
_x000D_
Just sharing the thoughts, feel free to ignore. _x000D_
_x000D_
Thank you again for your awesome support._x000D_
_x000D_
Kind Regards,_x000D_
Vijay_x000D_
_x000D_

title: TestCoreUnsealed does not work with vendoring since v1.9.0
body_text:

_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
One of the best things about Vault is the ability to execute a real Vault server inside your tests in Golang using `TestCoreUnsealed` and other helper functions._x000D_
_x000D_
It was even advertised by Mitchell in his talks: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yszygk1cpEc&t=3238s_x000D_
_x000D_
With [this commit](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/commit/8e7fd9e794f1b3be560728c126a28fb7a84b6ed7#diff-8007c524cdd10fede4c3b221868199ec601a0e82ae536372291c26eceb815fc4) in 1.9.0, the helper methods cannot be used anymore by the projects, which use go vendoring (arguably most of them), as the `go mod vendor` simply fails due to incorrect `go:embed` usage._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
The same issue was addressed in https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/12507, and quite an elegant solution was proposed by @heppu in https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/13646 _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
The following example code works  with `github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.8.7` in go.mod and vendoring, but starting from `github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.9.0` in go mod it cannot be vendored:_x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
package main_x000D_
_x000D_
import (_x000D_
        "net"_x000D_
        "testing"_x000D_
_x000D_
        "github.com/hashicorp/vault/api"_x000D_
        "github.com/hashicorp/vault/http"_x000D_
        "github.com/hashicorp/vault/vault"_x000D_
        "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"_x000D_
        "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"_x000D_
)_x000D_
_x000D_
func TestAgainstRealVaultServer(t *testing.T) {_x000D_
        serverListener, client := spinUpVault(t)_x000D_
        defer func() { _ = serverListener.Close() }()_x000D_
_x000D_
        // Execute some tests against a real vault server:_x000D_
_x000D_
        data := map[string]interface{}{_x000D_
                "secret": "bar",_x000D_
        }_x000D_
        _, err := client.Logical().Write("secret/foo", data)_x000D_
        require.NoError(t, err)_x000D_
_x000D_
        secret, err := client.Logical().Read("secret/foo")_x000D_
        require.NoError(t, err)_x000D_
_x000D_
        assert.Equal(t, data, secret.Data)_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
func spinUpVault(t *testing.T) (net.Listener, *api.Client) {_x000D_
        t.Helper()_x000D_
        core, _, rootToken := vault.TestCoreUnsealed(t)_x000D_
        ln, addr := http.TestServer(t, core)_x000D_
_x000D_
        client := createClient(t, addr, rootToken)_x000D_
_x000D_
        return ln, client_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
func createClient(t *testing.T, addr string, rootToken string) *api.Client {_x000D_
        conf := api.DefaultConfig()_x000D_
        conf.Address = addr_x000D_
_x000D_
        client, err := api.NewClient(conf)_x000D_
        if err != nil {_x000D_
                t.Fatal(err)_x000D_
        }_x000D_
        client.SetToken(rootToken)_x000D_
        return client_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
Executing `go get -d github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.9.0 && go mod vendor` fails with the following error:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
go mod vendor: pattern web_ui/*: no matching files found_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
Executing `go get -d github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.9.0 && go mod vendor` should succeed._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Go: 1.16_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
It would be great if you could accept https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/13646 or suggest another solution, so everyone can continue to benefit from the amazing testing API of Vault :)_x000D_

title: Support AWS role chaining for AWS secret engine
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
First of all, Vault is awesome :).  _x000D_
_x000D_
I have been trying to configure Vault AWS secret engine with x-account IAM trust to get credential_type assumed_role. The setup works fine for 1 level of indirection but does not work for 2+ levels._x000D_
_x000D_
Here's the setup_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault runs in AWS account A with IAM role - vault_x000D_
vault role is allowed to assume vault-secret role in Account B_x000D_
account B has a role called vault-secret. It has a trust relationship to allow A-vault to assume it. It can also assume any role in account B_x000D_
account B has several IAM roles. Some of these can be assumed by vault-secret role so that Vault could issue ephemeral creds for these roles._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I'd like the above setup to work. When creating the aws secret mount/role, an admin should be able to specify what role Vault should assume in order to get temporary creds for an aws role. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
An alternative is to remove the indirection, ie, allow A-vault to assume any role in account B and update the corresponding roles in account B to setup trust relationship with A-vault directly instead of B-vault-secret._x000D_
_x000D_
This works but it is operationally very expensive to manage, if there are a few hundred accounts like B with thousands of IAM roles managed by different deployment lifecycles. top_3_comments_text: ericl85: This seems to be more of a Windows OpenSSH problem (that it can't read UTF16LE encoded text files). I just ran into this and it took me forever to figure out what the actual problem was. There's another easy workaround other than `dos2unix` though that maybe just needs to be documented as the "Windows" method. The caveat is that you need to be in a Powershell prompt and not a regular command prompt. Instead of: ``` vault write -field=signed_key ssh-client-signer/sign/my-role public_key=@$HOME/.ssh/id_rsa.pub > signed-cert.pub ``` Use: ``` vault write -field=signed_key ssh-client-signer/sign/my-role public_key=@$HOME/.ssh/id_rsa.pub | out-file signed-cert.pub -encoding utf8 ``` | maxb: Unless I'm missing something, there's nothing at all Vault can do here - it's just a quirk of Powershell that Powershell users need to work around. | ericl85: That's why I said it's "more of a windows OpenSSH problem". The underlying issue is that the Powershell `>` operator redirects console text to a file encoded as UTF16LE. However, the Windows OpenSSH client cannot read UTF16LE encoded text files. Vault cannot fix either of those issues. However, they *could* mention in the documentation the work around: rather than direct it directly to a file, pipe it to the `Out-File` command with the explicit encoding. Either way, just wanted to share the alternative workaround to `dos2unix` for anyone else that stumbled on this. 🤷

title: Allow policies to control sub-fields of requests
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
The current policy system works well for controlling the allowed values of "shallow" fields: those at the root of a request. However, for fields that expect a map of values, only a few, restrictive options are currently available:_x000D_
- Existence checking the map, allowing / denying any values within_x000D_
- Perform exact string matches for the entire map against its JSON equivalents_x000D_
_x000D_
For a more concrete example, suppose you wanted to ensure that all `auth/token/create` requests for a given policy, have a populated `metadata` map containing a key (i.e. `creator_id`), set to any value i.e.:_x000D_
```_x000D_
POST auth/token/create_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "meta": {_x000D_
    "creator_id": "creator_1",_x000D_
    "some_other": "meta_key" _x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
As far as I'm aware, this cannot be handled by the current policy scheme. The current policy structure would require either: _x000D_
- Existence checking the map, allowing / denying any values within:_x000D_
  ```hcl_x000D_
  path "auth/token/create" {_x000D_
    allowed_parameters = {_x000D_
      "meta" = []_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  } _x000D_
  ```_x000D_
- Performing exact string matches for the entire map against its JSON equivalents:_x000D_
  ```hcl_x000D_
  path "auth/token/create" {_x000D_
    allowed_parameters = {_x000D_
      "meta" = [{"creator_id" = "creator_1"},_x000D_
        {"creator_id" = "creator_2"}, _x000D_
        {"creator_id" = "creator_1", "some_other" = "meta_key"},_x000D_
        ...]_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  } _x000D_
  ```_x000D_
_x000D_
, neither of which feasibly solves the problem._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
The policy handler should support "nested parameters": constraints on the contents of some field of a request. For example:_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
path "auth/token/create" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]_x000D_
  required_parameters = ["meta.creator_id"]_x000D_
  allowed_parameters = {_x000D_
    "meta.creator_id" = ["creator_*"]_x000D_
    "meta.*" = []_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This should ideally support an arbitrary depth._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Covered in the problem statement._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Any endpoint that accepts any map could benefit from this._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

title: Vault CLI uses unexpected ordering of AWS credential provider chain
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
The Vault CLI uses an AWS credential chain implemented by [hashicorp/go-secure-stdlib](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-secure-stdlib/blob/4b81925bd7d95cdb4ef2e44ae36701693920ab97/awsutil/generate_credentials.go#L123-L230).  This credential chain orders the providers in a different manner than the official AWS implementation of the default credential chain._x000D_
_x000D_
In particular, the credential chain that's being used by the Vault CLI places the `WebIdentityRoleProvider` at a higher precedence than the `EnvProvider`, when it should be the opposite._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
On a host with the Vault CLI installed, configure environment variables for AWS authentication:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Set up static credentials with the environment variables `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`_x000D_
2. Set up web identity token authentication with the environment variables `AWS_ROLE_ARN` and `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`._x000D_
_x000D_
Then, use the Vault CLI to login to a Vault server with AWS IAM authentication configured:_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
$ vault login -method aws role=foo region=us-east-1_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This will cause the Vault CLI to craft signed `STS.GetCallerIdentity` headers for the identity associated with the web identity token, when it should be using the static credentials instead._x000D_
_x000D_
You can verify this by running `aws sts get-caller-identity`, which will return the identity associated with the static credentials, not the web identity token._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
When both static credentials and web identity token authentication methods are specified, the Vault CLI should prefer the static credentials, similar to the official AWS implementation for the default credential provider chain._x000D_
_x000D_
Supporting documentation:_x000D_
_x000D_
- [AWS SDK for Go V2 documentation](https://aws.github.io/aws-sdk-go-v2/docs/configuring-sdk/#specifying-credentials) lists static credentials ahead of web identity tokens in order of precedence._x000D_
- [AWS SDK for Java documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-java/v1/developer-guide/credentials.html) also lists static credentials ahead of web identity tokens._x000D_
_x000D_
Also, as described above, you can observe the expected behavior using the AWS CLI.  When both static credentials and web identity token authentication are configured, the AWS CLI will prefer the static credentials._x000D_
_x000D_
**Suggested Fix**_x000D_
_x000D_
I believe the fix should be made within [hashicorp/go-secure-stdlib](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-secure-stdlib/blob/4b81925bd7d95cdb4ef2e44ae36701693920ab97/awsutil/generate_credentials.go#L123-L230), by moving the code that configures the `EnvProvider` ahead of the code that configures the `WebIdentityRoleProvider`.  I would be happy to submit a PR for this._x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks!

title: Instructions for obtaining Kubernetes service account token manually are incorrect
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/website/content/docs/auth/kubernetes.mdx describes how to obtain a Kubernetes service account token manually as:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
kubectl get secret "$(kubectl get serviceaccount default -o jsonpath='{.secrets[0].name}')"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This is scraping an auto-generated token, rather than requesting one for external use. The auto-generated tokens are only intended for mounting into pods, and with the transition away from secret-based tokens in Kubernetes 1.22+, new secret-based tokens will no longer be auto-generated in future Kubernetes releases (planned starting in Kubernetes 1.24)._x000D_
_x000D_
While use of secret-based tokens is discouraged due to their weaker security properties, if one is still needed, https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#manually-create-a-service-account-api-token has instructions for manually creating a secret to contain a long-lived token._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/website/content/docs/auth/kubernetes.mdx should update to align with or reference those instructions._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: tomhjp: Thanks for raising this - that's a great resource to link to. I agree on the security properties. I am half minded to remove the option altogether, especially now that we have support for auto-reloading projected tokens from 1.9.3. The only thing that gives me pause is the use-case when Vault is not running in the same Kubernetes cluster as the client. I think in most cases I would recommend using Kubernetes as an OIDC provider in that instance (and use Vault's JWT auth). In any case, I've raised #13852 to address this, but there will probably also be some more updates to the structure/wording of that section in the near future.

_x000D_

Multiple implementations are now available and I will list some of them. Depending on whether you work with an internal or external Vault cluster either refer to: 1. (_If working with an internal cluster_) The [documentation](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/auth/kubernetes#kubernetes-1-21) for working with the newly introduced [bound service account token volume](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/service-accounts-admin/#bound-service-account-token-volume) (introduced through beta in Kubernetes 1.21). On top of this you would have to upgrade to the [latest](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/releases/tag/v1.9.3) version of Vault to have the latest Kubernetes auth plugin which supports dynamically reloading short-lived tokens for internal clusters. 2. (_For both internal and external clusters_) The option `disable_iss_validation` to disable local issuer validation (mentioned in the article). This option is enabled by default since this [commit](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-kubernetes/commit/e2a3bbe7fa1c3403229415e007e852c4b2962da8#diff-c6f0305d05f9581c583eb2b15d17d32f412dcbc73809741b065ab801cc5d360e) and deprecated since [v0.7.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-kubernetes/releases/tag/v0.7.1) (included in Vault [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/releases/tag/v1.9.0)) of the Kubernetes auth plugin. With this option your cluster can still use [secret-based service account tokens](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/auth/kubernetes#continue-using-long-lived-tokens). Keep in mind that this option is mostly realizable when working with an **external** cluster. 3. (_For both internal and external clusters_) Personally I would recommend removing the `token_reviewer_jwt` (part of the [documentation](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/auth/kubernetes#:~:text=Use%20client%20JWT%20as%20reviewer%20JWT)), using `disable_iss_validation` to disable local issuer validation, and using a token that is capable of [acting on behalf](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/auth/kubernetes#use-the-vault-client-s-jwt-as-the-reviewer-jwt) of Vault when validating the sent-in service account token while upgrading an **external** cluster. Since you are upgrading it might be hard to fulfil the first option. In that case to fulfil this option downgrading your Openshift cluster might be your last resort, keep this in mind. If downgrading is not an option, I would attempt the second or third option in the list. Next to this: the article linked is no longer completely up-to-date and even holds bad practices in my opinion (such as recommending against disabling local issuer validation). This helped us a lot!! We were able to fix the issue and did not downgrade our cluster. Followed the guide that you have shared - https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/auth/kubernetes#kubernetes-1-21 Added the additional config to Vault using the vault CLI $vault write auth/kubernetes/config \ issuer="<your issuer>" \ token_reviewer_jwt="<your reviewer service account JWT>" \ kubernetes_host=https://IP:<your TCP port or blank for 443> \ kubernetes_ca_cert=@ca.crt \ disable_iss_validation=true And verified if issuer is updated $vault read auth/kubernetes/config Tada! If you don't want to upgrade and don't already use [long-lived-tokens](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/auth/kubernetes#continue-using-long-lived-tokens): I would recommend to start using the [Vault client's JWT as the reviewer JWT](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/auth/kubernetes#use-the-vault-client-s-jwt-as-the-reviewer-jwt)!

I have done the below steps. 1) Create a long live token and attach it to already linked service account in pod 2) update the kubernetes auth config via UI and set "Disable JWT Issuer Validation" and "Disable use of local CA and service account JWT" 3) Updated the Issuer 4) Restart one of the tfc-agent but still I have the same error. `2022-02-02T14:12:18.414Z [ERROR] auth.handler: error authenticating: error= | Error making API request. | | URL: PUT http://vault.vault.svc:8200/v1/auth/kubernetes/login | Code: 403. Errors: | | * permission denied backoff=13.95s`

When working with the long lived token you only need to disable the local JWT issuer validation. This also means that the "issuer" field does not need to be set, as this field is [not used](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-kubernetes/blob/d289258274b7eab9b0eda679ab996c0c91403e78/path_login.go#L257-L264). This token will only be used by Vault to send a `TokenReview` request to your Kubernetes cluster (hence the name). title: Unrecognized settings in vault-conf.hcl are silently ignored
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault is silently ignoring bad configuration settings (inside tcp listener stanzas at least)_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Add this configuration to vault:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
..._x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address = "[::]:18200"_x000D_
  proxy_protocol_behavior = "use_always"_x000D_
  proxy_protocol_authorized_address = "[::1]"_x000D_
  proxy_protocol_behavior = "deny_unauthorized"_x000D_
  tls_disable="true"_x000D_
}_x000D_
..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Note that there is an error in there.  The correct setting is [proxy_protocol_authorized_addrs](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/configuration/listener/tcp#proxy_protocol_authorized_addrs)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should either refuse to start, or should at least log a warning about an invalid setting._x000D_
_x000D_
**Actual behavior**_x000D_
Vault runs as if the bad setting were not present, and I see no mention in the stdout/stderr output captured by systemd (`journalctl -eu vault`)_x000D_
_x000D_
You can confirm the difference between the two cases by using `telnet ::1 18200`_x000D_
_x000D_
* When the correct `proxy_protocol_authorized_addrs` is used: the connection is accepted, and waits for more data_x000D_
* When the erroneous `proxy_protocol_authorized_address` is used: the connection is accepted but immediately dropped, since there is no matched authorized address._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.9.3_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): n/a_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 20.04.3 x86_64_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_

title: Ability to tolower() in ACL templating OR Ignore case with Okta auth method
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We currently have a workflow where terraform will retrieve group membership from Azure AD and create custom user roles for a secrets backend in Vault. So the roles end up looking like `database/static-roles/secret_role_mysamaccountname`._x000D_
_x000D_
Users will then use the Okta auth method and using ACL Policy Path Templating will get access to their role. The policy for ex:_x000D_
```tf_x000D_
resource "vault_policy" "mypolicy" {_x000D_
  name   = "mypolicy"_x000D_
  policy = <<EOT_x000D_
path "database/static-creds/secret_role_{{identity.entity.aliases.auth_okta_eexxxxxx.name}}" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
EOT_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The problem here is that Vault policies + routes are case sensitive whereas entities are sticky. If a user logs in the first time with an uppercase username the entity name is uppercase so the policy gives access to the path `database/static-creds/secret_role_UPPERCASENAME`. In this scenario the user cannot access their role and logging out and back in with a lowercase username does not work because the internal entity application logic is case insensitive so the existing entity will continue to be applied and silently haunt the user._x000D_
_x000D_
This requires us to manually intervene and delete the created entity and have the user log back in with a lowercase username which is not ideal._x000D_
_x000D_
**Solution**_x000D_
Either one of:_x000D_
1. An ability to tolower() in the policy templating so irregardless of entity casing the desired path will be allowed._x000D_
2. An ability to toggle created entity case somehow at the Okta auth method._x000D_
3. Generally ignore entity case._x000D_
4. Others I may not be aware of._x000D_
_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: cognifloyd: Another option might be to use the `login` returned by Okta as a "canonical username" so that Vault uses whatever case Okta uses when it creates the vault entity alias. When the okta auth backend makes the authn request here (or once MFA is complete if not bypassed): https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/0b12cdcfd17278d7cca25ec37ffacd96b8d5c6c7/builtin/credential/okta/backend.go#L121-L130 We can use this to get that `login`: ```go profile := *result.Embedded.User.Profile // map[string]interface{} canonicalUsername := profile["login"].(string) ``` Okta docs links: - The embedded user object: https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/api/authn/#user-object - The embedded user profile object: https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/api/authn/#user-profile-object One major benefit of this approach is that users can login with any of the variants that Okta accepts, including leaving off the email domain: `some.user@example.com`, `Some.User@Example.Com`, `SOME.USER@EXAMPLE.COM`, or just `some.user`. Merely lowercasing the user-provided username would still create duplicate entities for the shortand `some.user`. One shortcoming with this approach is that when the Vault admin (or terraform in your case?) defines users in the okta auth backend, they must use the same case that Okta considers canonical. But maybe, we could get the best of both approaches by lowercasing the `login` string: ```go profile := *result.Embedded.User.Profile // map[string]interface{} canonicalUsername := strings.ToLower(profile["login"].(string)) ``` On upgrade, we would need to migrate any existing okta auth method users (and their entity aliases) to the lowercase variant. PS: I don't have time to actually test this right now, but I hacked together a possible way to make the username case-insensitive and use the `login` as canonical username. https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/compare/main...cognifloyd:vault:okta-case-insensitive Does that look like it would resolve this issue? | peter-fe: #11063, would be a more general approach, what would also enable tolower() functionallity on policy side

This has been added a bit over 6 years ago so I fear the reasoning behind this decision is lost to time :sweat_smile: Looking through other CLI commands, the only other example I can find where we allow passing sensitive information to a Vault command via a env var seems to be [Github](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/github/cli.go#L27). body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
When you configure a scope like this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write identity/oidc/scope/profile \_x000D_
  description="Provides user info" \_x000D_
  template='{_x000D_
    "entity_name": {{identity.entity.name}},_x000D_
    "name": {{identity.entity.metadata.name}},_x000D_
    "organization": {{identity.entity.metadata.organization}},_x000D_
    "preferred_username": {{identity.entity.metadata.username}}_x000D_
}'_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
but the given metadata item(s) are missing from the entity, currently empty claims are returned in the JWT:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
{_x000D_
  ..._x000D_
  "entity_name": "Brian Candler",_x000D_
  "name": "",_x000D_
  "organization": "",_x000D_
  "preferred_username": "",_x000D_
  ..._x000D_
}_x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_

_x000D_
> If a Claim is not returned, that Claim Name SHOULD be omitted from the JSON object representing the Claims; it SHOULD NOT be present with a null or empty string value._x000D_
_x000D_
However, here it is talking about the response to the UserInfo endpoint, rather than the original identity token._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Retain the empty string.  It's a bit ugly though._x000D_
_x000D_
For a JSON claim like_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_

  description="Provides a list of group names" \_x000D_
  template='{_x000D_
    "groups": {{identity.entity.groups.names}}_x000D_
}'_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
(which returns a list) then maybe the empty list *is* still appropriate._x000D_

N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

title: Kubernetes Native Auth - improper entity alias name autogeneration
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
By default, the Kubernetes native auth engine automatically generates entity aliases based on the `serviceaccount_uid`. This  works well but leaves us with unpredictable entity aliases. In vault 1.9.3, the entity alias name source can be changed to `serviceaccount_name`. This is supposed to then generate the entity aliases in the following format: `<namespace>/<service account>` but instead creates the identity alias with the name of `/` (a single forward slash)._x000D_

_x000D_

Configure this engine with a role. Change the very first property of the role to be `serviceaccount_name` instead of the default `serviceaccount_uid`. Deploy an application to the integrated Kubernetes cluster that uses this role. Observe the entity alias that gets created will have the name of `/`. If you change the setting back to the default of `serviceaccount_uid` then delete the pod the Vault entity alias is properly constructed from the serviceaccount_uid as its name._x000D_
_x000D_

title: AppRole secret-id usage visibility
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When using an AppRole with multiple secret-ids, it can be hard to track which ones are being used and where in a secure fashion. This makes it challenging to ensure unused credentials are revoked and audit that only credentials that are expected to be valid are._x000D_
_x000D_
Like tokens, a secret-id has a less sensitive secret-id-accessor. Unfortunately when the secret-id is used to login, the secret-id-accessor is not logged. Additionally looking up a secret-id by it's accessor returns some helpful information such as created, last_updated, and expiration timestamps, it unfortunately does not include information about when the secret-id was last used to authenticate._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Adding the secret-id-accessor information to appauth login logs and storing a last used timestamp against the secret id which can be looked up in `/secret-id-accessor/lookup` and similar calls._x000D_
_x000D_
Noting that by default fields are HMAC'd in the audit logs, I don't expect adding secret-id-accessor to logs to cause any security issues if this was added._x000D_
_x000D_

title: OIDC Provider: "assignments" do not honor inherited groups
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Inherited groups are not honored in the groups list for an OIDC Provider client assignment._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
This requires an OIDC-capable application, in my case Grafana._x000D_
_x000D_
1. Create groups "staff" and "grafana-admin"_x000D_
2. Make the "grafana-admin" group have "staff" as a member group_x000D_
3. Create an OIDC provider assignment called "grafana" which lists the group_id for "grafana-admin"_x000D_
4. Connect the application to the OIDC provider, using this assignment_x000D_
5. Pick a user who is a member of the "staff" group, and try to login as that user._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault read identity/group/name/grafana-admin_x000D_
Key                  Value_x000D_
---                  -----_x000D_
..._x000D_
id                   91326332-7b6c-ed59-f3f4-84607a410ce9_x000D_
..._x000D_
_x000D_
$ vault write identity/oidc/assignment/grafana \_x000D_
    group_ids="91326332-7b6c-ed59-f3f4-84607a410ce9"_x000D_
_x000D_
$ vault write identity/oidc/client/grafana \_x000D_
    redirect_uris="https://xxxxxxxx:443/login/generic_oauth" \_x000D_
    assignments="grafana" \_x000D_

    id_token_ttl="12h" \_x000D_

_x000D_

_x000D_

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I recently conducted an exercise of doing a disaster recovery of a vault cluster (mysql storage backend, raft ha_storage) and discovered that if all of the machine local raft state is missing from all nodes (`raft.db` and `vault.db`) AND none of the nodes was a participant in the cluster previously that no node can be elected active. This makes sense since there is no raft cluster assembled in which to conduct the vote. However, the current bootstrap api (`sys/storage/raft/bootstrap`) will refuse to bootstrap a raft cluster because of the existence of the `core/raft/tls` key in the storage backend. Attempts to call the bootstrap API return an error like:_x000D_
```_x000D_
{"errors":["could not generate TLS keyring during bootstrap: TLS keyring already present"]}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
However if that key is manually removed from the storage backend, for instance by deleting it from mysql in my case, the bootstrap API once again becomes available and you can reassemble the raft cluster._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Ideally I'd like to not have to do "brain surgery" on the storage backend during a disaster recovery exercise. If the `sys/storage/raft/bootstrap` api could take an argument that would instruct it to destructively re-bootstrap in spite of evidence of an existing cluster it would be much cleaner._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
AFAICT the only alternative is to manually edit the storage backend._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
If the number of nodes in a cluster drops below the threshold to form a quorum this feature would also allow forcing a new master such that the members of the raft could be modified. Currently you cannot add or remove peers to the raft if there is no active leader.

No change of existing methods/signatures is required. New methods will be added. The only difference is using the context passed to the method as a parameter instead of `context.Background()`.

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When using the MongoDB Atlas connection type for a database secret, the role appears to ignore the **Generated credentials Time-to-Live (TTL)** when generating dynamic users/leases. 2. Add a connection to MongoDB Atlas_x000D_

4. Generate a credential_x000D_
5. Note that the TTL/expiration does not correspond to the default TTL set in the role._x000D_
_x000D_

The generated user/lease will expire based on the generated ttl setting on the role._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When upgrading a KVv1 mount to KVv2 on a server using the mysql backend the column width of `vault_key` will be insufficient for storing the values used with the KVv2 mount._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1.  Configure vault with a KVv1 mount `vault secrets enable -version=1 kv`_x000D_
2. Store some secrets in the KVv1 mount at an arbitrary depth ala `vault kv put /kv/foo/bar/bing/band/bong/ding/dong baz=boo`_x000D_
3. Upgrade mount with `vault kv enable-versioning secret/`_x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
In an attempt to hide path to secrets users aren't supposed to access, we managed to make it works but what is displayed on the webui is inconsistent._x000D_
We used the following policy:_x000D_
```_x000D_
path "secrets/metadata/+"_x000D_
{_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
path "secrets/metadata/+/+"_x000D_
{_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
path "secrets/metadata/+/subdir2-visible/*"_x000D_
{_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
path "secrets/data/+/subdir2-visible/*"_x000D_
{_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
User should be able to see sub-directories in: "secrets", "secrets/subdir1" and "secrets/subdir1/subdir2-visible/*"_x000D_
but not anything in "secrets/subdir1/subdir2-invisible" which is at the same level as "subdir2-visible"._x000D_
_x000D_
The policy is working as intended and on the web UI, if an user go to "secrets/subdir1/subdir2-invisible", it show nothing inside it which is normal. But if the user then goes back to the parent folder (subdir1), it doesn't list anything anymore until I refresh the page (it shows neither subdir2-visible or subdir2-invisible). _x000D_
Actually, nothing is listed anymore (if we go back further to the parent directory or if we chose to go to another path) until we refresh the page._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1) Set the mentionned policy._x000D_
2) Connect to the vault web ui using an user with the policy set._x000D_
3) Try to see the secret hidden behind the path that is supposed to work (it should works) then go back to a path which isn't supposed to work (you should not see any subdirectory) then go back to a directory where subdirectory are supposed to be shown, for example go up one time to the parent directory, and you should not be able to see any subdirectory (until you refresh the page) that you previously could._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Path/directories/subdirectories that can and are listed should still be listed even if an authorized user go once to a directory where the content can't be listed._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.9.3_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Enabling audit logs with `mode="0000"` changes file permissions
body_text:

_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
Per the vault audit device docs: https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/audit/file#mode_x000D_
_x000D_
Setting `mode="0000"` will prevent vault from modifying the file mode.  The expectation is that if a file is already being logged to and read from by something like cwagent or splunk, vault will not rewrite the file mode.  However, setting `mode="0000"` does not yield the intended result, and vault changes the file mode to the default of 0600._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run `touch /opt/vault/vault_audit.log`_x000D_
2. Run `chmod 0644 /opt/vault/vault_audit.log`_x000D_
3. Run `vault audit enable file file_path="/opt/vault/vault_audit.log" mode="0000"` or run the terraform config snippet below_x000D_
5. Verify file permissions `ls -asl /opt/vault/vault_audit.log` and see that they have been reverted to the default of `0600`_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
resource "vault_audit" "default" {_x000D_
  type = "file"_x000D_
_x000D_
  options = {_x000D_
    file_path = "/opt/vault/vault_audit.log"_x000D_
    mode      = "0000"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault will not touch the file and leave the permissions as they were: `-rw-r--r--`, or `0644`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.8.6+ent_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.8.6+ent_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: ubuntu 20.04_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
disable_performance_standby = true_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
disable_mlock = true_x000D_
storage "raft" {_x000D_
  path    = "/opt/vault/data"_x000D_
  node_id = "${instance_id}"_x000D_
  retry_join {_x000D_
    auto_join = "provider=aws region=us-east-1 tag_key=VaultName tag_value=testing"_x000D_
    auto_join_scheme = "https"_x000D_
    leader_tls_servername = "vault.server.com"_x000D_
    leader_ca_cert_file = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-ca.pem"_x000D_
    leader_client_cert_file = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-cert.pem"_x000D_
    leader_client_key_file = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-key.pem"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
cluster_addr = "https://${ip_addr}:8201"_x000D_
api_addr = "https://vault.server.com"_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address            = "0.0.0.0:8200"_x000D_
  tls_disable        = false_x000D_
  tls_cert_file      = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-cert.pem"_x000D_
  tls_key_file       = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-key.pem"_x000D_
  tls_client_ca_file = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-ca.pem"_x000D_
}_x000D_
seal "awskms" {_x000D_
  region     = "us-east-1"_x000D_
  kms_key_id = "<arn to kms key>"_x000D_
}_x000D_
telemetry {_x000D_
  prometheus_retention_time = "60s"_x000D_
  disable_hostname = true_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Note that when you set the value to something non-zero, like `0644`, it does work as expected.  However, setting it to 0000 per the docs does not work as intended.

title: OIDC Provider: state should be optional in OAuth Code Flow
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Note this report is very similar to "OIDC provider: `nonce` should be optional in authorization code flow" #13204 which has been made optional in Vault 1.9.1._x000D_
_x000D_
I am testing the Tech Preview of OIDC Provider in Vault 1.9.3 on an OpenBSD three node cluster._x000D_
_x000D_
Using the [thenativeweb/wolkenkit-boards](https://github.com/thenativeweb/wolkenkit-boards) as a client, I get the following response:_x000D_
`invalid_request: state parameter is required`_x000D_
_x000D_
However, according to the [OpenID Core Connect specification](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#AuthRequest) section 3.1.2.1, the `state` is "RECOMMENDED" in the Authorization Code Flow._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Setup the Demo application "wolkenkit-boards" from Wolkenkit, together with Auth0 as reference OIDC IdP, by following the Blog post [Learn to build real-time web applications using wolkenkit and how to add authentication to them](https://auth0.com/blog/building-real-time-web-applications-using-wolkenkit/#Preparing-authentication)._x000D_
2. Verify that the Single Page App (SPA) client of can AuthN/Z against Auth0._x000D_
3. Replace Auth0 by Vault OIDC Provider as Authentication Server, for ex. using simple "userpass" Auth Method. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should accept Authorization flow without `state`, as compliant applications are not required to provide `state`, though strongly recommended (unless using Code Flow with PKCE)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): Vault v1.9.3 (7dbdd57243a0d8d9d9e07cd01eb657369f8e1b8a)_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.9.3 (7dbdd57243a0d8d9d9e07cd01eb657369f8e1b8a)_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: OpenBSD-7.0 amd64 _x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
An experimental build of the Vault port on OpenBSD with this patch does not complain about missing `state` anymore_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ diff -u /usr/ports/pobj/vault-1.9.3/go/src/github.com/hashicorp/vault/vault/identity_store_oidc_provider.go_orig /usr/ports/pobj/vault-1.9.3/go/src/github.com/hashicorp/vault/vault/identity_store_oidc_provider.go_x000D_
--- identity_store_oidc_provider.go_orig        Thu Feb  3 14:51:35 2022_x000D_
+++ identity_store_oidc_provider.go     Tue Feb 22 13:16:23 2022_x000D_
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@_x000D_
+_x000D_
 package vault_x000D_
 _x000D_
 import (_x000D_
@@ -1446,7 +1447,8 @@_x000D_
 _x000D_
 func (i *IdentityStore) pathOIDCAuthorize(ctx context.Context, req *logical.Request, d *framework.FieldData) (*logical.Response, error) {_x000D_
        // Validate the state_x000D_
-       state := d.Get("state").(string)_x000D_
+       state := "rsFakeState"_x000D_
        if state == "" {_x000D_
                return authResponse("", "", ErrAuthInvalidRequest, "state parameter is required")_x000D_
        }_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
As expected, my flow now runs into the next problem, which is to be resolved on the client side of Wolkenkit whose SPA currently requests an Implicit Flow with `response_type="id_token token"`, instead of a Code Flow with `response_type="code id_token token"` which Vault supports currently in Tech Preview._x000D_
_x000D_
Note however that Spec in Section 5. says: _x000D_
_**For all these Response Types, the request MAY include a `state` parameter**, and if so, the Authorization Server MUST echo its value as a response parameter when issuing either a successful response or an error response._

title: strange net.LookupSRV behaviour
body_text:
I believe the net.LookupSRV behaviour is strange and does not really comply with rfc2782._x000D_
_x000D_
It assumes service http, and the code parses VAULT_ADDR as url._x000D_
_x000D_
Both is questionable because SRV records would make sense in prod setups (only) which usually should not run over http, but https protocol._x000D_
_x000D_
I think if VAULT_SRV_LOOKUP is true, the behaviour should be to call net.LookupSRV with empty service and proto with the VAULT_ADDR (not url.Parsed()), for example _x000D_
_x000D_
		_, addrs, err := net.LookupSRV("", "", "_vault._tcp.example.com")_x000D_
_x000D_
according to rfc2782. _x000D_
_x000D_
I somehow got it working with that pull req: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/14192_x000D_
_x000D_
Due to the url.Parse behaviour i set the addr.Path to "" and assume addr.Scheme as "https". _x000D_
_x000D_
I would like to have a discussion about what would be considered to be a correct behaviour._x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks!_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Kubernetes 1.21 - Serviceregistration is not reloading the service account token
body_text:
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
With https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/14144 the auth method for kubernetes was updated to be able to use the short-lived serviceaccount token. However, the service registration is still expecting a long-lived token as it is only loaded during initialization - https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/04195248444cad1dfb862f2946dc3250da3ccd5b/serviceregistration/kubernetes/client/client.go#L46 with https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/04195248444cad1dfb862f2946dc3250da3ccd5b/serviceregistration/kubernetes/client/config.go#L54  _x000D_
This will result in service registration no longer working in a future version of k8s or if k8s is configured with `--service-account-extend-token-expiration=false`._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Kubernetes with audit log to see if something is using a stale token, for minikube e.g. https://minikube.sigs.k8s.io/docs/tutorials/audit-policy/ . For example, I've used the following to start the cluster._x000D_
```_x000D_
mkdir -p ~/.minikube/files/etc/ssl/certs_x000D_
_x000D_
cat <<EOF > ~/.minikube/files/etc/ssl/certs/audit-policy.yaml_x000D_
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1_x000D_
kind: Policy_x000D_
rules:_x000D_
- level: Metadata_x000D_
EOF_x000D_
_x000D_

weitzj: @calvn Do you know the minimum capabilities one needs to revoke a lease using a glob path sys/leases/revoke-prefix/* read,update did not work Neither sudo
maxb: You need both update and sudo on the path. Additionally, because of an obscure detail of how Vault processes trailing slashes, if your policy is: ``` path "sys/leases/revoke-prefix/*" { capabilities = ["update", "sudo"] } ``` Then it will not match a write to `sys/leases/revoke-prefix/` itself - only `sys/leases/revoke-prefix/something`. title: UI - Patch Secret
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Some users don't have to have a read permission on secrets, but still are able patch a secret._x000D_
Such user is forced to use Vault CLI or API, because patch is not implemented in UI._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
UI supports "patch secret" in an user-friendly way._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Vault CLI or API._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
A developer should be able to rotate a secret, but not be able to use the secret for local development//testing._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: RemcoBuddelmeijer: I would argue that this is already implemented in the UI without a separate "patch" or "update" button. Whenever you patch a secret it will not remove unspecified old key-value pairs from your secret. It will only either update existing ones or add a new key-value pair. Whenever you update a secret it will completely overwrite the secret's content, this includes deleting old entries if not specified. Both of the operations create a new version. Now looking at the UI. If you press "create new version" it will pre-fill the already existing key-value pairs. You are now allowed to change these pairs or delete them. This is both derived from the patch and update functionality. I hope this helps! | heatherezell: Thank you, @RemcoBuddelmeijer! body_text:
A long, long time ago we ran vault with the Consul KV backend. Somewhere along the lines, Consul crapped itself. Doing a secrets disable on it either results in a 500 error, or a timeout._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I'd like to be able to forcibly disable a secret engine, no questions asked, no errors returned, just nuked completely. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
I've not encountered any other issues that would require the "nuclear" option, but... _x000D_

You are likely seeing the error during this process. Since you mentioned a timeout, the best course of action is likely to increase that timeout such that there is enough time for the secrets to be revoked. **Describe the bug**_x000D_
In [#11517](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/11517), the ability to notify systemd with the status of the vault server was added but the default Vault systemd unit file provided in the official packages does not set `Type=notify` so this feature doesn't ever get used when installing through package managers. _x000D_
_x000D_
I only happened to realize this was even a feature due to having debug logs enabled on a dev environment where I saw the log message saying `would have sent systemd notification (systemd not present)` and got a bit worried since this machine definitely is a systemd box. Took a bit of digging to find the commit adding this and the comment about the systemd service having to have the `Type=notify` in it._x000D_
_x000D_
I don't see any reason that the unit file for Vault shouldn't be updated with `Type=notify` set and am happy to open a PR if there aren't any objections to it._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Install vault from the official Apt repos_x000D_
2. Start vault with debug logging enabled_x000D_
3. Notice the message `would have sent systemd notification (systemd not present)`  shortly after starting up._x000D_
4. Run `systemctl edit vault` and paste the code below in the editor and save._x000D_
```_x000D_
[Service]_x000D_
Type=notify_x000D_
```_x000D_
5. Run `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart vault` and you will now see the message `sent systemd notification: notification=READY=1`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault's systemd unit file should properly configure it's type as `notify` when installed from a package._x000D_
_x000D_

title: raft disk space check and leader step-down
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
A few days ago our vault cluster went down hard, it's using the Raft backend, and the leader/active node had a completely full disk (that we didn't have an alert on, unfortunately). It basically caused Vault to stop working, yet the only error response we got was a 500 internal server error, with no explanation what exactly was erroring. This caused some delays in figuring out that it was actually a full disk, and not some other issue._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
It would be nice if a leader node can keep tabs on how much disk is available, and if the disk free hits a high water mark, to step down and not attempt to be re-elected until disk usage falls below a low water mark. Of course, with log entries to syslog to indicate that the high water mark has been reached. This of course being raft exclusive. _x000D_
_x000D_
The only drawback would be a situation where all nodes have hit high water mark and nobody gets elected; the end result would be the same, however, and it'd be a bit more obvious (I think, I may be wrong) to engineers that something is really wrong. _x000D_

title: Customizing num_uses and ttl per approle secret id
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When I generate a new secret ID for an approle, I would like to customize the TTL and/or num_uses for that secret ID, similarly to how I can customize the [cidr_list](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/auth/approle#cidr_list) and [token_bound_cidrs](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/auth/approle#token_bound_cidrs-1). _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Additional API parameters for the [approle secret ID creation](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/auth/approle#generate-new-secret-id) allowing custom values to be set for `num_uses` and `ttl`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Since `num_uses` and `ttl` are currently tied to the role configuration, any use case for an approle that requires a different value for either parameter than the default means I have to create an entirely new approle with identical policies but different configuration. This is possible, but tedious._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
In particular, this can be useful for the recommended [approle use pattern that involves wrapping](https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/pattern-approle?in=vault/recommended-patterns). For example, it would be very convenient to specify the `num_uses` for a new secret ID being passed to automation, even if the approle configuration did not have `num_uses` set._x000D_
_x000D_

top_3_comments_text: maxb: (Note: I'm not affiliated with HashiCorp; this issue just caught my eye whilst browsing the issue tracker) Vault doesn't have anything that would natively support this workflow. If you wanted to implement it in your reverse proxy that fronts Vault, it would need to log in to Vault on the user's behalf, using the Vault API, and add an X-Vault-Token header to the user's requests that it proxies. However, rather than trying to make this work, it would probably be better for you long term, to set up an OpenID Connect (OIDC) Identity Provider that users can log into using their LDAP password, and configure the Vault OIDC auth method. OIDC seems to be one of the major standards for web application SSO these days, so you'd likely be able to re-use the investment for other web applications you add to your SSO organisation, too. | yashra: Thank you @maxb, I agree but as our SSO is central and can't be integrated with ODIC so we thought to use http sso headers that can help to login with LDAP. Any way to implement that? | maxb: My previous idea: > If you wanted to implement it in your reverse proxy that fronts Vault, it would need to log in to Vault on the user's behalf, using the Vault API, and add an X-Vault-Token header to the user's requests that it proxies. is in fact not possible. I had neglected to consider that the Vault UI is a client side JavaScript application, and it gets confused and does not provide the desired behaviour if a token is inserted by a reverse proxy. Regarding your follow-up: > Thank you @maxb, I agree but as our SSO is central and can't be integrated with ODIC so we thought to use http sso headers that can help to login with LDAP. Any way to implement that? As the Vault UI is a client side JavaScript application, you can only use one of the authentication methods the application supports. (Unless you choose to maintain a fork of the Vault UI or write your own.) Of these methods, the only one that supports SSO is OIDC. title: Move certificate extensions to entity alias metadata
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
@peterverraedt submitted a PR #13348 to add TLS certificates ASN1 extensions as identity metadata in Vault when using the cert auth method. _x000D_
This would enable using certificates metadata in ACL templating to set a proper policy scope for each machine when accessing secrets._x000D_
However, it looks like extensions are not registered at all in Vault. It is expected that these should be set in the metadata property of an entity. _x000D_
_x000D_
When looking at an entity used by a client using cert method:_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
vault read identity/entity/id/<id> | grep metadata_x000D_
_x000D_
Key                    Value_x000D_
---                    -----_x000D_
metadata               <nil>_x000D_
```_x000D_
  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I propose to save certificate metadata in the alias instead of using the parent entity._x000D_
In addition to solving this issue, I think using the alias is a more coherent approach, as it is closely linked with the certificate unlike the parent entity which is more global to the user_x000D_
Related PR: #14419

title: Empty entity metadata for multiple auth methods
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
It looks like Vault doesn't register the _identity.entity.metadata_ property when logging in. This was detected in my case when using LDAP or cert authentication. Yet to be confirmed on other auth methods _x000D_
_x000D_
**Update on 29/06**_x000D_
> This appears to be by design because multiple auth methods can map to the same identity. To avoid reconciling conflicts as the aliases merge, the metadata is set to nil:_x000D_
> _x000D_
> https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/d537c2ebb4c0195a4332abf8973cef31a496b1ad/helper/identity/types.pb.go#L278-L285_x000D_
> _x000D_
> The metadata is available on the token in the `meta` field._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
For example, when using ldap authentication:_x000D_
_x000D_
We expect to register the following entity, according to _builtin/credential/ldap/path_login.go_ :_x000D_
```go_x000D_
	auth := &logical.Auth{_x000D_
		Metadata: map[string]string{_x000D_
			"username": username,_x000D_
		},_x000D_
		InternalData: map[string]interface{}{_x000D_
			"password": password,_x000D_
		},_x000D_
		DisplayName: username,_x000D_
		Alias: &logical.Alias{_x000D_
			Name: effectiveUsername,_x000D_
			Metadata: map[string]string{_x000D_
				"name": username,_x000D_
			},_x000D_
		},_x000D_
	}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Log in using LDAP auth and find the current identity id._x000D_
We should expect _identity.entity.metadata.username_ to be set. However, what I find is an empty metadata:_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
vault read identity/entity/id/3ce5e46d-cadc-9aa4-99b2-1e1866f91900 _x000D_
Key                    Value_x000D_
---                    -----_x000D_
metadata               <nil>_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
But, it's set properly in the alias (same value used):_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
vault read identity/entity-alias/id/16eec1e8-c975-ed5f-c9b0-b93a90b79846_x000D_
Key                    Value_x000D_
---                    -----_x000D_
metadata              map[name:maxime.genet]_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: v1.10.0-rc1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version: v1.9.4_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Kubernetes statefulset, based on Docker image vault:1.10.0-rc1_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file:_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
{_x000D_
        "api_addr" = "http://vault:8200"_x000D_
        "cluster_addr" = "http://$${.Env.POD_NAME}:8201"_x000D_
        "listener" = [{_x000D_
            "tcp" = {_x000D_
            "address" = "0.0.0.0:8300", # Ingress endpoint_x000D_
            "tls_cert_file" = "/tls/tls.crt",_x000D_
            "tls_key_file" = "/tls/tls.key"_x000D_
            }_x000D_
        },{_x000D_
          "tcp" = {_x000D_
            "address" = "0.0.0.0:8200", # Local endpoint_x000D_
            "tls_cert_file" = "/vault/tls/server.crt",_x000D_
            "tls_key_file" = "/vault/tls/server.key"_x000D_
          }_x000D_
_x000D_
            }]_x000D_
        "storage" = {_x000D_
          "raft" = {_x000D_
            "path" = "/vault/raft"_x000D_
          }_x000D_
        }_x000D_
        "telemetry" = {_x000D_
          "statsd_address" = "localhost:9125"_x000D_
        }_x000D_
        "ui" = true_x000D_
      }_x000D_
```_x000D_

title: Huge number of leases when using k8s auth method
body_text: We have vault deployed on k8s cluster and integrated with several other k8s clusters using CSI driver to provide secrets to workloads there - it all works ok but...:_x000D_ list of leases for every cluster is several thousand pages long... e.g._x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_ which corresponds to the huge size of vault.db:_x000D_ _x000D_ ```_x000D_ /vault/data $ ls -lh_x000D_ total 8G_x000D_ drwxrws--- 2 root vault 16.0K Nov 15 19:42 lost+found_x000D_ -rw-rw---- 1 vault vault 36 Nov 15 19:42 node-id_x000D_ drwxrwsr-x 3 vault vault 4.0K Nov 15 19:42 raft_x000D_ -rw------- 1 vault vault 8.0G Mar 16 16:33 vault.db_x000D_ ```_x000D_ and pods memory consumption:_x000D_ _x000D_ ```_x000D_ (⎈ |gke-devops-prod:vault) ~  k top pods_x000D_ NAME CPU(cores) MEMORY(bytes)_x000D_ in-cluster-vault-0 13m 79Mi_x000D_ in-cluster-vault-1 28m 369Mi_x000D_ in-cluster-vault-2 63m 9557Mi_x000D_ ```_x000D_ Is it expected? top_3_comments_text: swayne275: thanks for bringing this up. what sort of "disk" are you using? HDD? SSD? | harsimranmaan: > thanks for bringing this up. what sort of "disk" are you using? HDD? SSD? SSD | raskchanky: @harsimranmaan First, I'm so sorry you've run into some performance issues after upgrading to Vault 1.8. The good news is there are things we can do to improve this situation, but there are tradeoffs involved. First, a little background. BoltDB has a concept of a "freelist". When data is deleted, it's not actually removed from the database. Instead, the page(s) where that data resided are marked as free and added to the freelist. When Bolt goes to write new values in the future, it first consults the freelist, and if enough contiguous pages exist to fit the new value, then it reuses those pages instead of allocating new ones. Over time, especially with a lot of deletions, the freelist can grow large. Bolt has a configuration option that lets you toggle writing the freelist to disk. When it's enabled, the freelist is written to disk on every write. When it's disabled, the freelist only exists in memory, but it must be reconstructed from scratch, using the data on disk, whenever Bolt opens the database. If you have a large Vault database, or a database that's experienced high churn (so the freelist is large), rewriting that frequently can lead to poor write performance. Starting in Vault 1.8, we changed the default Bolt configuration to not persist the freelist to disk. The tradeoff here is that the freelist needs to be reconstructed when Vault restarts, and this explains the delay you're seeing. The upside is that since the freelist is no longer written to disk, even heavily fragmented databases won't suffer from degraded write performance. Last fall, while working on the 1.9 release cycle, we worked through a customer issue similar to yours, with increased start up time. We found that for customers wanting faster start up time but also wanting to avoid write performance degradation over time, there was a Bolt option called MAP_POPULATE that could be enabled. This was first released in Vault 1.9.3. This provides a sort of middle ground, where start up time is faster, but the freelist is still not written to disk. So all of this is to say there's 2 options for speeding up your startup time: 1. Since you're already on Vault 1.8.x, you can set the `VAULT_RAFT_FREELIST_SYNC` environment variable. Setting this to any non-empty value will cause Vault to revert to the behavior it had in 1.7, where the freelist is synced to disk. This will get you the fastest possible startup time, potentially at the expense of degraded write performance as your db grows larger and more fragmented. 1. Upgrading to 1.9.3 or newer and setting the `VAULT_RAFT_ENABLE_MAP_POPULATE` environment variable will turn on the MAP_POPULATE option, provided the size of your database is smaller than the available RAM on your Vault node. This will make your startup time faster than it is now (though not as fast as syncing the freelist) and will also avoid write performance degradation as your db grows larger.

title: LIfetime Watcher Ignores "increment" when computing grace period.
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
A clear and concise description of what the bug is._x000D_
_x000D_
In lifetime_watcher the grace period is calculated with the secret's lease duration, not the given "increment" value. _x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/da0155ba197e3dc9f50695f49c52288a18ba8f1e/api/lifetime_watcher.go#L260_x000D_
_x000D_
This means that for long lived leases, a client cannot submit it's own increment value that is less than the leases grace period without triggering and immediate return (without sleeping). _x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/da0155ba197e3dc9f50695f49c52288a18ba8f1e/api/lifetime_watcher.go#L364_x000D_
_x000D_
In my case, the initial lease duration is 12 hours, but I’m trying to check the secrete every 10 minutes (in case of a revocation). The grace period for 12 hours ends up being something near 2 hours which is greater than my increment value, forcing the return before the time.After call._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Grace period should be calculated using the minimum value of the lease duration and the client increment value. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Add any other context about the problem here._x000D_
_x000D_
Discussion forum: https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/vault-sdk-lifetime-watcher-client-increment-and-secret-lease-duration/36850_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Vault ecosystem implicitly handles "/data" for KV-V2 except for `vault kv put`.
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
A lot of tools, like consul-template, vault agent, etc. implicitly handle kv-v2's `/data` path. For example, from consul-template's `secret` documentation:_x000D_
_x000D_
> When using Vault versions 0.10.0/0.10.1, the secret path will have to be prefixed with "data", i.e. secret/data/passwords for the example above. This is not necessary for Vault versions after 0.10.1, as consul-template will detect the KV backend version being used._x000D_
_x000D_
However, `vault kv put` does *not* implicitly handle this `data` prefix, creating a very confusing and asymmetric behavior around paths._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Write a secret with an explicit `data` path: `vault kv put my-kv-v2-store/data/secret secret=foobar`_x000D_
2. Use `vault read` or the Vault agent's `secret` function: `vault read my-kv-v2-store/data/secret secret=foobar` -- this fails with:_x000D_
_x000D_
> No value found at my-kv-v2-store/data/secret_x000D_
3. Use `vault read` or the Vault agent's `secret` function with an *extra* /data prefix: `vault read my-kv-v2-store/data/data/secret secret=foobar` -- this works._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
After running:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault kv put my-kv-v2-store/data/secret secret=foobar_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I expect `vault read` to succeed on the same URL:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault read my-kv-v2-store/data/secret_x000D_
Key         Value_x000D_
---         -----_x000D_
data        map[api_secret:foobar]_x000D_
metadata    map[created_time:2022-03-23T16:04:18.234865248Z custom_metadata:<nil> deletion_time: destroyed:false version:2]_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.9.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.9.3_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: NixOS 21.11 / x86_64-linux_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
n/a_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
I'm not advocating for any specific behavior, other than a mix of implicit and explicit behavior creates confusing and surprising outcomes.
top_3_comments_text: digivava: Thanks for your input! I'm part of the new Vault Developer Experience team and we agree that the mix of implicit and explicit behavior with regard to the secret path can add a lot of confusion. For KV v2, it's best to think of the true path to your secret as "my-kv-v2-store/data/secret". However, in order to make the kv command backwards-compatible with v1, the kv command uses a shortened version of the path (my-kv-v2-store/secret). It's best to not think of this as the path at all, just a "friendly name" used by the KV commands only. `vault read`, `vault write`, and policy files use the full API path my-kv-v2-store/data/secret. So if you want to use the `kv` commands, you'll probably want to use `vault kv put my-kv-v2-store/secret` and then `vault kv get my-kv-v2-store/secret` again to retrieve the secret for consistency, rather than mixing `vault kv put` with `vault read`. This confusing discrepancy in behavior is definitely an important consideration of my team these days and we've recently been brainstorming various ways to mitigate this, so thanks for adding another data point that this is indeed confusing for our users! I will close this issue for now but know that it's definitely on our mind. One small mitigation we've just added in 1.10 is that the CLI will now output the "full secret path" after some of the commonly used `vault kv` commands, to make it a little more clear what path you're reading/writing to. Not a true fix for the issue obviously, but hopefully something that helps a little bit. (i.e. If you accidentally do `vault kv put secret/data/foo`, you will see in the output that you actually wrote to `secret/data/data/foo`.)
