title: Identity Backend Audit HMAC Request/Response Cannot Be Configured
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
It does not appear possible to allowlist fields to be printed in cleartext in the audit logs for requests/responses from the Identity backend._x000D_
_x000D_
Based on the Identity backend docs and poking around at a local Vault dev server, it appears that the `tune` option used to allow fields to be printed in plaintext rather than HMAC'd values in audit logs in secret/auth backends is not available for the Identity backend._x000D_
_x000D_
It would be useful to our operations and use of the Identity backend if we were able to allow specific fields (ex. `policies` or `member_entity_ids`) from the request or response of Identity backend request to be printed in plaintext in our audit logs _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
Run `vault server -dev` and configure VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_TOKEN to work with that:_x000D_
```_x000D_
> vault secrets tune -audit-non-hmac-request-keys=member_entity_ids -audit-non-hmac-request-keys=member_entity_ids identity_x000D_
Error tuning secrets engine identity/: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: POST http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/mounts/identity/tune_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* cannot tune "identity/"_x000D_
_x000D_
> vault write sys/mounts/identity/tune audit-non-hmac-request-keys=member_entity_ids_x000D_
Error writing data to sys/mounts/identity/tune: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/mounts/identity/tune_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* cannot tune "identity/"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
On the server logs, running the above client commands will result in:_x000D_
```_x000D_
2022-03-24T11:25:17.201-0400 [ERROR] secrets.system.system_fafb1c8d: cannot tune this mount: path=identity/_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
The Identity mount can be tuned to allow specific fields to be printed in audit logs in plaintext_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): v1.9.3_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.9.3_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: OS X, Linux_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s): n/a, reproduces on a `vault server -dev` instance_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
None

title: Use context in Kubernetes authentication
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Today the Login method via Kubernetes receives a context but does not use it: [api/auth/kubernetes/kubernetes.go#L70](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/kubernetes/kubernetes.go#L70)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Using the latest version of the api, we can solve this problem like this:_x000D_
_x000D_
[api/auth/kubernetes/kubernetes.go#L77](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/kubernetes/kubernetes.go#L77)_x000D_
```diff_x000D_
-       resp, err := client.Logical().Write(path, loginData)_x000D_
+       resp, err := client.Logical().WriteWithContext(ctx, path, loginData)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

title: Add a way to rename totp keys via API
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Currently, whenever I need to rename a TOTP Key, I have to reboot vault with sys/raw enabled, manually commit API shenanigans and remember every time how to even find the TOTP key, manually add the key again via [VaultUI](https://gitlab.com/ChaotiCryptidz/VaultUI) and then turn off sys/raw again._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
An API endpoint for the renaming of TOTP keys.
top_3_comments_text: csawyerYumaed: For people like me that just want to do this now, this is what I did (notes for future me) ``` $ # run a local consul and restore from backup: $ consul agent -dev $ consul kv import @consul.kv.export # configure vault, no security for fun! $ cat vault.hcl backend "consul" { address = "127.0.0.1:8500" path = "vault" } listener "tcp" { address = "127.0.0.1:8200" tls_disable = 1 } raw_storage_endpoint=true $ # run vault with no security. $ vault server -config vault.hcl $ vault operator unseal $ grep <name of totp key> consul.kv.export $ # remove the vault/ part from the key, so copy from logical/ onwards. $ curl -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/raw/<PATH FROM grep above> ``` With any luck, this will get you the raw data, and then you can add a new key with the name via the [api](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/totp#create-key) and then delete the old one to your production instance. ``` $ cat payload.json { "name":"DATA FROM ABOVE", "key":"MAGIC SECRET FROM ABOVE", "algorithm":"SHA1", "issuer":"DATA FROM ABOVE", "period":"30" } $ curl --header "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" --request POST --data @payload.json https://vault.service.consul:8200/v1/totp/keys/<NEWNAMEHERE> ```

stevendpclark: Hi @pbriet, So the mount points under the raw variable are core to Vault and/or are marked for replication (no matter if you are setup for replication or not). The default is for the paths to be within raw (replicated) and should always contain at least the /sys and /identity mount points. These two are critical to Vault and the only time they shouldn't exist, to my knowledge, is before the `vault operator init` has been performed. rawLocal will contain mount paths that have been enabled/setup with the local argument set when creating the mount path , see https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/commands/secrets/enable#local As an example on an initial setup of Vault post `vault operator init`, the Vault instance will have /sys and /identity within the raw and /cubbyhole mount within rawLocal. title: AWS Auth Login Metadata
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Yes, the proposed feature request is related to a problem with the audit trail when using AWS Auth Engine._x000D_
_x000D_
The scenario is that the AWS Auth engine is enabled and configured and the use of an AWS Auth Role is binded to an IAM Role as the principal entity. With the IAM Role bounded to a Vault Role, an IAM User is then capable of assuming this role to log into the Vault server. This authorization flow works well and allows for Vault access to be  controlled through IAM access to assume the role. Multiple IAM Users are capable of assuming this role. _x000D_
_x000D_
The issue specifically is the lack of observability on the audit trail. With the Vault server audit logs enabled, the following metadata format is supplied._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
"metadata": {_x000D_
	"client_user_id": <unique_id>,_x000D_
	"role_id": <role_id>,_x000D_
	"auth_type": "iam",_x000D_
	"canonical_arn": "arn:aws:iam::<aws_account>:role/<iam-role-name>,_x000D_
	"account_id": <aws_account>,_x000D_
	"client_arn": "arn:aws:sts::<aws_account>:assumed-role/<iam-role-name>/vaultSession"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The extra metadata fields are configured via the [iam_metadata endpoint](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/auth/aws#iam_metadata)._x000D_
_x000D_
None of these fields are unique to the IAM User who is assuming the role. This lack of observability as a result does not allow for specific actions to be traced back to a user during an audit. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
The request here is to develop a way in which a clear owner can be pinned to specific Vault actions with the use of IAM Roles. An AWS metadata field such as the `AWS::IAM::AccessKey` can be used to determine a unique individual based on cloudtrail lookups._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
The alternative at the moment is to bind the IAM User arn explicitly to the Vault Role. This direct binding will explicitly use the ARN of the IAM User. The drawback to this method is the need to consistently update the Vault AWS Auth Role for changes to who should and shouldn't have access. Being able to control this from outside of Vault would be helpful from an operational toil perspective._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
The additional/extended use case here is the combined use of the Vault DB Engine configuration. The DB Engine is configured such that it is creating temporary and unique roles for users of this Vault Role binded to the IAM Role. This feature of credentials creation is useful as it allows a user to access the Database in a scoped manner with short lived credentials. _x000D_
_x000D_
It should additionally be useful such that the [DB Engine username template](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/databases/postgresql#parameters) can be updated to use unique Vault Role names or IDs that can be easily traced back to a User. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
[Here is where the metadata for the AWS Auth Login is being configured](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/aws/path_login.go#L1411-L1422). This is where additional logic may be made to update the fields such that a unique field value can be used. _x000D_
_x000D_
I would like to argue that use of IAM Roles that are assumed could be dangerous to users who may not be able to audit specific actions. This might be worth calling out in the mean time within the documentation for visibility. _x000D_
top_3_comments_text: jlestrada: I just discovered that there is an ability of enforcement from AWS when executing the IAM action `AssumeRole` such that the `RoleSessionName` can be enforced to a username. The following AWS article describes this process [here](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/easily-control-naming-individual-iam-role-sessions/). If we assume this enforcement as a requirement then I believe there is a path forward for the scenario I described above. With the parameter `iam_alias` set to `unique_id` we would be capable of seeing the full ARN of the role, which contains the `RoleSessionName` within the metadata block. This parameter is described [here](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/auth/aws#configure-identity-integration). This would then allow for an easy way to traceback which IAM User executed specific Vault actions. This I think technically removes the block. Despite the audit traceback process being unblocked there is still a request of a feature specifically with regards to use of the Database engine. The engine relies on a username templating process for generating dynamic and unique username credentials. The engine relies only on two field names `DisplayName` and `RoleName`, please reference documentation [here](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/databases/postgresql#parameters). The field `RoleName` to the best of my knowledge is specific to the Vault Role and NOT the IAM assumed role. The `DisplayName` however does refer to the respective Auth engines configuration of the `DisplayName` field. This is where the request now comes. It is being requested that the AWS Auth engine can be configured or modified in such a way that the `DisplayName` is capable of being set to include the IAM `RoleSessionName`. At the moment it showcases the name of the IAM Role but not the set `RoleSessionName`. This is referenced as the `entity.FriendlyName` attribute [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/3b34ab872a07dfc39bdbec253fd9da989759e913/builtin/credential/aws/path_login.go#L1405). It is of my opinion that the attribute `FriendlyName` should include the `RoleSessionName` when IAM assume role process is used. The `FriendlyName` field is parsed in such a way that it extracts the `RoleSessionName` within the application logic [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/3b34ab872a07dfc39bdbec253fd9da989759e913/builtin/credential/aws/path_login.go#L1518-L1522). If this field were updated to include the `RoleSessionName` then we would be capable of generating dynamic and unique credentials that match an IAM user. This however does change the behavior of what the field showcases. I may be oblivious to how this field can be used by multiple users but I think it would be minimal impact. As an alternative and in my opinion a harder path to implement, an update can be made to the Postgres Engine such that a new field name can be used during username templating. I consider this to be a more challenging path because users of the engine may rely on different Auth types that do not contain the same fields. This is why I assume only `DisplayName` and `RoleName` are supported. I will go ahead and submit a PR to remove the extraction of the `RoleSessionName` from the attribute `FriendlyName`. I don't know how it will go but willing to give it a shot. cc @stevendpclark | calvn: Thanks for the thorough investigation and explanation on this! I'm still trying to understand this a bit more, but will be taking a closer look at the PR shortly. | jlestrada: > Thanks for the thorough investigation and explanation on this! I'm still trying to understand this a bit more, but will be taking a closer look at the PR shortly. Yeah totally feel free to ask questions or let me know if the behavior is not intended. From how i understand it and view it I don't see why adding the RoleSessionName is harmful but i could very well be missing something. title: LDAP aliases will be created with the login name not the corresponding LDAP user attribute
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
If LDAP authentication is activated then user accounts will be created in Vault on the first login. In that case, Vault creates an entity and an alias. The alias name is the same as the login name, entered by the user on the first login. This is unexpected because the alias name should match the LDAP user attribute._x000D_
_x000D_
In our case, we use the samAccountName as user attribute. The samAccountName might be, for example, "jdoe", but the user logins in with "JDoe" then the alias name will be created as "JDoe", but that doesn't match the samAccountName attribute._x000D_
In our case every user will get its own secret engine, in this example `users/JDoe` and the following policy will be added to each account:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
path "users/{{ identity.entity.aliases.auth_ldap_ff66461a.name }}/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["create", "update", "read", "list", "delete"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
So the secret engine's path must match the alias name (that's done by a tool that reads the alias name and create the secret engine if not present). But an external tool that tries to write a secret into the secret engine has difficulties getting the correct path because it's constructed from the accounts alias name, but that must not match the login name (`jdoe` vs `jDoe`) nor must it match the user attribute (samaccountname)._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
* Enable LDAP auth_x000D_
* Configure LDAP:_x000D_
```_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "binddn": "CN=...",_x000D_
  "bindpass": "secret",_x000D_
  "deny_null_bind": true,_x000D_
  "discoverdn": false,_x000D_
  "groupattr": "cn",_x000D_
  "groupdn": "OU=Groups,...",_x000D_
  "groupfilter": "(\u0026(objectClass=group)(member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:={{.UserDN}}))",_x000D_
  "insecure_tls": false,_x000D_
  "starttls": false,_x000D_
  "url": "ldaps://10.10.10.10:636",_x000D_
  "userattr": "sAMAccountName",_x000D_
  "userdn": "OU=Users,..."_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
* Chose a LDAP user to test the login. In this example the user is called John Doe with a samaccountname of "jdoe"._x000D_
* Login as "jdoe". An entity with the alias "jdoe" will be created_x000D_
* Remove the newly created entity_x000D_
* Login as "JDoe". An entity with the alias "JDoe" will be created_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
In every case, regardless of the user's login name "jdoe" or "JDoe", an alias name will be created that matches the LDAP user attribute._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.7.3_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.7.3_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Debian 10 (buster), x86_64_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
storage "file" {_x000D_
  path = "/data"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address = "0.0.0.0:8200"_x000D_
  cluster_address = "0.0.0.0:8201"_x000D_
  tls_cert_file = "/etc/vault.d/vault_cert.pem"_x000D_
  tls_key_file  = "/etc/vault.d/vault_privkey.pem"_x000D_
  telemetry {_x000D_
    unauthenticated_metrics_access = true_x000D_
  }_x000D_
  proxy_protocol_behavior = "allow_authorized"_x000D_
  proxy_protocol_authorized_addrs = "172.17.0.2"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
api_addr = "https://linux-debian-10"_x000D_
cluster_addr = "https://172.17.0.2:8201"_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
log_level = "info"_x000D_
_x000D_
default_lease_ttl = "25h"_x000D_
max_lease_ttl = "768h"_x000D_
_x000D_
default_max_request_duration = "90s"_x000D_
```_x000D_

title: consistent CLI interface, ie `-config=`
body_text:
#### Feature Description_x000D_
_x000D_
Consul and vault agents' install process (manual or rpm) is nearly identical. So close that I ended up writing a single chef resource that can do both. The differences between installing on linux vs windows are much bigger than that of consul vs vault._x000D_
_x000D_
In the process, I realized that consul expects `-config-file=/path/to/some/file` and vault wants `-config=/path/to/some/file`. These flags mean the same thing, but have different names. To be fair, this is easy to work around in chef._x000D_
_x000D_
It's not a huge deal, but generally speaking it would be a nice-to-have if they were able to present the same interface when the options overlap like this._x000D_
_x000D_
It might be that consul aliases `-config=` or vault aliases `-config-file=` for a few versions until one form or the other can be reasonably deprecated._x000D_
_x000D_
#### Use Case(s)_x000D_
_x000D_

title: sys: don't set `X-Vault-Namespace` header for root-only paths
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault exposes root-only API paths. For example: `[sys/health](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/enterprise/namespaces#sys-health)._x000D_
Ref: https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/enterprise/namespaces#root-only-api-paths_x000D_
_x000D_
However, a `vault.Client` with a namespace set via [`SetNamespace`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/vault/api#Client.SetNamespace) sends the `X-Vault-Namespace` header to those root-only API paths._x000D_
For example:_x000D_
```_x000D_
User-Agent: [Go-http-client/1.1]_x000D_
X-Vault-Namespace: [test]_x000D_
X-Vault-Request: [true]_x000D_
X-Vault-Token: [abc]_x000D_
Accept-Encoding: [gzip]_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This causes Vault `1.9.1` to respond with:_x000D_
```_x000D_
Code: 404. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
    unsupported path_x000D_
```  _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
As a simple reproducer - the 1st curl request succeeds while the 2nd fails:_x000D_
```_x000D_
curl -L -X GET "https://localhost:8200/v1/sys/health?drsecondarycode=299&performancestandbycode=299&sealedcode=299&standbycode=299&uninitcode=299"_x000D_
_x000D_
curl -L -X GET -H 'X-Vault-Namespace: test' "https://localhost:8200/v1/sys/health?drsecondarycode=299&performancestandbycode=299&sealedcode=299&standbycode=299&uninitcode=299"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Either the`vault.Client` should not send the `X-Vault-Namespace` header for root-only API paths or Vault itself should ignore this header in such a case._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): `1.9.1` _x000D_
* Vault SDK Version (retrieve with `vault version`):  `1.5.0`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: linux/amd64
top_3_comments_text: VinnyHC: Hello and thanks for opening this issue; I've confirmed the behavior you've described. I'll work this through our processes and get a solution together. Feel free to follow this issue for updates! | ncabatoff: I'm not sure the expected behaviour is a good idea. We may change some root-only paths to be available in namespaces in the future. And if you're specifying X-Vault-Namespace, you probably authenticated into that namespace, and won't be likely to have access to the root-only paths anyway unless they're unauthenticated. If the client doesn't provide the namespace header for root-only API paths, IMO that's putting too much knowledge of possibly version-specific Vault behaviour into the client. If Vault ignores the specific namespace because it knows that the request doesn't make sense in a namespace but would make sense in the root namespace, that feels like surprising magical behaviour that could come back to bite us in the future, that would be backwards incompatible, and that doesn't seem justified relative to the minor pain associated with having to set the namespace header appropriately for these root-level requests. Also note that on HCP Vault there is no access to the root namespace, so this behaviour wouldn't make sense at all there. My suggestion is that you either use two clients for the two different namespaces, or that we find some way to make it easier to specify a namespace on a per-request basis, but still require that it be an explicit choice in the client code that the code author must be aware of. | aead: Just to elaborate on a possible use case: A client is using a secret engine (K/V, transient, ...) and at the same time checks Vault's health status periodically. There are many reasons why the API could return an empty Secret (e.g., internal error on PKI `/ca` endpoints) -- but exposing this under the vague (and perhaps incorrect) "no value found" isn't the best _if_ a more informative 404 error message was actually returned. _x000D_

> {"errors":["no handler for route 'bogus-22119-31391-2449-31513/certs'"]}_x000D_
> ```_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
Vault CLI could expose the underlying error message from the server (indicating that the path was wrong, rather than a valid path with incorrectly configured mount or some other rationale for empty secret response)._x000D_

title: SGX integration to protect data in use
body_text:
Problem:_x000D_
Vault cannot keep confidentiality when the data processing in the memory, especially for those sensitive keys or secrets._x000D_
_x000D_
Proposals:_x000D_
Intel SGX provides an isolated enclave with encrypted memory to keep the security of data in use._x000D_
Here are two proposals:_x000D_
1. Intel is developing an SGX enclave-based KMS solution called [eHSM](https://github.com/intel/ehsm). It provides similar functionalities to AWS KMS, AliCloud KMS like CreateKey, GenerateDataKey, Encrypt/Decrypt, Sign/Verify etc. Its backend is SGX encalve but not HSM. Can [eHSM](https://github.com/intel/ehsm) act as a Vault secret engine plugin to provide alternative SGX solution?_x000D_
2. Running Vault in SGX libOS like [Gramine](https://github.com/gramineproject/gramine). In this way, no changes are required to Vault. But in order to fully leverage SGX capability, some optimizations can be applied. E.g. Vault unseal key can be protected by SGX sealing key._x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks._x000D_
_x000D_

title: Plugin development docs are silent on concurrency / data race issues
body_text:

title: OIDC Provider: filter list of returned groups per client
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
With Vault, I can create groups which represent the application-specific permissions a user has (sometimes known as "roles")._x000D_
_x000D_
For example: I can create groups called `grafana:admin`, `grafana:editor`, `grafana:viewer` to represent the permissions/roles when logged into Grafana.  I can then use Vault's nested groups to make these members of other groups, e.g. group "Staff" is a member of the `grafana:editor` group - or I can assign these permissions directly to individuals._x000D_
_x000D_
This works well, and it helps very much to avoid hard-coding in each *application* the lists of specific authorized users and groups. That is, it centralizes the authorization policy._x000D_
_x000D_
The problem is that the list of groups presented to the application gets very large.  The application sees not only the role groups for itself, but also the role groups for all other applications (which it doesn't care about), and the organizational groups (which I don't want it to see)._x000D_
_x000D_
Eventually I expect to see failures as applications hit limits, such as the length of HTTP headers, when the groups claim is passed as a HTTP header (typical for apps behind an OIDC reverse proxy such as mod_auth_openidc or oauth2-proxy)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Currently, the way I expose groups to the application is via a template in an OIDC scope:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write identity/oidc/scope/groups \_x000D_
  description="Provides a list of group names" \_x000D_
  template='{_x000D_
    "groups": {{identity.entity.groups.names}}_x000D_
}'_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I need a way to filter this templated value to a subset of groups, where the filter is different for each OIDC client._x000D_
_x000D_
The OIDC client object already has an "assignment", which is a list of permitted entity_ids and group_ids. Therefore, I propose a new `identity.entity.assignment_groups` attribute, which filters the list of groups to include only those in the assignment.  This attribute would be available in OIDC scope templates only._x000D_
_x000D_
This is a simple and logical change, and has the advantage that the application will also see exactly those groups of which the user must be a member (at least one), in order to access it._x000D_
_x000D_
I would then create a new scope:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write identity/oidc/scope/roles \_x000D_
  description="Provides a list of client roles" \_x000D_
  template='{_x000D_
    "roles": {{identity.entity.assignment_groups.names}}_x000D_
}'_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
In the template, I can choose whether to return role names or role ids to the application._x000D_
_x000D_
OIDC clients where the assignment is `allow_all` (system default introduced in Vault 1.10) would continue to see all groups._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
#### Separate attribute_x000D_
_x000D_
In the OIDC client, there could be a separate attribute like `allowed_group_ids` which is used to filter the `identity.entity.groups` in the role template, rather than re-using the assignment for this purpose._x000D_
_x000D_
#### Filter by name_x000D_
_x000D_
I can name the groups in such a way to make them easily filterable (e.g. all Grafana-related group names have prefix `grafana:`)_x000D_
_x000D_
Then it would be possible to define a separate scope per application, and have a regex-based list filter function in the template.  e.g._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write identity/oidc/scope/roles_grafana \_x000D_
  template='{_x000D_
    "roles": {{identity.entity.groups.names | grep "^grafana:"}}_x000D_
}'_x000D_
vault write identity/oidc/scope/roles_netbox \_x000D_
  template='{_x000D_
    "roles": {{identity.entity.groups.names | grep "^netbox:"}}_x000D_
}'_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
It means having to define a separate `roles_FOO` claim for each application, and each application has to request the correct scope, but I think it would work and is simple to implement._x000D_
_x000D_
#### Roles_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault could add an explicit concept of "roles".  "Roles" would be like "Groups", but would be limited to a specific OIDC client. This could be done for example by marking a group as a role, and giving a list of allowed client IDs; or by having the roles nested under `identity/oidc/client/<clientid>/roles/`.  Roles could have users, groups and other roles as members. This is a more invasive change to Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

title: OIDC Auth method: option to prevent dynamic entity creation, and for user to add entity alias
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Scenario: you want to allow trusted partners to authenticate to Vault. One reason is so that you can grant access to applications which you host, and which authenticate against your Vault's OpenID Provider._x000D_
_x000D_
You don't want to manage the individual passwords for all these external users, so you connect Vault to one or more social auth providers using the JWT/OIDC Auth Method.  For this discussion, let's say you choose Google._x000D_
_x000D_
There are two problems._x000D_
_x000D_
1. The smaller issue is that anyone with a GMail account can connect to your server and dynamically create an entity and entity alias. The 'default' policy allows various stateful actions such as creating child tokens and cubbyhole secrets, which makes it an easy target for denial of service (e.g. filling the database with garbage).  This can be mitigated by setting `token_no_default_policy`, and explicitly granting the `default` policy only to entities which have been added to a group.  However, it would still be nice to avoid "drive-by" account creation, and the corresponding entity crud._x000D_
_x000D_
2. Practically, I'd like to pre-create an entity for the user, and then connect their Google identity to it.  But if I follow OpenID Connect [best practice](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#ClaimStability) and use the `sub` claim as the [user_claim](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/auth/jwt#user_claim), I won't know it in advance - indeed, most end users won't even know their own `sub` value (for Google, it's a 21-digit number that they never see). Therefore I cannot pre-create the entity alias._x000D_
_x000D_
So at the moment the approach is:_x000D_
* Wait for the user to make a "drive-by" authentication, which creates an entity and entity alias_x000D_
* Scan through all unknown entities and identify the newly-created entity somehow - e.g. from one of the other claims on the entity alias._x000D_
* Configure this entity with necessary authorizations - or merge it into a pre-existing entity for this user._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I'd like to see two things:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. A way to disable, at the level of an individual auth method, the dynamic creation of entities and entity aliases.  If a user authenticates with an entity alias which doesn't exist, then the login is simply rejected with "user not known"._x000D_
2. A way for a user to authenticate themselves as an existing entity, and add a new entity alias from another auth method._x000D_
_x000D_
The mechanism I'm thinking of for (2) is as follows - assuming we've already created an entity for the new user._x000D_
_x000D_
1. Create a wrapped token which authenticates as this entity._x000D_
2. Get the wrapped token to the end user somehow, e.g. by sending it in an E-mail to an E-mail address we already know they have.  This can be in the form of a link, e.g. `https://vault.example.com/ui/add-alias?token=XXXXXXXX`_x000D_
3. The user clicks on the link. It does the following steps:_x000D_
    * Authenticates the user using OIDC (as part of hitting the web page)_x000D_
    * Unwraps the token and uses that to authenticate as the selected entity_x000D_
    * Creates an entity alias from the OIDC identity to the selected entity_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Now that Vault has an "allow_all" assignment (#14119), it's possible to write a standalone registration server which performs almost the same.  The user would connect to the web page, which would dynamically create an entity and entity alias.  The registration server could then unwrap and validate the given token, and then perform an [entity merge](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/identity/entity#merge-entities) to combine the original entity with the one newly created._x000D_
_x000D_
This may be workable, but: (a) it relies on the "drive-by" dynamic entity creation, and (b) it relies on the registration server having its own token with sufficient super-user privileges to perform entity merging.  If not done right, it may be subject to 'confused deputy' attacks which would allow one user to take over another user's account._x000D_
_x000D_
IMO, it would be much better if a user who has already authenticated as themselves, could be authorized to add a new entity alias to their own entity._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
With a little more work, this could also become a mechanism for user "self-care" to add their own OIDC entity aliases.  e.g. if Vault has enabled auth methods Userpass, OIDC1 and OIDC2, then a user could login with Userpass or OIDC1, and then attach an entity alias for OIDC2._x000D_
_x000D_
Being able to remove aliases would be a corresponding feature.  It should not leave the entity with zero aliases, of course._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

title: vault kv get fails with trailing whitespace
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
`vault kv get` fails to get secrets with trailing whitespace, e.g. `"secret/fail "`_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Create secret: `curl -X PUT -H "X-Vault-Request: true" -H "X-Vault-Token: $(vault print token)" -d '{"data":{"foo":"bar"},"options":{}}' http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/secret/data/fail%20`_x000D_
2. Observe trailing whitespace `vault kv list -format=json secret` (you will see that it's stored like: `"fail "`)_x000D_
3. `vault kv get "secret/fail "` responds with: `No value found at secret/data/fail`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The secret should be returned._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
_x000D_
I've tested with a plain container:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
podman run -it --rm -e VAULT_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID=myroot -p 8200:8200 --name vault docker.io/library/vault:1.10.0_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I also use vault/curl from inside the container:_x000D_
```_x000D_
podman exec -it vault sh_x000D_
apk add curl_x000D_
..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
This works: `curl -H "X-Vault-Request: true" -H "X-Vault-Token: $(vault print token)" http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/secret/data/fail%20`_x000D_
_x000D_
You won't be able to create the secret with `vault kv put`. The command seems to trim the trailing whitespace._x000D_
_x000D_
This looks similar to https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/6213_x000D_
_x000D_
Trailing whitespace is also mentioned here https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/6714

title: The location for command-line flags is needlessly picky
body_text:
We're using vault behind google's firewall (running on GCR), and want to authenticate users as an extra layer of security. That involves setting the `Authorization` header, which I do in a wrapper script:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
AUTH_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-identity-token ...)_x000D_
exec vault $@ -header "Authorization=Bearer $AUTH_TOKEN"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This works for simple things like `vault status`. However, this fails with commands like `kv put` where the `-header` flag has to be after the initial subcommand, but before the arguments to that subcommand._x000D_
_x000D_
I could imagine several solutions, in increasing order of complexity:_x000D_
 - add an env variable `VAULT_HEADERS` or `VAULT_FLAGS`_x000D_
 - make `vault -headers kv put ...` work_x000D_
 - make `vault kv put ... -headers` work_x000D_
 - add a client configuration at `~/.config/vault.hcl`, with options to overrides global flags

title: Vault +v1.9 - no_proxy is ignored
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
NO_PROXY env doesn't works anymore since upgrade from v1.8 to v1.9.4_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run `export VAULT_API_ADDR="https://vault:8200" VAULT_CLUSTER_ADDR="https://vault:8201" ETCD_ADDR="https://etcd1:2379" HTTPS_PROXY="http://PROXY:PORT/" NO_PROXY="etcd1"; vault server -config /vault`_x000D_
3. no_proxy seems not to works anymore_x000D_
```_x000D_
"error":"rpc e_x000D_
rror: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = latest balancer error: last connection error: connection error: desc = \"t[.... proxy output that tell us that it's internal resource so cannot works....]_x000D_
2022-04-13T18:58:48.426+0200 [INFO]  proxy environment: https_proxy=http://PROXY:PORT/ no_proxy="etcd1"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
I expect that proxy is ignored for etcd1 server._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.9.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.9.4_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
If I rollback to v1.8, all works._x000D_
With Vault 1.9, it seems to force the proxy and to ignore the no_proxy env even it's set in the logs._x000D_
Seems related to PR [#12582](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/12582)_x000D_
I also tried to unset/set VAULT_HTTP_PROXY / no_proxy / NO_PROXY but always the same issue.

title: `api_addr` is used for multiple purposes with sometimes differing requirements
body_text:
I have realised that `api_addr` is used for multiple purposes:_x000D_
_x000D_
* For redirecting external clients of Vault, if a request arrives at a standby node, in some cases_x000D_
_x000D_
* For allowing newly started Vault plugins to make initial contact with the cluster, to perform an unwrap operation to fetch their mTLS identity._x000D_
_x000D_
When you operate Vault at scale, it may be inappropriate to use the same URL for both of these purposes._x000D_
_x000D_
I am thinking of the case where the nodes are behind a firewall and external clients only have access via a load balancer (as documented at https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/concepts/ha#behind-load-balancers), but plugins should not attempt to use the load balancer for their mTLS bootstrap for one of several possible reasons:_x000D_
_x000D_
* The load balancer may be pointing at a different Vault cluster entirely, for HA reasons, at a time when a particular back end needs to start/restart a plugin executable._x000D_
_x000D_
* The load balancer external IP may not be accessible from the Vault node, due to network topology._x000D_
_x000D_
* The start-up procedure of Vault itself should not depend on an external load balancer, as it's an unexpected and unnecessary dependency._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
To remedy this, I believe there is a need to divide the existing `api_addr` setting (which has been known as `redirect_addr` in Vault's past) back into a separate redirect address for clients, and an API address for in-cluster communication.
top_3_comments_text: maxb: Since originally filing this issue, I've discovered `api_addr` is now used in a third way too: as a default URL for the Identity backend's OIDC provider: > issuer (string: \<optional>) - Specifies what will be used as the scheme://host:port component for the iss claim of ID tokens. This defaults to a URL with Vault's api_addr as the scheme://host:port component and /v1/:namespace/identity/oidc/provider/:name as the path component. If provided explicitly, it must point to a Vault instance that is network reachable by clients for ID token validation. -- https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/identity/oidc-provider There can be considerable variation in OIDC software, as the standard is quite loose, so this might be accurate in some cases. However, a popular Go OIDC library, https://github.com/coreos/go-oidc, as used in the Kubernetes API server, requires that the issuer URL used to access the `/.well-known/openid-configuration` endpoint is the same as the issuer claim in returned tokens. In such a configuration, it would be mandatory to set the issuer to an URL which points to a generic service address, probably a load-balancer or dynamic DNS name, which can fail over between Vault nodes, and even between Vault clusters if HA failover to a replica is to be supported. To be fair, the Identity backend's OIDC provider does allow the issuer to be directly set, and not depend on `api_addr` - so this is supported. I make this comment just to provide more illustration of the tension between whether `api_addr` should address a single Vault node or a generic endpoint capable of failover. | maxb: Since originally filing this issue, go-plugin's AutoMTLS feature has been rolled out as default for Vault plugins, which partially improves this situation, as the Vault instance's `api_addr` is no longer critical to the establishment of communication between Vault and its plugins (assuming up to date Vault versions and plugins compiled with an up to date SDK). There is still some tension between different usages of `api_addr`, though, as `api_addr` is used in various contexts where one would expect it to identify an individual node - including code testing to see if the current leader is the current node, and the output of `vault operator members` - as well as being used in contexts where individual node addresses should not be disclosed, if behind a loadbalancer not intended to drop out of the traffic path.

title: Override AWS_REGION Environment variable
body_text:
With dynamoDB backend storage we can today config table region in config file, but it's override with environment variable `AWS_REGION` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`. EKS cluster from 1.18 auto-inject `AWS_REGION` variable to each pod with cluster region. So if you want use table from default region, you need set this in config, but `AWS_REGION` override on this_x000D_
_x000D_
Solution:_x000D_
Change order of configuration can break current system, so we can add new environment variable  `AWS_DYNAMODB_REGION` before `AWS_REGION` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`. New order of config AWS_DYNAMODB_REGION=>AWS_REGION=>AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=>config file

title: Expose bcrypt hash functionality
body_text:
As far as I can see in the docs, /transit/hash offers sha* hashes._x000D_
It would be a plus, if bcrypt also would be offered. It seems to me,_x000D_
that bcrypt is already internally used for password hashes, so perhaps_x000D_
it would be easy to offer it as an alternative to the sha* hash algorithms.
top_3_comments_text: kitography: `bcrypt` is not currently offered as a function under `/transit/hash` because it isn’t a general hash function. In particular, it can’t take in arbitrarily sized input data. It also wasn’t designed for efficiency. Unfortunately, for some of those same reasons, `bcrypt` isn’t easy to add to this endpoint (though the pull request is appreciated): * There isn’t one `bcrypt` function. The `bcrypt` algorithm allows one to specify how many iterations to run the derivation algorithm over the password. We currently have no way to pass in that field (and that field would be not applicable for sha* hashing). * `bcrypt` is very resource intensive - that’s the goal. This is great for what it is used for (password verification) but could result in an unauthenticated endpoint that is prone to Denial of Service attacks. * Being able to derive precisely how fast `bcrypt` is on the server would make it substantially easier to figure out if a user existed or not from a timing attack on login. * Restriction on input length would have implications both in the errors returned and in the UI.

Thank you @maxb The command `vault login` is necessary always, but it will automatically read the `VAULT_TOKEN` environment variable, so you don't need to pass it through STDIN. If you're already performing `export VAULT_TOKEN=your_token` in a previous step of your script, you can just run `vault login` without anything else.
raskchanky: > The command vault login is necessary always, but it will automatically read the VAULT_TOKEN environment variable, so you don't need to pass it through STDIN. > If you're already performing export VAULT_TOKEN=your_token in a previous step of your script, you can just run vault login without anything else. This is actually not true. The main purpose of `vault login` is to authenticate the user and return a Vault token. If you already have a Vault token, you can set it in the `VAULT_TOKEN` env var, and `vault login` is no longer necessary. The Vault API only cares about the token.

maxb: A final comment to wrap this one up: The `vault login` implements three separate but related pieces of functionality: * Calling a Vault HTTP API, to exchange auth-method-dependent credentials for a Vault token * Calling a Vault HTTP API, to look up additional information about a directly provided token * Storing a Vault token in `~/.vault-token` or a configured token helper program The first is activated by the `-method` flag. The second takes place when the `-method` flag is not used, and a pre-existing token is supplied on the command line or via standard input. The third happens by default but can be disabled with the `-no-store` flag. Hopefully that helps explain why it is used in so many ways.

title: [ui] Redirect logic doesn't work on already logged users
body_text:
## Describe the bug_x000D_
_x000D_
In our enterprise setup:_x000D_
_x000D_
- We have a parent namespace (let's call it `root`) which has mounted the OIDC Auth Method under the `/oidc` path, there are plenty of entities with oidc aliases._x000D_
- We have a children namespace (let's call it `child`) which has a Group `oidc` with some policies to access diverse secrets. This Group has as members some entities from the `root` parent namespace with aliases for the OIDC Auth._x000D_
_x000D_
When I don't have an issued session, so I'm logged out, I can authenticate against the `root` namespace and then be redirected to a concrete secret within the `child` namespace. I'm using the following URL to get this behaviour:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://vault.XXXXX/ui/vault/auth?redirect_to=%2Fvault%2Fsecrets%2Fkv%2Fshow%2Fsecret-service%2Fgithubpat%3Fnamespace%3D%252Fchild&with=oidc_x000D_
_x000D_
This works perfect if I'm not logged in, I'm redirected to:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://vault.XXXXX/ui/vault/secrets/kv/show/secret-service/githubpat?namespace=%2Fchild_x000D_
_x000D_
The problem comes when I'm already logged in, since instead of being redirected to the secret, I'm just redirected to the parent namespace:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://vault.XXXXX/ui/vault/secrets?redirect_to=%2Fvault%2Fsecrets%2Fdxp-system%2Fshow%2Fsecret-service%2Fgithubpat%3Fnamespace%3D%252Fchild_x000D_
_x000D_
From what I see, the `redirect_to` query parameter is kept but it's being ignored._x000D_
_x000D_
### To Reproduce_x000D_
Problem on the UI, the steps are indicated above._x000D_
_x000D_
## Expected behaviour_x000D_
I would expect to be redirected to the secret in the specified namespace, as when I'm logged out, so the flow is consistent._x000D_
_x000D_
## Environment:_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): [Vault 1.8.6+ent](https://www.github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#186)_x000D_
_x000D_
### Addendum_x000D_
**From Tue 26. Apr 13:25**_x000D_
_x000D_
- I just set up a cluster in HVN to test the behaviour in **Vault 1.9.4+ent** with UserPass Auth Method, and it has the same issue._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
**From Thu 7. Jul 13:52**_x000D_

title: Web UI with policy to allow update of group membership gives "Permission Denied"
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Given a policy which allows you to update a group membership, but not other fields; and you try to edit the group in the web UI; when you save the group you get "Permission Denied", even if you haven't changed anything._x000D_
_x000D_
This appears to be because the web UI is resubmitting other unchanged fields, which the user does not have write access to, as part of its update request._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Create groups called "instructors" and "students"._x000D_
    * On the "students" group, for completeness you can add some arbitrary policy (just the "default" policy is fine) - although this is not necessary to reproduce the problem._x000D_
2. Create a policy which allows read and write access to the "students" group membership only:_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
    vault policy write students-group-admin - <<"EOH"_x000D_
    path "identity/group/id" {_x000D_
      capabilities = ["list"]_x000D_
    }_x000D_
_x000D_
    path "identity/entity/id" {_x000D_
      capabilities = ["list"]_x000D_
    }_x000D_
_x000D_
    path "identity/group/id/9425031b-f484-3d50-c8f0-d22f982cf7a1" {_x000D_
      capabilities = ["read", "update"]_x000D_
      allowed_parameters = {_x000D_
        "member_entity_ids" = []_x000D_
        "member_group_ids" = []_x000D_
      }_x000D_
    }_x000D_
    EOH_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
    Note that this policy only allows membership to be written, and in particular does not allow write to the "policies" field, which could result in privilege escalation._x000D_
_x000D_
3. Add this policy to the "instructors" group_x000D_
4. Login to the web UI as someone in the "instructors" group_x000D_
5. List the groups_x000D_
6. Open the "students" group to show its membership. (This works)._x000D_
7. Click "Edit group" then immediately "Save" - you don't even have to touch the list of members._x000D_
_x000D_
You will get "Permission Denied": _x000D_
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44789/165501749-22e9f8dc-a43c-49d9-88cb-57a4c03e80a1.png)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The above policy should allow the "instructor" to edit the membership of the "students" group in the web UI._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.10.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): N/A (using web UI)_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 20.04_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s): N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
In the browser developer console I can see that it is submitting **all** the group attributes in a PUT request:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "name": "students",_x000D_
  "type": "internal",_x000D_
  "metadata": {},_x000D_
  "policies": [_x000D_
    "default"_x000D_
  ],_x000D_
  "parent_group_ids": [_x000D_
    "6afa4505-40fe-0f2b-3c63-b36d23e52874"_x000D_
  ],_x000D_
  "member_entity_ids": [_x000D_
    "8509ce55-5ad0-4a62-1abc-e923879cad62"_x000D_
  ]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I believe it's this attempt to reapply values that don't need changing (e.g. "policies", "metadata" and/or "parent_group_ids") which is causing the permission error.  Aside: if the group doesn't have any policies then the PUT doesn't have a  "policies" member._x000D_
_x000D_
I think the fix would be either:_x000D_
1. in the web UI, compare the original and new values of the field, and don't submit any fields which have not changed; or_x000D_
2. in the backend, permit a "write" to a field if you are trying to write the existing value and you have only "read" access to that field._x000D_
_x000D_
I think option (1) is the less invasive as it does not change any of the existing API semantics.

title: Temporarily disable and re-enable an auth method
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
If I disable an auth method with `vault auth disable`, it is deleted.  All its entity aliases still exist, but they refer to the original mount accessor which no longer exists._x000D_
_x000D_
If I re-enable the same method with `vault auth enable` then it gets assigned a new mount accessor: this means that all the existing aliases no longer work, so I have to edit each one. (Aside: the web UI lets you choose between mount paths, not mount accessors)_x000D_
_x000D_
I can stop it being shown in the web login page using `vault auth tune -listing-visibility=`, but it is still available if the user explicitly selects the auth method and path._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
A flag to `vault auth tune` to disable an auth mount without deleting it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Allow the mount accessor to be specified in `vault auth enable`, rather than dynamically chosen, so it can be recreated as it was before.  This would also work._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

title: Vault 500s when calling a plugin and `api_addr` is not set or incorrect
body_text:
I recently set up a custom plugin, and was getting a 500 when interacting with it. The root issue was that I had `api_addr` set, but it was an https URL even though the `listener` block had `tls_disable = true`. For more context, see https://github.com/davidsbond/vault-plugin-tailscale/issues/16._x000D_
_x000D_
It's not clear where in the stack this is happening, but the error message was pretty unhelpful:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
URL: GET https://vault-xxx-run.app/v1/tailscale/config_x000D_
Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* 1 error occurred:_x000D_
	* Unrecognized remote plugin message:_x000D_
_x000D_
This usually means that the plugin is either invalid or simply_x000D_
needs to be recompiled to support the latest protocol._x000D_
```_x000D_
I think at a minimum, the error log should provide more information._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): `1.10.0`_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): `1.10.1`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Google Cloud Run (see linked issue for Dockerfile)

title: Configure renewal threshold for leased secrets
body_text:
We're using vault-agent as a sidecar to get credentials for an approle on AWS with a template for /.aws/credentials like this:_x000D_
```_x000D_
[default]_x000D_
{{- with secret "aws/logging/sts/vector" }}_x000D_
aws_access_key_id = {{ .Data.access_key }}_x000D_
aws_secret_access_key = {{ .Data.secret_key }}_x000D_
aws_session_token = {{ .Data.security_token }}_x000D_
{{- end }}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
It works :)_x000D_
The problem is with the update interval: the default ttl for this secret from vault is 60m, so vault-agent updates the template after about 53 minutes (which is neither 2/3 nor 85%? - see [here](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/agent/template)). The app "consuming" the credentials file checks for new credentials every 15 minutes. Now because these intervals overlap, there's a regular timeframe where the app will get credentials valid for less than 15 minutes (remaining), so the credentials will expire before the next check. I can get the app to check every 5 minutes (minimum, it seems), which makes the window smaller, but it's still there. Also changing the TTL on the leased secret only moves the expired-creds window around, but never eliminates it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
If I could tell vault-agent e.g. in the template, when it should renew the leased secret, in my scenario after 44 minutes, the consuming app would always get credentials that are still valid until the next check (>15m). In my scenario, if the leased secret where to be updated after 2/3 of the TTL, so 40m, it would solve my specific problem, but having it completely configurable would probably be better._x000D_
Something like:_x000D_
`{{- with secret "aws/logging/sts/vector" "renew-after:40m" }}`_x000D_
or_x000D_
`{{- with secret "aws/logging/sts/vector" "renew-after-percent-of-ttl:60" }}`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered._x000D_
Requesting a specific ttl for the lease only moves the window around._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
If there are any use-cases that would help us understand the use/need/value please share them as they can help us decide on acceptance and prioritization._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here._x000D_

JWT login is not working in the web UI, login from CLI/API works correctly._x000D_
Trying to login via the web UI using a JWT token fails with the error "Authentication failed: permission denied", but the /auth/jwt/login endpoint is never called._x000D_
_x000D_

**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run `vault auth enable jwt`_x000D_
2. Run `vault write auth/jwt/config oidc_discovery_url="https://login.example.com/" default_role="guest"`_x000D_
3. Open the web UI and try to login with a JWT token_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Login works correctly (given the *guest* roles exists), "Authentication failed: role "guest" could not be found" error otherwise._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: 1.10.1 (latest Vault version from https://releases.hashicorp.com/vault/)_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version: 1.10.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Fedora 35_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
storage "raft" {_x000D_
  path    = "/some/storage/path"_x000D_
  node_id = "node1"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_

```_x000D_

This bug is present in version 1.8.10, 1.9.5, 1.10.0 and 1.10.1. I haven't found other Vault version affected._x000D_
I think this bug might be related to PR #14545: in ui/app/components/auth-form.js, at line 248, changing back to `let backend = this.selectedAuthBackend || {};` the login works correctly, but I don't know if there are any other impacts._x000D_

title: Issues with `vault operator generate-root` CLI help message
body_text:
This part of the CLI help message is incorrect: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/967b2987e5a17a82f9b46b6d0b4f93b42fd550cd/command/operator_generate_root.go#L80-L82_x000D_
_x000D_
The `-otp` flag is not needed or used, when providing an unseal key shard. It is only for use in conjunction with `-init` or `-decode`._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
This earlier part of the CLI help message could be made more useful - it documents that you must use a multi-step process to begin an OTP-based root token generation:_x000D_
* `vault operator generate-root -generate-otp`_x000D_
* `vault operator generate-root -init -otp="..."`_x000D_
_x000D_
In fact you can use just:_x000D_
`vault operator generate-root -init`_x000D_
as shorthand for both steps in one command._x000D_
_x000D_
It would be nice to list this workflow option first, as it is the most simple and convenient for someone reading the help message with an immediate need to generate a root token. The other workflows are more relevant to someone implementing a more complex and pre-planned key ceremony.

title: Adjust APT instructions to use signed-by
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Download pages for all Hashicorp products, including Vault suggest using deprecated apt-key utility for installing a system-wide GPG key to trust the Hashicorp APT repo. See http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/jammy/man8/apt-key.8.html for deprecation information_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Adjust download instructions to use the new `signed-by` option per (https://wiki.debian.org/DebianRepository/UseThirdParty). Example below:_x000D_
```_x000D_
curl -fsSL https://apt.releases.hashicorp.com/gpg | gpg --dearmor > /usr/share/keyrings/hashicorp-keyring.gpg_x000D_
echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/hashicorp-keyring.gpg] https://apt.releases.hashicorp.com $(lsb_release -cs) main" > /etc/apt/source.list.d/hashicorp.list_x000D_
apt update && apt install vault_x000D_
```_x000D_

title: Vault API library should periodically force new connections in it's pool
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
When failing over via a DR it is very easy for an operator to forget the shutdown step.  When DNS is migrated to the newly failed over cluster there is a large chance of issues for a consumer to accidentally hold a connection open to the old cluster forever._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault's API library should periodically reconnect it's HTTP connections.  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Placing a proxy in front of Vault to do this for us._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
We had a large outage, and having this feature would've saved us several hours worth of time._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: averche: Hi @chuckyz! Thank you for bringing this to our attention! This is indeed a very interesting issue and it's hard to establish the exact root cause. From what I understand, the vast majority of Vault client connections are short lived: most request wrappers read the entire response bodies til EOF and close them. The only exception I can think of is [`client.Sys().Monitor(ctx)`](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/sys_monitor.go#L14), which continues steaming server logs until its context has been explicitly cancelled by the caller. If the issue is indeed caused by `Monitor(ctx)`, the solution may be to periodically cancel the context and call the function again. This, however, risks dropping some of the monitored logs, so it may not be a great generic solution to implement in the library itself. Having said this, we are also working on a new OpenAPI-based Vault client library. With more freedom to make potentially breaking changes there, we could consider reworking how `Monitor(ctx)` works. The other possibility that I can think of is that the issue is caused by the idle connections cached by `http.Transport`. From `net/http` [documentation](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-cleanhttp/blob/master/cleanhttp.go#L31): > By default, Transport caches connections for future re-use. This may leave many open connections when accessing many hosts. This behavior can be managed using Transport’s CloseIdleConnections method and the MaxIdleConnsPerHost and DisableKeepAlives fields. The default http client used by the Vault API library is `cleanhttp.DefaultPooledClient()`. It's a thin wrapper around `net/http`, which sets the [following](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-cleanhttp/blob/master/cleanhttp.go#L31): ```go MaxIdleConns: 100, IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second, ... MaxIdleConnsPerHost: runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0) + 1, ``` Vault api library also uses [`go-retryablehttp`](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-retryablehttp), which does not close idle connections on successful requests. If the idle connections are indeed the root cause, Vault client library allows overriding the http client and the retry behavior using the `Config` object. Using something like `cleanhttp.DefaultClient()` would disallow idle connections entirely. It might be worth trying it out just to see if that's the actual root cause. I would be hesitant to change the library's default HTTP client since it may adversely affect the performance. However, we could consider periodically calling `CloseIdleConnections()` on a separate go-routine if it would actually address the issue. I'd be happy to investigate this further and work with you to debug the actual root cause! :raised_hands: 🤜 🤛 | chuckyz: > However, we could consider periodically calling CloseIdleConnections() on a separate go-routine if it would actually address the issue. This would be my ideal solution and I think would've helped us tremendously. Something that is possible within C#'s SocketHttpHandler client is that you can even mark _active_ connections as 'as soon as this is idle, close it and force a new connection in the pool.' (https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.http.socketshttphandler.pooledconnectionlifetime?view=net-6.0#system-net-http-socketshttphandler-pooledconnectionlifetime) Is there anything like that within `net/http` ? That would be the absolute ideal case for us. | averche: Hi @chuckyz ! I tried to reproduce the issue using a fork of our official Go sample app, [hashicorp/hello-vault-go/sample-app](https://github.com/hashicorp/hello-vault-go/tree/main/sample-app). I [modified](https://github.com/averche/hello-vault-go/pull/1) the docker compose setup to use static IPs and a custom unbound DNS then ran a few tests to see if the connections are sticky. The full description of the tests I ran can be found in the updated [README.md](https://github.com/averche/hello-vault-go/blob/main/sample-app/README.md). TLDR: from what I see, all connections established to Vault server by our test app through `vault/api` library enter `TIME_WAIT` state immediately after the request and are fully closed within a minute or so. Switching the DNS to point to a different vault server works as expected -- all new requests create new connections to the new IP: ```shell-session $ docker exec -it sample-app-app-1 netstat -n | grep 8200 tcp 0 0 192.168.19.3:56208 192.168.19.4:8200 TIME_WAIT tcp 0 0 192.168.19.3:60596 192.168.19.5:8200 TIME_WAIT <- new connection tcp 0 0 192.168.19.3:56200 192.168.19.4:8200 TIME_WAIT tcp 0 0 192.168.19.3:56190 192.168.19.4:8200 TIME_WAIT tcp 0 0 192.168.19.3:56212 192.168.19.4:8200 TIME_WAIT ``` I also tried adding a goroutine which calls `CloseIdleConnections()` every 5 seconds in https://github.com/averche/hello-vault-go/pull/1/commits/786c0df91fcbdcf27bc1430a26eb25f79ea6c3a7 . This did not seem to affect the connection behaviour. I'm guessing that's because the connections are not entering idle state. Please feel free to clone https://github.com/averche/hello-vault-go and follow the steps I described in the [README](https://github.com/averche/hello-vault-go/blob/main/sample-app/README.md). Let me know if I should be testing it differently, I'd be happy to modify the test further!

title: Use assumed role to authenticate on Vault
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Cant use credentials of the assumed role to authenticate on Vault. The only way to pass AWS secrets to AWSAuth structure is to write them in ENV or file (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/aws/aws.go#L148) or rely on AWS metadata extraction (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/aws/aws.go#L154)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Some function, that allow you to change/push credentials in AWSAuth structure. Or make field "creds" public. https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/aws/aws.go#L19. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
The only solution I found is to write AWS secrets into env or file and this code block should "catch" them:_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/aws/aws.go#L139_x000D_
But It's not the best solution to keep secrets in file or env. I would like to keep them into memory._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
You have multiple EC2 instances with multiple profiles that should authenticate on vault and get access to some vault secrets. You don't want to share between them one profile, but it's more convenient to create assumable role that service should assume and then authenticate with it on Vault._x000D_
_x000D_

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I configured and OIDC auth provider to link Vault to our company's identities in Google G Suite. I wanted to have both a human-readable aliases (i.e. based on the users full name from G Suite), as well as a list of their G Suite groups pulled into Vault._x000D_

_x000D_
Now switch on group fetching:_x000D_

{_x000D_
    "oidc_discovery_url": "https://accounts.google.com",_x000D_

title: Duo MFA -- Add support for Access Device IP
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Duo's Authorized Networks Policies are useful for some sensitive application settings (i.e. "your request for MFA must come from A.B.C.D/X network"). Currently, however, Vault's implementation of the Duo Auth API doesn't include the clients IP address as part of the request info sent to Duo API, so we see the default: _x000D_
_x000D_
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10523950/167493704-22cf5df6-9602-427a-85c7-cf5ad68857ec.png)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
It looks like the [preauth calls[(https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/vault/login_mfa.go#L1733) are already sending the IP address of the client, so we likely just need to add the following around [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/vault/login_mfa.go#L1768):_x000D_
_x000D_
`options = append(options, authapi.AuthIpAddr(reqConnectionRemoteAddr)`_x000D_
_x000D_
Per the upstream docs [go](https://github.com/duosecurity/duo_api_golang/blob/master/authapi/authapi.go#L318) and [Duo](https://duo.com/docs/authapi#/auth)_x000D_
_x000D_

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When using the UI to access KV secrets, it does not show the metadata of a given secret although the tokens policies grant access to it. Only if the policy grants metadata read access to all secrets, the tab is shown._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Create a token with the following policy:_x000D_

# List top-level key/value secrets metadata._x000D_
path "secret/metadata/" {_x000D_

}_x000D_
_x000D_

}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "secret/metadata/team_acme/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read", "delete", "list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "secret/delete/team_acme/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "secret/undelete/team_acme/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "secret/destroy/team_acme/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_

_x000D_
_x000D_

The UI should show the `metadata` tab because the policy allows accessing it._x000D_
_x000D_

If the policy grants `list` and `read` access to all secrets, the `metadata` tab is shown in the secret details._x000D_

  capabilities = ["update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "secret/destroy/team_acme/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["update"]_x000D_

```_x000D_

title: Vault allows for incorrectly configured paths in policies to be deployed successfully
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We have recently discovered that some of our Vault users have been deploying incorrectly configured paths in policies, and Vault does not verify them._x000D_
_x000D_
Vault allows incorrectly configured paths in policies to be deployed through UI, CLI and Terraform. For example, with the below path:_x000D_
```_x000D_
path "path/" {_x000D_
  policy = "write"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
The following command is executed successfully:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault policy write -namespace=test test-incorrect-policy - <<EOH_x000D_
path "test/" {_x000D_
  policy = "write" _x000D_
}_x000D_
EOH_x000D_
_x000D_
Success! Uploaded policy: test-incorrect-policy_x000D_
```_x000D_
The path contains incorrect capability and incorrect key. An error message **is** displayed if the capability is within square brackets, but there **is no** error if brackets are missing. _x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Login to Vault_x000D_
2. Run the following command: _x000D_
```_x000D_
vault policy write test-incorrect-policy - <<EOH_x000D_
path "test/" {_x000D_
  policy = "write" _x000D_
}_x000D_
EOH_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
I would expect vault to check for the incorrect key (**policy**) regardless of the value and display an error message._x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): Tested in both Vault Enterprise 1.9.0+ent and 1.10.2+ent._x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.10.2_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Hosted in AKS

Yes, you can find the full mapping in the Vault source code here: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/74b1eec537394bbd9940e7e993c9c8e0ed8caf4f/vault/policy.go#L371-L385 with the referenced constants being at the top of that file. > Are there any plans to deprecate this backwards compatibility? title: Policy for transit engine not being respected, permission denied
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I want different people to have access to different keys._x000D_
Followed the tutorial https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/eaas-transit. _x000D_
Enabled the transit engine, created a new key, create a new policy in order to give access to the key, but when trying to use the key I get a permission denied. _x000D_
_x000D_
Problem is with the policies, as per documentation the following policy should work:_x000D_
```_x000D_
path "transit/encrypt/*-sec" {_x000D_
   capabilities = [ "update" ]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "transit/decrypt/*-sec" {_x000D_
   capabilities = [ "update" ]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
But I always got permission denied. The only way for it to work is to use the following policy, but this defeats the purpose as user will have access to all keys:_x000D_
`path "transit/*" {_x000D_
   capabilities = [ "update" ]_x000D_
}`_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
This can be tested with docker vault: _x000D_
1. `docker run -d -p8200:8200 vault:1.9.0 server -dev -dev-root-token-id=toor`_x000D_
2. `export VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8200`_x000D_
3. `export VAULT_TOKEN=toor`_x000D_
4. `vault secrets enable transit`_x000D_
5. `vault write transit/keys/prodkey-sec type=rsa-4096`_x000D_
6._x000D_
```_x000D_
vault policy write security -<<EOF_x000D_
path "transit/encrypt/*-sec" {_x000D_

title: ServiceAccount incompatability with EKS 1.21+
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Apologies if this is the wrong place. I received the following alert from AWS, and I think this indicates that Vault is not using a newer version of the Kubernetes client SDK, which will result in ServiceAccounts not working fairly shortly:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
We have identified applications running in one or more of your Amazon EKS clusters that are not refreshing service account tokens. Applications making requests to Kubernetes API server with expired tokens will fail. You can resolve the issue by updating your application and its dependencies to use newer versions of Kubernetes client SDK that automatically refreshes the tokens._x000D_
_x000D_
What is the problem?_x000D_
_x000D_
Kubernetes version 1.21 graduated BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume feature [1] to beta and enabled it by default. This feature improves security of service account tokens by requiring a one hour expiry time, over the previous default of no expiration. This means that applications that do not refetch service account tokens periodically will receive an HTTP 401 unauthorized error response on requests to Kubernetes API server with expired tokens. You can learn more about the BoundServiceAccountToken feature in EKS Kubernetes 1.21 release notes [2]._x000D_
_x000D_
To enable a smooth migration of applications to the newer time-bound service account tokens, EKS v1.21+ extends the lifetime of service account tokens to 90 days. Applications on EKS v1.21+ clusters that make API server requests with tokens that are older than 90 days will receive an HTTP 401 unauthorized  error response._x000D_
_x000D_
How can you resolve the issue?_x000D_
_x000D_
To make the transition to time bound service account tokens easier, Kubernetes has updated the below official versions of client SDKs to automatically refetch tokens before the one hour expiration:_x000D_
_x000D_
* Go v0.15.7 and later_x000D_
* Python v12.0.0 and later_x000D_
* Java v9.0.0 and later_x000D_
* Javascript v0.10.3 and later_x000D_
* Ruby master branch_x000D_
* Haskell v0.3.0.0_x000D_
_x000D_
We recommend that you update your application and its dependencies to use one of the above client SDK versions if you are on an older version. _x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Deploy Vault into EKS 1.22 (we used the official vault helm chart)_x000D_
2. Ensure that serviceaccount.create is 'true' and that an eks role-arn annotation is added to it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.10.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): n/a_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: EKS 1.22_x000D_

You might be able to provide these with a random port in some range. The OIDC provider would need to have the redirect URIs configured correctly, of course. Some OIDC providers allow for any port to be used so long as the redirect URI is on the loopback interface (see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252#section-7.3). That could potentially make the OIDC provider-side configuration less of a pain. I'd say this currently functions as designed. I'm going to remove the bug label and mark this as a feature request. I think we could potentially include an option to the OIDC auth CLI command to specify a range of ports to select from or use random selection.

msvticket: I still see this occasionally using vault 1.10.3 and EKS 1.28. We use [bank-vaults](https://bank-vaults.dev/) to configure vault. It doesn't seem like a coincidence It doesn't seem like a coincidence that the logs saying `login unauthorized due to: lookup failed: service account unauthorized; this could mean it has been deleted or recreated with a new token` started 90 days after the vault configurer component of bank-vaults had run the last time while ["For Amazon EKS clusters, the extended expiry period is 90 days."](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/service-accounts.html). The vault-configurer is the component that implements [this configuration](https://bank-vaults.dev/docs/concepts/external-configuration/). msvticket: For anybody ending up here looking for a solution: The problem in my case was the use of [bank vaults vault operator](https://github.com/bank-vaults/vault-operator) for administering vault.
