title: Allow Vault to auto-unseal restarted instances when in High Availability mode.
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Typically node maintenance for critical nodes is done one by one. A node becomes sealed after the maintenance and requires either manual unseal (inconvenient to do all the time), reliance on an external provider with no current way to manually unseal, or another vault cluster which also has the same problem and requires unseal during node maintenance._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Assuming most of the nodes are still unsealed (say 2/3 or 3/5) It would be nice if alive unsealed vault nodes could unseal the sealed one(s). So, initially, nodes are unsealed with Shamir's keys, and then the cluster auto-unseals itself if there are enough nodes._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered._x000D_
_x000D_
Not sure if this has been already considered and if some roadblocks found._x000D_
_x000D_
#6046 seems to be related. People asked for multiple recovery keys, which may be of different types (Shamir, KMS). Here we would likely need the same: Shamir + transit-like.
top_3_comments_text: maxb: Whilst I can see how this would be useful, it seems like it would weaken the security model. The problem is, how can the remaining unsealed nodes, successfully authenticate that the restarted node is legitimate. Today, a Shamir seal protects against a single admin slipping a modified Vault binary that allows them extra access onto a node, and restarting Vault to use it. (Whereas, auto-unseal does not, since the node can just auto-unseal.) This protection would be lost if a returning node could reacquire the key material from other cluster nodes. There are other attacks of concern too - e.g. shutting down an existing Vault node and starting up a new compromised host at the same IP address. I can theorise that perhaps a Vault cluster could - **optionally** - maintain a short lived encryption key and a short lived authentication secret on disk on each node, and unsealed nodes could be willing to disclose the root key, encrypted with the short lived key, over the network, if the authentication secret was presented. I think this would roughly equate to a kind of time-limited cluster-internal transit unseal. The question, though, is whether HashiCorp would want to entertain that level of additional complexity in critical security code, to support a lesser security level for customers who wanted a different security/convenience tradeoff. Or, perhaps there is a better way than what I have conjectured above. Meanwhile, there are a some possible compromises you can make today to create different unseal behaviours using the currently available building blocks: 1) You can just write the unseal key to disk unencrypted on the Vault nodes, and have a local wrapper script to inject it at startup. Very insecure, of course, but since we're discussing security for convenience, it seems worth mentioning. 2) You can create a super-secure service of your own, and give it enough Vault key shares to unseal Vault, which it transmits to the Vault API on request, subject to the business logic of your choice. It's no small undertaking, obviously, but it does open up the option for you to implement whatever rules you want, around disclosing the unseal key. | ksa-real: Sorry, as my questions may be naive. I don't have enough knowledge about Vault. So just trying to make some guesses. The documentation seems to be much focused on operational procedures with less focus on what happens underneath, what are the crypto suites used, and what are attack vectors the solution mitigates. For example, I don't understand why a chain of keys was used (root, encryption), as they are all stored with the data. My guess is that root is unencrypted only briefly to unencrypt the encryption key, and then the encryption key is held in memory unencrypted. Or maybe the encryption key is the same on all instances while encryption keys are different, but don't see why it would be needed. Or maybe there was a desire to rotate root keys without rotating the data. Not sure what the benefits would be though, as both keys likely have the same security strength. So, we are trying to make the usage more convenient but not make Vault less secure. > Today, a Shamir seal protects against a single admin slipping a modified Vault binary that allows them extra access onto a node, and restarting Vault to use it. (Whereas, auto-unseal does not, since the node can just auto-unseal.) Currently, the issue with the auto-unseal is that if something is wrong with the unseal authority, there is no fallback to something controlled by owners (e.g. Shamir keys holders). Obviously, there is a trade-off currently between using Shamir and auto-unseal. But if both methods were available at the same time, IMO the security wouldn't decrease. So we are comparing the proposed approach with the current auto-unseal. The issue with transit engine auto-unseal is that engines won't auto-unseal each other, because one engine should be up and running to unseal the other, the first one couldn't have been unsealed with the second one. So the only solution to this chicken-egg problem I see in multiple unseal options available at the same time. If an attacker has root access to the node, it can access RAM and retrieve the encryption key. So, we assume admins either don't have this possibility or are not considered a threat. As for tampering with the vault binary, what prevents copying the data and auto-unseal auth configs/secrets and using it with the new vault binary? Auto-unseal is currently assumed to be an acceptable option. There is enough unencrypted data stored with the vault to authenticate with remote HSM. So it wouldn't be worse if a vault instance stores unencrypted data to authenticate with another running vault instance. If it is desirable for instance to not have its own unseal key in the memory, we may have different unseal keys for different nodes. Basically, the idea is rough but probably doable unless we found why not. > The question, though, is whether HashiCorp would want to entertain that level of additional complexity in critical security code, to support a lesser security level for customers who wanted a different security/convenience tradeoff. I think it is first required to show there is really a lesser security level. >Meanwhile, there are some possible compromises you can make today to create different unseal behaviours using the currently available building blocks: > >1. You can just write the unseal key to disk unencrypted on the Vault nodes, and have a local wrapper script to inject it at startup. Very insecure, of course, but since we're discussing security for convenience, it seems worth mentioning. > >2. You can create a super-secure service of your own, and give it enough Vault key shares to unseal Vault, which it transmits to the Vault API on request, subject to the business logic of your choice. It's no small undertaking, obviously, but it does open up the option for you to implement whatever rules you want, around disclosing the unseal key. The first one renders away the encryption at rest. So, definitely not an option. The second one is probably not an option the way you mentioned it, as it is a single point of failure and potentially exposes a controlling set of Shamir keys to the single operator, or it is a vault by itself. One option I considered is a small very simple auto-unseal service that can hold a single Shamir key in memory. This would allow Shamir key holder to delegate their key to the trusted environment, controlled only by them. They start an instance, e.g. at their homes or on some different hosting providers, i.e. in the environment they have a high level of control and belief that multiple places won't be compromised at the same time. The service can do polling or some sort of an unseal request can be made from the vault cluster. A key holder can stop delegation by simply turning down the service. It is also ok for a single instance to be temporary down if there are enough other instances. But again, the preferable way would be auto-unseal with cloud provider with some sort of fallback possibility.

title: Agent hangs and doesn't refresh secret immediately
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
With renewable secrets with `max_ttl` set, sometimes the secrets expires while the agent is sleeping._x000D_
The agents wakes up after a while (could be hours after) and realize the lease doesn't exists and then refreshes the secret._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
Server:_x000D_
```_x000D_
wget https://github.com/exoscale/vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale/releases/download/v0.2.3/vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale_0.2.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz_x000D_
_x000D_
tar xvf vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale_0.2.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale_x000D_
_x000D_
rm vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale_0.2.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz_x000D_
_x000D_
vault server -dev -dev-root-token-id=root -dev-plugin-dir=$PWD_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Plugin:_x000D_
```_x000D_
export VAULT_ADDR='http://127.0.0.1:8200'_x000D_
export EXOSCALE_API_KEY='EXOb82f047a77d6af2563d83f81'_x000D_
export EXOSCALE_API_SECRET='(redacted)'_x000D_
VAULT_PLUGIN_SUM="$(sha256sum vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale | cut -d " " -f 1)"_x000D_
_x000D_
vault plugin register \_x000D_
	-sha256="${VAULT_PLUGIN_SUM}" \_x000D_
	-command=vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale \_x000D_
	secret vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale_x000D_
_x000D_
vault secrets enable -plugin-name="vault-plugin-secrets-exoscale" -path "exoscale" plugin_x000D_
_x000D_
vault write exoscale/config/root         \_x000D_
    root_api_key=${EXOSCALE_API_KEY}       \_x000D_
    root_api_secret=${EXOSCALE_API_SECRET} \_x000D_
    zone=ch-gva-2_x000D_
_x000D_
 vault write exoscale/role/list-only \_x000D_
	operations=list-zones \_x000D_
    ttl=10m \_x000D_
    max_ttl=30m_x000D_
_x000D_
vault read exoscale/apikey/list-only_x000D_
vault lease revoke exoscale/apikey/list-only/XXXX_x000D_
_x000D_
vault policy write "readsecret"  - <<EOF_x000D_
path "exoscale/apikey/list-only" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
EOF_x000D_
_x000D_
vault auth enable approle_x000D_
vault write auth/approle/role/my-role \_x000D_
    secret_id_ttl=240h \_x000D_
    token_num_uses=1000 \_x000D_
    token_ttl=240h \_x000D_
    token_max_ttl=240h \_x000D_
    secret_id_num_uses=1000 \_x000D_
    token_policies=readsecret_x000D_
_x000D_
vault read auth/approle/role/my-role/role-id -format=json | jq .data.role_id -r > role-id_x000D_
vault write -f auth/approle/role/my-role/secret-id -format=json | jq .data.secret_id -r > secret-id_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
agent.hcl:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
## Server_x000D_
vault {_x000D_
  address = "http://localhost:8200"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "unix" {_x000D_
  address      = "./vault-agent.socket"_x000D_
  tls_disable  = true_x000D_
  socket_mode  = "0600"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
## Authentication_x000D_
auto_auth {_x000D_
    method {_x000D_
        type      = "approle"_x000D_
        config = {_x000D_
            role_id_file_path = "./role-id"_x000D_
            secret_id_file_path = "./secret-id"_x000D_
            remove_secret_id_file_after_reading = false_x000D_
        }_x000D_
    }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
cache {_x000D_
    use_auto_auth_token = true_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
template {_x000D_
    destination      = "/home/antoine/iam.env"_x000D_
    perms            = "0640"_x000D_
_x000D_
    contents = <<EOH_x000D_
{{ with secret "exoscale/apikey/list-only" -}}_x000D_
EXOSCALE_API_KEY='{{ .Data.api_key }}'_x000D_
EXOSCALE_API_SECRET='(redacted)'_x000D_
{{ end }}_x000D_
EOH_x000D_
    error_on_missing_key = true_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Start the agent:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault agent -config ./agent.hcl -log-level=trace_x000D_
_x000D_
Wait (might take a few hours to trigger the issue):_x000D_
_x000D_
2022-07-20T07:27:08.574+0200 [WARN] vault.read(exoscale/apikey/list-only): failed to renew: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/leases/renew_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* lease not found_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The secret should be refreshed when we enter the 10-20% grace period._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`):_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.10.4 (6a1dde56c18c4a1be2756b931ce3c872d8ca5a76)_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux 5.4.x / Ubuntu 20.04 (focal) / amd64_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s): not relevant (can reproduce with the server started in `-dev` mode without a config file)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
We use `use_auto_auth_token = true` which automatically enable the caching, I suspect this is related to `LeaseCache`._x000D_
_x000D_

Freyert: To simplify the discussion so far I put together a flow diagram. There are 2 points where the Age header will be present and it currently is being ignored or there is no way to include the `Age` these are highlighted in orange. ```mermaid graph LR subgraph initProc miss[cache miss] --> fwd[forward request] fwd --> fill[insert cache entry]:::aged end subgraph renewProc renew:::aged --> calc calc[calculate grace period] --> sleep end fill --> renew sleep --> renew classDef aged fill:#f96; ``` ### Renew The main issue with renew is that we use a function from the `api` package that is ignorant of the `Age` header. There are worries that we need to know the original TTL + the Age in order to correctly calculate a grace period. https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/16439#issuecomment-1228495899 The math for calculating sleep: <details> <Summary> raw math jax </Summary> $$ remainingLease = \begin{cases} renewDisabled: loopStart + priorDuration - time.Now() \\ renewalFail: loopStart + leaseDuration - time.Now() \\ success: leaseDuration \end{cases} \\ minDuration = \begin{cases} (leaseDuration > increment) \land (increment > 0): increment \\ leaseDuration \end{cases} \\ grace = \begin{cases} minDuration \leq 0: 0 \\ 0.1 * leaseDuration + random \mod leaseDuration \end{cases} \\ sleepDuration = (remainingLease * 2/3) + (1/3 * gracePeriod) \\ sleepDuration = ((leaseDuration) * 2/3) + \\ (1/3 * 1/10 * (leaseDuratione) + \\ (random \mod (leaseDuration)) $$ If we modify the leaseDuration by subtracting Age. $$ sleepDuration = ((leaseDuration - Age) * 2/3) + \\ (1/3 * (1/10 * (leaseDuration - Age) + \\ (random \mod (leaseDuration - Age))) $$ </details> If we modify the TTL by the Age header. The Age value affects the equation too much. In the following example an age of 250 gives us a max sleepPeriod of 550. What we would want instead is for the max sleep period to be 733.33 - 250 = 483. | Original | Aged -- | -- | -- leaseDuration | 1000 | 750 Age | 0 | 250 gracePeriod | 200 | 150 sleepPeriod | 733.3333333 | 550 What we really want is to just subtract the `Age` from the sleep period. We need to modify [`type renewFunc(string, int) (*Secret, error)`](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/77189953922a4e6db44bd57e4d77470d8d25bdae/api/lifetime_watcher.go#L236) to be `type renewFunc(string, int) (*SendResponse, error)`. #### Grace Period Calculation [`lifetime_watcher.go#calculateGrace`](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/77189953922a4e6db44bd57e4d77470d8d25bdae/api/lifetime_watcher.go#L381) uses a pretty simple calculation to identify the gracePeriod. Paired with the grace period is the _sleep_ duration. The sleep duration is 2/3 of the total lease + 1/3 of the grace period ([lifetime_watcher.go#L356](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/77189953922a4e6db44bd57e4d77470d8d25bdae/api/lifetime_watcher.go#L356)). ### Fresh This one is a bit easier because we have access to the Age header. [`leas_cache.go#Send`](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/command/agent/cache/lease_cache.go#L213) works entirely with raw requests and therefore has access to the age header. The only change that would be required here is to modify the cache index's [`LastRenewed`](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/command/agent/cache/lease_cache.go#L304) date to incorporate the `Age`.

When an operator/admin configures a `max_ttl`, that's the maximum ttl that can ever be reached for a lease, regardless of how many times a secret is renewed. Once that max_ttl is reached, even if the secret 'claims' to be renewable it can't be, and you'd have to create (re-lease) an entirely new secret. `Age` (header): When using Vault Agent as a (caching) proxy to Vault, we cache the responses that Agent receives from Vault. When the response is returned to the calling client, Vault Agent will augment that response (where appropriate) with an `Age` header to let the client know how long that response has been in the cache. The ttl within the cached response isn't adjusted, and the client would need to decide how it wanted to handle the information it's been given in totality. We're wondering if this might have caused some confusion. Having reviewed the thread and attempted to reproduce, we can’t really tell what the problem is. Perhaps the secret has reached its max TTL, can’t be renewed, but the age headers are difficult to interpret. Perhaps there’s a bug where under some circumstances renewal is failing. Maybe there’s a problem somewhere else. Being able to either write a failing test or providing simpler reproduction steps would help us confirm specifically what the problematic behavior is. Without one of those, we’ve reached the limits of this investigation and will need to move on to other items. To @Freyert's point, we understand this isn't trivial - we weren't able to do this in a way that demonstrated unexpected behavior. It seems like @7fELF and @Freyert have identified similar but slightly different issues, and keeping them separate from each other would help rather than hinder our future investigations. To reduce confusion and to represent that we've reached the end of our current investigation, I'm going to close this issue, and ask for new GitHub issues reflecting specific problems with associated reproduction steps.

title: pki: can't issue a valid cross-signed certificate if vault was too old (SKID calculation)
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
If you issue an intermediate certificate with vault version <1.10, then upgrade vault to >1.11 to create another cross-signed intermediate (as said in https://learn.hashicorp.com/tutorials/vault/pki-engine#step-8-create-a-cross-signed-intermediate) using old one's key as key_ref - old leaf certificates won't verify using new cross-signed intermediate (as they should), as SKID will differ between them (but pubkey will be the same)_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
0. Start vault with version <1.10_x000D_
1. Create root pki_x000D_
`vault mount -path=pki -max-lease-ttl=87600h pki`_x000D_
2. Generate cert_x000D_
`vault write pki/root/generate/internal common_name="Root CA" ttl=87600h key_bits=4096`_x000D_
3. Create intermediate pki_x000D_
`vault secrets enable -path=pki_int -max-lease-ttl=43800h pki`_x000D_
4. Generate CSR_x000D_
`vault write pki_int/intermediate/generate/internal     common_name="Int CA"     ttl=43800h     key_bits=4096  | jq -r '.data.csr' | tee csr_int_old.csr_x000D_
` _x000D_
5. Sign it using root ca_x000D_
`vault write -format=json pki/root/sign-intermediate     csr=@csr_int_old.csr     common_name="Int CA"     ttl=43800h |  jq -r '.data.certificate' | tee ca_int_old.crt`_x000D_
6. Import it_x000D_
`vault write pki_int/intermediate/set-signed     certificate=@ca_int_old.crt`_x000D_
7. Create a role_x000D_
`vault write pki_int/roles/test     key_bits=2048     max_ttl=8760h     client_flag=true     key_usage="DigitalSignature",     ou="Test"     organization="Test"     country="TT"     require_cn=true     enforce_hostnames=false     allow_glob_domains=true     allow_bare_domains=true     server_flag=true     allow_any_name=true_x000D_
`_x000D_
8. Issue a certificate_x000D_
`vault write -format=json pki_int/issue/test     common_name='Leaf'     ttl=100h     format=pem     | tee >( jq -r '.data.certificate' > leaf_cert_old.crt)`_x000D_
9. Stop vault, upgrade to >1.11, start vault_x000D_
10. Rotate root pki_x000D_
`vault write -format=json pki/root/rotate/internal     common_name="Root CA"     issuer_name="root-2052"     ttl=262800h     key_bits=4096`_x000D_
11. Issue cross-signed csr, using old intermediate ca as key_ref_x000D_
`KEY_ID=$(vault read  -format=json pki_int/issuer/<uuid> | jq -r ".data.key_id")_x000D_
vault write -format=json pki_int/intermediate/cross-sign       common_name="Int CA"       ttl=262700h       key_ref="${KEY_ID}"       | jq -r '.data.csr' | tee csr_int_new.csr`_x000D_
12. Sign it using new root ca_x000D_
`vault write -format=json pki/issuer/root-2052/sign-intermediate       common_name="Int CA"       ttl=262600h       csr=@csr_int_new.csr       | jq -r '.data.certificate' | tee ca_int_new.crt`_x000D_
13. (optional) Import it_x000D_
`vault write pki_int/intermediate/set-signed     certificate=@ca_int_new.crt`_x000D_
14. (optional) Set new default for pki_int (or issue using :issuer)_x000D_
`vault write pki_int/root/replace default=<new_uuid>`_x000D_
15. (optional) Issue new leaf cert_x000D_
`vault write -format=json pki_int/issue/test     common_name='Leaf'     ttl=100h     format=pem     | tee >( jq -r '.data.certificate' > leaf_cert_new.crt)`_x000D_
16. Verify old leaf with new ca - it will fail_x000D_
`openssl verify -verbose -partial_chain -CAfile ca_int_new.crt leaf_cert_old.crt`_x000D_
(you can export root ca for full bundle - it doesn't matter in this case)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Old leaf certificate can be verified using new cross-signed CA_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
Old vault was version 1.0.0, updated it to 1.11.0_x000D_
```Key                    Value_x000D_
Seal Type              shamir_x000D_
Initialized            true_x000D_
Sealed                 false_x000D_
Total Shares           9_x000D_
Threshold              2_x000D_
Version                1.11.0_x000D_
Build Date             2022-06-17T15:48:44Z_x000D_
Storage Type           etcd_x000D_
```_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Version 1.10 changed GetSubjKeyID function (and added getSubjectKeyID), so we had to rollback it for us to issue a vaild certificate - https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/compare/main...melazyk:vault:vault-skid-patch_x000D_

top_3_comments_text: averche: Hi @Dentrax! We've discussed this request internally and we think that adding an `"upsert"` option to the Patch method could lead to potentially non-standard UX. The Patch method internally translates into a `PATCH` request, which [traditionally](https://restfulapi.net/http-methods/#patch) only modifies an existing resource and returns a 404 error if the resource is not found. Adding the "upsert" functionality would make `Patch` function as a mixture of `PATCH` and `PUT`. The code example you posted above is a good way to achieve the upsert behaviour. title: Cluster initialization hangs with retry_join
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I set up a 3 nodes Vault cluster (only servers) with the integrated raft storage backend. With `retry_join` stanza in configuration._x000D_
_x000D_
Since version 1.11.1, the cluster doesn't initialize properly. Only the first node is initialized, the other nodes hangs because they havent find an available leader early, and they do not retry infinitely (Only 2 times), waiting for the first node to be initialized. _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run a vault agents on 3 VMs _x000D_
2. Run `vault init` on the first node_x000D_
3. Run `vault unseal` on the first node_x000D_
4. Wait for the other nodes to be initialized (it fails here, only the first node is initialized)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
At the step 3, all three nodes of the cluster should be initialized, and nodes 2 and 3 could be unsealed next._x000D_
In orther words, nodes 2 and 3 should always retry to join the cluster for the initialization process. Not only 2 times._x000D_
_x000D_
**Possible workaround**_x000D_
After the first node is initilized, restarting vault agents on nodes 2 and 3 will succesfully terminate the cluster initialization. This is because we are forcing the retry join with a vault agent restart. And at this time, the first node is initialized and unsealed, so it's a leader available to init other nodes._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.11.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.11.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 22.04_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I've tested with vault `v1.11.0` and I do not experiment this issue. It's seems that the last security patch has introduced this issue._x000D_

There are some low level changes we're contemplating making that would make this impossible, but until then we ought to make KV handle half-deleted keys better. We could also delete the key versions from oldest to newest instead of in random order, so that an interrupted delete is less likely to have deleted the current version. > cause the respective secret to become permanently broken and vault to only return: Does this impact `DELETE secret/metadata/xyz` as well, or can you fix the problem by re-running the delete? > We saw this issue the first time a couple of days after raising the max_versions from the default 10 to 100, but I'm not sure whether this is related or just coincidence. title: Digital signature endpoint for PKI engines
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We are using Vault to deliver certificates for  mTLS in several services in a multitenant environment. For that we create a PKI engine for each tenant to avoid  interoperability between tenants._x000D_
_x000D_
Now we have the requirement to create digital signatures to avoid interoperability between tenants for some specific documents/data. Having a PKI for each tenant, it's quite straightforward to think about these pkis to sign the documents._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
As long as Vault implements PKI engines where we have a private key and a public key (certificacte) it would be great to offer the option to sign data with pki engines. Something similar to data encryotion._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
New PKI engine endpoint, something similar to_x000D_
_x000D_
| Method | Path                 | Signer                                                             |_x000D_
|--------|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|_x000D_
| POST   | /pki/data/sign/:name | Private key of PKI applying rules defined in role with name `name` |_x000D_
_x000D_
##### Parameters:_x000D_
name (path): the digital signature role where we define for example supported signature algorithms_x000D_
data_base64 (body): data to be signed_x000D_
algorithm (body): Signature algorithm to be used. Must be one of the supported algorithms defined in the role_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
The alternative if we want to use these PKIs is to store private key (from CA or a child pk) as secret and retrieve it to sign data. That's not so good  from security point of view.  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: cipherboy: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/3845 is very similar conceptually and likely how we'll implement this: Vault's PKI engine is a X509 CA PKI engine, not a X509 Leaf PKI engine, and will likely never support the latter types of operations. This data signature is something we'd like to support eventually, but its more likely to appear in Transit.

title: Okta login should set Client Request Context to enable stronger authentication security
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Vault doesn't but should set [Client Request Context](https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/core-okta-api/#client-request-context) for Okta login._x000D_
_x000D_
Okta evaluate various security policy with input from [Client Request Context](https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/core-okta-api/#client-request-context) (user-agent, IP, device fingerprint), which is set by a Okta broker client, (vault in this case) through HTTP headers. Okta strongly encourages to set those header so that threatInsight, and security policy can be properly evaluated to protect the user. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
1) Forward User-Agent from client User-Agent string,_x000D_
2) Set X-Forwarded-For header with client IP chain (client request X-Forwarded-For + client IP)_x000D_
3) Set X-Device-Fingerprint header with value calculated follow [Okta guide](https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/api/authn/#device-fingerprint-best-practices)_x000D_
4) Update document to inform users about the option to configure [Okta Trusted Proxy IP](https://developer.okta.com/docs/reference/core-okta-api/#ip-address)_x000D_

title: Delete service principal credential on azure/rotate-root
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
An application registration on Azure may have application password or service principal password or both. Both types of password can be used successfully as `client_secret` in the following Vault CLI command:_x000D_
_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
vault write azure/config use_microsoft_graph_api=true \_x000D_
                         tenant_id="$TENANT_ID" subscription_id="$SUBSCRIPTION_ID" \_x000D_
                         client_id="$CLIENT_ID" client_secret=- <<< "$SECRET"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
In a command like this, we specify the application ID of the application object as the `client_id`. But for the `client_secret` value, we may specify either an application credential or a service principal credential. If we then perform `vault write -f azure/rotate-root`, Vault does not delete the service principal credential and instead adds a new application credential._x000D_
_x000D_
Note: The `vault write -f azure/rotate-root` operation works fine without any surprises if we use an application password (i.e., the password directly belongs to the application object) to configure Vault's Azure secrets engine. The behaviour described above occurs only when we use a service principal password (i.e., the password belongs to the service principal object associated with the application object) to configure the Azure secrets engine._x000D_
_x000D_
Here are the steps to reproduce the behaviour described above. These steps require `az` and `jq` commands to be present:_x000D_
_x000D_
 1. Log into Azure using Azure CLI:_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```sh_x000D_
    az login_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
 2. Run the following shell script to create a new application named `foo-app` and its underlying service principal (SP) object along with a password each for the application object and the service principal object:_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```sh_x000D_
    set -ex_x000D_
    APP_ID=$(az ad app create --display-name foo-app | jq -r .appId)_x000D_
    az ad sp create --id "$APP_ID"_x000D_
    az ad app credential reset --id "$APP_ID"_x000D_
    az ad sp credential reset --id "$APP_ID"_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
    Copy the app ID, app password, and the SP password from the output and keep them handy. They will be needed in steps 4 and 7 below._x000D_
_x000D_
 3. Run the following commands to confirm that the `foo-app` application has an application password as well as a service principal password:_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```sh_x000D_
    set -ex_x000D_
    NAME=foo-app_x000D_
    APP_ID=$(az ad app list --display-name "$NAME" | jq -r '.[0].appId')_x000D_
    az ad app credential list --id "$APP_ID"_x000D_
    az ad sp credential list --id "$APP_ID"_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
 4. For good measure, double-check that indeed either application password or service principal password can be used to log into Azure with this script:_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```sh_x000D_
    set -ex_x000D_
    TENANT_ID=_x000D_
    APP_ID=_x000D_
    APP_SECRET=_x000D_
    SPN_SECRET=_x000D_
    az login --service-principal --allow-no-subscriptions -t "$TENANT_ID" -u "$APP_ID" -p "$APP_SECRET"_x000D_
    az login --service-principal --allow-no-subscriptions -t "$TENANT_ID" -u "$APP_ID" -p "$SPN_SECRET"_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
    Before running the script above, set the four variables at the top to appropriate values. The `APP_SECRET` should be set to the application password. The `SPN_SECRET` should be set to the service principal password._x000D_
_x000D_
 5. Go to https://portal.azure.com/ > Azure AD roles and administrators > Application Administrator > Add assignments. Then search for `foo-app`. Click the Add button. This completes the role assignment for `foo-app` needed to perform step 7 below._x000D_
_x000D_
 6. Start Vault server in development mode:_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```sh_x000D_
    vault server -dev_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
 7. Now run the following script after setting the four variables at the top with appropriate values:_x000D_
_x000D_
    ```sh_x000D_
    set -x_x000D_
_x000D_
    TENANT_ID=_x000D_
    SUBSCRIPTION_ID=_x000D_
    APP_ID=_x000D_
    SPN_SECRET=_x000D_
_x000D_
    export VAULT_ADDR='http://127.0.0.1:8200'_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault secrets enable azure_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write azure/config tenant_id="$TENANT_ID" subscription_id="$SUBSCRIPTION_ID" client_id="$APP_ID" client_secret=- use_microsoft_graph_api=true <<< "$SPN_SECRET"_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write -f azure/rotate-root_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
    The `SPN_SECRET` variable should be set to the service principal password (not the application password)._x000D_
_x000D_
 8. Now wait for 2-3 minutes for Azure to attain eventual consistency w.r.t. to the credentials._x000D_
_x000D_
 9. Now run the script in step 3 again. The output should show that while there is a new application password now, the service principal password created in step 2 is still intact._x000D_
_x000D_
I believe the behaviour described above occurs because Vault only resets application credential (not service principal credential) during the `azure/rotate-root` operation._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
It would be ideal if Vault deletes the service principal password, especially, when the Vault secrets engine is configured with the service principal password. This would ensure that the root secret used to configure Vault does not keep lying around._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
If the solution proposed in the previous section cannot be accomplished, then it would be nice to update the documentation at https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/secrets/azure to clarify that the client secret used to configure the Azure secrets engine (i.e., the root secret) must be an application credential, not a service principal credential, if we want the root secret to be deleted automatically on `azure/rotate-root`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
Azure secrets engine's `azure/rotate-root` operation seems to work without surprises only if Azure secrets engine is configured with an application password. However, it is possible in practice that a Vault admin configures the Azure secrets engine with a service principal password as the root secret._x000D_
_x000D_
For example, the Terraform [azuread_service_principal_password](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azuread/latest/docs/resources/service_principal_password) block creates a password that belongs to the service principal object (not the application object). A Vault administrator may end up configuring Vault's Azure secrets engine with this service principal password. Now when they perform the `azure/rotate-root` operation, they would be mistaken if they believe that the root secret (service principal password) has been deleted. Since the root secret still remains intact after `azure/rotate-root`, I believe this area needs to be taken a closer look at and either handled appropriately or clarified in the documentation.

AWS Secrets Engine does not remove the created IAM User in case the user has a login-profile (needed for web based management console access). _x000D_

title: LDAP UPNDomain option only works correctly if LDAP is Microsoft AD
body_text:
Hey there!_x000D_
_x000D_
I'm currently playing with LDAP and Kerberos in vault, and I've run into an issue. Basically, while the LDAP backend supports looking up the UPN, it assumes that the attribute the UPN is stored in is called `userPrincipalName` - however, that is only guaranteed to be the case if the LDAP happens to be Microsoft Active Directory. Given that LDAP schemas are not that well standardized across vendors, I believe this should be configurable, just like e.g. `groupattr`._x000D_
_x000D_
I checked the code at https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/sdk/helper/ldaputil/client.go#L269-L273, where the attribute is indeed hardcoded:_x000D_
```_x000D_
func (c *Client) GetUserDN(cfg *ConfigEntry, conn Connection, bindDN, username string) (string, error) {_x000D_
	userDN := ""_x000D_
	if cfg.UPNDomain != "" {_x000D_
		// Find the distinguished name for the user if userPrincipalName used for login_x000D_
		filter := fmt.Sprintf("(userPrincipalName=%s@%s)", EscapeLDAPValue(username), cfg.UPNDomain)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Unless there are specific reasons to do otherwise, I can just quickly raise a PR to add a config option to make this configurable.

title: Better handling of consul tokens for service_discovery
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When using vault to derive all consul tokens in an environment, you can't realistically use vault to derive the consul token that vault uses to register itself with.  This annoyingly breaks automatic bootstrapping._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
The cleanest possible way to fix this would be to extend the consul service_discovery to allow specifying a path in vault to retrieve the credentials from.  Baring that, making the token a field that is reloadable, rather than requiring the server to restart which seals it would also be an acceptable fix._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I considered using vault-agent to put the service registration in consul's config directory where it would be auto-loaded and then vault winds up in consul that way, but vault has some additional signaling logic that sets the active/standby labels and handles the TTL based health check._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
As the Hashicorp team focuses more and more effort on the Raft backend and less and less on the Consul one, it is important to not break existing users that are relying heavily on Consul service discovery to point services such as Nomad at the active vault node._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I've been poking at this for a while and have the whole thing working with a vault-agent that writes the service_discovery config into vault's config dir and restarts vault, but this obviously results in vault being sealed, and then when the token rotates, vault just keeps getting sealed.  Ideally I'd like to have a better option for setting up vault service registration.

title: Vault doesn't support the correctly named tls_cipher_suites TLS_ECDHE_*_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When specifying the TLS cipher suites `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` and `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` as specified in [RFC7905](https://www.iana.org/assignments/tls-parameters/tls-parameters.xml), Vault fails to start with an "unsupported cipher" error._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Set the tcp listener to use the above cipher suites:_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
..._x000D_
  tls_cipher_suites = "TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256"_x000D_
..._x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
and you will see an error such as_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
error loading configuration from /etc/vault/config.hcl: error parsing 'listener': listeners.0 invalid value for tls_cipher_suites: unsupported cipher "TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should start up with the above ciphers._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.11.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.11.2_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Centos 7_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
This bug happens because Go used to incorrectly list the ciphers without the `_SHA256` suffix, which must have carried over to the library Vault uses to look up the cipher: https://github.com/hashicorp/go-secure-stdlib/blob/1b80d53b4662d4b15ea0c23754dd81e3ae21d58b/tlsutil/tlsutil.go#L27. _x000D_
_x000D_
The golang git issue that brought it up is here: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/32061, and it was fixed in this commit: https://github.com/golang/go/commit/e2cac315082a9267135e96249b537d0bd0703175. _x000D_
_x000D_
I found this since the [docs state to look at the Go code to find which cipher suites are supported](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/configuration/listener/tcp#tls_cipher_suites), which does include the `TLS_ECDHE_*_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305` cipher suites: https://go.dev/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go _x000D_
_x000D_
The workaround is to not include the `_SHA256` suffix in the `tls_cipher_suites` listener config, in which case Vault does correctly start._x000D_

title: Race condition preventing Vault from joining quorum
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
We deploy Vault on AWS:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. We use AWSKMS to auto unseal_x000D_
2. A new Vault joins with no raft data to replace old Vault (immutable infrastructure)_x000D_
3. We set autopilot config as `Cleanup Dead Servers=true`, `Last Contact Threshold=10s` and `Dead Server Last Contact Threshold=10s`_x000D_
4. Our raft data is about 500MB_x000D_
_x000D_
There are about 20%~30% of the time, when a new Vault instance starts up, it fails to join the Raft quorum. Even restarting the process won't make it rejoin._x000D_
_x000D_
Checking our server log, we found that:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Auto unseal runs [every 5 seconds](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/0d6a42c79ef765e919db486c1cb78e527b47e010/command/server.go#L2607)_x000D_
2. The brand new Vault server managed to join the raft, then it installed snapshot from the leader during initialization. When the raft snapshot is big, it takes more than 5 seconds to transfer the data. So the Vault got unsealed by the second run of auto unseal, which is 10s._x000D_
3. During the initialization, the new Vault does not send any heartbeat. So exactly at 10s, the leader thought new Vault is dead and removed it from raft._x000D_
4. Depends on whether step 2/3 happens first, the new Vault will either join the quorum, or become a dead node._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Configure Vault with AWSKMS auto unseal_x000D_
2. Configure autopilot `Cleanup Dead Servers=true`, `Last Contact Threshold=4s` and `Dead Server Last Contact Threshold=4s`, so the leader will kick new node out before the first auto unseal._x000D_
3. Join a new node to the quorum._x000D_
4. The new node failed to join the quorum._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
The leader should not consider a new follower that is installing snapshot as a dead node._x000D_
_x000D_
This can be fixed by either _x000D_
- Follower sending heartbeats during the snapshot installation._x000D_
- Follower be removed from quorum first, install snapshot and unseal, then rejoin the quorum._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.10.3+ent_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`):_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture:

title: Vault UI ingress can't be configured when HA is enabled - need better documentation on how to do that

title: Help output should go to STDOUT
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault help should be written to STDOUT, not STDERR._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Don't work (and should)._x000D_
$ vault -h | less_x000D_
$ vault read -h | most_x000D_
$ vault write -h | view -_x000D_
_x000D_
Workaround._x000D_
$ vault -h 2>&1 | less_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
To be able to view help in pager without having to redirect STDERR._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
vault v1.11.2, Linux_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Standard CLI behavior is to output help on STDOUT when requested as it is not an error._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: cipherboy: Interestingly, while [GNU standards do say this](https://www.gnu.org/prep/standards/html_node/_002d_002dhelp.html) (see: `on standard output`), non-GNU programs like `openssl` and others consistently write help to stderr. As such, this is probably not a bug, but a feature request. In the past, it seems like there might've been an intent to allow users to customize this behavior via `RunCustom`, but I don't see any existing options to do so. From the core shared CLI code, it does support setting it to your choice of writer: https://github.com/mitchellh/cli/blob/25f4c7ceb617dfe9729b3ff32be02f7544ff7fb4/cli.go#L119-L123 but Vault explicitly overrides this: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/d46c655e6ed34da5030c46a78ee2862e7989e6be/command/main.go#L231 But its not clear as to what motivated this as no RunOpts support to configure CLI output behavior and nobody consumes this helper outside of the tests. It was at a time before `ErrorWriter` existed in cli... Regardless, I'm inclined to believe this is a breaking change and probably needs more discussion; existing scripts may break based on this behavior. | eikenb: The reason why I filed this as a bug is that the behavior is bad, particularly with long help output like many hashicorp products have. It is bad UX to have to redirect STDERR every time you want to pipe the help to a pager so you can read it using software intended for that purpose instead of having to rely on scrollback buffers. To put it more in terms of a feature... help to STDOUT lets you pipe it to a pager for easy reading providing a better UX. Help going to STDERR has no advantages and has a worse UX. Help would be better going to STDOUT. | cipherboy: Oh, I definitely agree with you, but at this point, Vault has had this behavior for N>5 years. This is something that is probably baked into the assumptions of scripts and other automation systems at this point. I worry that the only way this gets accepted is with an environment variable change (like what occurred with detailed LIST behavior #15417 or is also occurring with 404 not found/#14944's solution). _Maybe_ it gets in with interactive TTY detection, but...

As such, this is probably not a bug, but a feature request. In the past, it seems like there might've been an intent to allow users to customize this behavior via `RunCustom`, but I don't see any existing options to do so. From the core shared CLI code, it does support setting it to your choice of writer: https://github.com/mitchellh/cli/blob/25f4c7ceb617dfe9729b3ff32be02f7544ff7fb4/cli.go#L119-L123 but Vault explicitly overrides this: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/d46c655e6ed34da5030c46a78ee2862e7989e6be/command/main.go#L231 But its not clear as to what motivated this as no RunOpts support to configure CLI output behavior and nobody consumes this helper outside of the tests. It was at a time before `ErrorWriter` existed in cli... Regardless, I'm inclined to believe this is a breaking change and probably needs more discussion; existing scripts may break based on this behavior.
eikenb: The reason why I filed this as a bug is that the behavior is bad, particularly with long help output like many hashicorp products have. It is bad UX to have to redirect STDERR every time you want to pipe the help to a pager so you can read it using software intended for that purpose instead of having to rely on scrollback buffers. To put it more in terms of a feature... help to STDOUT lets you pipe it to a pager for easy reading providing a better UX. Help going to STDERR has no advantages and has a worse UX. Help would be better going to STDOUT.
cipherboy: Oh, I definitely agree with you, but at this point, Vault has had this behavior for N>5 years. This is something that is probably baked into the assumptions of scripts and other automation systems at this point. I worry that the only way this gets accepted is with an environment variable change (like what occurred with detailed LIST behavior #15417 or is also occurring with 404 not found/#14944's solution). _Maybe_ it gets in with interactive TTY detection, but...
eikenb: I agree that backwards compatibility is **very** important, but changing explicitly called help output should not impact automation as automation doesn't call help. IMO the UX benefit is enough to overcome the *remote* chance that help output automation is part of a critical path. Not my call though and I appreciate your considering it. Thanks.
cipherboy: Ah I see, the `HelpWriter` is strictly used for a case when `-help` exists on flags given to the program. `ErrorWriter` is used when Help is printed as part of Usage (i.e., bad flags, the case I was mostly worried about -- if we have bad flags and we print the help to stdout suddenly rather than stderr, that'd be bad). In that sense, I think I'm fine fixing this. I'll propose a PR.

**Vault with Integrated Storage: nodes unable to join the cluster after being stopped**_x000D_
We are testing Integrated Storage for Vault server. We setup test cluster using `docker-compose` with 5 containers connected by Docker network . We configured the cluster to removed dead server after 10s timeout and we shut down one of the nodes. The affected node gets ejected from the cluster as expected. However, when we start it and unseal it, it doesn't join the cluster._x000D_
_x000D_
The only way we were able to attach affected node to the cluster was by stopping Vault server, removing directory containing Vault files and starting Vault server again. In this case, ufter unsealing the node joins the cluster._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Setup test cluster with 5 servers or containers running Vault_x000D_
2. Start 1st Vault server, initiate it, note the root token and unseal key_x000D_
3. Unseal 1st Vault server_x000D_
4. On each of remaining 4 nodes or containers start and unseal Vault server_x000D_
5. Run `vault operator raft list-peers` to confirm 5 nodes in cluster, the leader and voter status of all nodes_x000D_
6. Configure Raft Autopilot:_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
   vault operator raft autopilot set-config \_x000D_
    -dead-server-last-contact-threshold=10 \_x000D_
    -server-stabilization-time=30 \_x000D_
    -cleanup-dead-servers=true \_x000D_
    -min-quorum=3_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
7. Select one of the Vault servers and stop it, wait until it is removed from list of Raft peers_x000D_
8. Start previously stopped Vault server and unseal it._x000D_
9. The server does not join the cluster_x000D_
10. Run command:_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
   vault operator raft join http://<leader_ip>:8200_x000D_

_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
We expected the restarted server to join cluster back after stabilization period of 30 seconds per Raft Autopilot configuration command in p.6_x000D_
_x000D_
Are we missing something here?_x000D_

raskchanky: The dead server last contact threshold can not be reset, which is why we recommend setting it to a high value. After that amount of time has elapsed, that node is considered dead and gone forever to Vault, never to return. As you've found, the only way of getting past that is by clearing the data directory and re-joining. The reason why that works is because by clearing the data directory, you've made it look like a brand new node to the raft cluster. I'm not sure if this will be helpful or not, but I'll attempt to lay out a sort of timeline for when a node comes up, and how autopilot sees it. When a Vault node first joins a raft cluster via the `vault operator raft join` command, it's added to the raft configuration immediately. After that, it and the leader node do a bit of handshaking and the leader node sends the newly joined node a raft snapshot to apply. Generating that snapshot, sending it over the network, receiving it, and applying it can take a bit of time. Once the newly joined node finishes applying the snapshot, it starts heartbeating to the leader, but this is a separate heartbeat from the raft one - it's Vault specific. If the time it takes to start heartbeating exceeds the dead server last contact threshold, autopilot will remove the newly added node before it ever has a chance to participate in the cluster. Once the new node has applied the raft snapshot, and is heartbeating, autopilot will consider the node unstable, and keep it as a non-voter. Once the node has been healthy from autopilot's perspective for at least the server stabilization time value, then autopilot considers the node stable, and promotes it to be a voter (unless it was started as a permanent non-voter). If the last contact threshold elapses without receiving a heartbeat, autopilot will consider the node unhealthy and demote it from voter to non-voter status. This is reversible though, as long as the heartbeat comes back before the dead server last contact threshold has elapsed. Assuming it does come back quickly enough, autopilot will promote the node back to voter status after the server stabilization time has elapsed. If the heartbeat doesn't come back quickly enough, and dead server last contact threshold elapses without a heartbeat, that node is permanently removed, which is not reversible (without destroying the data directory). In addition to the last contact threshold for specifying gaps in between heartbeats, there's also the max trailing logs configurable, which specifies how many raft logs behind the leader followers can be before they're considered unhealthy. Healthy/unhealthy from autopilot's perspective is mostly about voting/non-voting, up to the point where autopilot considers the node dead for good. Is that helpful? Dorra-B: In fact, the main problem is that 127.0.0.1:8200 is used by another process. Maybe vault.service is up and running and it is using the 8200 port. 1. `$ sudo systemctl stop vault.service` 2. `$ vault server -dev -dev-listen-address="1x.2xx.1xx.1xx:8200` This should work. If there is still the same error message , you have to do the following: 1. `$ netstat -a |grep 8200` If there is a port 8200 used, you have just to kill the process using it, so vault can take advantage of it: 2. `$ ps aux ` This command will show all the running processes where each has its own USER identified, CPU, PID, etc 3. `$ ps aux |grep 8200` This command will show the process using the port you need to set free, keep in mind the PID of the process XZY (usually in the second column from the left) 4. `$ kill -XZY pid` This command will Kill the process with pid 5. try `$ vault server -dev -dev-listen-address="1x.2xx.1xx.1xx:8200`
aphorise: > `$ vault server -dev -dev-listen-address="1x.2xx.1xx.1xx:8200` IMO - it's better to have all settings (specific or all encompassing `0.0.0.0`) only via the configuration file and using the listener stanza therein; this way changes and explicit bind values are more evident than having them set explicitly via launch (eg: systemd unit file). title: MySQL backend HA lock discuss
body_text:
I'm not sure where to post this discussion, so I posted it here._x000D_
_x000D_
Now, mysql backend have 2 classes related to HA lock, `MySQLHALock` and `MySQLLock`. They both establish mysql connections. _x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/81225745735ddb0ed36f5ea0ff9020672d2e2339/physical/mysql/mysql.go#L540-L555_x000D_
In `MySQLHALock`, it will run query every 5 seconds to check if leadership changed._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/81225745735ddb0ed36f5ea0ff9020672d2e2339/physical/mysql/mysql.go#L698_x000D_
But in `MySQLLock`, no query at all. Only try to get the lock, and update the `vault_lock` table after got lock successfully. That means, once the node got the leadership, the connection established by `MySQLLock` won't run any query unitl idle connection timeout. But on the other side, the connection established by `MySQLHALock` will query every 5 seconds._x000D_
_x000D_
Can we use one connection for both `MySQLHALock` and `MySQLLock`? So the leadership won't lost due to idle connection timeout.

_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When creating a password policy, it is possible to use `/` characters in the name. This allows a password policy to be placed at `/sys/policies/password/path/to/policy`, for example. However, `list` operation is only allowed on the endpoint `sys/policies/password`, and this produces an output of `path/`, which does not show the place the policy is stored. If you attempt to `list` on `sys/policies/password/path`, an unsupported operation error is returned. This creates a scenario where it is impossible to find all created password policies via the API._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Start a development server, i.e. `vault server -dev -dev-root-token-id=root` and set VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN_x000D_
2. Run `vault write sys/policies/password/path/to/policy @valid-payload.json`_x000D_
3. Run `vault list sys/policies/password`_x000D_
4. Run `vault list sys/policies/password/path`_x000D_
5. See error_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Either the sub-paths should support a list operation, OR password policies should not allow `/` characters to be provided._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: 1.11.3_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version: 1.11.3_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: MacOS Monterey 12.5.1_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
- None, reproducible in DEV server mode._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I tend to appreciate the ability to sort/organize things into folders, so I personally would prefer the outcome that `list` is supported on sub-paths here, but either resolution would result in a more consistent Vault API experience._x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
One of the integration tests for HVAC caught an issue introduced in Vault 1.11 (hvac/hvac#858). A POST to the configure endpoint for the Kubernetes auth method with [`token_reviewer_jwt`](https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/auth/kubernetes#token_reviewer_jwt) as a invalid JWT produces a different error message. Normally, errors due to screen scraping exception messages would be shrugged off and updated, but the new error message appears to be from `square/go-jose`, a library that's used by Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
1 error occurred:_x000D_
        * square/go-jose: compact JWS format must have three parts_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I'm not sure if this is expected. I've typically believed that it's bad practice to leak errors from internal libraries in API error messages, but I would also say that this error message is a little more descriptive. I'll defer to the Vault team to close this issue if this is intended behavior._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
The unit test that consistently reproduces this issue can be found with the link below:_x000D_
_x000D_

```_x000D_

```_x000D_

_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Start up a dev Vault server_x000D_
2. Enable the kubernetes auth method_x000D_

_x000D_

_x000D_

title: PROXY protocol listener with `deny_unauthorized` silently closes after a non-authorized request
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
A TCP listener configured with `proxy_protocol_behavior = "deny_unauthorize"` silently closes after receiving a request originating from an IP not listed within the `proxy_protocol_authorized_addrs` list._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run a vault server with the configuration provided below: `vault server -config=config.hcl`_x000D_
2. Validate that the service is running and bound to the expected port: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/health` / `ss -tlpn | grep 8200`_x000D_
3. Perform a query against the Vault server using an IP address not contained within the `proxy_protocol_authorized_addrs` list. In my case, `curl http://192.168.1.20:8200/v1/sys/health`_x000D_
4. Validate that the request was not serviced and the listener is no longer active: `ss -tlpn | grep 8200`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Either:_x000D_
1. Anything to log an error saying that the listener closed and why_x000D_
1. For the listener to reject the connection and carry on with listening_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): `Vault v1.11.3 (17250b25303c6418c283c95b1d5a9c9f16174fe8), built 2022-08-26T10:27:10Z`_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): `Vault v1.11.3 (17250b25303c6418c283c95b1d5a9c9f16174fe8), built 2022-08-26T10:27:10Z`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: OpenSUSE Tumbleweed x86_64_x000D_
_x000D_
Of note, the above environment is my home lab and reflects the simple configuration testing done/described in this issue. The problem was originally discovered in a production testing environment using a three node cluster of Ubuntu 18.04 nodes running Vault 1.11.1 from within Docker containers._x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
storage "file" {_x000D_
  path = "/tmp/vault/data"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address                         = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
  tls_disable                     = true_x000D_
  proxy_protocol_behavior         = "deny_unauthorized"_x000D_
  proxy_protocol_authorized_addrs = "127.0.0.1"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
log_level  = "trace"_x000D_
log_format = "json"_x000D_
ui         = false_x000D_
_x000D_
disable_mlock = true_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
This took me quite a long time to wrap my head around due to our configuration in the production testing environment, so there are a couple interesting bits I picked up along the way._x000D_
1. This behavior does not appear with `proxy_protocol_behavior` set to `use_always` nor `allow_authorized`_x000D_
2. The packet capture is what I expect (I think?) -- TCP handshake followed by a request and the Vault server sending a reset directly afterwards due to the lack of a PROXY protocol message_x000D_
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10523950/190283793-6a2bbef7-941f-4009-a8ed-b203b924de44.png)_x000D_
_x000D_
Passing `--haproxy-protocol` to curl resulted in the following:_x000D_
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10523950/190284152-08d82718-5582-42d4-9fa2-5714491394b6.png)_x000D_
_x000D_
3. Slightly surprising to me, the cluster port for the HA cluster is unaffected by the API port closure_x000D_
6. I _think_ there is a bug with how reject errors are handled in [the proxy protocol wrapping function](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/helper/proxyutil/proxyutil.go#L72) as the pires/go-proxyproto implementation seems to [blindly close the TCP connection](https://github.com/pires/go-proxyproto/blob/main/protocol.go#L71) any time a policy resolution returns an non-nil error. I am fairly confident this isn't related, but thought it interesting_x000D_
_x000D_
Finally, here is a screenshot of my local testing alongside the runtime logs --_x000D_
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10523950/190281814-66d4067b-557a-42e6-8c95-eaab6ffbb34f.png)_x000D_
_x000D_
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10523950/190281964-caa3bd9b-46ba-4ce4-8c7c-0bfbe88a269f.png)_x000D_

_x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I'm using Vault 1.11.3 with [Minio](https://min.io/) as S3 Storage Backend, and when I set `endpoint` and `bucket` variables in the `config` file it concatenates those variables using a dot (`.`) in between, something like `http://<bucket-name>.<endpoint-name>/`, so it causes a wrong endpoint name and bad name resolution._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run a [Minio container](https://docs.min.io/docs/minio-docker-quickstart-guide.html)_x000D_
2. Add `access_key` and `secret_key` variables to Vault `config` file as described [here](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/configuration/storage/s3)._x000D_
3. Run the [Vault container](https://hub.docker.com/_/vault) with the `config` file as `volume`._x000D_
4. Run `docker log <vault-container-name>`_x000D_
5. See the error:_x000D_
_x000D_
```log_x000D_
vault-server_1  | Error initializing storage of type s3: unable to access bucket "vault" in region "us-east-1": RequestError: send request failed_x000D_
vault-server_1  | caused by: Get "http://vault.minio:9000/": dial tcp: lookup vault.minio on 127.0.0.11:53: no such host_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault starts connecting to the Minio bucket in its right endpoint (`http://<endpoint-name>/`) and runs normally._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.11.3_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): N/A_x000D_

title: Support multi-issuers in SSH Engine
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
PKI engine support multi-issuers (CAs) now, https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/pki#notice-about-new-multi-issuer-functionality. We'd like the similar function to be supported in SSH engine._x000D_
_x000D_
As there are mount points limits https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/internals/limits, we'd like to use multi-issuers instead of multiple SSH engines to reduce the mount points._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Similar with PKI engine multi-issuers (CAs), able to read public key and sign based on issuer name._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Better persistence solution to lift the limits on mount points and namespaces. May suggest to store the sub root namespace in separate storage. Having these limits on sub root namespaces is much reasonable. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Multi-issuers (CAs) will help on the ssh engine CA rotation._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
No.

title: Mssql user not dropped from db when semicolon behind USE statement
body_text:
**Describe the bug + Reproduction**_x000D_
The MSSQL database engine does not drop a SQL user when a semicolon is used after a `USE` statement in a revocation statement._x000D_
This for example happens with the below revocation statement._x000D_
```sql_x000D_
USE [MyDatabase];_x000D_
DROP USER IF EXISTS [{{name}}];_x000D_
```_x000D_
What it looks like in Vault:_x000D_
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16191655/191280067-9b0a2892-4e42-465e-ac4c-7ada09dc35ae.png)_x000D_
_x000D_
The user is dropped however if it is changed to the following:_x000D_
```sql_x000D_
USE [MyDatabase]_x000D_
DROP USER IF EXISTS [{{name}}];_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Configurable pkiCert rendering interval
body_text:
**Problem Description**_x000D_
_x000D_
We're using vault PKI engine to generate certificates. One of the requirements is to have dependant on certificates services running without access to vault for at least a week (time required for recovery in worst case infrastructure/servers/datacenter outage). This means we have to have at least 1 week before the expiration for any certificate in any given time. Currently vault-agent re-issues the certificate [when 85% of the secrets time-to-live (TTL) is reached](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/agent/template#non-renewable-leased-secrets) and this is not configurable. Therefore shortest possibly certificate's TTL we can have is "7days / 0.15". We are looking for a way to get shorten certificates._x000D_
_x000D_
**Solution**_x000D_
_x000D_
It'd be great to have ability to configure when vault-agent have to re-issue the certificate. In described case if vault-agent re-issues certificates when 15% TTL is reached, then we can have 9-day-long (7days / 0.85) certificates instead of 47-day (7days / 0.15) which is much shorten certificates. _x000D_
Option could be similar similar to [static_secret_render_interval](https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/agent/template#static_secret_render_interval) but for pkiCert templating function._x000D_
_x000D_
**Considered alternatives**_x000D_
_x000D_
Using "secret" template function without a lease instead of pkiCert gives an ability to re-issue certificate on every token renew event which is 60 second in our case. We use short token renew period for security purpose. We also store certificates in the vault to be able to revoke them. Such scenario produces way too much certificates and affects storage backend performance.

title: CSR subject is not carried over to issued certificate
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
CSR subject field is not carried over to certificate subject while PKI signing process. By definition in the [RF5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.txthttps://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.txt) states that certificate `Subject` field should `identify the entity associated with the public key`. The only way to know it for the CA is to read it from the CSR `Subject` and if valid, pass it to the issued certificate. This is not the case for vault PKI. _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Generate CSR_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_

We're using k8s cert-manager with vault to issue certificates and it allows to specify (check more [here](https://cert-manager.io/docs/usage/certificate/#creating-certificate-resources)): ``` subject: organizations: - jetstack ``` Found out while digging, that the cert-manager is adding the `subject` to the CSR and calls a PKI role to sign, but the generated certificate is not having any organization (the PKI role doesn't define any in our case). Agree it's a security concern without validation, but eager to have once the `use_csr_rdns` option.
cipherboy: @phamrak Can you add the organization to the role that cert-manager is hitting? E.g., `vault write pki/roles/example-dot-com ... o=jetstack`? phamrak: @cipherboy yes, we can split the roles by organizations. My previous post was about that the cert-manager `subject` configuration is ignored. Understand the reason why it's like this on behind, but it's not obvious. A nice hint about in the documentation would be nice. But not sure where's the best place, probably in cert-manager itself.
Jwy-jump: @cipherboy @phamrak ``` `vault write test/roles/test_server key_bits=2048 max_ttl=8750h allow_any_name=true require_cn=false use_csr_common_name=true openssl req -new -key private.key -out req1.csr -subj "/C=CN/ST=London/L=London/O=example/OU=Personal/CN=we/emailAddress=aospace@com" `vault write -format=json test/issue/test_server common_name="example.com" csr=@req1.csr format=pem ttl="8660h" | jq -r '.data.certificate' > certificate.crt` ``` but the cert certificate has no csr subject informations? `
cipherboy: `C`, `ST`, `L`, `O`, `OU` are not the common name and thus won't be copied over. `use_csr_common_name=true` strictly uses the `Subject/CN` field that you should seen should be copied over... Other than you overriding it explicitly on the CLI with `common_name` perhaps (drop that and it definitely should be). If you want to sign CSRs as-is, including O/OU information, right now your best approach is using `sign-verbatim`, which requires pre-verification of the CSR. The [Hashicorp Vault Discuss](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault/30/) forum might be a better place for this discussion, tbh.

title: Validate cert key when enabling auth for kubernetes
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Hey! Pretty simple, I think it would be a nice QoL improvement if vault would throw an error if an invalid k8 cert key is provided when setting up the auth engine.  _x000D_
_x000D_
This comes from a very confusing couple of days that I spent banging my head against a wall, due to me simply passing an incorrect payload when configuring my auth engine.  I configure vault via terraform, and was setting up my kubernetes auth with the following hcl block _x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
resource "vault_kubernetes_auth_backend_config" "kubernetes" {_x000D_
  backend                = vault_auth_backend.kubernetes.path_x000D_
  kubernetes_host        = data.digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster.bkbn.endpoint_x000D_
  kubernetes_ca_cert     = data.digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster.bkbn.kube_config[0].cluster_ca_certificate_x000D_
  token_reviewer_jwt     = kubernetes_secret.vault-auth.data.token_x000D_
  disable_local_ca_jwt   = true_x000D_
  issuer                 = "https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This was applied to my cluster with seemingly no issues.  However, no matter what I did, I was getting `403` errors on any k8 login request.  After many frustrating hours, I read the config back via the cli `vault read auth/kubernetes-bkbn-sandbox/config` and saw that the `kubernetes_ca_cert` was base64 encoded 🤦 _x000D_
_x000D_
So the fix ended up being super simple, but I think it would be preferable if Vault caught this when creating the engine.  Or at least provided a warning of some kind_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Mentioned above, throw an error or at least provide a warning if an invalid ca_cert is detected. _x000D_

N/A _x000D_

-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
As per the recommendation [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/5107#issuecomment-413411072), we are using the `wrapped_token` query parameter to the `logout` endpoint in order to automatically log in. This works as expected it the client is already logged into the UI, i.e., the client is logged out of the UI, the wrapped token is unwrapped, and the client is logged into the UI with the unwrapped token._x000D_
However, this does not work if the client is **not** already logged into the UI. The token is successfully unwrapped once, but then the UI attempts to unwrap it again (with the HTTP response `{"errors":["wrapping token is not valid or does not exist"]}`), and the UI presents:_x000D_
```_x000D_
Error_x000D_
Token unwrap failed: wrapping token is not valid or does not exist_x000D_
```_x000D_
Interestingly, if the `namespace` query parameter is present, the wrapped token will only be unwrapped once regardless of whether the client is logged into the UI, and the flow succeeds._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. If signed in, sign out of the Vault UI_x000D_
2. Access the UI via `<vault_url>:8200/ui/vault/logout?wrapped_token=<wrapped_token_value>`_x000D_
3. See error_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Regardless of whether the client is signed into the Vault UI, navigating to the UI via `<vault_url>:8200/ui/vault/logout?wrapped_token=<wrapped_token_value>` should result in the client logging in successfully._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: 1.11.2_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: docker.io/vault:1.11.2_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
plugin_directory = "/usr/local/libexec/vault"_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
max_lease_ttl = "8760h"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
While the `auth` endpoint does work for clients in the logged out state, it does not work for clients already logged in. We would like a single endpoint that works regardless of whether the client is signed into the Vault UI._x000D_

title: PKI Secrets Engine, Import CA Certificates and Keys does not replace default issuer implicitly
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault v1.9.4 Import CA Certificates and Keys implicitly replace the default issuer,_x000D_
So when import CA using /pki/config/ca and then issue new certs using pki/issue/:name it signs the generated certs from the latest imported CA, _x000D_
Within v1.11.3 this behavior has been broken the /pki/config/ca does not replace the default issuer and instead it signs the generated certs from an orphan issuer. _x000D_
for workaround running /pki/root/replace with the issuer ID given from /pki/config/ca response mapping will sign the generated certs from the latest imported CA_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. export VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8300 _x000D_
2. vault operator init_x000D_
3. vault operator unseal _x000D_
4. export VAULT_TOKEN="[REDACTED_VAULT_TOKEN]"_x000D_
5. vault secrets enable pki_x000D_

title: Impossible to onboard new users after enforcing MFA TOTP on LDAP logins
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
