_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Once TOTP MFA is enforced on LDAP logins, it becomes almost impossible to onboard new users. When a new user tries to login, they are prompted to enter TOTP, for which they need a QR code scanned into any MFA authenticator app, which the user could have been able to generate only before TOTP was enforced. This leaves vault admin to generate QR code for the user using /identity/mfa/method/totp/admin-generate command which expects $ENTITY_ID which is only generated once user has attempted login. Not only is this process very difficult to automate. This makes the whole user onboarding experience to vault very clunky._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Enforce TOTP using `vault write /identity/mfa/login-enforcement/adtotp mfa_method_ids="$TOTP_METHOD_ID" auth_method_accessors=$LDAP_ACCESSOR`_x000D_
3. As vault admin, try to generate QR code for new user using command `vault write -field=barcode /identity/mfa/method/totp/admin_generate method_id=$TOTP_METHOD_ID entity_id=$ENTITY_ID`_x000D_
4. $ENTITY_ID won't exist in vault until user has already attempted login_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
When an LDAP user is trying to login for the first time to a vault that has TOTP enforcement, once user is successfully authenticated against LDAP, provide the user an option to generate their own QR code from UI or CLI._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version : 1.10.3_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version : 1.7.2_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Flatcar-stable-2765.2.6-hvm_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Login Enforcement: let choose between 2 MFA solution
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Actually, when activating MFA, the login enforcement applies a logical AND when selecting multiple MFA._x000D_
_x000D_
From the documentation:_x000D_
_x000D_
> If there are multiple login enforcements, each one needs to be satisfied before a login attempt succeeds. (https://www.vaultproject.io/api-docs/secret/identity/mfa/login-enforcement#create-a-login-enforcement)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Permits to apply a logical OR_x000D_
_x000D_
For example, when using username/password, I want to have the choice between Duo and TOTP because if I've no more battery on my smartphone, I can still have my TOTP_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Having a crazy setup:_x000D_
- userpass: user/password with TOTP_x000D_
- userpassd: user/password with DUO_x000D_
This is crazy also for the entity because it's not only 1 alias for userpass but 2 with possible 2 different passwords… honestly, it's really a bad solution

title: Vault on Kubernetes - node going down breaks HA?
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
After one of our kubernetes nodes went down today so did one of our vault instances._x000D_
We only noticed this because it completely broke the vault HA (and therefor all of our secrets-communications suddenly stopped working)._x000D_
_x000D_
We have a pool of 3 nodes which we run some of our services on, including vault. Due to some changes one of those nodes in the pool, one node had to be recycled. This node was running the pod `vault-1` one of the follower nodes in the raft._x000D_
_x000D_
My understanding is that when installing vault through the helm chart in HA mode a node going down like this should not stop the HA from working. (If so: then what's the purpose of HA in the first place)._x000D_
_x000D_
I got vault back up and running by simply using `kubectl exec -it vault-1 -- vault operator unseal`._x000D_
_x000D_
So my question here is: Why does this break HA? It's fine having to manually unseal that node if it goes down, but it should stop vault as a whole from working. (My CI/CD pipeline got an `vault is sealed` error thrown at it)._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run vault in 3-node HA_x000D_
2. Bring down one of the slave nodes and bring it back up again_x000D_
3. Try making requests to vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
When one of the 3 nodes in an HA setup goes down I expect vault to resume working normally._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.11.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): N/A_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Kubernetes on Debian (DigitalOcean Managed Kubernetes)_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
disable_mlock = true_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  tls_disable = 1_x000D_
  address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
  cluster_address = "[::]:8201"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
storage "raft" {_x000D_
  path = "/vault/data"_x000D_
  retry_join {_x000D_
   leader_api_addr = "http://vault-0.vault-internal:8200"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
  retry_join {_x000D_
   leader_api_addr = "http://vault-1.vault-internal:8200"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
  retry_join {_x000D_
   leader_api_addr = "http://vault-2.vault-internal:8200"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
  retry_join {_x000D_
    auto_join = "provider=k8s namespace=vault label-selector=\"app.kubernetes.io/name=vault\""_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
service_registration "kubernetes" {}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Support passthrough authentication in the vault UI
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
As an infrastructure operator, I want to provide a smooth login/SSO experience to the developers I maintain infrastructure for. To that end, I have a common identity provider (keycloak), and a common identity broker (oauth2-proxy), which communicate using OIDC and provide a common login interface/way to acquire an id_token and an access_token through a browser. The routes that point to my workloads automatically redirect to the identity broker if a token is not provided when it is required._x000D_
_x000D_
To that end, I'd like the Vault UI to simply accept the JWT provided by e.g. an Authorization header and automatically exchange it for a vault token without going through the UI/sign-in process. That way, my oauth2-proxy could coordinate the login process and then redirect to the vault UI with a valid login token for e.g. JWT auth._x000D_
_x000D_
Note that this feature actually already exists but only for pre-wrapped vault tokens. By providing ?wrapped_token=<...> to the vault UI root route query parameter, you can skip the sign-in process. This feature would simply extend this to provide tokens other than a vault token. I could also write a proxy that authenticates with the provided JWT and then forwards with a wrapped_token._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Provide an Authorization header to vault UI requests that vault UI can automatically use for auth on the first request._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Making a proxy that acts as a middle man and does this for me._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Any use case with a common login gateway._x000D_
_x000D_

'" }') } proxy_pass https://127.0.0.1:8200; } ``` | SoundGoof: and for true sso via web: ``` vault write sys/auth/jwt/tune listing_visibility="unauth" ```

title: Vault Agent should allow for configurable HTTP headers
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We run an instance of Vault that we protect via our zero-trust provider, Cloudflare (CF). As a human, you access Vault's web UI through the tunnel by first authenticating to CF using SAML. As a computer, there are number of ways - one of which is by using http headers._x000D_
_x000D_
The vault CLI has a `-header=<key=value>` feature that has been helpful. We'd like to do the same with the `vault agent` CLI._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I'd like to try writing the PR, so this is mostly a request to see if this is aligned with Vault's use case and direction._x000D_
_x000D_
I'd like to see the HCL config for Vault agent augmented to allow for headers, for example:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault {_x000D_
  address = "https://vault-fqdn:8200"_x000D_
  retry {_x000D_
    num_retries = 5_x000D_
  }_x000D_
  headers = {_x000D_
    header-1 = foo_x000D_
    header-2 = bar_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The new field would unmarshall in [config.go](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/c5b7047f34d5d517aebcea11109d3d2d48fcd7a6/command/agent/config/config.go#L70) and eventually make its way to the Vault client._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I don't know if there's an alternate feature within Vault that captures this feature. I've considered and discarded solutions that involve an http proxy as I would like to limit the complexity._x000D_

title: PKI: Error parsing CRL duration of '' when CRL is disabled
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We've recently upgraded Vault from 1.10.3 -> 1.12._x000D_
_x000D_
When we went to create a new CA, we received a 500 error._x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write pki/root/root/rotate/internal <fields>_x000D_
Error writing data to pki/root/root/rotate/internal: Error making API request._x000D_
URL: PUT https://<redacted>/v1/pki/root/root/rotate/internal_x000D_
Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
* 1 error occurred:_x000D_
	* error building CRLs: unable to build CRL for issuer (<issuer>): error parsing CRL duration of_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Our CRL is configured as follows:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault read pki/root/config/crl_x000D_
Key                          Value_x000D_
---                          -----_x000D_
auto_rebuild                 false_x000D_
auto_rebuild_grace_period    12h_x000D_
delta_rebuild_interval       n/a_x000D_
disable                      true_x000D_
enable_delta                 false_x000D_
expiry                       n/a_x000D_
ocsp_disable                 false_x000D_
ocsp_expiry                  12h_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Since the CRL is disabled, should it not be checking the expiry time? I believe that the expiry time should be be parsed below the disable check [here](https://cs.github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/fc2bdc37bf76431c29cf4f2c1d7e7e1785ee111a/builtin/logical/pki/crl_util.go#L1251-L1256)_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
We have our CRL disabled and we had the expiry unset (as seen by the above). With the expiry unset (`n/a`), attempt to rotate the credentials. We've upgraded Vault several times now, so it's possible we have a legacy config. However, if it's possible for the expiry time to be null, then this should be reproducible. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen._x000D_
_x000D_
I expected the rotation to complete without this error, since the CRL is disabled._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.7.3_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: _x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Add any other context about the problem here._x000D_

We'll have to do this outside of the version block as some clients (like yourself) have already upgraded. I'd set it to the default value. | cipherboy: Thanks for the PR with the fix!

title: PKI not getting a default issuer and failing after vault upgrade (1.9.1 -> 1.11.4)

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault upgrade from 1.9.1 to 1.11.4 didn't selected a default issuer for all PKIs in vault._x000D_
_x000D_
The affected PKI had no issuer & no default issuer after the upgrade, It was not possible to do any action with this PKI. Even getting the certificate with a request to the `pki/cert/ca` was failing with: _x000D_
```_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* no default issuer currently configured_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Only one out of many PKIs configured in the vault was affected_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
It's not clear how to reproduce that on a newly created vault as this happened only on 1 of the vault configured PKI. _x000D_
One of the possible cause is that the affected PKI was older than the others: it was created long time ago (approximately 6year ago), I'm not sure if that matters in this case._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
All PKIs are getting a default issuer (and an issuer) during the upgrade as mentioned in the documentation:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
 Vault automatically selects the default issuer from the current issuing certificate on migration from an older Vault version (Vault < 1.11.0)._x000D_
``` _x000D_
_x000D_
If not possible, this is mentioned in the upgrades notes as a possible issue._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.11.4 (after an upgrade from 1.9.1)_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.11.4_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Happy to help debug this, let me know if you need more information. I believe I can reproduce it by re-doing the upgrade on a backup of our vault 1.9.1 data_x000D_

We suspect what happened is at some point in the past, someone accidentally overwrote the PKI root key with this new intermediate key, and likely the new intermediate never got signed since the root has lost its keys. This would be verifiable by taking the root ca (from your `sys/raw` listing -- either on the 1.9.x or the upgraded cluster) and doing an import (`vault write pki-root/issuers/import/bundle pem_bundle="...."`). You'll get an `issuer_id` out of the import and see that it lacks a `key_id` on the issuer object (`vault read pki-root/issuer/:issuer_id`). This association would be automatic if there's a matching key. The newer 1.11 docs have a lot of good info about that and the structures exposed. This will (probably) show that the existing private key from the failed intermediate (which should've been successfully migrated -- hence no log messages about failures as we explicitly handled the intermediate CA creation in progress migration step -- and can be checked via `vault list pki/root/keys` prior to doing that import on the 1.11 instance) _doesn't match_ the newly imported root certificate. Thus there's some other (not present) key for the root certificate that needs to be found. What this likely means is you'll have to go back through your earlier backups and see if you can find one with the root's private key still available, restore it in a recovery instance like you've done, use `sys/raw` to read it out of the backup recovery instance, and import it to the production 1.11 cluster (either with the same `pem_bundle` command above or with the `pki-root/keys/import` endpoint). Otherwise, you'll need to start rotating the root CA, with the understanding this'll be harder to do as you can't cross sign new intermediates under old root, so you'll have to cross-sign the existing intermediates under the new root, distribute the parallel chains, finish deploying the new root everywhere, and then rotate to new intermediates without the cross signing. On 1.11.x+, we've explicitly opted to make all of these operations "add another" versus "silently replace" -- better to have more issuers than to remove something without a recover ...[truncated]

title: plugin list fails when audit is enabled
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When executing the command `vault plugin list` (or using the API) if audit is enabled vault will fail and report a error._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2022-10-28T07:19:22.397Z [ERROR] audit: panic during logging: request_path=sys/plugins/catalog error="reflect: reflect.Value.Set using value obtained using unexported field"_x000D_
2022-10-28T07:19:22.398Z [ERROR] core: failed to audit response: request_path=sys/plugins/catalog_x000D_
  error=_x000D_
  | 1 error occurred:_x000D_
  | 	* panic generating audit log_x000D_
  | _x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. enable audit_x000D_
2. Run `vault plugin list`_x000D_
3. See error_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
vault v1.12.0_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
I saw that there were some changes related to output version on plugins, so I guess it's related to that. I also found some issues (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/2687 and https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/1911) with the same error but they're from a long time ago._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: AnthonyHerman: Hitting this as well in v1.12.1 | jmthvt: If I understand correctly, it would be because of this [*version.Version](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/4e1958c07ccf72bcfb65f5835699fe31c53ca937/sdk/helper/pluginutil/runner.go#L99). ``` SemanticVersion *version.Version `json:"-"` ``` As per #1911: > reflect just goes as deep as it can, and the callbacks have to check if the fields can be set. So it eventually hits these [*version unexported fields](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-version/blob/main/version.go#L34-L40): ``` type Version struct { metadata string pre string segments []int64 si int original string } ``` | artur-borys1: Hi, are there any updates on this or should I use older (< 1.12.0) version of Vault?

It's not ideal, but the best listing workaround I can offer for now (other than disabling auditing which is obviously a no-go) is that the ["typed" list endpoints](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/plugins-catalog#list-plugins-1) don't suffer from this problem, so e.g. `vault list sys/plugins/catalog/database`, but they don't include versioned plugins right now. Affected Vault versions are 1.12.0, 1.12.1 and 1.12.2.

title: Database plugin MongoDB: writeconcern set by user is not applied in user deletion
body_text:
**Description**_x000D_
When Vault deletes a user on a MongoDB replica, it always uses WriteConcern = 'majority' despite the setting in the connection configuration._x000D_
_x000D_
This is proven by this function:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
dropUserCmd := &dropUserCommand{_x000D_
	Username:     req.Username,_x000D_
	WriteConcern: writeconcern.New(writeconcern.WMajority()),_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
in `\plugins\database\mongodb\mongodb.go` line 213._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Set up a replica set of MongoDB (also on Docker in a local instance)_x000D_
2. Configire in Vault a MongoDB connection with setting `WriteConcern = 1`  i.e. using_x000D_
```_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "W": 1,_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
3. Change log level in MongoDB: `db.setLogLevel(5, 'command')`_x000D_
4. Generate a credential for MongoDB _x000D_
5. Revoke the token in Vault (or generate the credential with a short lived TTL and wait)_x000D_
6. Have a look to the MongoDB log file where you can see that the deletion is made by Vault with write concern "majority"_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Also the deletion must be done using the write concern specified in the connection setting_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12.0_x000D_

title: Unit tests for Vault Agent Cache leak HTTP requests
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Some tests in the Vault Agent cache inadvertently make HTTP requests for `auth/token/renew-self` and `sys/leases/renew`_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
 1. Start a Vault development server with `vault server -dev`_x000D_
 2. Enable audit logging:_x000D_
```_x000D_
export VAULT_TOKEN=...  # token from dev server_x000D_
export VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8200_x000D_
vault audit enable file file_path=/tmp/vault-audit.log_x000D_
```_x000D_
 3. Run the affected tests:_x000D_
```_x000D_
go test  ./command/agent/cache/... -run TestLeaseCacheRestore_expired -run TestLeaseCacheRestore_expired -run TestLeaseCache_PersistAndRestore_x000D_
```_x000D_
 4. Observe unexpected requests in /tmp/vault-audit.log. Ex:_x000D_
 ```_x000D_
{"time":"2022-10-28T19:52:32.410243Z","type":"response","auth":{"token_type":"default"},"request":{"id":"252f7c5c-f8d4-cc97-186d-bbf5fd220405","operation":"update","mount_type":"system","client_token":"hmac-sha256:3742e3b4718a4e1d0a6f93107cb5d785bf13627c53a724958ad22b32d1a233ca","namespace":{"id":"root"},"path":"sys/leases/renew","data":{"increment":"hmac-sha256:013a2e7591ec607052af66e123a9329841011faf831896e589dfac23c236ecdb","lease_id":"hmac-sha256:1024575e2df3a83ad28080b054844a41a208b25cd919f0ef091b197a7c2412bc"},"remote_address":"127.0.0.1","remote_port":53295},"response":{"mount_type":"system","data":{"error":"hmac-sha256:62433f9ca58f19111df4e19132b2733c50b6e88210b13457f324f3d528cbe828"}},"error":"1 error occurred:\n\t* permission denied\n\n"}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Unit tests shouldn't be making external HTTP requests (even to localhost), especially to the `VAULT_ADDR` address or using the user's token. While these particular requests appear to be harmless, a user could inadvertently send requests to a running server._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
Running off of main as of 8ff7aaabc4a2b6c2a370ecc3fdccac6e45884e73, observed in 1.11.x as well._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I believe there are two issues:_x000D_
 _x000D_
_x000D_
First, running tests directly with `go test` (rather than `make test`) can leak `VAULT_` environment variables. In [lease_cache_test.go](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/8ff7aaabc4a2b6c2a370ecc3fdccac6e45884e73/command/agent/cache/lease_cache_test.go#L35), the following:_x000D_
 ```_x000D_
func testNewLeaseCache(t *testing.T, responses []*SendResponse) *LeaseCache {_x000D_
	t.Helper()_x000D_
_x000D_
	client, err := api.NewClient(api.DefaultConfig())_x000D_
	if err != nil {_x000D_
		t.Fatal(err)_x000D_
	}_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
call to `api.DefaultConfig` will absorb any environment variables or a token in `~/.vault-token`, so it might be worth clearing the environment in the test function._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
Second, the tests in `lease_cache_test` hit endpoints on `example.com`, but the default client URL winds up set to `https://127.0.0.1:8000` or `VAULT_ADDR` (if set). This should probably be overridden in the `client` and set explicitly to `example.com`._x000D_

title: Option to auto increment min_decryption_version on auto rotation
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I find it frustrating that there is an option to have keys automatically rotated but the min_decryption_version must be incremented manually._x000D_
_x000D_
I appreciate that in many use cases the `min_decryption_version` should be incremented manually, eg after all encrypted data has been rewrapped. However, my use case requires that all values encrypted more than 14 days ago can no longer be decrypted. I would therefore like auto rotation every day and `min_decryption_version` to always be kept 14 versions behind latest._x000D_
_x000D_
Currently I'd need to write something to make this API call, create an app role for it, and manage the deployment of that service to our infrastructure._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would like `min_decryption_version` and `min_encryption_version` to accept a negative value which represents the number of versions behind the latest version._x000D_
_x000D_
Eg.  _x000D_
If the `latest_version` is 50 and `min_decryption_version` is -1 then the effective minimum decryption version would be 49.  _x000D_
If the `latest_version` is 50 and `min_decryption_version` is -10 then the effective minimum decryption version would be 40._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Instead of negative values for `min_decryption_version` and `min_encryption_version`, two new key configuration properties could be added, but the negative values seems like a cleaner solution._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Any scenario in which the lifetime of the encrypted data is known up front or if it is known that the rewrapping of encrypted data will be completed within a certain timeframe._x000D_
_x000D_
**Out of scope**_x000D_
Automatic trimming of old keys_x000D_

title: Vault Init input validation is too strict (1.12.0)
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault 1.12.0 added support to validate operator init input. However Its breaking a community terraform module and supported server side behavior._x000D_
_x000D_
Refs_x000D_
[Vault PR adding validation](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/16379)_x000D_
[Terraform Community Module](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/rickardgranberg/vaultoperator/latest/docs/resources/init)_x000D_
_x000D_
This is due to the fact the author relied on passing in `0` to the  `recovery_`* params and then them being ignored by vault when secrets were specified as non zero. This is confusing in the code as the error does not match the expected state as defined._x000D_
_x000D_
This is **NOT** inline with the vault server code https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/dd891bc748f690cf90e5e5297304b4bc5f4d0902/http/sys_init.go#L154-L158_x000D_
_x000D_
Which implicitly allows you to pass `0` currently._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Using module write the following code_x000D_
```terraform_x000D_
 resource "vaultoperator_init" "scenario_vault_init" {_x000D_
   secret_shares    = 1_x000D_
   secret_threshold = 1_x000D_
 _x000D_
   depends_on = [_x000D_
     docker_container.scenario_vault_container,_x000D_
     time_sleep.wait_for_vault_startup,_x000D_
   ]_x000D_
 _x000D_
   lifecycle {_x000D_
     ignore_changes = all_x000D_
   }_x000D_
 }_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
3. Run `terraform apply`_x000D_
4. See error _x000D_
```_x000D_
Error: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/init_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* parameters recovery_shares,recovery_threshold not applicable to seal type shamir_x000D_
_x000D_
  on ../modules/vault-transit/main.tf line 7, in resource "vaultoperator_init" "scenario_vault_init":_x000D_
   7: resource "vaultoperator_init" "scenario_vault_init" {_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The provider specifiying `0` for recovery keys and >`0` for secret keys should pass validation. _x000D_
_x000D_
Based on semver this is a breaking change to the API, while I understand the need for validation I would say passing `0` to both params should negate that check given the server side code supporting that configuration. Further I think this scenario e.g.  `0` for the params was missed in the [go tests](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/0d6a42c79ef765e919db486c1cb78e527b47e010/http/sys_init_test.go#L133-L150), and if its was an expected behavior then it should be in the go tests for linked PR. Instead the PR/tests only assume a scenario where you incorrectly pass both params in with values instead of one with 0 and one with >0 value . Most importantly  its not inline with the actual server code referenced above which should be the source of truth here for validation._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version `1.12.0`:_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version`1.12.0`:_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture:_x000D_
_x000D_
[Docker](https://hub.docker.com/layers/hashicorp/vault-enterprise/1.12.0-ent/images/sha256-0e0c39f329ba3a0565a49f7fc7cecdd0648b61dc0a0774d312152e43c8854e94?context=explore) , but its not probably not relevant to this bug._x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl _x000D_
 disable_mlock = true_x000D_
 ui = true_x000D_
 _x000D_
 listener "tcp" {_x000D_
     tls_disable = "true"_x000D_
     address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
     cluster_address = "[::]:8201"_x000D_
 }_x000D_
 _x000D_
 storage "file" {_x000D_
   path = "/tmp"_x000D_
 }_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I have also filed a bug on the community provider here https://github.com/rickardgranberg/terraform-provider-vaultoperator/issues/7_x000D_
_x000D_
However strictly speaking again, this is a breaking change in the API on invalid semver bump so I think vault should likely fix it. The validation while good, should not fail to validate something that would not produce an invalid configuration e.g. `0` for recovery keys. _x000D_
_x000D_
Even if you expect the provider author to fix it, it is actually not that easy to fix for the though too:_x000D_
_x000D_
You can see the terraform vault provider code in question [here](https://github.com/rickardgranberg/terraform-provider-vaultoperator/blob/8df5a1db09ff6d60c8574b0876223c628cd551e0/internal/provider/resource_init.go#L244-L249)_x000D_
_x000D_
This is essentially by design in the terraform provider code as calling [Get](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/terraform/helper/schema#ResourceData.Get) will  implicitly return a `0` and not say `nil`, that would work here with `omitempty` if the upstream vault api module supported it. However even that won't work as vault doesn't use `omitempty` for the init request type._x000D_
_x000D_
From the terraform provider docs for `Get`_x000D_
> If the key does exist in the schema but doesn't exist in the configuration, then the default value for that type will be returned. For strings, this is "", for numbers it is 0, etc._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/746b089472bc231da9f536a7092ade75e10f91c1/api/sys_init.go#L58-L59_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Prune inactive entities
body_text:
## TL;DR_x000D_
_x000D_
We're considering a solution that will create a significant number of Entities in Vault's Identity backend. There appears to be no built-in functionality to (a) automatically prune Entities that have been inactive for some time or (b) determine when an Entity was last active. This means that the Identity backend would continue to grow unchecked over time._x000D_
_x000D_
Ideally, we'd like the ability to configure the Identity backend to automatically prune inactive Entities after "X" days. At a minimum, we'd like the ability to determine when each Entity was last active (so that we can script querying and deleting Entities)._x000D_
_x000D_
## The Long Form_x000D_
_x000D_
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
We're looking to issue TLS client certificates, using Vault's PKI backend, to machines in our infrastructure for mutual TLS authentication to a service. Ideally, the client certificates should contain an attribute that uniquely identifies the client. This then enables the service to positively identify each client and accurately record audit log entries. On AWS, the approach we're contemplating is as follows:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Configure clients to authenticate to Vault using the AWS authentication backend in the EC2 mode._x000D_
2. Configure the AWS authentication backend to base Entity Aliases on `instance_id` for EC2 authentications._x000D_
3. Create an ACL policy that points to the PKI role and limits the allowed values for the `common_name` parameter to `identity.entity.aliases.<mount accessor>.name`, where "mount accessor" refers to the AWS authentication backend._x000D_
_x000D_
The problem with this approach is that Vault will create an Entity and Entity Alias for each new EC2 instance that needs to interact with the service. With horizontal autoscaling, this could quickly bog down Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
The Identity engine should be configurable to automatically prune Entities that have been inactive for a set "X" number of days. Alternatively, there should be a record of when each Entity last authenticated to Vault that is returned with the [Read Entity](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/identity/entity#read-entity-by-id) API endpoints._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Ignore it and hope we can cope with all the Entities/Aliases long term._x000D_
2. Keep the AWS backend's aliases associated with Vault Role IDs instead of Instance IDs. The trade-off is that clients would need permission to specify arbitrary Common Names, possibly impersonating other clients. Nevertheless, we'd still have some degree of client authentication (clients still need access to Vault), and it's likely that impersonation attacks could at least be traced through Vault's own audit logs._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
While the use case we have in mind is very specific, the ability to clean up inactive Entities is likely useful to have in general._x000D_
_x000D_
~**Additional context**~_x000D_

title: Unclear documentation around cert auth CRLs
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault docs on [certificate auth revocation checking](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/cert#revocation-checking) contains the statement:_x000D_
_x000D_
> An authorized user can submit PEM-formatted CRLs identified by a given name; these can be updated or deleted at will. They may also set the URL of a trusted CRL distribution point, and have Vault fetch the CRL as needed._x000D_
_x000D_
This makes mention of configuring a CRL by providing a CRL distribution point, however, there is no mention of that configuration within the [api docs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/cert#create-crl). Digging in a bit further, we see that there is, in fact, a [`url` configuration option on the CRL creation endpoint](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/cert/path_crls.go#L35)._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Consistent documentation and guidance on publicly available APIs/configuration._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.12.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s): N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Couple of other interesting questions not found in the documentation:_x000D_
1. With what cadence is the CRL distribution point queried (and thereby the CRL refreshed)? This is particularly interesting since the answer seems to be a combo of the [CRL validity period](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/cert/backend.go#L98) and when the [periodicFunc is called](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/cert/backend.go#L48), with the CRL validity period being the most interesting as the documentation also mentions:_x000D_
_x000D_
    > In addition, since the method does not fetch the CRLs itself, the CRL's designated time to next update is not considered._x000D_
_x000D_
2. Why is the signature of the CRL not validated in either the direct CRL nor distribution point configuration?_x000D_
3. Why is PEM the only supported format when setting it manually and DER the only support format when the distribution point is queried?_x000D_
_x000D_
Happy to move these last two to feature requests if necessary.
top_3_comments_text: bmendric: Another undocumented parameter I just ran across -- [allowed_metadata_extensions](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/cert/path_certs.go#L117) The corresponding config option is also undocumented -- [enabled_identity_alias_metadata](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/cert/path_config.go#L20) | cipherboy: @bmendric Happy to take docs PRs around this if you'd like to submit one. Note that the periodic func gets called every minute, so in general it isn't that relevant (compared to the lifetime of the CRL itself). For 2, I think on the distribution point configuration we could support verifying the CRL signature, but note in general the CRL might be issued from a dedicated CRL signer. Other server applications like nginx/... punt on CRL verification and trust that you've properly verified the CRL before setting it in the config, and Vault is no different. title: Duo Passcode Implementation or Documentation Unclear
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The Duo MFA method can accept a TOTP passcode generated from the Duo Mobile app, or one associated with an end-users Duo account (ex. a Yubikey OTP). What is left out of the documentation is that the word `passcode=` must be appended for the Duo Login MFA provider to actually use that provided OTP or Yubikey OTP. If an end-user **only** specifies the TOTP code or Yubikey OTP, the Duo Login MFA provider will send a push anyways._x000D_
_x000D_
I was able to figure this out by looking at [login_mfa.go](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.12.0/vault/login_mfa.go#L1775-L1776). This, somewhat, makes sense to me - the way you'd specify on the CLI with legacy MFA was with `passcode=` after a `vault login` command. _x000D_
_x000D_
I'm not sure if this should be updated in documentation (maybe in the [Configure Duo MFA Method](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/identity/mfa/duo) doc? Or maybe a provider-specific callout in the [validate API docs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/mfa/validate)) or if the code should be updated to use passcode auth if an MFA cred is specified at all._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Configure Duo Login MFA and associate with an authentication method._x000D_
2. Configure a Duo user, set up Duo Mobile or associate a Yubikey OTP with the Duo user._x000D_
3. Attempt to log in - I use LDAP, so: `vault login -method=ldap -mfa <MFA_ID_HERE>:passcode=<YUBI_PRESS_OR_TOTP_HERE>`_x000D_
4. You'll receive a Duo push even though you specified a TOTP or Yubikey OTP_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
If you run `vault login -method=ldap -mfa <MFA_ID_HERE>:passcode=<YUBI_PRESS_OR_TOTP_HERE>` you'll receive login creds without a Duo push._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.12.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 20.04 on arm64_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The documentation should probably be updated to say that `passcode=` is required if it's not going to change. However, that's a bit janky in other places -- like when you log in via the Web UI, you have to remind your users to type in `passcode=` then press their Yubikey, but there's no indication of that in the UI either:_x000D_

title: Behavior of userfilter in ldap authtype
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Our use-case with the `ldap` authtype is to allow only those LDAP accounts that are members of the admin group to authenticate with Vault, and the `userfilter` config setting seems like the perfect place to encode enforcement. However, we have found that `userfilter` seems inert in our workflow._x000D_
_x000D_
The [documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/ldap#userfilter) clearly states:_x000D_
```_x000D_
The user search filter can be used to restrict what user can attempt to log in._x000D_
```_x000D_
Great, sounds perfect for our use case, and is fully aligned with the analogous setting in a vast array of other popular tooling. We are compelled to take this description at face value. Here is our actual config setting, confirmed as working properly in other LDAP tooling (substituting `UserAttr` and `Username` as appropriate):_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/ldap/config \_x000D_
  userfilter="(&(objectClass=person)({{.UserAttr}}={{.Username}})(memberOf=cn=admin,ou=groups,dc=acme,dc=com))" \_x000D_
  ..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Yet when we moved to produce a negative test case in an attempt to confirm proper operation, we discovered that `userfilter` seems to have no observable impact on who can authenticate. Even an LDAP search filter as utterly scandalous as the following doesn't hinder authentication:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/ldap/config \_x000D_
  userfilter="(objectClass=tortoise)" \_x000D_
  ..._x000D_
```_x000D_
So we're not sure what `userfilter` is meant to do and what it actually does! Have we overlooked something?_x000D_
_x000D_
(Note that the tortoise example above produces a warning from Vault but otherwise makes no difference)_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): Vault v1.12.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.12.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux, OpenLDAP 2.4_x000D_

The [code](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/cc570c11bbc63bd3810a56d8b2ec9e09902ca654/sdk/helper/ldaputil/client.go#L168-L173) assumes the bind DN can be derived immediately, without performing a user search request to the LDAP server, which means that the `userfilter` is completely ignored. 3. Once the bind DN is established, perform a bind request against the LDAP server (the actual authentication). 4. Once authenticated, fetch groups. 5. Retrieve policies based on groups.
enspritz: Thanks @raymonstah @bradjoss , looks like we are going with the `binddn/bindpass` approach. And yes, the clarify docs ;)

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When AWS credentials are set as variables, vault login fails, it seems `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` is ignored _x000D_

```_x000D_
ROLE_JSON=$(aws sts assume-role --role-arn XXX --role-session-name vault-login-session)_x000D_

export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_x000D_
_x000D_
export VAULT_ADDR=AAA_x000D_
export VAULT_SKIP_VERIFY=true_x000D_
vault status_x000D_
vault login -method=aws role=vault-role region=${region} _x000D_
```_x000D_
whereas when `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` value is passed to   `aws_security_token` option then vault login works._x000D_
_x000D_
Working configuration._x000D_

        aws_access_key_id=${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID} \_x000D_
        aws_secret_access_key=${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY} \_x000D_
        aws_security_token=${AWS_SESSION_TOKEN}_x000D_

If you do not have IAM credentials available at any of these locations, you can explicitly pass them in on the command line (though this is not recommended), omitting aws_security_token if not applicable._x000D_
`_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
- export AWS credentials variables as describes in step1 above._x000D_
- try vault login command with aws auth._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
- vault login should work with AWS STS credentials without the need for explicit `aws_security_token` configuration._x000D_

title: `vault login` should print MFA passphrase prompt on stderr
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The `vault login` command prints the prompt for an MFA passphrase on the standard output stream.  This interferes with output redirection.  For example, without MFA, this command would store the token in the `VAULT_TOKEN` environment variable:_x000D_
_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
export VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault login -no-store -token-only -method=ldap username=…)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The LDAP password prompt (`Password (will be hidden): `) is printed to standard error.  The resultant token is printed to standard output.  All is well._x000D_
_x000D_
With MFA enabled, though, the `Enter the passphrase for methodID "…" of type "…":` prompt is printed to standard output.  It thus gets captured in the `VAULT_TOKEN` environment variable and is not visible on the screen._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Enable LDAP auth and TOTP MFA_x000D_
2. Run `export VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault login -no-store -token-only -method=ldap username=…)`_x000D_
3. Observe that `Initiating Interactive MFA Validation` is printed to the screen, but `Enter the passphrase for method ID "…" of type "totp":` is not_x000D_
4. Enter the TOTP code anyway_x000D_
5. Observe that the `VAULT_TOKEN` environment variable contains the prompt string AND the token._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The `Enter the passphrase …` prompt should be printed to standard error, making it visible to the user even if standard output is captured or redirected._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.12.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux/x86_64_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: hghaf099: Thanks for filing this ticket. For now, to get passed the issue you are observing you can simply pass in the MFA request header to the CLI command and get the result. Example: ``` export VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault login -mfa="$mfa_method_id":"$totp_code" -no-store -token-only -method=ldap username=…) ``` Note the added parameter in the CLI: `-mfa="$mfa_method_id":"$totp_code"` I’ll take this feedback to product for further consideration, but in the meantime I’m going to go ahead and close this issue. Please feel free to reply again if there’s any problems with the workaround, though!”

From that page, `With every dynamic secret and service type authentication token, Vault creates a lease: metadata containing information such as a time duration, renewability, and more. Once the lease is expired, Vault can automatically revoke the data, and the consumer of the secret can no longer be certain that it is valid.` So, with what is described in the ticket, it is possible to define TTL of the lease to be `xxx days`, and then Vault will automatically revoke the secret. | heatherezell: Hi @reddy9694 - since it's been a little while since we've heard from you on this ticket, I'm going to go ahead and close it now. hghaf099: Thanks for filing this ticket. I would like to first point to our doc page on lease revocation [here](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/lease) to make sure what is already supported would meet your requirement. From that page, `With every dynamic secret and service type authentication token, Vault creates a lease: metadata containing information such as a time duration, renewability, and more. Vault promises that the data will be valid for the given duration, or Time To Live (TTL). Once the lease is expired, Vault can automatically revoke the data, and the consumer of the secret can no longer be certain that it is valid.` So, with what is described in the ticket, it is possible to define TTL of the lease to be `xxx days`, and then Vault will automatically revoke the secret.

title: When using integrated storage, sometimes nodes fail to join the cluster

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Sometimes, when I launch a new vault instance it doesn't join. If I restart vault on the new instance, it still doesn't join. If on the new instance I stop vault, delete its raft database files, and start vault, sometimes it joins. If I delete the instance entirely and create a new one with a new node_id and IP, *sometimes* it joins. The chance whether or not a node succeeds in joining seems to decrease as time progresses; originally it worked 100% of the time in this cluster._x000D_
_x000D_
I have a 5-node vault cluster running in Amazon AWS. I am using integrated storage and AWS tag-based discovery. I have autopilot configured with `-cleanup-dead-servers=true -dead-server-last-contact-threshold=30 -min-quorum=3 -server-stabilization-time=30`. _x000D_
_x000D_
My workflow is AMI-based and in order to update things on these systems, such as OS packages, I replace the instance entirely. This means a vault node is removed from the cluster, and eventually another one joins._x000D_
_x000D_
I have a script that submits the unseal keys to vault after the process starts and is listening on port 8200. _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
I don't know :(_x000D_
_x000D_

dpedu: I am using an aggressive dead server cleanup for the reason of avoiding breaking quorum. Here is a test I just performed using the 5-node n=3 cluster describe in the original post to demonstrate: 1. I reconfigured autopilot with `-cleanup-dead-servers=true -dead-server-last-contact-threshold=3600 -min-quorum=3 -server-stabilization-time=30`. One hour before dead servers are cleaned up. 2. I terminated two vault instances. Vault remains healthy because 3 servers are still up and healthy. The raft peer list still shows 5 members due to the increase timeout. 3. I wait for 2 new instances to come up and join the cluster, stabilize, etc. Now there are 7 servers in the peer list, 5 healthy, 2 offline. 4. I terminate 2 more instances and **quorum is lost and the vault cluster becomes unhealthy**. I see messages in the log about "Election timeout reached, restarting election". I can't see the list of nodes but we can reason that there would be 9 known nodes now, 4 offline, 3 that were healthy, and 2 more that will be attempting to join soon. It appears that dead but not-yet-removed servers are factored into deciding whether we have quorum or not. As I am running vault on a cloud platform and I do not have control over the underlying hardware, I cannot control how frequently vault nodes are removed and replaced. I can only control how many need to be present and healthy (healthy from the cloud platform's perspective) at one time. I think you are right about the cause of this problem. Too high and quorum is easily lost. >> Couldn't a node send heartbeats during the transfer to avoid this problem? > The problem is that until the node has pulled the raft logs or snapshot, it doesn't have the raft configuration, so it doesn't know where to send the heartbeat. I'm curious, since it is able to reach other nodes for the purpose of pulling raft logs or snapshots, how is it that it doesn't know where?
ncabatoff: > As I am running vault on a cloud platform and I do not have control over the underlying hardware, I cannot control how frequently vault nodes are removed and replaced. I can only control how many need to be present and healthy (healthy from the cloud platform's perspective) at one time. I don't understand this, can you elaborate? The only folks I've seen running into problems like this one is when they've decided they wanted to use autoscaling. > I'm curious, since it is able to reach other nodes for the purpose of pulling raft logs or snapshots, how is it that it doesn't know where? Two different layers. All the Raft RPCs are handled in https://github.com/hashicorp/raft, and these aren't really directly usable by Vault. The vault code (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/vault/request_forwarding_rpc.go#L160-L160) needs to know how to issue an RPC to the active node, but with raft still coming online locally, we don't really have that capacity yet. The biggest obstacle is probably the cert that we need to do mTLS, which lives in storage. I'm not saying it's not possible, theoretically, but it seems like it would be a really big and disruptive effort.
dpedu: I see. > > As I am running vault on a cloud platform and I do not have control over the underlying hardware, I cannot control how frequently vault nodes are removed and replaced. I can only control how many need to be present and healthy (healthy from the cloud platform's perspective) at one time. > > I don't understand this, can you elaborate? I'm not using autoscaling in the sense that I want my cluster to automatically change size based on load. No, I don't want that. I am however using an autoscaling group to spawn the instances, and it is set at a static count of 5. The reason for this is that autoscaling groups will automatically replace instances that suffer underlying hardware failure and user-specified health checks as well as handling addition/removal of the servers to a load balancer. Rather than having a human intervene. The alternative would be to manually launch one-off instances, which pretty much defeats the purpose of using a cloud platform as there isn't a mechanism to automatically replace these. Edit: that being said, this seems like an obstacle to those who do want to autoscale their cluster size as well?
agill17: > The only folks I've seen running into problems like this one is when they've decided they wanted to use autoscaling. @ncabatoff I may have this issue, what are best practices / configurations to use alongside autoscaling ?

In that case, `min-quorum` for this cluster needs to 5, not 3, which might help protect the cluster against unwanted removals.

I already increased the cleanup to 600 seconds, which allows 1 server to reboot and come back, but as soon as the second one goes offline, the cluster is dead (we have a 3 node cluster, n=3)
maxb: @koen-venly I suggest it would be best if you started a topic in https://discuss.hashicorp.com to talk through your problem in a separate conversation - even though your problem sounds somewhat related, merely rebooting a server shouldn't involve leaving and joining the cluster at all, so I wonder if you actually have a different problem or misconfiguration.
koen-venly: The error messages I get are Exactly the same... But ok, I'll check https://discuss.hashicorp.com/
dpedu: @koen-venly I believe the original cause for the problem I was having was having the server stabilization time too low, as ncabatoff pointed out. My database is somewhat large so it made sense that it was not enough time to transfer it to new nodes. My final tuning for my 5-node cluster ended up like this, and has been stable since last year: ``` $ vault operator raft autopilot get-config Key Value --- ----- Cleanup Dead Servers true Last Contact Threshold 10s Dead Server Last Contact Threshold 1m30s Server Stabilization Time 1m30s Min Quorum 3 Max Trailing Logs 1000 ``` Also, I believe if you replace nodes too quickly - at a pace where they are not removed from quorum calculations - you'll see the same problem. The rate of node replacement needs to be slower than the `Dead Server Last Contact Threshold` plus the `Last Contact Threshold` combined.
koen-venly: @dpedu thanks for your answer. In the mean time, because I have nothing but bad experiences with pure storage backends, we shifted away from raft. We now use a rds postgresql backend. Vault service is running on 3 ec2 machines. Surplus for this, is the fact that the ec2's can now have much lower specs and the data is safer to my opinion then on this raft storage backend. (Everything in previous is encrypted of course)
VioletHynes: I'm going to close this issue as it seems like it was an issue with Dead Server Last Contact Threshold. I've since updated a lot of the documentation to stress that this should be not set to a low amount of time. Setting this too low can be disastrous, so erring on the high side would be my recommendation. I would strongly recommend this value be set in the scale of hours or days and not minutes, as misconfiguration of this value has been a consistent pain point for those that set it too low. I would only touch this if you're absolutely sure what you're doing.

title: [Req] Implement GET on /pki/issue/:name/latest and /pki/issuer/:issuer_ref/issue/:name/latest
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Istio users that want to leverage Vault PKI, will typically use the `vault-agent-init` sidecar to bootstrap the istio control plane (istiod pods) with the necessary key material:_x000D_
 - private intermediate CA key_x000D_
 - public intermediate CA cert_x000D_
 - root CA cert_x000D_
 - cert chain (from intermediate CA cert all the way to root cert, all appended)_x000D_
 _x000D_
This process is documented [here](https://istio.io/latest/docs/tasks/security/cert-management/plugin-ca-cert/#plug-in-certificates-and-key-into-the-cluster)._x000D_
_x000D_
When we want to use the Vault pki API, we can leverage the `/pki/issue/:name` and `/pki/issuer/:issuer_ref/issue/:name` endpoints that provide a POST method to generate new intermediate certificates._x000D_
_x000D_
The problem however, is that we do not want to generate a new certificate for every `istiod` pod restart or scale-up. Furthermore, the CA private key generated is not persisted within the API._x000D_
_x000D_
As a work-around, we use the secret kv backend to store this data._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Implement HTTP GET on `/pki/issue/:name/latest` and `/pki/issuer/:issuer_ref/issue/:name/latest` which would return the latest the private CA key, public CA cert, root cert and cert chain. When a intermediate certificate rotation is needed, an out-of-band process (cicd pipeline or service portal) can leverage the POST method to issue a new cert/key pair. The latest issued certificate should be easily retrievable by certificate consumers (istio control plane pods as just one example)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Right now we issue the cert/key and store them in vault secret kv, which seems like double work/storage._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
An system where multiple certificate consumers need to sync on a common intermediate certificate. Kubernetes pods that require an intermediate certificate is a typical use case._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
Also posted this question [here](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/vault-as-pki-for-istio-intermediate-certs/47095?u=boeboe).
top_3_comments_text: cipherboy: Curious, have y'all further considered simply reissuing the intermediates? Unless you're pinning to them, using an ECDSA intermediate and root cert would allow it to be reissued almost as fast as reading it from storage. In general, we suggest treating leaf certificates (which, from the root's perspective, an intermediate is) as just another resource that gets refreshed and rotated. Whenever the pod gets restarted, or a new node need the cert, or whatever, you could issue a new intermediate and not worry about it. Ideally, these CI/CD or service portal processes shouldn't be necessary, because nothing really cares about the contents of the intermediate being exactly the same: only that it chains up to the root. The only case where this would be problematic is if you expect people to be able to get new leaves _under the same intermediate_, i.e., you're pinning intermediates. In this type of infra, I don't expect that to work well, and so I'd consider taking out the K/V step entirely. However, even if you're doing code signing, as long as the intermediate is still valid and can be distributed by the server nodes (missing chain components is a much bigger problem and out-of-band socialization of intermediates is not a good idea in general)... it should all work out (and the same leaf code signing cert could be re-signed under new intermediates if necessary). For a TLS traffic API, issuing new intermediates should really be a non-issue. When the (TLS server or client) gets a new leaf cert, it should get the new intermediate as well and send that along to its peer for validating the chain. Fundamentally though, I think there's a misunderstanding here of how Vault's PKI works. The PKI engine isn't a generic secrets engine for certificates. It doesn't do anything with leaves. It really is an X509 Certificate Authority engine only. Roles (which `/sign/:role` and `/issue/:role` use) are for leaf non-CA issuance only, and don't support signing intermediate CAs. One role is (generally) meant to be able to sign a multitude of non-identical certificates. This means the concept of a "latest" isn't useful, as sometimes you'd get e.g., a cert for `example.com` vs `www.example.com` vs `Steve Jobs` or whatever, _and you wouldn't have control over which name would be requested/returned. I _think_ the correct feature request here would be for a path like `/pki/*/sign-intermediate/latest`, but again, you run into parallel paths problem: some people _do_ run multiple parallel, active intermediates under their root, so you'd want some name query capabilities, which is a bit hard to do well (performance-wise) in a simple K/V store. In X.509, there's no _real_ concept of a renewal that'd make this feasible: reissuance is indistinguishable from first issuance, given only one cert. Its only from an operational perspective that renewal and reissuance make sense, but then mostly boils down to issuance in the first place. In other words, its hard to tell (objectively, from a x509/code perspective) whether a given CSR to this endpoint is meant to be a replacement of an existing path (refreshing/renewing it) or a separate path altogether. Furthermore, Vault presently doesn't persist (leaf) private key material at all! This would be Key Recovery and Archival (KRA) functionality, and we'd have fundamental safety issues of just... returning private key material to whoever asks. This is less than ideal, and we'd ideally want these operations to be approved by an admin (requiring another out-of-band process). Thanks a lot for the insightful information. I learned a lot from this! | cipherboy: \o cool, glad to hear @boeboe! I'm going to go ahead and close this, but let me know in the future if this doesn't end up working out. I think the only tricky thing here is that some clients need more encouragement than others to send intermediate CAs, but generally it should be possible with all I've tried.

top_3_comments_text: maxb: Making an HTTP request with multiple consecutive slashes in the URL-path to the Vault API does not have a defined behaviour. The actual behaviour is that Vault inherits the Go http library's default of responding with a 301 redirect to the path with the slashes deduplicated. If you possess a token, then you don't need to login to anything - logging in is what ultimately gives you a token, but the token itself is all Vault cares about. I'm going to close this for now, as it doesn't sound like there's anything actionable for the Vault team to do here, but I'm happy to reopen if that's not the case.

top_3_comments_text: anthonyralston: +1, we've seen a similar issue. | maxb: > **To Reproduce** The fault occurs whenever two Vault pods become leader, at the same time, for any length of time. Two pods becoming leader simultaneously is impossible, though - it's a core part of the Raft protocol's guarantees. It seems more likely that there's an as yet unexplored failure condition with synchronizing the active state to Kubernetes labels. | banks: I agree with @maxb this seems to be due to tooling around updating the labels (which I'm entierely unfamiliar with so will investigate). One question about this to anyone who has experienced this: what is the actual problem this causes you operationally? I understand the expectation and general desire that the service would only resolve to the true leader, but trying to gauge whether having it temporarily route to the old one is causing serious availability issues or minor confusion or something in between! As an aside (unrelated to the _synchronization_ of raft leader state and lables which is the core issue here), the statement below is very nearly true but there are subtleties to be aware of if you want to reason about distributed systems guarantees. > Two pods becoming leader simultaneously is impossible, though - it's a core part of the Raft protocol's guarantees. Raft guarantees that at most one node is _actually_ the leader at any given moment in the sense that at most one server can actively commit new writes to the cluster. But there will always be possible periods during network partitions (hopefully in the region of seconds or less) where more than one node _thinks_ it is the leader because it has not yet hit a timeout and discovered that it's partitioned from the rest of the cluster, meanwhile the rest of the cluster may have elected a new leader. I'd expect those to be very short, but it's fundamentally impossible to avoid this. The only correct way for a node to know it is still the leader for certain is to send a message to other nodes and get a quorum of reponses affirming it's leadership! All correct consensus protocols are designed to ensure that even when this kind of partition happens (because it will!) only one of the leaders will be able to actually make progress (i.e. commit new operations to the cluster), while the "old" leader(s) will fail and step down if they try to actually get the other nodes to write something new (or _eventually_ when they realise they are not getting heartbeat responses any more). Synchronizing K8s labels from multiple processes is a secondary complicated problem - if every server pod updates it's own label then a crashed node might leave it's label wrong. If it is done by a single external process then it could have missed a leadership change or be unable to contact enough servers due to a network partition even if the vault cluster is still up with a different leader. K8s as far as I know doesn't actually have sufficient API guarantees to be able to guarantee at-most-one of a set has a specific label because K8s API only guarantees strong consistency on a single object while these labels are split across separate objects per pod. So there is probably some limit to how correct this label approach can be. Back to this thread though, it seems likely we can do better than not updating when a server stands down but is still running. That said, the example here shows quite a few very long (2+ second) heartbeat failures which indicates a pretty unreliable network or overloaded CPUs which are challenging conditions to make strong guarantees about the timliness of K8s state updates too!

banks: So the logic for updating this state is in Vault itself in the Kubernetes `serviceregistration` subpackage: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/366693c78dec71212ab344e8d315637722b60d25/serviceregistration/kubernetes/retry_handler.go Things to note: * We make a best effort to keep the label in sync with actual HA status - whenever the core of Vault notices it no longer holds the HA lock it will notify and attempt to update the label right away. * If that update fails, it will retry every 5 seconds until a different update for that label is needed. * This likely not specific to Raft - any HABackend implementation notifies the registration component in the same way. I removed the raft label as it's really to do with the label-updating logic in `serviceregistration/kubernetes`. So in general the following anomalies may occur currently: 1. An old leader that is partitioned from both the other vault nodes and the K8s API server will _remain marked as active until the partition heals_ as well as the new leader that takes it's place. 2. A leader pod a a machine that abruptly powers off will continue to be marked as active in K8s labels until a new pod is scheduled, and the replacement Vault process comes up and resets it. Both of these mean that in practice it will be possible to observe 10s of second or minutes of multiple pods labelled active in K8s under certain circumstances. Attempting to do better than this would be rather complicated in general so it's worth understanding if this is a troublesome-enough issue to warrant that work. Last question for @WatsongRB though: in your case how long did you observe the "double label" in your cluster? The flaky network we see in evidence in your logs could explain why it took a while to update the label correctly, but once the network eventually stabilized it should have resolved itself. Is that what you saw or is there additionally a possible bug to investigate?
WatsongRB: _"what is the actual problem this causes you operationally?"_ Interactions with Vault, (e.g. secret read/write), are not possible. One developer reported the following error: "failed to persist packed storage entry: node is not the leader" One QA team member reported the following error: "error occurred:\\n\\t* node is not the leader" On two different Kubernetes clusters/Vault installations. This is using "Vault Sharp": https://github.com/rajanadar/VaultSharp _"in your case how long did you observe the "double label" in your cluster?"_ I observed the state for 10 - 15 minutes, during which the double label remained. I did not observe the issue resolve itself. The problem happens rarely and, unfortunately, I do not know how to reproduce it. I have not encountered the issue again for at least several months.
banks: Thanks @WatsongRB that is really useful!
banks: Looking at the logs here both servers actually become leader and loose it again at least a couple of times across this short period. I _think_ Vault-2 actually gets stuck in an invalid state which is the real bug here: ``` 2022-11-24T10:24:43.128Z [ERROR] core.raft: failed to rotate TLS key: error="failed to write keyring: node is not the leader" ***This last error repeats endlessly*** ``` It lost leadership _while it was still running postUnseal_ having won an election and it seems like it happened at just such a time that it never actually transistioned it's state correctly. If you compare it to the other server, vault-2 hits raft level log `storage.raft: failed to contact quorum of nodes, stepping down` but it never makes it to the core state. We know because we never see `core: leadership lost, stopping active operation`. Since the core of Vault never knew it was no longer the active node it never even attempted to update it's label in Vault. So I think the real issue here is not the potential for slightly stale K8s labels given all of the above discussion, but that in this (presumably rare) case you managed to hit a bug which left the old leader in a broken state where it is no longer the raft leader but also can't complete step down and get it's core back to non-active mode. That's probably worth additional investigation, though like you said it's probably not going to be easy to reproduce and reliant on exact timings. Given this, I think it's best to change the issue title and labels to reflect that the core bug here is around Raft + Vault step down getting stuck not the K8s labels in particular. > I did not observe the issue resolve itself. So based on my logic here, I'd guess that this only resolved itself after you restated the old leader pod or similar. Is that true?
WatsongRB: Yes. When the Vault pods are restarted, the issue resolves itself.
banks: I'm looking into this a bit more and _assuming the logs provided are complete and not filtering anything_ I think the issue is even deeper: it seems like Vault-2 (the first log) lost leadership at raft layer but failed to even notify the Core HA routine that is watching the active node lock. I say that based on the lack of observed logs. For example if you look at Vault-0 log you see all of these after it looses leadership: ``` 2022-11-24T09:20:09.296Z [WARN] storage.raft: failed to contact quorum of nodes, stepping down 2022-11-24T09:20:09.296Z [INFO] storage.raft: entering follower state: follower="Node at vault-0.vault-internal:8201 [Follower]" leader= 2022-11-24T09:20:09.296Z [INFO] storage.raft: aborting pipeline replication: peer="{Voter vault-1 vault-1.vault-internal:8201}" 2022-11-24T09:20:09.296Z [INFO] storage.raft: aborting pipeline replication: peer="{Voter vault-2 vault-2.vault-internal:8201}" 2022-11-24T09:20:09.296Z [WARN] core: leadership lost, stopping active operation 2022-11-24T09:20:09.296Z [INFO] core: pre-seal teardown starting 2022-11-24T09:20:09.797Z [INFO] core: stopping raft active node 2022-11-24T09:20:09.797Z [INFO] rollback: stopping rollback manager 2022-11-24T09:20:09.797Z [INFO] core: pre-seal teardown complete ``` But for Vault-2 (first set of logs) we never even see `core: leadership lost, stopping active operation` which is the first thing that happens after the core is notified about the active node lock being lost. So the bug seems to be not even in Vault core but specifically in the way our `raft` backend notifies about leadership changes in it's HA Lock implementation. Two other interesting observations: 1. While this was now reported on a fairly old version of Vault, I don't see any changes in the code paths around `raft` HA locking that I'm hypothesizing are the most likely culprits here. 2. Even on `Vault-0` there are three other times it lost quorum in the log excerpt here and one of them also doesn't appear to notify core for over 40 seconds before it regains leadership again: (see `2022-11-24T09:19:02.576Z [WARN] storage.raft: failed to contact quorum of nodes, stepping down`). That makes this seem like this is less a freak occurrence that might only occur in extremely unlikely circumstances because it seems it happened twice on two different nodes about 5 mins apart in this case! It was just only a problem on the node that ended up not being leader and so remained out-of-sync. This cluster seems to have had some relatively extreme connectivity issues during this time - enough to regularly exceed 2.5seconds with no heartbeats but connected enough to actually keep electing a new leader after a few minutes. @WatsongRB if you recall any of the following it might help work out what it might take to understand this failure more and just how it could be triggered: * Did you ever work out why this incident occurred? To get so many timeouts like that It seems like either the network between these pods was extremely disrupted (but not completely down) for an extended period (many minutes), _or_ it's possible that the CPUs on these hosts were totally overwhelmed and unable to schedule goroutines fast enough (but to get 2.5min delays that would have needed to be relatively extreme!). Do you have any metrics of recollection of what the resource utilization was like? * Can you confirm the logs you posted don't have anything filtered? i.e. you posted every log that Vault output between the first and last log lines? (just to make sure I'm not jumping to wrong conclusions about missing log lines). * Can you give us an idea of the workload on this cluster: rough number of mounts, rough idea of what types of requests it was handling and rough volume etc.?
WatsongRB: _• Did you ever work out why this incident occurred? / Do you have any metrics of recollection of what the resource utilization was like?_ - A heavily overprovisoned VMWare VSphere cluster on which the physical hosts are all too often maxed out on CPU, resulting in containers running slowly. - For a period, (not sure whether it affected back then), Kubernetes clusters were being generated by pipelines that had a conflicting Pod IP pool vs part of the company network, (the cluster often ran fine initially and then massive inter pod communication problems would appear). _• Can you confirm the logs you posted don't have anything filtered? i.e. you posted every log that Vault output between the first and last log lines? (just to make sure I'm not jumping to wrong conclusions about missing log lines)._ The logs are not filtered. The excepts are from the time/date on the first line seen in the opening post to the time/date on the last line seen in the opening post. Outside of the start and end times/date in those excerpts, I did not include. But there are no lines missing within the excerpts.

title: /sys/quotas/rate-limit does not allow multiple rate-limits with different properties
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The [/sys/quotas/rate-limit](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/rate-limit-quotas) endpoint does not allow multiple rate-limit configurations with the same path._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Make a namespace._x000D_
_x000D_
```shell_x000D_
curl --header "X-Vault-Token: ..." --request POST http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/namespaces/ns1_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
2. Add a rate-limit for that namespace._x000D_
_x000D_
```shell_x000D_
curl --header "X-Vault-Token: ..." --request POST http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/quotas/rate-limit/first \_x000D_
--data "path=ns1" \_x000D_
--data "rate=100"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
3. Add another rate-limit for that namespaces._x000D_
_x000D_
```shell_x000D_
curl --header "X-Vault-Token: ..." --request POST http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/quotas/rate-limit/second \_x000D_
--data "path=ns1" \_x000D_
--data "rate=1000" \_x000D_
--data "interval=60"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
I was expecting status `204`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: Vault v1.12.1+ent (d5c023cac2ecfb691b92082696e4b256dbab4a84), built 2022-10-28T12:10:32Z_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version: Vault v1.12.1+ent (d5c023cac2ecfb691b92082696e4b256dbab4a84), built 2022-10-28T12:10:32Z_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: CentOS 8 (x86_64)_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
storage "raft" {_x000D_
  path    = "/vault/data"_x000D_
  node_id = "vault-a-1"_x000D_
  retry_join {_x000D_
    leader_api_addr = "http://x:8200"_x000D_
  }_x000D_

  }_x000D_

}_x000D_
_x000D_

top_3_comments_text: VioletHynes: Hi there! You're right - we do not allow multiple quotas on the same path. Only a single rate limit quota can apply to a given request, so we do not allow you to make multiple quotas for the same path as a result. Ultimately, if you're trying to make two quotas for the same path where one has a limit of 50 and another has a limit of 500 within the same interval, the second quota is obsolete. The fix you posted was to prevent the creation of two quotas with the same factors, i.e. would result in creating a situation where there wasn't a unique quota for a single request. In other words, this is expected behaviour and not a bug. I hope that makes sense! I'm going to close based on this explanation - feel free to ask if things are unclear, though.
