title: Any plans to implement/allow HEAD for API requests that allow GET?
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I have verified empirically that a HTTP `GET` request to `/v1/{secret-engine-mount}/data/{secret-name}` works, while the corresponding `HEAD` does not where Vault server returns 405. Admittedly, this may be due to [default] capabilities configured on the server -- I am running `vault server -dev`.I think in general a HTTP server could always trivially and as a rule support `HEAD` method for requests for which `GET` is allowed. That would just be a client not needing a response body, normally. Saves on the overhead for both the server and the client. Besides it's a trivial thing to implement, arguably -- at the simplest, just omit the body if the method is `HEAD`. Use cases include client wanting to determine if a secret (with given path) exists (`2xx` HTTP status code) or doesn't (HTTP status code `404`)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Implement (or allow) `HEAD` requests for those resources for which `GET` is allowed._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Hard to say -- I want to determine if a secret that corresponds to a given secret path, exists -- I could issue a `GET` but ignore the response, but if the secret is large, that's overhead for transmission of the entire secret, not to mention a security factor (if I didn't actually need to read the secret value), also in cases where a principal may be allowed to check whether a secret exists but not actually _access_ (read) it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
No, the above should pretty much cover it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
No additional context, to the best of my understanding.
top_3_comments_text: maxb: (Note: I'm not a HashiCorp employee, just an interested 3rd party Vault user) What practical benefit do you seek to derive from the proposed feature, though? You've made mention of "overhead", but let's be realistic here - JSON marshalling and network transmission of small amounts of data (and the vast majority of Vault data is small) is not usually a major overhead. You've proposed that it might be trivial to implement - but it's only trivial to implement if it's a rather basic implementation that does all the request processing, and then throws away the result, resulting in fairly limited benefit. It's also necessary to consider that there are Vault endpoints - e.g. `ad/creds/:role_name` which conditionally perform write operations to backend systems during a `GET` request - if changing a password in an external system is needed to initially obtain it or comply with configured TTLs. Since Vault is a plugin architecture, it's difficult to enumerate which `GET` requests actually might cause internal side-effects - there are probably more in plugins I'm not familiar with. You've implied near the end of your post, that you'd like to see it be possible to write policy that allows `HEAD` but not `GET` - that's another way this stops being trivial. In conclusion, then, I think this issue is unlikely to go anywhere without more details of concrete use-cases for the proposed feature. | amn: Appreciate the elaborate response and explanations, thank you. This is not an issue I consider critical by any stretch -- certainly in practice I can get by issuing `GET` requests and ignore/discard the response body, in absence of support for the `HEAD` method. About my use case: I am implementing a very simple Linux file system over [FUSE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filesystem_in_Userspace) that maps Vault secrets to folders and secret key-value pairs to files. We have services that are written to require access to secrets _as files_, hence the motivation for such a file system. For obvious security reasons we want to avoid storing secrets as files on persistent storage (i.e. your "regular" file system) specifically, opting for a FUSE-mounted "virtual" file system instead with Vault being the [secure] backing storage there. As the file system responds to requests with arbitrary file/folder paths assumed to map to a secret or a key-value pair under one, practically, with `HEAD` I'd be able to just determine whether a corresponding secret even exists with a given path -- for some path requests I don't need the _data_ or much of _metadata_, only to determine whether there _is or isn't_ a corresponding secret in the Vault. Like I said, this isn't a critical issue, I am merely taking the opportunity to elaborate. I did not understand what you tried to describe with `GET` requests that may have internal side effects, but I should mention that HTTP requires `GET` to be [_idempotent_](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#idempotent.methods). This property should greatly help with any invariants during request processing that should in turn help with implementing processing of corresponding `HEAD`, at "no extra charge", ideally. But this of course depends on how Vault implements request processing in the first place, admittedly. Regarding policy, and this is a digression -- I had not found out whether Vault *prevents* me from doing `HEAD` requests that it otherwise supports, because the method isn't "whitelisted", or whether the latter method isn't supported in the first place. That's what prompted the speculation, but I admit that even if implemented, it would make sense to control this through policy -- `HEAD` doesn't have to require actual access to the resource the way a `GET` request implies, so one could have finer-grained security controls with that. | maxb: Thanks for all that additional information. I think a critical decision for you will be to decide whether you only need this to work for the Vault KV secrets engine, or if you are trying to make something that will cater for other parts of the Vault API as well. The Vault KV secrets engine is at least somewhat similar to a filesystem. Not entirely - here are a few notable differences: * You can have both a "file" and a "directory" of the same name, differentiated only by the presence or absence of a trailing slash * "Directories" have no real existence of their own. There's no such thing as an empty directory, as they immediately vanish when the last contained file is removed. Nor can you create an empty directory, they spontaneously appear when a file with a suitable path is being created. * The "list" operation exclusively lists directories. If you list "foobar", Vault will transparently add on an extra trailing slash, and give you the results as if you listed "foobar/" - even if "foobar/" doesn't exist. Other parts of the Vault API are even less like a filesystem. There are write-only endpoints for example, and the discovery APIs for finding out what APIs exist tend to require human intelligence to interpret - not something that can be easily processed into a directory listing. ---- **On idempotency** I'm well aware of what the HTTP spec says, but Vault arguably breaks this for some endpoints. If I make the request `GET /v1/ad/creds/foobar`, Vault may reach out to my Active Directory server and change the password of the `foobar` account. It would be *surprising* if a `HEAD` request triggered that, which it would, in the "request processing as normal but discard the result" implementation of `HEAD` requests.

title: RabbitMQ engine should use Orphan tokens
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Username and password generated by RabbitMQ Engine gets deleted immediately(1sec) if token TTL (which is used to call `vault read rabbitmq-engine/creds/role`) is set to e.g. 1 second._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Make sure username and password are generated by RabbitMQ Engine as orphan. It should not have a parent token to allow tools like ExternalSecrets Operator, Commandline `vault read engine/creds/role` creating RabbitMQ users on demand regardless of the TTL of the token. The specified TTL of RabbitMQ engine should still take care of removing user if TTL expires._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Tried to use the default token TTL (32days) to have valid username and password for a long time but in the end if token TTL expires all created RabbitMQ users gets deleted._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Related to this -> https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/13456_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: maxb: I think rather than orphan tokens, you're actually asking for the leases generated by reading secrets to be orphan leases. There is no direct precedent for this in Vault - the Vault architecture currently specifies that the lifetime of all dynamic secrets is bound to their tokens e.g. in https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/tokens ... ... and yet, I too have encountered a desire for the same behaviour you request at my workplace, in relationship to the database secrets engine, rather than the RabbitMQ one. Even though the Vault architecture currently specifies that the lifetime of all dynamic secrets is bound to their tokens, there are lots of things you can do with Vault that don't return leased dynamic secrets - e.g.: * Generate PKI certificates * Generate SSH certificates * Retrieve credentials from KV stores * Obtain lazily rotated AD passwords from the AD secrets engine When you have a bunch of developers used to those use-cases and then you add one more secrets engine that does return leased dynamic secrets (RabbitMQ for you, Database for me), you suddenly get surprised developers wondering why their credentials are being revoked from under them. Considering your use-case and mine, there may be a case for a new convention in Vault, that would affect every secrets engine that generates dynamic secrets - provide a new configuration option on secrets engine roles, to define whether the generated dynamic credential leases are orphaned from their creating token, or not.

title: Better auditing of dynamic credential backends
body_text:
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
We currently have numerous Vault roles for dynamic credentials, including MySQL, PostgreSQL and AWS. Currently developers are able to login and generate a dynamic credential for either of those backends which is great. However we are missing a view of what credentials users have generated. _x000D_
_x000D_
For example, I login to Vault and request credentials for a MySQL database. Ideally vault would log all details pertaining to the requestee as well as the generated username (or in the case of AWS log out the ACCESS_KEY_ID); both of which are not sensitive information. top_3_comments_text: heatherezell: Hi there! Can you tell me more about your use case here, with using consul-replication for vault replication? Simply replicating the storage will not guarantee consistent results from Vault, as you've seen. | maxb: IIUC, the behaviour observed here actually counts as "Vault functioning as intended". Vault expects and requires that it is the only thing that is writing to its storage, so by having consul-replicate write to storage that is also being used by a running Vault cluster, you create a situation where Vault will not function properly. If you wanted to make this setup work, you would need to build a locking system so that consul-replicate, and Vault in the secondary datacenter, are never both running at the same time. Even then, I'm not totally sure that consul-replicate would be able to preserve the ordering of operations well enough to guarantee it never places the destination Vault storage into a problematic state ... I'm thinking, what if it copies over storage entries encrypted by a new key, before the change to the keyring adding that new key? | alekhrj: I have some queries - I am trying to understand the reason behind caching the nil data. one can be to prevent against DOS attack on non-existent key. Also, I would like to understand what could possibly go wrong if we do not cache nil data as mentioned above - "you create a situation where Vault will not function properly." "I'm thinking, what if it copies over storage entries encrypted by a new key, before the change to the keyring adding that new key?" -> are we talking about the rotation of root key scenario?

maxb: With your questions above, you've skipped past the really big important point to focus on some specific tiny parts of it, so I need to reiterate: The Vault application is **NOT** written to support other software, such as consul-replicate, changing its data store underneath it whilst it is running. You must not run consul-replicate whilst also running any Vault server in the secondary datacenter.
heatherezell: @maxb is correct here (thanks Max!) We cannot guarantee the results you're looking for if you change the storage. Caching, raft membership, and "[eventual consistency](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/enterprise/consistency)" make this something that I don't believe we'll ever support. There are high-availability options available in Enterprise that can approximate what you're looking for (please see the page on Enterprise replication [here](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/enterprise/replication) ) but the way you're attempting to work around it will result in unexpected behavior at best and possible data corruption at worst. I'm going to close this issue now, but please feel free to open a new issue if you have further bug reports or enhancement requests. Thanks! :)
heatherezell: Although you're not using raft, apologies - the Integrated Storage versus Consul page makes it clear that [Consul is all in-memory](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/storage#integrated-storage-vs-consul-as-vault-storage), which further complicates your use case here.

title: Add support for Azure workload identity authentication for auto-unsealing
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
The vault auto-unseal mechanism should support Azure federated identities to connect to an Azure keyvault when this option is used._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Vault should implement and use the Azure federated identities credentials when available to connect to Azure resources (keyvault in particular)._x000D_
I created an issue on the [go-kms-wrapping](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-kms-wrapping/issues/117) repo with a suggested implementation that we are currently running successfully in our cluster._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
We could install vault on a VM setup or run the AAD pod identity v1 solution, which works with vault. However, the first one does not fit with our infrastructure concept and the second solution has been deprecated by Azure._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
We run Azure AKS clusters and use the new Azure workload identity (AAD pod identity v2) to connect k8s service accounts with Azure identities. This uses the Azure federated identity mechanism (magic) to inject the Azure credentials into the pods. Running vault in this configuration and using Azure keyvault for the auto unseal currently doesn't work, as the authentication mechanism isn't supported by vault._x000D_

title: Token auth backend: Support roles that enforce use of an entity ID
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
We recently became interested in using the Token auth backend's "create token with role" API, to allow a privileged orchestrator to create a tightly scoped token for a specific job type. We currently use AppRole for this but dislike this because it is a multi-step operation (create secret ID, redeem secret ID for token) which generates amplified write load to Vault, compared with one-step creation of a batch token, which requires no writes to storage._x000D_
_x000D_
We want to use entity tokens. Although we acknowledge that the client count handling of non-entity tokens has improved in more recent Vault versions (i.e. they no longer count as a separate client for every token, but are bucketed by (namespace, policy set)), the vast majority of our existing tokens are entity tokens, and they are easier to track back to a use-case in audit logs, than non-entity tokens._x000D_
_x000D_
Token roles already provide an `allowed_entity_aliases` option: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/token#allowed_entity_aliases. However, this relies on the code invoking the `auth/token/create/:role_name` API to also re-specify the entity-alias name in the API call. As Vault administrators/consultants we would strongly prefer to be able to advise integrators/developers to just call `auth/token/create/:role_name` rather than having to add on "and you must also pass the parameter `entity_alias=:role_name` even though it seems redundant". We'd also like to avoid needing to write extra `required_parameters` and `allowed_parameters` options into each Vault ACL policy permissioning `auth/token/create/:role_name` to enforce this happens._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
We'd like a new setting that can be configured on Token auth backend roles, which makes the token role *only* produce entity tokens using a specified entity_alias._x000D_
_x000D_
There are several options for actual implementation._x000D_
_x000D_
* Add a new boolean option, e.g. `entity_alias_enforced` which a) can only be true when `allowed_entity_aliases` is non-empty; b) when true and no `entity_alias` is set in the token creation API call, default the `entity_alias` to the first-or-only value set in `allowed_entity_aliases`; c) logic of `allowed_entity_aliases` is still enforced as it is now, so if set to only one value, that value is guaranteed to be set, or if set to multiple values, the user still has a choice but the first value is the default._x000D_
_x000D_
* Add a new string option, e.g. `mandatory_entity_alias` which a) is mutually exclusive with `allowed_entity_aliases`; b) is always used as the `entity_alias`; c) the caller of the token creation API call must either omit the `entity_alias` parameter or set it to the same as the mandatory value._x000D_
_x000D_
* Change the implicit default behaviour when `allowed_entity_aliases` is set to match that of `allowed_policies`. When `allowed_policies` is set, but no policies are specified in the token creation API call, the value of `allowed_policies` is **automatically** used. Make it so the (first-or-only) value of `allowed_entity_aliases` was also automatically used if none were specified. This would be a compatibility break, so normally I wouldn't even suggest it, except for the prior art of `allowed_policies` within the same endpoint already working this way. Semantically, this is equivalent to the first bullet, except without the new boolean option to toggle the behaviour off or on.

title: Feature Request: Secret References (Secrets that reference other secrets)
body_text:
TLDR - It would be useful to have secrets that are a "pointer" / "link" to another secret similar to how file links work on a filesystem._x000D_
_x000D_
### Overview_x000D_
There are many ways to organize secrets in vault. Two such ways are organizing by *consumer* (reader) and *producer* (owner)._x000D_
_x000D_
When organizing by **consumer** Vault may be structured like the example in the [Recommended Pattern for Vault ACL Policy Path Templates](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/recommended-patterns/pattern-policy-templates) documentation:_x000D_
_x000D_
`secret/<namespace>/<application>[/<secret>]`_x000D_
_x000D_
In this model every application has its own secret or set of secrets. It makes access straight forward at the cost of maintenance when values change. Should many applications share the same secret then when a credential is rotated it must be updated in all of the secrets of applications that use it._x000D_
_x000D_
When organizing by **owner** Vault may be structured like something below:_x000D_
_x000D_
`secret/<line_of_business>/<team>/[.../]<secret>`_x000D_
_x000D_
In this model a credential only exists once within a folder structure that relates to the owner of the secret. Updating the secret becomes straight forward as there is a single source of record for the value. This comes at the cost of complexity when consuming the secret - each application must maintain a catalog of secrets it needs to pull._x000D_
_x000D_
### Possible Solution : Secret References_x000D_
It's possible to get the best-of-both-worlds of the two approaches above by supporting secret "views". The view would represent a read-only view on a collection of secrets that can be read at an alias path. Applications would point to a "view" in Vault. _x000D_
_x000D_
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17504314/212110000-71343bc0-57b7-455d-984a-5e4687bfdc29.png)_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
Consider an example:_x000D_
_x000D_
`secret/it-dba/oracle-team/myorg-microservice-database-creds`_x000D_
* Contains keys for username and password owned and maintained by the oracle DBA team to connect to a shared database_x000D_
_x000D_
`secret/it-enterprise/user-management/userservice-creds`_x000D_
* Contains keys for username and password owned and maintained by the Enterprise Services user management team_x000D_
_x000D_
`Secret Ref: secret/cool-app-suite/microservice1/database-creds` -> `secret/it-dba/oracle-team/myorg-microservice-database-creds`_x000D_
* Refers to the contents of secret/it-dba/oracle-team/myorg-microservice-database-creds_x000D_
_x000D_
`Secret Ref: secret/cool-app-suite/microservice2/database-creds` -> `secret/it-dba/oracle-team/myorg-microservice-database-creds`_x000D_
* Refers to the contents of secret/it-dba/oracle-team/myorg-microservice-database-creds_x000D_
_x000D_
`Secret Ref: secret/cool-app-suite/microservice3/rest-creds` -> `secret/it-enterprise/user-management/userservice-creds`_x000D_
* Refers to the contents of secret/it-enterprise/user-management/userservice-creds_x000D_
_x000D_
In this example the password for the microservice-database only exists in one location. Updating the value thus becomes straight forward. Additionally, since applications use references to other secrets it's easy for a consumer to access anything it needs within the context of a folder optimized for reads._x000D_
_x000D_
Access control would occur in two places. First the reference must be granted access to read the secret it is referencing. Second, the alias path to the reference must have a policy setup for consumers to use it. Any such policy will always be a subset of the permissions granted to the targeted value._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
### Workaround_x000D_
It's possible to make up for the cases above through external systems in vault. In the case of secrets organized by **consumer** a credential rotation system must keep a catalog of all locations in vault where a secret must be updated. In the case of secrets organized by **owner** each application must keep a catalog of all secret paths it needs and pull them._x000D_
_x000D_
These workarounds could be avoided if vault supported secret references_x000D_

title: Generating credentials for MSSQL on AWS RDS, one host to many databases
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Our current AWS RDS environment has a single MSSQL RDS instance with multiple databases on it.  In the existing workflow, users must request a set of credentials for each database on the RDS instance.  _x000D_
_x000D_
This is fine for end users that only need access to a single database for a single application.  _x000D_
It's not ideal for administrative users who many have to run migrations across multiple databases at once.  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
The ideal solution is one of the following - _x000D_
_x000D_
1 - Vault is made aware of all databases on an MSSQL RDS instance via configuration, or can generate a list of all user (non-system) databases.  Once that list is known, Vault can create a set of credentials with the same level of access (readonly, read/write, owner) to all databases on the list without further prompting._x000D_
_x000D_
2 - Vault allows the creation_statement to contain more complex T-SQL code, so that we can build the appropriate commands ourselves to do the same process, similar to the following _x000D_
_x000D_
`_x000D_
      creation_statements = <<-SQL_x000D_
      USE [master];_x000D_
_x000D_
      CREATE LOGIN [{{name}}] WITH PASSWORD = '{{password}}';_x000D_
      DECLARE @dbname VARCHAR(50)   _x000D_
      DECLARE @statement NVARCHAR(max)_x000D_
_x000D_
      DECLARE db_cursor CURSOR _x000D_
      LOCAL FAST_FORWARD_x000D_
      FOR  _x000D_
      SELECT name_x000D_
      FROM sys.databases_x000D_
      WHERE name NOT IN ('master','model','msdb','tempdb','distribution','rdsaadmin')  _x000D_
      AND state_desc = 'ONLINE'_x000D_
      OPEN db_cursor  _x000D_
      FETCH NEXT FROM db_cursor INTO @dbname  _x000D_
      WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0  _x000D_
      BEGIN  _x000D_
_x000D_
      SELECT @statement = N'use ['+ @dbname +'];'+ 'CREATE USER ['+ {{name}} +'] FOR LOGIN [' + {{name}} +'];EXEC sp_addrolemember N''db_owner'', [' + {{name}} +']' _x000D_
      exec sp_executesql @statement_x000D_
_x000D_
      FETCH NEXT FROM db_cursor INTO @dbname  _x000D_
      END  _x000D_
      CLOSE db_cursor  _x000D_
      DEALLOCATE db_cursor _x000D_
_x000D_
      ALTER SERVER ROLE [localadmin] ADD MEMBER [{{name}}];_x000D_
_x000D_
      SQL_x000D_
`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
We have attempted option 2 above, however Vault does not allow the code to run.  We have not been able to figure out why._x000D_
We also have the option of manually maintaining the creation_statement to include all the necessary databases per instance, but that is tedious to maintain as databases may be added/removed as needs change._x000D_
_x000D_

title: Vault Agent - Prometheus PushGateway support
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We are using Vault Agent for retrieving secrets from Vault and rendering them into the files on a machine. Vault Agent is started during the deployment process and after the successful secret render is closed (with `-exit-after-auth` option)._x000D_
_x000D_
Since Vault Agent usually is closed quickly, there is no stable way to expose metrics via Prometheus endpoint. We are interested in the metrics since based on them we could set up alerts for auth errors._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I want to be able to push metrics from Vault Agent directly to Prometheus via Prometheus Pushgateway. I know that Pushgateway is not recommended way to work with metrics. But for short-lived jobs, there are no other alternatives._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I do not know a good alternative solution. The only possible solution I see is to set up scrape periodicity for Vault to some veeeery frequent value - but it's too ugly and kinda unstable._x000D_
_x000D_
Another option is just not to finish `vault agent` process and just restart it during the deployment process. Possibly, secret re-render could be done without a restart but the corresponding question is unanswered yet - https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/manually-trigger-secret-rendering-with-vault-agent/45395 ._x000D_

title: Vault OpenAPI is incorrect for new PKI secrets engine endpoints
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The Vault OpenAPI generator relies on reverse-engineering path regexps to correctly generate the OpenAPI document._x000D_
_x000D_
Several regexps used in the new (circa 1.11) PKI secrets engine are now too complicated for the OpenAPI generator to handle correctly._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Mount a PKI secrets engine_x000D_
2. Examine the generated OpenAPI_x000D_
3. Observe these clearly incorrect paths:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
/pki//delta_x000D_
/pki//delta/pem_x000D_
/pki//der_x000D_
/pki//json_x000D_
/pki//pem_x000D_
/pki/internal|exported_x000D_
/pki/{issuer_ref}/crl/pem|/der|/delta/pem_x000D_
/pki/{issuer_ref}/der|/pem_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The Vault OpenAPI generator should generate a document which accurately describes the Vault API._x000D_
_x000D_
In order to achieve this, it may well be helpful to define a strict subset of regexp syntax which can be used in Vault path regexps._x000D_
_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: maxb: These are the regexes that are currently being misinterpreted: ``` `crl(/pem|/delta(/pem)?)?` # pathFetchCRL "issuer/" + framework.GenericNameRegex(issuerRefParam) + "(/der|/pem|/json)?" # pathGetIssuer "issuer/" + framework.GenericNameRegex(issuerRefParam) + "/crl(/pem|/der|/delta(/pem|/der)?)?" # pathGetIssuerCRL "keys/generate/(internal|exported|kms)" # pathGenerateKey ``` | maxb: Further investigation shows that the following regexes are also being misinterpreted - they just result in paths which are less obviously wrong than the other group: ``` "issuers/import/(cert|bundle)" # pathImportIssuer `cert/(crl|delta-crl)` # pathFetchCRLViaCertPath ```

title: A new `vault patch` CLI command is needed
body_text:
One of the more helpful things about the Vault CLI, is that it mostly provides elegant CLI syntax for performing various HTTP API calls._x000D_
_x000D_
However, in recent Vault versions, the HTTP `PATCH` verb has started to be used. Support for this is **missing** in the Vault CLI._x000D_
_x000D_
I'm not referring specifically to KV v2 `PATCH`, for which there is `vault kv patch ...`. Rather, I'm thinking about APIs such as `pki/issuer/:issuer_ref` which require the `PATCH` method to perform reconfiguration of options, without wiping everything that has already been set. There is no way to invoke this from the CLI._x000D_
_x000D_
I propose the existing family of "basic HTTP operation" Vault CLI commands (read, write, list, delete) should be supplemented by the addition of `vault patch`, which functions identically to `vault write`, except that it uses the `PATCH` HTTP method.

title: `-output-policy` CLI flag is broken in multiple ways
body_text:
I've noticed the recently added `-output-policy` CLI flag. Unfortunately, the implementation suffers from multiple problems causing it to produce incorrect answers._x000D_
_x000D_
# Does not work for `vault kv ...` commands_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault kv get -output-policy kv/foobar_x000D_
This output flag requires the success of a preflight request _x000D_
to determine the version of a KV secrets engine. Please _x000D_
re-run this command with a token with read access to kv/foobar_x000D_
Unable to generate policy from command_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
(Contrary to the message, a token was supplied to this operation.)_x000D_
_x000D_
# Incorrect answers for `vault list` commands_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault list -output-policy something_x000D_
path "something" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
It should be recommending `list`, not `read`._x000D_
_x000D_
# Failure to recommend `sudo` for `auth/token/accessors/`_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault list -output-policy auth/token/accessors/_x000D_
path "auth/token/accessors" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Because the operation is a ListOperation and therefore defined with a trailing slash, but the slash has been stripped._x000D_
_x000D_
# Hardcoded assumptions about PKI secrets engines_x000D_
_x000D_
It suggests `sudo` for paths in the PKI secrets engine that need it, but **only** if the secrets engine is mounted at `pki/` exactly - if mounted at any other path, it does not._x000D_
_x000D_
# Failure to recommend `sudo` for paths in namespaces_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault read -output-policy ns1/sys/auth_x000D_
path "ns1/sys/auth" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
# In summary_x000D_
_x000D_
* The current approach of using adhoc regexps hardcoded into the api package is too fragile - a successful implementation of -output-policy needs to be able to query the server to find out if a path is `sudo`-protected - probably via a new `sys/` API. This could also enable it to give a clear indication of which endpoints actually support the `create` capability._x000D_
_x000D_
* The code needs to understand the difference between a ReadOperation and a ListOperation._x000D_
_x000D_
* Special handling around KV preflight requests is needed._x000D_

## ~~Removal of `generic_mount_paths` parameter incomplete~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~I opened #18558 to fix.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
EDIT: Resolved by reverting to re-introduce the functionality._x000D_
_x000D_
## ~~Introduction of overly broad regexp into CLI `-output-policy` processing~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~Following this change, the `-output-policy` CLI flag will now suggest that the `sudo` capability is needed for any path at all that ends in `/root`, including, for example, some ad-hoc user data in a KV secrets engine. Arguably this is due to a pre-existing defect in `-output-policy` relying too much on assumptions, though. I've also reported this in an issue about `-output-policy` - #18559 .~~_x000D_
_x000D_
EDIT: Resolved by revert._x000D_
_x000D_
## ~~Inconsistent handling of singleton mounts~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~The change to the OpenAPI singles out `sys/` and `identity/` for special handling, keeping those paths as literals in the OpenAPI document, when everything else is parameterised. I do realise that this was a pre-existing conditional in the code before this PR, but by forcibly opting everyone in to `generic_mount_paths`, it has now become much more prominent.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~If `sys/` and `identity/` are going to get special handling, shouldn't the other two special singleton mounts, `auth/token/` and `cubbyhole/` get the same treatment?~~_x000D_
_x000D_
EDIT: Resolution proposed in #18663 _x000D_
_x000D_
## ~~Inconsistent handling of KV secret engines~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~If I mount a KV secrets engine at, for example, `kv-v2/`, I end up with an OpenAPI document which contains `/{kv-v2_mount_path}/` in its paths, but `secret_mount_path` in its defined parameters. They don't match.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~This is because these two bits of code are inconsistent:~~_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/159b60a181bae2d54c666ad09ca607988e4bf5c5/sdk/framework/openapi.go#L268-L271_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/159b60a181bae2d54c666ad09ca607988e4bf5c5/vault/logical_system.go#L4577-L4584_x000D_
_x000D_
~~In the first, the engine **type** is being checked (yes, `requestResponsePrefix` is actually set to the plugin type, and not the plugin mount path... that is confusing too.)~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~In the second, the engine **path** is being checked.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~Hence, the conditions are different.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~I suggest the best fix here would be to just delete the `kv` -> `secret` special case entirely - I can't think of a good reason for it to exist.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
EDIT: Resolved by removal of that code._x000D_
_x000D_
## ~~Inconsistent insertion of `<mount-point>_mount_path` parameter~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~The addition of the `<mount-point>_mount_path` parameter to the OpenAPI parameters collection is handled in sdk/framework/ code.~~_x000D_
~~The patching of the operation path to include the `/{<mount-point>_mount_path}/` template is handled in Vault core code!~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~This mismatch causes multiple problems.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~The patching of the operation path **only** occurs in the code path for the `sys/internal/specs/openapi` endpoint. If, instead, you are retrieving an OpenAPI document for a single backend, or single path on a backend, via the `?help=1` route, each endpoint in the response includes this bogus addition:~~_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
        "parameters": [_x000D_
          {_x000D_
            "name": "_mount_path",_x000D_
            "description": "Path where the backend was mounted; the endpoint path will be offset by the mount path",_x000D_
            "in": "path",_x000D_
            "schema": {_x000D_
              "type": "string",_x000D_
              "default": ""_x000D_
            }_x000D_
          },_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
~~a parameter called `_mount_path`.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~The other problem caused by this, is that since half of the implementation is in the sdk/framework/ code, external plugins need to be rebuilt against a newer sdk version to pick up the change!~~_x000D_
_x000D_
~~For both of these reasons, I think it is critical that the addition of the parameter definition to the OpenAPI document be moved from the sdk/framework/ code to happen instead in `vault/logical_system.go`, in the same place as where the paths are prefixed.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
EDIT: Resolution proposed in #18663 _x000D_
_x000D_
## Lack of sanitization of esoteric characters in mount paths_x000D_
_x000D_
~~Suppose I have a secrets engine mounted at `foo/bar/baz/` - the current OpenAPI will end up with a parameter named `{foo/bar/baz_mount_path}`. Now, admittedly I can't find anything in the OpenAPI spec to say which characters are permitted in path template variables - but I imagine many people would intuitively expect parameter names to not contain special characters in this way.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
EDIT: The comment added in #18663 clarifying that `generic_mount_paths` is only really useful in a particular niche use case makes this far less important, to the point I'm happy to consider this closed.

title: Vault Agent cert auth method never reloads x509 key pair
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault Agent's cert auth method relies on local TLS certificates. Like any certificates, these have an expiration date. Vault Agent is great for automatically renewing certificates. Though it seems like Vault Agent caches the key pair it uses to authenticate and never rereads it from disk. This causes it to authenticate with expired credentials, even if the credentials were renewed between the last attempt and the next._x000D_
_x000D_
I was able to track the issue down to these lines:_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/159b60a181bae2d54c666ad09ca607988e4bf5c5/command/agent/auth/cert/cert.go#L110-L113_x000D_
_x000D_
The block of code above guards the `ConfigureTLS` method call that is responsible for reading the x509 key pair from disk:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/159b60a181bae2d54c666ad09ca607988e4bf5c5/command/agent/auth/cert/cert.go#L127-L130_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Setup a Vault cluster with a private certificate authority._x000D_
2. Configure the `vault-cluster` PKI role e.g. `vault write pki/roles/vault-cluster allowed_domains="vault.service.consul" max_ttl="24h"`_x000D_
3. Configure Vault Agent on a Vault server using the configuration file at the bottom of this issue. The initial key pair for Vault Agent would need to be generated using the PKI secrets engine in Vault. A short TTL is desirable here._x000D_
_x000D_
Alternatively, it might be possible to create a new unit test in [cert_test.go](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/159b60a181bae2d54c666ad09ca607988e4bf5c5/command/agent/auth/cert/cert_test.go) to verify the issue._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
I would expect it to reload the TLS key pair on every authentication attempt, or at the very least renew it after a % of the certificate's lifetime._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.12.2 (415e1fe3118eebd5df6cb60d13defdc01aa17b03)_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: `Linux 5.4.0-132-generic #148-Ubuntu SMP Mon Oct 17 16:02:06 UTC 2022 x86_64`_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
# Vault Agent configuration_x000D_
vault {_x000D_
  address     = "https://vault.service.consul:8200"_x000D_
  ca_cert     = "/opt/vault/tls/ca.crt.pem"_x000D_
  client_cert = "/opt/vault/tls/vault.crt.pem"_x000D_
  client_key  = "/opt/vault/tls/vault.key.pem"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
auto_auth {_x000D_
  method "cert" {_x000D_
    config {_x000D_
      name = "vault-cluster"_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  }_x000D_
_x000D_
  sink "file" {_x000D_
    config {_x000D_
      path = "/opt/vault/data/vault-token"_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
template {_x000D_
  source      = "/opt/vault/tls/vault.crt.pem.tmpl"_x000D_
  destination = "/opt/vault/tls/vault.crt.pem"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
template {_x000D_
  source      = "/opt/vault/tls/vault.key.pem.tmpl"_x000D_
  destination = "/opt/vault/tls/vault.key.pem"_x000D_
  command     = "/bin/kill --signal HUP $(systemctl show --property MainPID --value vault)"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The [docs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent/autoauth/methods/cert) mention populating the `client_cert` and `client_key` fields to prevent caching. However, I see nothing in the source code that would indicate that the cached client is ever invalidated, so I can't imagine that being the problem here._x000D_

title: consistent output ie version across hashicorp tools
body_text:
#### Feature Description_x000D_
_x000D_
This isn't vault specific, but is general ask for Hashicorp tools to be consistent in their responses to common/shared commands like `<command> --version`. At the moment boundary, consul, vault, terraform, and packer all respond differently to `--version`:_x000D_
_x000D_
* boundary (0.11.2): will not accept the `--version` flag, but supports a hidden `version` command:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ boundary version_x000D_
_x000D_
Version information:_x000D_
  Git Revision:        02e410af7a2606ae242b8637d8a02754f0a5f43e_x000D_
  Version Number:      0.11.2_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
(whitespace in the original)_x000D_
_x000D_
* consul (1.14.3):_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ consul --version_x000D_
Consul v1.14.3_x000D_
Revision bd257019_x000D_
Build Date 2022-12-13T17:13:55Z_x000D_
Protocol 2 spoken by default, understands 2 to 3 (agent will automatically use protocol >2 when speaking to compatible agents)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
* packer (1.8.5): provides the most succinct answer of all:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ packer --version_x000D_
1.8.5_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
* terraform (1.3.6):_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ terraform --version_x000D_
Terraform v1.3.6_x000D_
on darwin_arm64_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
* vault (1.12.2):_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault --version_x000D_
Vault v1.12.2 (415e1fe3118eebd5df6cb60d13defdc01aa17b03), built 2022-11-23T12:53:46Z_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Every tool presents its own version information with its own unique format and unique build details - some on one line, some output multiple lines, some the version is prefixed with a `v`, some are not._x000D_
_x000D_
#### Use Case(s)_x000D_
_x000D_
It would be nice that within the Hashicorp family of tools one could rely upon a response to `--version` (or other common commands?) without having to parse each command's output uniquely._x000D_
_x000D_
The (admittedly very) specific use case I'm hitting here is a single cookbook that can deploy/upgrade hashicorp agents (consul and vault now, boundary in the future). To see if an agent needs an upgrade (especially on windows...grr), one needs to ask the binary for its version number._x000D_
_x000D_
Distinct parsers that are aware of each tool's quirks are not the worst thing in the world - but ideally each binary could for example, report its version number (and only the version number ala how packer does this) on the first line, and then subsequent lines could provide more details if it wished.

body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_

_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_

_x000D_

At least 404_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (1.9.2):_x000D_

_x000D_

}_x000D_
_x000D_

top_3_comments_text: maxb: The 301 is being generated by default behaviour in the Go HTTP server library that Vault uses. It's not great behaviour for an API (it's more suited to websites), and this isn't the first time it has surprised users, also being reported in #18379 and #18062. | maxb: It would be quite nice to fix this but Go's `net/http.ServeMux` provides no way to customize this behaviour, so it would need a copy/paste of around 250 lines of code from the Go standard library into Vault, to make the necessary modifications. There is also a potential compatibility issue - some clients might be incorrectly relying on this behaviour to silently recover from incorrectly composing URLs containing multiple consecutive slashes. For clarity, I should point out that I do not work for HashiCorp, I'm just an interested user of Vault. Actual HashiCorp staff will need to take a decision on what direction to go in regarding this.

title: OpenAPI defect introduced by extracting request/response bodies to schema references
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
#14217 changed OpenAPI generation to extract the details of the JSON format of requests and responses, from being in-line with the relevant operations, to being defined in a separate portion of the document, and referenced by name._x000D_
_x000D_
Critically, the names assigned to these request/response schemas, are **not sufficiently unique**. This leads to some silently overwriting others, and generating an OpenAPI document that contains lies about actual requests/responses._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Start up a `vault server -dev` - use a 1.13-dev `make dev-ui` build for this, as it seems 1.12 isn't showing responses in the API explorer at all._x000D_
2. Enable an approle auth method_x000D_
3. Open up the API explorer_x000D_
4. Observe the `GET​ /auth​/{approle_mount_path}​/role/{role_name}` endpoint, specifically that it claims its response will look identical to the `GET​ /auth​/{approle_mount_path}​/role` endpoint - these are entirely different endpoints, but the response for one has overwritten the other during OpenAPI generation._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
With the introduction of plugin versioning in Vault 1.12, there is now a new related problem - you could be running multiple different versions of a plugin, which have different parameters for their APIs. The current approach of seeking to flatten all request/response formats into named references becomes even more problematic - you'd have to disambiguate between different versions of request/response for the same endpoint in plugin mounts running different versions._x000D_
_x000D_
For these reasons, I believe the change to use request/response schemas should be reverted, returning to inline definition, which will more reliably associate the correct parameters with each endpoint.
top_3_comments_text: averche: Hi @maxb! You are correct, this is indeed an issue with the current request/response naming function. I believe it should be resolved in #18321, which has a shared naming pattern for `operationId`s, request names and response names. For the examples you mentioned, the following `operationId`s and response names will be generated: ``` GET​ /auth​/{approle_mount_path}​/role OperationID: AppRoleListRoles Response name: AppRoleListRolesResponse GET​ /auth​/{approle_mount_path}​/role/{role_name}` OperationID: AppRoleReadRole Response name: AppRoleReadRoleResponse ``` For a bit of background, we are working on generating client libraries from this OpenAPI spec. Without extracting request and response bodies (and giving them sensible names), openapi generators have no way of knowing what to call these request/response objects in the generated libraries. This results in anonymous structs/classes being generated for requests and responses with meaningless names like `RequestStruct1`. | maxb: Right - but that does need to be balanced with avoiding naming clashes, that result in the incorrect Request/Response objects being associated with some APIs. Let's continue the thread of conversation in #18321, to avoid splitting it between an issue and a PR. | averche: Hi @maxb! The https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/19319 (OpenAPI naming changes) and ~40 related PR's have been successfully merged for all the builtin plugins (both within this repo and in `hashicorp/vault-plugin-*`). As a result, all the OperationID's for built-in plugins and the corresponding request/response names are now unique: ```go GET​ /auth​/{approle_mount_path}​/role OperationID: app-role-list-roles Response name: AppRoleListRolesResponse GET​ /auth​/{approle_mount_path}​/role/{role_name}` OperationID: app-role-read-role Response name: AppRoleReadRoleResponse ``` In general, ``` request name = titleCase(operationID) + "Request" response name = titleCase(operationID) + "Response" ``` Thanks again for bringing up this issue and contributing to the OpenAPI-related work!

title: PKI mounts may end up in a broken state due to intermittent storage errors
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Looks like intermittent storage failures during Vault startup/unseal can lead to PKI mounts ending up in a broken state. Vault will log the following lines:_x000D_
_x000D_
> [ERROR] secrets.pki.pki_2e0e9d63: Failed loading PKI migration status, staying in legacy mode: <..storage error..>_x000D_
> [ERROR] secrets.pki.pki_2e0e9d63: Error during migration of PKI mount: <..storage error..>_x000D_
> [ERROR] core: failed to initialize mount entry: path=pki/ error=<..storage error..>_x000D_
_x000D_
and then the PKI mount is unusable indefinitely, even after the storage becomes healthy._x000D_
When trying to e.g. generate a certificate, the following can be seen from Vault logs: _x000D_
_x000D_
> [INFO]  secrets.pki.pki_0c477ce6: Using legacy CA bundle as PKI migration has not completed._x000D_
_x000D_
and on the caller side: _x000D_
_x000D_
> Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
> 1 error occurred:_x000D_
> 	* could not fetch the CA certificate (was one set?): no legacy cert bundle exists_x000D_
_x000D_
This can be reproduced on latest version (v1.12.2). Looks like the fault can be reproduced on v1.11.x track as well, after the introduction of [initialize() function](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/logical/pki/backend.go#L352) in PKI. I believe the function is not re-executed if it fails, which leads to this problem._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
# 1. Start Vault_x000D_
vault server -config vault.hcl_x000D_
_x000D_
# 2. Initialize Vault_x000D_
vault operator init -key-shares=$shares -key-threshold=$shares_x000D_
_x000D_
# 3. Enable PKI backends_x000D_
create_root_ca  # see below_x000D_
create_sub_ca  # see below_x000D_
_x000D_
# 4. Stop Vault_x000D_
pkill vault_x000D_
_x000D_
# 5. Remove read permissions in PKI backend_x000D_
chmod 200 tmp/vault/vault-data/logical/bc2f917a-8c42-1fe6-808f-36e8d9cf6456/config/_legacyMigrationBundleLog_x000D_
_x000D_
# 6. Start Vault & unseal_x000D_
vault server -config vault.hcl_x000D_
vault operator unseal $key_x000D_
_x000D_
# 7. Observe errors, try to generate cert which fails_x000D_
vault write -format=json sub/issue/example-dot-com common_name="test.example.com" ttl="24h"_x000D_
_x000D_
# 8. Restore permissions in backend_x000D_
chmod 600 tmp/vault/vault-data/logical/bc2f917a-8c42-1fe6-808f-36e8d9cf6456/config/_legacyMigrationBundleLog_x000D_
_x000D_
# 9. PKI mount unusable, generate cert still fails_x000D_
vault write -format=json sub/issue/example-dot-com common_name="test.example.com" ttl="24h"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Intermittent storage errors should be handled. Perhaps the code should try to migrate the PKI backend again at a later stage if the first try was unsuccessful?_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): v1.11.0+_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.11.0+_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: any_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
$ cat vault.hcl _x000D_
_x000D_
storage "file" {_x000D_
    path = "/tmp/vault/vault-data"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address = "127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
  tls_disable = true_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
log_level = "trace"_x000D_
api_addr = "http://127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
PKI configuration:_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
cert_dir=/tmp/vault/vault-certs_x000D_
_x000D_
create_root_ca() {_x000D_
    vault secrets enable pki_x000D_
    vault secrets tune -max-lease-ttl=87600h pki_x000D_
_x000D_
    mkdir -p $cert_dir_x000D_
    vault write -field=certificate pki/root/generate/internal \_x000D_
        common_name="example.com" \_x000D_
        issuer_name="root" \_x000D_
        ttl=87600h > $cert_dir/root.pem_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write pki/roles/root-role allow_any_name=true_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write pki/config/urls \_x000D_
        issuing_certificates="$VAULT_ADDR/v1/pki/ca" \_x000D_
        crl_distribution_points="$VAULT_ADDR/v1/pki/crl"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
create_sub_ca() {_x000D_
    vault secrets enable -path=sub pki_x000D_
    vault secrets tune -max-lease-ttl=43800h sub_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write sub/config/urls \_x000D_
        issuing_certificates="$VAULT_ADDR/v1/sub/ca" \_x000D_
        crl_distribution_points="$VAULT_ADDR/v1/sub/crl"_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write -format=json sub/intermediate/generate/internal \_x000D_
        common_name="example.com Intermediate Authority" \_x000D_
        issuer_name="example-dot-com-intermediate" \_x000D_
        | jq -r '.data.csr' > $cert_dir/sub.csr_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write -format=json pki/root/sign-intermediate \_x000D_
        issuer_ref="root" \_x000D_
        csr=@$cert_dir/sub.csr \_x000D_
        format=pem_bundle ttl="43800h" \_x000D_
        | jq -r '.data.certificate' > $cert_dir/sub.pem_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write sub/intermediate/set-signed certificate=@$cert_dir/sub.pem_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault write sub/roles/example-dot-com \_x000D_
        issuer_ref="$(vault read -field=default sub/config/issuers)" \_x000D_
        allowed_domains="example.com" \_x000D_
        allow_subdomains=true \_x000D_
        max_ttl="720h"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
We have also seen this issue right after the mount point has been enabled, then the error seen is [this one](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/logical/pki/path_root.go#L109). Basically, if [migrateStorage()](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/logical/pki/backend.go#L388) fails, then pkiStorageVersion is never set to 1, so [useLegacyBundleCaStorage](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/logical/pki/backend.go#L398-L426) always returns 0/nil. So it looks like the same issue as above, but a bit more difficult to reproduce due to the timing aspect._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: nsimons: I have a feeling that this is a generic problem with the Initialize()-function logic. The function is executed as a one-shot thing, which if it fails is not retried. So theoretically any backend using Initialize() may exhibit problems if it fails. Code snippets: - startBackend sets the backend to _loaded_ before running Initialize() [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/plugin/backend.go#L178-L183) - But startBackend is only run if _loaded_ is false, [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/plugin/backend.go#L197-L202) I do understand that we cannot run the whole startBackend several times, but should the load/initialize logic be separated into it's own routine that is run until success? Just some thoughts. | cipherboy: To answer this, I think we don't really expect `initialize()` to run multiple times (e.g., until success) in the plugin. This would be a breaking change if implemented globally at the Vault level I believe. Certainly it gets run multiple times over the course of a Vault process, but note that the backend itself gets destroyed and recreated when e.g., cluster leadership changes. Within PKI, I think our expectation was that if something failed during the initialization, we'd let the operator deal with it and optionally reload the plugin. As your reproducer demonstrates, I don't think the PKI backend itself can necessarily resolve the issue, and indeed, Vault itself might not be able to either, so even if we were to re-attempt it, we'd need an upper bound. Fundamentally, I think within the PKI plugin, implementing this ourselves would require hooking _every_ single entry point into the plugin (routes, invalidate, periodic, ...) and checking if we weren't initialized, which seems like a very invasive change for something we might not be able to solve. The fallback behavior is a best-effort to allow _some_ operations to continue, but as you noticed, is by no means complete or sufficient. I wonder if we could limit the fallout a bit @stevendpclark if we don't see a `legacyCABundle` entry? E.g., if we can't read the log due to error, but we do know there is no legacy bundle, could we log the error and move into non-legacy mode anyways? I think we'd have to revert the behavior if we ever introduce a third migration, but given the second migration depends on legacyCABundle as the trigger... Thoughts? | stevendpclark: I tend to agree with @cipherboy's description of the issue. Singling out just the migration log entry I doubt is a realistic use-case of general storage errors, the most likely use case would be the entire path or something else has gone wrong. That leads me to believe the ability to recover just from that bad read would probably be of little value overall and just complicate the code base for little gain imho. I think deferring to the operator in the use-case would be best overall position we should take.

cipherboy: @nsimons It depends now on your Vault version. On Vault 1.11 and before, _all_ mount initialization occurred in parallel. As of a soon-to-be-released Vault 1.11.7 I believe, you can set an envvar to control how many [execute in parallel](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/18410). In 1.12+, due to plugin restructuring, only a single mount initialization occurred at a time, but [with a subsequent PR](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/18244) for 1.12.3+, you should be able to control parallelism there too. The variable is `VAULT_POSTUNSEAL_FUNC_CONCURRENCY` if you want to build a pre-release Vault version and test that. To revive a particular backend, note that you can run a [plugin reload](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/plugins-reload-backend#reload-plugins) with a `scope=global`, to cause it to be reloaded on all nodes, which'll reset the backend and reinitialize it. As noted in the 1.11 PR above, Rollback manager continues to execute in full parallel (after the initial run which sets up mounts on 1.11) -- even in 1.12+. Say you don't set the envvar, and reach say, 50% with storage errors. On second initialization run, you'll now "fix" some amount, say, leaving you with 25% left. Then maybe 12.5%... &c until eventually you get below the threshold to fix this. Which seems weird, as now your consumers are stuck waiting an unknown amount of time, since they don't know which is truly available (part of the 1.12 changes is Vault isn't considered up until all mounts have finished, versus in 1.11 where the mount initialization was done on a first-come basis, other than periodic func triggering them all). Or, you could just set the parallelism limiter to a value which, while slower, would allow you to avoid storage errors. :-) FWIW, storage errors do to concurrency/load/... would make me _really_ cautious to use that backend, as given a high enough load on the cluster normally, I'd expect you to still hit that anyways. Have you benchmarked the cluster and seen if you can reproduce these errors during steady-state operations? --- Looking at #18667 it kinda looks like you have unintentionally -- and that even post-startup, during PKI CA initialization, you still get transitive storage errors as you're just creating so much load. I think perhaps I'd suggest evaluating your storage backend, as _many_ things in Vault would not work ideally under load. E.g., even further, once these are setup, if you use `no_store=false` and generate tons of certs (perhaps EC based CA+leaves for speed), you'll likely hit the same storage transitive errors that might result in certs not being stored (but all the generation having been done, causing high load and forcing clients to retry), or similarly, issues with K/V usage or anything which reads/writes multiple entries. I.e., for any operation, you're going to end up chasing a lot of things trying to get Vault usable on flaky storage backend, which probably won't work out well without transactions and either way will cause lots of retries from clients. Out of curiosity, what storage backend are you using?
nsimons: I've probably been poorly explaining the background, sorry about that! It's not a load issue. We have Vault + ETCD backend running in Kubernetes and are looking to make our deployment more robust by pin-pointing error scenarios and their consequences. We have been striving to have Vault automatically survive sudden and intermittent infrastructure issues, whether it is network delay, disk delay, sudden pod crashes, DNS outage, or generally any of the ETCD failures listed [here](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.5/op-guide/failures/) (e.g. leader election leading to backend service outage). This is very important to us. In our case we have a Kubernetes operator (another microservice) that automatically generates PKI mounts on the request of clients, so the Vault operator/admin is not part of the equation and cannot do the reload. Now it seems that a sudden infrastructure problem during generation of a PKI mount can cause the PKI to never be migrated, yielding it unusable. Vault generally handles infrastructure issues very well, but these two new issues have popped up in Vault 1.11. There was [another issue reported](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-kubernetes/issues/169) in Kubernetes auth method plugin, basically due to the same one-time-execute nature of Initialize(), but fortunately it was fixed. We noticed that several PKI functions (e.g. root CA generation) check whether migration has happened or not, and then errors out. Is there some technical reason why this check couldn't kick off a migration? Just thinking of possible solutions. Edit: Another scenario could be when auto-unseal is in use and Vault goes from sealed to unsealed state during operation, completely unattended. The admin is not present to detect PKI migration failures and resolve them.
nsimons: @cipherboy, I would like to propose a PR where we check whether migration was done inside `periodicFunc`, if not we would try to run the migration. Would such PR be appreciated?
cipherboy: \o hey @nsimons! In discussing this more with the team, we've decided we won't be addressing this ticket. Thank you for the offer of a PR, but we would not merge it. Our concerns are mostly around burden on the Vault cluster and from a position of conservatism. We've had a few incidences where the large number of PKI mounts needing migration caused outages for customers. This manifested mostly as leadership thrashing, causing nodes to quit migrations partway through. Notably, this occurred post-Rollback Manager startup, as the quantity of mounts caused setup to past Rollback Manager starting. In some cases, this was exacerbated by the usage of Seal Wrapping, which we're unable to detect within the plugin itself. While we've added some mitigating controls, using the Rollback Manager (and thus, PKI's PeriodicFunc) in this way, especially without more controls around runtime concurrency limits, would not address the issue. We believe it would likely contribute to workload during PeriodicFunc, putting more pressure on Vault and potentially a Seal Wrap mechanism, leading to even more leadership election problems. While this leaves it up to operators to have monitoring in place to detect and remediate, given the concerns a Vault-initiated automated process could cause, we feel they're best situated to re-attempt (via [reloading of specific mounts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/plugins-reload-backend#reload-plugins)) migration and thus address this problem.
nsimons: Thanks @cipherboy for getting back to me! I wonder if I understand the Vault code correctly. Vault needs to check the migration status after each unseal, regardless if an actual migration needs to be done or not (`pkiStorageVersion` starts out with value `0` each time). An actual migration is not _necessarily_ happening after unseal, Vault simply asks the storage backend for the `migrationInfo`-related keys and then sets `pkiStorageVersion=1` if migration is already done. Surely this use case is not putting a burden on Vault? It's just standard configuration reads. The implications of leaving this to the user are quite drastic. In the case where auto-unseal is used, it would mean that the user would need to develop their own monitoring system that 1) detects that Vault has been unsealed 2) for each PKI backend, create a loop that sends a request to see if the backend has migrated successfully, if not send a reload command, then continue the loop to re-check if migration went through and so on. If this is really the way forward then I would hope to have this documented somewhere in the PKI section.
cipherboy: Right, but go a step deeper: what if a migration _does_ need to occur? We recently bumped `pkiStorageVersion=2` in 1.12. Why would we/operators expect a retry to load the mount post-migration, but not in the event of migration? :-) In the event of a migration needing to occur, the admin still needs that same type of monitoring. Relying on it only in the event of a migration needing to occur would mean it is a much less well tested system than otherwise. Plus, as mentioned before, this is not unique to the PKI engine at all. Transform and AWS Auth also have the same issue. Also, I feel there is a distinction between PKI/Transform/AWS Auth and CertAuth/K8S Auth is that the former are strictly doing migrations on startup and the latter are periodically refreshing configs from other nodes (reloading CRLs and TLS config respectively). The former set of plugins involves storage write operations, the latter appear to only require reads. All in all, shoring up the reliability and availability of the underlying storage system should be considered, IMO.
nsimons: > Why would we/operators expect a retry to load the mount post-migration, but not in the event of migration? :-) The fundamental problem is that we are trying to handle two use cases with the same code logic. 1. We have version upgrades which may cause migrations, so we do not retry due to load concerns. 2. and we have Vault unseal operation which will not cause a migration. The frequency and pre-conditions of these two use cases are vastly different. The first case happen (currently) at most two times, in two specific upgrade scenarios. The operator is knowingly executing the upgrade and is most likely present and can act on the various error scenarios. The operator might even have read the release notes and knows that a PKI migration is about to happen. The second case can happen any time during normal operation, for example in the case of Kubernetes, pod terminations are common place. Sure, the operator might be present to unseal Vault, but might not have the necessary knowledge to recognize PKI initialization failures, nor act on them. Then as I mentioned, we have the unmanaged case with auto-unsealers. I would argue that the second case is much more frequent than the first. In the extreme case, `pkiStorageVersion=2` is the last possible migration for years to come, but Vault will still need to be unsealed in the future. So I am of the strong opinion that the code should cater for the second use case, more so than the first. If load is an issue with the first use case, then I think we ought to make the trade-off that Vault works "asymmetrically" when handling potential retries. If the operator already expects that PKI migrations will need manual recovery, I don't see why they couldn't have the same expectation even in the future. We could even add a warning printed to the log periodically, to remind the operator that migration is not done and needs manual recovery. What I mean is, something like: ``` // retry logic if migrationDone() || migrationNotNeeded() { // happy path, nothing to do } else { // do not retry migration due to load concern, instead put a warning in the log. } ``` Luckily, checking `migrationDone()` can be done through the atomic integer, so it will not cause any reads to the storage backend. Alright, this is my final attempt to convince you, I will stop bugging you about this now, promise ;)

title: Potential vulnerability in wildcard processing
body_text:
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
An asterisk (`*`) in `allowed_parameters` `policies` value may lead to privilege escalation._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Write policy:_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
path "identity" _x000D_
{_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "identity/entity" _x000D_
{_x000D_
  capabilities = ["create", "read", "update"]_x000D_
  allowed_parameters = {_x000D_
    "name" = ["test-service-*"]_x000D_
    "policies" = ["test-approle-*"]_x000D_
    "*" = []_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "identity/entity/*"_x000D_
{_x000D_
  capabilities = ["read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_

Command_x000D_

 vault write identity/entity name="test-service-test10" policies="test-approle-empty, admin"_x000D_

returns successfully and create identity entity with given policies._x000D_

title: OpenAPI Explorer (Swagger UI) "Try it out" functionality broken for ListOperations / ones with query parameters
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
In the embedded Vault API Explorer (Swagger UI), the "Try it out" functionality for making requests from the UI does not work for ListOperations. It fails because the `?list=true` query parameter is not added to the request._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Open API explorer (Vault UI, open console dropdown, type "api")_x000D_
2. Find a list operation e.g. `/identity/entity-alias/id` and execute it via "Try it out"_x000D_
3. See error `"1 error occurred:\n\t* unsupported operation\n\n"`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
Vault 1.12.2 and 1.13-dev_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Issue is not unique to the mandatory list parameter on ListOperations - the `allowed_client_id` query parameter is also not populated into the generated request or displayed curl command properly for the `/identity/oidc/provider` endpoint, for example.

title: Logical.ReadRawWithDataWithContext cancels response body
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
To fetch the public certificates of certificate authorities from the PKI plugin, I was using the Client's `RawRequestWithContext` function, which has since been deprecated. I've migrated to the Logical client's `ReadRawWithDataWithContext` function, but found it to be inconsistently failing._x000D_
_x000D_
To support client HTTP timeouts, both implementations call `context.WithTimeout`. However, `RawRequestWithContext` never called the cancel function._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/c782b6678c35587849471a77fd2ad3e8b7f30870/api/client.go#L1268-L1277_x000D_
_x000D_
The replacement `ReadRawWithDataWithContext` does call cancel, which occasionally starts causing failures reading the response body._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/c782b6678c35587849471a77fd2ad3e8b7f30870/api/logical.go#L101-L106_x000D_
_x000D_
(Note that this code block eventually calls the above deprecated function via `readRawWithDataWithContext`)_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Since the failure seems to depend on the precise scheduling of the Go runtime, and behavior of select cases, I've been unable to develop an example that consistently fails. However, as an partial example:_x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
_x000D_
func GetCertifcateForAuthority(ctx context.Context, client *vault.Client, caName string) ([]byte, error) {_x000D_
	pemPath := path.Join(caName, "ca", "pem")_x000D_
	resp, err := client.Logical().ReadRawWithDataWithContext(ctx, pemPath, nil)_x000D_
	if err != nil {_x000D_
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetching certificate from Vault returned error: %w", err)_x000D_
	}_x000D_
	defer resp.Body.Close()_x000D_
_x000D_
	switch resp.StatusCode {_x000D_
	case http.StatusNoContent:_x000D_
		// Vault returns 204 when CA exists, but key material hasn't been submitted or generated_x000D_
		return []byte{}, nil_x000D_
	case http.StatusOK:_x000D_
		p, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)_x000D_
		if err != nil {_x000D_
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading body from Vault: %w", err)_x000D_
		}_x000D_
_x000D_
		block, _ := pem.Decode(p)_x000D_
		if block == nil {_x000D_
			return nil, errors.New("no PEM block returned by Vault")_x000D_
		} else if block.Type != "CERTIFICATE" {_x000D_
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown PEM %q block returned by Vault", block.Type)_x000D_
		}_x000D_
_x000D_
		return pem.EncodeToMemory(block), nil_x000D_
	default:_x000D_
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected status code returned by Vault: %d", resp.StatusCode)_x000D_
	}_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
With using a Vault client generated with `vault.DefaultConfig()`, this function will eventually unexpectedly fail with the following error: `reading body from Vault: context canceled`. After disabling the HTTP timeout in the Vault client (eg, `config.Timeout = 0`) I've been unable to reproduce this error._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
I can't see the use case for closing the body of a `ReadRaw*` request before the caller has a chance to inspect is the intended result of these APIs._x000D_
_x000D_
Should I open a PR to duplicate the note and behavior from Client? Or was this timeout behavior only intended on the non-raw paths?

title: Provide IP Address in Duo Request
body_text:
We are looking for Vault to provide the IP address of the request coming from Vault to a Duo challenge after successful LDAP authentication. _x000D_
_x000D_
We are trying to implement IP address restrictions for our instance of Vault. However, when a Duo challenge request is made, there is no IP address (IPv4 or v6) passed with that request (see screenshot from Duo audit logs, Vault sends 0.0.0.0) _x000D_
![no-ip-address](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/111926560/211731589-e46ac56e-5bfd-45a7-a6c0-58708348ab60.png). We are requesting that Vault send it's host system's IP address (ex: our AWS cluster where Vault is deployed) with any Duo request so that it can be recorded in Duo's logs and if not on the Duo whitelist, blocked._x000D_
_x000D_
This is a p0 blocker for us as we need Vault to send the IP address of the host/requesting system to Duo so our Duo api can record the incoming IP address from these access requests, log them, and filter those that are not in the range that we have whitelisted._x000D_
_x000D_
The desired outcome for this FR is that when a Duo mfa challenge happens, the corresponding request, with the Duo passcode, that comes from our Vault instance includes the IP address of the host system so that it can a) be blocked if it is not in the whitelisted range and b) be recorded in the Duo audit logs. Currently there is no workaround for this._x000D_
_x000D_
We have [this PR](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/15337). There is also a similar PR from Duo: [here](["Networks for API access" feature for Auth API](https://duo--c.na147.visual.force.com/servlet/servlet.Integration?lid=0660g000000btV8&ic=1&linkToken=VmpFPSxNakF5TXkwd01TMHhNMVF3TURveE5Ub3dOQzQzTXpSYSxNYzBHeDVHaUhsUnJOYXd1eGRkWDcyLFlXWmtNR0po))_x000D_
_x000D_
tl;dr: We want Vault to include it's source IP address when sending any Duo request_x000D_

title: Vault [on k8s] control audit log size and step down when reaching a watermark
body_text:
Hey *_x000D_
_x000D_
This is a feature request._x000D_
_x000D_
We are experiencing a somewhat-issue on Vault deployed on Kubernetes. We have an `emptydir` (which could as well be a `pv` does not matter) which handles the [audit file](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/audit/file). Whenever the `emptydir` runs full, the pod either gets OOM killed (when `emptydir` is a ramdisk) or `kublet` is killing the pod because of the `maxsize`  of the `emptydir` (here again, the `PV` would just be full and refuse writes, which then would trigger the Vault instance to die, since it’s `audit` device is not writable anymore. The documentation requires a `SIGHUP` after a logrotation anyways, which in K8s will make the pod go away._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
** Proposed solution **_x000D_
So it would be great if there would be a configurable parameter, which defines a watermark (in size and/or percentage) for the audit file, which would then trigger the vault instance to gracefully `step-down` and then `SIGHUP` to destroy the content of the `emptydir` which would make the newly created instance viable as a `primary` again.  _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
While the primary vault instance will be killed somehow (either through `oom`, `kubelet`, or vault kills itself due to out-of-diskspace) and vault continues to operate as expected, this mostly likely (or at least _should_) trigger a monitoring alert, which then needs to be investigated. And when this occurs often, the alert is likely being silenced, which makes it much harder to react when something really goes wrong and is not just an occasional `oh, the primary vault instance somehow died, primary election went through, we are good`._x000D_
_x000D_
Would the proposed solution be viable for you?_x000D_
_x000D_
cheers_x000D_
