title: Root CA getting generated even if error is returned
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We came across a scenario where generating root CA failed (error was returned) but the CA was actually generated successfully._x000D_
_x000D_
Upon inspecting the code, the culprit is [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/logical/pki/path_root.go#L229). The CA is generated and persisted but there are other actions that follow. If any of those actions fail, an error is returned to the caller, which suggests that the CA generation failed. But actually it succeeded. For example, in our case the function errors out when trying to build the CRL: [b.crlBuilder.rebuild()](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/logical/pki/path_root.go#L272-L276)._x000D_
_x000D_
This can lead to some nasty side effects_x000D_
- client does not know if the CA was actually generated or not_x000D_
- client saw the error and tries to generate a new CA even though one already exists, accidentally creating a second one or getting a new error_x000D_
- client is not sure did all necessary "post-actions" after CA generation succeed_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Easiest way is to modify the code to always return an error from b.crlBuilder.rebuild()._x000D_
Then simply try to generate a root CA by following the tutorial: [Generate Root CA](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/secrets-management/pki-engine#step-1-generate-root-ca)._x000D_
Even if an error is returned the CA is visible e.g. through the /issuers endpoint._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
An error should not be returned if CA generation is actually successful._x000D_
Alternatively, CA should not be persisted if an error is being returned._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Happened on 1.11.3, but also reproducible on current main branch.
top_3_comments_text: cipherboy: @nsimons I think this is desired behavior, within the bounds of Vault today. A warning is meant to indicate there is more to do, or something might not have been done quite as intended. An error indicates something went wrong, and IMO, may not necessarily be fatal. In our case, Vault today lacks storage transactions, making it nearly impossible to _fully and cleanly_ revert a partial operation. Here, an error occurred during CRL building. This isn't fatal -- the issuer was still generated and is discoverable under the APIs -- but indicates that more-up-to-date CRLs _will_ be unavailable until this is addressed and rectified. This could lead to operational issues if not addressed, as if clients attempt to fetch more up-to-date CRLs, none may be available. | nsimons: Right, yeah it's a classical problem. Would it then make sense that the client always tries to delete the issuer and start over if it encounters an error? Because the client cannot really know whether an error is something that it can ignore (e.g. CRL will be rebuilt later) or something that it should act on (CA generated, but e.g. serial number was not [stored](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.12.2/builtin/logical/pki/path_root.go#L259-L269) (so revoke not possible?)). We can't really inspect error messages since those can change between Vault versions. | cipherboy: I don't think that's sufficient in all cases. To take your other issue (#18583 - sorry :-), if you were to `chmod` revocation entries, you could end up with a state wherein 1. all previous issuer creations would've succeeded, and 2. any subsequent issuer creation would fail since CRL building will now fail. Here, the client cleaning up and retrying wouldn't necessarily help: the issue isn't with the new issuer, but some other underlying bug with storage. In general, as much as we can, we do attempt to keep key substrings of error messages stable, but I do agree in general you can't rely on it... What about a usage-based testing approach? You can list issuers+keys before/after, and attempt to issue a new (short-lived) cert under it, attempt to revoke it, rotate the CRL (and optionally, run a tidy with a short safety buffer once the temporary leaf has expired). If you don't see the issuer, you know it really is a fatal error somewhere (perhaps bad parameters?), if you're able to use it but just not able to revoke (and so could flag the mount to a human operator), or if it all works fine. (The assumption here is that you need automated creation of Root CAs, which seems a little interesting as a use case but could be an interesting problem in general :-)

cipherboy: @nsimons I think this is desired behavior, within the bounds of Vault today. A warning is meant to indicate there is more to do, or something might not have been done quite as intended. An error indicates something went wrong, and IMO, may not necessarily be fatal. In our case, Vault today lacks storage transactions, making it nearly impossible to _fully and cleanly_ revert a partial operation. Here, an error occurred during CRL building. This isn't fatal -- the issuer was still generated and is discoverable under the APIs -- but indicates that more-up-to-date CRLs _will_ be unavailable until this is addressed and rectified. This could lead to operational issues if not addressed, as if clients attempt to fetch more up-to-date CRLs, none may be available.
nsimons: Right, yeah it's a classical problem. Would it then make sense that the client always tries to delete the issuer and start over if it encounters an error? Because the client cannot really know whether an error is something that it can ignore (e.g. CRL will be rebuilt later) or something that it should act on (CA generated, but e.g. serial number was not [stored](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.12.2/builtin/logical/pki/path_root.go#L259-L269) (so revoke not possible?)). We can't really inspect error messages since those can change between Vault versions.
cipherboy: I don't think that's sufficient in all cases. To take your other issue (#18583 - sorry :-), if you were to `chmod` revocation entries, you could end up with a state wherein 1. all previous issuer creations would've succeeded, and 2. any subsequent issuer creation would fail since CRL building will now fail. Here, the client cleaning up and retrying wouldn't necessarily help: the issue isn't with the new issuer, but some other underlying bug with storage. In general, as much as we can, we do attempt to keep key substrings of error messages stable, but I do agree in general you can't rely on it... What about a usage-based testing approach? You can list issuers+keys before/after, and attempt to issue a new (short-lived) cert under it, attempt to revoke it, rotate the CRL (and optionally, run a tidy with a short safety buffer once the temporary leaf has expired). If you don't see the issuer, you know it really is a fatal error somewhere (perhaps bad parameters?), if you're able to use it but just not able to revoke (and so could flag the mount to a human operator), or if it all works fine. (The assumption here is that you need automated creation of Root CAs, which seems a little interesting as a use case but could be an interesting problem in general :-)
nsimons: No worries, the background info are the same across the two issues ;), basically we have hundreds of PKI backends and sometimes the storage has a hiccup. So for us re-creating the issuer and trying again could help I believe (we only have one issuer per PKI mount). Usage-based testing is a good idea and that's what we are now trying to do. We check the issuers endpoint in order to determine whether the CA was created or not. So far it works, but I feel it's not that future proof. If CRL (re)building is not fatal, would it make sense to handle the error case differently? ``` // Build a fresh CRL err = b.crlBuilder.rebuild(sc, true) if err != nil { return nil, err } ``` Issue a warning and continue (`resp.AddWarning`), return `resp, err`, or kick off the CRL rebuild as a go-routine and continue?

title: SSH certificate KRL signing
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We use Vault for SSH certificates but manage/distribute our own KRL. It is hard for us to verify the integrity of the distributed KRL file._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
We'd love to see a method added to the Vault SSH engine that would allow us to sign an arbitrary KRL file with the SSH CA key held in Vault. This would allow us to verify the integrity of the KRL with the SSH CA public key, without the overheads of Vault having to generate and manage the KRL internally._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
We've considered also signing the KRL with our own arbitrary key, but this would require us to store, track, and distribute another key along-side the SSH CA key._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
This would greatly help in securing SSH certificate auth with Vault, as servers can then verify that the KRL was signed by one of the SSH CA keys it has knowledge of._x000D_

title: The K/V v2 API docs are ambiguous about the `cas` (check-and-set) field
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
The K/V v2 API docs for [Create/Update Secret](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#create-update-secret) and [Patch Secret](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#patch-secret) are ambiguous about the position of the `cas` field._x000D_
_x000D_
The [Parameters](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#parameters-2) section implies that the `options`, `cas`, and `data` fields are at the same level, with a payload that looks like this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```json_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "options": {},_x000D_
  "cas": 0,_x000D_
  "data": {_x000D_
    "foo": "bar",_x000D_
    "zip": "zap"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
However the [Sample payload](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#sample-payload-1) section shows a payload with the `cas` field inside the `options` map:_x000D_
_x000D_
```json_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "options": {_x000D_
    "cas": 0_x000D_
  },_x000D_
  "data": {_x000D_
    "foo": "bar",_x000D_
    "zip": "zap"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
In practice, only the second payload works. The first payload gets an error response saying the check-and-set parameter is not set._x000D_
_x000D_

       --cap-add=IPC_LOCK \_x000D_
       --detach \_x000D_
       --publish=8200:8200 \_x000D_
       --name=vault \_x000D_
       hashicorp/vault:1.12.2_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
2. Get the root auth token from startup logs for future use:_x000D_
_x000D_
   ```bash_x000D_
   # At startup, Vault logs the following line:_x000D_
   # Root Token: [REDACTED_VAULT_TOKEN]
   vault_token="$(docker logs vault 2>/dev/null | awk '/Root Token:/ { print $3 }')"_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
3. Configure engine to require check-and-set:_x000D_
_x000D_

   curl \_x000D_
       --header "X-Vault-Token: $vault_token" \_x000D_
       --request POST \_x000D_
       --data '{ "cas_required": true }' \_x000D_
       localhost:8200/v1/secret/config_x000D_

       localhost:8200/v1/secret/data/my-secret_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_

   {_x000D_
     "errors": ["check-and-set parameter required for this call"]_x000D_
   }_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
5. Try to create a secret with the check-and-set field positioned according to the [Parameters](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#parameters-2) section of the docs:_x000D_
_x000D_

   ```_x000D_

   **This fails unexpectedly**, with the following response body:_x000D_
_x000D_

   {_x000D_
     "errors": ["check-and-set parameter required for this call"]_x000D_

6. Try to create a secret with the check-and-set field positioned according to the [Sample payload](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#sample-payload-1) section of the docs:_x000D_

   curl \_x000D_
       --header "X-Vault-Token: $vault_token" \_x000D_
       --request POST \_x000D_
       --data '{ "data": { "my_key": "my_value" }, "options": { "cas": 0 } }' \_x000D_

   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
   **This works as expected**, with the following response body:_x000D_
_x000D_
   ```json_x000D_

     "request_id": "ef28e8f6-4ebd-99f1-b9ce-acea21d812f1",_x000D_

title: Remove instance from peerlist when shutting down
body_text:
**Problem**_x000D_
When vault is shutting down (e.g. for restart or upgrade) other peers are still trying to reach out to the instance. This is the cause for the error: "failed to appendEntries to", "dial tcp: lookup <hostname of instance> on <ip address>:53: no such host". Vault should not try to 'append Entries' to an instance that (temporary) down._x000D_
_x000D_
**Possible solution**_x000D_
I would like a solution where Vault does remove itself from the list of peers._x000D_
_x000D_
**Context**_x000D_
I am running Vault HA with 5 instances on a Kubernetes cluster using the integrated storage back-end.
top_3_comments_text: maxb: I don't think this is the right approach. From my experience working with Consul clusters, I know that removing and re-adding a Raft peer is a fairly slow operation, which is unnecessary when a node is just being restarted, and introduces extra complexity in understanding and managing the cluster quorum, since the cluster size is now changing as nodes join and leave. I have a feeling there would be extra complexity in translating this generic Raft knowledge to Vault, since IIUC Vault actually requires the unseal keys to be available to complete a Raft join. I think that Vault also deliberately doesn't support joining a cluster once a node has any local data stored, to safeguard against overwrites - so that's another thing in the way of this proposal. Perhaps there is a way to better mitigate the volume of noisy log messaging, without modifying the Raft peer set when nodes are temporarily down.

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When trying to get value from kv store using CLI, it works fine. I can use the -field flag to get a specific field. Using the -wrapp-ttl flag also works fine. However, if I use both of these flags at once, I get `No data found at kv/data/<secret_path>`._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run `vault kv get -wrap-ttl=5m -field="<field>" <path>.`_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
I receive a wrapped response from Vault for the desired field. _x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`):  1.12.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.12.2 (415e1fe3118eebd5df6cb60d13defdc01aa17b03)_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Debian 11_x000D_
_x000D_
If this is the intended behaviour, I could not find it mentioned in the documentation. _x000D_
top_3_comments_text: maxb: The root cause why this doesn't work, is that `-field` flag is purely client side filtering applied by the CLI, it doesn't get sent to the server to be incorporated into the wrapped response. My guess is that's unlikely to change. On top of that, `vault kv get` seems to have a bug or inconsistency, that it disables some of the usual processing of `-field` when working with a KV v2, which is responsible for the misleading `No data found at kv/data/<secret_path>` message, **and** also `-field=wrapping_token` not working (which would be nice, to provide an easy way to save just the wrapping token to a shell variable). And then, whilst `vault unwrap` does also support the `-field` option, so you might think to try `vault unwrap -field="<field>"`, it doesn't implement the special extra code for dealing with the quirks of KV v2s, with their extra nested data dictionary, so that ends up not working either. I think your best option right now is to do: ``` wrapping_token=$(vault kv get -format=json -wrap-ttl=5m kv/secret_path | jq -r .wrap_info.token) vault unwrap -format=json $wrapping_token | jq -r .data.data.your_field ``` | heatherezell: Hi @xskrasek - please let me know if the suggestion from @maxb helps or if you have further questions. It does unfortunately not fix the bug discussed, that leads to the misleading `No data found at kv/data/<secret_path>` error message. title: Database secrets engine should support specifying the next rotation
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I have a pair of static roles for an application to gracefully switch users as passwords rotate. The `rotation_period` for each is currently six months, but their offset should be three months apart. There is no support for specifying this in static role configuration api._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
The [create static role](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/databases#create-static-role) api endpoint could support an optional `ttl` parameter as well as a `rotation_period`. Additionally (preferred), or alternately, the [rotate static role credentials](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/databases#rotate-static-role-credentials) endpoint could implement this `ttl` option. In either case, when the "override" TTL expires, the `rotation_period` will define the next TTL per existing logic._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
The only alternative I have for my use case is to manually force a rotation to establish the offset cadence, or to create each role 3 months apart. In my case, I set a reminder for 3 months from the initial configuration. I missed this reminder. Both passwords rotated within seconds of each other, causing a brief production outage._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
This could also be beneficial when one wants to expire a password, but not immediately. It could be used to schedule the next rotation to happen during off hours, for example._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
This is the current state of things. Their next rotation is nearly synchronized. This caused a brief outage at the last rotation. I want to add 2160 hours to the ttl of `app2`._x000D_
```_x000D_
❯ vault read database/pg/static-creds/app1_x000D_
last_vault_rotation    2022-09-14T22:28:43.036186412Z_x000D_
rotation_period        4320h_x000D_
ttl                    425h47m20s_x000D_
❯ vault read database/pg/static-creds/app2_x000D_
last_vault_rotation    2022-09-14T22:28:45.186708385Z_x000D_
rotation_period        4320h_x000D_

title: Feature: Configure the x509 field used to bind entities to a cert alias
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Users of our Vault cluster authenticate using mTLS certificates issued by our internal CA, our systems all use the subject email address field to identify a user by their cert._x000D_
_x000D_
We use the TLS certificate auth method in Vault to store the mTLS certs of our users. When presented with a cert, Vault uses the subject common name field to look up the entity accessor._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
We would like the ability to pick which field of the TLS cert is used when mapping it to an entity accessor. In our case: subject email address._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Our in-house onboarding tool performs creation of CA certificate roles for new users users of our Vault cluster. When a user attempts to push their cert, the tool will first check if any existing certificates share the same Subject Common Name as that of the new cert. If a match is found, the tool will refuse to add that users certificate._x000D_
_x000D_
Though effective at preventing "collisions", this workaround means some users cannot be onboarded without requesting another cert from our CA with a custom CN field, specifically for use with Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Internal systems are often fronted by web servers that use mTLS termination to identify corporate users by their email address. Having Vault support using that same field when mapping certificates to entities would be useful any organisation using mTLS certificates internally._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
In general, the TLS auth method feels preferentially geared towards handling server side (site) certs, rather than client side mTLS certs. However the documentation does not make it clear if the TLS auth method should not be used for client certs._x000D_
_x000D_
The included diagram shows how a "collision" between two certs with the same CN can lead to a user being identified as the "wrong" entity._x000D_
_x000D_
![Vault entity-cert collision](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61699770/213474453-ab2f7e13-05df-40cd-937b-6ac912b6b34a.png)

title: Ability to limit IP sans in PKI roles
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Sometimes, it is necessary to be able to add IP sans to a certificate. Vault helpfully provides the [allow_ip_sans](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#allow_ip_sans) setting for a role on the PKI path for this._x000D_
_x000D_
However, as this feature documents, "No authorization checking is performed except to verify that the given values are valid IP addresses."._x000D_
_x000D_
This allows users to request certificates with IPs for machines they don't own. For example, if team A has been assigned the range of `192.0.2.0/24`, the lack of limitation means they are also able to request certificates outside of their range (even including values like `127.0.0.1`) and thus can impersonate machines from other teams that use IP based SSL connections._x000D_
_x000D_
As I understand it, the ability to request and be granted certificates for machines the team in question does not own breaks a part of the point of SSL certificates: the ability to be sure you are talking to who someone claims to be. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would like to be able to limit IP sans to specific ranges or values, much like the current [allowed_uri_sans](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#allowed_uri_sans), to ensure that teams will not be granted any certificates outside of the IP range assigned to them._x000D_
_x000D_
I am imagining a comma-delimited list of IPs and IP ranges allowed much like `allowed_uri_sans`'s implementation would be very helpful._x000D_
_x000D_
As an example, to allow team A to use the `192.0.2.0/24` and `2001:DB8::/32` ranges, a role field could be defined like follows:_x000D_
```_x000D_
allowed_ip_sans: "192.0.2.0/24,2001:DB8::/32"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I am not able to think of any alternative myself, but I would happily discuss possible alternative solutions._x000D_
_x000D_
The main alternative we have considered is to disable IP sans completely. Sadly, this is not always a possibility because some applications want to connect over IP addresses instead of hostname._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Some applications allow using IP sans for added security. For example, [etcd allows limiting the peers it will authenticate using IP sans](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.5/op-guide/security/#notes-for-tls-authentication)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I have looked through Vault's code and, as I understand, this is currently not possible. Vault currently uses an all-or-nothing approach for IP sans: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/b6c02b15f5672f250e509d616c2201112b22b1c1/builtin/logical/pki/cert_util.go#L1208-L1235_x000D_
_x000D_
I have not been able to find other issues or forum threads discussing this issue.

title: `sys/internal/counters/activity/monthly` returns mount accessors in a field that should contain mount paths
body_text:
The activity reporting APIs return data mentioning mount paths using this structure:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/3ded1388cbd838b5a1253af40808c823d6d4336d/vault/activity_log.go#L1482-L1485_x000D_
_x000D_
which is populated from this very similar structure:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/92cc175eb6f19b27ed7ba075eed307fa2b51307b/vault/activity/query.go#L48-L51_x000D_
_x000D_
The `MountPath` field is filled in in various places. In these two, it is actually filled in with mount paths:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/3ded1388cbd838b5a1253af40808c823d6d4336d/vault/activity_log.go#L2168-L2181_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/3ded1388cbd838b5a1253af40808c823d6d4336d/vault/activity_log.go#L2341-L2361_x000D_
_x000D_
but in this code:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/92cc175eb6f19b27ed7ba075eed307fa2b51307b/vault/activity_log_util_common.go#L208-L221_x000D_
_x000D_
the name given to the local variable would have you believe it is being filled with the mount path, but if you check the map it is being passed, it is actually a map keyed on mount **accessor** not **path**. This has the result of mount accessors erroneously showing up in some fields supposed to contain mount paths, when querying the current month's data.

_x000D_

}_x000D_

{_x000D_
  "key_type": "ec",_x000D_

  "cert_type": "user"_x000D_
}_x000D_

title: The `sys/storage/raft/*` APIs OpenAPI documentation cannot be retrieved from `vault server -dev` instance
body_text:
Running a `vault server -dev` instance briefly, to retrieve OpenAPI documentation from it, is a useful practice when you want the OpenAPI doc for further processing._x000D_
_x000D_
This practice is even codified in `scripts/gen_openapi.sh` in the Vault repo._x000D_
_x000D_
An OpenAPI document generated in this way will be missing the `sys/storage/raft/*` APIs._x000D_
_x000D_
This is because these are only actually configured in a running Vault server when it is using Raft storage, and there is no way to make this true with a `-dev` server._x000D_
_x000D_
I propose that we register the `sys/raft/*` APIs with the URL routing system unconditionally. Most but not all of them already include a further runtime check to error if Raft storage is not in use:_x000D_
```_x000D_
		raftBackend := b.Core.getRaftBackend()_x000D_
		if raftBackend == nil {_x000D_
			return logical.ErrorResponse("raft storage is not in use"), logical.ErrInvalidRequest_x000D_
		}_x000D_
```_x000D_
We would simply extend this to the remaining ones._x000D_
_x000D_
I did consider the alternative of adding another flag, such as `-dev-raft`, to start a dev server that uses Raft storage... however that's a fairly complicated option just to get the correct API definitions, and Raft takes time to initialise. I'm not so fond of this option._x000D_
_x000D_
@averche FYI as I know this is relevant for your generated API project.
top_3_comments_text: maxb: Also, it seems like Enterprise registers its `sys/storage/raft/snapshot-auto/*` with the router regardless of whether Raft is enabled or not, so it would be good to be consistent with that behaviour for the rest of `sys/storage/raft/*`, too.

_x000D_

title: Feature request: secrets engine for Cloudflare
body_text:
A secrets engine for creating [Cloudflare API tokens](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/create-token/) seems like a shoe-in for Vault. The engine would work in a way identical to other secrets engine whereby Vault is provided with a highly-privileged API token and accepts requests to create and hand out additional API tokens, given a set of parameters._x000D_
_x000D_
Desirable features would correspond to what Cloudflare lets you do when creating an API token:_x000D_

title: WebAssembly support in plugin system
body_text:
Plugin support currently requires us to build and bundle a specific version of Vault instead of using a stock Vault version. This intermediate artifact or layer of indirection has several drawbacks:_x000D_
* Security tools don't identify this as official releases and thus don't identify CVEs and propose critical security patches._x000D_
* Adds more complexity and maintainability on the consumer side. This includes among other things: CI/CD pipelines, supply-chain related stuff (SBOM, signing, ...), ..._x000D_
* The technical and product difficulties make this hard to include it on cloud offerings by HashiCorp like HCP Vault_x000D_
_x000D_
**Enter WebAssembly.**_x000D_
_x000D_
One way to overcome these problems would be to allow injecting user code in the form of a plugin directly in Vault._x000D_
In the same vein others are envisioning it like Fastly with Compute@Edge and Cloudflare with Workers._x000D_
Even open-source projects like Envoyproxy already support it long time ago._x000D_
_x000D_
This is what WebAssembly would allow us to do._x000D_
In any programming language that can compile to it (Rust, Go with TinyGo, AssemblyScript and more as we write)._x000D_
_x000D_
There is an unstoppable trend towards its adoption, as stated by [CNCF survey](https://www.cncf.io/reports/cncf-annual-survey-2022/)._x000D_
_x000D_
I would recommend to take into consideration this feature request as part of the [re-thinking process it seems to be happening within HashiCorp and the plugin system](https://www.hashicorp.com/resources/vault-roadmap-hashiconf-global-2022)._x000D_
This can be a great opportunity to further improve the adoption of this extension point of HashiCorp Vault and HCP Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
I purposely avoided any specific functional or technical details to get an early feedback if this is an idea that could be considered or not.

title: INFORMATION NEEDED: identifier for macOS signed binary artifact is CHANGED to a.out, permanently?
body_text:
This is an observation more than a bug _necessarily_ as functionality is unchanged, but when it comes to trustworthiness of a signing pipeline any observed change feels worth reporting. If a value I rely on for what makes up part of a cryptographic signature needs to be updated, I'd hope it's intentional and 'permanent' instead of arbitrary and potentially unreliable._x000D_
_x000D_
I'm assuming the signing for vault uses something like [gon](https://github.com/mitchellh/gon), and that it is secured adequately all the way up to being posted for release/download. I don't see anything in the release notes that indicates the observation I'm reporting is a temporary or permanent change or intentionally altered configuration._x000D_
A common tool for macOS software distribution for institutions (in comparison to homebrew which manually :yolo:'s whatever a maintainer attests is The Canonical Binary™+hash for a resource) is the [autopkg](https://autopkg.github.io/autopkg/) project. It uses [code signature verification](https://github.com/autopkg/autopkg/wiki/Using-CodeSignatureVerification), which in turn relies on the codesign binary (via the --display -r- --deep -v flags with the path to the binary) on the Mac to determine if an artifacts 'designated' field matches a [recorded string](https://github.com/autopkg/hjuutilainen-recipes/blob/7c3af44674e5a1e2c256d45014c956cc5ce60345/HashiCorp/Vault.download.recipe#L60) exactly. As of the 1.12.3 darwin releases, the 'signature' doesn't match because instead of recording the cert values with the 'vault' identifier for the binary, it's instead using [a.out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.out), ye olde 'assembler output' format/naming of yore that golang adopted as a default. I can't imagine this is cause for alarm, but the difference breaks our recipe until we (the autopkg community) update the value._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. curl/download the 1.12.2 and 1.12.3 darwin arm64 or amd64 releases from https://releases.hashicorp.com_x000D_
2. unzip the 1.12.2 version to a distinct path or /tmp and rename output from filename 'vault' to vault1.12.2 _x000D_
3. run `codesign --display -r- --deep -v /path/to/vault1.12.2`_x000D_
4. note the second line in the output `Identifier=vault` and beginning of the last line `designated => identifier vault...`_x000D_
5. unzip the 1.12.3 version to a distinct path or /tmp and rename output from filename 'vault' to vault1.12.3_x000D_
6. run `codesign --display -r- --deep -v /path/to/vault1.12.3`_x000D_
7. note `Identifier=a.out` in the output and beginning of the last line `designated => identifier "a.out"`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The designated => field should match the `identifier vault` string prefix previously used, or confirmation this will be how the compiled binary is signed/identified in the future_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): n/a, but I work at an Enterprise Vault customer and we're running Vault 1.10.6+ent_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): $current_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: n/a_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
n/a_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Thank you for your time and attention! 🙇

_x000D_
Since Prometheus does not support adding a `X-Vault-Token` header and documentation implies Bearer tokens should work, I expected them to work._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Enable Prometheus metrics:_x000D_

  disable_hostname = true        _x000D_
}  _x000D_

title: Logic behind forcing DUO auth to be push instead of push or phone call?
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Recently enabled DUO MFA on our cluster and we have some people in our org who have older phones that don't support the duo app. They would like to authenticate via phone call, but that is not possible with any current release of vault. Solution: change factor from push to auto_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
In [login_mfa.go](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/vault/login_mfa.go#L1951-L1967) the factor is hardcoded to either "push" or "password", but the duo api /auth [endpoint](https://duo.com/docs/authapi#/auth) supports additional modes such as "sms" "phone" and "auto", where auto lets duo choose which one to do. Is there any reason that I'm not aware of that auto is not chosen? Seems to be the most flexible to me, but I haven't worked with duo API directly at all. Maybe auto has some downside to it. Looks like the relevant code came from [this commit](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/14025) so @raskchanky if you happen to see this and remember why you set it to push, that would probably be the most efficient way to answer my question, don't want to waste y'alls time. If you don't remember, I don't blame you haha I never remember random little intricacies of my old code, that shit is impossible. Anyways, I'd be happy to make a quick PR to change it from "push" to "auto" if no one has any reservations. Thank you for taking the time to read this! _x000D_

title: Support nested teams with Github authentication
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
The Github authentication method allows you to attach policies based on Github team membership. This is useful for implementing role-based permissions._x000D_
_x000D_
Github itself allows teams to be subteams of other teams. Permissions from parent teams are inherited, and additional permissions can be granted to subteams._x000D_
_x000D_
Vault does not support this behaviour; if you are only assigned the policies attached to a team if you are a direct member of that team. Indirect members, i.e. members of a team that is part of the larger one, are not assigned the policies. This makes managing permissions more annoying._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
I would like Vault to support these hierarchical teams in the same manner that github does, where being a member of a subteam of a larger team also makes you a member of the parent team. To illustrate:_x000D_
_x000D_
```mermaid_x000D_
flowchart TB_x000D_
    t1(Team 1) --> t2(Team 2) --> m1[Alice]_x000D_
    t1 --> m2[Bob]_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Alice should be perceived as a member of Team 1 and Team 2, while Bob is only a member of Team 2. This is also how Github implements the permissions on teams._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
We currently implement a workaround where we manually grant the permissions to all subteams directly. This works but requires more upkeep and is prone to human error when subteams change._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
n/a_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
n/a

top_3_comments_text: maxb: Vault Enterprise includes the concept of "Control Groups" which are a mechanism for approvals. However, it is not without caveats. Who can approve a request, is determined by group membership. However if a user who makes a request is also a member of the approval group, they can approve their own requests, defeating the security. This can to some extent be mitigated by use of Sentinel policies, but this then puts you in the position of having to configure two parts of the control in different ways, and it is relatively easy to fail to do this correctly, resulting in the control not being enforced. Furthermore, the Sentinel policy language lacks a way to test whether a control group has been applied to a request, without also triggering response wrapping behaviour as a side effect. This means that if you use a Sentinel EGP to mitigate self approval, it can be tricky to avoid imposing unwanted response wrapping on automated processes which should be allowed to read the same secret without approval. If you are operating in an environment where one human may be able to log in to Vault as multiple identities (e.g. regular and elevated privileges), you have a further threat of one user being able to place a request with one identity and approve with the other, unless you add more governance to prevent this. The control groups feature lacks any way for a user to review the open requests pending their approval - instead the requesting user must communicate a request ID out of band to the approving user. The approving user is shown some information about the request they are about to approve, but not as much as I would like. Once a four eyes process has been approved, you still have a situation where the approved retriever now has possession of the secret, and you need to build your own policies and procedures so they can't write it down and re-use it forever. (Ideally, it should be single-use.) ---- In short: four eyes is really hard to get right, and whilst Vault (Enterprise) has some relevant parts, there is still a lot of effort left to the individual implementor, and even then there are still rough edges.

title: api.LifeTimeWatcher is not aware of `Age` headers
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
This is a reduction of https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/16439_x000D_
_x000D_
Because the LifetimeWatcher that handles renews is not aware of `Age` headers it can not correctly calculate grace periods and sleep durations when reading credentials through a caching proxy._x000D_
_x000D_
Let's look at _one_ of the functions that LifetimeWatcher uses to renew: [`api.Sys().Renew()`](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/api/v1.9.0/api/sys_leases.go#L13-L34)_x000D_
_x000D_
👉 When we are looking at this `api.Sys().Renew()`, what I want to look for is:_x000D_
_x000D_
A) Is the `Age` header examined at all?_x000D_
B) Does the return result from the function include the `Age` header so downstream consumers who need this information use it._x000D_
_x000D_
🎯 The answer in both cases is: no._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Set up a Vault Server_x000D_
2. Set up a caching proxy_x000D_
3. Read a secret into the proxy using `api.Logical().Read()`_x000D_
4. Call Vault through the caching proxy using `api.Sys().Renew()`_x000D_
5. Wait_x000D_
6. Call Vault through the caching proxy using `api.Sys().Renew()`_x000D_
_x000D_
🔍 For any of those `api.Sys().Renew()` calls, are you able to know the value of the `Age` header? Not with the current GO API._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
`api.Sys().Renew()` and other such functions should give access to the `Age` header through their return value._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Central Vault Caching Proxies are critical in Kubernetes environments._x000D_
_x000D_
While Vault can handle tons of requests, Vault's secret backends can not. If a K8S deployments requests 100 database users from the Atlas Database Plugin using dynamic credentials it will lock the Atlas environment._x000D_
_x000D_
Without the `Age` header, new pod instances will not know when to properly renew their secret templates. This happens all the time with autoscaling groups. 30 pods start at time 0, 20 pods at time 20. Credentials expire at time 30 (MAX_TTL). Will the second batch of pods know that the credential has expired? Not until time 50 (20 + MAX_TTL)._x000D_
_x000D_
Once the `Age` header value is accessible by downstream consumers such as LifetimeWatcher, those consumers should be upgraded to acknowledge the `Age` header._x000D_

title: unauthenticated ssh engine public key text/plain response
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The [unauthenticated endpoint](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/ssh#read-public-key-unauthenticated) for retrieving the ssh engine CA public key returns text/plain, while typically vault responds to requests with a JSON object._x000D_
_x000D_
This breaks the unauthenticated `vault read /path/to/ssh/public_key`, but more importantly it breaks the same trying to render a template, presumably because the view/renderer is expecting JSON._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run `vault read /ssh/public_key`_x000D_
2. See error below_x000D_
_x000D_
CLI:_x000D_
```_x000D_
╰─± vault read /ssh/public_key_x000D_
Error reading /ssh/public_key: invalid character 's' looking for beginning of value_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
template:_x000D_
```_x000D_
Feb 18 23:34:14 ip-172-20-20-40 vault[12298]: 2023-02-18T23:34:14.652Z [ERROR] runtime error encountered: error="template server: vault.read(/ssh/public_key): vault.read(/ssh/public_key): invalid character 's' looking for beginning of value"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The first part of the ssh key is is `ssh-rsa` - I believe where the message `invalid character 's'` is coming from._x000D_
_x000D_
Further, attempts to coerce the server into replying with JSON are ignored:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ curl -vvvvv -H "Accept: application/json" https://my.vault.com:8200/v1/ssh/public_key_x000D_
> GET /ssh/public_key HTTP/2_x000D_
> Host: vault.sev1tech.com:8200_x000D_
> User-Agent: curl/7.61.1_x000D_
> Accept: application/json_x000D_
>_x000D_
* Connection state changed (MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS == 128)!_x000D_
< HTTP/2 200_x000D_
< date: Sat, 18 Feb 2023 23:19:07 GMT_x000D_
< content-type: text/plain_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Most likely one of these two things are expected to happen:_x000D_
1. The endpoint should either honor an `Accept: application/json` header, outright return JSON instead of plain/text, or default to JSON but allow and honor a client's `Accept: text/plain` header._x000D_
2. The renderer/viewer honors the server's `Content-Type` header `text/plain` and handles it accordingly, rather than assuming the response is JSON and crashing/erroring._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: 1.12.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version: 1.12.2_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux/x86_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional Context:**_x000D_
_x000D_
AFAICT, this issue forces the use of the authenticated endpoint for retrieving the `public_key` in a vault template, which also forces granting `read` capability to `/ssh/config/ca`. I haven't been able, by trial or reading the consul template docs, to modify the behavior to handle a `text/plain` server response.

Long before I knew the vault agent was even a thing, I built an internal library on top of `vault-ruby` for chef to be able to retrieve kv secrets on behalf of cookbooks, and that's primarily what we use to get the secret values from vault to where they need to be. Using the agent as more than a pass-through/proxy/caching entity for a localhost is a relatively new approach for us. It's quite reasonable to make a raw HTTP call to the unauthenticated endpoint for the signing key, but somewhere in my head it seemed to make sense that the agent would be the thing to handle this case. Maybe a case of hammer, meet what looks like a nail. The logic wasn't so much focused on the key's TTL, but rather the agent's capability to take a template and create a file for other processes like sshd to consume, and as a sort of side effect ensure if the key needed to be renewed/refreshed the agent would handle it transparently.

echo-qin: Thanks for your answer! I'm checking with our security team. I would leave this issue open until I get response with our security team and I will add any details if have then.
maxb: I realised something else I could add - if you look at the Git tags in this repository you will find the regular Vault release tags look like e.g. `v1.12.3` - but you will also see tags named e.g. `api/v1.9.0` - these tags which incorporate a subdirectory path in their name, are how Go modules handle separate release versions for modules that share a repository.
heatherezell: Max is correct. The API and SDK packages versions are numbered differently from the Vault core package. Since this is unlikely to change and is not a security issue, I'm going to go ahead and close this issue now. Thanks.
echo-qin: @maxb Thanks for your reply! Sorry I forgot to leave messages before. It was approved by our security team. Another thing is we were asked another question again (we are going on another round of review). Which vault version is used exactly by vault/api v1.9.0? I heard that it should be 1.13.x, is it 1.13.1? Thanks a lot for your help.
maxb: There is not an exact correspondence between api/sdk versions and Vault releases. The api/sdk tags are made on particular Git commits which seem to generally not be exactly the same ones as the actual Vault releases. api/v1.9.0 was tagged on the Vault main branch, shortly before the 1.13 branch was created - so it's a release "around the time of Vault 1.13".

maxb: To understand whether a whole-of-Vault CVE is relevant to just the code in the `api/` directory, you would have to assess the nature of the CVE, and use technical knowledge and judgement to decide whether it applied to the `api/` code. Most won't be, since the `api/` code is a tiny subset.

top_3_comments_text: Monkeychip: @ps3460 thank you for the issue. There has been some work done in this area and more work to come. Some noteable places and upcoming changes: * The Vault Usage Metrics dashboard. See `/ui/vault/clients/dashboard` This will show things about your cluster. And as the name indicates it focuses on your cluster's usage. Work on this view has been pushed in various releases since about 1.12. * The PKI engine has been revamped in the UI. A beta version was release in 1.13 and the full version will be ready in 1.14. While the dashboard on this new engine only shows things like number of issuers and roles, if you navigate to the certificates tab and click on the cert it will show you when it's going to expire. Similar to the PKI overview page it focuses on counts and quick actions. Throttled or disrupted AWS EC2 and IAM calls from the auth plugin can lead to accumulation of abandoned inflight requests when combined with Vault client timeout+retry behavior._x000D_

title: Allow mTLS for mysql storage backend
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
The MySQL storage backend supports SSL/TLS as of #439. The MySQL/MariaDB secrets engine in the meantime has been extended to support mTLS configuration. This was requested at least in #6444 and seems to have been implemented with #9181._x000D_
To me it appears odd that_x000D_
- the secrets engine supports mTLS, while the storage backend does not and_x000D_
- the TLS parameter names of [secret engine](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/databases/mysql-maria) and [storage backend](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/storage/mysql) differ._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would hence like to propose that the storage backend is extended with similar options like the options of the secrets engine. If backwards compatibility allows for that, I'd also like to propose to adjust the options to a common naming scheme. I understand, however, that the latter might not be reasonable._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
In our case we would prefer a mutual SSL/TLS database connection to the storage backend, because the Vault and database servers are not separated within a private network. Placing these two servers in their own private network might be advisable. In addition, #6444 mentions that one could make use of proxying instead._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
One could use certificate-based authentication once mTLS capabilities are established.

title: AWS Secrets Engine templated session tags
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Not a problem per se. Perhaps it may lead to being able to better conform to certain AWS IAM best practices around using tags and ABAC-style policies._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
I have an example use case where it would be desirable for the AWS secrets backend to be able to apply session tags on credentials issued by the `aws/sts/creds` API. This would allow greater dynamism in the AWS backend._x000D_
_x000D_
example use case:_x000D_
_x000D_
I want to auth OIDC tokens from my CI using the `auth/jwt` backend and a single auth role. Most CI providers are offering per-job OIDC tokens now. I will use Buildkite in this example but it applies to GHA and others._x000D_
_x000D_
- I want to be able to auth OIDC tokens from any repo in the org without having to create a new `auth/jwt/role/<REPO>` role for each._x000D_
- I want a single AWS Secrets role that each repo can get IAM creds (assumed_role) from and have the claims from the JWT applied as session tags._x000D_
- The session tags allow me to treat each issued AWS credential as unique by writing ABAC-style policies that use tags to differentiate each "user" (repo/pipeline in this example)_x000D_
_x000D_
How this might look in practice:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Setup a single `auth/jwt` role `buildkite-pipelines`:_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
vault write auth/jwt/buildkite-pipelines \_x000D_
  bound_audiences="vault" \_x000D_
  policies="buildkite-pipelines" \_x000D_
  user_claim="pipeline_slug" \_x000D_
  claim_mappings="pipeline_slug=pipeline_slug" \_x000D_
  role_type=jwt_x000D_
```_x000D_
2. Create an AWS IAM role `buildkite-pipelines`. This role will be assumed by any BK pipeline in our org._x000D_
3. Create a single Vault AWS Secrets role named `buildkite-pipelines` that will assume the role created in the previous step:_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
vault write aws/role/buildkite-pipelines \_x000D_
  credential_type="assumed_role" \_x000D_
  role_arns="arn:aws:iam:123456789012:role/buildkite-pipelines" \_x000D_
  session_tags="pipeline_slug={{ identity.entity.alias.mount_jwt_1234567.custom_metadata.pipeline_slug }}"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Buildkite pipelines would use their OIDC token to auth to vault and fetch AWS creds. These creds would have a `pipeline_slug` session tag._x000D_
_x000D_
Then, an S3 bucket could be made available for all pipelines to use with a single bucket policy. They would be restricted to read/write/list on the path `cache/<PIPELINE>` where `<PIPELINE>` is the `pipeline_slug` conveyed from the claims on the BK OIDC token down to a session tag on the AWS IAM creds:_x000D_
_x000D_
```json_x000D_
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::my-bk-cache-bucket/cache/${aws:PrincipalTag/pipeline_slug}/*",_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
1. Using Vault, the alternative is to explicitly create jwt auth roles and secrets/aws roles for each pipeline._x000D_
2. This is a lambda-based example using GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. In this example a GHA job would send its JWT to the lambda which would parse out the claims and call the `sts:AssumeRole` API with those claims as session tags, returning the resulting creds to the caller. https://github.com/glassechidna/ghaoidc/blob/main/api/api.go_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
In general I think this would go a long way towards allowing folks to expressing more ABAC-style IAM policies with Vault._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_

_x000D_
# Read entity alias and verify that custom_metadata is empty_x000D_
vault read identity/entity-alias/id/$AID_x000D_
_x000D_
# Attempt to update only the custom_metadata field (fails with 500)_x000D_
vault write identity/entity-alias/id/$AID \_x000D_
   - <<<'{"custom_metadata":{"foo":"bar"}}'_x000D_
   _x000D_
Error writing data to identity/entity-alias/id/5b6add1d-a796-4fda-7f13-fee0a6885b44: Error making API request._x000D_
URL: PUT http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/identity/entity-alias/id/5b6add1d-a796-4fda-7f13-fee0a6885b44_x000D_
Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
* 1 error occurred:_x000D_

_x000D_

title: Vault Agent 1.13.0 requires a listener block when its documented as optional
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
In Vault 1.13.0, not defining a `listener` block in a `vault agent` configuration will cause the following error at startup:_x000D_
_x000D_
`error validating configuration: configuring the api_proxy requires at least 1 listener to be defined`_x000D_
_x000D_
This was introduced [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/commit/c2abcccb949fedf1fff1f027592d1bd3df356a13#diff-f309f8618f6d7bea196a7f4eb10f16a73ecc98da0b4dddfdf39278c35b1067afR296-R309)_x000D_
_x000D_
This is a specially opinionated decision given the fact the `api_proxy` is also not declared in the config and both directives are documented as `optional` [here](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent#listener)_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run a vault agent without the `listener` and `api_proxy` stanzas defined_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault agent will start without failures and not allocate a listener_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
# Paste your Vault config here._x000D_
# Be sure to scrub any sensitive values_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
In our use case we use Vault Agent to render certificates and configuration file templates but we don't need any listener binding since we don't have any other processes talking to Vault. In this case, the vault agent is acting more like a `client` rather than a `proxy`. So for our specific use case, this is a breaking change.

body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/15869 changed the `aws` secrets engine such that it no longer returns leases for STS credentials, which makes sense. However, it also no longer returns a `lease_duration`._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_

```sh_x000D_
$ vault server -dev_x000D_
```_x000D_

_x000D_
$ vault write aws/config/root access_key=<redacted> secret_key=<redacted> region=us-east-1_x000D_
_x000D_
$ vault write aws/roles/my-role credential_type=assumed_role role_arns="<redacted>" max_sts_ttl=900_x000D_
_x000D_
$ vault read aws/sts/my-role_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
A `lease_duration` is returned with the STS credentials._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): `Vault v1.13.0 (a4cf0dc4437de35fce4860857b64569d092a9b5a), built 2023-03-01T14:58:13Z`_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): `Vault v1.13.0 (a4cf0dc4437de35fce4860857b64569d092a9b5a), built 2023-03-01T14:58:13Z`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS on AMD64_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
The KV v1 engine returns a `lease_duration` without a `lease_id`, so there is precedent for this.

Since no lease duration is returned, vault agent will not refresh them. https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent/template#renewable-secrets This makes Vault agent treat STS credentials as non-renewable. | robmonte: Hi @mancej I was wondering if you could provide more info regarding this issue and how it relates to Vault agent. This breaks the functionality of consul-template with regards to Vault secrets. Before the change, the secrets were marked [non-renewable](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/15869/files#diff-f968287284d93e6aa5ceb137bf33c9b789b3bccfe6c3055897d2a526eb720d54L172). The documentation you refer to explains different behavior for non-renewable leased secrets in the [section below](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent/template#non-renewable-leased-secrets) it.
lindleywhite: `consul-template` Is used to read secrets from Vault and populate them to files and then send signals to processes. This breaks the functionality of consul-template with regards to Vault secrets. If the secret is non-renewable the `lease_duration` instructs consul-template to wait that time before re-issuing a read to Vault. https://github.com/hashicorp/consul-template/blob/b26991a4e924c996996eaf9dc655046370dbb340/dependency/vault_read.go#L90-L94 https://github.com/hashicorp/consul-template/blob/b26991a4e924c996996eaf9dc655046370dbb340/dependency/vault_common.go#L113 If `lease_duration` is `0` consul-template will just continue to renew the secret.
mancej: >Hi @mancej I was wondering if you could provide more info regarding this issue and how it relates to Vault agent. Do you >have setup where agent was able to renew STS secrets for you? Before the change, the secrets were marked [non->renewable](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/15869/files#diff->f968287284d93e6aa5ceb137bf33c9b789b3bccfe6c3055897d2a526eb720d54L172). The documentation you refer to >explains different behavior for non-renewable leased secrets in the [section below](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent/template#non-renewable-leased-secrets) it. I may have been a bit off on the exact cause and terminology, as I had limited time to fully investigate, but what I can say with certainty is that the 1.13 upgrade caused our sidecar containers running vault agent and configured via consul-template to stop refreshing STS credentials. It seems likely that what lindley referenced above is the root cause of what we experienced.

Vault version 1.11.0 added the feature of having multiple root CAs under the same pki engine mount._x000D_

_x000D_
One can request all issuers `<pki>/issuers` which returns the ids and iterate over them `<pki>/issuer/<id>` but in my opinion that's unnecessary boilerplate._x000D_
_x000D_
I'm happy to open a PR if we can agree on how the response should look like._x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
$ curl "$VAULT_ADDR/v1/<pki>/cert/ca" | jq -r ._x000D_
{_x000D_
   "request_id": "...",_x000D_
   "...",_x000D_

title: Support float64 gauge metrics
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
It can be useful to report Unix timestamps as gauge metrics. For Prometheus, the recommended unit is Unix timestamps (in seconds) https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/naming/. Vault uses the go-metrics library which stores metrics as float32s, later upcast for Prometheus. For Unix times, this isn't enough precision (https://go.dev/play/p/RvJ11Y8R7Cz) and truncates the value to about ~2 minute precision._x000D_
_x000D_
Vault has at least one instance of this, probably unnoticed: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/2dd4528ed8a8be83e0c1e0b48b1f23dab701181f/builtin/logical/pki/path_tidy.go#L1209_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Either update go-metrics to use float64 values, or add a Gauge64 (something like this fork https://github.com/rcrowley/go-metrics/blob/cf1acfcdf4751e0554ffa765d03e479ec491cad6/gauge_float64.go)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Storing timestamps with a different epoch would work, but be difficult to integrate with tools like Grafana. It also just kicks the can down the road._x000D_
Recording the metric as a "time since event"/"age" would also work, but is brittle in cases where metrics have gaps._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Specifically for Vault Agent, it is useful to record things like last authentication time and other timestamps for alerting._x000D_
_x000D_
go-metrics issue opened here: https://github.com/hashicorp/go-metrics/issues/150_x000D_

title: API documentation for KV is too ambiguous and needs to be clarified
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Referencing the documentation for LIST Secrets here (but could apply to any of the KV secrets APIs): https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#list-secrets_x000D_
_x000D_
For example:_x000D_
`LIST /secret/metadata/:path`_x000D_
_x000D_
The documentation indicates that for KV version 2 for the list secrets api, you are supposed to prefix paths with `<vault_url>/v1/secret/metadata/:path`. However, upon lots of trial and error, and googling this issue, it appears that you are actually supposed to use `<vault_url>/v1/<secret-engine-name>/metadata/<path-to-secret>` (no colon). What is infuriating here is that as a first time user of the Vault API, I shouldn't have to make the following assumptions:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. That "secret" in the API is actually a _secret-engine_ and not a magic API keyword named _secret__x000D_
2. That the ":" in the documented API is also just a variable identifier, and not actually real_x000D_
_x000D_
I am aware that for 1) there is a yellow box at the top of the documentation indicating that secret is a secret-engine, but that is _not at all clear_ until after you run into this problem. I think there is a lack of consistency in the documentation. "secret" should be prefixed by a ":" to match the terminology used for ":path", and "secret" should be renamed to ":secret-engine" to clearly indicate what it actually is._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Attempt to use KV v2 API documentation_x000D_
2. For example, using the documentation, attempt to make an API call to /v1/secret/metadata/:path/to/secret/_x000D_
3. It will fail with the unhelpful error: `{"errors":["no handler for route \"secret/metadata/:path/to/secret/\". route entry not found."]}`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
You should get back a response from the API, because you followed the documentation._x000D_
1. For example, the response would look like `{"request_id":"96013718-2244-8c8a-fa5d-47dfc209e56e","lease_id":"","renewable":false,"lease_duration":0,"data":{"keys":["orgs/"]},"wrap_info":null,"warnings":null,"auth":null}`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I am sure this is obvious for anyone that is a longtime user of the Vault API, but as a new user of the API this is entirely confusing. The documentation should be clear what _is_ and _is not_ a variable, for each API listed, and the examples should reflect that._x000D_

title: Vault Agent lease cache interferes with template refresh for dynamic secrets
body_text:
### Describe the bug_x000D_ The Vault Agent template server can fail to refresh secrets before lease expiration when the Vault Agent is configured with_x000D_ * A `template` stanza using a dynamic (leased) secret_x000D_ * A `cache` stanza (lease-cache enabled)_x000D_ * `use_auto_auth_token` set to either `true` or `"force"`_x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_ All requests issued by the Template server are sent via the Agent's API Proxy using the current Auto-Auth token. When `use_auto_auth_token` is enabled, the current Auto-Auth token is [registered in the Lease Cache](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.13.0/command/agent/sink/inmem/inmem_sink.go). As a result, the Lease Cache will intercept all requests made by the Template server and internally handle renewal of any leases returned to the Template server.[^1] _x000D_ _x000D_ The Lease Cache will _also_ intercept requests from the Template server to `v1/sys/leases/renew` **_and will cache these responses_** because the response message is interpreted as a secret due to its `"lease_id"` field.[^2] As a result, until the Lease Cache's internal renewal loop finishes, all future renewal attempts from the Template server will be served from the cache -- even as the lease is approaching it's `max_ttl`, the Template server will be receive responses which suggest the lease is still being renewed for the entire default `ttl` (rather than the true truncated duration up to the `max_ttl`). This results in the Template server waiting up to `ttl*2/3` seconds (the normal lease renewal period) _after the lease has expired_ before requesting a new secret and re-rendering the template._x000D_ _x000D_ ### To Reproduce_x000D_

Configure a dynamic secret on a Vault Server with a short TTL and Maximum TTL (recommend 5m TTL and 10m MaxTTL)._x000D_ 2. Login with sufficient rights to fetch the secret and renew leases._x000D_ 3. title: Lease since first use
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Consider the scenario of secure introduction were you would create a token for (trusted?) orchestrator which would setup the required stuff and exit, but the token lingers around for sometime._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I propose a new feature called `ttl_after_first_use` or `ttl_since_first_use` - The lease starts "only" the first time the token gets used. The idea is that we can roughly guess (either from previous runs or some perceived timeout), how much time the orchestrator might run and the token expires just after the expected time to run._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
* TTLs are a good way to solve this. But TTLs are hard to get right - With a very long TTL, the token exists even after the orchestrator is run. For a very short TTL, the orchestrator may not complete its job._x000D_
* Fixing number of uses - but this means we should know how many times the token will be used - which is hard if we provision resources automatically._x000D_
* We can try to manually revoke the token after the orchestrator exits._x000D_
* Another automated job, to revoke the token after the orchestrator exits - need one more token (which can be abused)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
While there can be other uses for such a feature, the above mentioned scenario is the main problem. Using ttl + ttl_since_first_use can be a powerful combination._x000D_
_x000D_

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here._x000D_

That is the Vault **client** config file, and is completely separate to the Vault **server** config file - a totally different set of options, which should be in entirely separate files. title: vault ssh may print misleading warning message
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/16683 changed the way vault generates warnings on potential errors regarding flags. This has a side effect when using `vault ssh` which  now generates a (unhelpful) warning _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault ssh -mode=ca -role=role -strict-host-key-checking=false -valid-principals=prince 10.227.12.248 -- pwd -P_x000D_
Command flags must be provided before positional arguments. The following arguments will not be parsed as flags: [--,-P]_x000D_
/home/prince_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
No warning printed_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`):  1.11.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`):  v1.13.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: macos (bash)_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Maybe stop parsing flags after the double dash. Workaround: _x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault ssh -mode=ca -role=role -strict-host-key-checking=false -valid-principals=prince 10.227.12.248 -- pwd -P 2>/dev/null_x000D_
/home/prince_x000D_
```_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: hghaf099: Thanks for filing this ticket, and welcome to HashiCorp Vault community. The warning messages are not misleading as it informs the user which input arguments are not considered flags. Such a warning is not printed if you pass in the `--format=json`. The errors regarding flag errors are still printed if the flags are in the correct position: ``` $> vault ssh -mode=ca -role=role -strict-host-key-checking=false -notDefined=2 -valid-principals=prince 10.227.12.248 Command flags must be provided before positional arguments. The following arguments will not be parsed as flags: [-valid-principals=prince] flag provided but not defined: -notDefined ``` I am going to close this issue for now. Please feel free to open a new ticket or if you have further concerns please let us know and we reopen the issue for further discussions. | maxb: Hi @hghaf099 , I think this issue should be reopened, as it is reporting a genuine defect: The `vault ssh` command has the unusual purpose of being a wrapper that invokes the real `ssh` command (after obtaining credentials). Moreover, the `ssh` command can take another command on its command line, to run on the remote machine. Because of this, there are multiple ways in which it can be a normal use-case for there to be option-like arguments later in the command line, which are deliberately intended either for `ssh`, or for a command being run via `ssh` on the remote machine. This is quite unlike most other commands, where option-like things occurring after positional arguments are often a mistake. It doesn't make sense to try to provide users with a helpful wrapper for Vault SSH operations, but then have it nag them with spurious warnings when they use it in the intended fashion. | hghaf099: This issue should have been fixed. I am closing this, please feel free to reopen this issue or open a new one for further discussions.

title: Vault Agent templating: use Kubernetes annotations to inject PKI cert and key into different files
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I need to generate certificates for my Prometheus server on a Kubernetes cluster to use mTLS. I use the agent injector with annotations to push generated certificates into my Prometheus pod._x000D_
However, Prometheus configuration needs one file for the certificate, one file for the secret, and one file for the CA._x000D_
I use the following configuration:_x000D_
```yaml_x000D_
spec:_x000D_
  template:_x000D_
    metadata:_x000D_
      annotations:_x000D_
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: 'true'_x000D_
        vault.hashicorp.com/role: 'issuer'_x000D_
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-secret-certif.pem: 'pki/issue/cert' _x000D_
        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-template-certif.pem: |_x000D_
          {{- with pkiCert "pki/issue/cert" "common_name=test.example.com" "ttl=2h" -}}_x000D_

solidgoldbomb: I hit the same issue when switching from `dev` mode (which disables `mlock`) to a production deployment. Disabling `mlock` isn't something I wanted to do in a production environment. It wasn't obvious for me how to fix this so I'm dropping some pointers here in case it helps you or someone else to solve this more easily. For those who want to keep `mlock` enabled, the "cannot allocate memory" issue can can be solved by setting the appropriate capability (`cap_ipc_lock`) on the plugin binary like this: ``` sudo setcap cap_ipc_lock=+ep /path/to/your/plugin ``` The docs do mention this requirement but it didn't turn up for me when searching for this issue: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/plugins/plugin-architecture#plugin-execution The error messages for this scenario aren't very helpful but here are a few bread crumbs that might tie the error message back to mlock in case this helps someone out in the future: * "Cannot allocate memory" is the text associated with the `ENOMEM` return code (https://www.gnu.org/software/libc/manual/html_node/Error-Codes.html#index-ENOMEM) * ENOMEM is returned by the `mlock(2)` call when `CAP_IPC_LOCK` a process tries to lock more than its allowed locked memory limit. `CAP_IPC_LOCK` capability allows this limit to be ignored (https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/mlock.2.html#ERRORS). FWIW, this is where `mlock` is called in the plugin (via the plugin sdk): https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/sdk/plugin/serve.go#L133 The `mlock` call is conditionally invoked in the plugin based on an environment variable (`VAULT_PLUGIN_MLOCK_ENABLED`) which is passed through from the `vault` binary when it executes the plugin. I believe this comes directly from the `disable_mlock` config parameter given to `vault`.

title: Fixed token metadata for policy templating
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
There is a clear demand to template policies based on token metadata. Currently, there is no way to do so, because of potential security risks of child tokens changing their metadata and walking around policies._x000D_
_x000D_
Here's an example issue: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/10460_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
The solution could work analogously to orphan tokens. I have 2 possible options:_x000D_
_x000D_
We can create "fixed" metadata with one the following:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. `sudo` or `root` access to the `auth/token/create` and setting `fixed_metadata` parameter to true._x000D_
2. Access to the `auth/token/create/:role` that has `fix_metadata` set._x000D_
_x000D_
Then policies may template `{{ token.metadata }}`, if and only if `fixed_metadata` is set to true. Pseudocode of how this would be handled in code:_x000D_
_x000D_
```py_x000D_
def metadata_key(self, key):_x000D_
    if not self.fixed_metadata or not key in self.metadata:_x000D_
        return None_x000D_
    self.metadata[key]_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
`fixed_metadata` "sticks" to all child non-orphan tokens, and whenever that key is set to true, the token is refused write access to token metadata._x000D_
_x000D_
Another option would be additional field in tokens, called `fixed_metadata`. We can create "fixed" metadata with one of the following:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. `sudo` or `root` access to the `auth/token/create` and setting `fixed_metadata` parameter to the metadata we want to fix to the token._x000D_
2. Access to the `auth/token/create/:role` that has `fix_metadata` set to true, and setting `fixed_metadata` to the metadata we want to fix to the token._x000D_
_x000D_
Same as the previous option, `fixed_metadata` "sticks" to all child non-orphan tokens._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Multiple AppRoles. While that works, it limits flexibility a lot, because we have a generic model of where we put secrets for different apps, and keeping track of that in terraform is very verbose. All we want is the following policy:_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
path "secret/data/{{ token.metadata.subpath }}/*" {_x000D_
    capabilities = ["read", "list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "secret/metadata/{{ token.metadata.subpath }}/*" {_x000D_
    capabilities = ["read", "list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```

title: Vault agent: Need a way to persist/see the lease ids of issued leases
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault administrators in our organization have restricted a number of attempts you can request a lease for a secret to exactly *ONE*. And the TTL is 786h :( So, whenever I want to restart my SQL client, that uses Vault integration, I am screwed and I have to manually ask for my leases to be revoked. _x000D_
_x000D_
Which is VERY annoying. _x000D_
_x000D_
I found out there's a thing called Vault Agent. I've even managed to have it running. And if I request ("read") a secret from CLI, all is good - I can see the lease id so I can revoke it later and then request it again. But none of the SQL integrations have this capability. They request lease in the background, and no matter which verbosity level I put for Agent config, (even TRACE) would not let me see the lease id in the logs_x000D_
_x000D_
I've tried caching, but "persistent" cache only works for Kubernetes, and I work on Windows machine. _x000D_
_x000D_
I've tried templates, but turns out it is kinda .. alongside the cache, so even though I was able to receive a secret via template, it does not have the lease_id (all I see in the output of template is `map[username:foo;password:bar]`) (it's KV v2 secrets) and if I try to get a lease from an SQL client; it's not in the cache => goes to Vault server => 500 error because lease is already given. _x000D_
_x000D_
And I am screwed again_x000D_
_x000D_
Also, even if I were able to see the lease_id in the template output, that would still be of no use; because an SQL client would have to request a new lease anyway. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I don't even know what the solution could look like but you hopefully get the point, There has to be a way to see lease_ids somewhere, preferably I could specify some "log file" for output so that even when agent dies, I can find all my leases and revoke them as needed_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I can only think of 2 alternatives right now_x000D_
- Manually request Vault operators to revoke my leases_x000D_
- I've also tried to request "list" permissions for *my leases in particular* but I am not sure if Vault would allow for that_x000D_
- Add capability to Vault API to just "revoke all my leases" _x000D_
- Just use templates and not use Vault integration in the SQL client (sad :( )_x000D_
- MITM solution to observe lease ids as they fly thru_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
If there are any use-cases that would help us understand the use/need/value please share them as they can help us decide on acceptance and prioritization._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here._x000D_
