title: Database connection and role should be decoupled
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
A database secret backend has a concept of connections and roles.  Currently, one connection can list multiple allowed roles and each role must list one connection._x000D_
_x000D_
Because credentials are created from roles, this setup creates an unavoidable coupling of role to a connection.  This has several consequences:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. `allowed_roles` on a connection is pointless.  Because a role can not be attached to multiple connections, the role either is or isn't attached to the connection._x000D_
2. We can have a single "read only" role, but if we want to use it on two connections, we must duplicate the role.  In practice, this transformes an M+N problem (M connections, N roles) to M * N problem, having con1-role1, con2-role1, con1-role2, con2-role2, instead of saying which connection can use which role._x000D_
_x000D_
Note that many things in vault already work with decouples "roles" or "policies". For example, the PKI backend allows me to create a role with a list of allowed domains.  When I request a certificate from the role, I also supply the list of domains, which must be a subset of allowed domains.  Entities are created irrespective of policies, and I can attach one policy to many entities.  _x000D_
_x000D_
The way the database engine now works would be like having multiple copies of a single user, each one with one policy attached, so that I can read stuff with one account, but to write a secret I would need to relogin to another.  Further, for a second user, I would have to duplicate the policies._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Connections and roles should be completely decoupled.  Role should not require `db_name` at all.  A connection then specifies what roles it can use, or a role specifies which connections it can use.  We can have both directions, but they must be m-to-n._x000D_
2. Credentials are created from a combination of connection and a role: `vault read database/creds/con/role`.  If the `con` allows the `role`, credentials are generated, otherwise I get an error.  The path could also be `role/con` or `role` with a con argument, here we need to think more what is the most common usecase._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. We can write a script to automate generating a matrix of connections and roles.  In principle, this does not scale at all.  With 10 databases and 10 roles we get 100 combinations._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
None_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
I have been thinking today about why there even is multiple connections per database mount and I simply can't find any use-case for the feature as it is now.  What was the intend behind having multiple connections in one mount?_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: maxb: As community contributor, I have no insight at all into the design process that let to the current API, and can only speculate based on the end result - but a couple of observations occur to me: 1) The existence of `allowed_roles` on a connection is surprising to me too. The circumstance in which it would be practically useful, would be if different administrative access to configure roles was given to different name prefixes, and `allowed_roles` was used to guard a sensitive connection from use except by particular named roles, not reconfigurable by lower-privileged administrators. But that seems like a stretch. Surely at that point, you'd be better off just using separate database secret engine mounts. 2) I **can** see a possible use-case for wanting users to not need to know or care which connection their role is associated with: Imagine failing over to a different database cluster (via DNS or LB), and wanting new credentials to be issued on the new cluster, whilst existing credentials continue to be revoked from the old cluster as they expire. Rare, possibly, but I just wanted to put out there a case in which role implying connection on the server side could be useful.

title: docs: external auth method considerations need clarification
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I was confused when I read the following warning in the external auth method docs; it needs clarification:_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/042dd57811c900c9f6e2c85b5460d50560f79105/website/content/docs/auth/index.mdx?plain=1#L52-L56_x000D_
I initially thought this was trying to say that you could not revoke tokens when an external auth method was enabled, and it wasn't clear to me whether that applied solely to tokens issued by the external auth method or all tokens in general.  After testing and reviewing other updates in the author's original p/r, it looks to me like they were trying to warn that tokens may remain valid in Vault after an account is disabled in an external service, though it doesn't actually make such a statement._x000D_
_x000D_
Further, I tried to test these limitations and discovered that, contrary to the cited warning, neither renewal or re-authentication will actually invalidate an existing token.  I used the `userpass` auth method instead of `github`.  Perhaps the described behavior is specific to the GitHub auth method, in which case it should be described in the docs for the GitHub auth method and not here as behavior of external auth methods in general._x000D_
_x000D_

Steps used to test behavior of renewal and re-authentication:_x000D_

maxb: @cipherboy The current phrasing of the deprecation notice at https://hub.docker.com/_/vault seems to imply future 1.13.x releases and those from active older series would continue to be published until those release series go end of life. If that's not the case, and all publishing to https://hub.docker.com/_/vault has now ceased, it would be nice if the statement of deprecation could be amended for clarity.
cipherboy: @maxb Yeah, this is in line with Consul's language though too: > Upcoming in Consul 1.16, we will stop publishing official Dockerhub images and publish only our Verified Publisher images. Users of Docker images should pull from [hashicorp/consul](https://hub.docker.com/r/hashicorp/consul) instead of [consul](https://hub.docker.com/_/consul). Verified Publisher images can be found at https://hub.docker.com/r/hashicorp/consul. vs > Upcoming in Vault 1.14, we will stop publishing official Dockerhub images and publish only our Verified Publisher images. Users of Docker images should pull from [hashicorp/vault](https://hub.docker.com/r/hashicorp/vault) instead of [vault](https://hub.docker.com/_/vault). Verified Publisher images can be found at https://hub.docker.com/r/hashicorp/vault. --- Do you have suggestions here? Maybe: > Upcoming in Vault 1.14, we will stop publishing [**all**] official Dockerhub images [versions] and publish only our Verified Publisher images. Users of Docker images should pull from [hashicorp/vault](https://hub.docker.com/r/hashicorp/vault) instead of [vault](https://hub.docker.com/_/vault). Verified Publisher images can be found at https://hub.docker.com/r/hashicorp/vault.
maxb: The issue is that the "Upcoming in Vault 1.14" language primes someone who is used to thinking of software in terms of release series / branches, to view the rest of the text as a change introduced on main, first released in the 1.14 release series. (Whilst earlier release branches remain operating via previous release engineering tooling.) Such a policy would have been most convenient for end users, as it would allow an end user currently following the 1.13.x series to continue to obtain images for future patch releases in that series, without needing to migrate to a different image flavour. (I recall someone mentioning that the `library/vault` and `hashicorp/vault` images were based on different Alpine versions, so are not necessarily trivial drop-in replacements.) A phrasing such as: > **From the day of release of Vault 1.14.0,** we will stop publishing official Dockerhub images and publish only our Verified Publisher images. **This will also apply to patch releases of Vault 1.13.x and earlier release branches, released after that time.** would be effective in eliminating that alternative interpretation.

body_text:

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
A clear and concise description of what the bug is._x000D_
After upgrading our HashiCorp Vault to version 1.13.1, we have encountered latency issues with authentication (auth) calls. We have been using AWS authentication in our setup and the below summary is based on the same, although this would apply to other auth methods as well. Upon thorough investigation, we have identified that this latency is a result of a recently introduced feature: "Enable role based quotas for lease-count quotas" (commit: 614cee3178f3a0d99a92f194ddbb888eb15b539f) in the Vault GitHub repository._x000D_
_x000D_
The root cause of the latency stems from a new method called DetermineRoleFromLoginRequest, which is utilized specifically for determining the role. In our case, this method invokes the Security Token Service (STS) every time it is called. Prior to this feature, the STS was only invoked once for AWS authentication. However, with the implementation of DetermineRoleFromLoginRequest, every auth call now triggers three additional invocations of STS for AWS authentication thus increasing the latency by ~3x._x000D_
_x000D_
These three invocations occur from the following points within the code:_x000D_
_x000D_
Rate limiting handler: [util.go#L70](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/e3dad5b6da871c82d8688467fcc7279f484c24d4/http/util.go#L70)_x000D_
HandleLoginRequest: [request_handling.go#L1482](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/e3dad5b6da871c82d8688467fcc7279f484c24d4/vault/request_handling.go#L1482)_x000D_
CreateLoginToken: [request_handling.go#L1788](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/e3dad5b6da871c82d8688467fcc7279f484c24d4/vault/request_handling.go#L1788)_x000D_
_x000D_
This increased frequency of STS calls for AWS authentication has led to noticeable latency in our authentication workflow. We believe it would be beneficial to optimize this implementation to reduce the number of STS invocations and alleviate the resulting latency impact._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Enable AWS auth - vault auth enable aws_x000D_
2. Create a test policy and a test role and associate AWS IAM principal to it_x000D_
3. vault login -method=aws role=test-role_x000D_
4. Observe latency difference_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Inconsistent namespace behaviour using Terraform to read HCP Vault Secrets
body_text:

_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Received odd `No secrets found at...` error using Terraform to read secrets in HCP Vault 1.12.3+ent. Typically, we use the following block to read secrets and this has worked for us through numerous applications. _x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
data "vault_generic_secret" "our_secret" {_x000D_
  namespace = "admin/<child_namespace>"_x000D_
  path      = "<secret_path>"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
However, today we noticed that we had to remove the parent namespace, admin, in order for it to work. All other settings/configs seem to be consistent. Curious why/how this happened?_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
data "vault_generic_secret" "our_secret" {_x000D_
  namespace = "<child_namespace>"_x000D_
  path      = "<secret_path>"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
- See above. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
I'd expect the below block to work_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
data "vault_generic_secret" "our_secret" {_x000D_
  namespace = "admin/<child_namespace>"_x000D_
  path      = "<secret_path>"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
HCP Vault - 1.12.3+ent_x000D_
Terraform Vault Provider - 3.15.2_x000D_
Terraform version - 1.5.1_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
The variables are specified in the Terraform Cloud workspace. _x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
provider "vault" {_x000D_
  auth_login_userpass {_x000D_
    namespace = "admin"_x000D_
    username  = var.hcp_vault_username_x000D_
    password  = var.hcp_vault_password_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_

And now, I no longer work for a company with an Enterprise subscription. However I do remember reading in <https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/vault/latest/docs#namespace-support>: > All resource's namespace will be made relative to the provider's configured namespace. The behaviour you observe seems to suggest that your "provider's configured namespace" has changed from the root namespace to "admin". The provider configuration snippet that you've shown does not set the "provider's configured namespace" (which is different from a namespace specified within any `auth` block), so it would pick up any namespace specified in a `VAULT_NAMESPACE` environment variable. Is it possible that the `VAULT_NAMESPACE` environment variable has been set to `admin` in the context performing your Terraform runs? | tyu0912: Hi @maxb , I was able to resolve this. In version 3.15.2, you're able to specify parent and children namespaces together in the read but it seems in 3.16.0 they've updated it to be relative to whatever is specified in the auth block which I have as `admin` above. Not sure if this is a feature or bug but it does seem to have been reported elsewhere: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-vault/issues/1903.

title: Audit Log logging issue when browsing the Web UI in KV Secrets
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Through the Web UI, in the KV Secret Engine, if a user navigates to a secret, even not clicking on the eye icon to effectively  "read" the value of the secret, the Vault stores in the Audit Log the information that the user has read the secret._x000D_
_x000D_
![Captura de tela 2023-06-23 225425](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/11522957/cf405528-9d72-4c7b-a084-5b891413d12f)_x000D_
_x000D_
Analyzing the Web UI, even if the user does not click on the eye icon to display the secret, it has already been redeemed and is available in the frontend._x000D_
_x000D_
![Captura de tela 2023-06-23 225900](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/11522957/ff0c6940-1fb4-48cc-ae88-3278057d889c)_x000D_
_x000D_
This causes confusion when analyzing the Audit Log... it's impossible to know which users actually read the secret, or which ones are just analyzing the available keys or the structure of the KV Secret._x000D_
_x000D_
I believe that the best approach here would be to fetch the secret from the vault only when the user clicks on the eye icon, before that, the secret must not be retrieved from the Vault... only the list of keys._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Access Vault Web Interface (UI)_x000D_
2. Navigate to a Secret in KV Secret Engine_x000D_
3. Don't click on the eye icon to show the secret_x000D_
4. Analyze the Audit Log and realize that was already logged that the secret was read by the user, even not clicking on the eye icon._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The Audit Log should record that the secret was actually read only when the user clicks on the eye icon._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.14.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.14.0 (13a649f860186dffe3f3a4459814d87191efc321), built 2023-06-19T11:40:23Z_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Windows
top_3_comments_text: maxb: (Note: I'm not a HashiCorp employee, I'm just a Vault user and sometimes community contributor.) Let's break this down into two separate components: **Component 1** The entire architecture of the KV secrets engine API is built around working with **secrets at paths** - in your case here, `example/secret`. These secrets are natively JSON objects which can have potentially multiple keys - in your case here, `key`. Talking about the KV secrets engine frequently gets rather ambiguous, as when a user uses words like "secret" or "key", do they mean the thing at an URL-path (`example/secret`) or a single key within it (`key`). Individually revealing individual keys would require a conceptual jump in design, as currently there is no individual access to keys in the Vault API at all, and consequently they can neither be separately permissioned, nor do the appear separately in the audit log. The API always treats the whole entity at the path as a single thing. **Component 2** On the other hand, some versions back, support for retrieving just the keys within a path, with the values replaced with nulls, was added to Vault: <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#read-secret-subkeys> So, conceptually, the capability is there in the existing API, so that a future UI version could progressively display the keys only, and then fetch **all** of the values to go with them once **any one** of them is requested. --- Bear in mind I don't work for HashiCorp - but if you share your reaction to this breakdown of your initial posting, you may give them more information to work with, when deciding if/when to do any work in this direction. | heatherezell: Thank you, @maxb as always :)

title: Vault no longer respects AWS_ROLE_ARN or AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE for AWS KMS
labels: auth/oidc, core/seal, ecosystem, helmchart, k8s, secret/aws
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
AWS KMS seals no longer respect the `AWS_ROLE_ARN` or `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` environment variables, which are required for assuming  IAM roles via Kubernetes ServiceAccount tokens. Instead, Vault attempts to use the EC2 instance's IAM role (if available) to access the KMS key instead of using the Kubernetes ServiceAccount._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Create an AWS EKS cluster_x000D_
2. [Connect the EKS cluster as an OIDC provider for AWS IAM_x000D_
](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/enable-iam-roles-for-service-accounts.html)_x000D_
3. Create an AWS KMS key_x000D_
4. [Create an AWS IAM role with an assume-role policy authorizing that OIDC provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/associate-service-account-role.html), and an inline policy authorizing that IAM role for actions on the KMS key you created_x000D_
5. Deploy Vault with an `"awskms"` seal, setting only `kms_key_id`, and adding a ServiceAccount annotation `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: <IAM role ARN>`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should assume the IAM role configured in the Kubernetes ServiceAccount annotation and referenced by `AWS_ROLE_ARN` (injected by EKS because of the annotation), using the Kubernetes ServiceAccount token file referenced by `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` (also injected by EKS) for authentication with AWS._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: 1.14.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: running on EKS 1.24, deployed using Vault's official Helm chart v0.25.0_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  tls_disable = 1_x000D_
  address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
  cluster_address = "[::]:8201"_x000D_
  x_forwarded_for_authorized_addrs = ["####", "####"]_x000D_
  x_forwarded_for_reject_not_present = false_x000D_
}_x000D_
storage "consul" {_x000D_
  path = "vault"_x000D_
  address = "HOST_IP:8500"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
service_registration "kubernetes" {}_x000D_
_x000D_
seal "awskms" {_x000D_
  region     = "us-east-1"_x000D_
  kms_key_id = "######"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
There is an easy workaround for this bug, which is to set `role_arn` and `web_identity_token_file` in the seal settings like so:_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
seal "awskms" {_x000D_
  region     = "us-east-1"_x000D_
  kms_key_id = "######"_x000D_
_x000D_
  # Fixes for Vault 1.14+_x000D_
  role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::<account ID>:role/<role name>"_x000D_
  web_identity_token_file = "/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Also, as far as I could trace it, the issue seems to come from this list of approved(?) environment variables for the AWS KMS wrapper?: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/commit/254d8f835614e8417e89155c2c94c2767177831c#diff-8669cb5f3518deb7d1841c405e7e8b222348751cf85f81e6077a1184e9ed767dR15-R23_x000D_
_x000D_
Hopefully the fix is as easy as adding `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` and `AWS_ROLE_ARN` to that list._x000D_

title: Vault > 1.13.0 will not start up if dsa1024 PGP key was used to encrypt seal secret shares initially
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
After upgrading from Vault 1.12.1 to a version > 1.13.0, our Vault installation will fail to start up with the following error:_x000D_
_x000D_
> Error initializing core: Error checking for existing seal: failed to validate barrier seal configuration at migration check time: error parsing given PGP key: openpgp: invalid data: subkey signature invalid: openpgp: invalid signature: hash tag doesn't match _x000D_
_x000D_
During setup, we opted to have the seal secret shares encrypted with PGP keys, and during investigation of the issue, I discovered that one of these keys had been a very very old, insecure, dsa1024 key that should never have been used in the first place._x000D_
_x000D_
I was able to remediate the issue by manually manipulating the `pgp_keys` field in the seal-config, replacing the offending key, but really this shouldn't be a hard error, since, as I understand it, the PGP keys are only used during initial setup or re-keying. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Set up Vault 1.12.1 or earlier with seal secret shares encrypted with a very old DSA PGP key_x000D_
2. Upgrade to Vault 1.13.0 or later_x000D_
3. See error_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
* Vault starts_x000D_
* Vault should warn about insecure/unusable keys._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): v1.13.1, v1.14.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.13.1, v1.14.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Fedora CoreOS Linux, Kernel 6.2.15, x86_64_x000D_
_x000D_

If running into this issue, downgrade to Vault 1.12 and run the `vault operator rekey` operation, passing the `-pgp-keys` option, pointing to RSA keys instead: ``` -pgp-keys=<keybase:user1, keybase:user2, ...> Comma-separated list of paths to files on disk containing public PGP keys OR a comma-separated list of Keybase usernames using the format "keybase:<username>". I will have a bit more time now. > @Malshtur Yes, this is definitely one approach; support for multiple chains in the same role. > > Alternatively, separate roles with individual chains could be used as well, if there is a root CA rotation and you wish to keep each role to a single root. > > But yes, happy to review docs pull requests on this! As it has been while since I opened this issue, let's take the following example to describe a three-layered PKI. I hope it will cover all scenarios to make sure I can come with a proper PR. 1. Root CA v1 2. Intermediate CA v1.1 3. Issuing CA Infra v1.1.1 and Issuing CA Web v1.1.1 In this example, the roles are based on the Issuing CA Infra v1.1.1 and its Web counter-part is a real secret engine for another purpose. To make sure the authentication is properly made, the CA used for Auth TLS should be the Issuing CA Infra v1.1.1 otherwise the web ones could be used if they have overlapping end entity informations. If Issuing CA infra v1.1.1 is to be rotated with Issuing CA infra v1.1.2, both will share a period of validity to avoid interruption of service. On the PKI subject, i've read that a CA should issue child certs with lifetimes at most half of its own, i.e : CA cert is valid for 1 year then child certs should last at most 6 months. This CA should be rotated at the half of it to make he can't issue certificates lasting longer than itself. The new CA will become the new default issuer 6 months after the creation of the former CA. With all of this, if Root CA v1 or Intermediate CA v1.1 rotate a new Issuing CA Infra vx.x.1 must be created to prevent breaking the authentication service. **Question 1 :** To make sure I understood you and since it has been a bit long since I opened the issue, can you confirm that the `certificate` field in /auth/cert/certs/:name (endpoint to create a CA certificate Role) is able to handle the former CA and the new one ? If it is possible, then should I concatenate them in pem format like this ? ` -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIEtzCCA5+.......ZRtAfQ6r\nwlW975rYa1ZqEdA=\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----` (Former CA) `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIEtzCCA5+.......ZRtAfQ6r\nwlW975rYa1ZqEdA=\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----` (Newer CA) Otherwise, what would you advice ? **Question 2 :** Also, should the PEM-format CA be a bundle including the full chain to the root or only Issuing CA infra v1.1.1 is enough ? Creating different roles is easier but requires a bit more intervention because every role has to be duplicated with the new Issuing CA infra vx.x.x. Preserving the same role is a bit more obscure because i don't really know how to make two CA certs fill the `certificate` field in /auth/cert/certs/:name endpoint. cipherboy: \o hey @Malshtur sorry about the delay -- I was on vacation when you posted this :-) > ... > > With all of this, if Root CA v1 or Intermediate CA v1.1 rotate a new Issuing CA Infra vx.x.1 must be created to prevent breaking the authentication service. All of this sound good up to here! > Question 1 : ... > > If it is possible, then should I concatenate them in pem format like this ? ... Correct, that's what I'd recommend. :-) This allows the authenticating user to pass as much -- or as little -- chain as they'd like. They could just use their leaf certificate, or if they pass chaining up through the Root CA v1, it doesn't matter much. As you rotate, by putting both CA certificates in the same role (because they're otherwise equivalent), you treat them the same and thus limit duplication of roles unnecessarily. > Question 2 : ... > > Also, should the PEM-format CA be a bundle including the full chain to the root or only Issuing CA infra v1.1.1 is enough ? If you're pinning to a specific intermediate because you have other intermediates that have issued non-auth leaf certificates, I would likely include on that specific intermediate. However, if you have a different mechanism for limiting authentication (e.g., using ExtKeyUsage in a restrictive mode so that servers only have ServerAuth and only valid client certificates have ClientAuth --- or using an extension on the client auth certificates e.g., a Usage=Vault extension), then specifying the full CA chain would be useful as it gracefully allows authentication. Clients present a (subset of a) valid chain: either just the leaf cert, the leaf and its immediate issuing CA, or the leaf and some number of parent issuing CAs. So the client will never send, e.g., the root CA (skip several intermediates) and the leaf and expect to be able to authenticate. In the former case described by you, because the intermediate is what ultimately dictates trust and authorization (and not the root -- the root: it dictates trust but not authorization), you should set the intermediate. But in the latter, where the root is sufficient (with potentially other mitigating controls), you can set the root + intermediates to allow leaf-only connections (or otherwise gracefully handle missing CA certs the client hasn't sent).

title: Keyring corrupted: unseal failed, invalid key
body_text:
_x000D_ _x000D_ I'm not sure if this is a bug but I'm hoping you can help us understand what is going on._x000D_ _x000D_ On a couple of occasions, we have seen Vault fail to unseal with the error `Unseal failed, invalid key`. The issue is permanent and the only way to recover is to restore a working backup._x000D_ _x000D_ The unseal keys seem to be correct because the error originates from decrypting the keyring (`core/keyring` in vault storage). That becomes after the unseal key was already successfully used to decrypt the storage root key (`core/hsm/barrier-unseal-keys` in vault storage). When running Vault under the debugger I can see the callstack is below [1]. The error message from `gcmAsm.Open()` is `cipher: message authentication failed`._x000D_ _x000D_ The data in the keyring seems to be OK: its length is the same as in the working backup and it begins with a valid header that Vault appends to encrypted values `{"Value":"AAAAAQ....`_x000D_ _x000D_ We have not been able to reproduce the issue on demand, and the exact circumstances when the fault happened are not known, but we have speculated with the following scenarios_x000D_ _x000D_ - Backup & restore scenario: Vault might have been initialized with empty storage and unsealed, then storage was restored from a backup while Vault was still running. Since Vault periodically writes the keyring it, could overwrite the one restored from the backup. The keyring would be encrypted with a different key, not matching the storage root key._x000D_ - Memory corruption: The storage root key might be corrupted in runtime memory (e.g. due to a bug) and when Vault periodically writes the keyring, it got encrypted with the corrupted key._x000D_ _x000D_ We are using etcd as the storage backend._x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_ Questions:_x000D_ _x000D_ Have you seen keyring corruption before?_x000D_ Can you think of any theories on how this issue could happen?_x000D_ Do you have any suggestions on how to go about troubleshooting this kind of issue and avoid it in the future?_x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_
[1] callstack_x000D_ 
_x000D_
# The topmost function is the most recent_x000D_
#    decrypting keyring results in "cipher: message authentication failed" here:_x000D_
go/src/crypto/aes/aes_gcm.go:gcmAsm.Open()    # https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.20.5:src/crypto/aes/aes_gcm.go;l=182_x000D_
vault/barrier_aes_gcm.go:AESGCMBarrier:decrypt()    # https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/325233ea7dba833e987909b21af547d0933751e3/vault/barrier_aes_gcm.go#L1037_x000D_
vault/barrier_aes_gcm.go:AESGCMBarrier.Unseal()    # https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/325233ea7dba833e987909b21af547d0933751e3/vault/barrier_aes_gcm.go#L453)_x000D_

title: A way to configure a timeout in Database Engine Roles
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
We have a particular database for which dynamic credentials revocation consistently fails, due to timeout. It's not a network issue, it really just takes a while. I'm able to login to the database from the same network as Vault and run the same queries configured as revocation statement and they work fine, albeit slowly._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
A way to configure a timeout in Database Engine Roles, so that Vault does not give up before things have enough time to succeed._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
I haven't been able to come up other alternatives that don't require deep architectural changes for product development teams that use our platform. I would rather if we could at least alleviate the issue on our end without being too intrusive. A timeout seems simple enough._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
The failure to revoke leads to leases living on forever, and Vault continues to periodically attempt to revoke them, causing a higher resource consumption and sometimes leading to saturation if we don't manually remove the leases (and roles from the Database)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
This is an AWS RDS, which notably require custom-made revocation statements because the root user isn't _really_ root/superuser. Its privileges are capped and we don't have access to the actual superuser, only AWS does.

title: Allow identity engine to register custom public keys
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I'm provisioning a service into my main Kubernetes cluster (EKS), which other clusters (EKS, AKS, self-hosted, etc...) can access into._x000D_
so, I'm trying to use the pod's default service account token for authentication._x000D_
the cluster is created or destroyed dynamically and the service's issuer configuration cannot be modified dynamically (it must restart)._x000D_
so, in this situation, I need to discovery additional issuers using jwks_uri. (`KUBERNETES_DISCOVERY_TRUST_ISSUER` flow)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
add a API to add user-provided x509 public key to identity engine._x000D_
public key needs to be registered without (vault identity engine's) key and role, and served on `jwks_uri`_x000D_
current API: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/identity/tokens_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I also thought using vault as a token issuer and each cluster requesting the token that is need, but I think it was not possible, and using service account is easier to manage as the token is generated automatically by kubernetes apiserver._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I'm not sure but I've found issues that might be related to this._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/8307_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/19209

title: Enhanced metrics for DynamoDB backend
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
We recently had a multi-hour outage on a vault cluster using DynamoDB backend and our investigation was challenging due to limited information in logs and metrics.  Vault was reporting a very low RATE(dynamodb_get_total_count) close to zero, but the AWS console was reporting ~25k qps of DynamoDB read requests.  The number of core_in_flight_requests spiked to 200k, and we had large numbers of go routines and high memory usage.  We suspect the DynamoDB backend was returning errors and the AWS client was doing infinite retries (we did not have AWS_DYNAMODB_MAX_RETRIES set, but that is fixed now).  If that was the case, then most likely we reached the limit on the DynamoDB PermitPool causing all the other requests to wait on that lock.  But as far as we can tell, there is nothing in the logs or metrics that would indicate we have reached the limit of our PermitPool._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Metrics covering the DynamoDB PermitPool would be very useful.  If we had gauge metrics for `Active Permits`, `Pool Size`, and `Permits Waiting` we could quickly determine that DynamoDB layer is the cause of requests backing up._x000D_

title: Postgres database secret engine fails to connect when password contains URI-reserved characters such as @ or /
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Using a configured Postgres database connection (see https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/databases/postgresql#configure-connection ) with URI:_x000D_
```_x000D_
postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@postgres-database-host:5432/database-name_x000D_
```_x000D_
fails when the password contains URI-reserved characters, such as `@` or `/`._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
* Enable the Postgres database engine in Vault_x000D_
* Configure a connection with a URI containing the `{{username}}` and `{{password}}` templates_x000D_
* Attempt to use this connection with a database role_x000D_
=> this fails with error:_x000D_
```_x000D_
error verifying connection: failed to connect to `host=postgres-database-host user={{username}} database=database-name`: failed SASL auth (FATAL: password authentication failed for user "{{username}}")_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The database engine should be able to successfully connect to the database._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version : `1.13.0`_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version: `1.13.0`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: `linux x86_64`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
The problem stems from the fact that these values *must be URI percent encoded* as described in https://www.postgresql.org/docs/15/libpq-connect.html#LIBPQ-CONNSTRING:_x000D_
> The connection URI needs to be encoded with [percent-encoding](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-2.1) if it includes symbols with special meaning in any of its parts._x000D_
_x000D_
This percent encoding must be done for ANY template-rendered value: this means that this problem also exists with `{{username}}` (any character is allowed by Postgres when using double-quoted identifiers as described in https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-syntax-lexical.html#SQL-SYNTAX-IDENTIFIERS ._x000D_
Unicode characters can even be used for identifiers (role/user name here) as well which can contain URI-reserved characters:_x000D_
> Unicode characters can be specified in escaped form by writing a backslash followed by the four-digit hexadecimal code point number or alternatively a backslash followed by a *plus sign* followed by a six-digit hexadecimal code point number._x000D_
_x000D_
Note that when using [GH-19616](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/6910) (available with version 1.14.0), the scram-sha-256 value is base64 encoded, which means that it can still contain URI-reserved characters such as `/` and `+`(see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648#section-4), and problem is even more difficult to spot._x000D_
_x000D_
Finally, using a Keyword/Value Connection Strings may help to work around the issue (the pgx library supports this) but some characters still need to be escaped, which brings us to square one: templated values must be escaped.

maxb: The Vault cluster listener refers to the private communications on port 8201 which are only ever between one Vault server and another. This listener does not use user-provided TLS certificates. Certificates are internally generated within the Vault code, and kept within the Vault storage backend. For the cluster listener to somehow not have any certificates, should not really be possible. Perhaps you could share more of your debug logs?

title: Improved logging for Vault Agent when a 500 error is encountered via cache
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When a vault agent that has `cache` enabled encounters a 500 error response when attempting to render a secret to template, the logs for the agent does not surface the actual error. This can make it confusing to troubleshoot._x000D_
_x000D_
I think this user encountered this behavior but the underlying cause of the 500 error was resolved so it never went anywhere_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/17900_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Utilize Linux Kernel Keystore to protect in-memory secrets
body_text:
As a Vault operator, I want vault to make maximal use of all available protections to prevent secrets it protects from being exposed. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Evaluate the Linux Key Retention Service per_x000D_
* https://blog.cloudflare.com/the-linux-kernel-key-retention-service-and-why-you-should-use-it-in-your-next-application/_x000D_
* https://kernel.org/doc/html/v6.0/security/keys/core.html#key-overview_x000D_
* https://youtu.be/7djRRjxaCKk_x000D_
_x000D_
for suitability in storing sensitive data outside of the Vault memory space._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/security indicates that memory safety of Vault is not one of the threats addressed by Vault, so I can see this might be considered 'out of scope'.
top_3_comments_text: cipherboy: Fundamentally, as an approach to protect Vault server's managed secrets, this is not suitable as it won't solve the problem. There are many equivalent secrets that leak in memory that cannot be stored in the kernel keyring due to design restrictions of both the keyring and of the Go toolchain. Consider: 1. TLS session keys. Go does not understand placing them in the kernel keyring and further, simply storing them in the keyring would necessitate moving them back to memory (for actual encryption operations). A better kernel keyring design so that encryption operations can occur within it seems impractical, given it competes with things like e.g., TPMs, PKCS#11 tokens, &c. With these keys, an attacker can decrypt any and all traffic coming to/from Vault, stealing high-privileged tokens, or even just passively reading session traffic. 2. (inner) HTTP traffic, including auth tokens, login info, and transited secrets. Skipping breaking TLS, secrets are transmitted within the inner HTTP stream, and these could be read from memory. Here, unless Go updates to support decrypting _into_ kernel keyring space (which again, seems unlikely -- and bodies can be somewhat large, I think our default is 30MB), the TLS decrypt operation would (temporarily) leak any in-flight decryption requests at memory snapshot time. 3. Other similar approaches to the above apply _many_ places within Vault (Transit keys, PKI CAs, reading/writing from KV, database creds, at token creation time, ...) &c. Then there's the scalability aspect: based on https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/keyrings.7.html , there's only (by default) 200x 20KB secrets for non-root users (which we don't recommend running Vault as root!). With root, that's 20,000x 20MB, which is much better suited for running Vault at scale. But this means that operators would need to tune their Kernel instance at scale, to support reading/writing more secrets. (Thanks to @swenson, we believe https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v5.8/security/keys/core.html could help with some of the e.g., TLS termination concerns, but without deep Go enablement, would still likely result in HTTP request being in memory when Go parses the HTTP body). Instead, I think the technology that would be best suited here would be full memory encryption: e.g., [one of our partners](https://www.hashicorp.com/partners/tech/anjuna): https://www.anjuna.io/blog/runtime-protection-for-secrets-management --- However, what _is_ a good use of this technology, and one I've personally been wanting to see, is a protocol for reading secrets from keyring instead of envvars. E.g., to [parse path](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-secure-stdlib/blob/1a4b95565d57828244cbb7879b8d3a8f3d20522a/parseutil/parsepath.go#L20-L39) so that a `keyring://` schema could be used to transparently fetch secrets out of kernel keyring (mostly used server-side I believe). Or, further, to enhance our server config to directly read sensitive values from kernel keyring. Or, via vault agent's [templating functionality](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/agent/template), to allow Agent to place fetched secrets into keyring on the client, where available. Here, I think we'd welcome pull requests in this direction! My 2c. :-) | jhmartin: Thank you for the detailed analysis! Would it have any applicability to protecting the unseal key (as in, after the vault has been unsealed; keep the master key out of the memory space)? | cipherboy: Hmm, I can't find the diagram quickly here, but I think this is good enough: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/architecture Essentially, with manual shamir's unseal, there's the following key hierarchy: ``` shamir splits =combines-to-form=> shamir protected unseal key =encrypts=> root key =encrypts=> barrier key ring =encrypts=> secrets on disk ``` Here, the root key is purged from memory as soon as it is done being used, leaving only the barrier keyring in memory. Secrets that are actively being read/written are accessible of course, but the ability to unseal Vault again (from a memory dump, +/- root key actually being purged from memory/overwritten by the OS) is prohibited. I think to protect the barrier keyring, you'd need to have Kernel support for encrypting/decrypting data via AES, which isn't currently possible _I believe from the link above_. Again, a TPM/PKCS#11/... might be more relevant here, and using Seal Wrapping provides the same protection (for critical security parameters/CSPs). My 2c., obviously there's defense in depth, but at some point, running on compromised hosts provides limited utility. To be able to read memory, you'd need to have root level access, at which point, how do you even know it is Vault running and not some other compromised software?

E.g., to [parse path](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-secure-stdlib/blob/1a4b95565d57828244cbb7879b8d3a8f3d20522a/parseutil/parsepath.go#L20-L39) so that a `keyring://` schema could be used to transparently fetch secrets out of kernel keyring (mostly used server-side I believe). Or, further, to enhance our server config to directly read sensitive values from kernel keyring. Or, via vault agent's [templating functionality](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/agent/template), to allow Agent to place fetched secrets into keyring on the client, where available. Here, I think we'd welcome pull requests in this direction! My 2c. :-)
jhmartin: Thank you for the detailed analysis! Would it have any applicability to protecting the unseal key (as in, after the vault has been unsealed; keep the master key out of the memory space)?
cipherboy: Hmm, I can't find the diagram quickly here, but I think this is good enough: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/architecture Essentially, with manual shamir's unseal, there's the following key hierarchy: ``` shamir splits =combines-to-form=> shamir protected unseal key =encrypts=> root key =encrypts=> barrier key ring =encrypts=> secrets on disk ``` Here, the root key is purged from memory as soon as it is done being used, leaving only the barrier keyring in memory. Secrets that are actively being read/written are accessible of course, but the ability to unseal Vault again (from a memory dump, +/- root key actually being purged from memory/overwritten by the OS) is prohibited. I think to protect the barrier keyring, you'd need to have Kernel support for encrypting/decrypting data via AES, which isn't currently possible _I believe from the link above_. Again, a TPM/PKCS#11/... might be more relevant here, and using Seal Wrapping provides the same protection (for critical security parameters/CSPs). My 2c., obviously there's defense in depth, but at some point, running on compromised hosts provides limited utility. To be able to read memory, you'd need to have root level access, at which point, how do you even know it is Vault running and not some other compromised software?
victorr: I am closing this issue since there is no specific feature to implement. Thank you @jhmartin for your well documented request.

title: Templated ACL does not resolve group id by name
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When using ACL for resolving the id of a group by name for a path access in a policy, this seems not to work._x000D_
Example policy:_x000D_
```_x000D_
path "identity/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "identity/entity-alias/*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list", "read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
path "identity/group/id/{{identity.groups.names.secret_users.id}}" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list", "read", "create", "update"]_x000D_
  allowed_parameters = {_x000D_
    "policies" = [["secret_rw"]]_x000D_
    "*" = []_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
Attempting to modify the group with this policy ends in permission denied._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run a vault dev server_x000D_
2. Create a new auth method (e.g. userpass) and a user **testing** (including identity)_x000D_
3. Create two internal groups (**secret_admin** and **secret_users**)_x000D_
4. Assign the user **testing** to the group **secret_admin**_x000D_
5. Grant policy described above to the group **secret_admin**_x000D_
6. Login  as **testing** and attempt to modify (or even read)  **secret_users**_x000D_
7. See error_x000D_
_x000D_
Replacing the template with the group id directly (by looking it up), fixes the issue (group can be modified as intended)._x000D_
Example:_x000D_
```_x000D_
path "identity/group/id/{{identity.groups.names.secret_users.id}}" {_x000D_
```_x000D_
-->_x000D_
```_x000D_
path "identity/group/id/b55713c6-54aa-1db1-039b-2240e36347d7" {_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Using the ACL with the template should work._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault status_x000D_
Key             Value_x000D_
---             -----_x000D_
Seal Type       shamir_x000D_
Initialized     true_x000D_
Sealed          false_x000D_
Total Shares    1_x000D_
Threshold       1_x000D_
Version         1.14.0_x000D_
Build Date      2023-06-19T11:40:23Z_x000D_
Storage Type    inmem_x000D_
Cluster Name    vault-cluster-b65c7ab8_x000D_
Cluster ID      4fa74630-04c7-9f90-2805-08e6c98d11cd_x000D_
HA Enabled      false_x000D_
```_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault version_x000D_
Vault v1.14.0 (13a649f860186dffe3f3a4459814d87191efc321), built 2023-06-19T11:40:23Z_x000D_
```_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: maxb: This is functioning as designed, although the Vault documentation is severely lacking in a correct explanation of what the design is... The `identity.groups.` lookups are not only a way to avoid writing IDs in policy text - they also cause the entire `path` block to conditionally only apply at run time, if the entity being checked against the policy, is a member of the relevant group. Since your user `testing` is not a member of `secret_users`, the described policy does not apply to it. | mdegel: Thanks for the answer. title: `Retry-After` HTTP header when hiting Rate Limit
body_text:
Hello world!_x000D_
_x000D_
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
We use vault to update a lot of passwords with a random sleep to avoid updating them in one shot._x000D_
In some cases we hit the rate limit with 429 which is expected._x000D_
_x000D_
But usually when I hit this limit, most of API set a [Retry-After](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After) with 503 / 429 error code ([RFC](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-10.2.3))_x000D_
_x000D_
Example with [Gitlab API](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/administration/settings/user_and_ip_rate_limits.html#response-headers)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
When hiting rate limit, it will be very helpful to have the retry-after header set telling us the time to wait before counter are reset for example so we could retry._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
A blind "retry" from code could cover that case but we also have some protections that ban when we reach too many HTTP error code. So it could be a double pain._x000D_
_x000D_
Or we could increase the quota limit but it could impact other users/teams and it shouldn't._x000D_
_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: VioletHynes: Hi there! Great news: we actually already support this! The medium-news is that it's not currently well documented, but that's something that I'm going to be fixing shortly. See the config option here: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/quotas-config#enable_rate_limit_response_headers If set to true, a `Retry-After` (and some other headers, `X-Ratelimit-Limit`, `X-Ratelimit-Remaining`, and `X-Ratelimit-Reset`) will be available to calling clients. 3. `vault login -method=token` and paste your root token_x000D_
4. `vault secrets enable -path='test' pki_x000D_
5. List secret engines with `vault secrets list`. You should see a secret engine of type pki enabled at path 'test'_x000D_

I'm able to mount a secret engine at path _x000D_

You have enabled a secrets engine at path `test`. This means all sub-paths under `test/` are now reserved for operations on that secrets engine. title: Coding style question: Vault backend operation handlers
body_text:
I have noticed that there is a mix of coding styles for Vault backend operation handler functions, and similar._x000D_
_x000D_
I found the difference confusing at first, but have come to believe that there's no functional reason to prefer one or the other._x000D_
_x000D_
I would like to ask HashiCorp:_x000D_
* Is there a defined house style for new Vault code?_x000D_
* Has anyone investigated whether there is a performance penalty in using the more complicated style?_x000D_
* Are PRs to re-style code more consistently welcomed?_x000D_
_x000D_
Style A:_x000D_
```_x000D_
func (b *backend) handleRead(ctx context.Context, req *logical.Request, data *framework.FieldData) (*logical.Response, error) {_x000D_
	return someResponse, nil_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Style B:_x000D_
```_x000D_
func (b *backend) handleRead() framework.OperationFunc {_x000D_
	return func(ctx context.Context, req *logical.Request, data *framework.FieldData) (*logical.Response, error) {_x000D_
		return someResponse, nil_x000D_
	}_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
It seems to me that style B adds more complexity, and a closure, for the dubious benefit of asserting directly in code that the function signature is a `framework.OperationFunc`._x000D_
_x000D_
My attention became particularly focussed on this issue, when I realised that the source code for KV v1 was re-styled from style A to style B when it was copied out of the Vault repo to start the separate KV plugin - as a result, there is now a further discrepancy between the two parallel pieces of code, which hinders diffing them to assess divergence.

title: Vault 1.14.0 no longer uses AWS IRSA role
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault version 1.14.0 no longer uses the IAM roles for service account (IRSA) role to connect to DynamoDB. This issue was introduced in Vault v1.14.0. I tested this in Vault v1.12.x and 1.13.x with no issues._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Deploy Vault Helm chart to EKS, using the DynamoDB storage backed and an IRSA role._x000D_
_x000D_
    Example Helm values file:_x000D_
    _x000D_
    ```yaml_x000D_
    server:_x000D_
      serviceAccount:_x000D_
        annotations:_x000D_
          eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws-us-gov:iam::123456789012:role/MyIRSArole_x000D_
        name: vault_x000D_
      dataStorage:_x000D_
        enabled: false_x000D_
      ha:_x000D_
        enabled: true_x000D_
        config: |_x000D_
          ui = true_x000D_
    _x000D_
          listener "tcp" {_x000D_
            tls_disable = 1_x000D_
            address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
            cluster_address = "[::]:8201"_x000D_
          }_x000D_
    _x000D_
          storage "dynamodb" {_x000D_
            ha_enabled = "true"_x000D_
            region     = "us-gov-west-1"_x000D_
            table      = "TABLE_NAME"_x000D_
          }_x000D_
    _x000D_
          service_registration "kubernetes" {}_x000D_
    _x000D_
          seal "awskms" {_x000D_
            region     = "us-gov-west-1"_x000D_
            kms_key_id = "KEY_ID"_x000D_
          }_x000D_
    ```_x000D_
_x000D_
2. The Vault pods fail to start with the following error:_x000D_
_x000D_
    >Error initializing storage of type dynamodb: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws-us-gov:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/EC2-ROLE/EC2-instance-id is not authorized to perform: dynamodb:DescribeTable on resource: arn:aws-us-gov:dynamodb:us-gov-west-1:123456789012:table/TABLE_NAME because no identity-based policy allows the dynamodb:DescribeTable action_x000D_
    _x000D_
    The output indicates that Vault is attempting to use the EC2 instance role instead of the IRSA role._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should use the IRSA role to connect to DynamoDB._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: 1.14.0_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The required environment variables for IRSA are set within the Vault pod, but Vault does not seem to be prioritizing IRSA for authentication._x000D_
_x000D_
The environment variables set by IRSA include:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
AWS_ROLE_ARN=arn:aws-us-gov:iam::123456789012:role/MyIRSArole_x000D_
AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE=/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token_x000D_
AWS_STS_REGIONAL_ENDPOINTS=regional_x000D_
AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-gov-west-1_x000D_
AWS_REGION=us-gov-west-1_x000D_
```_x000D_

top_3_comments_text: maxb: This line shows a misunderstanding: > ```yaml > tls_client_ca_file = "/vault/userconfig/vault-ha-tls/vault.ca" > ``` You are not using client certificate authentication, so you should not set this. It does not break anything, but it misleads you and others reading the configuration into thinking you have set a relevant setting, when you have not. > ```yaml > VAULT_CACERT: /vault/userconfig/vault-ha-tls/vault.ca > ``` This environment variable is primarily intended for configuring a Vault **client**, not a **server**. title: Ability to specify 'token_no_default_policy=false' when enabling an auth method
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We want to allow users of our vault to be able to create their own roles for auth methods, but we also want to always enforce a default policy._x000D_
Currently users can disable the default policy when creating a role for an auth method, by setting 'token_no_default_policy=true'_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
We would like to be able to specify 'token_no_default_policy=false' when enabling an auth method. This would apply for all roles created under that auth method path._x000D_
_x000D_
In our vault we currently restrict users from enabling auth methods unless through our own API, which is where we can enforce 'token_no_default_policy=false' on enabling an auth method._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
We have tried adding this to the default policy:_x000D_
```_x000D_
# Disable bypassing the default policy_x000D_
path "auth/+/role/*" {_x000D_
    capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "patch", "delete", "list"]_x000D_
    denied_parameters = { _x000D_
        "token_no_default_policy" = [true, "true"]_x000D_
    }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
The problem with this solution is that it auto grants everyone full capabilities on path `"auth/+/role/*"`_x000D_
_x000D_
We tried narrowing this down to:_x000D_
```_x000D_
# Disable bypassing the default policy_x000D_
path "auth/+/role/*" {_x000D_
    capabilities = ["create", "update"]_x000D_
    denied_parameters = { _x000D_
        "token_no_default_policy" = [true, "true"]_x000D_
    }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
but this denies everyone the ability to `"read", "patch", "delete", "list"` on path `"auth/+/role/*"`, unless explicitly granted again._x000D_
_x000D_
We also tried removing the capabilities list in the hopes that it would not enforce any capability restrictions, other than the `denied_parameters` list e.g._x000D_
```_x000D_
# Disable bypassing the default policy_x000D_
path "auth/+/role/*" {_x000D_
    denied_parameters = { _x000D_
        "token_no_default_policy" = [true, "true"]_x000D_
    }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
but this denied all access to path `"auth/+/role/*"`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Another feature request could be to allow only specifying the `denied_parameters` list and not enforcing any capability restrictions e.g._x000D_
```_x000D_
# Disable bypassing the default policy_x000D_
path "auth/+/role/*" {_x000D_
    denied_parameters = { _x000D_
        "token_no_default_policy" = [true, "true"]_x000D_
    }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
P.S. I would be happy to work on a PR for these features if it seems like the right way to go 🙂

_x000D_

so users are able to view roles similar to secrets roles list, and just select the role name from a list instead of typing it._x000D_

maxb: @heliobmartins This is a different issue to what was originally reported - the original issue was about people trying to import Vault itself as a Go module. The purpose of ExistenceCheck is to allow Vault to decide whether an HTTP PUT/POST is processed as a CreateOperation or an UpdateOperation. When no ExistenceCheck is defined, Vault treats everything as an UpdateOperation. Some people don't know this, and end up implementing a CreateOperation handler even though they have not implemented ExistenceCheck. When this happens, the CreateOperation handler is redundant unreachable code, and Vault's OpenAPI generator used to end up incorrectly claiming `x-vault-createSupported` for such APIs even though they don't actually support create properly. So I implemented an extra check that detects this incorrect code, and forces it to be corrected. If you have existing code that is triggering it, you can simply delete your CreateOperation implementation to resolve the problem. https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-auth-plugin-example requires no update for this, it is already correct.

title: BLAKE-family hashing within Transit Secrets Engine
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm using Vault+Consul+Nomad in open-source to automate my homelab. I'd like to store crypto keys using Transit Secrets Engine, but I need BLAKE-224 and BLAKE-256 hashing with Ed25519 signatures.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Transit already supports Ed25519 according to the spec; however, it remains to support BLAKE-family hashing. I'd like this done.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I'm currently storing my keys as a KV-pair in Consul. This is fine, but then the value would have to be injected into the application. I'd prefer to have support in Transit instead so it's not needed to inject anything.

**Explain any additional use-cases**
It'd help the encryption story, as this scheme is perhaps the most secure mainstream asymmetric encryption possible.
top_3_comments_text: schultz-is: Howdy, @HariAmoor-professional! Support for the BLAKE family of hash functions in Transit isn't on our roadmap to support, but we're happy to review any PR from the community that adds this. One important thing to note though is that go's Ed25519 library (which Vault makes use of) [doesn't support arbitrary hash functions](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/ed25519#Options) for signature generation or verification. Input can only be prehashed with SHA-512 for Ed25519ph or unhashed for standard Ed25519 operation. | HariAmoor-professional: > Go's Ed25519 library doesn't support arbitrary hash functions @schultz-is Looking at the doc you linked, it supports any of the `crypto.Hash` variations, which [include the BLAKE-2B functions](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto#Hash) I need. I could be wrong, but would it not be simple to implement given this consideration? Granted, it doesn't support 224-bit BLAKE, but that's something I could live without. Let me know your thoughts! Edit: I could be wrong on this too; it might not generalize over the full range of `crypto.Hash`. | cipherboy: AFAICT, `sign` doesn't support a `WithOptions` variant, but only `Verify` does: https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/ed25519#Sign vs https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/ed25519#VerifyWithOptions -- but the private key signing variety does support `crypto.Hash` options: https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/ed25519#PrivateKey.Sign Looking at the implementation for `Sign`, it doesn't seem like it does what you want: https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.21.0:src/crypto/ed25519/ed25519.go;l=79-117 Can you point us to a reference implementation that pairs BLAKE+ed25519 in this way? AFAIK, according to the spec (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8032#section-5.1), even ed25519ph requires SHA-512 and this is not configurable. A different choice of hash function would best be applied as `raw-curve-op(sha512(blake(msg)))`, and not as `raw-curve-op(blake(msg))`.

title: Allow users to disable TLS certificate verification for testing Duo MFA method
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When automating Vault configuration using Terraform, I would like to be able to deploy and test this configuration in isolated development environments. Currently I am using Docker containers for this purpose, and I am able to create and run local instances of Vault as well as its various dependencies such as LDAP, Kerberos, and AWS (using LocalStack), and I can test that my configuration behaves as expected without having to rely on shared external services, or even on a working internet connection._x000D_
_x000D_
Unfortunately, I can't do this for my Duo MFA configuration: there is a [mock Duo API docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/authelia/integration-duo/), but Vault [uses the Duo golang client](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/6b31e4531734b1a4e5735381bb7efd74ef548ca1/vault/login_mfa.go#L20), which [hardcodes its root CA certificates](https://github.com/duosecurity/duo_api_golang/blob/096d3306c0297ae13d0e7cbd9f79a80a12e4acc9/duoapi.go#L152-L154), making it impossible to use a self-signed certificate with the mock Duo API. This causes `vault login` to fail with TLS verification errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: POST http://localhost:8200/v1/sys/mfa/validate_x000D_
Code: 403. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* failed to satisfy enforcement duo. error: 2 errors occurred:_x000D_
        * Get "https://localhost/auth/v2/check": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate is not valid for any names, but wanted to match localhost_x000D_
        * login MFA validation failed for methodID: [6c7ace2d-64e2-0e8b-2683-aa7b1ac1d7c1]_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The Duo golang client does [provide an option](https://github.com/duosecurity/duo_api_golang/blob/096d3306c0297ae13d0e7cbd9f79a80a12e4acc9/duoapi.go#L160) [to disable](https://github.com/duosecurity/duo_api_golang/blob/096d3306c0297ae13d0e7cbd9f79a80a12e4acc9/duoapi.go#L94) [tls verification](https://github.com/duosecurity/duo_api_golang/blob/096d3306c0297ae13d0e7cbd9f79a80a12e4acc9/duoapi.go#L110-L114), but [Vault does not currently expose any way to set it](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/6b31e4531734b1a4e5735381bb7efd74ef548ca1/vault/login_mfa.go#L1864-L1869)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would like to propose the addition of an `insecure` or `insecure_tls` field to Vault's Duo MFA configuration, explicitly only for use in integration testing scenarios. To discourage its use in non-testing scenarios, it might be sensible to omit it from the Vault UI._x000D_
_x000D_
I have implemented this change [in a fork](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/compare/main...zanecodes:vault:duo-insecure), but have not yet added any tests around the functionality; I would be more than happy to add tests further down the line if this feature is accepted._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I was unable to find an alternative way to achieve this, and would have to either resign myself to relying on a real Duo server for development, or omit Duo MFA from our development configuration entirely, neither of which is ideal. There are also no other straightforward ways to implement a solution in Vault, short of replacing use of the Duo golang library and writing a wrapper library from scratch which does not implement certificate pinning, which doesn't seem like a good solution.

body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I have a few java applications that use JKS files for storing client private keys for things like DB certificates. Once these certificates get renewed I'd like an easy way to edit jks file, and replace the old key._x000D_
_x000D_
The problem is storing these JKS files. Obviously they shouldn't be in the repository, so instead i want to use a secret management tool like Vault but it doesn't seem like it particularly support JKS files so everyone ends up encoding them to base64 and storing them that way. Using that method, you have to read the secret, decode it, and then use some tool like keytool or openssl to edit the certificates inside, and I would like a better solution that would be easier for the developers to maintain._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I looked for some other tools to provide a UI to edit these JKS files and the only decent thing I found was Keystore Explorer which is a desktop app and I'd like to deploy a web app so everyone would be able to easily use it, similarly to Vault._x000D_
I considered developing a feature for Vault to edit JKS files inside the UI and contribute it or just create another app to specifically do this._x000D_
Finally I thought about not using JKS files at all even though they are well suited for Java applications, and use seperated certificate files instead._x000D_

```_x000D_
#!/bin/bash_x000D_
_x000D_
stderr() { echo -n "$@" 1>&2; }_x000D_
_x000D_
if [ ! "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then_x000D_
    exit 1_x000D_
fi_x000D_
_x000D_
if [[ -z "$VAULT_ADDR" || ! -n "$VAULT_ADDR" ]]; then_x000D_
    exit 1_x000D_
fi_x000D_
_x000D_
FILE="$HOME/.vault-token"_x000D_
ACTION=$1_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_

title: Startup Option to prevent Vault to revoke leases
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When we need to restore a cluster based on a DynamoDB PITR table (after a KV Engine accidental deletion, in example), the restored cluster will attempt to revoke any "expired" DB lease._x000D_
The problem is that the Restored Cluster is not aware that these leases have been renewed between the PITR restore and the current time when it starts. Consequently, the Restored Vault Cluster will revoke several DB logins still used by our applications._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
We would like a command switch that could be actioned at Vault Command to prevent Vault from revoking DB leases (or just ignoring Vault DB restoration). _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
The alternative we've considered is to block any database connectivity from the Vault Restored Cluster, so it cannot join and revoke the leases (and delete the roles on the database)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use cases**_x000D_
A Vault "prevent revocation mode" or "database read-only mode" could also be used for debugging or troubleshooting purposes. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I have asked to the HashiCorp Community Forum and I have been told that Vault was not offering a "prevent revoke" mode_x000D_
_x000D_
https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/how-to-properly-restore-a-pitr-dynamodb-backend/52415/2

title: Dynamic Secrets: Remove rotated secret after custom time period
body_text:
Hi there!_x000D_
Let’s assume we have a deployment with an app that uses Postgres_x000D_
Dynamic secret provision is enabled and mounted as environment variables via k8s secrets. _x000D_
Secret TTL and Max TTL are 5 min and 30 min. _x000D_
The initial start of the pod takes 20 seconds. So if I have 6 replicas I need approx 120 sec to finish rolling the update _x000D_
When new creds were requested the old one will be deleted in 30 sec. _x000D_
In that case, only 2 of 6 pods will be restarted to apply new creds and others won't be able to use the connection to Postgres because previously used creds were deleted. More than 60% of deployments won't be able to serve the traffic. _x000D_
It would be great if it would be possible to set a custom deletion time after the TTL of creds

Are you able to tune this such that there is some leeway for old credentials to stick around until the pod updates are completed? | vosmax: Hi @austingebauer I think I got wrong how the 30-number appeared, sorry for misleading here. Im using the Vault operator. The operator requests a new lease when the current token reached 67% of its TTL. Here is a test that I've done (changed TTL to 2 min and Max TTL to 10 min). Data from Postgres ``` The initial start of deployment (1) app_user_2023_08_12T04_18_51Z | Password valid until 2023-08-12 04:20:56+00 Lease updated (2) app_user_2023_08_12T04_18_51Z | Password valid until 2023-08-12 04:22:19+00 ... (3) app_user_2023_08_12T04_18_51Z | Password valid until 2023-08-12 04:26:35+00 (4) app_user_2023_08_12T04_18_51Z | Password valid until 2023-08-12 04:28:05+00 The last lease (5) app_user_2023_08_12T04_18_51Z | Password valid until 2023-08-12 04:28:56+00 New user (6) app_user_2023_08_12T04_27_22Z | Password valid until 2023-08-12 04:29:27+00 ``` Please confirm if my thoughts are correct. Here is how in high-level things happen underhood 1. Vault operator checked that lease has been taken in line 5 and reached 67% of its TTL, request a new token (user) because the Max TTL of the token (user) has been reached. 2. New token (user) was generated in line 6 and a rolling update of deployment was initiated That means deployment has ~94 seconds (difference between lines 5 and 6 (04:28:56 and 04_27_22) to finish all pod replacement before user app_user_2023_08_12T04_18_51Z will be deleted In the given case above we have a deployment of 6 replicas, with a rollingupdate policy "one by one", pod is ready to serve traffic in 20 seconds after the start.
