title: Allow use of `token` metadata when templating OIDC claims
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We store additional information in token metadata for tracing, such as the host that the token was issued to.  _x000D_
I'd like to reference this metadata in OIDC claims so, in the case of a compromised OIDC token, we can identify what host the OIDC token was issued to.  _x000D_
Presently, we can can see the identity the OIDC token was issued for, however we can't access more granular information about the token._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
When writing a template for usage in an OIDC role (eg. `vault write identity/oidc/role/some-role -template=$TEMPLATE`), it'd be useful to access both the whole token meta field, as well as individual fields on the token metadata._x000D_
_x000D_
### Example_x000D_
_x000D_
Given the following template_x000D_
_x000D_
```json_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "host": {{token.metadata.host}},_x000D_
  "meta": {{token.metadata}}_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
A token created with `--metadata=host=host-abc --metadata=somefield=blah` could then have claims resembling:_x000D_
```json_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "host": "host-abc",_x000D_
  "meta": {_x000D_
    "host": "host-abc",_x000D_
    "somefield": "blah"_x000D_
  },_x000D_
  "aud": ...,_x000D_
  "exp": ...,_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Alternative 1.  _x000D_
Each host could be a separate identity, however at our scale we would quickly exhaust the 250,000 [identity storage limit](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/limits#storage-related-limits)_x000D_
_x000D_
Alternative 2._x000D_
Create a secret-engine plugin that otherwise behaves the same as the Identity secret engine, but allows referencing token metadata. However, this would take a significant amount of maintenance for what would otherwise be a minor change._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
If updating the templating mechanism to allow token metadata, it could also be used for ACL templates, but in our case that is just a nice to have and can be a separate ticket._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: maxb: The general issue raised in https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/7761#issuecomment-547717153 still applies... Both token display name **and token metadata** can often be set by relatively low privileged users, such as anyone given access to `auth/token/create` for the purposes of creating child tokens. | jackadamson: That makes sense that in some (or many) environments, token metadata is relatively untrusted. Do you think that this could be mitigated via documentation or naming, eg. having the field be named `token.untrusted_metadata` or similar? | jackadamson: I'd also be happy if the change was just to claim metadata and not used for ACLs. Then combined with renaming the field to `token.untrusted_metadata`, to prevent it from usage in authorization within vault, and communicating to users that it should not be trusted unless they adequately understand the consequences. Do you think this could be possible avenue?
all_comments_text:
maxb: The general issue raised in https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/7761#issuecomment-547717153 still applies... Both token display name **and token metadata** can often be set by relatively low privileged users, such as anyone given access to `auth/token/create` for the purposes of creating child tokens.
jackadamson: That makes sense that in some (or many) environments, token metadata is relatively untrusted. Do you think that this could be mitigated via documentation or naming, eg. having the field be named `token.untrusted_metadata` or similar?
jackadamson: I'd also be happy if the change was just to claim metadata and not used for ACLs. Then combined with renaming the field to `token.untrusted_metadata`, to prevent it from usage in authorization within vault, and communicating to users that it should not be trusted unless they adequately understand the consequences. Do you think this could be possible avenue?
VioletHynes: We discussed this internally, and this isn't something we're planning to support. See also: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/10460 + https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/10682 In particular, there are two parts of our responses to these that explain our position and hopefully offer an alternative. Hopefully the following answers satisfy you: >I think you can achieve the result you're aiming for by creating an entity and alias for each role that needs distinct policies, put the metadata into the entity, and bind the entity alias to the token role. and >Thank you for the contribution. Unfortunately I'm afraid that we have decided to refuse it. We view this change as dangerous, since a user can create child tokens with whatever arbitrary metadata they like. This means policy templating using token metadata is vulnerable to any attacker who's aware of what policies are in use. I expect that you could come up with safeguards in your environment to protect against this (e.g. not granting access to the create token endpoints), but we as vault devs have to be vigilant against introducing features that allow for insecure by default behaviour. Thanks for raising this, and we appreciate the contribution. However, we feel like the 'right' way to do this is using the identity system. Token metadata is quite low privilege.
VioletHynes: All this being said, I've opened the discussion about specifically the OIDC use case with the team, and we'll be discussing that later today
jackadamson: Thanks for the thorough and swift feedback. Just for my own understanding, do you have any recommendations on how to include data about the host the OIDC claim was issued to? Specifically for cases where the number of hosts is >250,000 (which to my understanding rules out a distinct identity per host due to [storage limits](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/limits#storage-related-limits). One idea was to have an alias per host, but my later understanding was that an identity can have one alias per auth mount, so that wouldn't be feasible.
jackadamson: Maybe an alternative would be to expose fields from `req.Auth.InternalData`, which as best as I can tell can be set by auth plugins, but not during manual token creation. Do you know whether using that could be acceptable?
austingebauer: Hi @jackadamson. I don't think using `req.Auth.InternalData` would be the right approach. That data is meant to be internal to auth methods for token revoke and renew decisions. I understand this could be less than desirable with the number of hosts you have, but have you considered created an [identity token role](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/identity/tokens#create-or-update-a-role) per host? The host information could be a part of the claims template. I understand the security concern around supporting token metadata in ACL policy path templating. I'm a bit undecided, but I don't see why it would be a security concern (from Vault's perspective) to allow templating token metadata into [identity token](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/identity/identity-token) and [OIDC provider](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/identity/oidc-provider) claims. These JWTs don't provide authn/authz to Vault. I suppose a malicious Vault token creator could generate a JWT that provides authorization to a different system, but that seems like it would require a good bit of Vault authorization and knowledge of how those claims are being used for authorization within the different system. Would you be able to give us a little more information on how you're using these identity token JWTs?
jackadamson: Thanks for the response @austingebauer, I suspect that for our use case, creating an identity token role per host would be hard due to our high rate of host creation and deletion (well over 1000 hosts per day) Completely understand the issues around usage of token metadata in ACL, and very happy leaving that out. Our use case of the JWTs is for machine authentication to internal services. The claims that we want to use the token metadata would primarily be used for logging purposes, so we can track what individual hosts are accessing internal services, rather than just what class of host. Do you think that allowing the token metadata in OIDC claims could be feasible? (possibly named `token.untrusted_metadata` as a further mitigation against users accidentally trusting the data too much)
austingebauer: Thanks for the context, @jackadamson! That all makes sense to me. I'm curious which auth method you are using to create these tokens with the additional metadata? I've brought this up internally for discussion. I don't have any concrete answers yet but will follow up with you.
jackadamson: I highly appreciate it @austingebauer, in our case, we have an in-house auth plugin that uses certificate details from our VPN connections (with Nebula VPN)
maxb: Using token metadata in ACL policies, and using it in OIDC claims, are both expression of security properties. One is just a bit more indirect than the other. To me, it seems what is needed is to be able to refer to token metadata, with a guarantee that it came from a particular auth method or group of auth methods, or just a specific type of auth method. Though, the Vault templating language is currently a very simple thing, and it might be difficult to allow for that without a more sophisticated parser.
jackadamson: Being able to refer to token metadata from a particular auth method sounds like an interesting proposal. Possibly it could be presented similarly to how you can currently use identity info from a given auth mount `{{identity.entity.aliases.auth_token_45ccd648.name}}` So perhaps it could be accessed with eg. `{{token.AUTH_ACCESSOR.metadata.FIELD}}`, which only exposes metadata set by the given auth mount? I'm aware this would require changes beyond just the templating to track the information, so could be a large body of work. (apologies if I am mixing up terminology regarding auth mounts/auth plugins/accessors)
maxb: > I'm aware this would require changes beyond just the templating to track the information, so could be a large body of work. Actually that part is pretty easy. The information is already tracked. Token metadata is only set at token creation time. The auth method that created a token is already saved into the token as the token's path attribute (in Enterprise, this needs to be qualified by the token's namespace ID). The harder part IMO is figuring out a design that accounts for people having several of the same or similar auth methods mounted, and wanting to resolve token metadata from any within that set - whilst excluding others, such as the token auth method, which AFAIK is fairly unique in allowing the requester to supply their own metadata. One might imagine, for instance, a collection of kubernetes auth methods each bound to a different cluster, and wanting to refer to the `role` metadata set by any one of them.
jackadamson: A few options which might suit: ## A - Globbing Allow specifying the auth accessor as a glob, eg. ``` {{token.auth_kubernetes_*.metadata.somefield}} {{token.auth_kubernetes_{aaaaaa,bbbbbb}.metadata.somefield}} ``` ## B - Specify in a list and filter nulls eg. when templating a JSON document, assuming that the given token was issued by a mount with accessor `auth_kubernetes_aaaaaa`, which set `somefield = "somevalue" ``` { "somefield": [ {{token.auth_kubernetes_aaaaaa.metadata.somefield}}, {{token.auth_kubernetes_bbbbbb.metadata.somefield}} ] } ``` renders to ```json { "somefield": [ "somevalue" ] } ``` ## C - Define a "coalesce" function Syntax could be like ``` {{token.auth_kubernetes_aaaaaa.metadata.somefield || token.auth_kubernetes_bbbbbb.metadata.somefield}} ``` or ``` {{coalesce(token.auth_kubernetes_aaaaaa.metadata.somefield, token.auth_kubernetes_bbbbbb.metadata.somefield)}} ```
jackadamson: Or maybe, `token.metadata.somefield` and token auth providers are just not accepted for providing metadata fields?

title: api/client.go#clone() re-claims a non-re-entrant lock
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
In api/client.go, [clone()](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/262bdc067f7d0db470929039cca38969f1d1c34a/api/client.go#L1167) claims the same read lock twice.  The second time is via [Headers()](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/262bdc067f7d0db470929039cca38969f1d1c34a/api/client.go#L1025)._x000D_
_x000D_
The doc on RWMutex says in [here](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/14a3ffc3d2165ef03c3ffd0037a4fa6dbb776026/src/sync/rwmutex.go#L22) and [here](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/14a3ffc3d2165ef03c3ffd0037a4fa6dbb776026/src/sync/rwmutex.go#L61) that re-entrance is not allowed._x000D_
_x000D_
We ran into this problem when a goroutine called CloneWithHeaders() and another called SetCloneToken()._x000D_
After CloneWithHeaders() acquired the first read lock, SetCloneToken() tried to claim a write lock.  As a result,_x000D_
no new read lock could be claimed and goroutine one couldn't release the existing read lock.  As a result,_x000D_
goroutine two couldn't acquire the write lock.  Below are the stacktraces._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
goroutine 12055 [semacquire, 147 minutes]:_x000D_
sync.runtime_SemacquireMutex(0x151c280?, 0x10?, 0x1708100?)_x000D_
GOROOT/src/runtime/sema.go:77 +0x25_x000D_
sync.(*RWMutex).RLock(...)_x000D_
GOROOT/src/sync/rwmutex.go:71_x000D_
github.com/hashicorp/vault/api.(*Client).Headers(0xc000d98a00)_x000D_
external/com_github_hashicorp_vault_api/client.go:1005 +0x6e_x000D_
github.com/hashicorp/vault/api.(*Client).clone(0xc000d98a00, 0x1)_x000D_
external/com_github_hashicorp_vault_api/client.go:1177 +0x2b6_x000D_
github.com/hashicorp/vault/api.(*Client).CloneWithHeaders(...)_x000D_
external/com_github_hashicorp_vault_api/client.go:1141_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
goroutine 11984 [semacquire, 147 minutes]:_x000D_
sync.runtime_SemacquireMutex(0x203000?, 0x0?, 0xc0016e0030?)_x000D_
	GOROOT/src/runtime/sema.go:77 +0x25_x000D_
sync.(*RWMutex).Lock(0x4852de?)_x000D_
	GOROOT/src/sync/rwmutex.go:152 +0x71_x000D_
github.com/hashicorp/vault/api.(*Client).SetCloneToken(0xc000d98a00, 0x1)_x000D_
	external/com_github_hashicorp_vault_api/client.go:1079 +0x33_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
To reproduce this issue, you need to have a small piece of code that has the following operations._x000D_
We had them back-to-back._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
		client.SetCloneToken(true)_x000D_
		c, err := client.CloneWithHeaders()_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Then you need to execute this small piece of code with multiple threads non-stop._x000D_
You will see the problem if you are (un)lucky enough._x000D_
_x000D_
Note that regardless of the reproduction, please consider Go's documentation on RWMutex._x000D_
_x000D_
We use [pprof](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http/pprof) to spy on the goroutines._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
No deadlocking._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.8.3_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Unbuntu 18.04_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
n/a_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
A problem I can see that makes client.go risky is that top-level functions can invoke each other._x000D_
I think if you structure the code so that only top-level functions can claim locks and that top-level_x000D_
functions cannot invoke each other, then it's unlikely for lock-related issues to take place._x000D_
_x000D_
See [this post](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-nuts/c/XqW1qcuZgKg/m/Ui3nQkeLV80J?pli=1) on why golang doesn't offer re-entrant locks in the first place.

title: Add Role ARN to AWS IAM Authentication Entity Alias Names.
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Hi,_x000D_
_x000D_
Currently the AWS IAM Auth plugin has 3 possible Entity Alias Names._x000D_
None are used anywhere else in configuration for authentication._x000D_
_x000D_
The bound_principal_arns uses the Role ARN not the assumed role ARN._x000D_
_x000D_
1. A random UUID (role_id -- default)._x000D_
2. The AWS Role Unique Id (unique_id)._x000D_
3. The Assumed Role ARN (full_arn)._x000D_
_x000D_
- 1 is not predictable at all._x000D_
- 2 is, but it would be better as the Role ARN which is what it is linked too. It is a pain to get and one already needs the role ARN._x000D_
- 3 is not predictable with some workloads (i.e. EC2 and Code Build). The session name can be randomised and thus not of use if you need predictability._x000D_
_x000D_
Giving users the ability to specify the role arn as the entity alias name is much more useful._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Adding the role arn as a entity alias name would be what I would like._x000D_
It is an extra option for config that is trivial to implement._x000D_
_x000D_
I already implemented it here -> https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/22460 ._x000D_
_x000D_
So if you could please review that PR I would be grateful._x000D_
_x000D_
This is a quality of life change that I think will help people and not harm._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Not considered any other options. this is a good functional change that makes user quality of life easier._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
None._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
None._x000D_

title: Running vault v1.14.1 without DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS set and no /run/user/<uid>/bus launches a persistent dbus-daemon

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Running `vault` as a user without `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` set and no  `/run/user/<uid>/bus` file causes vault to run `dbus-launch` which launches a persistent dbus-daemon process like this:_x000D_
`/usr/bin/dbus-daemon --syslog --fork --print-pid 4 --print-address 6 --session`._x000D_
_x000D_
A new dbus-daemon will be launched every time vault is run._x000D_
_x000D_
The dbus-daemon processes use inotify instances, so if vault is executed enough times (configuration management in our instance) the user running vault will run into the `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` limit or fd limits causing issues for systemd etc._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run `vault --version` with no `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` set and no `/run/user/<uid>/bus` file_x000D_
2. See that there is now a new `dbus-daemon` process running as the user that ran vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
There should be no extra processes left running._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.14.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 18.04/22.04 amd64_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
This is related to the godbus/dbus issue raised here https://github.com/godbus/dbus/issues/372_x000D_
Testing this as a workaround does avoid the issue:_x000D_
```_x000D_
env DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus vault --version_x000D_
```

title: Vault agent silently DoSes Vault server when token policy does not include auth/token/renew-self
body_text:
# Summary_x000D_
_x000D_
When the capability for a token to renew itself is missing from a renewable token's policies, vault agent silently DoS's the Vault server with failing requests to `auth/token/renew-self` which result in error: `1 error occurred:\n\t* permission denied\n\n` with a 403 return code._x000D_
_x000D_
There are no errors reported from Vault Agent and there appears to be no backoff present as it is issuing hundreds of requests a second to Vault Server._x000D_
_x000D_
# How to Reproduce_x000D_
_x000D_
Pull the `hashicorp/vault:1.14.1` Docker image - we will use this as both the server and the client._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
docker pull hashicorp/vault:1.14.1_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Start a container acting as Vault Server. For ease of inter-container networking, we define a custom network as the default bridge network provided by Docker does not have container-DNS for some reason._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
docker network create vault_x000D_
docker run --rm --cap-add=IPC_LOCK -e 'VAULT_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID=hvault-root' -p 8200:8200 --network vault --name vault-server hashicorp/vault:1.14.1_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Start an interactive Vault container to use as the client. Note that it is also on the custom `vault` network so that it can communicate with the server. Also configure it so that it can talk to Vault Server using the root token:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
docker run --rm -it --network vault hashicorp/vault:1.14.1 ash_x000D_
/ # export VAULT_ADDR=http://vault-server:8200_x000D_
/ # export VAULT_TOKEN=hvault-root_x000D_
/ # vault token lookup_x000D_
Key                 Value_x000D_
---                 -----_x000D_
accessor            5YfkHXssoq9bM2MnkajuboWt_x000D_
creation_time       1691319976_x000D_
..._x000D_
policies            [root]_x000D_
renewable           false_x000D_
ttl                 0s_x000D_
type                service_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Next we need to alter the default policy to remove the ability for tokens to renew themselves. This can be done by using the Vault CLI for reading, editing, and writing the default policy but it can also be done via the web ui at `http://localhost:8200`. The policy should be edited to remove or comment out this capability:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
# Allow tokens to renew themselves_x000D_
path "auth/token/renew-self" {_x000D_
    capabilities = ["update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
As Vault Agent does not log any errors, we need to enable audit logging in Vault Server so that we can see the deluge of requests arriving from Vault agent:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault audit enable file file_path=stdout_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
We are now nearly ready to launch vault agent. We need to create a renewable service token with the default policy, put it in a file, create the Vault agent config file, and then start Vault Agent:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
# Create vault token and write to file_x000D_
vault token create -ttl 600 -renewable -policy default -field token > /tmp/vault-token_x000D_
_x000D_
# Write out vault agent config file_x000D_
cat >/tmp/vault-agent.conf <<EOL_x000D_
vault {_x000D_
  address = "https://vault-fqdn:8200"_x000D_
  retry {_x000D_
    num_retries = 5_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
auto_auth {_x000D_
  method {_x000D_
    type = "token_file"_x000D_
_x000D_
    config = {_x000D_
      token_file_path = "/tmp/vault-token"_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  }_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
  sink "file" {_x000D_
    config = {_x000D_
      path = "/tmp/new-vault-token"_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
log_level = "trace"_x000D_
EOL_x000D_
_x000D_
# Start vault agent_x000D_
vault agent -config /tmp/vault-agent.conf_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
At this point, the audit log in the stdout of the Vault Server instance will become very active with a continuous stream of requests for the token to renew itself but the Vault agent log will remain quiet even though trace logging is enabled. Restoring the capability to update `auth/token/renew-self` to the default policy stops the deluge of requests from vault agent and it appears to operate as normal afterwards.

One notable is that you mark the token as renewable: `vault token create -ttl 600 -renewable -policy default -field token > /tmp/vault-token` In particular, `-renewable` marks the token as renewable. I agree that we should be more resilient in this case, but I wanted to indicate why this happens and a workaround in the meantime. **Describe the bug**_x000D_
Similar to bug #17850, the gcpckms auto-unseal method when run from terraform deploys containers in a ```CrashLoopBackOff``` state. The logs from any of the containers will read:_x000D_
```_x000D_
Error parsing Seal configuration: failed to encrypt with GCP CKMS - ensure the key exists and the service account has at least roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter permission: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = Request had insufficient authentication scopes._x000D_

2023-08-27T06:06:23.690Z [WARN]  storage.raft.fsm: raft FSM db file has wider permissions than needed: needed=-rw------- existing=-rw-rw----_x000D_
```_x000D_
I tried to deploy the vault purely from helm with a local values file with the same settings as mt terraform config. At first, there is a lack of documentation in the helm chart that there is a new required field for gcpckms; ```credentials = <value>```. I did find the documentation for the new requirement under the vault documentation: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/seal/gcpckms#credentials_x000D_
_x000D_
Once I entered the value with a local json key, it worked as expected and deployed vault automatically unsealed. This means that how terraform interacts with helm is flawed when it works within helm alone but not when terraform deploys vault from helm_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
*Helm provider's token is set from: data.google_client_config.current.access_token_x000D_
_x000D_
1. You will need a GKE cluster, a service account with sufficient privs (cloudkms.viewer and EncryptorDecryptor), and a KMS key and keyring. _x000D_
2. Either write the variables or replace the variables with strings_x000D_
3. Terrafrom apply then look for the running pods via kubectl get pods --namespace=vault_x000D_
4. If in crashloop, get logs with: kubectl logs --namespace=vault vault-0_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_

title: AWS Secrets Engine - Root IAM credentials can't be rotated with the `region` parameter set and AWS credentials can't be generated without the `region` parameter set.
body_text:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe._x000D_
_x000D_
We have found the need to add the `sts_region` parameter to the AWS secret engine just as it is already available in the [AWS auth method](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/aws#sts_region). Currently only these parameters exist: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/aws#parameters_x000D_
_x000D_
The reason is that for `sts_endpoint` we use proxies, let's say:_x000D_
_x000D_
```jq_x000D_
sts_endpoint = "sts.proxy.com"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
And since we use these proxies, we cannot specify the AWS region in the `sts_endpoint` as `sts.${aws_region}.amazonaws.com` but, we can use the `region` parameter, say:_x000D_
_x000D_
```jq_x000D_
region = "eu-west-1"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Now here we run into the problem, if we specify the `region` parameter then we will not be able to [rotate the root IAM credentials](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/aws#rotate-root-iam-credentials)._x000D_
If we do not specify the `region` parameter we will be able to rotate the root IAM     credentials but the generation of credentials and roles (assumed_role, federation_token or iam_user) will fail because no region is found_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
We are not sure if this is intentional or a bug, but we believe that having the `sts_region` parameter may fix our problem._x000D_
_x000D_
#### Describe the solution you'd like_x000D_
We would like to be able to use the `sts_region` parameter in the AWS Vault secrets engine._x000D_
_x000D_
##### Additional context_x000D_
The error message for when we try to rotate credentials with the `region` set or generate AWS credentials without the `region` parameter set is the same:_x000D_
```jq_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "errors": [_x000D_
    "1 error occurred:_x000D_
        * error calling GetUser: SignatureDoesNotMatch: Credential should be scoped to a valid region._x000D_
        status code: 403, _x000D_
        request id: 97c6347f-xxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxx1900d"_x000D_
  ]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```

title: Kubernetes TokenReview: Support short lived tokens
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When Vault submits a `TokenReview` to a Kubernetes cluster, it either uses a keypair signed by the cluster's CA or the JWT of a `ServiceAccount`.  Both of these are long lived tokens who's use are anti-patterns.  Certificate's can't be revoked and `ServiceAccount` tokens are no longer designed to be long lived and were never meant to be used from outside of a cluster._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
A Kubernetes cluster can trust a Vault deployment's OIDC issuer in one of three ways:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Configure the OIDC provider for a cluster to trust Vault for all tokens_x000D_
2. Use an impersonating proxy, such as kube-oidc-proxy (https://github.com/tremolosecurity/kube-oidc-proxy),  to trust Vault's OIDC issuer and then forward requests via impersonation to the API server_x000D_
3. User Kubernetes' upcoming `StructeredAuthenticationConfig` that will support multiple token issuers_x000D_
_x000D_
Once a cluster trusts the Vault OIDC issuer, Vault can mint its own OIDC tokens that are very short lived for interacting with the cluster.  This eliminates the need for a cluster issued certificate or a long lived `ServiceAccount` JWT._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
The alternative would be to automate generating new `ServiceAccount` JWTs or issuing new CA certs on a regular basis and calling the Vault API to update.  This is costly and risky because you're introducing a new process that can break and requires remote authentication to the vault API._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Any interaction with a remote Kubernetes cluster_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here._x000D_

title: Add allow_organizations to cert credential backend for TLS certificate auth
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
This is related to https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/cert._x000D_
_x000D_
Currently for a CA certificate role, while the cert credential backend supports a few parameters for validating the client cert, e.g., [allowed_common_names](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/cert#allowed_common_names), [allowed_email_sans](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/cert#allowed_email_sans), it cannot match on organizations listed in the cert Subject. There are some access control systems that create certificate with roles using the organization fields. Teleport is one example. _x000D_
_x000D_
This problem prevents the vault end users to use the certificates assigned by the access control system to access hc-vault using the TLS certificate auth method._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
We'd like to see allow_organizations to be added to the parameter list, so that vault can validate the CA cert role by checking these fields._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
n/a_x000D_

title: Vault HA Standby Mode After Kuberenetes 1.25 Upgrade
body_text:
We are using Vault 1.14.1 and `0.25.0` of the Vault Helm Chart._x000D_
_x000D_
We were on EKS 1.24 and Vault seemed to be working fine and we could access the UI and add/retrieve secrets without issue._x000D_
_x000D_
We upgrade our EKS cluster to 1.25 and now Vault is in standby mode. As far as we are aware, there was nothing changed at all on the Vault config side of things._x000D_

          # or through a Kube secret.  For more information see:_x000D_

          config: |_x000D_

    }_x000D_

      client_id       = ""_x000D_
      client_secret   = ""_x000D_
      tenant_id       = "***REDACTED****"_x000D_
      vault_name      = "***REDACTED****"_x000D_
      key_name        = "vault-unseal-key"_x000D_

    }_x000D_

title: CRL config entries cannot be saved due to large size
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We are running Consul Connect, with Vault in use as the Connect CA.  DynamoDB is used for Vault storage. When Consul switches leadership it does a "CA initialization" routine, which generates a new PKI issuer each time.  Over time the number of issuers grows, and eventually it reaches a point where the CA initialization fails, because the CRL rebuild step tries saving a CRL config entry so large that it exceeds the DynamoDB max record size, and Consul CA initialization does not complete on the Consul side._x000D_
_x000D_
This is the error that Consul reports, which includes the embedded error strings from Vault:_x000D_
```_x000D_
"level":"error"_x000D_
_x000D_
"message":"Failed to initialize Connect CA","module":"connect.ca","error":"error generating intermediate cert: Error making API request.URL: PUT https://vault/v1/<pki name>/intermediate/set-signed Code: 500. _x000D_
Errors:* 1 error occurred:* Rebuilding the CRL failed. While this is indicative of a problem with the imported issuers (perhaps because of their revocation_signature_algorithm), they did import successfully and are now usable. _x000D_
It is strongly suggested to fix the CRL building errors before continuing. _x000D_
The original error is reproduced below:error building CRLs: unable to persist updated cluster-local CRL config: ValidationException: Item size has exceeded the maximum allowed size status code: 400"_x000D_
_x000D_
"routine":"CA initialization"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Based on the specific error strings included in the log, the problem is occurring when an internalCRLConfigEntry is written to DynamoDB: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/2e30ad5a938de2b417fb33538f7e5378f5380101/builtin/logical/pki/storage.go#L189-L197_x000D_
_x000D_
After analysis of the entries in the DynamoDB table, at the path `logical/<secret engine UUID>/crls` there is an item with a key `config` where this config entry is stored. When the CRL build occurs it cannot save the entry to DynamoDB because the size is now larger than DynamoDB's max field size of 400KB. _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Set up Consul Connect with Vault as the CA_x000D_
2. Let a number of Consul leadership transitions occur over time_x000D_
3. The number of issuers in Vault under the path `/v1/<pki name>/issuer/<UUID>/` grows_x000D_
4. Eventually a leadership transition in Consul occurs and the error above will occur because the CRL config cannot be saved when Consul Connect does its ca initialization._x000D_
_x000D_
We manually deleted a number of the issuers from DynamoDB in order to get past the condition and get Consul functioning again, as there did not seem to be any operator commands that would help (tidy did not help because the issuers were not expired yet)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
We would like to know:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Our CRLs are actually empty, can we simply disable CRL builds to avoid running into this problem?_x000D_
2. Manually deleting issuer records from DynamoDB seems like a less-than-ideal remediation step, are there any vault operator commands that can address this type of issue?_x000D_
3. We intend to modify the TTL of the Consul Connect CA intermediate cert to hopefully cut down the number of active issuers, it is currently still set as the Consul default of 1 year (8760h).  Are there any other configuration settings we should look into that can reduce the size of the CRL config entry that is stored in DynamoDB? _x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.14.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.12.4_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Alpine Linux v.3.15 (using the Vault docker image from https://hub.docker.com/layers/hashicorp/vault/1.14/images/sha256-7491542ac45b0d76b2eda4504a1b2310a4577a24cab7f7c1c34f274fcd4698f4?context=explore) _x000D_
* Consul version: 1.15.3_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
(let me know what specific hcl is helpful here and I can edit the original post)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
1. It seems that when manually deleting old issuers, the amount of space freed in the CRL config entry (~78 bytes) is less than the amount of space consumed in the storage when a new issuer is added (~240 bytes). So even if you delete old issuers regularly the size of the CRL config will still continue to grow and may eventually run into this problem. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. When Consul Connect is unable complete it's "CA Initialization" when encountering the CRL max record size issue it tries to reinitialize repeatedly. These attempts to initialize actually generates new issuers in Vault each time, but meanwhile Consul Connect does not actually function when it encounters the error.  The repeated creation of more issuers that are unused by Consul compounds the problem, and then requires a lot more manual cleanup of the issuers that were created by Consul when Connect was in a non-functioning state._x000D_

title: pki/intermediate/set-signed missing issuer_name parameter to set issuer name easily on creation
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When generating root certificates, one can provide an `issuer_name` parameter to the `pki/root/generate/:type` endpoint to provide the issuer that will get generated with a name. This is not possible on the `pki/intermediate/generate/:type` endpoint, nor on the `pki/intermediate/set-signed` endpoint. Thus one needs to perform an extra call to provide the issuer a meaningful name everytime one generates an issuer._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Either the `pki/intermediate/generate/:type` or the `pki/intermediate/set-signed` endpoint provides an `issuer_name` parameter, allowing to set the issuer name directly as it gets created. I am a bit unsure which endpoint makes the most sense. I have the feeling the `set-signed` endpoint makes more sense though, as it is only after that call that an issuer actually gets created._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Rename the issuer with a separate API call after having created it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
We have use cases where we create issuers automatically on the fly. A large number of issuers might be generated every single day. Having to rename these, and not being able to rely on the fact that our issuer names are directly set on the issuers is a bit of a pain._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: cipherboy: @f4z3r This is because `set-signed` is not a different endpoint but [an alias of import](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#import-ca-certificates-and-keys) in Vault 1.11+, in part because it behaves exactly the same minus disallowing the import of keys: one or more CA certificates could be imported (e.g., root CA + intermediate, or two cross-signed versions of the same intermediate, &c)...In the latter case especially, these would be two peers and could reasonably have the same name-ish (needs to be different for the API obviously, but...) So the harder problem is how do you solve naming for general CA import... One idea was make it a map of PEM certificate->name (assumes you know it ahead of time based on the certificates you've sent -- else you could also do two parallel arrays of the same length, one of certificates one of names), or to make `issuer_name` only work if you only specify a single certificate (do you error or warn if not?)... And, how would you handle already imported certificates if the given name doesn't match? In short, it is a bit harder from a what works best perspective.

title: Lack of input validation with lists in CLI when missing commas
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The vault CLI allows the user to input invalid lists for policy/config attributes.  There are two different results we've seen from this._x000D_
1.  When inputting token_bound_cidrs for an approle, adding a list of cidrs without a comma results in complete inability to read the current approle configuration._x000D_
2.  When inputting allowed_roles for a database config, inputting a list with spaces makes the roles invalid.  However, whether the list is input with spaces or commas, it is always displayed with spaces making it impossible to tell where the issue is._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
For 1)_x000D_
This works fine:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/approle/role/dop_test_role secret_id_ttl=10m token_num_uses=10 token_ttl=20m token_max_ttl=30m secret_id_num_uses=40 token_bound_cidrs="10.0.0.0/24,10.0.1.0/24" token_policies="default,root"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This next one tells you it was successful, but then you can't read the data back:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/approle/role/dop_test_role     secret_id_ttl=10m     token_num_uses=10     token_ttl=20m     token_max_ttl=30m     secret_id_num_uses=40 token_bound_cidrs="10.0.0.0/24 10.0.1.0/24" token_policies="default,root"_x000D_
Success! Data written to: auth/approle/role/dop_test_role_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
However, now the app_role is unreadable:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault read auth/approle/role/dop_test_role_x000D_
_x000D_
Error reading auth/approle/role/dop_test_role: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: GET https://redacted:8200/v1/auth/approle/role/dop_test_role_x000D_
Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* internal error_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
For 2)_x000D_
A bit more complex because our test case requires having a database setup.  Setup is basically this if you have docker:_x000D_
```_x000D_
docker run --name vault-postgres -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=vaulttestpassword -d postgres_x000D_
docker run -it --rm postgres psql -h 172.17.0.2 -U postgres_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
At the psql prompt:_x000D_
```_x000D_
CREATE DATABASE vault;_x000D_
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE vault TO postgres;_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Now we configure the base database config and test role:_x000D_
```vault write database/config/vault-db-bug plugin_name="postgresql-database-plugin" allowed_roles="*" connection_url="postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@172.17.0.2:5432" username="postgres" password="vaulttestpassword"_x000D_
_x000D_
vault write database/roles/dop-role db_name="vault-db-bug" creation_statements="CREATE ROLE \"{{name}}\" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '{{password}}' VALID UNTIL '{{expiration}}'; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO \"{{name}}\";" default_ttl="1h" max_ttl="24h"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Now we can break it._x000D_
_x000D_
This works:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write database/config/vault-db-bug allowed_roles="default,dop-role"_x000D_
vault read database/creds/dop-role_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This does not:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write database/config/vault-db-bug allowed_roles="default dop-role"_x000D_
vault read database/creds/dop-role_x000D_
_x000D_
Error reading database/creds/dop-role: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: GET https://redacted:8200/v1/database/creds/dop-role_x000D_
Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* 1 error occurred:_x000D_
	* "dop-role" is not an allowed role_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
In both cases they look the same in the read output, showing as separated by a space:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault read database/config/vault-db-bug_x000D_
Key                                   Value_x000D_
---                                   -----_x000D_
allowed_roles                         [default dop-role]_x000D_
connection_details                    map[connection_url:postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@172.17.0.2:5432 username:postgres]_x000D_
password_policy                       n/a_x000D_
plugin_name                           postgresql-database-plugin_x000D_
plugin_version                        n/a_x000D_
root_credentials_rotate_statements    []_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The CLI should try to check if you're inputing things without spaces and should also check that the list elements are valid cidrs in the case of the first issue._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
Version 1.13.1+ent_x000D_
Vault v1.13.1+ent (8949fec986c7ccd4508e4689d554c4b8d182fe89), built 2023-03-23T20:09:57Z_x000D_
Linux Ubuntu (debian bookworm/sid)_x000D_
_x000D_

wardob: Hello. I've resolved my issue. The issue was in TCP connection between Vault and etcd: when the etcd leader is lost TCP connection remains in established state on the Vault side. Next to the secret engine, I have multiple paths (1 per team)._x000D_

team A can list everything, which is confusing because they don't (and should not) have access to other paths and secrets._x000D_

 Using this policy only:_x000D_
 _x000D_
 ```_x000D_

}_x000D_

_x000D_
team A cannot navigate using the UI._x000D_

title: `vault login` calls the token helper with `get` and expects that to succeed
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
When I run `vault login`, and a [token helper](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands/token-helper) is configured, Vault will call the token helper with `get`. This `get` might fail, the token helper might not have a token. The reason for running `vault login` in the first place, is to obtain a token and store it using the token helper. But even if the token helper has no token yet, Vault forces it to exit with exit code 0. If it exits with a nonzero exit code, then `vault login` fails, and we never get to the `store` step._x000D_
_x000D_
We can of course make the token helper exit with exit code 0, but then if you run e.g. `vault kv get`, and the token helper has no token, then the token helper no longer has the ability to make the `kv get` fail. Instead the `kv get` will fail with a misleading “permission denied” error. Permission is denied, because no `X-Vault-Token` was included in the request. Vault did not include a token, because the token helper did not return one but signalled success either way._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Configure a token helper in `~/.vault` by putting e.g. `token_helper = "/tmp/token_helper.sh"` there._x000D_
2. In that file, put the following and make the file executable:_x000D_
   ```bash_x000D_
   #!/usr/bin/bash_x000D_
   echo "$@" >&2_x000D_
   exit 1_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
4. Run `vault login`._x000D_
5. Observe how the script got called with `get`._x000D_
6. Observe how returning 1 from that `get` prevented `vault login` from doing any login._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
I would expect `vault login` to not call the token helper with `get`. It should only call the token helper with `store`._x000D_
_x000D_
Once `vault login` does not call the token helper with `get`, it becomes possible to return 1 when a get lookup fails (because the token does not exist), and that enables the token helper to print a helpful error message in that case, instead of leaving the user with a misleading permission denied error._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): irrelevant, we don’t even get tot he point where `vault` talks to a server_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): `Vault v1.14.3 (cgo)`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux 6.5.3 / x86-64_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s): irrelevant

title: Error 500 when submitting a request with a namespaced token (from a Vault Enterprise) to a Vault OSS
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We use 2 Vault instances : one OSS and one Enterprise, via Terraform (on a Terraform Enterprise). Terraform Enterprise generate the VAULT_TOKEN (thanks to the Dynamic Provider Credential feature)._x000D_
I have 2 vault providers in my terraform code : _x000D_
- the Enterprise one is auto-configured by environment variables_x000D_
- the OSS one is configured to use a AppRole as login method (but the issue occur with any type of auth)_x000D_
_x000D_
Since `terraform-provider-vault` take the `$VAULT_TOKEN` value even if there is a `token = ...` attribute in provider configuration (!), i can't avoid the provider to create a request to Vault OSS with a `X-Vault-Token` header._x000D_
_x000D_
The issue is when the `VAULT_TOKEN` contain a "namespaced" Vault Enterprise token, vault try to convert the token in the "internal token" format._x000D_
See: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/6ef2a6031453b8bdc62fe9cb9511c223323a9e66/vault/token_store.go#L1570C2-L1578C1_x000D_
_x000D_
If the "internal token" contain a namespace suffix, we got this error :_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/vault/token_store.go#L1589_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior (specific token provided here is important to reproduce the issue):_x000D_
1. Run `vault server -dev -dev-root-token-id root`_x000D_
1. Run VAULT_ADDR="http://localhost:8200" VAULT_TOKEN="root" vault auth enable approle_x000D_
2. Run `VAULT_TOKEN=[REDACTED_VAULT_TOKEN] VAULT_ADDR=http://localhost:8200 vault write auth/approle/login role_id=x secret_id=y`_x000D_
3. or if you prefer, use the internal form of the token : `VAULT_TOKEN=[REDACTED_VAULT_TOKEN].EaBHG VAULT_ADDR=http://localhost:8200 vault write auth/approle/login role_id=x secret_id=y`_x000D_
5. See error_x000D_
```_x000D_
Error writing data to auth/userpass/login: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT http://localhost:8200/v1/auth/approle/login_x000D_
Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* error performing token check: failed to look up namespace from the token: no namespace_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
With an invalid role and any VAULT_TOKEN that not match the "namespaced" token format, the error should be : _x000D_
```_x000D_
Error writing data to auth/approle/login: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT http://localhost:8200/v1/auth/approle/login_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* invalid role ID_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
And with a valid role_id/secret_id => the return must be a valid token_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12, 1.14.3_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.12, 1.14.3_x000D_

title: Check the groups claim in the access token when using OIDC auth method
body_text:
**Summary**_x000D_
I would like to propose the addition of checking the "Groups Claim" into the Access Token (in addition to id Token) when using the Vault's OIDC authentication method. This feature would involve including user group memberships as claims within the access token. These group claims would be used by the resource server to make fine-grained access control decisions based on group permissions._x000D_
**Solution**_x000D_
ID Token: The ID token in OIDC is primarily designed for identity and user information. It provides information about the authenticated user, such as their username, email ..... It is meant to be consumed by the client application to identify the user._x000D_
Access Token: The access token, on the other hand, is designed to authorize access to protected resources, such as APIs or services. It typically contains information necessary for making access control decisions on the resource server._x000D_
_x000D_
I propose to extend the OIDC authentication method to allow the inclusion of user group claims into the access token. This groups claim should be populated based on the user's group memberships as provided by the identity provider during the OIDC authentication flow._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Use case**_x000D_
In some authentication and authorization scenarios, user group memberships define their level of access and permissions. For example, certain vault resources or functionalities may be accessible only to users who belong to specific groups (e.g., "admin," "editor," "viewer"). This is the case, for example, when OIDC authentication uses the default role, which, in turn, uses the group claim in combination with an external group and an alias_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Support Organizational Unit as Cert Auth Alias in addition to Common Name
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
There are cases where multiple client certs are issued with different common names (for e.g. ephemeral host names), but the same OU field that contains a role (for e.g. a service). I want a single entity when multiple logins happen with the cert role. Vault's default and only alias - common name, leads to entity explosion in these cases resulting in performance issues and the need to clean up the entities._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Add support for OU field as another alias for cert auth. CommonName will be the default._x000D_
This can be configured in auth/cert/config path with a new config entry - CertAlias._x000D_
It takes "CommonName" and "OrganizationalUnit" as allowed values. The former is the default and preserves the current state._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
There's no alternative other than regular clean up of entities. It hurts performance and adds maintenance cost._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
The unmitigated growth of entities in Cert Auth affects Vault service SLA_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I would like to submit a PR for this feature._x000D_

title: jwt auth: token with union of policies from all roles matching jwt
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
The [builtin jwt auth plugin](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-jwt) requires a role-name to be specified during authentication. When authenticated, access is only granted based on the policies of that single role. Even though the JWT satisfies multiple roles' bound claims. Thus, multiple logins with different role names are required when policies are split across multiple roles, resulting in multiple tokens which cannot be used interchangeably._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Automatically determine which roles' bound claims a JWT matches. Then grants access to the union of all the matching roles' policies. Thus a single login is sufficient to get a token with combined access, with the JWT as the sole login parameter. Could be disabled by default in the builtin jwt auth plugin, and enabled through config._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
A custom plugin is able to achieve the desired behavoir: [statnett/vault-plugin-auth-jwt-auto-roles](https://github.com/statnett/vault-plugin-auth-jwt-auto-roles).  _x000D_
However, it relies on the builtin jwt auth plugin (see [working-details](https://github.com/statnett/vault-plugin-auth-jwt-auto-roles#working-details)). It would be nice to get such a feture into the official jwt plugin. The feature could be activated by not specifying _role_ during login, or be locked behind a default-false configuration option.

willhaines: Hi @biazmoreira, I'd be happy to clarify that. ### Without MFA Before enabling MFA in Vault, we would often use the following workflow to authenticate and capture the result to an env variable: ``` $ export VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault login -no-store -token-only -method=ldap username=<user>) Password (will be hidden): ``` It worked really well because the password prompt was printed to `stderr` and only the token was printed to `stdout`. This way the user sees the expected interactive steps in their terminal, and the VAULT_TOKEN env variable is correctly populated with the new token, like so: ``` $ echo $VAULT_TOKEN hvs.<token> ``` ### With MFA With MFA now enabled on our Vault server, the `vault login` command generates additional prompts (which makes total sense). Unfortunately, one of those prompts is printed to `stdout`, which breaks the convenient separation we were taking advantage of. Now when the user tries to capture the `VAULT_TOKEN` in the same way, they do not see the second MFA prompt in their terminal, which can be confusing. ``` $ export VAULT_TOKEN=$(vault login -no-store -token-only -method=ldap username=<user>) Password (will be hidden): Initiating Interactive MFA Validation... ``` What's worse, though, is that the `VAULT_TOKEN` env variable now contains some prompt text in addition to the actual token and thus is not valid for executing Vault requests. ``` $ echo $VAULT_TOKEN Enter the passphrase for methodID "4d073558-5c90-11ee-8c99-0242ac120002" of type "duo": hvs.<token> ``` ### Background We started using this workflow because some of our workstations did not have encrypted disks, and we did not want to persist tokens in plaintext. Even with an encrypted disk, we've found it to be quite useful when working with multiple Vault servers (eg dev, test, prod) because you can authenticate with each server in a separate terminal. It is also useful when testing permissions if you need to compare the behavior of `test-user1` and `test-user2`, for instance. Even if this is a niche use-case that is not widely shared, I still think that the login process should be consistent. All three prompts should be printed to the same place, whether that is `stdout` or `stderr`. The authentication workflow shouldn't be split across the two streams.

title: Excessive memory usage when processing cert logins
body_text:

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
Vault server runs out of memory when many clients try to log in with certificate._x000D_
_x000D_
We use client certificates for authentication and every client has a separate role. When a whole environment has been shut down and restarted after maintenance, Vault keeps running out of memory and crashes._x000D_
_x000D_
In our testing with ~2000 cert roles and ~500 simultaneous logins, Vault process uses some 11GB of RAM while normally the usage is ~700MB_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Enable cert auth:_x000D_
`vault auth enable cert`_x000D_
2. Add many roles_x000D_
`for i in {1..1000}; do ../bin/vault write auth/cert/certs/crt$i certificate=@ca.pem; done`_x000D_
3. Trigger many simultaneous logins (codesenberg/bombardier used here):_x000D_
`./bombardier-linux-amd64 -k -t 120s -c 500 -n 500 --cert=crt.pem --key=key.pem -a -m POST https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/cert/login`_x000D_
4. Observe sharp rise in Vault's memory usage_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault processes logins, maybe rejects some, but memory usage does not explode_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.15.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux/amd64_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
Minimal config for reproducing the problem_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address = "0.0.0.0:8200"_x000D_
  cluster_address = "0.0.0.0:8201"_x000D_
  tls_cert_file = "/tmp/server.crt.pem"_x000D_
  tls_key_file = "/tmp/key.pem"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
storage "file" {_x000D_
  path = "/tmp/data"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
There are no problems with other API calls after clients have logged in and received tokens. Vault happily gives out secrets even with thousands of simultaneous requests coming in.

title: Certificate Verification Error with Vault Using Consul over HTTPS Despite Valid Certificates
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When using Vault with Consul as the storage backend over HTTPS, Vault continuously logs a _x000D_
```_x000D_
"tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"_x000D_
``` _x000D_
error. This error occurs despite correct configuration, and even when the certificates are verified manually using tools like `curl`, for example:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
sudo -u vault curl --cacert /etc/consul.d/consul-agent-ca.pem --cert /etc/consul.d/velp-server-consul-0.pem --key /etc/consul.d/velp-server-consul-0-key.pem -H "X-Consul-Token: [TOKEN]" https://consul.service.consul:8501/v1/kv/vault/core/migration_x000D_
```_x000D_
It works just fine, but when I try to run the server, I get this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
sudo -u vault /usr/bin/vault server -config=/etc/vault.d/vault.hcl -log-level=debug -dev_x000D_
_x000D_
WARNING! Unable to read storage migration status._x000D_
2023-09-30T21:23:37.325+0300 [INFO]  proxy environment: http_proxy="" https_proxy="" no_proxy=""_x000D_
2023-09-30T21:23:37.325+0300 [DEBUG] storage.consul: config path set: path=vault/_x000D_
2023-09-30T21:23:37.325+0300 [DEBUG] storage.consul: config address set: address=consul.service.consul:8501_x000D_

2023-09-30T21:23:37.325+0300 [DEBUG] storage.consul: configured TLS_x000D_
2023-09-30T21:23:37.342+0300 [WARN]  storage migration check error: error="Get \"https://consul.service.consul:8501/v1/kv/vault/core/migration\": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Set up Vault with Consul as the storage backend, using HTTPS for communication._x000D_
2. Configure TLS for Vault and Consul using the respective certificates._x000D_
3. Start the Vault server._x000D_
4. Observe the continuous logging of the error "tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority", even though tools like `curl` verify the certificates successfully._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should successfully connect to Consul over HTTPS without any certificate verification errors, especially when the certificates have been verified to be correct._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: 1.15.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version: 1.15.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 22.04_x000D_
* Consul Server Version: 1.16.2_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
# Enable UI for demo purposes_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
_x000D_
# Cluster addresses_x000D_
cluster_addr = "https://[IP_ADDRESS]:8201"_x000D_
api_addr     = "https://[IP_ADDRESS]:8200"_x000D_
_x000D_
# Consul storage backend_x000D_
storage "consul" {_x000D_
  address = "consul.service.consul:8501"_x000D_
  scheme = "https"_x000D_
  path    = "vault/"_x000D_
  token   = "[TOKEN]"_x000D_
_x000D_
  ca_file   = "/etc/consul.d/consul-agent-ca.pem"_x000D_
  cert_file = "/etc/consul.d/velp-server-consul-0.pem"_x000D_
  key_file  = "/etc/consul.d/velp-server-consul-0-key.pem"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
# TLS Listener_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address            = "0.0.0.0:8200"_x000D_
  tls_cert_file      = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-cert.pem"_x000D_
  tls_key_file       = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-key.pem"_x000D_
  tls_client_ca_file = "/opt/vault/tls/vault-ca.pem"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
We verified that the certificates were correctly set up by successfully connecting to the Consul server using `curl` with the specified certificates. The error seems to be specific to Vault's interaction with Consul over HTTPS. Although I'm very very new on the HashiCorp stack, so I might be missing something simple?

title: [1.15.0] Number Challenge Missing for Okta Verify in Vault UI
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'setOktaNumberChallenge')_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Log in to Vault Web App via Okta auth: https://$VAULT:$PORT/ui/vault/auth?with=okta -- with Username and Password._x000D_
2. Receive an Okta MFA prompt -- _Did you just try to sign in?_ -- and select _Yes, it's me__x000D_
3. The message _Which number do you see on your other screen?_ will be shown in the next mobile app window, with 3 random numbers to choose._x000D_
4. The corresponding matching number never shows up in the Vault Web App UI sign-in screen._x000D_
5. See error below in Chrome Console: _x000D_
_x000D_
![image](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/72526360/ef7740ed-33c1-4dd8-b183-47286da8a271)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
In the Vault UI Web App, select the correct verification number when using the Okta authentication method with the Number Challenge for Okta Verify after providing the right credentials and acknowledging the MFA prompt._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.0_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.15.0_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Amazon Linux 2_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
N/A; We have a vanilla configuration with file storage and TLS enabled. There's not much to talk about here._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The Number Challenge for Okta Verify feature was previously working without any issues in the Vault UI Web App, and there are no material changes that would explain this new behavior beyond the bump to version 1.15.0. **Important Note**: The Vault CLI does not seem to be impacted and still works great with the Number Challenge feature for Okta Verify._x000D_

title: transit mount, storage gcs, error: rollback: error rolling back - context deadline exceeded
body_text:
We face the issue in our dev and production environments._x000D_
To reproduce the issue with fresh vault I tested some versions locally on a MacBook with empty storage backend gcs._x000D_
I found that version 1.9.4 and 1.9.10 do not have the issue._x000D_
With 1.10.0 and eg 1.11.1 or 1.14.4 the error can be reproduced._x000D_
So I believe this bug was introduced in 1.10.0 and has never been fixed in higher versions._x000D_
_x000D_
**Bug description**_x000D_
3-5 mins after startup of the server and then every hour we see in the log:_x000D_
```_x000D_
[ERROR] rollback: error rolling back: path=customer-keys/_x000D_
  error=_x000D_
  | 75013 errors occurred:_x000D_
  | \t* failed to read value for "logical/<uuid>/policy/0001": Get "https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket-name>/logical/<uuid>/policy/0001": context deadline exceeded_x000D_
..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Install vault locally, eg `brew install vault`_x000D_
2. Create a config file `vault-config.hcl` with following contents, use a nice bucket name:_x000D_
```_x000D_
disable_mlock = true_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address = "127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
  tls_disable = "true"_x000D_
}_x000D_
storage "gcs" {_x000D_
  bucket = "mycompany-myproject-vault-gcs-test"_x000D_
  ha_enabled = "true"_x000D_
}_x000D_
api_addr = "http://127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
```_x000D_
3. Create the GCS bucket:_x000D_
```_x000D_
gsutil mb -p my-gcp-project -l europe-west3 -c standard gs://mycompany-myproject-vault-gcs-test_x000D_
```_x000D_
4. Start server: `vault server -config vault-config.hcl`_x000D_
5. In 2nd terminal, init vault and create new transit endpoint:_x000D_
```_x000D_
export VAULT_ADDR='http://127.0.0.1:8200'_x000D_
vault operator init -key-shares=1 -key-threshold=1 > init_response_x000D_
cat init_response | grep 'Unseal Key 1:' | sed 's/Unseal Key 1: //' > unseal_key_x000D_
cat init_response | grep 'Initial Root Token:' | sed 's/Initial Root Token: //' > root_token_x000D_
vault operator unseal $(cat unseal_key)_x000D_
vault login $(cat root_token)_x000D_
vault secrets enable -path=customer-keys -force-no-cache=true transit_x000D_
```_x000D_
6. Create 5000 keys with a shell script `add_keys.sh`:_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
#!/usr/bin/env bash_x000D_
_x000D_
total=50_x000D_
for c in `seq -w 0 $((total-1))`; do_x000D_
    for i in `seq -w 0 99`; do _x000D_
        vault write -f customer-keys/keys/$c$i >/dev/null &_x000D_
    done >/dev/null 2>&1_x000D_
    wait_x000D_
    echo $((1$c+1-100))00/${total}00_x000D_
done_x000D_
```_x000D_
```_x000D_
chmod +x add_keys.sh_x000D_
./add_keys.sh_x000D_
# count written keys, 4000 keys or more is enough to reproduce the issue_x000D_
vault list -format=yaml customer-keys/keys | wc -l_x000D_
```_x000D_
7. Stop server in 1st terminal with CTRL+C, start server in 1st terminal, _x000D_
   `vault server -config vault-config.hcl 2>&1 | grep -v "failed to read value"`_x000D_
   The piped grep statement removes the trace lines from the error msg to better see the first line of the error msg._x000D_
8. In 2nd terminal: `vault operator unseal $(cat unseal_key)` (**Important step! Do not forget this unseal step!**)_x000D_
9. Wait 3-5 minutes_x000D_
10. See error in server log in 1st terminal_x000D_
```_x000D_
[ERROR] rollback: error rolling back: path=customer-keys/_x000D_
```_x000D_
11. Cleanup:_x000D_
- Stop server in 1st terminal with CTRL+C_x000D_
- Delete GCS bucket `gsutil -m rm -r gs://mycompany-myproject-vault-gcs-test 2>/dev/null`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version 1.10.0 to 1.14.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version 1.10.0 to 1.14.4_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
This error does not happen when keycount is low, eg 1000._x000D_
This error does not happen with versions smaller than 1.10.0._x000D_
Raft storage does not produce the error._x000D_
When creating the transit backend the option `-force-no-cache=true` can be omitted, the error is reproducible also without this option._x000D_
_x000D_
**Questions**_x000D_
_x000D_
What does the rollback manager do at startup and every hour?_x000D_
Is this error critical? What are the consequences of this error?_x000D_
Can/should we rollback production environment from 1.12.x to 1.9.x?_x000D_
Can someone reproduce and fix the error?_x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks in advance,_x000D_
Craftey_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Note:**_x000D_
To install older vault versions with brew I did:_x000D_
```_x000D_
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/a0ce0e6ce3c921a26db90dfe8c38b4df9f227669/Formula/vault.rb > /tmp/vault.rb # version 1.10.0_x000D_
_x000D_
brew reinstall --formula /tmp/vault.rb _x000D_

_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
paths for secrets in eventing add a /data/ element to the path.  So, for a secret with path secret/my_secret  policies must be written _x000D_
path "secret/data/mysecret" {}_x000D_
_x000D_
and the json output from eventing likewise references secret/data/my_secret._x000D_
_x000D_
Documentation says to write policies like this::_x000D_
_x000D_
path "secret/my-data" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list", "subscribe"]_x000D_
  subscribe_event_types = ["*"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
but this will not work._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. create a secret secret/my_secret_x000D_
2. create a policy: _x000D_
path "sys/events/subscribe/*" {_x000D_
    capabilities = ["read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
path "secret/my_secret" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list", "subscribe"]_x000D_
  subscribe_event_types = ["*"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
3. Wire up a user, role and token for eventing:_x000D_
(user and alias created in ui)_x000D_
export VAULT_ADDR=http://localhost:8200_x000D_
vault write auth/token/roles/eventer \_x000D_
  allowed_policies="eventing" \_x000D_
  orphan=true \_x000D_
  period=24h_x000D_
---_x000D_
export VAULT_ADDR=http://localhost:8200_x000D_

title: Vault 1.15 audit log (SIGHUP) reload doesn't release and reopen file
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We have Vault 1.15 running for 8+ days and got an alert today that the disk of the audit log is close to reaching 10 GB. After inspecting what's been going on, I noticed that the audit log file was 0 bytes but the disk itself (only mounted for the audit log) is close to 10 GB but no file present._x000D_
_x000D_
Example where the `/var/log` is 4M but via df -h it's > 200M._x000D_
```shell_x000D_
/var/log # ls -lh_x000D_
total 4M_x000D_
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root        8.0K Oct 11 08:14 audit.db_x000D_
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root       32.0K Oct 11 08:15 audit.db-shm_x000D_
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root        3.9M Oct 11 08:15 audit.db-wal_x000D_
drwx------    2 root     root       16.0K Jul 13  2021 lost+found_x000D_
-rw-------    1 root     root           0 Oct 11 08:15 vault_audit.log_x000D_
---_x000D_
df -h_x000D_
/dev/sdb                  9.7G    211.9M      9.5G   2% /var/log_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Our setup is using fluent-bit to read the logfile to push the data to BigQuery and we rotate the log with logrotate every 200 MB and send a `SIGHUP` to Vault. It has always worked so far and I tested it with 1.14 earlier and is still working._x000D_
_x000D_
We have 3 Vault instances for different envs (dev / stage / prod) and all of them are experiencing the issue._x000D_
My theory is that the SIGHUP is not releasing the existing file and reloading the new file. On the filesystem it's gone but somehow Vault continues logging to the old file and not the new one._x000D_
Nothing changed on the logrotate side and I can also see the reload (via `SIGHUP`) in the log._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Vault 1.15 instance with file audit log to `/var/log`_x000D_
2. Logrotate as side container with shared process space to rotate the log and send SIGHUP via `POSTROTATE` to Vault._x000D_
3. See that the file is empty but the disk keeps growing, even though it's only mounted there + fits Vault audit disk usage._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
`SIGHUP` should release the file and reload the new file, just like it did in 1.14 and earlier._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.0, built 2023-09-22T16:53:10Z_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.15.0 (b4d07277a6c5318bb50d3b94bbd6135dccb4c601), built 2023-09-22T16:53:10Z_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Kubernetes GKE cluster - 1.27.3_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault is setup via Terraform._x000D_
Relevant config:_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
resource "vault_audit" "file_logs" {_x000D_
  type  = "file"_x000D_
  local = true_x000D_
_x000D_
  options = {_x000D_
    file_path = "/var/log/vault_audit.log"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I checked the docs and changelog and nothing obvious changed around the file audit log._x000D_
_x000D_
The [docs](https://support.hashicorp.com/hc/en-us/articles/5767318985107-Vault-SIGHUP-Behavior) state_x000D_
```_x000D_
Vault will continue writing to the same audit log file even if it was moved or renamed as part of log rotation; issuing a SIGHUP to the Vault process is necessary for the file to be released. _x000D_
```_x000D_
and I feel like the first part is exactly what's happening even though `SIGHUP` was triggered.
