title: Single node (in a cluster of three) is able to force elections during network issues
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
We've seen two different issues in our Vault cluster that I believe might be the same underlying reason, so I'm reporting them both here._x000D_
_x000D_
They both seem related to a single non-leader node not having full network connectivity for a few different reasons, so it tries to start an election, as is expected. However, when network connectivity is re-established with the rest of the cluster, the leader shows a log message like this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
[ERROR] storage.raft: peer has newer term, stopping replication: peer="{Voter e053bfdc-72ec-49ed-9098-4fbc0199f27a prod-vault-0.prod-vault-internal:8201}"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
And then immediately steps down._x000D_
_x000D_
More details on the two scenarios where we've seen this:_x000D_
_x000D_
Both scenarios we run Vault in Kubernetes using [the Helm chart](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-helm)._x000D_
_x000D_
### Scenario A_x000D_
_x000D_
In this scenario, we are restarting a pod using `kubectl delete pod prod-vault-0`. Due to a bug in another component in our cluster, the pod had its networking connectivity torn down too quickly, and quickly hit the heartbeat timeout and tried to call an election:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2023-10-11T11:10:41.021Z [WARN]  storage.raft: heartbeat timeout reached, starting election: last-leader-addr=prod-vault-2.prod-vault-internal:8201 last-leader-id=f198d8f1-598c-572e-e9f9-0d24177a1481_x000D_
2023-10-11T11:10:41.021Z [INFO]  storage.raft: entering candidate state: node="Node at prod-vault-a.prod-vault-internal:8201 [Candidate]" term=1882_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
At this time, our `performance_multiplier` was set to 1, so the pod managed to hit 6 election timeouts and restart the election 6 times before it was killed._x000D_
_x000D_
When the `prod-vault-0` node came back online, from its point of view it came out without much issue, it rejoined the cluster as a follower and had no errors. However, looking at `prod-vault-2` (the current leader), we see the following:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2023-10-11T11:10:58.711Z [ERROR] storage.raft: peer has newer term, stopping replication: peer="{Voter 4c6f2be2-8aba-87d8-4ec5-d94a3ecac5ed prod-vault-0.prod-vault-internal:8201}"_x000D_
2023-10-11T11:10:58.711Z [INFO]  storage.raft: aborting pipeline replication: peer="{Voter 6d139636-e635-83fc-f7a0-2b9042973b59 prod-vault-1.prod-vault-internal:8201}"_x000D_
2023-10-11T11:10:58.711Z [WARN]  core: leadership lost, stopping active operation2023-10-11T11:10:58.711Z [INFO]  storage.raft: entering follower state: follower="Node at prod-vault-2.prod-vault-internal:8201 [Follower]" leader-address= leader-id=_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This leads to a short (a couple of seconds) outage in our Vault setup that we'd like to avoid when the majority of nodes are fine._x000D_
_x000D_
### Scenario B_x000D_
_x000D_
This case is also related to restarting a non-active node. In this case, the following happens:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. `prod-vault-0` is the active, `prod-vault-1` and `prod-vault-2` are voting followers._x000D_
2. `prod-vault-2` is restarted using `kubectl delete pod prod-vault-2`_x000D_
3. `prod-vault-0` almost immediately logs an error sending heartbeats to `prod-vault-2` and tries to reconnect, but since the `prod-vault-2` pod is still technically being torn down, the DNS entry still resolves to the "old" pod IP, which is no longer accepting connections. This leads to `prod-vault-0` being stuck in the Dial phase, which it will hit the timeout for 10 seconds later._x000D_
4. While `prod-vault-0` is trying to re-dial `prod-vault-2`, `prod-vault-2` has restarted and come back online. It launches, but because `prod-vault-0` hasn't connected yet, it's not receiving a heartbeat, and hits the initial heartbeat timeout, and calls for an election. Both `prod-vault-0` and `prod-vault-1` receive this election request, but reject it due to already having a leader. The reject vote from `prod-vault-0` does not seem to make it to `prod-vault-2` (I'm guessing because `prod-vault-0` is still dialing)._x000D_
5. `prod-vault-2` hits the election timeout, and calls another election. This repeats over and over until `prod-vault-0` hits the 10 second dial timeout._x000D_
6. `prod-vault-0` hits the dial timeout, and redials. This time the DNS is updated and it connects. It then immediately prints the "peer has newer term, stopping replication" message, and steps down. `prod-vault-2` is still doing it's "request election" loop, so it ends up getting elected quickly after._x000D_
_x000D_
In this case, part of our issue seems to be that we have set `performance_multiplier` to 1, which leads to very short heartbeat timeouts, but the dial timeout is still hardcoded to 10 seconds: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/d5df561032fb361534536be1c4f7947489445e17/physical/raft/raft.go#L950 . We were able to resolve this issue by increasing the performance multiplier to 4, thus leading to initial heartbeat timeouts greater than 10 seconds, but this seems like a workaround more than a fix._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
I am not sure how to reproduce Scenario A outside of our cluster, since I've yet to nail down the issue causing networking to be torn down too quickly. Scenario B, however, I've been able to reliably reproduce using minikube._x000D_
_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Set up a minikube cluster. I am running minikube version v1.31.2, with Kubernetes version 1.25.11._x000D_
2. Have some form of Vault auto-unseal mechanism available. I ran a Vault dev instance on my laptop (the minikube host) and used the transit unseal mechanism, but other options should be possible too, but without auto-unseal the pod doesn't come online fast enough to trigger the issue reliably._x000D_
3. Have some sort of self-signed TLS CA (this might not be required, but I couldn't easily figure out how to disable all the TLS features._x000D_
4. Install Vault using `helm upgrade hashicorp/vault sarah-test-vault --version 0.25.0 --values values.yaml --install`, the values file is in the folded section after this list. You can chose a different name for the release, but some config options will need to be changed (mainly `retry_join`)_x000D_
5. Bootstrap the cluster._x000D_
6. Once the cluster is running and initialised, try deleting one of the non-active pods with `kubectl delete`._x000D_
7. Observe that shortly after the pod is deleted, it comes back online and then becomes the active node a few seconds later._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
<details><summary>Helm values file</summary>_x000D_
_x000D_
```YAML_x000D_
---_x000D_
global:_x000D_
  enabled: true_x000D_
  tlsDisable: false_x000D_
_x000D_
ui:_x000D_
  enabled: true_x000D_
_x000D_
server:_x000D_
  enabled: true_x000D_
  preStopSleepSeconds: 5_x000D_
  service:_x000D_
    type: ClusterIP_x000D_
  image:_x000D_
    repository: hashicorp/vault_x000D_
    tag: "1.14.4"_x000D_
  affinity: ""_x000D_
  volumes:  _x000D_
    - name: sarah-test-vault-tls_x000D_
      secret:_x000D_
        secretName: sarah-test-vault-tls_x000D_
    - name: sarah-test-vault-internal-ca_x000D_
      secret:_x000D_
        secretName: sarah-test-vault-internal-ca_x000D_
  volumeMounts:_x000D_
    - mountPath: /vault/tls_x000D_
      name: sarah-test-vault-tls_x000D_
      readOnly: true_x000D_
    - mountPath: /vault/tls-ca_x000D_
      name: sarah-test-vault-internal-ca_x000D_
      readOnly: true_x000D_
  ha:_x000D_
    enabled: true_x000D_
    raft:_x000D_
      enabled: true_x000D_
      config: |_x000D_
        log_level = "trace"_x000D_
        cluster_name = "sarah-test"_x000D_
        ui = true_x000D_
        disable_mlock = true_x000D_
        listener "tcp" {_x000D_
          address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
          cluster_address = "[::]:8201"_x000D_
          tls_cert_file = "/vault/tls/tls.crt"_x000D_
          tls_key_file = "/vault/tls/tls.key"_x000D_
          tls_disable_client_certs = true_x000D_
          telemetry {_x000D_
            unauthenticated_metrics_access = true_x000D_
          }_x000D_
        }_x000D_
        seal "transit" {_x000D_
          address = "http://host.minikube.internal:8200"_x000D_
          token = "[insert your own token here]"_x000D_
          disable_renewal = "false"_x000D_
          key_name = "autounseal"_x000D_
          mount_path = "transit/"_x000D_
        }_x000D_
        storage "raft" {_x000D_
          path = "/vault/data"_x000D_
          performance_multiplier = 1_x000D_
          retry_join {_x000D_
            leader_api_addr = "https://sarah-test-vault-0.sarah-test-vault-internal.default.svc.cluster.local:8200"_x000D_
            leader_tls_servername = "sarah-test-vault.default.svc.cluster.local"_x000D_
            leader_ca_cert_file = "/vault/tls-ca/ca.crt"_x000D_
          }_x000D_
          retry_join {_x000D_
            leader_api_addr = "https://sarah-test-vault-1.sarah-test-vault-internal.default.svc.cluster.local:8200"_x000D_
            leader_tls_servername = "sarah-test-vault.default.svc.cluster.local"_x000D_
            leader_ca_cert_file = "/vault/tls-ca/ca.crt"_x000D_
          }_x000D_
          retry_join {_x000D_
            leader_api_addr = "https://sarah-test-vault-2.sarah-test-vault-internal.default.svc.cluster.local:8200"_x000D_
            leader_tls_servername = "sarah-test-vault.default.svc.cluster.local"_x000D_
            leader_ca_cert_file = "/vault/tls-ca/ca.crt"_x000D_
          }_x000D_
        }_x000D_
        service_registration "kubernetes" {}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
</details>_x000D_

title: Customize the automatic creation of entities based on auth backend tune
body_text:
One problem I encounter while using Vault is that when I configure an external authentication method such as OIDC or Kubernetes, every individual user who is authorized to use that authentication backend (such as users from my organization's OIDC provider or all service accounts in my Kubernetes cluster) is automatically granted access to Vault and an entity (along with an alias) is generated for them._x000D_
_x000D_
 I would like to personally maintain a list of entities and their aliases through either an IaC or UI. When a user attempts to authenticate, Vault will first check the entity aliases for the user. If a corresponding alias and entity exist, the user will be authenticated and assigned a token, otherwise, the login gets rejected._x000D_
_x000D_
I can implement the required scenario and submit a pull request. The solution involves adding an option to each authentication backend tune to determine the dynamic creation of entities. However, I need to ensure that this behavior aligns with Vault's overall policies and is acceptable.

title: Support for Multiple Connections to Different Databases within the Same PostgreSQL Instance
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Currently, in PostgreSQL, there isn't a capability to grant permissions to schemas or tables in database A while being connected to database B. Due to this, there's a need to set up multiple database connections in Vault to create roles and grant permissions within these databases. However, this approach presents a challenge. If we use multiple connections, we must use distinct roles for each connection. This is because if Vault rotates the password for one connection, the other connections using the same role would break due to password discrepancies._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Solution A:_x000D_
Dynamic Database Specification during Role Management:_x000D_
Allow users to specify (or overwrite) the target database name when executing create/renew/revoke statements. This flexibility would mean a single connection could be used to manage roles across different databases in the same PostgreSQL instance._x000D_
Decoupling Credentials from Connection Configuration:_x000D_
_x000D_
Solution B:_x000D_
Separate the credentials (username and password) from the connection configuration. This would allow multiple connections to share the same set of credentials. By decoupling them, the password rotation for one connection wouldn't adversely affect others that share the same credentials._x000D_
_x000D_

title: Consul Multihost Secrets Backend
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
As we continue to scale out both Enterprise and Community Consul clusters, managing 1 Consul Secrets Engine per Consul cluster is becoming a huge number of mounts which is not necessary. Pairing that with the fact that wan fed is gong away and everything is moving to peering, we can't set things up how we used to._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Update the Consul Secrets Engine so that you can configure multiple clusters/hosts per engine so that different roles can connect with different clusters but all under the same secrets engine. _x000D_
_x000D_
This would be very similiar to how other engines work. Example when setting up MySQL, you can specific multiple hosts and different roles point to the different hosts/connections_x000D_
https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/databases/mysql-maria_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write database/config/my-mysql-database \_x000D_
    plugin_name=mysql-database-plugin \_x000D_
    connection_url="{{username}}:{{password}}@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/" \_x000D_
    allowed_roles="my-role" \_x000D_
    username="vaultuser" \_x000D_
    password="vaultpass"_x000D_
_x000D_
 vault write database/roles/my-role \_x000D_
    db_name=my-mysql-database \_x000D_
    creation_statements="CREATE USER '{{name}}'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY '{{password}}';GRANT SELECT ON *.* TO '{{name}}'@'%';" \_x000D_
    default_ttl="1h" \_x000D_
    max_ttl="24h"_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
This allows for simplicity, supports this new Consul Peering methodology, and is just overall easier

title: Consul Service and Node Identities Scaling
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
If a group wants to use Vault to manage node identities tokens, they easily run into scaling issues with configuration. The issue is if you have 5 service identities or 5 node identities, you have to create 5 distinct roles on the Vault side. If you have 5,000 nodes, you need 5,000 unique roles. It just doesn't scale. _x000D_
_x000D_
When we pair that with all the workload identities goals, it makes it difficult to use Vault_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Update the Consul secrets engine so that instead of the role or service identity being tied specifically to the role, make it an argument so that you can specify the node identity during the checkout so you can have 10 different nodes with different node identities using the same Vault Consul role_x000D_
_x000D_
If the role is created with a specific node or service identity, then it would function exactly as is making this a backwards compatible, non breaking change_x000D_
_x000D_
This pairs nicely with https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/23782 _x000D_

title: The List method in the etcd backend does not work as expected

But we got the error after we exceeded 1.4 million active tokens._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
In the current implementation, the List method always performs a Get request to etcd and always gets a key and a value in return._x000D_
We looked at the implementation of List methods in other backends and noticed that in those methods, list always gets only the keys._x000D_
_x000D_
We noticed that before the problem occurs, vault performs a list query on the path /vault/sys/expire/id/ and fails after a while._x000D_
In the logs we see an error:_x000D_

top_3_comments_text: grzechukol: This issue is somehow similar to https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/8761. | npurdy-tyro: We recently experienced this error. In our case it was not limited to the `auth/k8s` but extended to our `auth/aws` auth backend. Just like you it didn't happen consistently, but instead happened sporadically. But it appeared to be happening more frequently. Looking at the error we identified that when an entity was being written to DynamoDB it was somehow exceeding the 400kb row limit. This seemed impossible to us because the entity struct was quite small. After digging into the Vault code we made some discoveries: Vault does not store a single entity in a single storage (DynamoDB) row. It instead maintains a set of 256 hashed buckets that map 1 to 1 to a storage row. This is done through the [StoragePacker](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a7b6f3490f59cfeef8b63fe12ceec31279388221/helper/storagepacker/storagepacker.go#L33), It then places auth entities into one of these 256 entities, based on the first byte of the [MD5 sum](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a7b6f3490f59cfeef8b63fe12ceec31279388221/helper/storagepacker/storagepacker.go#L118) of the entity ID. The entity ID is simply a [UUID generated](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a7b6f3490f59cfeef8b63fe12ceec31279388221/vault/identity_store_util.go#L1367) when an entity is created. Therefore the problem effects all Auth backends in vault. Vault also does not delete old entities, and in some cases like us it just keeps creating them, so there were hundreds of thousands of them. So what begins to happen is these buckets begin to fill up. The contents are compressed so it takes a while. Maybe ~600,000 entities later. Once a bucket is full its no longer useable, and any hashed entity IDs that land in it will fail to persist to DynamoDB and you will see this error. This is why the error appears randomly, and without a pattern. To 'fix' the problem you must delete entities that are no longer in use. If you have a max TTL that you configure and use the entities last accessed date then I believe its pretty safe. Be warned however, if you do not fix the problem then more of the buckets will fill up until they are all full. Once they are all full you will be unable to login to vault at all. If you cannot login to Vault you may not be able to clean the entities and you may need to delete from DynamoDB directly to regain access. Also be aware that a hostile client could leverage this knowledge to cause a denial of service on your Vault, so be sure to set appropriate rate limits to limit the speed that they can generate entities. Moving forwards I wonder if implementing a `identity/entity/tidy` endpoint (like the PKI one) that takes a time input and deletes entities that haven't been accessed for greater than that time would make sense. In your case @grzechukol for Kubernetes auth entities it could be worth researching if using the [alias_name_source](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/kubernetes#alias_name_source) could help curb created entities.

title: Error "event not processed by enough 'sink' nodes" when file audit enabled in Vault 1.15
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Since upgrading to Vault 1.15, we are seeing occasional errors in the logs such as:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2023-10-26T22:04:43.804+0100 [ERROR] secrets.system.system_9ba98b00: lease renewal failed: lease_id=database/creds/readonly/weDQJArsWMkCUwVBf7zzOVwg_x000D_
  error=_x000D_
  | failed to renew entry: resp: (*logical.Response)(nil) err: 1 error occurred:_x000D_
  | \t* timeout: context canceled_x000D_
  | _x000D_
  _x000D_
2023-10-26T22:04:43.805+0100 [ERROR] core: failed to audit response: request_path=sys/leases/renew_x000D_
  error=_x000D_
  | 1 error occurred:_x000D_
  | \t* event not processed by enough 'sink' nodes_x000D_
  | _x000D_
  _x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The first error is possible due to network latency/timeouts to a database when using dynamic credentials. The second error is new and is due to the new audit logging behaviour in Vault 1.15. This causes the [`vault_audit_log_request_failure`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/telemetry/metrics/audit#vault-audit-log_request_failure) telemetry metric to be incremented and therefore could trigger alerts unnecessarily._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
I've managed to reproduce this with a `vault server -dev` instance locally:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Follow the [getting started guide](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/db-credentials/database-secrets) using a local Vault instance and a local postgres instance running in docker. _x000D_
2. Enable audit logs with `vault audit enable file file_path=/tmp/vault_audit.log`_x000D_
3. Install [toxiproxy](https://github.com/Shopify/toxiproxy) locally which we will use to simulate some network latency/jitter. Start the server with `toxiproxy-server`._x000D_
4. Set up a backend in toxiproxy `toxiproxy-cli create -l localhost:5433 -u localhost:5432 postgres`_x000D_
5. Add a "toxic" to simulate some network latency/jitter `toxiproxy-cli toxic add -t latency -a latency=1000 -a jitter=2000 postgres`_x000D_
6. Tell Vault to use toxiproxy instead of postgres direct:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write database/config/postgresql \                                _x000D_
     plugin_name=postgresql-database-plugin \_x000D_
     connection_url="postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@$POSTGRES_URL:5433/postgres?sslmode=disable" \_x000D_
     allowed_roles=readonly \_x000D_
     username="root" \_x000D_
     password="rootpassword"_x000D_
```_x000D_
7. Create some dynamic credentials: `vault read database/creds/readonly`_x000D_
8. Generate a curl command to renew the lease: `vault lease renew --output-curl-string database/creds/readonly/weDQJArsWMkCUwVBf7zzOVwg` (update the lease ID as needed)_x000D_
9. Update the curl command to have a timeout and run the command: `curl --max-time 1.2 -X PUT -H "X-Vault-Request: true" -H "X-Vault-Token: $(vault print token)" -d '{"increment":0,"lease_id":"database/creds/readonly/weDQJArsWMkCUwVBf7zzOVwg"}' http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/leases/renew`_x000D_
10. Review the Vault error log_x000D_
_x000D_
You should see an `event not processed by enough 'sink' nodes` error here. This error can happen in a dynamic environment where requests are made to renew leases, which can take a bit of time, and the request is cancelled while it's being processed. This can happen in k8s when pods are spinning up/down frequently._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Although the lease renewal failed, I would not expect this to cause an error when writing to the audit file. I don't believe it caused a problem in earlier versions of Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.15.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: MacOS arm64/Linux amd64_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s): Not applicable as this is using a `vault server -dev` instance with no special configuration._x000D_
_x000D_
Setting `VAULT_AUDIT_DISABLE_EVENTLOGGER=true` as an env var to revert back to the previous audit log behaviour stops the error appearing in the logs:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2023-10-27T10:02:31.007+0100 [ERROR] secrets.system.system_d1c6c5f9: lease renewal failed: lease_id=database/creds/readonly/vHGElhu0CbF6VB9XgAbXIHGa_x000D_
  error=_x000D_
  | failed to renew entry: resp: (*logical.Response)(nil) err: 1 error occurred:_x000D_
  | \t* context canceled_x000D_
  |_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Only the "context canceled" error is displayed when the lease renewal request is cancelled.

title: Root rotation for RabbitMQ secrets engine
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Credentials given to Vault using the RabbitMQ secrets engine cannot be rotated as they can be in other secrets engines._x000D_
For example, the [database](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/db-credentials/database-root-rotation), [Azure](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/azure#rotate-root) and [AWS](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/aws#rotate-root-iam-credentials) secrets engines allow for the rotation of root credentials to improve the security of the target system._x000D_
_x000D_
The RabbitMQ secrets engine does not do this, meaning that the credentials provided to vault need to be rotated manually to gain the same level of security._x000D_
_x000D_
As outlined on the [Database root credential rotation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/db-credentials/database-root-rotation#challenge) page:_x000D_
_x000D_
> Therefore, it is very common to give Vault your root credentials._x000D_
> _x000D_
> However, these credentials are often long-lived and never change once configured on Vault. This may violate the Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) policies surrounding that data stored in the database._x000D_
_x000D_
This same statement applies to data transiting through RabbitMQ._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Extension of the RabbitMQ secrets engine to support a `rotate-root` API which will rotate the credentials stored in Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Alternatives require additional logic to be implemented elsewhere that pull out the credentials, do the rotation and store the result._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

title: service account names and 403 errors should have a debug option that clarifies exactly what caused the 403
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I think this could be a feature ... it's maybe a feature we should add that is exposed when debugging or audit logging.

**Problem**

I believe account name related 403 errors can happen in situations which are widely variant:
-  the pki or policies aren't setup properly... 
- the service account name is incorrect
- in the age of webhooks it's easy to interpret this 403 as possibly originating from the k8s apiserver instead of vault itself.


But enabling -debug and audit logs don't necessarily give you any hints as far as how to remediate a  403, and doesn't describe much about what a service account is and is not able to do.   This makes it not clear as to what policy entries needs to be updated.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like it if debug logs can be turned up to the point that they tell you what is and isn't allowed for a given 403 error. I think it would be awesome if you got these for free when running with debug option.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Patching the service account parts of the codebase for one off logging in the specific code path where the 403s are returned. 

**Additional context**

Sorry I did not document the exact error. I exec into that node and checked with netstat, it was not listening on port 8201. At the time I was running version 1.17.2 I ran across #24604 so I tried adding `publishNotReadyAddresses: true` to the vault service. That resolved the DNS lookup failures, but still did not result in the broken nodes properly joining and unsealing. The k8s documentation does have a note related to DNS that states: > Also, the Pod needs to be ready in order to have a record unless publishNotReadyAddresses=True is set on the Service. Next I added an init pod with command set to `sleep 30` I then deleted the bad pod, exec into the init, deleted all the data, `vault.db` and `raft` folder. At the same time I was logged into the vault leader and issued `vault operator raft remove-peer node-name-here` before the 30 seconds was up. This did not change anything, still seeing the same unseal keys error. I manually deleted all of the 1.17.2 pods, in order so they would restart as 1.17.3. title: Add kv configuration or policy option disallowing users to "Download secret value".
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
This feature appeared a while ago. When I go to vault I'm reminded that authenticated users can now save secret data as a plaintext file. I'm not sure how this feature made it into vault /ui/ but giving users the ability to save any secret they want onto a potentially unmanaged and unencrypted machine with one click and no protection on said secret isn't wonderful. Monitoring the Network tab under Developer Tools reveals that the Vault web client doesn't reach out with another API call and instead just saves what it has in memory with JS._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
A per-kv-engine or policy option to disable the download button feature on kv secret values._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Removing this feature._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
I cannot think of any good reason for Vault to offer users the opportunity of exporting secrets as a plaintext files in their Downloads folder._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
Searching online returns no results relating to this secret download feature or any discussion about it. A little confusing while searching for ways to disable the feature or learn more about it such as the release it were added in or relevant documentation. It appears to be part of `ui/lib/core/addon/components/masked-input.hbs` with relevant commits 01d5d1dc3a1, 43258c28fa3, 88ed074287d, b5e82f5ad1f and even includes a line `{{#if @allowDownload}}` though I cannot seem to find documentation about this feature with my poor searching skills.

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The endpoint [Read Secret ID](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/approle#read-approle-secret-id) will return an empty body with a status 2xx if the secret ID was not generated by the endpoint the [Generate Secret ID](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/approle#generate-new-secret-id) and therefore, not found._x000D_
_x000D_
However, for other endpoints (for [AppRole](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/approle)), when an element is not found ([Read Role](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/approle#read-approle), [Read Secret ID Accessor](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/approle#read-approle-secret-id-accessor), [List](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/approle#list-roles), etc.), the API will return a 4xx status code and not a 2xx with empty body._x000D_
_x000D_

- [Create approle](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/approle#create-update-approle)_x000D_

_x000D_

-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When we're using [Read Auth Method Configuration](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/auth#read-auth-method-configuration) the API will return too much information (duplicate)._x000D_
_x000D_
As explained in the documentation, the response should be something like:_x000D_
```json_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "request_id": "8d2a1e33-4c00-46a5-f50d-4dc5f5d96f12",_x000D_
  "lease_id": "",_x000D_
  "lease_duration": 0,_x000D_
  "renewable": false,_x000D_
  "data": {_x000D_
    "accessor": "auth_github_badd7fd0",_x000D_
    "config": {_x000D_
      "default_lease_ttl": 0,_x000D_
      "force_no_cache": false,_x000D_
      "max_lease_ttl": 0,_x000D_
      "token_type": "default-service"_x000D_
    },_x000D_
    "deprecation_status": "supported",_x000D_
    "description": "",_x000D_
    "external_entropy_access": false,_x000D_
    "local": false,_x000D_
    "options": null,_x000D_
    "plugin_version": "",_x000D_
    "running_plugin_version": "v1.12.0+builtin.vault",_x000D_
    "running_sha256": "",_x000D_
    "seal_wrap": false,_x000D_
    "type": "github",_x000D_
    "uuid": "4b42d1a4-0a0d-3c88-ae90-997e0c8b41be"_x000D_
  },_x000D_
  "warnings": null_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
In a lot of endpoints, we have this format, the field `data` contains the information about what we need._x000D_
_x000D_
However, the endpoint will return this response format:_x000D_
```json_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "deprecation_status": "supported",_x000D_
  "accessor": "auth_approle_801d7acf",_x000D_
  "local": false,_x000D_
  "external_entropy_access": false,_x000D_
  "running_plugin_version": "v1.15.1+builtin.vault",_x000D_
  "description": "",_x000D_

    "token_type": "default-service"_x000D_
  },_x000D_

  "request_id": "f7062456-f586-b808-e286-78470181b300",_x000D_
  "lease_id": "",_x000D_
  "renewable": false,_x000D_
  "lease_duration": 0,_x000D_
  "data": {_x000D_
    "accessor": "auth_approle_801d7acf",_x000D_
    "config": {_x000D_
      "default_lease_ttl": 0,_x000D_
      "force_no_cache": false,_x000D_
      "max_lease_ttl": 0,_x000D_
      "token_type": "default-service"_x000D_
    },_x000D_
    "deprecation_status": "supported",_x000D_
    "description": "",_x000D_
    "external_entropy_access": false,_x000D_
    "local": false,_x000D_
    "options": {},_x000D_
    "plugin_version": "",_x000D_

    "type": "approle",_x000D_
    "uuid": "c3ac0e5f-8f71-dbf3-8aab-c5d14ac874fc"_x000D_
  },_x000D_

}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
As visible, the API will send the information in `$.data` but also in `$` (root), so the data is duplicated_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
[Enable approle auth method](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/auth#enable-auth-method)_x000D_
[Read Auth Method Configuration](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/auth#read-auth-method-configuration)_x000D_

title: Add filtering on list requests (for but not limited to transit API)
body_text:
Using the [list request of the transit API](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/transit#list-keys) always returns all the keys. There's no way of limiting the amount of keys returned in the response._x000D_
This becomes an issue when the number of keys increases : responses are getting fat and the request takes more and more time to get processed. Vault should have a way to limit the response size and processing time for this operation._x000D_
_x000D_
A natural solution to this would be introducing a pagination mechanism (#10887). However this looks hard to achieve because the storage system works in a "one-shot" mode (see discussion in #21164)._x000D_
This ticket suggest another approach : introduce a filter parameter in the list request. This would allow limiting the amount of results in the backend, and may be easier to integrate in the "one-shot" mode of the storage subsystem (the operation still run one-shot with a filter)._x000D_
Using filtering you can do a kind of simple pagination by requesting all objects starting with "a*", then all starting with "b*", etc. You don't get a strong warranty on the amount of returned results, but this is effective in reducing the amount of data returned and make the list operation useable on huge datasets._x000D_
Of course this only works if you have an id or text field on which you can apply the filter (which is the case for key IDs on the transit API)_x000D_
_x000D_
Adding a filter capability also makes sense just for getting a subset of the keys (for transit API, but can of course be extended to others APIs)._x000D_
_x000D_
Why this matters ?_x000D_
The list operation may be very important for some usages. When managing keys the user may keep the list of keys identifiers in a separated software/database (for example to add some metadata on each key). As the amount of keys grows, there is a need to do consistency checks between the vault content and others storages having key related data. The list operation allows to do this, and it needs to do this in reasonable time / size response._x000D_
_x000D_
Complements: _x000D_
* In the UI there is a pagination mechanism, but it is applied locally in the UI not server side._x000D_
* #10887 Request for adding pagination_x000D_

title: Vault Enterprise sync value issue.
body_text:
_x000D_
_x000D_
when using the vault enterprise sync feature to google secret manager it seems like because vault follows the formation of_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
secret_x000D_
key:value_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
yet Google secret manager follows _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
secret_x000D_
value_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
thus if the sync feature does not return just the value but also include the key from vault, we will get {"value":{"value":" or {"key":"value"} as the secret, and we cannot just ingest as a secret from google secret manager due to the json wrapping. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
is there a workaround for this? _x000D_
top_3_comments_text: maxcoulombe: Hey @nia-potato! There is no workaround at the moment but we are interested in making the format of synced secrets configurable so it fits more use cases. To clarify the behavior you are looking for, let's say we have this secret on the Vault-side: ``` max:~/projects/vault-enterprise$ vault kv get -mount=secret my-secret-1 ===== Secret Path ===== secret/data/my-secret-1 ======= Metadata ======= Key Value --- ----- created_time 2023-11-14T15:20:54.076052574Z custom_metadata <nil> deletion_time n/a destroyed false version 1 === Data === Key Value --- ----- baz buzz foo bar ``` Is the expectation that each key-value pair for `my-secret-1` would be a distinct name-value pair on GCP without any prefix or additional information, such as: ![gcp_secret](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/109547106/ae8861f0-a766-48d3-8af8-692911b3c616) If yes and this format removes all entropy from the secret name, are you worried about name collisions and what are your expectations if Vault tries to sync a secret, but the name already exists in your GCP project? Should the sync operation fail or Vault should take over and overwrite the existing value? | nia-potato: Hi @maxcoulombe Thanks for the update, i would worry about the name collision, but would assume that the secrets that are going to be sync'd from vault to google secret manager would only have 1 kv pair instead of multiple. (at least for my usecase, we are migrating existing google secret manager secrets to vault, then sync'd back to GSM so that secrets stay managed in vault, but sync'd to GSM to reduce code changes) However the current forced naming convention seems a bit aggressive in that if the user has a long path ie: `path/to/secret/in/path/subpath/secretname` Then the synced secret name would be `vault_<accessor_ID>/path/to/secret/in/path/subpath/secretname` However i believe the naming issue might be easier to address since we could just add a `-path` variable, then the final name would just be `vault_<accessor_id>/secretname` To address your original question, i think if we are going with the forced naming convention of pre-pending the accessor id, i dont think we will hit any naming collisions. But if the path moving forward is to remove that, and just let it have normal names + hashicorp_vault label, then i think the behavior should be fail the sync since we already detect it, then let the user delete from GSM and the sync should then succeed. thats just my two cents, open to suggestions. The naming issue we can currently live with, since it is just a long string, but not being able to sync the actual secret value to GSM properly has been blocking us for quite some time, since the final value that is being sync'd is `{"foo":"bar"}` instead of just `bar` if its a parsing error on GSM side let me know if you want to start a three way ticket with them so we can figure out why its blocking vault from parsing it incorrectly. | maxcoulombe: @nia-potato got it thanks for the details. I'm happy to report that we implemented a customizable name template option so people can decide on any pattern that suits their use case. We also plan to implement an option to "flatten" each Vault secret key into individual entries at the destination instead of encoding all KV pairs as a single JSON string on a single entry at the destination. This one is not implemented yet but is high on our priorities for the upcoming release. title: SSH: add `not_before` to precisely set validity window start timestamp
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
It is not possible to set validity window start to a specific value currently. This is because `not_before_duration` field accepts a duration to be set at configuration-time._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
`not_before` field should be added to accept an absolute timestamp._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
1. Add toggle to disable validity window. This would work for some use-cases but not for all._x000D_
2. Use special or large value to make `not_before_duration` work. This does not work currently because of underflow. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
1. Many air-gapped system without GPS and/or RTC bootup with their clocks set to Unix epoch. These cannot accept a validity window starting at `utc_now - not_before_duration`._x000D_
2. Certificates could be generated ahead-of-time for key rotation or other similar exercise with a future `not_before` date and remain invalid until rotation occurs._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
See https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/13608

title: SSH: accept a regex or pattern in allowed_users
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
`allowed_users` determines principals that a user could request when generating a certificate. It is not possible to know all principals that a user may need when configuring roles. This only accepts a catch-all wildcard `*`, fixed string or specific templated strings. This makes it impossible to create a role that could issue principals unknown at the time of configuration._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Make `allowed_users` support a regex or a simple pattern of fixed strings + wildcards. (e.g. `qwe-*-rty`)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
One could use `*` by itself but it is too permissive._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
A system could expect a unique principal that Vault cannot know ahead-of-time but could be configured to accept based on regex/pattern rule._x000D_

title: docs: MongoDB Atlas eventual consistency
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When requesting dynamic credentials using the MongoDB atlas database secrets engine, there is a delay from when the credential is provided to Vault and when the credential is accepted by the hosted cluster in the Atlas project. This behavior has been reviewed previously and discussed with MongoDB. They have confirmed it is working as designed and it's an eventual consistency model for how the Admin API propagates the credential to the hosted cluster._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Since this is a known behavior, I'd like to add a note the documentation page for the MongoDB atlas database secrets engine to notify so the end user is aware._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
It was considered once to include polling logic as part of the secrets engine so the user would only receive the credential when it was available, but that was decided against in this PR:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-mongodbatlas/issues/10_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
None_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
None_x000D_

title: /bin/kill (from procps) is a missing dependency of the Vault package
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The (Debian, likely RedHat as well) package for Vault uses `/bin/kill` for the `ExecReload` systemd service command:_x000D_
_x000D_
This is the service file:_x000D_
_x000D_
```ini_x000D_
systemctl cat vault_x000D_
# /lib/systemd/system/vault.service_x000D_
[Unit]_x000D_
Description="HashiCorp Vault - A tool for managing secrets"_x000D_
Documentation=https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs_x000D_
Requires=network-online.target_x000D_
After=network-online.target_x000D_
ConditionFileNotEmpty=/etc/vault.d/vault.hcl_x000D_
StartLimitIntervalSec=60_x000D_
StartLimitBurst=3_x000D_
_x000D_
[Service]_x000D_
Type=notify_x000D_
EnvironmentFile=/etc/vault.d/vault.env_x000D_
User=vault_x000D_
Group=vault_x000D_
ProtectSystem=full_x000D_
ProtectHome=read-only_x000D_
PrivateTmp=yes_x000D_
PrivateDevices=yes_x000D_
SecureBits=keep-caps_x000D_
AmbientCapabilities=CAP_IPC_LOCK_x000D_
CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_SYSLOG CAP_IPC_LOCK_x000D_
NoNewPrivileges=yes_x000D_
ExecStart=/usr/bin/vault server -config=/etc/vault.d/vault.hcl_x000D_
ExecReload=/bin/kill --signal HUP $MAINPID_x000D_
KillMode=process_x000D_
KillSignal=SIGINT_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The interesting line is `ExecReload=/bin/kill --signal HUP $MAINPID`. The command `/bin/kill` is not always available. This `/bin/kill` command comes from the package `procps` (Both Debian and RedHat)_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Make sure the package procps is not installed. Some containers don't have this package._x000D_
2. Run `apt install vault`, `dnf install vault` or `yum install vault`_x000D_
3. Run `systemctl reload vault`_x000D_
4. See error_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
A "normal" reload ._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`):_x000D_
```text_x000D_
vault --version_x000D_
Vault v1.15.2 (cf1b5cafa047bc8e4a3f93444fcb4011593b92cb), built 2023-11-06T11:33:28Z_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture:_x000D_
Debian (11) and RedHat (8), I guess any Debian and RedHat._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The package for vault should have a dependency on the package `procps` or the binary `/bin/kill`.

title: Add support for downloading pgp keys from GitHub
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Keybase, which vault can use to download pgp keys, has seen development pace slow down in the past few years and long term future of the project is not entirely clear._x000D_
At the same time it's very convenient to be able to use usernames during `operator init` or `operator rekey` workflows._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
I'd like to be able to pull keys from GitHub, in a similar they can be pulled from keybase._x000D_
GitHub exposes gpg key for each user under https://github.com/${user}.gpg. If we could do something like this it would be useful:_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault operator init -key-shares=5 -key-threshold=2 -pgp-keys="github:<github_user_1>,github:<github_user_2>..."_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_

title: auth/aws iam method sts request url constructed incorrectly
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The `aws` authentication method has a configuration option `STS Endpoint` and a login path with a `iam_request_url` parameter. The endpoint and parameter values are combined incorrectly to create the sts request url resulting in one or two trailing `/`s._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Create an `auth/aws` authentication method and configure the `STS Endpoint`: http://1.2.3.4:8888/_x000D_
Perform a login action against `auth/aws` providing a `iam_request_url` parameter with the base64 encoded version of: http://1.2.3.4:8888/_x000D_
_x000D_
Note that the URL used for the STS request is: http://1.2.3.4:8888/// (two trailing /s), due to:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.15.2/builtin/credential/aws/path_login.go#L1697-L1730_x000D_
_x000D_
i.e. endpoint has slash, pattern adds slash, uri is slash._x000D_
_x000D_
These values are just examples, you can use any endpoint with a trailing `/`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Build a correct target url, e.g.:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
	endpointUrl, _ := url.Parse(endpoint)_x000D_
	parsedUri, _ := url.Parse(parsedUrl.RequestURI())_x000D_
	targetUrl := endpointUrl.ResolveReference(parsedUri).String()_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
but with error handling._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): tested with 1.12.1 and 1.15.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): _x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture:_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The incorrect sts url does not (currently) cause a problem with AWS but may cause failures with other implementations of AWS apis.

title: Keycloak Authorization and Authentication by Client Roles
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Hey There. I'm trying to manage authentication and authorization to Vault through Keycloak and one of the requirements is that each team has a client and a client role associate, but this means that the ID Token that it is returned by keycloak cannot be (or rather I don't know how to..) parsed by  Vault in order to associate the proper identity groups to the User._x000D_
_x000D_
The setup is the following:_x000D_
_x000D_
Keycloak:_x000D_
```yaml_x000D_
Team A (Realm Client):_x000D_
 Roles (Client Role): _x000D_
   - owner_x000D_
   - reader_x000D_
 _x000D_
Team B (Realm Client):_x000D_
  Roles (Client Role):_x000D_
   - owner_x000D_
   - reader_x000D_
_x000D_
... and so on_x000D_
```_x000D_
The user has the `owner` role on `Team A` and `reader` on `Team B`. This will generate the following ID Token:_x000D_
```JSON_x000D_
{_x000D_
..._x000D_
    "resource_access":_x000D_
    {_x000D_
        "account":_x000D_
        {_x000D_
            "roles":_x000D_
            [_x000D_
                "manage-account",_x000D_
                "manage-account-links",_x000D_
                "view-profile"_x000D_
            ]_x000D_
        },_x000D_
        "team_a":_x000D_
        {_x000D_
            "roles":_x000D_
            [_x000D_
                "owner"_x000D_
            ]_x000D_
        },_x000D_
        "team_b":_x000D_
        {_x000D_
            "roles":_x000D_
            [_x000D_
                "reader"_x000D_
            ]_x000D_
        }_x000D_
    },_x000D_
..._x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
And I would like to have this user login with the default role and be associated with an Identity Group which has a policy that gives him permissions to do anything on `Team A` secret backend and another group with a policy that only allows this user to view and read `Team B` secret backend:_x000D_
```Yaml_x000D_

  - Role : "default"_x000D_
  - Groups: ["team_a_owner", "team_b_reader"]_x000D_

_x000D_
Is there any way to do this at the moment?_x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks in advance_x000D_

Be able to use JSON Object in order to attribute an Identity Group or enable the user to assume several roles at the same time._x000D_

None so far._x000D_

title: Stream large uploads to disk instead of reading everything into memory
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When given a large snapshot to restore, it seems Vault will read the entire snapshot into memory; from observation, memory consumption will be about 4 times the snapshot size. This leads to fun times when you restore a ~30Gb snapshot on a machine with 64Gb of memory due to the vault process being OOM-killed. Adding swap space alleviates the problem but slows things down to a speed that'd bore a snail to death._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
For any upload larger than, say, a few Gb, stream the request body to a temporary file and move that into the right location once the request completes. If this is already the case (unsure since I don't read go code for breakfast) then reducing the memory consumption should be a thing. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
No alternatives ;)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Snapshots, really..._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
It's considered bad form to read a large request body into memory, most (if not all) frameworks support switching to using a temporary file on disk if a request is larger than a configured size, so unsure why this isn't already done. If it is done, unsure as to why vault will use that much memory. The actual application of the snapshot once it's uploaded takes next to no resources. _x000D_

title: agent log filename - disable timestamp/rotation
body_text:
Many Java applications like to color outside the standard lines and control the entire lifecycle of their own log files - from how they're named, to when (time, size, startup, etc) the files are rotated etc. It's frustrating from a SEIM and system management perspective to deal with a bunch of different ways that log files are managed, catering to this or that specific application's specialness. It appears as if vault agent when told explicitly to write to a log file - is doing a similar thing[1]:_x000D_
_x000D_
> [`-log-file`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/agent#_log_file) - writes all the Vault agent log messages to a file. This value is used as a prefix for the log file name. **The current timestamp is appended to the file name.**_x000D_
_x000D_
(emphasis mine)_x000D_
_x000D_
This forced dynamic filename removes our ability to always have one single log file with a consistent filename, which makes it much harder to use log aggregation tools and prevents log rotation tools (ie logrotate) from operating properly without a bunch of nonsense._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Because windows (unix uses syslog automatically), the solution I'd like is to be able to turn off the dynamic naming, and disable vault's built-in log rotation. I would like for vault to do only one thing with the logs - write them to the same file always and let me handle everything else related to the file's lifecycle._x000D_
_x000D_
While I appreciate the option to have vault automatically name the log files dynamically, and the built-in rotation mechanism, I strongly prefer to do this myself. It's much, much easier to point Splunk, Datadog, etc at a single always-named-the-same file like `vault.log`, and this also makes sure that `logrotate` can do its job without something else competing._x000D_
_x000D_
When dealing with log files, we prefer to use a single tool - logrotate - leveraging a single, well-known configuration language/syntax to handle log rotation needs. We're able to use logrotate on both unix and windows[2] with the same config language._x000D_
_x000D_
We already use syslog on our unix boxes, and that is handled very nicely without any additional vault logging config, just a couple of rsyslog filtering rules. The place I'm having a hard time is vault windows agents because it is necessary to explicitly define the logging target file in the agent config so that it writes logs to the disk at all._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
If there is a way to get the vault agent to instead write its logs to the Windows Event subsystem, I would be happy to consider such an alternative. If this is possible, the logs are handled via the windows Events, which have their own way of being monitored by log aggregators and rotated as part of the event subsystem without having to rely on the specific application's config (ie vault) for this._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
[1] https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/agent#_log_file_x000D_
[2] https://sourceforge.net/projects/logrotatewin/

title: Vault performance standby nodes are not honoring `X-Vault-No-Request-Forwarding` header
body_text:

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

-->

**Describe the bug**

👋  Hello, I was testing vault performance standby (https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/enterprise/performance-standbys) and wanted to verify the read requests are processed by the performance standby node.

Following https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/ha#request-forwarding documentation:

`If X-Vault-No-Request-Forwarding header in the request is set to a non-empty value, the standby nodes will redirect the client using a 307 status code to the active node's redirect address.`

My understanding is that if I'm using this header, it would allow me to confirm if the requests are handled by the node or redirected as the request transparent forwarding is disabled in favor of an HTTP redirection.


I tested reading a secret on both a performance standby node (with vault enterprise license) and a standby node (OSS version of vault), this is the result:

- Enterprise performance standby node: HTTP 200 with secret content
- OSS standby node: HTTP/2 307 redirection to the vault leader address

Which is what I expected, and confirmed this header is working.

What I don't understand is when I try writing a secret (kv2 secret), with the same header, I get the following result:

- Enterprise performance standby node: HTTP 200 with secret metadatas returned - secret was updated correctly.
- OSS standby node: HTTP/2 307 redirection to the vault leader address


I'm confused as I understood that the performance standby cannot handle write requests (based on t[he performance standby documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/enterprise/performance-standbys)). Is it not honoring the header or is it processing requests? 


**To Reproduce**
 1. Create a vault enterprise cluster with a standby node
 2. Enable secret kv2 engine and add a dummy secret
 3. Run `curl --header "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" --request POST --data @payload.json --header "X-Vault-No-Request-Forwarding: true"  https://${HOSTNAME}:8200/v1/secret-kv2/data/apps/shaeli/_testing` on the standby node
 4. Get an HTTP 200 instead of a HTTP 307

**Expected behavior**

I expected a HTTP 307 instead of 200 when doing write requests with the `X-Vault-No-Request-Forwarding` header on a vault enterprise performance standby node.

title: Malformed Response Header from the KMIP Secrets Engine for a KMIP 1.0 Request

Since the tag is introduced only since KMIP 1.4 specification, such a response breaks message decoding in the KMIP 1.0 client, which considers `ServerCorrelationValue` as an unknown tag._x000D_
Please see an excerpt from the Vault log in the `Additional context` section at the end of the bug report._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Configure KMIP Secrets Engine as described in the [documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/adp/kmip-engine)_x000D_
2. [Install](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server-for-mongodb/6.0/install/yum.html) Percona Server for MongoDB_x000D_
3. Run Percona Server for MongoDB exactly as MongoDB is being launched in the [documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/adp/kmip-engine#kmip-client-configuration)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
No `ServerCorrelationValue` in the response header for protocol versions below 1.4_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`):  1.15.2+ent_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.15.2+ent_x000D_

_x000D_

```_x000D_

**Additional context**_x000D_

```_x000D_

  object=_x000D_
  |_x000D_
  |_x000D_
  | Tag: RequestMessage_x000D_
  |   Type: Structure_x000D_

title: Support Azure multi-tenant app registrations for OIDC authentication
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Azure app registrations support different account types (see [Quickstart: Register an application with the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app#register-an-application) for some background on Microsoft identity platform apps and [Tenancy in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/single-and-multi-tenant-apps) for tenancy definitions). Vault currently only supports *single-tenant* Azure app registrations (see **Accounts in this organizational directory only** for more details). _x000D_
_x000D_
Attempting to register a *multi-tenant* app registration (see **Accounts in any organizational directory** or **Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts** for more details) results in the following on the CLI:_x000D_
_x000D_
```shell-session_x000D_
$ vault write auth/azure/config default_role=default_role oidc_discovery_url=https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0                                                               _x000D_
Error writing data to auth/azure/config: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT http://localhost:8200/v1/auth/azure/config_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* error checking oidc discovery URL_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
and the following in the Vault log:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2023-12-01T05:58:22.087Z [ERROR] auth.jwt.auth_jwt_a2e50c0a: error checking oidc discovery URL: error="issuer did not match the returned issuer, expected \"https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0\" got \"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantid}/v2.0\""_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The only solution to this problem is to have each tenant individually create a single-tenant app registration to be used to configure a Vault auth method._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Add support for Azure multi-tenant issuer validation as described in [Update your code to handle multiple issuer values](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-convert-app-to-be-multi-tenant#update-your-code-to-handle-multiple-issuer-values), and more specifically, [Validate the issuer - Multi-tenant applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/access-tokens#multi-tenant-applications)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Some applications, e.g., [oauth2-proxy](https://github.com/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy/blob/fc6e7fdbd11f979de2c4e5c1d3d7eb8b214566be/docs/docs/configuration/overview.md?plain=1#L132C62-L132C62),  have a flag to skip issuer verification when configuring an auth provider. The [coreos/go-oidc](https://github.com/coreos/go-oidc) repo that Vault relies on via [hashicorp/cap](https://github.com/hashicorp/cap) already accommodates this (see [`oidc.go`](https://github.com/coreos/go-oidc/blob/6d6be43e852de391805e5a5bc14146ba3cdd4195/oidc/oidc.go#L68-L85)). Being able to relax the issuer verification might be sufficient for some deployments.

title: Issue with processing comma values in framework.TypeCommaStringSlice
body_text:
We are currently facing an issue with the HashiCorp Vault SDK, specifically related to the processing of comma values inside `framework.TypeCommaStringSlice`._x000D_
_x000D_
In our implementation using the Vault SDK Framework, we are setting custom fields using the following code snippet: [Link to code](https://github.com/Venafi/vault-pki-backend-venafi/blob/master/plugin/pki/path_venafi_cert_enroll.go#L69-L72) (Venafi code).  The problem arises when we send comma-separated values inside a string that is already comma-separated. The Vault SDK splits these values, which is not the desired behavior. Here is HashiCorp Vault SDK code for field_type:  https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/sdk/framework/field_type.go_x000D_
_x000D_
**Example Payload:**_x000D_
```_x000D_
{_x000D_
    "csr": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST----- ... o9JHgoS08vaUisd7\nOZPoXsqUv7B4eYKjuQ==\n-----END CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----",_x000D_
    "custom_fields": "'custom=vaultTest,bob@venafi.com,alice@venafi.com',cfList=item2,cfListMulti=tier1,cfListMulti=tier4"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
### In Golang code_x000D_
_x000D_
**Current Result:** _x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
customFields -> [ 'custom=vaultTest bob@venafi.com alice@venafi.com' cfList=item2 cfListMulti=tier1 cfListMulti=tier4 ]_x000D_
```_x000D_
This is a list of strings with the following values:_x000D_
_x000D_
- `'custom=vaultTest`_x000D_
- `bob@venafi.com`_x000D_
- `alice@venafi.com'`_x000D_
- `cfList=item2`_x000D_
- `cfListMulti=tier1`_x000D_
- `cfListMulti=tier4`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Desired Result:** _x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
customFields -> [ custom=vaultTest,bob@venafi.com,alice@venafi.com cfList=item2 cfListMulti=tier1 cfListMulti=tier4 ]_x000D_
```_x000D_
Then the list of strings would hold the following values:_x000D_
_x000D_
- `custom=vaultTest,bob@venafi.com,alice@venafi.com`_x000D_
- `cfList=item2`_x000D_
- `cfListMulti=tier1`_x000D_
- `cfListMulti=tier4`_x000D_

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
After upgrading to Vault 1.15.3 I am still observing "event not processed by enough 'sink' nodes" errors in our Vault log. #23871 has partially fixed the problem, however it only addresses audit responses and not audit requests. Is there a similar fix to apply for audit requests too?_x000D_

  error=_x000D_

  | \t* timeout: context canceled_x000D_
  | _x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
TBC - I'm going to see if I can reproduce it in a clean dev Vault install._x000D_
_x000D_

No error message._x000D_
_x000D_

Starting in Vault 1.15.0, a different framework is used to publish audit log records (for both request and response) to their various Audit Devices (which is what 'sink' is referring to in the error). This new framework will return an error if the request deadline has been exceed (tracked by the context); whereas the old framework did not check if the deadline had been exceeded before writing the audit record. The API response was the same though, an error would be returned because the request took too long to service. The difference being that in 1.15.x, the response audit record is missing from the Audit Devices and the server logs include the above mentioned error; contrasted with < 1.15.x, where there was a response audit record showing the error returned to the API client written to the Audit Devices and no error in the server logs. | marcboudreau: Quick update: as of Vault 1.15.4, a change was introduce to avoid this exact issue. A new context with a fresh timeout value of 5 seconds is used to publish the response audit log record to the Audit Devices, so Value should now exhibit the same behaviour as prior to 1.15.0 when the context deadline has been reached while processing a request, which is that the response audit log will be written and will show the error that was sent back to the client.

title: v1/sys/metrics on standby redirects with HTTP 307, i. e. no forward
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I have 3 oss vault-instance cluster with raft storage. Only one can be a leader, others are followers._x000D_
And I want to monitor this cluster with prometheus using `/v1/sys/metrics?format=prometheus`._x000D_
Here is a problem I faced with:_x000D_
Followers redirect `/v1/sys/metrics` to leader with HTTP 307. Not sure why it happens, but the documentation is misleading here. [It says](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/v1.15.x/concepts/ha#request-forwarding) redirect is old fallback behavior. If this is expected, then HA doc page should be updated to reflect that for some endpoints you will always get redirects instead of forwarding. Others endpoints do forward, not redirect in my case._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Create 3 vault instance: HOST1, HOST2 and HOST3._x000D_
Use this config on each of them._x000D_
Replace HOST_N with the IP of the host where the config is used._x000D_
Replace HOST_1, HOST_2 and HOST_3 with the IP addresses of these 3 instances._x000D_

title: Enhancement for KV Engine UI Behavior
body_text:
### **Problem Description**_x000D_
Our current challenge arises from a functionality change in the KV engine. The system detects nested JSON by checking for "{}" in KV values. However, our randomly generated values occasionally include these characters, leading to unintended behavior. The UI currently reveals more secrets on the screen than necessary, posing a security risk. We aim to maintain the default UI state of "hidden/unhidden" to minimize this exposure._x000D_
_x000D_
### **Proposed Solution**_x000D_
We suggest two potential solutions:_x000D_
1. Introduce a UI setting in the KV engine configuration to control the default view state._x000D_
2. Temporarily revert to the previous UI behavior, allowing the radio button for "hidden/unhidden" state to be toggleable and not permanently greyed out._x000D_
_x000D_
### **Alternative Considered**_x000D_
We could update our value generation process to avoid "{}" sequences, but this would require significant code modifications. As of version 1.15.4, this issue remains unresolved._x000D_
_x000D_
### **Additional Use-Cases**_x000D_
This change is crucial for enhancing security. The current UI behavior poses a risk in scenarios where screen contents might be observed by others, such as during team demonstrations or walkthroughs. The "hide/unhide" feature in the KV engine is vital for maintaining confidentiality._x000D_
_x000D_
### **Context and References**_x000D_
Relevant Commit: [f42d50826fb0129bc54903532192e1e96a352b8b](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/commit/f42d50826fb0129bc54903532192e1e96a352b8b)_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Identity group should support multiple aliases - as entity does
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Identity groups only support a single alias per group, which makes an extra overhead when providing multiple auth source which all uses the same IdP at the end (one ldap and one oidc for ex). Right now, providing two identity group alias with same name but different mount accessor will only keep the latest._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault write identity/group-alias name=MyGroup mount_accessor=auth_oidc_6b9ba80d canonical_id=e1f10bdb-c22a-f42c-e188-a9c005e3fef1v_x000D_
$ vault read identity/group-alias/id/xxxx < id from previous command output, OK_x000D_
$ vault write identity/group-alias name=MyGroup mount_accessor=auth_jwt_65f53ce1 canonical_id=e1f10bdb-c22a-f42c-e188-a9c005e3fef1  # same canonical id, different mount_accessors_x000D_
$ vault read identity/group-alias/id/yyyyy < id from previous command, OK_x000D_
$ vault read identity/group-alias/id/xxxx < id from first command >> KO, doesn't exist anymore  <<_x000D_
```_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Entity already support multiple aliases, Group should have the same behaviour and allow multiple aliases with same name but different mount accessors (so, auth source)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.14.5_x000D_

There are multiple 👍 on the comments in the PR, but it seems to have lost momentum after the indecision as to whether it belongs in the `api` or `sdk`. Thanks!
banks: @james0209 thanks for that context - that other PR isn't something I'd come across yet! I agree it's unfortunate that a helper of that kind that encodes canonical behavior that many tools might want to share is not importable. I'll see what I can do to resolve the direction around that as it seems useful to many in the eco-system and should remove an incentive for vault module imports.
banks: I'm going to keep pushing #9786 as I think it's pretty close to being something we can merge and solve that reason to import vault at least. I'm also going to close this for now because a) this is not supposed to be a supported way to use Vault code and b) we should be releasing a new api package version in the next week or two anyway. If others have additional context for why they might still choose to import Vault feel free to let us know or open other issues to resolve those issues and avoid the need for the import.

title: Add Login MFA support for Okta TOTP
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I need to require MFA (on login) for all my users using Okta as the Idp and without enabling Okta push verification._x000D_

My organization prohibits the use of Okta Push, but Okta Login MFA only supports push verification, so I can't use Login MFA as it is today._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Add Support for Okta's TOTP factors to Login MFA, similar to the how Duo Login MFA supports both push and passcodes._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
1. **Okta Auth method**: The Okta Auth method has partial support for using TOTP, but only if using the CLI to login; The UI does not support Okta TOTP with the Okta Auth method. So, I can't use the Okta Auth method to enable MFA._x000D_
2. **Okta via OIDC Auth method**: I tried to use the OIDC auth method, but OIDC limits logins to machines with a browser. So, I cannot login with OIDC on the CLI of a remote VM._x000D_
3. **Login MFA w/ builtin TOTP method**: I have to support several vault clusters, so requiring all users to setup the TOTP method for each Vault cluster is onerous and error prone._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
My users must use MFA when logging into vault, whether they are logging in locally (via UI or CLI) or remotely (via CLI). My company uses Okta as our Idp and for MFA._x000D_

PR submitted: #24563_x000D_

title: "publishNotReadyAddresses: false" Prevents new vault nodes from joining raft.

**Describe the bug**_x000D_

2. We want to scale our vault up to 5 pods from 3 to reduce the possibility of losing quorum and vault if a single node reboots._x000D_
_x000D_

title: Cassandra backend does not respect the configured consistency level on initial connection
body_text:
While attempting to leverage AWS Keyspaces (Apache Cassandra compatible serverless implementation) as a backend, Vault is unable to establish an initial connection. When the connection is initially established, the consistency level is hard coded to `Quorum` for the connection and then is updated _after_ the connection is established._x000D_
_x000D_
AWS Kesyspaces only supports the following consistency levels:_x000D_
 * ONE_x000D_
 * LOCAL_ONE_x000D_
 * LOCAL_QUORUM_x000D_
_x000D_
During the setup of the connection, the Cassandra backend verifies that the consistency is set and defaults to `LOCAL_QUORUM` which _is_ supported by AWS Keyspaces however that default consistency is not passed to the `gocql` driver prior to starting the session. If the consistency is not passed to `gocql` prior to initialization, the client defaults to `QUORUM` which is not supported._x000D_
_x000D_
The configured consistency is validated with the `cassandra.go` physical package:_x000D_
```go_x000D_
           if cs, ok := conf["consistency"]; ok {_x000D_
		switch cs {_x000D_
		case "ANY":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.Any_x000D_
		case "ONE":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.One_x000D_
		case "TWO":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.Two_x000D_
		case "THREE":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.Three_x000D_
		case "QUORUM":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.Quorum_x000D_
		case "ALL":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.All_x000D_
		case "LOCAL_QUORUM":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.LocalQuorum_x000D_
		case "EACH_QUORUM":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.EachQuorum_x000D_
		case "LOCAL_ONE":_x000D_
			consistency = gocql.LocalOne_x000D_
		default:_x000D_
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("'consistency' must be one of {ANY, ONE, TWO, THREE, QUORUM, ALL, LOCAL_QUORUM, EACH_QUORUM, LOCAL_ONE}")_x000D_
		}_x000D_
	}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
After validation however, the session is established _prior_ to setting the consistency level within the gocql client:_x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
        connectStart := time.Now()_x000D_
	cluster := gocql.NewCluster(hosts...)_x000D_
	cluster.Port = port_x000D_
	cluster.Keyspace = keyspace_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
	sess, err := cluster.CreateSession()_x000D_
	if err != nil {_x000D_
		return nil, err_x000D_
	}_x000D_
	metrics.MeasureSince([]string{"cassandra", "connect"}, connectStart)_x000D_
	sess.SetConsistency(consistency)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Within the `gocql` driver used for the underlying connection, the Consitency is defaulted to `Quorum` if it is not set *prior* to calling `CreateSession`: _x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
func NewCluster(hosts ...string) *ClusterConfig {_x000D_
	cfg := &ClusterConfig{_x000D_
		Hosts:                  hosts,_x000D_
		CQLVersion:             "3.0.0",_x000D_
		Timeout:                600 * time.Millisecond,_x000D_
		ConnectTimeout:         600 * time.Millisecond,_x000D_
		Port:                   9042,_x000D_
		NumConns:               2,_x000D_
		Consistency:            Quorum,_x000D_
		MaxPreparedStmts:       defaultMaxPreparedStmts,_x000D_
		MaxRoutingKeyInfo:      1000,_x000D_
		PageSize:               5000,_x000D_
		DefaultTimestamp:       true,_x000D_
		MaxWaitSchemaAgreement: 60 * time.Second,_x000D_
		ReconnectInterval:      60 * time.Second,_x000D_
		ConvictionPolicy:       &SimpleConvictionPolicy{},_x000D_
		ReconnectionPolicy:     &ConstantReconnectionPolicy{MaxRetries: 3, Interval: 1 * time.Second},_x000D_
		WriteCoalesceWaitTime:  200 * time.Microsecond,_x000D_
	}_x000D_
	return cfg_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Create a basic configuration for Vault that uses an AWS Keyspaces table:_x000D_
  ```hcl_x000D_
ui            = true_x000D_
cluster_addr  = "http://127.0.0.1:8201"_x000D_
