title: Vault agent can DOS vault server if template suffers I/O errors
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
We recently suffered a self-inflicted DOS attack on our Vault server. Investigation revealed that it was our own vault agents embedded in our own system container images that hammered our server after a permission refactoring on a file the vault agent templates read went wrong._x000D_
_x000D_
It seems that in the case of I/O errors while rendering templates, the vault agent does not pause and back off when retrying. If the vault-agent needed to make any Vault API requests to the server as part of rendering the template, that means such API requests are retried in a tight loop with no back-off, leading to a "thundering herd" DOS type scenario._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
On Linux the steps are:_x000D_
_x000D_
In the first terminal, start a vault dev server: `vault server -dev`_x000D_
_x000D_
In a second terminal, launch a tcpdump to watch for traffic to the dev server: `sudo tcpdump -i lo dst host 127.0.0.1 and dst port 8200`_x000D_
_x000D_
Write the dev server's root token to a file: `echo -n TOKEN > /tmp/.vault-token`_x000D_
_x000D_
Write /tmp/agent-config.hcl as follows:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
auto_auth {_x000D_
    method "token_file" {_x000D_
        config = {_x000D_
            token_file_path = "/tmp/.vault-token"_x000D_
        }_x000D_
    }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
template {_x000D_
    source      = "/tmp/template.ctmpl"_x000D_
    destination = "/tmp/dest"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Write /tmp/template.ctmpl as follows:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
{{ with secret "pki/issue/foo" (printf "common_name=%s" (file "/nonexistent")) -}}_x000D_
{{ .Data.private_key }}_x000D_
{{ end }}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
In a third terminal, launch the vault-agent with `export VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8200; vault agent -config /tmp/agent-config.hcl`._x000D_
_x000D_
The vault agent will spew reams and reams of output as the template fails over and over due to the nonexistent file it is trying to read._x000D_
_x000D_
Switch back to the tcpdump terminal. You will see reams and reams of packets flying to the dev server._x000D_
_x000D_
As an aside, it is curious that the vault agent communicated with the vault server at all while evaluating the given template. If it was unable to read the nonexistent file, it wouldn't know what "common_name" should be, and wouldn't be in a position to even know what API request to make._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
I would expect the agent to retry with a back-off similar to how the agent retries failing requests to the Vault server._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with vault status): 1.15.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with vault version): 1.15.4_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux x86_64

Setting an API limit on the Vault API inside the vault server itself did not really help, we had to do the rate limiting on a firewall level.

title: Vault agent telemetry should provide metrics on template errors
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
As I am planning to build out usage of Vault agent to our production servers, I realise how important it is to be able to monitor the correct functioning of the agents. If an agent fails to render a template, or lacks permissions to the relevant vault secrets, it may mean that our production servers silently run with outdated configuration or credentials._x000D_
_x000D_
In addition, we build container images as part of our CI toolchain. These images have a vault agent embedded into them. Currently we have no robust way to programmaticaly check if the vault agent runs correctly, if the templates have syntax errors, etc., so that we can highlight these errors in our toolchain. Due to https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/24657 I am especially keen to not let broken vault agent configs escape CI ever again._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
A sophisticated solution would be to emit multiple metrics, one for each destination file name, with a gauge that is 0 if that template failed, and 1 if it succeeded. Something like:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault.agent.template.status{dest='/etc/ssl/private/acme.key'} = 0_x000D_
vault.agent.template.status{dest='/etc/ssh/known-hosts'} = 1_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This more sophisticated approach would allow a monitoring system to create alerts that give support staff an idea of what server functionality is likely to be affected._x000D_
_x000D_
A simpler approach be to just add a simple gauge `vault.agent.template.error` that counts the number of templates that failed to render during the most recent run. If the problems are transient, then this number will decrease when the templates are re-run. While you are at it, a `vault.agent.template.success` gauge would be useful too._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
I considered scraping the agent log output for error messages. But that means I would need to build up a regex for how template errors look like in the log file. There is always the risk that my regex does not cover a certain class of errors I did not anticipate, or that future changes to the agent logging code breaks the regex._x000D_
_x000D_
An alternative would be to scrape the agent log file for the number of template successes, and count if I see the expected number. But that requires the code that does the counting to know in advance how many templates there are in the config file, and this count can easily get out of date as the agent config is refactored._x000D_
_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: pieter-lautus: I proposed above that the metric should be a gauge (0 means last template run failed, 1 means it succeeded). This is different from the existing metrics that are counters. For example, `vault.agent.auth.success` counts the number of times auth has succeeded since startup. The gauges as I suggested are more useful than the counters. I am currently struggling to figure out how I am supposed to use the existing `vault.agent.auth.success` and `vault.agent.auth.failure` metrics to implement monitoring that answers the question "which vault agents are currently not authenticated to the vault?". The only way that I can see to do so is to figure out which of the two counters most recently changed - if the failure metric was most recently incremented, the vault agent is in an error state. But such a query - if it is even possible in PromQL - would be horrible expensive, because it would require scanning backwards across the time series for the two metrics to find the point in time when the metric flipped. Much more useful would have been a `vault.agent.auth.status` metric that tells me whether the agent is *currently* authenticated. The same reasoning applies to the new metrics I propose here.

title: Incorrect processing of sinks `aad_env_var` with proxy/agent
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
As [documented](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/autoauth#auto-auth-examples), sinks can be provided two ways using HCL:_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
auto_auth {_x000D_
  sinks {_x000D_
    sink {_x000D_
    }_x000D_
   }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
or_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
auto_auth {_x000D_
  sink {_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
When there is an outer `sinks` block, the `aad_env_var` field is never processed.  This processing is handled in `parseSinks`.  However, with the outer `sinks` block, `parseSinks` immediately returns because `sinkList` is empty (since it's filtering on "sink" not "sinks")._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/ec584a271e484271116cafc16e76d9bd311d53ed/command/proxy/config/config.go#L792-L797_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/ec584a271e484271116cafc16e76d9bd311d53ed/command/proxy/config/config.go#L832-L835_x000D_
_x000D_
The same issue is seen in the agent code._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
This issue is difficult to reproduce and identify unless you have corresponding code to process the encrypted tokens with additional authenticated data (AAD) as described [here](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/autoauth#encrypting-tokens):_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Run `vault proxy -config ...` with an `auto_auth` config in the first format described above and using the `aad_env_var` setting (as well as `dh_type` and `dh_path`)_x000D_
2. The `encrypted_payload` provided in the sink file will not decrypt properly using the AAD value in the provided environment variable_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The `aad_env_var` setting is honored using both documented methods of providing sinks._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.15.4_x000D_

_x000D_
We run Vault for years without any big configuration changes on 3 EC2 instances in an Autoscaling group with an ALB in front of it and DynamoDB as the storage backend._x000D_
_x000D_
Before the version upgrade, we never experienced issues with a provisioned write capacity of 20 with Autoscaling enabled to 100._x000D_
Now after the upgrade, we have regular spikes to several hundred. So we increased the provisioned write capacity to 50 and allow autoscaling to 1000 but the autoscaling is too slow so we have a service interruption on every spike._x000D_
_x000D_
![image](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/6483939/5c06aec1-af2e-4c6d-b880-8477a201aec6)_x000D_

  region = "eu-central-1"_x000D_
  table  = "xxxxxxxxxxx"_x000D_
  max_parallel = "25"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
but it didn't improve the write usage._x000D_
_x000D_
We already set `log_level = "trace"` but didn't yet found a trigger for the spike._x000D_
Maybe its a background task?_x000D_
_x000D_
The DynamoDB table is not that big. Item count: 148,682, Table size: 68.6 megabytes_x000D_
6 Kubernetes clusters are connected, 4 of them with Consul PKI._x000D_
Vault client count: 247_x000D_
_x000D_
during such a spike, which takes up to an hour, the following keys of the DynamoDB table are accessed_x000D_
![image](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/6483939/1227c5c6-988f-400d-8434-3e9809c9b234)_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
No spikes in write usage, or at least some log messages to get an idea of whats happening at this time._x000D_
Respecting max_parallel setting in DynamoDB storage config_x000D_

[This discussion](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/monitoring-vault-seal-status/46413/6) hinted that it may be due to the `prometheus_retention_time` config field. _x000D_
Increasing it does make the metric stick around longer, but only until the retention time elapses. When the seal status does change, the metric comes back, and alerting can kick in, but in the meantime our dashboards and alerts show "no data", which is not ideal._x000D_

**Describe the bug**_x000D_

**To Reproduce**_x000D_

title: Vault ignored Basic Constraints extension specified in CSR during issuance
body_text:
**Describtion**_x000D_
When I try to use `/pki_int/sign-verbatim` endpoint to sign a new certificate based upon the provided CSR with added `basicConstraints=critical,CA:false`, I get the following warning in request response:_x000D_
  `warnings":["specified CSR contained a Basic Constraints extension that was ignored during issuance"]`_x000D_
_x000D_
The issued cert has no any basic constrains. _x000D_
_x000D_
According to Openssl documentation  (see https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.1.1/man5/x509v3_config.html) for some application it is required to have  `basicConstraints=critical,CA:false` in case of end-entity certificate but vault ignore explicitly provide constrains._x000D_
_x000D_
> _x000D_
> Basic Constraints._x000D_
> _x000D_
> This is a multi valued extension which indicates whether a certificate is a CA certificate. The first (mandatory) name is CA followed by TRUE or FALSE. If CA is TRUE then an optional pathlen name followed by an non-negative value can be included._x000D_
> _x000D_
> For example:_x000D_
>  basicConstraints=CA:TRUE_x000D_
>  basicConstraints=CA:FALSE_x000D_
>  basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE, pathlen:0_x000D_
> _x000D_
> A CA certificate must include the basicConstraints value with the CA field set to TRUE. An end user certificate must either set CA to FALSE or exclude the extension entirely. Some software may require the inclusion of basicConstraints with CA set to FALSE for end entity certificates. _x000D_
_x000D_
Perhaps in case of `/pki_int/sign-verbatim` there should be parameter similar to [`use_csr_values`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#use_csr_values) as for `/pki_int/root/sign-intermediate`._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Perform first 2 steps from https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/secrets-management/pki-engine_x000D_
2. Run `openssl genrsa -out end-entity-pk.pem 4096`_x000D_
3. Run _x000D_
```_x000D_
openssl req \_x000D_
    -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:false" \_x000D_
    -new -sha256 -key end-entity-pk.pem \_x000D_
    -subj "/C=/L=/O=/OU=/CN=foo" \_x000D_
    -out end-entity-cert.csr_x000D_
```_x000D_
4. Run_x000D_
```_x000D_
cat > payload.json<<EOF_x000D_
{_x000D_
    "format":"pem",_x000D_
    "csr":"$(sed ':a;N;$!ba;s/\n/\\n/g' end-entity-cert.csr)",_x000D_
    "ttl":"180d"_x000D_
}_x000D_
EOF_x000D_
_x000D_
curl \_x000D_
    --header "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" \_x000D_
    --request POST \_x000D_
    --data @payload.json \_x000D_
    $VAULT_ADDR/v1/pki_int/sign-verbatim_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Issued certificate contains the following:_x000D_
```_x000D_
X509v3 Basic Constraints critical:_x000D_
CA:FALSE_x000D_
```

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Since terraform doesn't support auto-tidy in the official module, I created a small module to enable it:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
terraform {_x000D_
  required_version = ">= 1.4.0"_x000D_
  required_providers {_x000D_
    vault = {_x000D_

      version = ">= 3.18.0"_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
resource "vault_generic_endpoint" "pki-auto-tidy" {_x000D_
  path = "${var.pki_path}/config/auto-tidy"_x000D_
  ignore_absent_fields = true_x000D_
  disable_delete       = true_x000D_
  data_json = jsonencode({_x000D_
    enabled                                  = var.enabled_x000D_
    interval_duration                        = var.interval_duration_x000D_
    maintain_stored_certificate_counts       = var.maintain_stored_certificate_counts_x000D_
    publish_stored_certificate_count_metrics = var.publish_stored_certificate_count_metrics_x000D_
  })_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
you can easily guess at the vars in place. _x000D_
_x000D_
When applying the module though, I receive the following error:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
│ Error: error writing to Vault: Error making API request._x000D_
│ _x000D_
│ URL: PUT https://myvault/v1/pki/config/auto-tidy_x000D_
│ Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
│ _x000D_
│ * Auto-tidy enabled but no tidy operations were requested. Enable at least one tidy operation to be run (tidy_cert_store / tidy_revoked_certs / tidy_revoked_cert_issuer_associations / tidy_expired_issuers / tidy_move_legacy_ca_bundle / tidy_revocation_queue / tidy_cross_cluster_revoked_certs / tidy_acme)._x000D_
│ _x000D_
│   with module.auto_tidy.vault_generic_endpoint.pki-auto-tidy,_x000D_
│   on ../../../modules/auto-tidy/main.tf line 26, in resource "vault_generic_endpoint" "pki-auto-tidy":_x000D_
│   26: resource "vault_generic_endpoint" "pki-auto-tidy" {_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I looked around for the error, and it seems to not be documented at all, so I had a run at the code instead. _x000D_
_x000D_
The line triggering the error is https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/7049ce027ea20da1c60c749cf6720c40ff188c6d/builtin/logical/pki/path_tidy.go#L831_x000D_
_x000D_
It gets triggered by a check, config.IsAnyTidyEnabled() from here: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/7049ce027ea20da1c60c749cf6720c40ff188c6d/builtin/logical/pki/path_tidy.go#L102_x000D_
_x000D_
it essentially checks for the following settings, with at least one needing to be enabled:_x000D_
`tc.CertStore || tc.RevokedCerts || tc.IssuerAssocs || tc.ExpiredIssuers || tc.BackupBundle || tc.TidyAcme || tc.CrossRevokedCerts || tc.RevocationQueue`_x000D_
_x000D_
The defaults are all disabled, see https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/7049ce027ea20da1c60c749cf6720c40ff188c6d/builtin/logical/pki/path_tidy.go#L110_x000D_
_x000D_
This means we'd need to enable some of these first I suppose. The issue is with both the lacking documentation and the error itself, why can I not simply have auto-tidy enabled, and never run if none of these settings are enabled, until they are?_x000D_
_x000D_
Docs I checked and didn't find any mention of this requirement: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#set-automatic-tidy-configuration_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
see above_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
- Fix documentation, _x000D_
- allow for enabling auto-tidy and simply not triggering it when none of the tidy actions are enabled._x000D_
- If this is a warning and not an error, code 400 needs to be updated to something "friendlier" from the 2xx range.  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
1.14ent_x000D_
_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture:_x000D_
Linux x86_64_x000D_

title: Allow multiple aliases for the same (entity, mount_accessor) tuple
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
For some auth methods (e.g. Kerberos) multiple AuthN identities (someuser@REALM1 and someusere@REALM2) may map to the same AuthZ identity (someuser). With the current uniqueness constraint in place, we're forced to create duplicate entities, even though they don't differ at all._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Remove the (entity, mount_accessor) uniqueness constraint (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/bc9be554cb4cc991a4e8d4bc806751cb4609c984/vault/identity_store_aliases.go#L303-L307). I don't see any benefit to it, or harm in removing it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
- Maintain multiple duplicate entities, which is error prone, complicates audit queries, and artificially drives up license usage_x000D_
- Do identity mapping in a custom auth plugin (which is what we do now, but we'd rather retire our custom code)

hashishaw: @Garagoth no, after the fix #25766 (which is also in 1.16.2 as you stated) there are no updates needed for the default policy, as the UI was updated to always call the resultant-acl endpoint in the user's relative root namespace, where they should already have the default policy applied.

hashishaw: @Garagoth the resultant-acl block in the default policy was [added in 1.10](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/4386). It is an internal path because the format may change at any time # based on how the internal ACL features and capabilities change. path "sys/internal/ui/resultant-acl" { capabilities = ["read"] } ``` Adding the block or updating to the latest default will have the added benefit of allowing the UI to work better, only showing nav links to things that the logged in user has access to.

title: Add EKUs to intermediate certificates to support mTLS with GCP load balancer
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
GCP now supports [mTLS on application load balancers](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/mtls). I'd like to use Vault for PKI to issue clients with certificates and have them authenticate using the GCP load balancer. However there is a particular [requirement](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/mtls#certificate-requirements) which I don't believe can currently be met by Vault:_x000D_
_x000D_
> The [Extended Key Usage](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.12) extension should contain the clientAuth field. This is required for the certificate that issues the client certificate._x000D_
_x000D_
~~Seems like an unusual requirement to me however~~ This is to ensure the intermediate certificate is "[technically constrained](https://cabforum.org/baseline-requirements-documents/)". I can confirm that client authentication fails without the EKU present on the intermediate certificate. Crafting an intermediate certificate outside Vault which does include the clientAuth EKU works._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Possible solutions include:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Allow specifying EKUs on the `/pki/root/sign-intermediate` endpoint._x000D_
2. Allow specifying EKUs on the "generate intermediate CSR" endpoints, which could be used in combination with the `use_csr_values` flag when signing._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Generate the intermediate certificate outside Vault to create a CSR including the EKU then having Vault sign it, and importing the key into Vault., This approach involves managing private key material safely outside Vault which is not ideal._x000D_
2. Use GCP's Certificate Authority Service instead of Vault for PKI._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
If one of the solutions seems reasonable, would a PR be accepted (perhaps with some guidance)?

title: Tailscale Auth Method
body_text:
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Tailscale (https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale) now supports "application capabilities" in their ACL files._x000D_
See https://tailscale.com/blog/acl-grants_x000D_
_x000D_
It would be good if Vault had an authentication method where roles could simply be created and mapped to ACLs in Tailscale. Vault could then lookup the user identify via a whois call to the local tailscaled daemon to validate the identity of the user._x000D_
_x000D_
E.g_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/tailscale/role/demo \_x000D_
  bound_allowed_roles=vault_role_demo \_x000D_
  policies=default \_x000D_
  ttl=1h_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Corresponding Tailscale ACL:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "grants": [{_x000D_
    "src": ["group:developers"],_x000D_
    "dst": ["tag:vault_server"],_x000D_
    "app": {_x000D_
      "vaultproject.io/cap/auth": [_x000D_
        {_x000D_
          "allowed_roles": ["vault_role_demo"]_x000D_
        }_x000D_
      ]_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  }]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
It's possible to whitelist Tailscale IP addresses in Vault but this requires whitelisting each individual device or user, whereas the above solution could allow for permitting access to entire groups of tagged devices / users._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
This would reduce friction for authenticating to Vault when used in conjunction with Tailscale. No login tokens would be needed as Tailscale can prove the identity of the device itself.

title: ParseSecret hides difference between empty results 404 and missing route 404
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
In my use case, I am trying to build a namespace "folder tree" to match our organization's team structure. To minimize the number of requests, I am using `ListWithContext` to get a picture of the current state. Based on that, I plan to fire a minimal number of Create and Delete requests to build the namespace tree._x000D_
_x000D_
When listing Vault Namespaces, I'm trying to use this code:_x000D_
```go_x000D_
client = client.WithNamespace(ns)_x000D_
secret, err := client.Logical().ListWithContext(ctx, "sys/namespaces")_x000D_
```_x000D_
However, the client API makes it impossible to tell the difference between "your namespace doesn't exist" and "your namespace has no children." In both cases, `ListWithContext` returns `nil, nil`._x000D_
_x000D_
The server actually does distinguish these two cases in its response, but the client API hides this information._x000D_
_x000D_
Leaf namespace with no children:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ curl -v H "X-Vault-Token: $(vault print token)" -H "X-Vault-Request: true" -H "X-Vault-Namespace: leafNamespace" http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/namespaces?list=true"_x000D_
*   Trying 127.0.0.1..._x000D_
..._x000D_
< HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found_x000D_
..._x000D_
{"errors":[]}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Nonexistent namespace:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ curl -v H "X-Vault-Token: $(vault print token)" -H "X-Vault-Request: true" -H "X-Vault-Namespace: nonexistentNamespace" http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/namespaces?list=true"_x000D_
*   Trying 127.0.0.1..._x000D_
..._x000D_
< HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found_x000D_
..._x000D_
{"errors":["no handler for route \"nonexistentNamespace/\". route entry not found."]}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would like `ParseSecret` to distinguish between the two server responses. A missing resource and an empty resource should not appear the same._x000D_
_x000D_
I would be ok with returning a non-nil Secret with an empty `Data` field for an empty resource that exists, and a `*Secret(nil)` for a missing resource._x000D_
_x000D_
Another possibility would be to return `nil, nil` for an empty resource that exists, while returning the already-defined `ErrSecretNotFound` for missing resources._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
* `client.RawRequestWithContext` would work, but is deprecated. It would also mean copying and modifying lots code from the vault client API to parse the response. This is many subtle LOC, which makes code maintenance difficult._x000D_
* `net/http` methods. These are not deprecated, but they take even more LOC, and mean strictly more subtlety and more difficulty to maintain than the previous idea._x000D_
* If I receive `nil, nil` from `ListWithContext`, fire another request to List the parent namespace. This wastes a network request and a few LOC, but not as many LOC as the previous ideas.

title: vault raft snapshot restore unseal step requesting more keys parts than exists
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Possibly this is unavoidable because of how sealing works. But unsealing after a snapshot restore depends on the snapshot and the restoration vault server having the same key configurations otherwise the unseal process will continue to request key parts after all the extant parts have been provided for the backup. It should be possible to handle/warn of this situation in a cleaner manner than currently?_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
* save a snapshot with vault operator raft snapshot save /vault/config/vault1.snap_x000D_
* halt the vault server (if using container `docker-compose rm -s -v vault1`)_x000D_
* remove the vault files `sudo rm -fr ./vault1/file/vault.db ./vault1/file/raft/`_x000D_
* bring back up the vault container `docker-compose up --build --detach vault1`_x000D_
* check it’s a fresh vault with `docker-compose exec vault1 /bin/sh` and  `vault status`_x000D_
* being restoration with, the normal vault init (ensure the same configuration is used as for the original or the second unseal will not work), unseal, login then vault operator raft snapshot restore --force /vault/config/vault1.snap (force is needed as the fresh vault has different keys to the old vault)_x000D_
* after the force restore the vault will be resealed and need unsealing again (if a different configuration was given, the unseal command will request the wrong number of keys)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Current workaround**_x000D_
Ensure the fresh container is `init` with the same key configuration as the backup snapshot, then the restore unseal will request the right number of keys._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behaviour**_x000D_
The unseal process after the snapshot restore should be using the key configuration of the snapshot e.g. 1 of 1 keys instead of the fresh empty vault configuration e.g. 3 of 5 keys. If the unseal is unable to know the restored configuration, then it should be possible to tell the unseal process how many keys are to be provided._x000D_
_x000D_

    * Vault Server Version (retrieve with vault status): Version                  1.14.8_x000D_

title: “unable to create provider: oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider” with keycloak idp
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When configuring a `jwt_auth_backend` in vault with a provider that vault reaches through a different URL than the `issuer` URL, vault fails with `unable to create provider: oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider`_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
When configuring vault with keycloak IPD so that keycloak authenticates vault users through oidc, we have a problem with a verification that vault makes on the issuer field._x000D_
We have a specific setup with keycloak:_x000D_
_x000D_
- Vault reaches keycloak through a private network (backend url)_x000D_
- end users reach keycloak from a public network (frontend url)_x000D_
_x000D_
With this setup, keycloak considers the issuer as a frontend element: in the .well-known/openid-configuration discovery URL, the `issuer` field is `https://<frontend-keycloak-hostname>/auth/realms/myrealm`_x000D_
_x000D_
Upon initializing the oidc configuration (when building the auth backend), vault makes a verification about the issuer that makes the process fail : it seems that vault is trying to guess what the issuer should be by concatenating_x000D_
- the hostname vault is using to reach keycloak : `https://<backend-keycloak-hostname>`_x000D_
- with the path configured in the oidc_discovery_url: `/auth/realms/myrealm`_x000D_
_x000D_
We can see in vault logs:_x000D_
```_x000D_
2024-01-16T11:57:12.474+0100 [ERROR] auth.oidc.auth_oidc_xxxx: error checking oidc discovery URL: error="error creating provider with given values: NewProvider: _x000D_
	unable to create provider: oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider, _x000D_
	expected \"https://<backend-keycloak-hostname>/auth/realms/myrealm\"_x000D_
	     got \"https://<frontend-keycloak-hostname>/auth/realms/myrealm\""_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The assumption that the `issuer` must have the same hostname as the `oidc_discovery_url` address is incorrect when the idp can be reached from different URLS._x000D_
_x000D_
The error appears even when `bound_issuer` is configured in the auth backend. Vault could simply compare the value of `bound_issuer` with the `issuer` given by the discovery URL in that case rather than assuming what the `issuer` hostname should be. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
Setup:_x000D_
vault (terraform)_x000D_
```_x000D_
resource "vault_jwt_auth_backend" "keycloak" {_x000D_
  description        = "Keycloak"_x000D_
  path               = "oidc"_x000D_
  type               = "oidc"_x000D_
  oidc_discovery_url = "https://<backend-keycloak-hostname>/auth/realms/myrealm"_x000D_
  bound_issuer       = "https://<frontend-keycloak-hostname>/auth/realms/myrealm"_x000D_
  oidc_client_id     = var.keycloak_client_id_x000D_
  oidc_client_secret = var.keycloak_client_secret_x000D_
  default_role       = "default-keycloak"_x000D_
  tune {_x000D_
    default_lease_ttl            = "2h"_x000D_
    max_lease_ttl                = "8h"_x000D_
    allowed_response_headers     = []_x000D_
    audit_non_hmac_request_keys  = []_x000D_
    audit_non_hmac_response_keys = []_x000D_
    listing_visibility           = "unauth"_x000D_
    passthrough_request_headers  = []_x000D_
    token_type                   = "default-service"_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
resource "vault_jwt_auth_backend_role" "default_keycloak" {_x000D_
  backend        = vault_jwt_auth_backend.keycloak.path_x000D_
  role_name      = "default-keycloak"_x000D_
  token_policies = ["default"]_x000D_
_x000D_
  user_claim            = "xxx"_x000D_
  groups_claim          = "groups"_x000D_
  role_type             = "oidc"_x000D_
  allowed_redirect_uris = var.oidc_authorized_redirects_x000D_
  verbose_oidc_logging  = true_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
keycloak:_x000D_
_x000D_
- `KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT=false` : backend urls are built based on the request_x000D_
- `KC_HOSTNAME_URL=https://<frontend-keycloak-hostname>/auth` : The front-end url is forced in keycloak with so that end users are not redirected to the backend URL_x000D_
_x000D_
With this setup, accessing to `https://<backend-keycloak-hostname>/auth/realm/myrealm/.well-known/openid-configuration` displays the issuer as `https://<frontend-keycloak-hostname>/auth/realm/myrealm`_x000D_
_x000D_
Issue could be circumvented by making vault access keycloak through the public URL `https://<frontend-keycloak-hostname>` but it’s not what we want to do from a network point of view._x000D_
_x000D_
Another solution would be to not use the discovery URL but `jwks_url` instead but that doesn't seem to be working at the moment: see _x000D_
- https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-jwt/issues/272_x000D_
- https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-jwt/issues/169#issuecomment-1905828055_x000D_
_x000D_
FYI related discussions on keycloak side:_x000D_
- [New hostname config UX · Issue #24252 · keycloak/keycloak · GitHub 1](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/24252#issuecomment-1895907170)_x000D_
- https://groups.google.com/g/keycloak-user/c/xot6XrGCM8k_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should be able to log users authenticated through keycloak using oidc_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
- hashicorp vault 1.15.4+ent_x000D_
- keycloak 23.0.4_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
In 1.15.4, when viewing a secret in the the read-only JSON view, the drop-down menu to select a different version of the secret does not reload or update the content of the JSON view. This appears to occur for both complex and non-complex kv secrets. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
For example, version 2 of a secret, using the JSON view:_x000D_
![Screenshot 2024-01-24 at 8 36 27 AM](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/4422163/f6ede6dc-2227-4601-a388-4a0f04e5fd07)_x000D_
_x000D_
then selecting version 1 from the drop-down, the version number and creation time change, but the content does not:_x000D_
![Screenshot 2024-01-24 at 8 36 34 AM](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/4422163/65a473cf-0265-4478-9cfe-1f15754c4f6d)_x000D_
_x000D_
However, when viewing the secret in the "default" view, the content does change. Version 2:_x000D_
_x000D_
![Screenshot 2024-01-24 at 8 39 25 AM](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/4422163/b8a9c4d5-5deb-421d-9d59-82c85d79c900)_x000D_
_x000D_
and then version 1:_x000D_
_x000D_
![Screenshot 2024-01-24 at 8 39 32 AM](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/4422163/3f30632c-ab4e-4771-9f09-b23bd6450f81)_x000D_
_x000D_
I believe this may be related to #24290, as I can confirm what I believe to be the correct behavior works in 1.15.2._x000D_
_x000D_

1. Create a new kv secret, using default or JSON editor_x000D_
2. Create a second version of the secret with different contents_x000D_
3. Toggle the JSON view on_x000D_
4. Switch back and forth between versions using the drop-down, secret contents do not change_x000D_
5. Toggle JSON view off_x000D_
6. Switch back and forth between versions using drop-down, secret contents do change_x000D_
_x000D_

The JSON view should update its contents to reflect the content of the version of the secret currently selected._x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Reading the details of a rabbitmq role from vault appears to crash the process_x000D_
_x000D_
I am able to add a new role successfully, but reading the details of the role after creation causes strange errors and appears to make the vault container crash and restart._x000D_
_x000D_
I found the problem because it was crashing our terraform deployments, however I am able to reproduce it through the http api and the web ui command line._x000D_
_x000D_
Comparing the rabbitmq secret backend and the database one, the only difference I can see is e.g._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/2acac70160962a61b21f2e1355fa052e464f7f75/builtin/logical/rabbitmq/path_roles.go#L110 - the database plugin constructs a map[string]interface{} rather than _x000D_
structs.New(role).Map().  (this may be my amateur reading of the go code though)._x000D_
_x000D_
Failing that, my other hunch is that the the interaction between the plugin and the storage is not quite right, so the role creation is storing something that blows up when read back out_x000D_
_x000D_
Are there any pointers about how the plugins work so I could contribute some useful debugging information?_x000D_
_x000D_
I can also see that path_roles.go lacks its test file so I will try to poke around there too_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. vault secrets enable rabbitmq_x000D_
2. vault write rabbitmq/config/connection connection_uri=xxx username=xxx password=xxx_x000D_
3. vault write rabbitmq/roles/newrole vhosts='{"/":{"write": ".*", "read": ".*"}}'_x000D_
4. vault read rabbitmq/roles/newrole_x000D_
_x000D_
In the web ui, a redirect is returned causing the command to not return.  From the logs it appears the redirect is masking a restart of the container._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
The role details as defined within vault are returned as per the api_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
Vault 1.15.1_x000D_
Backend dynamodb_x000D_
EKS - installed with helm chart_x000D_
3 node cluster_x000D_

title: Allow Vault to make updates to the DynamoDB table it creates
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When Vault is set up to use DynamoDB as the storage backend, it will create the table if it doesn't exist and will no-op if it does exist._x000D_
It would be nice if Vault could make updates to the table, to change the provisioned throughput or the billing mode (ie from provisioned to pay-per-request)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Along with the settings and environment variables for `read_capacity` and `write_capacity`, there could be two more: `billing_mode` and `allow_updates`. Billing mode specifies if the table is provisioned, or pay-per-request. If `allow_updates` is set, then Vault would check if the existing table differs from the provided values, and if it does, Vault makes an UpdateTable API call._x000D_
The defaults of these would retain the existing behaviour (billing mode of provisioned, and a no-op if the table already exists)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
The only other alternative is to manage the dynamo table in Terraform (or some other way) and continue to have Vault no-op when the table exists._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
We've got several Vault clusters running with DynamoDB, and in a desire to reduce some costs we've spotted that changing these tables to pay per request would be cheaper. Right now that means either manually making the change to the table, or importing the dynamodb table into a Terraform set up for every Vault cluster running. This is a bit of a pain as it requires access to every production cluster we have running._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
The DynamoDB storage backend is community supported so I'm more than happy to make the changes if this feature request is acceptable._x000D_

title: Support testable CalculateTTL for plugins
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When writing a secrets plugin, TTL calculation is especially relevant when supporting secret renewal. For this purpose, Vault supports [CalculateTTL](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/framework#CalculateTTL). However, it is hard to correctly write unit tests for anything that uses this function since in its implementation it uses `time.Now` to calculate the current time. This makes testing of renewal implementations hard, at least as far as validating TTLs is concerned. This is an issue if the backend supports its own TTL/expiry and the plugin wants to extend the token's lifetime in the secret backend. An example in the existing Vault code is the database secret backend with its [renewal](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/d8df857561530b34757bd97096f864e7339a8354/builtin/logical/database/secret_creds.go#L61) and [create](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/d8df857561530b34757bd97096f864e7339a8354/builtin/logical/database/path_creds_create.go#L108) implementations._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
A framework function that is more testable when TTLs are involved._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I've copied the code from the framework into my own `lease.go` and made a slight tweak to the function:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
diff --git a/sdk/framework/lease.go b/sdk/framework/lease.go_x000D_
index 24824ca52a..c3cf5783e8 100644_x000D_
--- a/sdk/framework/lease.go_x000D_
+++ b/sdk/framework/lease.go_x000D_
@@ -33,10 +33,10 @@ func LeaseExtend(backendIncrement, backendMax time.Duration, systemView logical._x000D_
_x000D_
 // CalculateTTL takes all the user-specified, backend, and system inputs and calculates_x000D_
 // a TTL for a lease_x000D_
-func CalculateTTL(sysView logical.SystemView, increment, backendTTL, period, backendMaxTTL, explicitMaxTTL time.Duration, startTime time.Time) (ttl time.Duration, warnings []string, errors error) {_x000D_
+func CalculateTTL(sysView logical.SystemView, increment, backendTTL, period, backendMaxTTL, explicitMaxTTL time.Duration, startTime time.Time, currentTime time.Time) (ttl time.Duration, warnings []string, errors error) {_x000D_
        // Truncate all times to the second since that is the lowest precision for_x000D_
        // TTLs_x000D_
-       now := time.Now().Truncate(time.Second)_x000D_
+       now := currentTime.Truncate(time.Second)_x000D_
        if startTime.IsZero() {_x000D_
                startTime = now_x000D_
        } else {_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This change introduces a `currentTime` argument and allows me to use the rest of the logic as is. Ideally, this would be included in the framework. I understand that the current function can't easily be changed but a new `CalculateTTLWithCurrentTime` could, for example, be made available._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
There's a related issue I came across in https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/9222 that poses some good questions about TTLs as a whole. While my issue here is just about this one particular issue, the other one raises valid questions, some of which are outdated now, but others I have also run into. This might be an area worth improving docs for. The tutorial doesn't explain TTLs, it just shows you the code you need to have there._x000D_

title: ED25519 Public Key Format
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When retrieving the public key of an ed25519 key pair from the transit API the key is formatted in a strange encoding.  After checking it, i found out that the key is simply a base64 encoding of ed25519.PublicKey which is the internal go type representation. _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Generate ed25519 keypair and use the private one to extract the public: _x000D_
```_x000D_
p := key.Public().(ed25519.PublicKey)_x000D_
b := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(p)_x000D_
```_x000D_
Output is an base64 string which is not a PEM or anything else "usable" by openssl.  Something like this: DixHOIHXtDW0l6DHE2qGCRCfC/XjS5CHxHS+sEUICH0=_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Convert the key into a PEM format/standard encoding that it matches with the other key pair types in format (they use all pub keys in PEM format) to have this format: _x000D_
_x000D_
-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----_x000D_
MCowBQYDK2VwAyEA8eIBpK/74foJBEzRn2kCImhWyVnOcqV5aX1L8DSHyxA=_x000D_
-----END PUBLIC KEY-----_x000D_
_x000D_
This is then readable by openssl. _x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
bytes, err := x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey(key.PublicKey())_x000D_
_x000D_
if err != nil {_x000D_
return nil, err_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
pemBlock := &pem.Block{_x000D_
Type:  "PUBLIC KEY",_x000D_
Bytes: bytes,_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
pubkey_bytes := pem.EncodeToMemory(pemBlock)_x000D_
_x000D_
```

When MySQL is used as storage backend for Vault and **autocommit** is off in MySQL, vault does not work. Global Autocommit is turned off in MySQL for performance reason. _x000D_
```_x000D_
2024-02-01T13:25:00.563Z [INFO]  core: seal configuration missing, not initialized_x000D_
2024-02-01T13:25:01.562Z [INFO]  core: security barrier not initialized_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I enabled logging of all queries in MySQL and I see vault making a remote connection to it and running some queries to insert data. But since AutoCommit is turned off, this data does not get written._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Deploy vault through the vault helm chart with the configuration specified below_x000D_
2. Run `/bin/vault operator init`_x000D_
3. Try to manually unseal vault using `/bin/vault operator unseal`_x000D_
4. See error in vault logs_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault should get unsealed and ready to store data._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.15.2 (cf1b5cafa047bc8e4a3f93444fcb4011593b92cb), built 2023-11-06T11:33:28Z_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Rocky Linux release 8.9 (Green Obsidian)_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
disable_mlock = true_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
 address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_

}_x000D_
storage "mysql" {_x000D_
    username = "****",_x000D_
    password = "****",_x000D_
    database = "vault",_x000D_
    address = "mysql-host:3306"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
There is a [connection_url](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/storage/postgresql) parameter that can be passed to postgressSQL if its used as storage backend and we can pass in 'autocommit=true' for this session which would probably resolve this issue, but MySQL as storage backend does not support this parameter. **Describe the bug**_x000D_
Given a policy which allows you to list, read, create and update to a kv_v2 mount point, but not having delete permissions; and you try to delete a particular version of secret in kv_v2 mount in the web UI; you are successfully able to delete the secret version._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_

 path "store1*" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["list", "read", "create", "update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
3. Add a test user 'testUser1' and assign above policy to 'testUser1'_x000D_
4. Login into UI as 'testUser1'_x000D_
5. Navigate to 'test' secret inside 'store1' and click on delete -> delete this version._x000D_
4. The UI gives -  version1 of the secret has been deleted._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The above policy should not allow the user to delete the secrets version. The operation should be rejected with "permission denied"._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): NA_x000D_

top_3_comments_text: ccapurso: Hi, @subin-seb. title: Allow the ability to disable leases for generated STS tokens
body_text:
Scaling Vault is difficult when dealing with engines that create leases.  I'd like to allow the ability to disable leases for the AWS engine when working with STS tokens.  This will allow high-churn jobs (e.g.: batch workloads, or daemonsets/system jobs across many thousands of hosts) to not impact the reliability and performance of Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
I'd like a flag that disables lease creation for all STS methods, this includes AssumeRole and GetFederationToken.  I accept that disabling that *will not* provide a TTL on return, and any given application will be required to manage token lifecycle itself at that point._x000D_
_x000D_
At the moment we work around this by, quite simply, not using Vault very effectively._x000D_

title: [Deadlock] Hanging when reading a transit key
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Earlier today, we noticed that out of 10s of transit key, we couldn't read one.  The symptom was a time out._x000D_
I am using `broken_transit_key` in place of the real key name._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault read -format=json transit/keys/broken_transit_key_x000D_
Error reading transit/keys/broken_transit_key: context deadline exceeded_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Our set-up has five nodes in a raft cluster.  In this case, a non-leader node received the requests_x000D_
and tried to forward them to the leader.  The non-leader node always logged the following error_x000D_
when serving this request.  When we tried to read other good transit keys, the same node didn't_x000D_
log such an error._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
Feb  8 21:10:31 ip-xx-xx-xx-xx xxx[xxxx]: 2024-02-08T21:10:31.125Z [ERROR] core: error during forwarded RPC request: error="rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled"_x000D_
Feb  8 21:10:31 ip-xx-xx-xx-xx xxx[xxxx]: 2024-02-08T21:10:31.125Z [ERROR] core: forward request error: error="error during forwarding RPC request"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The graph showed that the leader had been accumulating in-flight requests since the start of the problem._x000D_
_x000D_
![Screenshot from 2024-02-08 15-27-12](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/1553860/4704d3d3-a71d-4fee-b72b-4ea6156b5eec)_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
We enabled debug and trace log globally and saw 0 log entries related to this transit key or the transit_x000D_
secret engine in general._x000D_
_x000D_
We deeply regret that we didn't grab a thread dump with the following command._x000D_
For anyone who runs into this problem, get a thread dump!!!_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
sudo kill -SIGUSR2 $(pidof vault)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
We do not know how to reproduce the problem.  Our engineer said they did the following_x000D_
repeatedly with the key.  They used a python script via its http library.  The commands below_x000D_
are for demonstration purpose.  Note that we haven't confirmed that this directly led to the_x000D_
problem._x000D_
_x000D_
1. read the public key_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault read -format=json transit/keys/broken_transit_key_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
2. sign something_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write transit/sign/broken_transit_key/none input=aGVsbG8gd29ybGQuCg== prehashed=true signature_algorithm=pkcs1v15_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This might or might not be a red-herring, but we recently started using [none](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/transit#none)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Reading a transit key should not be blocked this way._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.1 (OSS)_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.15.1 (OSS)_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 18.04_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
We suspect that there is a deadlock somewhere_x000D_
in the transit secret engine code.  This reminds me of https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/22393._x000D_
_x000D_
Eventually, we tried to step down the leader with_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault operator step-down_x000D_
```_x000D_
The leader hung there so eventually we killed the instance and the cluster recovered._x000D_
At that point, the cluster was able to serve the secret again.

Basically, when caching is off, the code actually holds a read lock. When trying to change the config, thread number 2 will attempt to acquire a write lock, which prevents future acquisition of any read locks. This thread will hang here forever. We leak a read lock and a goroutine at this point. Now, when thread 3 comes along wanting to read the key, a read lock is required but can never be obtained. This thread is leaked by deadlocking. Our problem shares the same pattern but was caused by a different access pattern/sequence. The best way to reproduce our problem is the following. First a local dev server is required (`vault server -dev`). ``` vault secrets enable transit vault write transit/keys/broken_transit_key type=rsa-2048 <------ has to be rsa-2048. vault write transit/sign/broken_transit_key input=aGVsbG8gd29ybGQuCg== prehashed=false hash_algorithm=none vault read transit/keys/broken_transit_key <---- hangs when called after 3-5 minutes since the above commands ``` Shocking huh? mju: In fact, I also just reproduced this with an rsa-4096 key. So as soon as I started a local vault server, I started a stop watch. It locks up right after almost exactly a minute. After tracing the code for auto-rotate, I found the following default. ``` c.rollbackPeriod = conf.RollbackPeriod if c.rollbackPeriod <= 0 { // Default to 1 minute c.rollbackPeriod = 1 * time.Minute } ``` https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/914482535610c8b087f9e5223a69076f8b0f56f2/vault/core.go#L1233 is the source. mju: Another observation: When we changed the logging level, there weren't any debug log entries or trace log entries printed. I am not sure if it was intended to log less. To help narrowing down what the problem could be, I feel vault can log more aggressively at debug and trace level.

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I rotate my awskms seal configuration for vault every 7 days using vault agent and I have recently been seeing _x000D_

_x000D_
whenever I perform SIGHUP on a non-leader vault node, it has an error rotating the seal_x000D_

My understanding of what is happening is_x000D_
1. for some reason after 7 days, vault transferred leadership from the primary node to a secondary node (not sure this step is necessary since there is the constant health check)_x000D_

3. After 7 days, the lease on the AWS credentials expires which causes 'UnrecognizedClientException: The security token included in the request is invalid.'_x000D_
_x000D_
The only way to recover from this is restarting vault which reinitialize the seal from scratch_x000D_
_x000D_

1. create a vault cluster with 1 primary and 1 secondary node configured with awskms seal_x000D_

      region     = "us-west-2"_x000D_
      access_key = "<redcated>"_x000D_
      secret_key = "<redacted>"_x000D_
      kms_key_id = "<redacted>"_x000D_

title: Searching for Solutions for Vault's Auto-Unseal Transit without Using Third-Party Cloud Services
body_text:
Hello everyone,_x000D_
_x000D_
I am currently working on implementing a central Vault server within a Kubernetes cluster, intended to serve as a key provider to automate the unseal process for other Vault instances deployed in the same cluster. My goal is to simplify this process by making it fully automatic, thus eliminating the need for manual intervention to unlock Vault instances._x000D_
_x000D_
As part of this project, I followed the tutorial available at: [Vault Auto-Unseal Using Transit Secret Engine on Kubernetes](https://luafanti.medium.com/vault-auto-unseal-using-transit-secret-engine-on-kubernetes) to install and configure the central Vault server via Helm. This guide was invaluable for the initial setup but fell short of achieving complete process automation for unseal. In an attempt to go further, I explored the use of the postStart function based on [Vault's official GitHub](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-helm/blob/50f7439fb298d98a223d2fdf58ece2bad2d816bc/values.yaml#L572) documentation, without achieving a functional solution._x000D_
_x000D_
Beyond these attempts, I am looking to see if other community members have successfully set up a similar system without resorting to third-party services like Google KMS or AWS KMS, preferring a self-hosted approach for the key manager._x000D_
_x000D_
Moreover, I am interested in exploring the use of tools such as GitLab for CI/CD and [Flux](https://fluxcd.io/flux/guides/sealed-secrets/) for GitOps, aiming to further automate the Vault installation and unseal process. I wonder if anyone has integrated these tools into a similar automation strategy or could offer advice on how to effectively use them in this context._x000D_
_x000D_
Here are the specific points on which I am seeking feedback and advice:_x000D_
1. Experiences and examples of setting up an internal or self-hosted auto-unseal mechanism for Vault, without depending on third-party cloud services._x000D_
2. Advice on using GitLab or Flux to automate the installation and unseal process of Vault in a Kubernetes environment._x000D_
3. Documentation, guides, or any other resources that could assist in implementing a custom and secure auto-unseal solution for Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
I am open to any suggestions, advice, or caution based on your personal experiences. My goal is to build a robust and secure solution that respects our constraints and our desire for independence from third-party cloud service providers._x000D_
_x000D_
Thank you in advance for your time and valuable assistance._x000D_
_x000D_
Best regards

title: Private DNS name of AWS EC2 instance cannot be used for templated policies
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I use the `IAM` AWS auth method from EC2 instances to generate TLS certificates. I’d like to be able to force that the common name of the issued certificate is the private DNS of the requesting instance (`ip-10-x-x-x.ec2.internal`). This guarantees that the identity of the EC2 instance, as presented in the TLS certificate, is trustworthy._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I think templated policies are a way to do this._x000D_
_x000D_
Today, with Identity Integration, it’s already possible to leverage templated policies to control that the common name is “<auth_metadata>”, where <auth_metadata> is one of account_id, auth_type, canonical_arn, client_arn, client_user_id, inferred_aws_region, inferred_entity_id, inferred_entity_type (see error message for `vault write auth/aws/config/identity iam_metadata=xxx`)._x000D_
_x000D_
Adding a new type of authentication metadata in Vault entities and populating it with the instance  private DNS (which are already retrieved in the validateInstance method) would solve this problem._x000D_

title: Improvements on the current shamir implementation
body_text:
Hello everyone, _x000D_
_x000D_
I stumbled upon the `vault/shamir/shamir.go` implementation while porting mine to Rust ([wavefnx/shamirs](https://github.com/wavefnx/shamirs)) and found out that there are several improvements that could be easily achieved. I won't open an issue for each separately to keep things compact._x000D_
_x000D_
### Deprecated `math/rand` Seed [[shamir#L158](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a1fc106008c308f0b1e1aa82db1bc5891d857484/shamir/shamir.go#L158)]_x000D_
Currently, x-coordinates are being generated using  `math/rand` seeded with `time.Now().UnixNano()` and then permutations are being created using the same package._x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
mathrand.Seed(time.Now().UnixNano())_x000D_
xCoordinates := mathrand.Perm(255)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The first issue arises with `Seed` being deprecated. However, if you still want to utilize `math/rand` for this case, the updated syntax would be: _x000D_
```go_x000D_
mathrand.New(mathrand.NewSource(time.Now().UnixNano()))_x000D_
xCoordinates := mathrand.Perm(255)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
> mathrand.Seed is deprecated: As of Go 1.20 there is no reason to call Seed with a random value. Programs that call Seed with a known value to get a specific sequence of results should use New(NewSource(seed)) to obtain a local random generator._x000D_
_x000D_
### The `math/rand` package is not a `CSPRNG` [[shamir#L159](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a1fc106008c308f0b1e1aa82db1bc5891d857484/shamir/shamir.go#L159)]_x000D_
_x000D_
Even if the x-coordinates themself do not specifically expose any information about the secret, the use of `CSPRNGs` is advisable. The Fisher-Yates (Knuth Shuffle) algorithm can be easily implemented in `O(n)` to generate permutations while also utilizing `crypto/rand` which is a `CSPRNG`._x000D_
_x000D_
Additionally, the `Perm(i)` function generates permutations in the range `(0..i-1)` while the suggested implementation could be `Perm(min, max)` and be used as `Perm(1, 255)`. That leads us to the next issue._x000D_
_x000D_
### Evaluation at `x=0` should not be permitted [[shamir#L49](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a1fc106008c308f0b1e1aa82db1bc5891d857484/shamir/shamir.go#L49)]_x000D_
Even if evaluation at `x=0` is mathematically correct, such case would return the constant-term which in this case is a secret byte. _x000D_
Currently after every iteration on the x-coordinates there's the need to add `+1` ([shamir#L167](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a1fc106008c308f0b1e1aa82db1bc5891d857484/shamir/shamir.go#L167), [shamir#L184](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a1fc106008c308f0b1e1aa82db1bc5891d857484/shamir/shamir.go#L184)) to get them in the required range `(1..n-1)`, with `n` being the order of the `GF(2^8)`. In order to avoid any developer mistakes and not rely on these two `+1` lines, the implementation of the `Perm(min, max)` function above is suggested and encouraged._x000D_
_x000D_
Furthermore, as an additional safety measure and good practice it's advisable to `panic(...)`  instead of returning the constant-term, since that should never be the case ([shamir#L49](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a1fc106008c308f0b1e1aa82db1bc5891d857484/shamir/shamir.go#L49)). _x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
func (p *polynomial) evaluate(x uint8) uint8 {_x000D_
    // ..._x000D_
    if x == 0 {_x000D_
         panic("evaluation at x=0 is not allowed")_x000D_
    }_x000D_
    ..._x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
### Readability of the `inverse(x)` function [[shamir#L100](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a1fc106008c308f0b1e1aa82db1bc5891d857484/shamir/shamir.go#L100)]  (optional) _x000D_
Lastly, the `inverse(x)` can be computed in a more clean and compact way while also maintaining constant-time execution._x000D_
Except from the fact that this could increase the understanding of the repository by developers in the community, it also minimizes the risk of errors by those already working on it._x000D_
```go_x000D_
func inverse(a uint8) uint8 {_x000D_
    // initialization: b = a -> a^1_x000D_
    b := a_x000D_
_x000D_
    for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {_x000D_
        // 1st iteration: b = a^2 then b= a^3_x000D_
        // 2nd iteration: b = a^6 then b= a^7_x000D_
	// 3rd iteration: b = a^14 then b= a^15_x000D_
	// 4th iteration: b = a^30 then b= a^31_x000D_
	// 5th iteration: b = a^62 then b= a^63_x000D_
	// 6th iteration: b = a^126 then b= a^127_x000D_
	b = mult(b, b)_x000D_
	b = mult(b, a)_x000D_
    }_x000D_
_x000D_
    // finalization: b = a^254 -> a^-1_x000D_
    return mult(b, b)_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I can gladly suggest more but I'll be keeping the scope minimal. _x000D_
I'd also be glad to do separate pull requests for any or all of these._x000D_
Keep up the good work!

title: PKI: Allow allowed_domains to be a comma seperated string
body_text:
This is pretty much #11038 but for PKI._x000D_
_x000D_
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I have machines that need multiple names in their certificates. I want the machines to be able to issue certificates for their own names but not others. I want to solve this without having one pki role for each machine._x000D_
My understanding is that vault does not allow complex types in entity metadata so I can not use the allowed_domains role option for templating multiple names._x000D_
Reading the code seems to indicate that this was possible before. https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/c5d39c816a06d0f6b049691d178a43233ce59f98/builtin/logical/pki/issuing/roles.go#L209_x000D_
`allowed_uri_sans` seems to allow comma separated strings so allowed_domains should be consistent._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would like to have `{"metadata": {"cnames": "foo.bar.com,baz.bar.com"}}` in my entity and `allowed_domains = "{{ identity.entity.metadata.names }}"` in my pki issuing role._x000D_
The string should be split on comma for evaluation._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I could have a pki role for each individual host. This feels like an increase in complexity._x000D_
_x000D_
There might also be a way to combine a single templated string and globbing to make it work but it sounds a bit hacky and prone to security issues._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
This is already implemented as mentioned in allowed_uri_sans according to the API documentation, but the code seems to take a list and I can not find any place where split on `,` occurs. _x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/c5d39c816a06d0f6b049691d178a43233ce59f98/builtin/logical/pki/issuing/roles.go#L80_x000D_

_x000D_

title: Cannot clean up old expired tokens after backend storage disk was full
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Scenario: A buggy client is fetching tokens in uncontrolled manner. Eventually there is no more space in backend storage to write more since it is filled by tokens in the token store.  In my case the storage is etcd, which allows configuring write quota, that makes etcd not accept more writes even if disk is not actually full yet._x000D_
_x000D_
Even when token expires, Vault attempts Put to the (already filled) backend storage to update the status of the token. It seems that expiry bails out early at first error and does not proceed to delete the token. The `sys/expire/` entries get deleted though, even when backend does not accept any more data - which means we will be unable to expire the tokens automatically after storage full issue has been fixed._x000D_
_x000D_
After more space is arranged for the storage backend, I'm sending request to endpoint `auth/token/tidy` in attempt to clean up the situation. At this stage, the accessors `sys/token/accessor/*` get deleted BUT the tokens `sys/token/id/*` are not always deleted and storage seems to get out of sync. When this bug happens, there does not seem to be way to clean up the tokens that still fill the disk as Vault seems unaware of tokens with no matching accessors._x000D_
_x000D_
**Question:** what is the procedure to recover when `sys/token/accessor/*` and `sys/token/id/*` already got out of sync?_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Create masses of tokens that fill the disk (up to backend quota in case of etcd)._x000D_
2. Observe that tokens expire and errors get printed _"failed to revoke token: failed to revoke entry: failed to persist entry: etcdserver: mvcc: database space exceeded"_. Observe that expiration manager entries `/sys/expire/` are deleted._x000D_
3. Re-configure etcd (e.g. remove quota) and disarm the etcd alarm `alarm:NOSPACE` to allow writes again._x000D_
4. Send request to `/auth/token/tidy` ._x000D_
5. Check if only `sys/token/accessor/*` got deleted and that `sys/token/id/*` remain._x000D_
_x000D_
If Vault is restarted after step (2) but before (4) then both `sys/token/accessor/*` and `sys/token/id/*` get deleted correctly and the bug does not happen. Bug is triggered if  `/auth/token/tidy` is requested between the time the disk gets full and Vault gets restarted. After the bug is triggered, restarting Vault again and re-requesting token tidy will not help anymore - there is no way to get rid of tokens without accessors._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
* Tokens should be deleted at expiry even if there is no more space and Put fails. In etcd, deletes still work when ETCD_QUOTA_BACKEND_BYTES is reached._x000D_
* It should not be possible to end up with tokens in `sys/token/id/*` that cannot be cleaned up anymore_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: main_x000D_
* Storage: etcd_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_

title: [Kubernetes Secrets Engine] Allow ClusterRoles to be used as reference for RoleBinding
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I'm using a workflow where I pre-define the Role/ClusterRole in K8s and in the K8s secrets role I'm providing the `kubernetes_role_name`. Then I noticed the following behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
- when `kubernetes_role_type` is set to `Role` but the `kubernetes_role_name` is the name of a `ClusterRole` the binding is not created properly: the `RoleBinding` that vault is trying to create is using in the role reference a type `Role` instead of `ClusterRole`_x000D_
_x000D_
In summary, having a generic `ClusterRole` (let's called "ABC") with some permissions and then creating a K8s secrets engine role of type `Role` using the `ClusterRole` name "ABC" the final `RoleBinding` is not able to identify that the reference role is of type `ClusterRole` and instead creates a reference of type `Role`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would like to have one additional parameter while creating the K8s Secrets Engine Role that allows me to specify if the reference role used for the `RoleBinding` is of type `Role` or `ClusterRole`, to stay backward compatible, I would give it a default value from the value of the parameter `kubernetes_role_type`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
All alternatives will end up in a much less pleasant experience:_x000D_
- I don't want to repeat that "generic" `ClusterRole` as `Role` for every namespace_x000D_
- I don't want to escalate the role type from `Role` to `ClusterRole` just to use that generic `ClusterRole`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
The main use case is to have the ability to create generic ClusterRoles to save a lot of scaffold and configuration and then use those to create `Role` for the target namespaces_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: tomhjp: Thanks for the interest! I want to check that I understand the request properly. Currently in the Vault role config, you set up a reference to either a Kubernetes `Role` or `ClusterRole`. When a Vault client generates the creds, if you chose `ClusterRole` the client gets the chance to specify if they want to create a `RoleBinding` or `ClusterRoleBinding` against that `ClusterRole`. If you chose a `Role`, they don't get a choice, they can only generate a `RoleBinding` against the `Role`. It seems like what you want is a single reusable `ClusterRole` definition that can only be used to generate `RoleBinding`s? It's perhaps not the most intuitive UX, so I'm open to discussing alternatives, but if you set [`cluster_role_binding`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kubernetes#cluster_role_binding) as one of the [`denied_parameters`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/policies#denied_parameters) in clients' policies, would that achieve the same outcome? To be clear, that means you would set the `kubernetes_role_type` on the role as `ClusterRole`, so that the plugin correctly finds the referenced k8s resource, but Vault clients wouldn't be able to generate `ClusterRoleBinding`s against it. | refucktor: thanks for the comment 👋🏻 1. yes, you explained the current behavior perfectly! >It seems like what you want is a single reusable ClusterRole definition that can only be used to generate RoleBindings? 2. More or less, to rephrase it, I would like to have the **possibility** to create vault roles using `kubernetes_role_type=Role` and using any existing k8s role name whether or not that role is `Role` or `ClusterRole`, and the problem for me is that I have no option to define that last part 3. your alternative is an excellent workaround that we already considered but it comes with a few drawbacks which IMHO are somehow relevant - by definition we are allowing an escalation of the permissions, so we are forced to always make sure to add the `denied_parameters` in the policies. That makes the administration slightly worse - it feels weird to create a workaround for something that is natively supported in K8s (Create a `RoleBinding` using a `ClusterRole` as role ref) - we learned the hard way that one of the easiest things to get out of hands in Vault are the policies, therefore we did a huge refactoring to reduce almost 80% of our policies by creating a combination of Identity Groups + Policies with path templating, that allow us to create less amount and more generic policies (this approach I would highly recommend to any team managing a mid~big size Vault instance). Hence, we don't want to go back to write more individual policies just to add a `denied_parameters` I slightly disagree on the possible complexity for UX 😊, we are talking about 1 extra optional parameter for configuring the vault role which, if not set, should use the value from `kubernetes_role_type`, then on the client side to generate the credentials there is no change at all. sorry if I made a long comment, I actually enjoyed our exchange 🤓, looking forward to read your thoughts | tomhjp: Thanks, that makes sense. By the way, this comment > It's perhaps not the most intuitive UX was in reference to my own suggestion. I agree it's awkward to grant permissions and then have to subsequently and consistently take some of them away. But it helps me to understand the use-case better to have your reasoning on that idea laid out, thanks! Given this is only a binary choice anyway, how about a new `disallow_cluster_role_binding` parameter on the Vault role? I think it still allows the full amount of flexibility you need, but with a more intuitive/localised UX than relying on policies, and is pretty easy to reason about. I think setting it while `kuberenetes_role_type` is set to `Role` should be rejected as invalid config, and it can keep backwards compatibility by defaulting to false. But if you set it while `kubernetes_role_type` is `ClusterRole`, then clients can only generate `RoleBinding`s against the `ClusterRole`.

title: Multiple quotas on a single endpoint
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I'm looking to implement a tool that will bulk decrypt emails, there is a valid use case for adhoc queries (e.g. notifications product recalls, shipping delays etc...) each row of personal data is encrypted with a derived key using the vault transit api so to get an email list a tool is needed to decrypt each row with a suitable context._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
The quota tool looked the ideal way to throttle user usage to give a balance between allowing them to get hold of an email list, while preventing them from getting a complete list, without enough time for logging and monitoring to pick up on the suspicious usage._x000D_
_x000D_
However for this to work ideal would like to be able to implement more than one quota. The first quota to operate over short intervals, and the second quota for a larger amount over a longer interval to defeat any user attempting to throttle requests to beat the first quota. An example would be something like a user should be limited to say 1 key a second, but also a second quota of 1,000 keys per day._x000D_
_x000D_
However this isn't possible by design: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/18164_x000D_
While it makes sense that having two quotas for the same interval shouldn't be allowed, different quotas operating on different timescales should be valid._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I've considered client side restrictions, but a clever user would be able to tweak the script to give more generous limits._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Such a solution would also allow for scaling lock outs, with the larger rate/intervals having a longer lockout._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
none

For example, let's say that you have created a very restrict 1 key/second rate limit on the `my_namespace/transit/my_key` path, you could further create a larger rate limit (ie. 1000 keys/second) on `my_namespace/transit` so as to limit any requests made to this path as a catch all.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Some applications generate a CSR with a serial number in the certificate's subject (not the serial number field). Sometimes it's desirable to ignore this value._x000D_
The other values that can be taken from the CSR, namely SANs and `common_name`, have a `use_csr_*` option to control whether or not they take their values from the CSR. `serial_number` does not._x000D_
_x000D_

A `use_csr_serial_number` role parameter which controls whether or not the serial number in the CSR is used._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Some applications do not have the ability to remove the serial number from the generated CSR._x000D_
_x000D_
`/pki/sign-verbatim` is not an option since it is not possible to restrict the values of other certificate attributes._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Vault Agent flooding the server with "/v1/sys/leases/renew" requests after the lease expired
body_text:
I have noticed a strange pattern, when looking through vault server load balancer metrics. There were tons of request, with "403 Forbidden" response code recorded. Quick investigation led me to instances of vault agent, configured with AWS IAM auto_auth and dynamic credentials caching enabled._x000D_
_x000D_
tcpdump showed, that after some time from obtaining first auth token and a set of dynamic credentials, agent started flooding the server with the lease renewal request (/v1/sys/leases/renew), that at that time were no longer in vault (evicted due to the auth token expiration). The server kept responding with "403 Forbidden", because the lease was no longer valid and the agent kept repeating the request over and over again._x000D_
The interesting part was that those request were not visible in agent logs, even with most detailed "TRACE" log level._x000D_
_x000D_
I think, that this happens, when vault agent tries to determine whether cached credentials are still valid or if they can be renewed. In usual use case a response is returned, which is then used to decide if data should be evicted from the cache or renewed. When the auth token (with which credentials were generated) has expired, that is no longer possible. Program gets trapped in a loop and keeps sending the "/v1/sys/leases/renew" request._x000D_
_x000D_
Details specific to the configuration which triggers the issue:_x000D_
_x000D_
agent-config.hcl:_x000D_
```_x000D_
pid_file = "./agent.pid"_x000D_
log_level = "trace"_x000D_
_x000D_
vault {_x000D_
  address = "http://vault_addr:8200"_x000D_
  retry {_x000D_
    num_retries = 5_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
auto_auth {_x000D_
  method "aws" {_x000D_
    mount_path = "auth/aws"_x000D_
_x000D_
