      type = "iam"_x000D_
      role = "auth_role"_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
cache {_x000D_
  use_auto_auth_token = true_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address = "0.0.0.0:8100"_x000D_
  tls_disable = true_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
auth_role:_x000D_
```_x000D_

token_bound_cidrs                 []_x000D_
token_explicit_max_ttl            0s_x000D_
token_max_ttl                     1m_x000D_
token_no_default_policy           false_x000D_

```_x000D_
_x000D_
database role details:_x000D_

_x000D_
What's important to note here is that the issue appears when the token type is set to "service" and max_ttl is applied (not a periodic token)._x000D_
_x000D_
I see 2 possible solutions:_x000D_
- When auto_auth token expires and new one is obtained - make sure that all the cache related to the previous token is evicted._x000D_
- When "403 Forbidden" is received, when trying to renew cached lease, treat it as it was no longer valid, and evict from cache._x000D_
_x000D_

title: Vault OIDC Provider Scopes Should Support JSON (or at least lint for common problems)
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Setting the following OIDC scope:_x000D_
```shell_x000D_
vault write identity/oidc/scope/groups template='{"groups":"{{identity.entity.groups.names}}"}'_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Will be accepted by the API, however, will quietly error into the console the following messages when attempting to log in as some identity (in this case, who is part of the `foobar` group) and the client requests that scope:_x000D_
```_x000D_
<timestamp> [WARN] secrets.identity.<identity_accessor>: error parsing OIDC template: template="{\"groups\":\"{{identity.entity.groups.names}}\"}" err="invalid character 'f' after object key:value pair"_x000D_
<timestamp> [WARN] secrets.identity.<identity_accessor>: error parsing OIDC template: template="{\"groups\":\"[\"foobar\"]\"}" err="invalid character 'f' after object key:value pair"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The net result is that a valid token is returned to the OIDC client, however, it will not include the claim._x000D_
_x000D_
This behavior is _very loosely_ defined in the documentation; specifically, [here](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/identity/oidc-provider#create-or-update-a-scope) we see that `template` is defined as a "JSON template" string and should be passed as encoded JSON. Following the link through to [`JSON templates`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/oidc-provider#scopes) we get some more details about what templates are, but no real specifics._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
OIDC Scope templates should properly handle JSON objects. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Couple of alternatives:_x000D_
1. Update documentation to make it more obvious and explicit about what is being expected. While straight forward, this option still puts onus on the Vault administrators to be aware of these constraints._x000D_
2. Update the Create/Update API for scopes to better lint against common problems like this. This option helps in surfacing the error(s), but not in addressing the knowledge/complexity gaps._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
I believe there are two main points of value here:_x000D_
1. Documentation becomes far more understandable. Instead of documenting this strange pseudo-JSON concept of "encoded JSON templates" simply let it be JSON._x000D_
2. Working with JSON is infinitely easier than working with pseudo-JSON. For example, doing the following in Terraform would become possible:_x000D_
_x000D_
```terraform_x000D_
resource "vault_identity_oidc_scope" "groups" {_x000D_
  name     = "groups"_x000D_
  template = jsonencode({groups = "{{identity.entity.groups.names}}"})_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
PS -- this is weird enough that the [provider docs](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-vault/blob/v3.25.0/website/docs/r/identity_oidc_provider.html.md?plain=1#L47) also get it wrong._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Related to https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-vault/issues/1474

title: Vault's PKI signed certificate contains redundant Extended Key Usage claims
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_

_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault's signed certificates are incompatible with Notary V2 notation CLI, because they contain redundant Extended Key Usage (later EKU) claims:_x000D_
- TLS Web Server Authentication_x000D_
- TLS Web Client Authentication_x000D_
_x000D_
Notation requires certificates to have only Digital Signature key usage and no other KeyUsage/EKU enabled._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Enable pki engine_x000D_
2. Create issuer in UI (root CA, internal, CN=foo.tld, name foo, key rsa2048, valid 365 days)_x000D_
3. Create pki role in UI _x000D_
  - name: foo_x000D_
  - ttl 30 days_x000D_
  - allowed domains: foo.tld (Domain Handling)_x000D_
  - checked allow Bare domains (Domain Handling)_x000D_
  - checked allow subdomains (Domain Handling)_x000D_
  - key parameters: rsa 2048_x000D_
  - checked Digital Signature(Key usage)_x000D_
  - IMPORTANT: Uncheck all other Key usage and Extended Key Usage checkboxes)_x000D_
  - Other fields unchanged_x000D_
5. Generate certificate with PKI role_x000D_
  - Common Name: signed.foo.tld_x000D_
6. Save certificate to file_x000D_
7. Get details of certificate with command:_x000D_
```openssl x509 -in <CERTFILE-NAME>.pem -text```_x000D_
8. The certificate have enabled unnecessary EKUs_x000D_
```text_x000D_
Certificate:_x000D_
    Data:_x000D_
        Version: 3 (0x2)_x000D_
        Serial Number:_x000D_
            1d:b4:7a:65:c2:28:23:2e:ce:08:98:79:55:74:db:95:5e:7e:5d:80_x000D_
        Signature Algorithm: sha256WithRSAEncryption_x000D_
        Issuer: CN=foo.tld_x000D_
        Validity_x000D_
            Not Before: Mar  8 15:47:19 2024 GMT_x000D_
            Not After : Mar  9 15:47:49 2024 GMT_x000D_
        Subject: CN=signed.foo.tld_x000D_
        Subject Public Key Info:_x000D_
            Public Key Algorithm: rsaEncryption_x000D_
                Public-Key: (2048 bit)_x000D_
                Modulus:_x000D_
                    00:bb:(...)_x000D_
                    8d:99_x000D_
                Exponent: 65537 (0x10001)_x000D_
        X509v3 extensions:_x000D_
            X509v3 Key Usage: critical_x000D_
                Digital Signature_x000D_
            X509v3 Extended Key Usage: _x000D_

title: PKI Role Case Sensitity Declaration for Config Parameters
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We were unsure about the case-sensitivity of several domain related parameters for PKI roles in Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
These are documented here:  https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#create-update-role_x000D_
_x000D_
E.g. in case of the parameter `allowed_domains` we were not sure if the values entered are normalized in some way (as they are DNS names) or if they are case-sensitive during evaluation within Vault. We found that they are indeed case-sensitive. This is not explicitly stated in the docs._x000D_
_x000D_
However some parameters state explicitly that they are **not** case-sensitive, e.g.: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#key_usage-1 - but in the whole docs page there is not statement given that per default values are case-sensitive and the exception is marked accordingly._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would like to see either a general statement that config parameters are case-sensitive and exceptions are marked accordingly. Or the case-sensitivity of the option should be stated explicitly (however this would hurt readability probably)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
If I'm missing some statement in docs docs clarifying please point that out. Otherwise I'm also willing to provide a PR for whatever variant the Vault teams sees a better fit._x000D_

title: `api_addr` forces port in service registration
body_text:
I have a Vault cluster behind a load balancer._x000D_
_x000D_
My load balancer is Caddy. When it receives a request for `https://vault.my.domain`, it looks up the SRV record for `active.vault.service.consul` and proxies the request there._x000D_
_x000D_
Up until now, I've had this in my config:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
api_addr = "https://node-name.my.domain:8200/"`_x000D_
service_registration {_x000D_
  token = "not-going-to-share-that-on-Github-duh"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This results in a catalog entry with `ServiceAddress = "node-name.my.domain"` and `ServicePort = 8200`, and everything has been fine._x000D_
_x000D_
I now have clients that cannot reach individual nodes, but only the load balancer and only on port 443. This feels like a pretty normal use case, so I'm wondering if I'm missing something. I want api_addr to reflect the load balanced address AND I want Vault to maintain its own registration in Consul AND I want Consul's catalog to reflect a direct address to each individual node._x000D_
_x000D_
I've tried all the combos:_x000D_
_x000D_
| `api_addr`                          | `service_address`       | What ends up in Consul                   |_x000D_
|-------------------------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------------------|_x000D_
| `https://node-name.my.domain:8200/` | unset                   | `node-name.my.domain:8200`               |_x000D_
| `https://node-name.my.domain:8200/` | `""`                    | `10.123.123.123:8200` (the node's IP)    |_x000D_
| `https://node-name.my.domain:8200/` | `"1.2.3.4"`             | `1.2.3.4:8200`                           |_x000D_
| `https://node-name.my.domain:8200/` | `"node-name.my.domain"` | `node-name.my.domain:8200`               |_x000D_
| `https://node-name.my.domain:8200/` | `"random %:nonsense"`   | `random %:nonsense:8200` (I kid you not) |_x000D_
| `https://vault.my.domain/`          | unset                   | `10.123.123.123:443` (the node's IP)     |_x000D_
| `https://vault.my.domain/`          | `""`                    | `10.123.123.123:443` (the node's IP)     |_x000D_
| `https://vault.my.domain/`          | `"1.2.3.4"`             | `1.2.3.4:443`                            |_x000D_
| `https://vault.my.domain/`          | `"node-name.my.domain"` | `node-name.my.domain:443`                |_x000D_
| `https://vault.my.domain/`          | `"random %:nonsense"`   | `random %:nonsense:443`                  |_x000D_
_x000D_
The immediate problem is my load balancer which can't locate Vault anymore, since it's not actually running on the port that's in Consul. I can tell Caddy to use A records and force port 8200, but anyone else looking Vault up in Consul will be lied to._x000D_
_x000D_
As far as I can tell, `github.com/hashicorp/vault/serviceregistration/consul.serviceRegistration.setRedirectAddr` is the only place where `consul.serviceRegistration.redirectPort` gets set, and it'll always be based on the redirect address which is what I set as `api_addr` in my server config._x000D_
_x000D_
If `service_registration.service_address` could be parsed so that a port number would override the port from the api_addr, that would solve it for me.

title: Please document that error 404 could also mean an empty list.
body_text:
When using a list endpoint, if there is no item to list, the API returns an error 404._x000D_
_x000D_
As explain [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/20740#issuecomment-1563404557), this unusual behavior is kept for backward compatibility. The original rational can be found here https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/1365 _x000D_
_x000D_
This has been a painful point for users since a long time, as we can see by the number of related issues_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/20740 https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/13043 https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/24964 https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/1958 https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/5861  https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/8833 https://github.com/hvac/hvac/issues/928_x000D_
_x000D_
I think this will keep hurting users, again and again, if the behavior continues to be undocumented._x000D_
_x000D_
I suggest updating the documentation about the [error codes returned by the API](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs#http-status-codes) to mention that 404 could also mean an empty list._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
The more I dug into it, the more this looks like a Vault proper issue, rather than a bug in TF or the vault provider. (Though if type coercion were somehow possible in the provider before the type comparison happens, that might be a work-around.)_x000D_

1. Run `vault read identity/group/id/be50c371-178b-8f45-70df-xxxxx`_x000D_

title: PKI: Imported Issuer Clarity
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I am working on a project to automate CA rotation in PKI mounts. When using the `pki/intermediate/set-signed` endpoint the response generally looks like this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```json_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "request_id": "235a392a-6aab-6ced-3c6e-ab0fb7dca760",_x000D_
  "lease_id": "",_x000D_
  "lease_duration": 0,_x000D_
  "renewable": false,_x000D_
  "data": {_x000D_
    "existing_issuers": [_x000D_
      "27dd1484-7695-a508-9bf5-0c44ef5037a0",_x000D_
      "1fbb3cd9-122c-c775-4b9f-6687c67eb039"_x000D_
    ],_x000D_
    "existing_keys": null,_x000D_
    "imported_issuers": [_x000D_
      "a44facfa-5fd5-fd1f-5ac7-79348ef61ee4"_x000D_
    ],_x000D_
    "imported_keys": null,_x000D_
    "mapping": {_x000D_
      "1fbb3cd9-122c-c775-4b9f-6687c67eb039": "",_x000D_
      "27dd1484-7695-a508-9bf5-0c44ef5037a0": "",_x000D_
      "a44facfa-5fd5-fd1f-5ac7-79348ef61ee4": "9a5e7782-18f5-20ca-41fe-7469e062a602"_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  },_x000D_
  "warnings": null_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This output was for a newly signed certificate for an intermediate where the chain has not changed._x000D_
_x000D_
It is frustrating that of all the issuers returned (`imported_issuers` in this case was 1 in this case but would be more if it were the first time parent CA(s) were being imported) there is not a field to specify the one that is for the new intermediate. This is important because it is the one you might want to feed through to following commands to perform actions such as updating it to have a friendly name, make it the default issuer for a role, make it the default issuer for the mount, etc._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
What would be ideal is that `set-signed` could determine the issuer reference of all the returned issuers so it could be fed through to the following commands. Alternatively, if there is some sort of consistency to the returned values (for example if `imported_issuers` or `mapping` can also be determined based on the input then this could be calculated._x000D_
_x000D_
For example, in testing it seems that the `mapping` field has the keys returned in the order that a bundle was imported. For example, if I had a root, 2nd tier intermediate, and third tier intermediate, and I specifically built the PEM bundle to be in that order, the final key was the correct reference. If this is the case then a documentation update to make this clear that the order is _always_ consistent would allow for those writing automation to ensure they have a consistent approach to building chains. Particularly if they only needed to ensure the final certificate was the new certificate that had just been signed._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
An alternative was to take a read of all the existing keys before performing `set-signed` and then comparing that to a list after the fact. This worked most of the time but did not feel as consistent._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
The use cases above I feel cover the problem well._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
No other context comes to mind but happy to field questions and provide what I can.

title: Vault as an OIDC Provider - access token should be a  Json Web token (JWT) [rfc7523](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7523.txt)
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When using Vault as an OIDC Provider in the case of a client application that wants to connect to an api server, the api server (as the resource server in this case) has to validate the access token for every api request._x000D_
_x000D_
Currently this validation can not happen on the resource server, instead a request to the vault api has to be made validating the access token (since it is a batch token which in its structure is opaque to the resource server)._x000D_
_x000D_
This becomes problematic when a lot of api requests are made on different apis that all need to validate the access tokens via vault._x000D_
_x000D_
It also makes integration with common libraries for OpenID Connect difficult (e.g. authlib), since these assume access tokens to be Json Web tokens._x000D_
_x000D_
The ID Token already is a Json Web Token, just the access token is not._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I would like the access token to be a Json Web Token (JWT), that can be validated locally with the keys available at the jwks uri._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Batch tokens can be validated by using the specific endpoint for batch token validation, which would lead to a lot of traffic on that vault endpoint._x000D_
_x000D_
Another alternative is the usage of an introspection endpoint, as requested in this [PR](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/15659). While solving some issues regarding token specificity for a specific service, this solution would pose the same problem of a lot of traffic on vault. An introspection endpoint would nevertheless be a useful addition to vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
This would make the OIDC Provider feature much more usable and would facilitate integration with established OIDC libraries._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
This issue is related to the [feature request for refresh tokens](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/16134), which would be another great integration to make Vault as an OIDC Provider even more usable and convenient._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: siepkes: I could be missing something but doesn't this simply "reverse" the problem? Because if you use a JWT you now have to check if the JWT hasn't been revoked? I guess you could cache the result but the same is also true for the information retrieved of a token? | misc-herrera: Good point, thank you for thinking of that. As I understand it, token revocation in OIDC is described in this OAuth2 standard: Implementations MUST support the revocation of refresh tokens and SHOULD support the revocation of access tokens (see Implementation Note). See [rfc7009](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7009). So in the case that access tokens may be revoked as well, you are completely correct. But otherwise connecting to Vault would only be necessary client-side to refresh the access token with the refresh token. And since these access tokens are short-lived, implementing revocation is not as crucial here, I think.

title: Mark X509v3 Subject Alternative Name extension as critical
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
There is no way to mark the X509v3 Subject Alternative Name as critical in Vault (for certificates and intermediate CAs)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Add an option to mark the X509v3 Subject Alternative Name as critical, also when using curl API to generate the certificate/intermediate CA._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Didn't find any alternative with using vault pki engine._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
A very similar case is this: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/9779_x000D_
The above case is just another extension_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I think it's worth having all extensions configurable as critical/non-critical (non critical can be the default for backward compatibility). It can add much needed flexibility when creating certificates and it will be very convenient when having scenarios where replacing old certificates, that were created by other tools, to new certificates that must be created using vault and must include specific extensions configured in specific manner._x000D_
_x000D_
in my example, I need the Subject Alternative Name extension to change from this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
            X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:_x000D_
                DNS:example.com_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
to this:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
            X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: critical_x000D_
                DNS:example.com_x000D_
```_x000D_

**To Reproduce**_x000D_

Running the following test script:_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_

key_type=ed25519_x000D_
_x000D_
vault secrets disable pki_${key_type}_x000D_
vault secrets disable pki_int_${key_type}_x000D_
_x000D_
# Create root CA_x000D_
vault secrets enable -path pki_${key_type} pki_x000D_
vault secrets tune -max-lease-ttl=87600h pki_${key_type}_x000D_
_x000D_
vault write -field=certificate pki_${key_type}/root/generate/internal \_x000D_
     common_name="example.com" \_x000D_
     issuer_name="root-2023" \_x000D_
     key_type=${key_type} \_x000D_
     ttl=87600h > root_2023_ca.crt_x000D_
_x000D_

vault write pki_${key_type}/config/urls \_x000D_
     issuing_certificates="$VAULT_ADDR/v1/pki/ca" \_x000D_
     crl_distribution_points="$VAULT_ADDR/v1/pki/crl"_x000D_
_x000D_
# Create intermediate CA_x000D_
vault secrets enable -path=pki_int_${key_type} pki_x000D_
vault secrets tune -max-lease-ttl=43800h pki_int_${key_type}_x000D_
_x000D_
vault write -format=json pki_int_${key_type}/intermediate/generate/internal \_x000D_
     common_name="example.com Intermediate Authority" \_x000D_
     issuer_name="example-dot-com-intermediate" \_x000D_
     key_type=${key_type} \_x000D_

title: Querying PKI Issuers does not return expiry/ttl information
body_text:
I am in the process of automating Vault PKI Certificate Authority management, and part of that is rotating the CA certificates when appropriate. In order to do this, I need to be able to iterate over potentially 100's of CAs to determine which ones are close enough to their `notAfter` date to need replacing. Currently, this information does not seem to be exposed by the API._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
There is already a whole set of API endpoints for retrieving the Issuer information, both for whatever the current "default" issuer is, and also for specific issuers. Those APIs will return fields such as the certificate itself, the chain, issuer names and key usage settings. Those should also include the `notAfter` and `notBefore` fields._x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
vault read -format=json pki/issuer/default_x000D_
```_x000D_
(the actual certs have been skipped for brevity)_x000D_
_x000D_
This is the current output, and the start/end dates should be within the "data" portion:_x000D_
_x000D_
```json_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "request_id": "21826cdd-dd7f-ac00-6445-fe7005746396",_x000D_
  "lease_id": "",_x000D_
  "lease_duration": 0,_x000D_
  "renewable": false,_x000D_
  "data": {_x000D_
    "ca_chain": ["-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----", "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----"],_x000D_
    "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----",_x000D_
    "crl_distribution_points": [],_x000D_
    "issuer_id": "28bbca57-093c-cf42-1011-7b84f3d29d2a",_x000D_
    "issuer_name": "issuer_v1-1",_x000D_
    "issuing_certificates": [],_x000D_
    "key_id": "c149be2a-8989-c8ee-b7b3-3be533d039df",_x000D_

    "manual_chain": null,_x000D_
    "ocsp_servers": [],_x000D_
    "revocation_signature_algorithm": "",_x000D_
    "revoked": false,_x000D_
    "usage": "crl-signing,issuing-certificates,ocsp-signing,read-only"_x000D_
  },_x000D_
  "warnings": null_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
A CLI workaround is to extract the `certificate` from the API, and then pipe it through external tools such as `openssl x509 --enddate` to get the date or into `openssl x509 --checkend` to check proximity to the expiry._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Being able to use Vault to implement robust, HSM-backed corporate-scale PKI without unecessary manual intervention is a huge selling-point for Vault Enterprise._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
* The GUI does expose this information as "Not valid before" and "Not valid after"._x000D_
* The PKI health-check output has a section for `.ca_validity_period`,  that will raise criticals if the expiry is too close, so it really should be easy to explicity check the validity without resorting to scraping the health-check output messages._x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
[The latest version of Chrome (123) added preflight checks to calls to private (local) networks](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-123-beta#private_network_access_checks_for_navigation_requests_warning-only_mode). This results in an OPTIONS request being sent by Chrome ahead of the GET to `/oidc/callback?code=`, but this callback server doesn't appear to be equipped to handle that OPTIONS request. The request fails and the user is presented with "Vault login failed. Expired or missing OAuth state."_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Using Vault 1.14.4 (`ccdd48d1f7b95fc99fd11d67fc1c687576b338de+CHANGES`) and Chrome 123.0.6312.59, attempt to log in with `vault login -method=oidc`. Notice error message: "Vault login failed. Expired or missing OAuth state."_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Successful login._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): `1.14.8+ent`_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): `Vault v1.14.4 ('ccdd48d1f7b95fc99fd11d67fc1c687576b338de+CHANGES'), built 2023-09-22T21:29:05Z`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: macOS M1 Pro_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
- Custom `VAULT_ADDR` and `VAULT_CACERT` is set._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Add any other context about the problem here._x000D_

It fails with an error when it sees the preflight request, which is an `OPTIONS` request without the auth form data. This causes the CLI to error out and quit before receiving the actual auth request. My install of Chrome is not issuing these preflights for some reason, but I can reproduce the error by sending a curl request during before the OIDC login completes: ``` curl -X OPTIONS http://localhost:8250/oidc/callback ``` ``` Waiting for OIDC authentication to complete... body_text:

_x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
There is a really nasty issue in OIDC authentication that bugged me for quite some time. Sometimes I had to retry "Sign in with OIDC provider" like tens of times to succeed. The problem reproduced only in Firefox and only on my laptop. However, the experience was maddening so I had to figure it out._x000D_
_x000D_
It seems like there is a race between the window with button "Sign in with OIDC provider" and the popup window, that does second part of authentication._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Use Firefox. Set `dom.min_background_timeout_value_without_budget_throttling` to 100000 ms in about:config to make the issue 100% reproducible (default value is 1000 ms)._x000D_
2. Open sign in page (Vault should be set up with OIDC auth)_x000D_
3. Press "Sign in with OIDC provider"_x000D_
4. Wait a little bit_x000D_
5. See the error "The provider window was closed before authentication was complete. Please click Sign In to try again"._x000D_
_x000D_
On my particular hardware+software setup on the default Firefox settings the reproducibility is in the ballpark of 90%._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Sign in should succeed._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.12.2_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.15.6 (cgo) (not needed to reproduce the issue)_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Manjaro Linux 23.1.3_x000D_
* Firefox: 124.0_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I believe there is some kind of sleep in JavaScript in the window with the "Sign in with OIDC provider" button. This sleep is being throttled when the window goes to background. This results in waking up too late, when the popup window is already closed._x000D_
_x000D_
If I manually switch focus from the popup window to the main one, making it foreground, the issue doesn't reproduce.

title: Build your own CA tutorial misleadingly sets issuer_name on intermediate
body_text:
In the [Build Your own CA](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/secrets-management/pki-engine), the step [Generate intermediate CA](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/secrets-management/pki-engine) misleadingly adds an `issuer_name` parameter in this call:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write -format=json pki_int/intermediate/generate/internal \_x000D_
     common_name="example.com Intermediate Authority" \_x000D_
     issuer_name="example-dot-com-intermediate" \_x000D_
     | jq -r '.data.csr' > pki_intermediate.csr_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This has no effect, the issuer_name can only be set after import of the signed certificate, using the `pki_int/issuer/<identifier>` endpoint. _x000D_
_x000D_
Somewhat related to https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/22992

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Prior to 1.16.0, we had scripts that ran without a $HOME directory set. Then in vault 1.16.0, we encountered this issue:_x000D_

Previously, this would work:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault login -method=aws_x000D_
Success! You are now authenticated. The token information displayed below_x000D_
is already stored in the token helper. You do NOT need to run "vault login"_x000D_

_x000D_

Not applicable_x000D_

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When Prometheus server scrapes metrics from the Vault `/v1/sys/metrics` endpoint, it receives a 400 Bad Request response. _x000D_
The issue seems to be related to the Accept header sent by Prometheus in the request._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Create a policy for reading sys/metrics with _x000D_
```bash_x000D_
vault policy write prometheus-policy - <<EOF_x000D_
path "sys/metrics" {_x000D_
    capabilities = ["read"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
EOF_x000D_
```_x000D_
2. Save token to the vault_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
token_output=$(vault token create -policy=prometheus-policy -format=json)_x000D_
token=$(echo "$token_output" | jq -r '.auth.client_token')_x000D_
_x000D_
vault kv put internal/prometheus-token token="$token"_x000D_
```_x000D_
3. Use wget with the accept header that Prometheus uses_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
wget --header="Accept: application/openmetrics-text;version=1.0.0;q=0.5,application/openmetrics-text;version=0.0.1;q=0.4,text/plain;version=0.0.4;q=0.3,*/*;q=0.2" --header="Authorization: Bearer <token>" -O- "http://vault.vault.svc.cluster.local:8200/v1/sys/metrics"_x000D_

title: TCP listener: bind on `cluster_address` only.
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Vault supports binding the API (`address`) to a [Unix domain socket](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/listener/unix) (UDS). However, creating a [TCP listener](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/listener/tcp) currently forces listening on both `address` and `cluster_address`, even if already listening on `address` via the UDS listener method._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Ability to create a TCP listener that binds on `cluster_address` only. For example by introducing a `disable_api` flag that defaults to `false`:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
api_addr     = "https://active.vault.service.consul:8200"_x000D_
cluster_addr = "https://vault.service.consul:8201" _x000D_
_x000D_
listener "unix" {_x000D_
  address = "/run/vault-api.sock"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  disable_api     = true // Don't start the API TCP listener _x000D_
  cluster_address = "10.3.6.9:8201"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
storage "raft" {_x000D_
..._x000D_
}_x000D_
``` _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Using UDS listener only._x000D_
   - Does not currently support creating a socket for `cluster_address`._x000D_
_x000D_
2. Setting `address = "127.0.0.1:8200"`_x000D_
   - Extra port unnecessarily being used._x000D_
   - API accessible by any local process._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
Limit local connectivity to Vault API via Unix socket only, leveraging Unix file permissions to restrict access to a specific user/group. Inbound access to Vault API via Consul Connect Service Mesh._x000D_

body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Vault Agent currently only supports persistent caching for Kubernetes. There are lots of other cases where Vault Agent is not running in Kubernetes, but would still benefit from persistent caching. Being able to cache to a file or a folder of files would be extremely useful._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Being able to persist the cache to a file or a folder of files._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
None._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
None._x000D_
_x000D_

As the cache is a BoltDB file, it should not require too much engineering effort to cache this to a file on disk or some other storage.
top_3_comments_text: carlzogh: +1 to this | carlzogh: We have worked around this and currently have Vault Agent / Proxy set up with persistent caching in "kubernetes" mode without actually running in Kubernetes. "type = kubernetes" really only signals the Agent/Proxy to fetch the Service Account JWT from the path specified in `service_account_token_file`. This token file is read and its value is used as the encryption key for the local cache. Our cache configuration: ```hcl # ref. https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/proxy/caching cache { disable_caching_dynamic_secrets = true # ref. https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/proxy/caching/static-secret-caching cache_static_secrets = true persist { type = "kubernetes" # mocking k8s by providing a (secret) static service account JWT token as AAD path = "/var/run/cache" service_account_token_file = "/etc/config/cache-persistence-token" keep_after_import = true } } ``` In our model, we inject a secret into the `/var/run/cache-persistence-token` file to ensure that the cache can be encrypted and decrypted only by these instances of Vault Agent/Proxy. ---- Vault Agent/Proxy really shouldn't care about whether the environment it is running in is Kubernetes or not, as it only needs a filesystem path to store the cache in, and an encryption secret. This could instead be modeled as (following conventions set by other stanzas, eg. [`auto-auth` sinks](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/autoauth#aad)): ```hcl cache { # ... persist { type = "filesystem" path = "/var/run/cache" aad_file = "/etc/config/cache-persistence-token" # alternatively, "aad" / "aad_env_var" could be specified keep_after_import = true } } ```

body_text:

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We have Vault Agent configured to render multiple templates, with each template retrieving certain secrets from Vault using the `{{- with secret "xxx" }}` function. If one template fails to retrieve a secret (perhaps due to a permissions/policy issues), it triggers a retry. At the end of the retry, the runner restarts, forcing all secrets for all templates to be retrieved again and rerendered. This goes into a loop, which effective DDoses our Vault server._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Set up vault agent's config to render multiple templates:_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
vault {_x000D_
  address = "https://localhost:8200"_x000D_
  retry {_x000D_
    num_retries = 5_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
auto_auth {_x000D_
  method {_x000D_
    type = "token_file"_x000D_
    config = {_x000D_
      token_file_path = "/home/username/.vault-token"_x000D_
    }_x000D_
  }_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
cache {}_x000D_

title: vault agent certificate renewal troubles
body_text:
Have decided to replace our CA with Vault but I'm now facing 2 issues:_x000D_
1. Vault Agent won't reload the renewed certificate. There's an issue open but it says it was resolved. Apparently, it wasn't or this is a new issue. What's interesting is that it happens randomly and sporadically._x000D_
2. ~~Vault Agent will DoS the server if it can't renew the certificate.~~_x000D_
_x000D_
The setup over here is pretty straightforward: Vault pki is used to issue the certificates and Vault agent is used to TLS cert auth against Vault server to request a renewed certificate. It's a chicken-and-egg scenario where initial certificate is issued manually and then gets indefinitely renewed. It's a poor man's certbot alternative that was supposed to work beautifully but it doesn't. _x000D_
_x000D_
Vault agent host:_x000D_
```_x000D_

title: Exponential backoff on api.LifetimeWatcher does not work
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We were using the Vault `LifetimeWatcher` from the `api` package in an internal project and noticed an issue with the backoff behavior of token renewal that was causing a bunch of our tests to fail when we upgraded to a new version of Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
The bug is here:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/1274f2d79a1ae6f589ad64af2c1ab930545943c0/api/lifetime_watcher.go#L348-L354_x000D_
_x000D_
`sleepDuration` appears to be the `time.Duration` used prior to re-running the renewal loop. In the case when `errBackoff` is `nil`, then a simple backoff duration is calculated based on the call to `calculateSleepDuration`. If `errBackoff` is **not nil** then `sleepDuration` is never set and the timeout in the following select block immediately fires again._x000D_
_x000D_
In our testing environment this was caught because our mock Vault server was returning an invalid response, so the renew operation was failing and we were getting an inordinate amount of immediate retries._x000D_
_x000D_
The fix is just refactoring the above block to capture the `errBackoff.NextBackoff()` value as `sleepDuration`. I'll open a PR shortly.

title: Enable bound CIDRs for LDAP and Kerberos groups and users
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Bound CIDRs can be defined for entities, groups, and backend roles, but this same security feature cannot be defined for LDAP or Kerberos groups and/or users. It doesn't seem to me like this limitation should be there._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Enable the "common token arguments" used in [backend roles](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/vault/latest/docs/resources/approle_auth_backend_role#common-token-arguments) for LDAP: `token_ttl`, `token_max_ttl`, `token_period`, `token_policies`, `token_bound_cidrs`, `token_explicit_max_ttl`, `token_no_default_policy`, `token_num_uses`, `token_type`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
We could try to use a Sentinel policy on the given policy to restrict access by IP address._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
None._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
It seems strange that other resources would have this security feature but not LDAP._x000D_

marcboudreau: Something that struck me is that the you included in the issue description is not valid as is. If your KV secrets engine is mounted at `secrets/`, this minimalistic policy will allow copying from `secrets` > `folder1` > `secret`: ``` path "secrets/data/folder1/secret" { capabilities = ["read"] } ``` This policy won't allow you to navigate to the secret by typing, but if prompted for a secret path, you can enter `secrets/folder1/secret` and the obfuscated secret details will be shown. You can click the copy to clipboard icon next to a key and its value will be copied. The above policy can be augmented to allow navigation to any key within the KV secrets engine mounted at `secrets/` as follows: ``` path "secrets/data/folder1/secret" { capabilities = ["read"] } path "secrets/metadata/*" { capabilities = ["list"] } ```
Monkeychip: We have updated the language on the flash message to mention that the CopyClipboard api requires a secure context, e.g. https vs http—PR [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/27045). I'm going to go ahead and close this ticket.

title: Unable to ascertain `vault agent` authentication status from metrics
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Currently `vault agent` only exposes counters for authentication failures and successes. It does not expose a metric to tell you the current state of authentication (i.e. `vault agent` has successfully authenticated and has a valid token or `vault agent` has been unable to authenticate and does not have a valid token)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
It would be good to expose a gauge (`vault.agent.auth.authenticated`) that is set to `1` if `vault agent` has a valid token or `0` if it does not._x000D_
This metric could then be used for alerting to act if `vault agent` does not have a valid token._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Currently this can be done in a round about way for looking at the value of `vault.agent.auth.failure` and `vault.agent.auth.success` in a sliding window, however, it would be nicer if there was a single metric that told you the current status of `vault agent` authentication._x000D_

title: add remove_roots_from_chain to more endpoints
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Before Vault 1.11.0 , the root CA were not included in the chain, and I believe rightfully so._x000D_
Then the root CAs were added from   a user’s request (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/13489), and then removed again with a special option in https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/16935 . This was motivated by the concern raised in this comment https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/16057#issuecomment-1164759195 , which were_x000D_
_x000D_
> Either they already have the root CA in their trust store, and don't need another copy of it - or they do not, in which case sending a self-signed certificate in the TLS handshake is not going to induce them to start trusting it_x000D_
_x000D_
Sadly, the root CAs are still included by default in some endpoint without the possibility to remove them. To me it means that I must manually parse the CA chain, meaning adding a crypto dependency on the client side to do so, just to remove the Root CA(s). It's kind of frustrating because Vault has already the information of which CA is Root in the chain._x000D_
_x000D_
I know I could just send them over the wire and the Root CA will just be ignored, but that a waste of resources. Besides, with postquantum the certificates will be become much bigger, and we will want to squeeze every octet in order to fit the MTU._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Please restore the old behavior, not sending the root CA(s), by adding the `remove_roots_from_chain` option to more endpoints._x000D_
_x000D_
The one that I see:_x000D_
- GET	/pki/cert/:serial_x000D_
- GET	/pki/cert/:serial/raw_x000D_
- GET	/pki/cert/:serial/raw/pem_x000D_
_x000D_
They are probably others_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Manually parse the certificates at the level of the vault client.

I suppose you could be referring to the, `GET /pki/cert/ca_chain` API, but you could just use `GET /pki/cert/ca` instead if you have a simple root/intermediary CA setup. | stormshield-gt: Thank you for your quick answer! As stipulated in the note inside the [API doc](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#read-certificate) : > As of Vault 1.11.0, these endpoints return the full chain (including this certificate and all parent issuers known to Vault) in the ca_chain response, for both the certificate and newer ca_chain fields. title: DynamoDB backed HA fails to release locks
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Our clusters use s3 for storage and dynamoDB for ha_storage in a 3 replica configuration on EKS. We have had a few instances where an underlying node has failed and when this happens and vault happens to be running on that host we are seeing vault fail. Looking at this issue it appears in instances where the master node gets disabled by any method other than someone terminating the pod the other replicas fail to take control and as a result vault stops working. This looks to be due to the lockfile in dynamodb preventing a new one taking over despite the fact that the code [suggest a TTL for this being 15s](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/physical/dynamodb/dynamodb.go#L60)_x000D_
_x000D_
Things we have tried that all resulted in failure of vault_x000D_
- Removing network interfaces from underlying hosts_x000D_
- Removing security groups_x000D_
- Disabling kubelet on underlying host_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Install vault using the included config_x000D_
2. Disable an underlying host somehow that hosts the current master (removing the security groups allowing communication probably the easiest)_x000D_
3. See that the other vault hosts do not take over (I timed up to 30 minutes but docs seem to suggest 15s TTL)_x000D_
_x000D_

Within 15 seconds of the master vault becoming unavailable or unable to service requests one of the others takes over_x000D_

title: Option to Hide Vault Version in UI for Enhanced Security
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
Currently, the HashiCorp Vault UI prominently displays the Vault version in the footer. While this is helpful for troubleshooting and support, it can pose a security concern in environments where exposing software versions is considered a risk. This issue requests the addition of a feature to optionally hide the Vault version number from the UI. In many security-sensitive environments, revealing software versions is discouraged as it can provide attackers with useful information for crafting targeted attacks._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
I propose adding a configuration option in the Vault server's configuration file that controls the display of the Vault version in the UI. This option could be a simple boolean flag:_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
ui_hide_version = true_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Using a Reverse Proxy: Setting up rewrite rules in a reverse proxy to remove the version number from the HTML. But this adds network complexity and can be error-prone._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
The addition of this feature would greatly benefit organizations that are bound by strict security and compliance regulations. It would allow them to use Vault without compromising on their security policies regarding information disclosure._x000D_

title: Allow aws engine to create orphaned credentials
body_text:
**Problem**_x000D_
I ran into an issue where I kept having AWS `iam_user` credentials generated by vault expire before their TTL was reached which was about 3 mins after creation when the TTL on the lease for the credentials was 1 hour.  This was very hard to track down and was counter intuitive to what the TTL represented on the lease.  I eventually found out that the generated credentials are tied to the TTL of the vault role that generated them.  For security purposes we want to have a low TTL on the actual role an end user or service gets but have a larger TTL for the generated/retrieved credentials.  It appears that this is not the case and the generated/retrieved credentials are limited to the max TTL of the token that generated them. _x000D_
_x000D_
It appears that someone else has also ran into this same exact issue and solved this by increasing the max TTL on the role used for credential generation.  We would not like to do this if possible for security purposes._x000D_
_x000D_
**Solution**_x000D_
I would like to introduce the ability to orphan the credentials retrieved/generated from the parent role.  This would allow for the TTL of the generated/retrieved credentials to actually be independent and work as one would think.  This [option](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands/token/create#orphan) already exists when creating a vault token itself and would be appreciated if this option could also exist for secret engine credentials._x000D_
_x000D_
**alternatives**_x000D_
The only alternative that I have considered is making the parent roles TTL as large as the max of the generated/retrieved credentials which we would like to avoid if possible for security purposes._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
References:_x000D_
- https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/9532_x000D_

title: Rate Limiting on /ui
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
We implemented several [Resource quotas](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/resource-quotas) to protect our Vault cluster the best as we can._x000D_
_x000D_
In parallel we created several metrics to follow rate limit events in our Vault Audit logs. _x000D_
_x000D_
Our setup configures a "very strict" rate limit global threshold and then we have several customized rate limit rules on our Auth Methods and Secret Engines. _x000D_
_x000D_
Our setup is good but it appears that since recent Vault versions (I do not know which one) we encounter several Rate Limit events on the `/ui` path in our Vault Audit Logs._x000D_
_x000D_
Here is a sample._x000D_
_x000D_
![image](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/assets/1327782/a53607b3-4d67-424c-8d47-8bdc42c0b2e5)_x000D_
_x000D_
 I read the source code of the _x000D_
[queryQuota](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a65d9133a1900acc43b8c1cdfc241f5d6c9bad59/vault/quotas/quotas.go#L534) function to understand how it works internally and it seems to me that the code could provide a quota for `/ui`._x000D_
_x000D_
But, when we try to create a quota for `/ui` it seems not possible._x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
vault write /sys/quotas/rate-limit/ui block_interval=60 interval=60 path=ui/ rate=60_x000D_
Error writing data to sys/quotas/rate-limit/ui: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT https://vault-sit-infra.secret.sit-infra.cloud.mymoneybank.fr/v1/sys/quotas/rate-limit/ui_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* invalid mount path "ui/"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Be able to create Resource Quotas on the `/ui` path._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Increase our global Resource Quota rule but in our opinion this is not ideal because it forces us to have a too high global rate limiting threshold.
top_3_comments_text: divyaac: Hi @bgaillard thank you for raising this issue! What is likely occurring here, is that there is a global quota and any request to the path `ui/` is causing this global rate limit quota to be exceeded. As of now, the reason we can't create a rate limit on a path like `ui/` is that ui is not a mount. If we were to enable rate limits on paths other than just mounts, customers might run into problems where they rate limit entire api paths, causing them to be inaccessible.

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault etcd storage backend uses etcd client v3.5.7 which does not work with TLSv1.3 ([link](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/215b53cf3b48ee761f4c40908b3874b2e5e95e9f/client/pkg/transport/listener.go#L572-L575)). The problem can be fixed by bumping the go.etcd.io/etcd/client version to [v3.5.8](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-3.5.md) or later ([link](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/15156))._x000D_

**Issue Description**_x000D_
I attempted to add the HashiCorp Apt repository on Ubuntu 24.04 "noble" using the recommended installation command, but encountered an error due to the absence of a release file for this distribution._x000D_
_x000D_
**Steps to Reproduce**_x000D_

2. Run the recommended command to add the HashiCorp repository:_x000D_

echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/hashicorp-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.releases.hashicorp.com $(lsb_release -cs) main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/hashicorp.list_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
3. Run `sudo apt update` and observe the error related to the missing Release file._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected Behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
The HashiCorp repository should support Ubuntu 24.04 "noble", allowing the successful addition of the repository and subsequent installation of HashiCorp packages._x000D_
_x000D_
**Actual Behavior**_x000D_

The attempt to update the package list from the repository fails with the following error:_x000D_
```_x000D_
Ign:5 https://apt.releases.hashicorp.com noble InRelease_x000D_
Err:6 https://apt.releases.hashicorp.com noble Release_x000D_
  404  Not Found [IP: 2600:9000:223d:e800:18:566b:ecc0:93a1 443]_x000D_
Reading package lists... Done_x000D_
E: The repository 'https://apt.releases.hashicorp.com noble Release' does not have a Release file._x000D_
N: Updating from such a repository can't be done securely, and is therefore disabled by default._x000D_

_x000D_
***Additional Context***_x000D_
Ubuntu 24.04 "noble" was released on April 25th, and it's [not officially supported](https://www.hashicorp.com/official-packaging-guide) in repository support. I am opening this issue to inquire about and track the progress of adding "noble" support to the HashiCorp repository._x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Rotating the client certificate/key used in a Consul secret backend for Vault does not seem possible when Vault itself is used to bootstrap the Consul ACL system. The `/{mount}/config/access` endpoint which is used to set the certificate/key will overwrite all fields, so when we send an updated cert without the bootstrap token, Vault assumes that we want to bootstrap the ACL system of the associated Consul cluster, which fails since Consul says No.  We don't have the token because Vault swallows it when it issues the bootstrap command to Consul, and we shouldn't need to know it since Vault is in charge of the process and should have it stored somewhere._x000D_
_x000D_
This failure looks like:_x000D_

vault_consul_secret_backend.consul-dev: Modifying... [id=consul-dev]_x000D_
╷_x000D_
│ Error: error configuring Consul configuration for "consul-dev": Error making API request._x000D_
│_x000D_
│ URL: PUT https://vault.dev.supercompany.com:8200/v1/consul-dev/config/access_x000D_

│_x000D_
│   with vault_consul_secret_backend.consul-dev,_x000D_
│   on consul-dev.tf line 32, in resource "vault_consul_secret_backend" "consul-dev":_x000D_
│   32: resource "vault_consul_secret_backend" "consul-dev" {_x000D_
│_x000D_
╵_x000D_
```_x000D_

title: Missing retry logic when using GCS backend might lead to cluster unavailable
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When acquiring the leadership, a Vault replica will start restoring leases. If a single restore fails because GCS is unavailable, then that vault instance gets sealed. In a fairly large environment with lots of leases there're chances where this can happen to all the vault replicas in a short period of time, causing the whole cluster to seal. This has happened to us in a production cluster with GCS returning just a few (5) 503 (which it's considered a retryable error and the golang client used in this vault version (v1.30.1) should retry by default unless the context is canceled which I couldn't spot it)._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Hard to reproduce as it depends on a third party being unavailable._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The golang GCS client library will retry as it's considered a retryble operation and status code_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.15.4_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v.1.15.6 (irrelevant) _x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Vault cluster 3 replicas running on kubernetes using GCS as the backend and kms to encrypt the keys_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
            api_addr     = "https://vault.{{ .Release.Namespace }}.svc:8200"_x000D_
            cluster_addr = "https://$(POD_IP_ADDR):8201"_x000D_

              region     = "{{ include "elvlib.cluster.gcpRegion" $ }}"_x000D_
              key_ring   = "{{ include "vault.config.keyRing" $ }}"_x000D_
              crypto_key = "{{ .Values.cryptoKey }}"_x000D_
            }_x000D_

**Additional context**_x000D_
The golang client library for GCS supports retries by default. The response code (503) is a retryable error and the HTTP method (GET) is considered idempotent so it should be retrying unless the context is canceled which I could not spot it (and doesn't seem so as the Restore function error will be different as per the code:_x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
defer func() {_x000D_
_x000D_
		// Turn off restore mode. We can do this safely without the lock because_x000D_
_x000D_
		// if restore mode finished successfully, restore mode was already_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
		// Stop() function to shut everything down._x000D_
_x000D_
		atomic.StoreInt32(m.restoreMode, 0)_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
		switch {_x000D_
_x000D_
		case retErr == nil:_x000D_
_x000D_
		case strings.Contains(retErr.Error(), context.Canceled.Error()):_x000D_
_x000D_
			// Don't run error func because we lost leadership_x000D_
_x000D_
			m.logger.Warn("context canceled while restoring leases, stopping lease loading")_x000D_
_x000D_
			retErr = nil_x000D_
_x000D_
		case errwrap.Contains(retErr, ErrBarrierSealed.Error()):_x000D_
_x000D_
			// Don't run error func because we're likely already shutting down_x000D_
_x000D_
			m.logger.Warn("barrier sealed while restoring leases, stopping lease loading")_x000D_
_x000D_
			retErr = nil_x000D_
_x000D_
		default:_x000D_
_x000D_
			m.logger.Error("error restoring leases", "error", retErr)_x000D_
_x000D_
			if errorFunc != nil {_x000D_
_x000D_
				errorFunc()_x000D_
_x000D_
			}_x000D_
_x000D_
		}_x000D_
_x000D_
	}()_x000D_
```_x000D_
	_x000D_
	Google Cloud Support confirmed we're not receiving a lot of 503s and also our monitoring confirms the same, during the time window where the loop of:_x000D_
	for i in [0,1,2]:_x000D_
	- acquire lock_x000D_
	- restore leases_x000D_
	- fail to read lease with 503_x000D_
_x000D_
We only see 3 503s, 1 per replica._x000D_

title: [PKI, ACME] Allow configuration of challenge port for http-01
body_text:
When requesting certificates using `certbot certonly --standalone` one can specify a different port for serving the `http-01` challenge (by using `--http-01-port`). This is useful if port 80 is already in use by other means (for example it's being redirected to the https port 443 by a reverse proxying web server)._x000D_
_x000D_
Since `certbot` allows to specify a different port, it would be great if this could be configured in Vault, too (defaulting to 80).

Dereference the URL using an HTTP GET request. This request MUST be sent to TCP port 80 on the HTTP server. title: Update dependent Prometheus library versions
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Hi there! An issue I noticed is that Vault is using fairly outdated 	github.com/prometheus/client_golang and github.com/prometheus/common versions. In the latest Vault v1.16.2 go.mod, I noticed that the versions used are:_x000D_
> github.com/prometheus/client_golang v1.14.0 (Nov 8, 2022)_x000D_
> github.com/prometheus/common v0.37.0 (Jul 14, 2022)_x000D_
_x000D_
Whereas the newest versions for these prometheus libraries are:_x000D_
> github.com/prometheus/client_golang v1.19.0 (Feb 27, 2024)_x000D_
> github.com/prometheus/common v0.53.0 (Apr 18, 2024)_x000D_
_x000D_
And because of this, Vault is conflicting with other components that are using newer prometheus libraries in our product. The incompatibility occurs because for [github.com/prometheus/common v0.48.0](https://github.com/prometheus/common/releases/tag/v0.48.0) or newer, they unexported format strings which Vault has been using, specifically expfmt.FmtText. It appears that Vault side code change will be needed in metricsutil.go to update these dependency versions:_x000D_
_x000D_
> 	e := expfmt.NewEncoder(buf, expfmt.FmtText)_x000D_
> 	......_x000D_
> 	resp.Data[logical.HTTPContentType] = string(expfmt.FmtText)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
The best solution is probably to update to the new dependency versions, and make implementation tweaks in Vault to be compatible. It would be greatly appreciated if you could please consider this request! If needed I can create a PR for this as well. :)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
N/A. I think for quality and security reasons, Vault should use these newer versions eventually._x000D_
_x000D_

N/A._x000D_

title: Proxy: Support chroot_namespace on listener block
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
As a platform engineer, I want to configure Vault Proxy to authenticate to an Enterprise HCP Vault that is namespaced. I don't want to expose clients such as the cert-manager CSI driver, to the detail of having to know the namespace. I would like Vault Proxy to send all requests with a `X-Vault-Namespace` comprised of the Vault Proxy namespace possibly combined with a child namespace passed in by the client of the proxy._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
`chroot_namespace` added to the listener block with the same behavior as described in https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/listener/tcp#chroot_namespace_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Using a Kubernetes pod running a Vault proxy sidecar:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
# ps aux_x000D_
PID   USER     TIME  COMMAND_x000D_
    1 root      0:01 vault proxy -config=/etc/vault/config_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Approaches I tried that didn't work:_x000D_
_x000D_
## Namespace in `vault` stanza._x000D_
```_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address            = "127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
  tls_disable        = true_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
vault {_x000D_
  address   = "REDACTED"_x000D_
  ca_cert   = "/etc/vault/ca.crt"_x000D_
  namespace = "REDACTED"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
## Namespace in `listener` stanza_x000D_
```_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address            = "127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
  tls_disable        = true_x000D_
  chroot_namespace   = "REDACTED"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
vault {_x000D_
  address   = "REDACTED"_x000D_
  ca_cert   = "/etc/vault/ca.crt"_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
In a Vault Proxy chrooted to the given namespace, I would like client HTTP requests whether coming from the Vault CLI, SDK, or custom HTTP client to be mutated such that the X-Vault-Namespace header is added automatically if not present and that the value of the header be the chroot_namespace, and if the header is present, that it's assumed to be a child namespace and therefore the value is mutated by prepending the parent namespace, similar to how chroot_namespace functions._x000D_
_x000D_

This sounds like exactly the option I want, and I think I will use it for some of our applications. It doesn't appear to work for cert-manager, but I have a workaround. any web browser_x000D_

title: Document token format
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I worked on https://github.com/github/redacting-logger/pull/48 and didn't find an easy answer to "what is the format used for tokens?"

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I would like this to be written in the doc. Something as simple as:

---

Vault tokens are comprised of a prefix and a body.

- The prefix indicates the token's type:

  Token Type | Vault 1.9.x or earlier | Vault 1.10 and later
  -- | -- | --
  Service tokens | s. | hvs.
  Batch tokens | b. | hvb.
  Recovery tokens | r. | hvr.

- The body is a randomly-generated 24 characters [Base62](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base62) string.

Token are expected to match the following regexp: `(hv)?[sbr]\.[a-zA-Z0-9]{24}`

---

Obviously, not all the info is required, but would ease the understanding.

**Explain any additional use-cases**

When writing a regex or a tool to detect vault tokens, an official source would be appreciated.

**Additional context**

cc https://github.com/github/redacting-logger/pull/48

title: Can static role autorotation be disabled and only manual api rotation work?
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Right now AFAICT you have an api call to force an early rotation. However you cannot turn off auto rotation. We want exact control by a coordinating app so we can a) have more control over when rotation occurs (rotation_schedule isn't sufficient), and b) we can rotate it ourselves and then trigger a redeploy in k8s of the app to switch between two different roles (with overlapping activity). I see no way to have auto rotation without downtime._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
If rotation_period is set to 0 or -1 (your choice) auto rotation no longer occurs and only the api call for manual rotation works_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
An event based system would work. However vault doesn't have events for these rotations, AND they would have to be 100% reliable AND to avoid downtime we'd need pairs of interrelated roles to switch the app on._x000D_

title: Go Client Libraries can't be used as MPL without BUSL code being distributed
body_text:
Hashicorp has said left the various client libraries for their projects as open source under the MPL license. That includes the Go Client libraries for Vault. All the files are labeled as MPL, as is the license._x000D_
_x000D_
The problem is that Go doesn't understand folders all that well. In order to install the client libraries the entire Vault repository is downloaded, including the closed source code. This can cause issues around licenses and legal headaches for people who want to use the open source licensed code._x000D_
_x000D_
The ideal solution would be to split the API code into a stand alone repository with just the open source licensed code.

title: Hexadecimal certificate serial number in entity alias metadata would be great
body_text:
_x000D_
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
When using TLS authentication with the metadata of entity aliases activated with [enable_identity_alias_metadata](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/cert#enable_identity_alias_metadata), the serial number is returned as a string representation of  its decimal value. _x000D_
For instance "207720964414718439776028734852258731377870138924"._x000D_
_x000D_
Here is the following code that does that:_x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/d1e30badfadfd026c8846810193e41120d3a7a94/builtin/credential/cert/path_login.go#L149_x000D_
_x000D_
This representation is not very convenient to use, because all the endpoints of the PKI API take the  hexadecimal representation of the serial number separated with colon._x000D_
We can still recreate this representation at the client side, but because the integer is bigger than u128, for most of the programming languages, we must use an external library to parse it. As supply chain attacks are a big concern for me, I would like to have the fewest dependency as possible._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Would you be OK to return the hexadecimal representation directly?_x000D_
I think it's just a matter of calling this function https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/d1e30badfadfd026c8846810193e41120d3a7a94/sdk/helper/certutil/helpers.go#L112_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Adding an external library at the client side and build the hexadecimal representation from here._x000D_
_x000D_

title: Configure Vault rotate to automatically AWS root credentials periodically
body_text:
First off, I searched for other similar requests and I couldn't find anything. I appologize if this has already been discussed and I missed it. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Today, Vault has the capability to rotate root AWS credentials manually as well as to rotate static role credentials automatically at a configured interval, but there is no functionality to automatically rotate root credentials._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
When the root AWS credentials are provided to vault, there should be an option to have Vault rotate those credentials at configurable interval._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I've attempted to create a static role for the same AWS user as my root credentials and Vault can rotate those credentials periodically. Vault, though, does not update its root credentials when it rotates the credentials for this AWS user._x000D_
_x000D_
This could be accomplished with a cron job, but it'd be much simpler and cleaner to be able to accomplish this natively with Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
Adding "proxy_protocol_behavior" = "deny_unauthorized" produces the following error:_x000D_
```_x000D_
error parsing 'listener': listeners.0: unsupported value supplied for proxy_protocol_behavior: "deny_unauthorized"_x000D_

_x000D_
After checking the source, it became clear the option was actually called "deny_authorized"_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
Changing the configuration to "proxy_protocol_behavior" = "deny_authorized" produces the following error:_x000D_
```_x000D_
Error initializing listener of type tcp: failed configuring PROXY protocol wrapper: unknown behavior type for proxy proto config_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
After further examination of the source, it became clear "deny_authorized" was also not a valid choice._x000D_
_x000D_
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/7dc4255a13db355f3157215450b02faffad1ae30/helper/proxyutil/proxyutil.go#L52_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Add the option `proxy_protocol_behavior = "deny_unauthorized"` to configuration_x000D_
2. Start vault_x000D_
4. See error_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Normal operation_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (master)_x000D_
_x000D_

title: JWT authentication checks bound_audiences despite bound_claims is defined in v1.16.3
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
When authenticating to Vault using JWT auth method and a JWT role, the `bound_audiences` is checked even if `bound_claims` is defined in the role._x000D_
_x000D_
When the `bound_audiences` of the JWT role is empty, it results in the following error: `Authentication failed: audience claim found in JWT but no audiences bound to the role`, even if the provided JWT meets the required bound claims_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Configure a JWT Back-End_x000D_
_x000D_
2. Configure a JWT role for this Back-End_x000D_
_x000D_
```console_x000D_
vault write auth/jwt/role/my-role - <<EOF_x000D_
{_x000D_
   "role_type": "jwt",_x000D_
   "user_claim": "user_email",_x000D_
   "policies": "my-policy",_x000D_
   "ttl": "1h",_x000D_
   "bound_claims": { "project_id": ["123"] }_x000D_
}_x000D_
EOF_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
The JWT role should define a `bound_claims`. I have used `project_id` as I have used GitLab as a JWT auth Back-End._x000D_
_x000D_
3. Log in Vault through the UI by selecting the JWT auth method and using the configured JWT role `my-role`._x000D_
_x000D_
4. It should display `audience claim found in JWT but no audiences bound to the role`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
As `bound_claims` is defined in the role, `bound_audiences` should not be checked when authenticating._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`):_x000D_
_x000D_
```console_x000D_
Key             Value_x000D_
---             -----_x000D_
Seal Type       shamir_x000D_
Initialized     true_x000D_
Sealed          false_x000D_

Threshold       1_x000D_

Cluster Name    ***_x000D_
Cluster ID      ***_x000D_
HA Enabled      false_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`):_x000D_
_x000D_
```console_x000D_
Vault v1.16.3 (e92d9a57018f43360e2e3717b3b6a7f650c88f4c), built 2024-05-29T14:28:42Z_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture:_x000D_
_x000D_
Running on Windows_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
storage "file" {_x000D_
  path = "C:/Program Files/Vault/1.16.3/file"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
  cluster_address = "[::]:8201"_x000D_
  tls_disable = 1_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
plugin_directory = "C:/Program Files/Vault/1.16.3/plugins"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
The issue does not occur in v1.16.2._x000D_
It looks to be a regression on Vault v1.16.3.

title: web ui cli not focused when opened
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
When opening the web CLI "Vault Web REPL" by clicking on the button in the upper left, the CLI opens, but you have to manually give the prompt focus to use it. You can't simply give the black area that is the CLI focus as if it were a unit, you have to specifically go to the prompt area at the bottom._x000D_
_x000D_
Relatedly, to close the web CLI, you have to go back to the button at the upper left of the screen._x000D_
_x000D_
These are sort of minor quality-of-life / ease-of-use improvements._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
It would be nice if - like a normal terminal application launching - when the button was clicked to open the web CLI, the prompt got focus immediately instead of requiring manual intervention. _x000D_
_x000D_
Relatedly, it would be a little nicer if the CLI had a little [x] (upper right?) to click and close it, would accept a ctrl-d, or some such to be able to close it without having to journey back to the top left of the screen to make it go away._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
The alternative is to give the prompt focus manually when it is opened, and close it the only way that's currently possible by clicking the little icon in the upper left of the screen._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
One of our specific use cases is fetching a TOTP token. We store the TOTP path as part of the kv secret. So while visiting that kv secret in the web UI, we copy the TOTP path, open the CLI and are ready to type `vault read <paste_totp_path>` but this is interrupted because the CLI (unexpectedly) doesn't have focus yet._x000D_
