title: `VAULT_AGENT_ADDR` has higher precedence than `-agent-address`
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
From [the docs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands#environment-variables):_x000D_
> Flags always take precedence over the environment variables._x000D_
_x000D_
Thus, given_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
export VAULT_AGENT_ADDR=http://env-host_x000D_
vault <cmd> -agent-address http://cli-host <...>_x000D_
```_x000D_
I would expect the 'cli-host' to be used.  I do not know if this holds true for every sub-command, but `vault status` and `vault read` use the environment variable (I suspect it affects the majority of sub-commands, if not all)._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
I encountered this issue in a live environment (actual running server and agent), but the actual issue does not require these and using `-output-curl-string` is a convenient/quick way to illustrate in isolation._x000D_
```sh_x000D_
$ export VAULT_AGENT_ADDR=http://env.invalid_x000D_
$ env | grep -i vault_x000D_
VAULT_AGENT_ADDR=http://env.invalid_x000D_
$ vault status -agent-address http://cli.invalid -output-curl-string _x000D_
curl -H "X-Vault-Request: true" -H "X-Vault-Token: $(vault print token)" http://env.invalid/v1/sys/seal-status_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
$ export VAULT_AGENT_ADDR=http://env.invalid_x000D_
$ env | grep -i vault_x000D_
VAULT_AGENT_ADDR=http://env.invalid_x000D_
$ vault status -agent-address http://cli.invalid -output-curl-string _x000D_
curl -H "X-Vault-Request: true" -H "X-Vault-Token: $(vault print token)" http://cli.invalid/v1/sys/seal-status_x000D_
```_x000D_
(using address `http://cli.invalid`, not `http://env.invalid`)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): `1.12.6` (but not relevant)_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): verified with `1.11.6`, `1.12.6`, `1.16.3`, and `main`_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: alpine/amd64 (but not relevant)_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
I created a longer reproduction to_x000D_
* assert/verify some of the combinations of "agent wins over server" and "flags win over environment"_x000D_
* show the code flow (with injected logging) to pinpoint the issue_x000D_
_x000D_
```sh_x000D_
#!/bin/sh_x000D_
_x000D_
: "${VAULT:=./bin/vault}"_x000D_
_x000D_
export CLI_AGENT_ADDR=http://cli-agent.test_x000D_
export CLI_ADDR=http://cli-server.test_x000D_
export ENV_AGENT_ADDR=http://env-agent.test_x000D_
export ENV_ADDR=http://env-server.test_x000D_
_x000D_
unset VAULT_ADDR_x000D_
unset VAULT_AGENT_ADDR_x000D_
_x000D_
"$VAULT" -version_x000D_
echo_x000D_
(_x000D_
  echo "[WORKS] expect cli-agent.test (agent flag trumps server flag)"_x000D_
  "$VAULT" status -address="$CLI_ADDR" -agent-address="$CLI_AGENT_ADDR" -output-curl-string_x000D_
)_x000D_
echo_x000D_

When Vault is run in Kubernetes with database backend, and each pod thinks about it as a separate Vault instance, created on one pod auth/role and secret storage are not available in other pods until they are restarted._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Deploy Vault via Helm chart on Kubernetes cluster with MySQL database backend._x000D_
2. Set more than 1 pod for Vault._x000D_
3. Wait for pods to form more than 1 cluster, check that by running `vault operator members` in each pod._x000D_
4. Once step 3 is completed, create a new Kubernetes auth for other Kubernetes cluster, along with policy, role, and secret storage_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault auth enable --path="${CLUSTER_NAME}" kubernetes_x000D_
_x000D_
vault write "auth/${CLUSTER_NAME}/config" \_x000D_
token_reviewer_jwt="$(cat ./token_jwt.txt)" \_x000D_
kubernetes_host="https://$(cat ./apiserver.txt):6443" \_x000D_
kubernetes_ca_cert="$(cat ./ca.crt)" \_x000D_
issuer="https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local" \_x000D_
disable_local_ca_jwt="true"_x000D_
_x000D_
vault policy write "${CLUSTER_NAME}-service-policy" - <"${CLUSTER_NAME}.json"_x000D_
_x000D_
vault write "auth/${CLUSTER_NAME}/role/${CLUSTER_NAME}-role" \_x000D_
    bound_service_account_names="${SERVICE_ACCOUNT}" \_x000D_
    bound_service_account_namespaces="${APP_NAMESPACES}" \_x000D_
    policies="${CLUSTER_NAME}-service-policy" \_x000D_
    ttl=24h_x000D_
_x000D_
vault secrets enable -path="${CLUSTER_NAME}" --description="${CLUSTER_NAME} secrets" kv-v2_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Calling_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault auth list_x000D_
vault policy list_x000D_
vault list auth/"${CLUSTER_NAME}"/role_x000D_
vault secrets list_x000D_
```_x000D_
Would show newly created objects in each pod._x000D_
_x000D_
**Actual behavior**_x000D_
Calling the commands above shows auth/role/secrets only in pod/group where it was created. Nevertheless, policy is seen in all pods._x000D_
Restarting pod from other group, even if it would not join the group above, allows it to see the auth/role/secrets._x000D_

title: Vault creates second AWS access key with AWS Static Roles after rotation period expires
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When managing an AWS IAM user's credentials using static roles, if a single access key exists and the rotation period expires, Vault will create a second key rather than rotate the existing key. At a minimum, this conflicts with [Vault documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/aws) that reads:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
At each rotation, Vault will rotate the oldest existing credential._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Ideally, we should be able to maintain a single key with Vault. We have security requirements that specify keys must be rotated after X days. Essentially, the configured `rotation_period` would need to be X/2 in order for us to meet this requirement. Otherwise, the oldest key will not be rotated until twice the configured `rotation_period` has passed._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Within the AWS console, create IAM user `my-test-user`. Ensure no access keys exist._x000D_
2. Run `vault write aws/static-roles/test username=my-test-user rotation_period=300`_x000D_
3. Within the AWS console, verify a single access key for `my-test-user` has been created._x000D_
4. Wait five minutes. Within the AWS console, observe that there are now two access keys._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Only a single access key should exist._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.16.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.15.4_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS_x000D_

From the documentation there is a note that reads `Vault will create a new credential upon configuration, and if the maximum number of access keys already exist, Vault will rotate the oldest one. Vault must do this to know the credential.` The maximum number of keys for an IAM User is actually 2, so Vault's first creates a second key on the static account user. On the next rotation, it then does what you quoted by rotating the key of the oldest credential which will be your first one. | ebarrett-Ocient: @robmonte I don't believe what I'm observing conflicts with the documentation. Per the documentation you quoted, upon configuration of a static role, Vault will rotate the oldest key upon configuration _if_ it exists. In the scenario I'm describing, no IAM keys exist when the static role is configured so Vault creates one. Upon the expiration of the rotation period, rather than rotate the key it created, it creates a brand new one. Then, once the rotation period expires again, it rotates that original key. If this is intentional, then I believe the documentation should be updated to better reflect this. Regardless of whether it's intentional or not, I believe it would be more valuable if Vault only ever maintained a single access key. | robmonte: @ebarrett-Ocient I think it is intentional, yeah. title: Missing breadcrumbs when navigating secrets v1 engine in Vault UI

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
In the UI for a secrets v1 engine, the breadcrumbs at the top of the UI only update when viewing a secret itself, but not when viewing any of the "folders" above the secrets._x000D_
_x000D_
In other words, if I have a secrets v1 engine mounted at `secret/`, and I click on that engine on the home page of the UI dashboard, the breadcrumb at the top reads `Secrets / secret`. Then, if I navigate to a secret that lives at `secret/apps/portal-app/prod/db-password` by clicking on each of the folders in turn, the breadcrumb at the top continues to simply read `Secrets / secret` until I finally click on the actual `db-password` entry, when the breadcrumbs finally update to read `secret / apps / portal-app / prod / db-password`._x000D_

This is different from the UI for the secrets v2 engine, which includes all the "subfolders" in the breadcrumbs as they are navigated._x000D_

3. From the home page of the Vault UI, navigate serially through the "folders" to get to the new secret, and watch the breadcrumbs at the top of the UI._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
Is it possible that the context has _already_ been cancelled by the time we are asking the audit broker to write an entry in the audit devices, and therefore we get this error?_x000D_

the cluster_name is very useful when discovering metrics/dashboards however the auto generated names don't say much. _x000D_

_x000D_

* https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/11988

title: Clarify and Improve FieldData.GetOk
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
While working with the vault SDK to build a plugin, I wanted to set a parameter that has a default value. To do that I set `Default` in [FieldSchema](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/framework#FieldSchema) and then called [FieldData.GetOk](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk/framework#FieldData.GetOk) to get the default value out. To my surprise, when the value isn't set, the default value isn't returned. I then found https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/23963 which describes the exact same problem I have: `GetOk` does not return a default value if no value is provided. `Get` _will_ return a default value, but will panic if the field name is wrong. Conceptually it seems `GetOk` should also return a default, but the issue discussion points out that this would be backwards incompatible. I wonder if it would be possible to a) document this difference in behaviour and b) introduce a method `GetOkOrDefault` that handles this better?_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
A method that returns a default like `Get` but doesn't panic like `GetOk` does._x000D_
Documentation on `GetOk` that explicitly points out that default values will not be returned._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
N/A_x000D_

This is the pattern that we usually use in Vault: ```go if val, ok := d.GetOk("foo"); ok { f = val.(string) } else if req.Operation == logical.CreateOperation { // grab the Default value f = d.Get("foo").(string) } if f == "" { return logical.ErrorResponse("f is empty string"), nil } ``` | fairclothjm: Hello @fruechel-canva! Another option, if you want safety around the field name is `GetOkErr`: ```go result, ok, err := d.GetOkErr("foo") if err != nil { fmt.Println("error reading", "foo", err) } if ok && result == nil { // grab the default here result = d.Schema["foo"].DefaultOrZero() } else if !ok && result == nil { fmt.Println("not ok, result is nil") } else { // happy path fmt.Println("result: ", result.(string)) } ``` I realize both of those options are quite verbose. I think adding something like `GetOkOrDefault` is probably a good idea.

title: Feature request: defer the release of dynamic AAD/Entra ID credentials until ready
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
When we've started our HCP Vault journey one of the key features sold to us was ability to utilize dynamic credentials. Unfortunately, we've discovered that it's not as simple as it may sound. We've soon discovered that once new secret is generated by Azure and returned to HCP Vault it is not immediately ready to be used due to the slow nature of Azure AD (Entra Id) API. It takes time for the secret to propagate through Azure fabric. According to our observations on good days it may take 2 minutes for dynamic secret to be ready, while on bad days it can be up to 10m (or even more). We are aware that if credentials are retrieved via Terraform HCP Vault provider then you have some basic logic implemented to check credentials are ready to be used within Terraform, but we don't retrieve our credentials via Terraform. Instead we make them available for the CI job within GitLab runners, and assign them to env variables such as `ARM_CLIENT_ID`, `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` - meaning these are available to Terraform job and also outside of it._x000D_
_x000D_
We have implemented our own logic to defer the release of credentials using sliding window algorithm (slightly improved logic of your Go implementation for Terraform). However, it still sometimes gives us false positives._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
We'd like Vault to be able to validate dynamic credentials and deferring their release to the user until such time when these can be safely used with guaranteed outcome. This can be done as an optional feature - i.e. when credentials are requested from Vault, an additional param `defer: true` can control this logic on/off (we appreciate not everyone wants to wait - but we do, as it is critical from our CI job perspective). Also, you have WAY more capabilities to implement and evolve this logic better than us. We don't want to look after this complex validation logic._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
An alternative to this approach would be another feature implemented by you - rotation of static Azure credentials. So, if we have Azure creds stored in KV2, an ability to at least rotate the secret on a regular basis would be deemed as an acceptable alternative, similar to how you rotate root creds for Azure integration, although it needs to happen on a scheduled basis. This might not be a KV2 engine (because we understand it's not designed for rotation), it may be an improvement to Dynamic creds logic - e.g. rotate a secret for Azure creds every 60 minutes and invalidate old creds 30 minutes after... something between those lines. It's not pure dynamic per job credentials, but it's BETTER than static secret stored in KV2 engine._x000D_
_x000D_
Here's our code snippet for creds validation written in Python:_x000D_
_x000D_
```python_x000D_
async def validate_azure_token(client_id, client_secret, tenant_id):_x000D_
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:_x000D_
        async with session.post(_x000D_
            f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/oauth2/v2.0/token",_x000D_
            data={_x000D_
                'grant_type': 'client_credentials',_x000D_
                'client_id': client_id,_x000D_
                'client_secret': client_secret,_x000D_
                'scope': 'https://management.azure.com/.default'_x000D_
            },_x000D_
            timeout=requests_timeouts_x000D_
        ) as response:_x000D_
            if response.status == 401:_x000D_
                return False_x000D_
            response.raise_for_status()_x000D_
            return True_x000D_
_x000D_
async def validate_azure_credentials(client_id, client_secret):_x000D_
    tenant_id = os.getenv("ARM_TENANT_ID")_x000D_
    if not tenant_id:_x000D_
        nprint("Unable to validate Azure credentials "_x000D_
               "because ARM_TENANT_ID is not set.", file=sys.stderr)_x000D_
        return False_x000D_
    nprint(f"Validating {client_id[0]} and {client_secret[0]}.")_x000D_
_x000D_
    isw_size = int(os.getenv('VAULT_VALIDATION_ISW_SIZE', 20))_x000D_
    isw_rate = float(os.getenv('VAULT_VALIDATION_ISW_RATE', 1))_x000D_
    osw_size = int(os.getenv('VAULT_VALIDATION_OSW_SIZE', 5 * isw_size))_x000D_
    osw_rate = float(os.getenv('VAULT_VALIDATION_OSW_RATE', 0.6))_x000D_
    wait_slot_s = float(os.getenv('VAULT_VALIDATION_WAIT_SLOT', 1))_x000D_
    max_wait_time_s = float(os.getenv('VAULT_VALIDATION_TIMEOUT', 900))_x000D_
_x000D_
    attempts = []_x000D_
    now_time = time.time()_x000D_
    end_time = now_time + max_wait_time_s_x000D_
    nprint(f"Validating {client_id[0]} and {client_secret[0]}: "_x000D_
          f"Delaying 1st attempt by {isw_size * wait_slot_s:.2f}s.")_x000D_
    await asyncio.sleep(isw_size * wait_slot_s)_x000D_
    while True:_x000D_
        if time.time() > end_time:_x000D_
            nprint(f"Azure credentials {client_id[0]} and {client_secret[0]} "_x000D_
                    "take too much time to propagate. Skipping...", file=sys.stderr)_x000D_
            return False_x000D_
_x000D_
        try:_x000D_
            attempts.append(_x000D_
                await validate_azure_token(client_id[1], client_secret[1], tenant_id)_x000D_
            )_x000D_
_x000D_
            try:_x000D_
                # Calculate inner sliding window score:_x000D_
                # - Remove last element from the list [:-1] (we assume it's False)_x000D_
                # - Reverse the list [::-1]_x000D_
                # - Find the index of the first False element .index(False)_x000D_
                #   (it is last in the original list)_x000D_
                # - Sum all elements from the index of the first False element_x000D_
                #   in the original list_x000D_
                # If there are no False elements, then exception is raised, where_x000D_
                # we just sum all elements from the original list_x000D_
                isw_score = sum(attempts[len(attempts) - attempts[:-1][::-1].index(False) - 1:])_x000D_
            except ValueError:_x000D_
                isw_score = sum(attempts)_x000D_
_x000D_
            wait_slot = wait_slot_s_x000D_
            if not attempts[-1]:_x000D_
                wait_slot = round(isw_size / ((isw_score + 1) % isw_size), 2)_x000D_
                nprint(f"Validating {client_id[0]} and {client_secret[0]}: "_x000D_
                       f"Attempt #{len(attempts):03d} has failed. "_x000D_
                       f"Restarting in {wait_slot:.2f}s.")_x000D_
            elif isw_score / isw_size >= isw_rate:_x000D_
                # Outer sliding window results_x000D_
                osw_score = sum(attempts[-(osw_size + isw_size):-isw_size])_x000D_
                if osw_score / osw_size >= osw_rate:_x000D_
                    nprint(f"Azure credentials {client_id[0]} and {client_secret[0]} "_x000D_
                            "are valid and ready to be used.")_x000D_
                    # Print statistics to help with fine tuning_x000D_
                    # Remove before production_x000D_
                    nprint("Parameters:")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"  - Outer sliding window size: {osw_size}.")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"  - Outer sliding window rate: {osw_rate}.")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"  - Inner sliding window size: {isw_size}.")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"  - Max wait time: {max_wait_time_s} s.")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"  - Wait slot: {wait_slot_s} s.")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"Total validation time: {time.time() - now_time}.")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"Total attempts: {len(attempts)}.")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"Total successful attempts: {sum(attempts)}.")_x000D_
                    nprint(f"Total successful attempts over a sliding window: {osw_score}.")_x000D_
                    return True_x000D_
            await asyncio.sleep(wait_slot)_x000D_
        except Exception as e:_x000D_
            nprint("Unable to validate Azure credentials "_x000D_
                  f"{client_id[0]} and {client_secret[0]}: {e}",_x000D_
                  file=sys.stderr)_x000D_
            return False_x000D_
```

title: Allow revocation of expired certificates
body_text:
This is a follow-up of https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/19452._x000D_
_x000D_
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
This is for embedded software development._x000D_
_x000D_
We use the Vault PKI to sign software releases. Releases themselves are signed by a certificate which has a very short expiration date (hours), since they should not be used for anything else than signing the current release and then the private key is thrown away._x000D_
_x000D_
If however we have a software release which is deemed insecure, we use the CRL to block software updates to that version. Since a CVE / security finding can happen at any point in the years (!) to come, we need to be able to revoke an already expired certificate._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
We would like an optional parameter to the `/pki/revoke` endpoint which skips the [expiration check](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/89276a56b2267ca49041be0bd9c7be7c96d3b94d/builtin/logical/pki/crl_util.go#L998) in `crl_util.go`._x000D_
_x000D_
Alternatively, it might be even better and even easier to augment `/pki/config/crl` to a boolean option `allow_expired_cert_revocation`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
Extending the lifetime of the code signing certificate to match the intermediate. However, since also intermediates are rotated on a yearly or 6-months basis, we still have the same issue as any leaf certificate expiration will be bounded by that, and a revocation can happen far later._x000D_
_x000D_
We can obviously use `/pki/issuer/:issuer_ref/sign-revocation-list` and maintain that ourselves._x000D_
_x000D_
Else we would need to sign the "CRL" with a detached signature (and handle that in code)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
See https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/19452._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
N/A

title: Incorrect lease duration - aws secret mount
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
We have two AWS secret mounts - `aws-dev` and `aws-prod`. Both have the same lease config:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
~ vault read sys/mounts/aws-dev/tune  _x000D_
Key                  Value_x000D_
---                  -----_x000D_
default_lease_ttl    2h_x000D_
description          n/a_x000D_
force_no_cache       false_x000D_
max_lease_ttl        1008h_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
~ vault read sys/mounts/aws-prod/tune _x000D_
Key                  Value_x000D_
---                  -----_x000D_
default_lease_ttl    2h_x000D_
description          n/a_x000D_
force_no_cache       false_x000D_
max_lease_ttl        1008h_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
When generating credentials through these mounts using the same authentication method the TTL for `aws-prod` is not 2h as it should be:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
~ vault read aws-dev/creds/service_x000D_
Key                Value_x000D_
---                -----_x000D_
..._x000D_
lease_duration     2h_x000D_
lease_renewable    true_x000D_
..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
~ vault read aws-prod/creds/service_x000D_
Key                Value_x000D_
---                -----_x000D_
..._x000D_
lease_duration     5m_x000D_
lease_renewable    true_x000D_
..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The lease duration for credentials generated through secret mounts with the same default lease TTL when using the same authentication method should be the same._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.16.1_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.17.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: AL2

body_text:

```_x000D_

title: Unable to create/update AWS authentication role after 1.17.0 - unable to resolve ARN to internal ID: InvalidParameter: 1 validation error(s) found
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Unable to create/update AWS authentication role after 1.17.0_x000D_
Error: unable to resolve ARN to internal ID: InvalidParameter: 1 validation error(s) found_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Try to create/update AWS Auth Role after update to version 1.17.0:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault write auth/aws/role/app-dev-role bound_iam_principal_arn="arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/role-lambda"_x000D_
_x000D_
Error writing data to auth/aws/role/app-dev-role: Error making API request._x000D_
URL: PUT https://vault.dev/v1/auth/aws/role/app-dev-role_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* unable to resolve ARN "arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/role-lambda" to internal ID: InvalidParameter: 1 validation error(s) found. - minimum field size of 2, AssumeRoleInput.ExternalId._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
2. Read the STS Configuration:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault read auth/aws/config/sts/123456789123_x000D_
Key         Value_x000D_
---         -----_x000D_
sts_role    arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/vault-dev_x000D_
```_x000D_
3. As an alternative solution, the external_id parameter was defined in the STS configuration (this parameter should be optional, but in this case seems it's not):_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/aws/config/sts/123456789123 sts_role=arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/vault-dev external_id="123"_x000D_
Success! Data written to: auth/aws/config/sts/123456789123_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault read auth/aws/config/sts/123456789123_x000D_
Key            Value_x000D_
---            -----_x000D_
external_id    123_x000D_
sts_role       arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/vault-dev_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
4. After defining this parameter, it was possible to configure the AWS authentication role:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/aws/role/app-dev-role bound_iam_principal_arn="arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/role-lambda"_x000D_
Success! Data written to: auth/aws/role/app-dev-role_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
5. After updating the authentication role, the external_id parameter was removed from the STS configuration:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/aws/config/sts/123456789123 sts_role=arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/vault-dev external_id=""_x000D_
Success! Data written to: auth/aws/config/sts/123456789123_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault read auth/aws/config/sts/123456789123_x000D_
Key         Value_x000D_
---         -----_x000D_
sts_role    arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/vault-dev_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
6. After removing the parameter external_id, it was possible to configure the AWS authentication role again (meaning that it correctly assumed the destination role):_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write auth/aws/role/app-dev-role bound_iam_principal_arn="arn:aws:iam::123456789123:role/role-lambda"_x000D_
Success! Data written to: auth/aws/role/app-dev-role_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
After upgrading to version 1.17.0, the STS configuration requires the external_id parameter to be defined (even though it is defined in the documentation as an optional parameter). It is not possible to make changes to AWS authentication roles for accounts that already have the STS configuration defined._x000D_

title: Allow setting unseal threshold at 1 when multiple shares are created
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
_x000D_
When generating unseal keys, if more than one share is created the threshold cannot be set to 1. In this event, the following error is produced:_x000D_
_x000D_
> threshold must be greater than one for multiple shares_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
_x000D_
Remove this limitation (allow setting the threshold to 1 when multiple secret shares are created)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe relevant use-case and alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
_x000D_
I am a fan of Vault's ability to generate unseal keys pre-encrypted using PGP keys. This entirely eliminates the unseal key distribution problem as the encrypted unseal keys can be trivially distributed._x000D_
_x000D_
In certain cases, we would prefer *not* to require multiple unseal key shares (i.e. we'd like to use a threshold of 1) to reduce operational friction where the additional security is not required. For example, this would enable operations where only one member of our small team is available._x000D_
_x000D_
Unfortunately, the only alternatives I can think of:_x000D_
_x000D_
* Manually encrypting a single unseal key -- This would lead to a very different workflows (including extra manual effort to perform the necessary encryption) compared with the shared keys workflow. It would also preclude any potential audit trail about which unseal keys were used to perform a given operation._x000D_
* Using multiple key shares and giving each person multiple shares -- This is a bit gross and feels like a workaround for an artificial limitation rather than a real solution._x000D_
_x000D_
Thanks for your consideration!
top_3_comments_text: kasimon: +1 to this. One possible unseal design we currently consider is: 1 unseal key goes into the team's password store, one key goes to the team lead. Unseal threshold is one, so the team can unseal vault whenever they need (for example on-call at night), but operations that require quorum needs the team lead's second key (for things like rekey, new root token). Currently vault would require us to double the number of keys, so 2 keys go to team, 2 to team lead and unseal threshold is 2. But that limitation seems artificial.

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When upgrading Vault, there is intermittent downtime for the user as the UI sometimes does not load. There are no network issues in the browser, rather console errors. After the upgrade, the issue is also gone. _x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Setup a Vault cluster of 3 or 5 with raft configured using e.g. version 1.17.0_x000D_
2. Upgrade to 1.17.1_x000D_
3. F5 until you see the issue occur intermittently_x000D_
_x000D_
The errors match this old issue: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/13357_x000D_
_x000D_
Sometimes there are random exceptions, the console errors are slightly different. When these different errors occur, sometimes it's not entirely blank but e.g. loads very ugly with badly sized logo etc._x000D_
_x000D_
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa5aeec4-fe4b-4f07-a39f-e6359b5a0f46)_x000D_
_x000D_
There are a few critical notes here. We use a Google MIG to distribute the nodes between at max 3 zones. This means an upgrade cycle of -> 3 old -> 3 old, 2 new -> 1 old, 3 new -> 3 new. The loadbalancer is configured to route with -> /v1/sys/health?activecode=200&standbycode=200. This means either leader or standby node (via redirection) serves the webrequests._x000D_
_x000D_
Our best hypothesis thus far, is that it somehow is because of how we route requests - but given the past issue, this could also be Vault itself. Good thing to know, this was not the case before. We're unsure since which version this started, but we have used Vault since version 1.15 in this configuration. We are however certain this has been the case for at least this YTD (1 jan 2024)._x000D_
_x000D_
This happens on Brave and Chrome, on the latest OSX, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and Windows 11 canary releases._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
No downtime during upgrades._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
We run on 1.17.0 when upgrading to 1.17.1. It's fully docker based using COS images of Google._x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
      ui = true_x000D_
      disable_mlock = true_x000D_
_x000D_
      storage "raft" {_x000D_

        retry_join {_x000D_
          auto_join               = "provider=gce tag_value=${resource_name_prefix}-vault zone_pattern=${zone_pattern}"_x000D_
          auto_join_scheme        = "https"_x000D_
          leader_tls_servername   = "${leader_tls_servername}"_x000D_
          leader_ca_cert_file     = "/vault/certs/vault-ca.pem"_x000D_
          leader_client_cert_file = "/vault/certs/vault-cert.pem"_x000D_
          leader_client_key_file  = "/vault/certs/vault-key.pem"_x000D_
        }_x000D_
      }_x000D_
_x000D_
      cluster_addr  = "https://LOCAL_IPV4:8201"_x000D_
      api_addr      = "https://LOCAL_IPV4:8200"_x000D_
_x000D_
      listener "tcp" {_x000D_
        address            = "0.0.0.0:8200"_x000D_
        tls_disable        = false_x000D_
        tls_cert_file      = "/vault/certs/vault-cert.pem"_x000D_
        tls_key_file       = "/vault/certs/vault-key.pem"_x000D_
        tls_client_ca_file = "/vault/certs/vault-ca.pem"_x000D_
      }_x000D_
_x000D_
      seal "gcpckms" {_x000D_
        project    = "${project}"_x000D_
        region     = "${kms_region}"_x000D_

        crypto_key = "${crypto_key}"_x000D_

        stackdriver_namespace = "${resource_name_prefix}-vault"_x000D_
        disable_hostname = true_x000D_
        enable_hostname_label = true_x000D_
        filter_default = false_x000D_
        prefix_filter = ["+vault.token", "-vault.expire", "+vault.expire.num_leases", "+vault.expire.renew-token", "+vault.audit", "+vault.core.leadership_lost", "+vault.core.leadership_setup_failed", "+vault.core.handle_login_request", "+vault.core.handle_request", "+vault.core.post_unseal"]_x000D_
      }_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Vault OIDC flow breaks fails to prompt users to login when their client tokens have expired
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
In older versions of vault a user would be prompted to log back into Vault when their Web UI client token had expired._x000D_
_x000D_
Newer versions of vault do not prompt users to log back in, instead they just send an error message back to the oauth client that initiated the OIDC auth flow._x000D_
_x000D_
This is annoying because I have to tell those using our vault deployment that they need to go and manually log into vault before they can use any application we have OIDC enabled on._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
Run two versions of vault:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. a version of vault where this was not an issue: **1.15.6**_x000D_
2. a recent version of vault where OIDC flows are busted: **1.17.2** (I think it broke in 1.16)_x000D_
_x000D_
I have an example [docker-compose.yml](https://gist.github.com/BrandonIngalls/469c37350739031df9cd7bfcbe4cb6f6#file-docker-compose-yml)  that I have been using to reproduce this issue_x000D_
_x000D_
I also have a terraform file ([main.tf](https://gist.github.com/BrandonIngalls/469c37350739031df9cd7bfcbe4cb6f6#file-main-tf)) that I use to quickly configure the dev vault instances in a similar way._x000D_
_x000D_
This terraform state does the following:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. setup a vault user + userpass_x000D_
2. configure vault to allow CORS from an OIDC Debugging service (https://oidcdebugger.com/)_x000D_
3. add a public oidc client for the OIDC debugger_x000D_
_x000D_
For my testing I do the following:_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
# start the two versions of vault_x000D_
[~]$ docker compose up_x000D_
_x000D_
# configure terraform_x000D_
[~]$    terraform init \_x000D_
; terraform workspace new broken \_x000D_
; terraform workspace new working_x000D_
_x000D_
# bootstrap the older version of vault that wasn't busted (v1.15.6)_x000D_
[~]$ terraform workspace select working_x000D_
_x000D_
[~]$ terraform apply -var=vault_addr=http://localhost:8200_x000D_
_x000D_
# bootstrap a more modern version where vault appears busted_x000D_
[~]$ terraform workspace select broken_x000D_
_x000D_
[~]$ terraform apply -var=vault_addr=http://localhost:8201_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I then open two tabs of https://oidcdebugger.com/ and fill out the required information to test out the OIDC provider feature of Vault._x000D_
_x000D_
I then login to the vault ui for both versions using the test creds `user:password`_x000D_
_x000D_
- [working older vault](http://localhost:8200/)_x000D_
- [broken newer vault](http://localhost:8201/)_x000D_
_x000D_
and manually revoke their web ui client tokens (this is so I don't need to wait for them to naturally expire)_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
[~]$ vault token revoke \_x000D_
  -address=http://localhost:8200 \_x000D_
    hvs...._x000D_
_x000D_
[~]$ vault token revoke \_x000D_
  -address=http://localhost:8201 \_x000D_
    hvs...._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
I then start the OIDC flow in both of my OIDC debugger tabs._x000D_
_x000D_
You'll see that the older version of vault will prompt you to login again, and if you enter the test creds again vault will complete the OIDC flow and the OIDC debugger will be happy._x000D_
_x000D_
In the modern version of Vault the vault ui will flash by in an instant as you are imidetily redirected back to the OIDC debugger with an error saying your client token is not valid._x000D_
_x000D_

Looks like this was indeed broken in `1.17.0`, specifically by adding rather [innocent condition in a MR](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/25953/files#diff-85091b6628302ae2d5455bef1ff50cc1bf31289a6aac0b29c2e99f249cbac879R630). Changes uploaded [oidc-fix branch](https://github.com/dezeroku/vault/tree/oidc-fix) I suspect that there are some conditions in place that go crazy when they encounter different errors than those thrown in the past. I'll try to dig deeper into that
dezeroku: Ok, so it looks like frontend and backend have different expectations of how the auth response should be formatted. This is visible for requests to the following endpoints (at least): * `/v1/identity/oidc/provider/default/authorize` * `/v1/sys/internal/ui/resultant-acl` When auth fails, backend responds with 403 and attaches JSON response describing exact errors that occurred. So for the "correct" versions <1.17.0 we have response that looks like this: ``` errors: [ "permission denied" ] ``` On the frontend side we iterate over the list of returned errors and if we find `permission denied` string a redirect to auth website is performed. This can be seen in code [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/ui/app/routes/vault/cluster/oidc-provider.js#L151) Now, with [this PR](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/25953) a new error 'invalid token' was introduced to differentiate between "you have no permissions to access this endpoint" and "your token is expired/does not exist". With this change in place, the returned error list actually contains two errors: * "permission denied", same as in the past * "invalid token" because, well, in our case this token actually IS invalid as it's either expired or manually revoked by us for testing This would work fine if the returned errors were formatted as a proper list, but they're not. For Vault versions >=1.17.0 we have response that looks like this: ``` "errors": [ "2 errors occurred:\n\t* permission denied\n\t* invalid token\n\n" ] ``` As you can see, the returned error "list" is actually a single string that contains two errors and some boilerplate. This string follows the default format used by [`go-multierror` package](https://github.com/hashicorp/go-multierror/blob/main/format.go#L28). There are two ways to proceed here: 1. properly format the output on backend's side (as a list) 2. align on the frontend I can't really comment on how big the change would be on backend, but on frontend a naive "fix" of matching the received errors "list" with regex and not exact match takes one line and seems to work fine: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/commit/262da983094b64711692cb34e1bf3b3ceacfecae
joeshaw: Came here from #28792, and want to point out that it affects any user of the API, not just the OIDC flow. Because errors are returned as strings in the API, the formatting and content implicitly becomes part of the API contract. I have a tool which is (reasonably, IMO) looking for the exact string `permission denied` in the JSON errors array, and the change broke that. As a workaround we now do `strings.Contains(err, "permission denied")` but this is a generally imprecise check that I don't like having. So a fix to the frontend would only fix the narrow issue of the OIDC flow but not the fact that this is effectively a breaking change to the Vault HTTP API.

_x000D_
_n/a__x000D_

title: Add support for private keys for database authentication to use passphrases
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Our security team would like to add an additional passphrase control to our private keys generated by the snowflake secrets engine as an extra measure so that in the event that a key is intercepted there is an additional protection in place.  This work would also benefit other database engines as well and not just the snowflake engine._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Add support for passphrase encryption to private keys generated with the vault provided libraries for secret engines._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Other alternatives we have considered would be to use a PKI tool to add a passphrase to the key before it is handed off to the end client but this would require a large amount of effort to process in the middle of a transaction._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
All other database engines would be able to benefit from this change as the needed change is in the main vault code_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Upon a look at the [code](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/3f90e9ac385a706d9247caefdece644ff4a054b6/builtin/logical/database/credentials.go#L79)  it seems that passphrases are not supported in the main vault SDK which explains why I could not find an existing database engine that supports passphrase encrypted private keys for authentication._x000D_
_x000D_
Current options for credential configuration_x000D_
- https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/databases#credential_config_x000D_

title: Update AWS SDK to enable support for AWS EKS Pod Identities
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
I'm running my Vault cluster within an AWS EKS cluster and must create an IAM user with the proper permissions and then provide Vault with a static ACCESS_KEY/ACCESS_SECRET_KEY in order to enable many of the Vault AWS features like AWS Auth, Secrets Sync, and AWS Secrets Engine._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
AWS provides the EKS Pod Identity capability whereby I can specify an K8s service account that is allowed to assume a role within AWS, and thus I no longer need to provide static credentials to my Vault installation. This capability is native and transparent to the application, as long as the application is using a version of the AWS SDK that's newer than November 2023. This feature request is to simply update the AWS SDK that Vault uses, which would enable the use of EKS Pod Identities _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I have briefly looked at AWS IRSA, which would also potentially work to enable EKS pods to assume an AWS role, although the configuration is cumbersome and EKS Pod Identities is much cleaner._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
This type of feature should be in line with the goals of Vault to easily enable dynamic credentials._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2023/11/amazon-eks-pod-identity/_x000D_
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/pod-identities.html_x000D_

title: Trust CAs injected via VAULT_CACERT as S3 target for vault helm chart
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Currently there is no option to inject a self signed ca for using it as s3 snapshot target. Vault already has the option to inject a CA using the envVar VAULT_CACERT. However, this CA is not injected into the trust store of the image but only used for the Vault application. So there is no native option to specify the s3 ca. This isn't a problem if using a public s3 storage like aws or gcp, but if you're using your own s3 storage with a private ca, there is no option for it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
That the content of VAULT_CACERT get injected into the system image, so that the s3 client is trusting the self signed injected ca. If the env var could not be used for this purpose there should be another var for this purpose._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Fork the vault image and do injection there or use an initContainer. There is no documentation about it and both solutions are associated with more complex maintenance_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: aquisx: I figured out a (dirty) way using ubi images without using root rights. First there is need for a configMap "ca-inject-cm" which includes the ca cert. **Describe the bug**_x000D_

5. Restart & unseal Vault and compare Consul logs and service status._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_

* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.17.3 (and 1.17.2)_x000D_

title: UI: Stretch text field to fit content in JSON editor
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Sometimes a large number of nested variables are kept secret, but you can only view/edit such variables by switching to JSON editing mode._x000D_
Such nested variables are difficult to find on the page and we have to resort to the browser's "search on page" tool._x000D_
_x000D_
In JSON mode, the text field is very small and if you try to find the desired variable using the browser's "search in page" tool (`Ctrl+f`), nothing will work if it is outside the text field, since it does not yet exist for the browser, it is not rendered._x000D_
_x000D_
To find the desired variable, you have to scroll the contents of the text field a little and press the `F3` key to repeat the search - and so on until the desired variable is highlighted by the browser._x000D_
_x000D_
Also, the keys are sorted in an unnatural order (this is normal, expected and does not raise questions), so it is very difficult to search for the desired variable by eye, and searching on the page is the most reliable option to find the desired variable._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
In my opinion, it will be convenient if at the moment of switching to the JSON mode the text field is stretched to the size of the content - it is more convenient to scroll the entire page than to scroll the text in a small text field, in addition, the "search on page" (`Ctrl+f`) will work correctly_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
Maybe you can make it so that the content is rendered outside the small text box, then "search on page" (`Ctrl+f`)  will also work, and when you press `F3` and the scrolling of the page is done automatically_x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Due to the fact that the text has to be scrolled and the search repeated, you can accidentally scroll more than necessary and miss the variable you are looking for. I encountered this several times and had to repeat everything from the beginning, but scroll very slowly, literally one line at a time, so as not to make a mistake and be sure that the required variable will be found or make sure that it is missing._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
In this video I keep pressing `F3` and scrolling the contents of a small text field back and forth. You can see that only when I scroll to the desired variable does the browser see it and highlight it, but if I scroll further the browser doesn't see it again._x000D_

title: Wrong policy reported for "operator seal/unseal"
body_text:
I wanted to seal the vault using the output policy report by vault, i.e._x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault operator seal -output-policy_x000D_
path "sys/seal" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
$ vault policy read admin | grep -FA 2 seal_x000D_
path "sys/seal" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
But it fails:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault operator seal_x000D_
Error sealing: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT https://...:8200/v1/sys/seal_x000D_
Code: 403. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* 1 error occurred:_x000D_
	* permission denied_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
So the `seal` operation requires "sudo" to be present, so that is missing in the output of `-output-policy`._x000D_
_x000D_
Similar the output for the unseal operation is also wrong:_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault operator unseal -output-policy_x000D_
Unseal Key (will be hidden): _x000D_
path "sys/unseal" {_x000D_
  capabilities = ["create", "update"]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This suggests I need a token attached to a policy with those capabilities while in fact I don't even need any token, just the unseal key._x000D_
_x000D_
So the bugfix/improvement I'm suggesting is that the output of `-output-policy` should be authoritative and hence always correct._x000D_
_x000D_
The [documentation on seal](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/seal) e.g. isn't fully clear to me:_x000D_
_x000D_
> Requires a token with root policy or sudo capability on the path._x000D_
_x000D_
It sounds like I need `capabilities = ["sudo"]`, so why does vault print `"create", "update"` instead? Especially as I would expect only one of them (together with sudo)_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault Version         1.17.0

title: Handling Token Renewal with Vault Agent
body_text:
Hi,_x000D_
_x000D_
I’m working on integrating HashiCorp Vault into our application using Vault Agent for authentication. The initial setup works well, where the application reads the Vault token from a file generated by Vault Agent and uses it to authenticate with the Vault server._x000D_
_x000D_
However, I’m concerned about handling scenarios where the token’s max TTL is reached, and a new token is generated by Vault Agent._x000D_
_x000D_
Currently, our application reads the token once during initialization and uses it for subsequent operations. If the token expires and a new one is generated, the application wouldn’t automatically know about the new token, which could lead to failed operations._x000D_
_x000D_
To address this, I am thinking to implement a file watcher that monitors the token file for changes. When a new token is generated, the watcher reloads the token and updates the Vault client. While this seems to work in theory, I want to ensure that we’re following best practices and not missing any important considerations._x000D_
_x000D_
Here are the specific questions I have:_x000D_
_x000D_
    Is monitoring the token file for changes and reloading the token dynamically the recommended approach for handling token renewal with Vault Agent?_x000D_
    Are there any potential pitfalls or edge cases I should be aware of when implementing this solution?_x000D_
    Are there more efficient or reliable methods to ensure the application always has access to a valid token, especially in high-availability or production environments?_x000D_
_x000D_
I’d appreciate any feedback or suggestions on improving this implementation._x000D_
top_3_comments_text: VioletHynes: One option you could use is the Process Supervisor Mode: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/agent/process-supervisor This mode injects secrets as environment variables and can be configured to restart the process it's supervising when a new secret is present in a rendered template. If you're using file templating, it's somewhat up to the client application how it wants to monitor its own config files. Ultimately, this issue will exist however new config is provided to your application. I know some frameworks can deal with this kind of thing automatically, but the recommended approach will depend largely on how your application reads its config -- there's no one-size fits-all recommendation for every language/framework since e.g. SpringBoot might want to handle this differently than a framework-less Java. A watcher on the file that updates things if there are changes in the file seems like a pretty reasonable solution to me. title: [DOCS] LTS Documentation has contradictory timeline
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
The end of Extended maintenance for a given LTS release is documented two different ways at https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/enterprise/lts._x000D_
_x000D_
For a reader, reading that page, the End-of-Extended-Maintenance Date can be read two different ways:_x000D_

### End of Standard Maintenance + 1year_x000D_
_x000D_
This is what the text implies. _x000D_
_x000D_
> After the first year, LTS Vault versions move from standard maintenance to extended maintenance for an additional year _x000D_
_x000D_
### End of Standard Maintenance + 3 major releases_x000D_
_x000D_
This is what the table implies by penning down the date for 1.16 as "CY26 Q1 (1.22 release)"._x000D_
_x000D_
While these two will likely match in normal cases, in case of a change in timeline for 1.22 (for any reason) - the dates can differ, resulting in ambiguity._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The page should not have contradicting information. It might be simpler to just say "the latest 2 LTS releases are supported at any given time, following a N-1 policy. Since Vault releases 3 releases every year, this results in approximately 1 year of standard maintenance, followed by one year of extended maintenance".

title: [BUG] Vault Proxy static secrets cache does not consider secrets version
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
When using the Vault Proxy with `cache_static_secrets: true` (ref. [docs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/proxy/caching#cache_static_secrets)) we are observing inconsistent responses that we believe to have traced back to the cache key of the Vault Proxy's static secrets caching._x000D_
_x000D_
**This is a critical issue & blocker for us trying to adopt the Vault Proxy in Vault Enterprise**_x000D_
_x000D_
The issue is that the cache key does not consider the `version` parameter when requesting secrets from a versioned secrets engine. This results in clients receiving outdated and sometimes inconsistent responses from the Vault Proxy, regardless of whether they specify the desired version (with `?version=N` in the URL or `-version N` in the CLI) or not._x000D_
_x000D_
This function considers only the request `Path` and the `X-Vault-Namespace` header when it is set, however it needs to also consider query parameters such as `version` in order to work for versioned storage engines (ref. https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/secrets-management/versioned-kv)._x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
// getStaticSecretPathFromRequest gets the canonical path for a_x000D_
// request, taking into account intricacies relating to /v1/ and namespaces_x000D_
// in the header._x000D_
// Returns a path like foo/bar or ns1/foo/bar._x000D_
// We opt for this form as namespace.Canonicalize returns a namespace in the_x000D_
// form of "ns1/", so we keep consistent with path canonicalization._x000D_
func getStaticSecretPathFromRequest(req *SendRequest) string {_x000D_
	path := req.Request.URL.Path_x000D_
	// Static secrets always have /v1 as a prefix. This enables us to_x000D_
	// enable a pass-through and never attempt to cache or view-from-cache_x000D_
	// any request without the /v1 prefix._x000D_
	if !strings.HasPrefix(path, "/v1") {_x000D_
		return ""_x000D_
	}_x000D_
	var namespace string_x000D_
	if header := req.Request.Header; header != nil {_x000D_
		namespace = header.Get(api.NamespaceHeaderName)_x000D_
	}_x000D_
	return canonicalizeStaticSecretPath(path, namespace)_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
code ref. https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/command/agentproxyshared/cache/lease_cache.go#L888-L907_x000D_

The cache key for dynamic secrets does not seem to have this issue (code ref. https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/command/agentproxyshared/cache/lease_cache.go#L837-L862)_x000D_

We intend on requesting a "known" set of secrets from Vault Proxy on a regular basis (eg. every few minutes) to ensure its cache is up-to-date and that it is able to serve these secrets to applications that require them. It is crucial in our design that: 1. Vault Proxy does not fail client requests when Vault Server is unreachable and the secret version explicitly requested is available in the Vault Proxy cache. There is no need to reach out to Vault Server when the artifact is available locally. 2. Vault Proxy does not fail client requests when Vault Server is unreachable and the latest version of the secret is requested. It would be ideal to be able to configure a retry strategy in such cases, to avoid client requests timing out while the Proxy is (unsuccessfully) retrying requests for "latest" from the Server. 3. Vault Proxy is able to recover its persisted cache completely offline, start up and successfully serve secrets that are cached, without requiring a synchronous connection to Vault Server. title: [Proxy] Unable to restart offline with persistent cache
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Vault Proxy with persistent static secrets cache & auto-auth enabled is unable to start up offline without trying to connect to Vault Server to renew its token._x000D_

title: Single-use token used to create a snapshot reappears in the restored database and is irrevocable
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
If a single use (e.g. `-use-limit=1`) token is used to create a [raft snapshot](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands/operator/raft#snapshot), the expired token reappears when the snapshot is restored. The expired token shows a `num_uses` of -1 and appears to not be usable. The restored token also appears to be irrevocable and in some kind of stuck state._x000D_
_x000D_
Because the reappearing token (appears) not to be usable, this doesn't present an immediate security problem. It does, however, seem to be leading to some kind of "impossible" database state which might be concerning from the perspective of database integrity. It also complicates auditing of tokens in a live system as these "stuck and unusable" tokens must be manually eliminated from any checks._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
*1. Create a vault cluster using raft based storage.*_x000D_
_x000D_
<details>_x000D_
<summary>Sample minimal vault config (click to expand)</summary>_x000D_
_x000D_
Setup a quick-and-dirty vault server:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ cat << EOF > config.hcl_x000D_
   storage "raft" {_x000D_
     path = "data"_x000D_
     node_id = "vault"_x000D_
   }_x000D_
   listener "tcp" {_x000D_
     address = "127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
     cluster_address = "127.0.0.1:8201"_x000D_
     tls_disable = true_x000D_
   }_x000D_
   api_addr = "http://127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
   cluster_addr = "https://127.0.0.1:8201"_x000D_
   disable_mlock = true_x000D_
EOF_x000D_
$ mkdir data_x000D_
$ vault server -config config.hcl_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Initialise, unseal and authenticate:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ export VAULT_ADDR="http://127.0.0.1:8200"_x000D_
$ vault operator init -key-shares=1 -key-threshold=1_x000D_
$ vault operator unseal <unseal key printed during init>_x000D_
$ vault login <root token printed during init>_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
</details>_x000D_
_x000D_
*2. Create a single-use token with the ability to hit the snapshot endpoint. For example:*_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault token create -policy=root -use-limit=1_x000D_
Key                  Value_x000D_
---                  -----_x000D_
token                [REDACTED_VAULT_TOKEN]
token_accessor       LF7kIL16LczrVisluHZSSdVJ_x000D_
..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
*3. See that the token exists:*_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault token lookup -accessor LF7kIL16LczrVisluHZSSdVJ_x000D_
Key                 Value_x000D_
---                 -----_x000D_
accessor            LF7kIL16LczrVisluHZSSdVJ_x000D_
..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
*4. Create snapshot using the single-use token:*_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ VAULT_TOKEN=[REDACTED_VAULT_TOKEN] vault operator raft snapshot save raft.snap_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
*5. Verify that token has expired:*_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault token lookup -accessor LF7kIL16LczrVisluHZSSdVJ_x000D_
Error looking up token: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: POST http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/token/lookup-accessor_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* 1 error occurred:_x000D_
        * invalid accessor_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
*6. Restore snapshot:*_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ operator raft snapshot restore raft.snap_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
*7. Observe that the expired token now exists again (though it isn't usable as num_uses is -1):*_x000D_
_x000D_

accessor            LF7kIL16LczrVisluHZSSdVJ_x000D_

_x000D_
* permission denied_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
*8. Also observe that the token cannot be revoked.*_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
$ vault token revoke -accessor LF7kIL16LczrVisluHZSSdVJ_x000D_
Error revoking token: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: POST http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/token/revoke-accessor_x000D_
Code: 400. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* token not found_x000D_
$ vault token lookup -accessor LF7kIL16LczrVisluHZSSdVJ_x000D_
Key                 Value_x000D_
---                 -----_x000D_
accessor            LF7kIL16LczrVisluHZSSdVJ_x000D_
..._x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
I would expect that a single-use token used to create a snapshot would not appear in the backup (I would expect that it would have been deleted as part of the checking process before the snapshot started)._x000D_
_x000D_
I would also expect to be able to revoke the back-from-the-dead token after restoring a snapshot (even if it is in an unusable state)._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Extra detail: time and use limited tokens**_x000D_
_x000D_
In case it is useful, I have observed that in the case of a single-use token also having a finite TTL, the stuck token in the restored database will eventually be removed when the TTL expires._x000D_
_x000D_
*1. Create token with single-use limit and a short TTL:*_x000D_

$ vault token create -policy=root -use-limit=1 -ttl=5m_x000D_

*2. Create snapshot using the token and then restore from that snapshot.*_x000D_
_x000D_

$ VAULT_TOKEN=[REDACTED_VAULT_TOKEN] vault operator raft snapshot save raft.snap_x000D_
$ vault operator raft snapshot restore raft.snap_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
*3. Observe that the token comes back to life but is unusable and cannot be revoked, as before.*_x000D_
_x000D_

title: Enhancing LDAP Integration Logs and Auditing for Better Debugging
body_text:
When configuring Vault's LDAP integration, administrators face significant difficulties in debugging issues related to group mappings and LDAP queries. Currently, even with detailed logging enabled (debug mode), the Vault audit logs do not provide enough insight into the LDAP queries being made, particularly during group search operations._x000D_
_x000D_
This lack of visibility makes it difficult to identify and troubleshoot issues like incorrect group filters or attribute mappings. The administrator is left guessing the exact LDAP queries Vault is executing, leading to a trial-and-error approach that is time-consuming and error-prone._x000D_
_x000D_
Request:_x000D_
_x000D_
Enhancing the LDAP authentication backend by adding more detailed logging, specifically:_x000D_
_x000D_
    Log exact LDAP queries performed (including filters, attributes requested, and base DNs used) during both user and group search operations._x000D_
_x000D_
    Audit log entries for LDAP queries should include:_x000D_
        The full query issued (base DN, filter, attributes requested)._x000D_
        Whether the query succeeded or failed._x000D_
        The number of entries returned from the LDAP server._x000D_
        Any specific errors encountered during the search._x000D_
_x000D_
    If possible, provide an option to toggle the verbosity of LDAP-related logs (to balance performance and debugging needs)._x000D_
_x000D_
Use Case:_x000D_
_x000D_
In a situation where LDAP group policies are not being applied correctly, the administrator currently has no way of knowing:_x000D_
_x000D_
    What exact LDAP query Vault is sending to retrieve groups._x000D_
    Whether the query returned results and if so, what results were returned._x000D_
_x000D_
This information is critical for fine-tuning LDAP configurations such as groupdn, groupfilter, groupattr, and troubleshooting why certain groups are not being found or mapped correctly. Having this visibility would significantly reduce the time spent diagnosing LDAP issues._x000D_
_x000D_
Steps to Reproduce:_x000D_
_x000D_
    Configure Vault with LDAP authentication backend._x000D_
    Set up group filters and policies._x000D_
    Attempt to log in as a user who should inherit policies from LDAP groups._x000D_
    Observe the lack of detailed LDAP query logs in the debug or audit logs._x000D_
_x000D_
Expected Outcome: The Vault logs or audit logs should show:_x000D_
_x000D_
    The exact LDAP query that was issued._x000D_
    Information on whether the query returned results or failed._x000D_
    The groups and attributes returned by the LDAP server._x000D_
_x000D_
This would allow administrators to compare the actual query with their expected configuration and make adjustments accordingly._x000D_
_x000D_
Impact:_x000D_
_x000D_
This improvement would drastically improve the efficiency of debugging LDAP issues in Vault, providing administrators with the necessary insight into LDAP operations and helping to prevent unnecessary misconfigurations or extended downtime.

title: DynamoDB backend cannot assume role in a different AWS account due to awsutil limitations
body_text:
When using the DynamoDB physical backend for Vault in an EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) environment, we are unable to access a DynamoDB instance located in a different AWS account using IAM role assumption. The current implementation using awsutil does not support assuming roles via the shared config file (`~/.aws/config`), which prevents Vault from accessing DynamoDB across AWS accounts._x000D_
_x000D_
Details:_x000D_
_x000D_
Environment:_x000D_
* Vault running in EKS_x000D_
* DynamoDB located in a different AWS account_x000D_
* Access to DynamoDB should be obtained via IAM role assumption_x000D_
_x000D_
Problem:_x000D_
The DynamoDB backend uses `github.com/hashicorp/go-secure-stdlib/awsutil` for credential management, which does not support loading profiles and assuming roles defined in the shared AWS config file (`~/.aws/config`). This limitation makes it impossible to configure Vault to assume a role in another AWS account to access DynamoDB._x000D_
_x000D_
Attempted Workaround:_x000D_
_x000D_
We tried configuring the shared AWS config file inside the pod with the following content:_x000D_
```_x000D_
[profile default]_x000D_
source_profile = local_x000D_
role_arn = arn:aws:iam::AAAAAAAA:role/vault-role_x000D_
_x000D_
[profile local]_x000D_
web_identity_token_file = /var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token_x000D_
role_arn = arn:aws:iam::BBBBBBBBB:role/vault-role_x000D_
```_x000D_
However, awsutil does not recognize or properly handle this configuration, and as a result, Vault cannot assume the role to access DynamoDB in the other AWS account._x000D_
_x000D_
Analysis:_x000D_
_x000D_
The standard AWS SDK for Go supports loading credentials and configuration from the shared config file and can handle role assumption chains, including those using web identity tokens (such as those provided by EKS service accounts). The use of awsutil in the DynamoDB backend bypasses this functionality, limiting the ways in which credentials can be provided._x000D_
_x000D_
Expected Behavior:_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault should be able to use the standard AWS SDK credential providers to assume roles defined in the shared config file, allowing it to access DynamoDB instances in other AWS accounts. This includes supporting complex credential chains and role assumptions that are commonly used in multi-account AWS environments.

body_text:

_x000D_

Add a `derive` path for keys in the transit secrets engine allowing the caller to provide a public key and returning the shared secret._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
The key can be made exportable and the ecdh operation performed outside of vault, this is not ideal as it is less secure._x000D_

title: Automatically add tables when selecting postgresql as secret storage
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
According to current documentation (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/website/content/docs/configuration/storage/postgresql.mdx vault cannot create tables automatically. I use helm chart from bank vault to deploy vault (https://github.com/bank-vaults/vault-helm-chart). At the moment I am unfolding the tables manually. When deploying manually, the first installation always fails, because vault initially creates roles, users and a vault database in PostgreSQL, and then creates tables on top of that. Pre-installation in PostgreSQL is difficult because user credentials created before helm deployment will have different passwords and the application will not be able to get into the database (to create tables, the vault_owner_user user is used, which is automatically created when helm is deployed, and the password is put in secrets)._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
Automatically add tables (vault_kv_store, vault_ha_locks) and function (vault_kv_put) when selecting postgresql as secret storage. _x000D_

title: Exponential backoff in the LifetimeWatcher does not send an error to doneCh if we reach the lease expiration while failing to renew
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
In https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/26868, the backoff package was upgraded to V4. Part of the difference between V3 and V4 of backoff is that the backoff.ExponentialBackOff struct now takes a "Stop" field, indicating the value to return when we should no longer retry the operation._x000D_
_x000D_
In the constructor they provide (backoff.NewExpontentialBackOff - https://github.com/cenkalti/backoff/blob/v4/exponential.go#L94), the Stop value is set to the constant in the package, a duration of -1 second. The Vault code however directly initialises the struct (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/c8e6169d5dbc82d99d904e468852902de98ebfd0/api/lifetime_watcher.go) and thus we end up with a duration of zero seconds for the "Stop" field._x000D_
_x000D_
The lifetime watcher later checks the returned value from the backoff to see if it's `backoff.Stop`. It never is, as the ExponentialBackoff we've initialised returns a time.Duration of zero seconds._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Try to use the lifetime watcher and have it error out when we've unsuccessfully retried to renew the lease and the lease duration has expired._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
`r.doneCh` should receive an error._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
	github.com/hashicorp/vault/api v1.15.0_x000D_
	github.com/hashicorp/vault/api/auth/kubernetes v0.8.0_x000D_
```_x000D_

title: Support connecting to endpoints using a SOCKS5/HTTP proxy
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Vault needs to have network access to different components as secret engines. This might not be feasible when:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. The target is in a private network and does not have a public IP address_x000D_
2. The target is in a network where only outbound connections are allowedE_x000D_
3. One doesn't want to expose the target on a public network_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
While providing direct network access might not be secure and maintainable, if Vault could connect to targets through a proxy server, the proxy server could do the heavy-lifting of routing, access control, audit, etc. Implementing the socks5/http proxy for handling TCP connections could be generic enough, so that the user could bring their own implementation of proxies._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
The proxying could be performed through a transparent proxy mechanism, but that is less than ideal since it's all or nothing and less configurable._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
- The user might have an existing zero-trust network, and would like to leverage that for connecting to its endpoints. The zero-trust network might be Boundary #11459_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_

title: Add support for entity_name_template parameter in all Auth Methods (LDAP, OIDC, JWT, etc.)
body_text:
Hello,_x000D_
_x000D_
I would like to request an enhancement to the HashiCorp Vault authentication methods._x000D_
_x000D_
Background:_x000D_
_x000D_
Currently, some auth methods like OIDC and JWT support parameters like entity_alias_name and entity_alias_name_template, which allow administrators to define custom templates for entity alias names based on token claims. However, there is no support for an entity_name_template parameter that allows setting a custom template for the entity name itself._x000D_
_x000D_
This limitation affects all auth methods, including LDAP, OIDC, and JWT. Entities are created with auto-generated UUIDs, and while aliases can be customized, managing entities with meaningful names would greatly simplify administration._x000D_
_x000D_
Feature Request:_x000D_
_x000D_
    Add support for an entity_name_template parameter in all Auth Methods, allowing administrators to define custom templates for entity names using user attributes (e.g., LDAP attributes, token claims)._x000D_
    Align functionality across all auth methods, providing consistency and improved usability._x000D_
_x000D_
Use Case:_x000D_
_x000D_
In our organization, we rely heavily on LDAP for authentication. Having the ability to assign custom names to entities based on user attributes like uid would:_x000D_
_x000D_
    Enhance the readability and management of entities within Vault._x000D_
    Simplify the association of entities to groups without dealing with auto-generated UUIDs._x000D_
    Improve the administrative experience by providing consistent naming conventions across different auth methods._x000D_
_x000D_
Benefits:_x000D_
_x000D_
    Improved Administration: Easier management of entities with meaningful names._x000D_
    Consistency: Aligns the capabilities of all auth methods, making Vault more intuitive._x000D_
    Scalability: Facilitates management in large environments with many users._x000D_
_x000D_
Thank you for considering this feature request.
