title: Hierarchal? Policies
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
Not a bug, just a desired feature, to be able to handle policies in more of a hierarchal way, where you might have one user that is an "admin" type user with lots of access, but then you might have a lower "maintainer" that just needs to be able to go in and modify service accounts or something.  Not currently seeing features that offer clear separation on that regard, just some tricks that don't quite accomplish what I'm thinking._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
There are probably a multitude of ways to do this, but just as an example, using a group-based policy making process where created policies can be tied to a group, meaning only those in that group (or a sub-group) can modify those policies.  They also wouldn't be able to modify the policy in ways that affect permissions they don't have themselves.  So a user who manages services accounts, can't add full access to everything to that service account and then sign in with it, they can only add up to the same level of access they currently have themselves via the associated group's policy._x000D_
_x000D_
With this, it would seem to make sense to make the policies apply by precedence, then by specificity.  If I'm in the "maintenance" group that has access x, y, but explicitly not z, but I'm also in an "admin" group (that includes the "maintainer" group) that has x, y, and implicitly z, I should get access to z even if it's defined with higher "specificity" in the "maintenance" group that I don't have it._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
I've tried setting up a policy for a "maintainer" that allows them to only modify policies that start with a `service-*` prefix, thus they can't edit their own policy, only service defined ones, but then they could just give the service account full access and sign in as them._x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
Having a separation of ability between users is always needed, and though in many ways that does already exist in the current policy strategies, it's just not very fine grain control for specific resources, such as be able to distinguish different types of entities someone should be able to manage, and allowing limited access to defining policies._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
Nothing else to add_x000D_

title: Option to let vault token renew (CLI) fail on non-fulfillable request
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When building scripts and pipeline using Vault CLI, we often have the requirement to check for token validity and try to renew the token for the amount expected script runtime. Of course it is possible to renew the token with `vault token renew` but the CLI just prints a warning to `stderr` in case it can not fulfill the requested time increase and caps it to the max value. This makes it cumbersome to parse that WARNING or the TTL and then dicide based on the result to propably re-login. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
It would be nice if the `vault token renew` command had an option to let the command fail in case the request can not be fulfilled. This would make it possible to chain Vault CLI executions like that:_x000D_
_x000D_
    vault token renew -increment=5m || vault login ..._x000D_
_x000D_

title: Offline rootCA Revocation List Upload
body_text:
**Description:**_x000D_
When using an offline Root CA in HashiCorp Vault, it's not currently possible to revoke an intermediate CA properly, as there is no built-in API endpoint to upload a signed Certificate Revocation List (CRL). The offline Root CA model means that Vault cannot automatically sign and upload CRLs without manual intervention or external plugins like the ACME plugin. This makes it challenging to maintain CRL distribution and ensure proper revocation processes for Intermediate CAs._x000D_
_x000D_
**Proposed Solution:**_x000D_
I suggest creating a new API endpoint that would allow users to manually upload a pre-signed CRL. This would facilitate better support for offline Root CAs without relying on external tools or plugins. By adding this feature, administrators could manually upload the signed CRL from their offline Root CA, which would then be distributed by Vault for certificate revocation.

title: Cannot issue intermediates from cross-signed intermediate due to error validating chain
body_text:

_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
I've followed the [Build your own CA tutorial](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/secrets-management/pki-engine?variants=vault-deploy%3Aselfhosted#step-9-create-a-cross-signed-intermediate), and set up a cross-signed intermediate using a new root. In the tutorial this involves setting the `manual_chain` attribute on both the existing and cross-signed intermediate so that when new intermediate or leaf certs are issued, the chain includes the multiple trust paths to both roots._x000D_
_x000D_
The problem comes if you want to issue a new intermediate from an intermediate that has multiple trust paths. The following error occurs when attempting to sign a CSR using an intermediate with multiple trust paths:_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write -format=json pki_int/issuer/xc-example-dot-com-intermediate/sign-intermediate \_x000D_
     csr=@pki_intermediate_two.csr \_x000D_
     format=pem_bundle ttl="43800h" \_x000D_
     | jq -r '.data.certificate' > intermediate_two.cert.pem_x000D_
Error writing data to pki_int/issuer/xc-example-dot-com-intermediate/sign-intermediate: Error making API request._x000D_
_x000D_
URL: PUT http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/pki_int/issuer/xc-example-dot-com-intermediate/sign-intermediate_x000D_
Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* 1 error occurred:_x000D_
	* verification of parsed bundle failed: certificate 2 of certificate chain ca trust path is incorrect ("example.com Intermediate Authority"/"example.com Intermediate Authority") (7FF8A6666B32CCD3E87669EC99D60104943D8B6D/B2C40D49346490E05B2044C8B1CD88B5B76A1168)_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
Reading the code that verifies the chain, it looks like it only handles a single trust path: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/9097689d2a9623013ffe3522f1c78d95b44de6dc/sdk/helper/certutil/types.go#L388-L398_x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Follow the [build your own CA tutorial](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/secrets-management/pki-engine?variants=vault-deploy%3Aselfhosted#step-9-create-a-cross-signed-intermediate), specifically steps 1, 2, 3, 7 and 9. It's important that you set the `manual_chain` attribute by running: _x000D_
```_x000D_
vault patch pki_int/issuer/xc-example-dot-com-intermediate \_x000D_
    manual_chain=self,"$(vault read -field=default pki_int/config/issuers)"_x000D_
```_x000D_
3. Enable a new pki secrets engine `vault secrets enable -path=pki_int_two pki`_x000D_
4. Tune the secrets engine `vault secrets tune -max-lease-ttl=43800h pki_int_two`_x000D_
5. Generate an intermediate CSR _x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write -format=json pki_int_two/intermediate/generate/internal \                 _x000D_
     common_name="example.com Intermediate Two Authority" \_x000D_
     issuer_name="example-dot-com-intermediate-two" \_x000D_
     | jq -r '.data.csr' > pki_intermediate_two.csr_x000D_
```_x000D_
6. Sign the intermediate certificate_x000D_
```_x000D_
vault write -format=json pki_int/issuer/xc-example-dot-com-intermediate/sign-intermediate \_x000D_
     csr=@pki_intermediate_two.csr \_x000D_
     format=pem_bundle ttl="43800h" \_x000D_
     | jq -r '.data.certificate' > intermediate_two.cert.pem_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
The sign-intermediate command should sign the new intermediate._x000D_
_x000D_
Instead we get `verification of parsed bundle failed: certificate 2 of certificate chain ca trust path is incorrect`._x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.16.11 (but also reproduced with `main` branch, currently 1.19.0-beta1)_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.17.3_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux/MacOS_x000D_

title: Vault api sending multiple errors as a single string in json
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Starting with version 1.17.*, Vault API is sending multiple errors in a single json. This new json format is hard to parse because the errors are lumped together in a single string, separated by newline characters, rather than as discrete items in an array. This makes string parsing complex since we cannot simply iterate over the items._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Write a secret_x000D_
2. Try reading the same secret with a token which doesn't have permissions to read it._x000D_
3. See the error:_x000D_
_x000D_
API: `{"errors":["2 errors occurred:\n\t* permission denied\n\t* invalid token\n\n"]}`_x000D_
_x000D_
CLI: _x000D_
`_x000D_
* 2 errors occurred:_x000D_
	* permission denied_x000D_
	* invalid token_x000D_
`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Ideally, we would like to see the error messages be sent in the standard json format as separate items like below:_x000D_
`"errors": ["permission denied", "invalid token"]`_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
* Vault Server Version: We tested this on version 1.17.0 and 1.17.6_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.16.1_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Kubernetes pods_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault server configuration file(s):_x000D_
We don't think this issue has nything to do with config file. If needed we can share it at a later stage based on your troubleshooting._x000D_
_x000D_

title: HashiCorp Vault Secret barrier encryption: Is there plan to make it configurable?
body_text:
HashiCorp Vault Secret barrier encryption is based on ‘256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)’. This seems to be fixed one as per current support. Is there plan to make this configurable, in case any other encryption mechanism is needed?_x000D_
_x000D_
Reference: [Security Model | Vault | HashiCorp Developer 2](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/internals/security)_x000D_
"The storage backends used by Vault are also untrusted by design. Vault uses a security barrier for all requests made to the backend. The security barrier automatically encrypts all data leaving Vault using a 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) cipher in the Galois Counter Mode (GCM) with 96-bit nonces. The nonce is randomly generated for every encrypted object. When data is read from the security barrier, the GCM authentication tag is verified during the decryption process to detect any tampering._x000D_
_x000D_
https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/hashicorp-vault-secret-barrier-encryption-is-there-plan-to-make-it-configurable/70793/1_x000D_
top_3_comments_text: victorr: There are currently no plans to make the barrier encryption configurable. Please note that an additional layer of encryption can be enabled via seal-wrapping: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/enterprise/sealwrap

title: /sys/health doesn't accurate reflect the health of Vault

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We have file-based audit logs in place. File system got to 100% full. /sys/health still reported everything as healthy, even though all commands were failing due to inability to access file system. This meant our AWS Target Group still saw it as healthy and didn't take it out of rotation._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
/sys/health should provide a deeper health check to more properly check for issues with vault (in this case, logging in was failing in addition to most read/write commands, due to the file space being full)_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
We are taking workarounds to prevent this, but this would be needed as a valid solution outside of putting something like nginx or something in front of vault which seems unnecessary._x000D_

N/A_x000D_

**Describe the bug**_x000D_
_x000D_
We have a development cluster of Vault that is a few years old, with a 3-out-of-7 Shamir seal structure. After having migrated it to raft, I took a raft snapshot via the API, then proceeded to restore it in another 5-node cluster (also 3-out-of-7 Shamir seal structure). The API call to restore does succeed._x000D_

When trying to unseal the newly restored cluster, I get the following error after the last unseal key._x000D_

```_x000D_

_x000D_

Code: 500. Errors:_x000D_
_x000D_
* failed to create cipher: crypto/aes: invalid key size 0_x000D_
```_x000D_

The default listener for `[::]:8200` seems to work, but the `[::]:8201` cluster address fails. It isn't apparent that `[::]:8201` fails until after the node is unsealed. Here's me unsealing a `vault-0` instance after I initialized it. On vault-0: ``` 2025-09-08T17:48:06.257Z [DEBUG] cluster listener addresses synthesized: cluster_addresses=[[::]:8201] ... 2025-09-08T17:50:02.618Z [INFO] core.cluster-listener.tcp: starting listener: listener_address=[::]:8201 2025-09-08T17:50:02.621Z [ERROR] core.cluster-listener.tcp: error starting listener: error="listen tcp [::]:8201: socket: address family not supported by protocol" ``` This causes the cluster to get in this strange state where I'm able to communicate with the first leader node and join additional nodes to the cluster, but the nodes can't sync on `:8201`. Here's me unsealing a `vault-1` instance that has `retry_join` config for `vault-0`. On vault-1: ``` 2025-09-08T17:55:48.591Z [INFO] core.cluster-listener.tcp: starting listener: listener_address=[::]:8201 2025-09-08T17:55:48.594Z [ERROR] core.cluster-listener.tcp: error starting listener: error="listen tcp [::]:8201: socket: address family not supported by protocol" ... 2025-09-08T17:55:48.594Z [TRACE] storage.raft: setting up raft cluster ... 2025-09-08T17:55:48.634Z [TRACE] storage.raft: finished setting up raft cluster 2025-09-08T17:55:48.634Z [INFO] core: successfully joined the raft cluster: leader_addr=https://vault-0:8200 2025-09-08T17:55:48.634Z [INFO] core: security barrier not initialized ... ``` It looks like `vault-1` joined the cluster with `vault-0`, but `vault-1` didn't unseal and a subsequent unseal attempt results in the original error reported: On vault-1: ``` Error unsealing: Error making API request. URL: PUT https://vault-1:8200/v1/sys/unseal Code: 500. Errors: * failed to create cipher: crypto/aes: invalid key size 0 ``` I'm guessing this is because raft attempts to sync the root/encryption keys on `:8201`, but fails in my case and therefore a null key is stored in the nodes I try to join to the cluster. Updating my config to listen on IPv4 API address `0.0.0.0:8200` and cluster address `0.0.0.0:8201` resolves the issue (127.0.0.1 would obviously be fine also, if you only want localhost listening). ``` api_addr = "https://0.0.0.0:8200" cluster_addr = "https://0.0.0.0:8201" ``` You may not have this exact scenario of IPv6 being disabled messing with the default listeners, but it'd be interesting to see if there are any communication issues within your cluster on the cluster address. If my root cause assumption is correct for my use case, it seems Vault needs better error logging if the root/encryption key is unable to be synced.

title: Add support for JWT Auth Method in Golang SDK
body_text:
## Problem_x000D_
Currently, supported auth methods in the Go SDK are limited to:_x000D_
- approle _x000D_
- aws _x000D_
- azure_x000D_
- gcp_x000D_
- kubernetes_x000D_
- ldap _x000D_
- userpass_x000D_
_x000D_
The JWT method is missing from this list._x000D_
_x000D_
## Prefered Solution_x000D_
_x000D_
Add support for JWT under `github.com/hashicorp/vault/api/auth` so that it can be consumed easily._x000D_
_x000D_
i.e._x000D_
```go_x000D_
package main_x000D_
_x000D_
import (_x000D_
	"context"_x000D_
	"fmt"_x000D_
_x000D_
	vault "github.com/hashicorp/vault/api"_x000D_
	auth "github.com/hashicorp/vault/api/auth/jwt"_x000D_
)_x000D_
_x000D_
func example(jwtToken string) (string, error) {_x000D_
	client, _ := vault.NewClient(nil)_x000D_
_x000D_
	jwtAuth, err := auth.NewJWTAuth(_x000D_
		jwtToken,       // JWT token_x000D_
		"dev-role-jwt", // Vault role_x000D_
	)_x000D_
	if err != nil {_x000D_
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unable to initialize JWT auth method: %w", err)_x000D_
	}_x000D_
_x000D_
	authInfo, err := client.Auth().Login(context.Background(), jwtAuth)_x000D_
	[...]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
## Alternatives_x000D_
1. Use https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-client-go which supports it (Beta library - NOT for production)_x000D_
2. Code the auth method yourself in a private package._x000D_
_x000D_
## Additional context_x000D_
This would make login through GitHub Actions OIDC more straightforward._x000D_

When opening a kv-v2 mount the Vault UI will do an initial [List Secrets](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#list-secrets) call and if that fails it shows the `View secret` prompt. To show the full list of secrets in the mount you can try to add this to the policy applied to the OIDC auth method: > > ```hcl > path "secret/metadata/*" { > capabilities = ["list"] > } > ``` Hello, thank you for the response There are 50 users and every user has its own policy which give me the access to his path(s) If i add in their policy the capability to list the secret/metadata/* they will see all the paths of everybody i want them to see only the paths they are authorized to see for example i tried this but it does not work, i always have to enter the path manually ```hcl path "secrets/metadata/mypath" { capabilities = ["list"] } and path "secrets/metadata/mypath/*" { capabilities = ["list"] } ``` regards
bosouza: I see, you seem to want a way of filtering the results of the list operations based on user permissions. That is not supported by the list API, as per the [docs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/kv/kv-v2#list-secrets): ``` Note that no policy-based filtering is performed on keys; do not encode sensitive information in key names. ``` and ``` To list secrets for KV v2, a user must have a policy granting them the list capability on this /metadata/ path - even if all the rest of their interactions with the KV v2 are via the /data/ APIs. Access to at least list the /metadata/ path should typically also be granted. ``` The guidance here is to not include sensitive information on the keys, exactly so that such list rights can be widely granted. This filter-less list behavior seems to be consistent across all secret engine list APIs so it's not something we'd consider changing without good reason. Something that might help you with restricting list access is to use prefixes for different levels of access then restrict list rights based on those prefixes. Users would still have to remember their prefix to see the list of certificates though.

body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
We currently have KV engines across 2 primary namespaces for individual git repositories, EKS clusters, and multiple applications/microservices. Similar to defining custom metadata on individual secrets, being able to define custom metadata at the KV engine level._x000D_

title: Kubernetes auth method: namespace selector not working with client-provided login token
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
Using `bound_service_account_namespace_selector` in a kubernetes auth role fails if the auth method is configured with `disable_local_ca_jwt`._x000D_
_x000D_
**To Reproduce**_x000D_
1. Enable a kubernetes auth method like_x000D_
   ```bash_x000D_
   vault auth enable -path=kubernetes-playground kubernetes_x000D_
   vault write auth/kubernetes-playground/config \_x000D_
     kubernetes_host=https://playground.kubernetes.internal \_x000D_
     kubernetes_ca_cert="..." \_x000D_
     disable_local_ca_jwt="true"_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
   (leaving out the CA certificate for readability)_x000D_
_x000D_
2. Create a role using label selector such as_x000D_
   ```bash_x000D_
   vault write auth/kubernetes-playground/role/testing \_x000D_
     bound_service_account_names="*" \_x000D_
     bound_service_account_namespace_selector="{\"matchLabels\":{\"allow-vault\":\"true\"}}" \_x000D_
     audience="https://playground.kubernetes.internal" \_x000D_
     policies="kv-reader" \_x000D_
     token_ttl=2m_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
3. In the Kubernetes cluster, create a service account (e.g. `vault-test/vault-reader`) and give it permission to review tokens and to read namespaces:_x000D_
   ```bash_x000D_
   kubectl create namespace vault-test_x000D_
   kubectl label namespace vault-test allow-vault=true_x000D_
   kubectl -n vault-test create sa vault-reader_x000D_
   kubectl create clusterrolebinding vault-reader:token-review \_x000D_
     --clusterrole system:auth-delegator \_x000D_
     --serviceaccount vault-test:vault-reader_x000D_
   kubectl create clusterrolebinding vault-reader:view \_x000D_
     --clusterrole view \_x000D_
     --serviceaccount vault-test:vault-reader_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
   Then create a token for that service account:_x000D_
   ```bash_x000D_
   kubectl -n vault-test create token vault-reader_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
4. Use that token to login to the auth method_x000D_
   ```bash_x000D_
   TOKEN=<token from step 3>_x000D_
   curl --request POST -v \_x000D_
     --data "{\"role\":\"testing\",\"jwt\":\"$TOKEN\"}" \_x000D_
     $VAULT_ADDR/v1/auth/kubernetes-playground/login_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
   Returns 403 with:_x000D_
   ```json_x000D_
   {"errors":["namespace not authorized err=namespace lookup failed: TokenReviewer JWT needs to be configured to use namespace selectors"]}_x000D_
   ```_x000D_
_x000D_
   Note that the login works well when replacing `bound_service_account_namespace_selector` by a matching `bound_service_account_namespaces`._x000D_
_x000D_
   Also note that login works with namespace selector (as expected) when setting this (or another sufficiently authorized) token statically as `token_reviewer_jwt` in the method config._x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
Vault probably should use the same token it uses for the token review (in that case, the one presented by the client during login) for the namespace lookup. At least it should not insist to have a static long-living `token_reviewer_jwt` configured on the method._x000D_
_x000D_

    ---             -----_x000D_
    Seal Type       shamir_x000D_

    HA Enabled      true_x000D_
    HA Cluster      https://vault-2.vault-internal:8201_x000D_

title: Redirect URL listener bind should be configurable
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**_x000D_
When doing an `oidc` vault login, the listener for the response will only receive on localhost. This behavior is mostly fine, except when trying to perform authorization within a container. The response to the listener fails because its bound to the local container interface and won't allow connections from the host._x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe the solution you'd like**_x000D_
It would be nice if we could bind the `8250` listener on `0.0.0.0` as a configurable switch. This would allow the response from the OIDC provider to filter through to the container. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Describe alternatives you've considered**_x000D_
An alternative solution would be to allow alternative ports in the `redirect_uris` configuration and do some kind of forwarding via `socat` or otherwise. This is obviously kludgy and prone to failure. _x000D_
_x000D_
**Explain any additional use-cases**_x000D_
This could help customers test their solutions in containerized environments._x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
**Current**_x000D_
```_x000D_
> vault login -token-only -method='oidc'_x000D_
```_x000D_
```_x000D_
> netstat -tuln_x000D_
Proto Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address           Foreign Address         State      _x000D_
tcp        0      0 127.0.0.1:8250          0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN  _x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Proposed**_x000D_
```_x000D_
> vault login -token-only -method='oidc' bind=0.0.0.0_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
> netstat -tuln_x000D_
Proto Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address           Foreign Address         State      _x000D_
tcp        0      0 0.0.0.0:8250          0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN  _x000D_
```_x000D_

title: PKI: Progressive performance degradation upon CA/issuer rotation
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests._x000D_
_x000D_
For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker._x000D_
_x000D_
Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/)._x000D_
_x000D_
-->_x000D_
_x000D_
## Describe the bug_x000D_
_x000D_
HA Vault PKI engine with raft storage experiences progressive and permanent performance degradation upon CA/issuer generate (root) or import (root or intermediate) operations._x000D_
Separate PKI engines are not impacted (but experience the same progressive and permanent performance degradation)._x000D_
Performance can be restored by disabling and then re-enabling the engine at the previous endpoint._x000D_
_x000D_
**Testing parameters:**_x000D_
_x000D_
- CA private key (root or intermediate):_x000D_
    - type: `internal`_x000D_
    - algorithm: RSA or EC_x000D_
    - bits: EC 256, 384, 521; RSA 2048, 4096, 8192_x000D_
- Vault cluster: 3 nodes, raft integrated storage_x000D_
- Platform: _x000D_
    - distro: RKE2 `v1.24.15+rke2r1`_x000D_
    - storage: Longhorn_x000D_
- Workload:_x000D_
    - type: StatefulSet_x000D_
    - requests/limits: none (unlimited)_x000D_
_x000D_
This performance issue is not experienced for CA CSR generation._x000D_
To me, this indicates that this issue is not tied to the private key, but to the issuer._x000D_
_x000D_
**Observations:**_x000D_
_x000D_
- **CPU Usage:** Peaks at ~900m on the raft leader pod (vault-0) during operation (25% of the 4 vCPUs available)_x000D_
- **Memory Usage:** less than 5% of the node's allocated memory across all pods_x000D_
- **Disk I/O:** negligible (`%iowait` less than ~0.07 on all pods)_x000D_
- **Inter-Pod Latency:**_x000D_
	- Ping tests between Vault pods show negligible latency (<1ms)_x000D_
	- Pods are in the same availability zone_x000D_
- **OpenSSL Benchmark**:_x000D_
	- RSA 4096 key generation on cluster nodes is fast, completing **60 keys in less than 50 seconds**_x000D_
	- Indicates no issues with cryptographic library performance or hardware acceleration_x000D_
- **AES-NI Availability:**_x000D_
	- Verified inside Vault containers using `/proc/cpuinfo`_x000D_
	- The `aes` flag is present, confirming support for hardware-accelerated crypto_x000D_
- **Entropy**_x000D_
	- `sudo cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep rand` showed `rdrand` available on all nodes_x000D_
	- `sudo cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/entropy_avail` showed >3500 on all cluster nodes_x000D_
	- `rng-tools` package installed to test `/dev/random` and `/dev/urandom`_x000D_
	- `rngtest -c 10000 </dev/urandom` showed >1000x speed over `rngtest -c 10000 </dev/random` (expected)_x000D_
	- started `rngd` service with `sudo systemctl enable --now rngd`, observed significant performance improvement in `/dev/random` speed with `rngtest`_x000D_
	- `rngtest` on `/dev/random` and `/dev/urandom` now within one order of magnitude (26s vs 2.6s, respectively)_x000D_
	- no observable impact in Vault PKI keypair generation speed_x000D_
_x000D_
**Tracing:**_x000D_
_x000D_
On a Vault cluster that is experiencing PKI engine performance degradation, I called the [trace endpoint](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/system/pprof#trace) `/v1/sys/pprof/trace` with the parameter `seconds=60`, after which I called the PKI engine's generate root endpoint. _x000D_
Analysis under `go tool trace <file>` showed high latency in the synchronization blocking profile, specifically this goroutine: `github.com/hashicorp/raft.(*raftState).goFunc.func1`._x000D_
Under the synchronization blocking profile page, I noticed the graph showed edges with times greater than 60s and nodes showed `0 of <time> (<percent>%)` where `<time>` and `<percent>` are non-zero._x000D_
_x000D_
## To Reproduce_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Deploy Vault in HA on Kubernetes with Helm chart with raft integrated storage and awskms seal_x000D_
2. Run `vault secrets enable pki`_x000D_
3. Run `for i in $(seq 1 60); do time curl -k -X POST "https://<vault_url>/v1/pki/root/generate/internal" -H "X-Vault-Token: <vault_token>" --data '{"common_name": "TEST CURL ROOT", "key_type": "rsa", "key_bits": 2048}'; done`_x000D_
4. Observe increasing delay in responses_x000D_
5. Run `sleep 600; time curl -k -X POST "https://<vault_url>/v1/pki/root/generate/internal" -H "X-Vault-Token: <vault_token>" --data '{"common_name": "TEST CURL ROOT", "key_type": "rsa", "key_bits": 2048}'`_x000D_
6. Observe no decrease in delay in responses_x000D_
_x000D_
## Expected behavior_x000D_
Vault PKI engine performance should not degrade, or at least recover._x000D_
_x000D_
## Environment_x000D_
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.18.1 built 2024-10-29T14:21:31Z_x000D_
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.18.1 (f479e5c85462477c9334564bc8f69531cdb03b65), built 2024-10-29T14:21:31Z_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: RHEL 8.8 4.18.0-477.15.1.el8_8.x86_64_x000D_
* Platform Architecture: RKE2 v1.24.15+rke2r1 on AWS EC2 (5+ nodes), 3 dedicated C6i.xlarge nodes for Vault_x000D_
_x000D_
## Vault server configuration file(s)_x000D_
_x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
disable_mlock = true_x000D_
ui = true_x000D_
_x000D_
listener "tcp" {_x000D_
  tls_disable = true_x000D_
  address = "[::]:8200"_x000D_
  cluster_address = "[::]:8201"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
storage "raft" {_x000D_
  path = "/vault/data"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
seal "awskms" {_x000D_
  region = "eu-west-2"_x000D_
  kms_key_id = "<clipped>"_x000D_
  endpoint     = "http://local-kms:8081"_x000D_
  access_key   = "dummy"_x000D_
  secret_key   = "dummy"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
service_registration "kubernetes" {}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
## Additional context_x000D_
_x000D_
**Attempted remediations:**_x000D_
_x000D_
- **Improve single core performance:** pinned vault pod to nodes, from t3.xlarge to c3i.xlarge - very minor effect, permanent_x000D_
- **Isolate Vault pods:** isolated vault workload to dedicated c3i.xlarge nodes - very minor effect, permanent_x000D_
- **Increase worker count:** `vault write sys/mounts/pki/config/tune options=worker_count=4` - no effect_x000D_
- **Decrease max lease:** `vault secrets tune -max-lease-ttl=1h pki` - no effect_x000D_
- **Tidy PKI engine:** `vault write pki/tidy tidy_cert_store=true tidy_revoked_certs=true` - no effect_x000D_
- **Snapshot and import raft log:** `vault operator raft snapshot save snapshot.snap; vault operator raft snapshot restore snapshot.snap`_x000D_
- **Enable and disable PKI engine:** `vault secrets disable pki; vault secrets enable -path=pki pki` - greatest effect, non-permanent_x000D_

stevendpclark: Hi @aescaler-raft, I really appreciate the offer to work on this. This won't be a trivial fix to address overall within the PKI engine at this stage. Historically the PKI engine only supported a single issuer, we added multi-issuer support to help with rotating that issuer, it was never meant to have a large number of distinct issuers within the mount itself. CRL rebuilding on initial CA creation is one item but depending on how many issuers you are talking about the following items might also need to be tackled, off the top of my head (this isn't an exhaustive list) - There's a single config object that stores the mapping of issuer to CRL, this might hit limitations on storage size if too many issuers are active within a mount - OCSP queries iterate over all issuers within the mount to identify the proper issuer which might become an issue with a large list - All revocations are stored in a single folder for all issuers, which will lead to lengthy CRL rebuilds if you have a lot of revocations across many issuers. - Within the various operational paths, if the issuer name and/or key name is used instead of UUIDs we iterate over the list of issuers to identify the issuer requested which if large enough could end up with additional delays and storage hits. So this will be a pretty significant effort to make the PKI engine do what you want. > Regarding the documentation, is there any specific reason why this isn't documented in the page linked? I can't think of any particular reason, this should probably be called out though in that same section as another reason we do not recommend running a large number of issuers within an individual mount.

In order to meet my customer's requirements, I don't see any other options than: - build an additional service which re-implements features that Vault already has, additionally routes data/operations from/to multiple PKI engines, and persists state in an additional external system --or-- - implement the changes needed directly in Vault I'm partial to contributing directly to Vault, but this of course assumes appetite from maintainers and contributors such as yourself. Please advise.

I think this should work as vault still owns the file, but it doesn't. # 2) WORKING PERMISSIONS However, if I do this before my scp: ``` tmp_cmd=$(cat <<EOF sudo chown -R ubuntu:ubuntu /opt/vault/tls sudo chown ubuntu:ubuntu /opt/vault/tls/tls.crt sudo chown ubuntu:ubuntu /opt/vault/tls/tls.key sudo chmod -R u+x /opt/vault/tls sudo chmod -R u+rw /opt/vault/tls sudo chmod u+rw /opt/vault/tls/tls.crt sudo chmod u+rw /opt/vault/tls/tls.key EOF ) ssh -i "$pem" "$user@$url" "${tmp_cmd}" ``` And after: ``` tmp_cmd=$(cat <<EOF sudo chown -R vault:vault /opt/vault/tls EOF ) ssh -i "$pem" "$user@$url" "${tmp_cmd}" ``` This does work. Why does one work and the other doesn't? Seems Vault wants to own the key files and directory and not have any read/write/execute permission allowed to anyone else or it fails. Which is fine if so but we need clear rules in documentation or error messages to explain it. This is just by trial and error at this point. Just FYI @stevendpclark if you are looking into documenting this or giving a useful and specific error to explain the issue. ie. What precise permissions are allowed or not allowed on the keys to work.
stevendpclark: Hi @jonmdev, There's only so much we can document, for example removing the execution bit from a directory in Linux forbids users from listing/reading it's contents. So yes the /opt/vault/tls/ needs at a minimum u+x permissions from the `vault` user to read files within it. And you probably don't want to give the Vault user read and write permissions to those TLS keys, read should be sufficient unless you want Vault itself to be able to update them. You might want to look into the `vault operator diagnose -config=/etc/vault/config.hcl` which does have a lot of these checks and reporting built into it.

_x000D_

_x000D_
The impact is considered medium as an attacker could use the disclosed information to research any attack vectors related to the version of software disclosed, however the likelihood is low as an attacker would require access to both the application and the environment._x000D_
_x000D_
Recommendation_x000D_
_x000D_
It is recommended that all web application error messages are configured so that they do not disclose information unnecessarily. They should be as static as possible, containing only text such as "Sorry, there has been an error with the application. Please contact the system administrator if the problem persists"._x000D_
_x000D_
Ideally, users should not be informed that an error has occurred; instead the application should continue to work as normal as this will reduce the likelihood of an attacker being able to enumerate the internal workings of the system. It should be noted, however, that this approach may cause a problem if a genuine bug is present in the system.

title: Vault SDK/Custom Auth Plugin — RemotePort in Client Connection Always Returns 0
body_text:
**Describe the Bug**  _x000D_
When implementing a Vault authentication plugin, the `RemoteAddr` field correctly reflects the IP address of the Vault client. However, the `RemotePort` field always returns `0`, regardless of the client's actual port.  _x000D_
_x000D_
This makes it impossible to implement functionality that distinguishes between privileged and unprivileged client ports, even though the `RemotePort` field is present in the API.  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Steps to Reproduce**  _x000D_
1. Clone HashiCorp's [[Vault auth plugin example](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-auth-plugin-example.git)](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-auth-plugin-example.git).  _x000D_
2. Modify the plugin code to include logging for `req.Connection.RemotePort`, as shown below:  _x000D_
_x000D_
```go_x000D_
func (b *backend) pathAuthLogin(_ context.Context, req *logical.Request, d *framework.FieldData) (*logical.Response, error) {_x000D_
    b.Logger().Info("login requested :)")_x000D_
_x000D_
    if req.Connection == nil {_x000D_
        b.Logger().Error("connection is nil")_x000D_
    } else {_x000D_
        b.Logger().Info("connection details",_x000D_
            "remoteAddr", req.Connection.RemoteAddr,_x000D_
            "remotePort", req.Connection.RemotePort)_x000D_
    }_x000D_
_x000D_
    if req.Connection.RemotePort >= 1024 {_x000D_
        b.Logger().Error("unprivileged port", "err", logical.ErrPermissionDenied.Error())_x000D_
        return nil, logical.ErrPermissionDenied_x000D_
    }_x000D_
_x000D_
    password := d.Get("password").(string)_x000D_
_x000D_
    [...]_x000D_
}_x000D_
```  _x000D_
_x000D_
3. Build and test the plugin using `./docker-test.sh`.  _x000D_
4. Check the logs with `docker logs $(docker ps -lq)`. The logs will show `remotePort=0`, e.g.:  _x000D_
_x000D_
```_x000D_
2024-12-13T08:53:13.428Z [INFO]  auth.example-auth-plugin.auth_example-auth-plugin_647ba2e9.example-auth-plugin.vault-auth-plugin-example: login requested :): timestamp=2024-12-13T08:53:13.428Z_x000D_
2024-12-13T08:53:13.428Z [INFO]  auth.example-auth-plugin.auth_example-auth-plugin_647ba2e9.example-auth-plugin.vault-auth-plugin-example: connection details: remoteAddr=192.168.127.1 remotePort=0 timestamp=2024-12-13T08:53:13.428Z_x000D_
```  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected Behavior**  _x000D_
The `RemotePort` field should reflect the actual ephemeral port used by the Vault client, similar to how it is captured in Vault audit logs. For example, an expected output might show:  _x000D_
_x000D_
```json_x000D_
"request": {_x000D_
    "remote_address": "10.0.101.5",_x000D_
    "remote_port": 56946_x000D_
}_x000D_
```  _x000D_
_x000D_
This would allow developers to differentiate between privileged (≤1023) and unprivileged (≥1024) ports.  _x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment**  _x000D_
- **Vault Server Version**: `hashicorp/vault:latest` (1.18.2)  _x000D_

- Alternatively, use the `VAULT_TOKEN` environment variable._x000D_

https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/seal/transit#token_x000D_
[token](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/seal/transit#token) (string: <required>): The Vault token to use. This may also be specified by the VAULT_TOKEN environment variable._x000D_

title: Service reload is deregistering the consul service

We have a vault cluster running the latest v1.18.3 which is using consul as storage and also registering the service in consul:_x000D_
_x000D_
> storage "consul" {_x000D_
      address = "127.0.0.1:8500"_x000D_
      path = "vault/poc"_x000D_
      service = "vault-poc"_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
Also we have enabled audit logs in vault and configured logrotate config to rotate the logs on daily basis. We also have added a command to reload it as mentioned in the docs (basically sending a HUP signal to the process)_x000D_
_x000D_
> {_x000D_
      daily_x000D_
      missingok_x000D_
      maxage 30_x000D_
      sharedscripts_x000D_
      rotate 10_x000D_
      compress_x000D_
      delaycompress_x000D_
      notifempty_x000D_
      copytruncate_x000D_
      postrotate_x000D_
        /usr/bin/systemctl reload vault 2> /dev/null || true_x000D_
      endscript_x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
The issue here is with `systemctl reload vault` . We have tested it with different versions of vault and it is deregistering the consul service starting v1.17.0 version when it is working properly in v1.16.3. when I reload vault in v1.17.0 or later I get this in the logs:_x000D_
_x000D_
`[DEBUG] service_registration.consul: registration is now empty, deregistering service from consul`_x000D_
_x000D_
The consul dns entry for the vault cluster is used widely by the other apps and is a very important component in our installation, but we lose it after logrotate proceeds with the rotation._x000D_
To fix this I have to restart the service and unseal the nodes to get the consul service registered again._x000D_
_x000D_
I didn't find anything in release notes or issues regarding this specific issue. Are we doing something wrong or is this indeed a bug? _x000D_
Thank you.

title: Vault Okta Plugin Fails to Support Custom Domains for Authentication (Malformed base_URLs)
body_text:
**Describe the bug**_x000D_
The Vault Okta plugin incorrectly forms the API endpoint when both base_url and org_name are used. It treats org_name as a subdomain and appends it incorrectly to the base_url. This results in a malformed URL when using a custom Okta domain._x000D_
 _x000D_
For example:_x000D_
_x000D_
Configured:_x000D_
 **base_url**_x000D_
```_x000D_
"https://sso.MyCustomDomain.ca" _x000D_
```_x000D_
**org_name**_x000D_
```_x000D_
"dev-123456"_x000D_
```_x000D_
Expected: _x000D_
```_x000D_
https://sso.MyCustomDomain.ca/api/v1/authn_x000D_
```_x000D_
Actual:  when trying to login with a user _x000D_
```bash_x000D_
$ vault login -method=okta   username="johnDoe@gmail.com"   password="NoCanDo" _x000D_
_x000D_
Okta auth failed: Post "https://dev-123456.sso.MyCustomDomain.ca/api/v1/authn":_x000D_
 dial tcp: lookup dev-123456.sso.MyCustomDomain.ca on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
This issue occurs when attempting to configure Vault to use a custom Okta domain (e.g., https://sso.MyCustomDomain.ca). _x000D_
Vault expects `org_name` for constructing Okta API calls but mishandles it when combined with a `custom domain`._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
- The vault auth configuration works when using the default base_url `"okta.com" + org_name`_x000D_
- DNS and REST API requests work : _x000D_
```hcl_x000D_
dig sso.MyCustomDomain.ca_x000D_
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 59642_x000D_
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 6, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1_x000D_
_x000D_
---_x000D_
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json"  -d '{"username":"johnDoe@gmail.com","password":"NoCanDo"}' _x000D_
 https://sso.MyCustomDomain.ca/api/v1/authn | jq ._x000D_
_x000D_
{_x000D_
  "expiresAt": "2025-01-06T03:11:26.000Z",_x000D_
  "status": "SUCCESS",_x000D_
..._x000D_
}_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
# To Reproduce_x000D_
prereq: config okta new [brand/ custom domain](https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/custom-url-domain/main/)_x000D_
Steps to reproduce the behavior:_x000D_
1. Configure Vault with a custom domain:_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash _x000D_
vault write auth/okta/config \_x000D_
    base_url="https://sso.MyCustomDomain.ca" \_x000D_
    org_name="dev-123456" \_x000D_
    api_token="<api_token>"_x000D_
```_x000D_
2. Attempt to log in:_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash _x000D_
vault login -method=okta \_x000D_
    username="johnDoe@gmail.com" \_x000D_
    password="NoCanDo"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
3. Observe the malformed API request in the Vault logs:_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash_x000D_
https://dev-123456.sso.MyCustomDomain.ca/api/v1/authn_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
4. The resulting error:_x000D_
_x000D_
```yaml _x000D_
dial tcp: lookup dev-123456.sso.MyCustomDomain.ca on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Expected behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault should correctly construct the API endpoint as https://sso.MyCustomDomain.ca/api/v1/authn when a custom domain is used._x000D_
login command for the user should be successful _x000D_
```vault login -method=okta  username="johnDoe@gmail.com" password="NoCanDo" ```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Actual Behavior**_x000D_
_x000D_
Vault constructs an invalid API endpoint by concatenating `org_name` and `base_url` improperly, treating `org_name` as a subdomain._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
**Environment:**_x000D_
_x000D_
* Server Operating System/Architecture: ubuntu 22_x000D_
```_x000D_
Key                     Value_x000D_
---                     -----_x000D_
Seal Type               shamir_x000D_
Initialized             true_x000D_
Sealed                  false_x000D_
Total Shares            3_x000D_
Threshold               2_x000D_
Version                 1.18.3_x000D_
Build Date              2024-12-16T14:00:53Z_x000D_
Storage Type            raft_x000D_
Cluster Name            vault-cluster-e5180399_x000D_
Cluster ID              025e327c-13e0-6781-868f-ae8eb66da076_x000D_
HA Enabled              true_x000D_
HA Cluster              https://<IP>:8201_x000D_
HA Mode                 active_x000D_
Active Since            2025-01-05T02:01:12.9281897-05:00_x000D_
Raft Committed Index    382_x000D_
Raft Applied Index      382_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Additional context**_x000D_
_x000D_
- I attempted to configure Vault with the following:_x000D_
```bash _x000D_
vault write auth/okta/config \_x000D_
    base_url="https://sso.MyCustomDomain.ca" \_x000D_
    org_name="" \_x000D_
    api_token="<api_token>"_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
- Resulted in another malformed URL but it's the closest to the real url I could get:_x000D_
```bash _x000D_
https://.sso.MyCustomDomain.ca/api/v1/authn_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
**Temporary Workaround**_x000D_
_x000D_
This issue makes it difficult to use custom Okta domains for authentication. The current workaround is to use the default Okta domain:   (base_url="okta.com")  _x000D_
_x000D_
```bash _x000D_
vault write auth/okta/config \_x000D_
    base_url="okta.com" \_x000D_
    org_name="dev-123456" \_x000D_
    api_token="<api_token>"_x000D_
```_x000D_
This results in the correct API endpoint:_x000D_
_x000D_
```bash _x000D_
https://dev-123456.okta.com/api/v1/authn_x000D_
```_x000D_
_x000D_
# Request_x000D_
Please provide support for custom Okta domains without requiring org_name, or handle it correctly to avoid malformed URLs. Or advise if I did anything wrong_x000D_

title: Conditional policies
body_text:
Currently, Vault's KV v2 secrets engine does not natively support dynamic access control based on secret metadata. While it is possible to organize secrets by paths and create policies for each path, this approach becomes cumbersome and inefficient when dealing with a large number of secrets or when secrets need to be shared across multiple teams or contexts._x000D_
_x000D_
For example:_x000D_
Secrets are stored in a single path (e.g., secret/data/shared/*)._x000D_
Each secret has metadata (e.g., team=engineering, environment=production)._x000D_
_x000D_
We want to grant access to secrets based on their metadata (e.g., only instances with team=engineering can access secrets tagged with team=engineering)._x000D_
_x000D_
Currently, this requires workarounds that could be so difficult to achieve:_x000D_
Path-based organization: Duplicating secrets across multiple paths, which is not scalable._x000D_
_x000D_
so is there any vault feature that i may not know and could help me to have contitional policy based on metadata or another parameter that can be used as a tag of the secrets and instead of add all the secrets paths in the policie i only add the metadata name as condition _x000D_
_x000D_
For exemple :_x000D_
_x000D_
secrets:_x000D_
secret/data/shared/secret1_x000D_
         metadata= team=1_x000D_
secret/data/shared/secret2_x000D_
         metadata= team=1_x000D_
secret/data/shared/secret3_x000D_
         metadata= team=2_x000D_
_x000D_
policy_x000D_
resource "vault_policy" "user-1" {  _x000D_
  name = "user-1"  _x000D_
_x000D_
policy = <<EOT  _x000D_
  path "secrets/data/shared/*" {  _x000D_
    capabilities = ["read"]    _x000D_
    condition = {  _x000D_
      expr = "metadata.team == '1'"  _x000D_
    }  _x000D_
  }  _x000D_
EOT  _x000D_
}_x000D_
_x000D_
i already see this: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/policies#required_parameters  but unfortunatly it is not compatible with kv v2

title: Vault storage migration from MySQL to RAFT results in uninitialized cluster despite successful migration
body_text:
Describe the bug
I'm trying to migrate from a MySQL storage backend to a RAFT storage backend following the official documentation, but the migration process results in an uninitialized cluster, preventing me from proceeding with the migration. 
I follow this document: https://support.hashicorp.com/hc/en-us/articles/17295423360403-How-to-migrate-Vault-s-storage-backend-to-a-new-Vault-cluster-in-Kubernetes
To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

Have a source Vault cluster running with MySQL storage backend (verified running and unsealed)
Deploy a new Vault instance configured with RAFT storage (uninitialized as per documentation)
Create and apply the migration configuration file
Run vault operator migrate -config migrate.hcl
Check new cluster status showing uninitialized state instead of initialized as documented

Expected behavior
According to the documentation, after migration, the new RAFT cluster should be initialized and ready to unseal, but instead, it remains uninitialized.
Environment:

Source Vault Server Version: 1.13.2
Destination Vault Server Version: 1.18.1
Server Operating System/Architecture: OpenShift 4.14
Both source and destination Vault instances are running in the same OpenShift cluster

Migration configuration file:

```storage_source "mysql" {
  username = "mysql_user"
  password = "XXXXXXXXXXXXX"
  database = "vault"
  address = "vault-mariadb:3306"
}

storage_destination "raft" {
  path = "/vault/data/dyn-migrate"
  node_id = "vault-0"
}
cluster_addr = "http://127.0.0.1:8201"
```

Additional context
The migration command completes successfully with the message "Success! All of the keys have been migrated." However, when checking the status of the new cluster, it shows as uninitialized:

```
Key                Value
---                -----
Seal Type          shamir
Initialized        false
Sealed             true
Total Shares       0
Threshold          0
Unseal Progress    0/0
Unseal Nonce       n/a
Version            1.18.1
Build Date         2024-10-29T14:21:31Z
Storage Type       raft
HA Enabled         true
```

The source cluster status was properly initialized and unsealed before the migration attempt.

title: Vault creates mysql Secret Engines Connection error, mysql password contains # error, parsed as %23
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
Vault creates mysql Secret Engines Connection error, mysql password contains # error, parsed as %23

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run `vault secrets enable --path=db-mysql database`
2. Run `
vault write db-mysql/config/admin-mysql-connection \
plugin_name=mysql-database-plugin \
connection_url="{{username}}:{{password}}@tcp(mysql.vault.svc.cluster.local:3306)/" \
allowed_roles="create-mysql-user-role" \
username="v11@uat#test" \
password="v22@test" \
disable_escaping=true \
max_open_connections=10
`
3. See error
Error writing data to db-mysq/config/admin-mysql-connection: Error making API request.

URL: PUT https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/db-mysql/config/admin-mysql-connection
Code: 400. Errors:

* error creating database object: error verifying - ping: Error 1045 (42000): Access denied for user 'v11@uat%23test'@'mysql.vault.svc.cluster.local' (using password: YES)

**Expected behavior**
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.16.1
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.16.1

title: Incorrect Fedora Installation Instructions on HashiCorp Vault Documentation
body_text:
### **Incorrect Fedora Installation Instructions on HashiCorp Vault Documentation**

#### **Describe the Bug**
The installation instructions for Vault on Fedora, as listed on the [official HashiCorp Vault installation guide](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/install), contain an incorrect command when adding the HashiCorp repository using `dnf config-manager`.

If users follow the provided instructions and run:

```sh
sudo dnf config-manager addrepo --from-repofile=https://rpm.releases.hashicorp.com/fedora/hashicorp.repo
```

They will encounter the following error:

```
sudo dnf config-manager addrepo --from-repofile=https://rpm.releases.hashicorp.com/fedora/hashicorp.repo
usage: dnf config-manager [-c [config file]] [-q] [-v] [--version] [--installroot [path]] [--nodocs] [--noplugins] [--enableplugin [plugin]] [--disableplugin [plugin]] [--releasever RELEASEVER] [--setopt SETOPTS] [--skip-broken] [-h]
                          [--allowerasing] [-b | --nobest] [-C] [-R [minutes]] [-d [debug level]] [--debugsolver] [--showduplicates] [-e ERRORLEVEL] [--obsoletes] [--rpmverbosity [debug level name]] [-y] [--assumeno]
                          [--enablerepo [repo]] [--disablerepo [repo] | --repo [repo]] [--enable | --disable] [-x [package]] [--disableexcludes [repo]] [--repofrompath [repo,path]] [--noautoremove] [--nogpgcheck] [--color COLOR]
                          [--refresh] [-4] [-6] [--destdir DESTDIR] [--downloadonly] [--comment COMMENT] [--bugfix] [--enhancement] [--newpackage] [--security] [--advisory ADVISORY] [--bz BUGZILLA] [--cve CVES]
                          [--sec-severity {Critical,Important,Moderate,Low}] [--forcearch ARCH] [--save] [--add-repo URL] [--dump] [--dump-variables] [--set-enabled | --set-disabled]
                          [section ...]
dnf config-manager: error: unrecognized arguments: --from-repofile=https://rpm.releases.hashicorp.com/fedora/hashicorp.repo

```

This happens because `dnf config-manager` does **not** support the `--from-repofile` option.

#### **Expected Behavior**
The correct way to add the repository using `dnf` is by using the `--add-repo` option:

```sh
sudo dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo https://rpm.releases.hashicorp.com/fedora/hashicorp.repo
sudo dnf -y install vault
```

#### **Proposed Fix**
Update the Fedora installation instructions on the [Vault installation page](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/install) to use `--add-repo` instead of `--from-repofile`.

title: Using a shell to exec the `token_helper` is unreliable
body_text:
There are many ways using a shell to exec the sub-command can go wrong. Whether that is unexpected spaces in the command or that the shell reads config files that output unexpected values. We encountered the unexpected output due to a very strange interaction with vault being used in a shell. We ran into this using GNU `bash`, version `5.0.17(1)-release (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu)` in a pipe over an ssh connection.

This stemmed from folks setting a default `export VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com` in their `~/.bashrc`, and that somehow when [compiled with `SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC` defined](https://github.com/bminor/bash/blob/6794b5478f660256a1023712b5fc169196ed0a22/shell.c#L1136-L1138) as is apparently the default in some linux distributions, when bash detects it is used in a pipe and that variable is set (as it is when you have ssh'd to a remote host), bash will source `~/.bashrc`, overriding the desired `VAULT_ADDR`. This would happen, for example, with `vault list -address https://test-vault.example.com foo | cat`. This fails to login because the `token_helper` returns the token for `vault.example.com` instead of `test-vault.example.com`. It is also an issue with updating the `VAULT_ADDR` in your environment to something other than the default before executing vault.

**Expected behavior**
Given the existing restriction on using [only absolute paths](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/04e75372fb30a4ec03645ca1de60bba54c2bc9dc/api/tokenhelper/helper_external.go#L23), the token helper commands should be executed directly without involving the shell.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): `1.18.3`
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): `Vault v1.18.3 (7ae4eca5403bf574f142cd8f987b8d83bafcd1de), built 2024-12-16T14:00:53Z`

title: Workload Identity forces disabling of mutual TLS client verification, contradicting Nomad’s own best practices
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
When using Nomad Workload Identity (JWT-based) to integrate with Vault, Nomad’s documentation states:

> “It is highly recommended to use mutual TLS in production deployments of Nomad. With mTLS enabled, the `tls.verify_https_client` configuration must be set to false since it is not possible to provide client certificates to the Vault auth method.”

This effectively disables Nomad’s mutual TLS client verification for Vault calls. Requiring tls.verify_https_client = false directly conflicts with the general recommendation to use mTLS in production. This omission forces operators to choose between best-practice security (mTLS everywhere) and enabling JWT-based workload identity.

In other words, we are asked to run our cluster in a way that is not aligned with the very security best practices Nomad prescribes.

**To Reproduce**
1. Configure Nomad for JWT-based Workload Identity.
2. Enable mutual TLS across the Nomad cluster.
3. Attempt to use `tls.verify_https_client = true` for Vault calls.
4. Observe that JWT authentication to Vault fails because you cannot provide client certificates on the Vault JWT auth method.

**Expected behavior**
We expect full mTLS support during JWT authentication to Vault. Ideally, Vault’s JWT auth method (or Nomad’s usage of it) should be able to present a client certificate to Nomad, such that we can keep `tls.verify_https_client = true` while still using workload identities.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): a version supporting jwt/oidc
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): a version supporting jwt/oidc
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux of some kind

Vault server configuration file(s):

```hcl
jwt_validation_pubkeys = [...]
jwks_ca_pem = "..."
```

Nomad service configuration file(s):

```hcl
tls {
  http = true
  rpc  = true

  verify_server_hostname = true
  verify_https_client    = true  # Fails with JWT-based workload identity
}
```

**Additional context**

The docs explicitly state to disable `tls.verify_https_client`, despite also saying mTLS is recommended.

**_Security Impact_**

Disabling client verification undermines the otherwise strong security model that mTLS provides. With client certificate authentication disabled, we rely solely on token-based authentication without the additional layer of cryptographic identity verification at the TLS layer.

**_Request_**

Please add official support for presenting client certificates through the Vault JWT auth method, or provide an alternative approach that does not require disabling `tls.verify_https_client`. This feature would align Nomad Workload Identity with the recommended production security posture.

Or, don't deprecate Vault Token authentication until Workload Identity is at feature parity while adhering to best practices. (Nomad docs say vault token authentication goes away in 1.10, and latest tag is 1.9.5)

I couldn't find an open issue after some quick searching, so I opened this.

edit: Opened hashicorp/nomad#24970 to push out the deprecation again, or until this feature exists

title: Rewrap does not work if data is encrypted using associated data
top_3_comments_text: aslamovamir: Hi @d3bt3ch thanks for opening the issue with us! Hmm, looks like what you assume is right: `rewrap` operation in Vault's transit secret engine does not support `associated_data` as a parameter. The reason why this error might be happening is that given the `rewrap` operation is supposed to re-encrypt data using a newer version of the encryption key without modifying any authenticated data, if `associated_data` was used during encryption but is not supported during `rewrap`, the new encryption process fails because Vault cannot properly validate the auth tag. The `associated_data` is used in AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data) encryption operations, like encrypt and decrypt, but it is not required or used in rewrap. If your use case involves AEAD and you need to rewrap while maintaining authentication with `associated_data`, you would have to decrypt the data first and then re-encrypt it with the new key version, manually providing the `associated_data`. So, the suggestion would be to 1) Read and decrypt the data using the original `associated_data` 2) Encrypt the data again with `associated_data` using the latest key version 3) Store the newly encrypted data. If you would like more information about the `rewrap` operation, [this link](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/encryption-as-a-service/eaas-transit-rewrap) might help more! | d3bt3ch: > So, the suggestion would be to 1) Read and decrypt the data using the original associated_data 2) Encrypt the data again with associated_data using the latest key version 3) Store the newly encrypted data. title: Invalid flags during plugin registration are silently ignored
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
When registering a plugin using `vault plugin register`, if the plugin doesn't check the error return from `flags.Parse()`, invalid flags are silently ignored and the registration succeeds. This could lead to confusion as users might think their configuration flags are being applied when they're actually being ignored.

This bug can be found from various built-in Vault plugins, such as:

- `credential/approle`
- `logical/aws`
- `logical/pki`

However, it is mostly a code quality issue as the plugins are not dynamically loaded. But the approach has propagated beyond this repository as it's part of the Vault plugin documentation as well. For third party plugins this missing error check might be more than a code quality issue though.

I've had a proposal to fix this for a while in #28692. This PR has links to related & affected plugins with the same issue.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a simple plugin that doesn't check the error from `flags.Parse()`:
```go
func main() {
    apiClientMeta := &api.PluginAPIClientMeta{}
    flags := apiClientMeta.FlagSet()
    flags.Parse(os.Args[1:]) // Error not checked
    // ... rest of plugin code ...
}
```

2. Register the plugin with an invalid flag:
```bash
vault plugin register -sha256=$SHA256 -command=vault-plugin-auth-dummy -args="-invalid-flag=test" auth dummy
```

3. The registration succeeds despite the invalid flag

## Expected behavior
The plugin registration should fail when invalid flags are provided, as these flags might be intended for configuration but are being silently ignored. If the return value is checked, Vault prints this upon plugin register:

```bash
Unrecognized remote plugin message: Error parsing flags: flag provided but not defined: -invalid-flag
```

## Actual behavior
The plugin registration succeeds, silently ignoring the invalid flags.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): v1.19.0-beta1 (built latest from `main`)
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`):  v1.19.0-beta1 (built latest from `main`)
* Server Operating System/Architecture: arm64

title: Go client SDK retries on transit/restore if key already exists
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
Restoring a key in the transit engine fails with HTTP status 500 if the key already exists. The Vault go client SDK handles that by default with a timeout + retry (*), which unnecessarily causes waiting on the client side and additional requests on the server side.

(*) This appears to be caused by the `DefaultRetryPolicy`:
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/afd7b1a59040def739355a631f4a061570828759/api/client.go#L1885
https://github.com/hashicorp/go-retryablehttp/blob/9dfd949154e507c91ee569367ffa461991b80950/client.go#L472
https://github.com/hashicorp/go-retryablehttp/blob/9dfd949154e507c91ee569367ffa461991b80950/client.go#L538

It is of course possible to adjust this via `MaxRetry` and `CheckRetry` on the client object, but in my opinion the default should also not retry for this error.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run `vault secrets enable transit`
2. Run `vault write transit/keys/foo exportable=true allow_plaintext_backup=true`
3. Run `vault read --field=data --field=backup transit/backup/foo > backup`
4. Write a go program that uses `vault/api`:
```
client := api.NewClient()
_, err := client.Logical().Write("transit/restore/foo", map[string]any{"data": backupData})
```
The `client` will retry the operation multiple times until it finally rejects the operation.

**Expected behavior**
Immediate failure on the first try of restoring a key that already exists.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.13.3
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.13.3
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux/x86_64

title: tcp_mem keeps increasing

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1) Deploy 1.18.3 vault in ubuntu 22.04-arm64
2) Use Vault secret operator or csi driver to consume secrets. Run a small scale (500 read request per minute) loadtest for a day.
3) you will observe that tcp mem is consuming memory. Eventually, vault will become very slow unless you restart the service.

**Expected behavior**
Vault service should not be the reason for OOM kill.

Vault server configuration file(s):
```
storage "raft" {
    node_id = "xxx"

title: Multiple configs not merged correctly for `vault-agent`
top_3_comments_text: blueberry-pi: I believe what's happening is the combination of two things: 1. When merging configs, we always apply them in the order that's provided, so if two configs change the same field, the second one overwrites the change of the first 2. When a config does not have a `template_config` stanza, we give it an empty template config with just `MaxConnectionsPerHost` set to the default - this is to make sure the default is enforced even if no template config is provided So the template config provided in `base.json` is getting overwritten by a mostly empty one we created when we parsed `templates.json`. We can validate this is the case because swapping the order of the two configs when calling `vault agent` gives the correct config values. I can put up a fix for this.

title: ldap.LDAPAuth type does not handle alternate namespaces
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
When authenticating Vault Enterprise namespaces using the ldap.LDAPAuth type,there is no way to pass in the namespace to authenticate against.

Based on the REST API docs, I would expect that either of the following mechanisms would work to authenticate to a specific namespace:
 - add namespace to path e.g. `/v1/${NAMESPACE}/auth/ldap/login/${USERNAME}`
 - add X-Vault-Namespace header to request

The existing `Path` parameter can be used to inject additional components between `auth` and `ldap`, but in order to use namespaces, the additional path component must be between `v1` and `auth` ref https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/ldap/ldap.go#L112

For additional context, my usecase involves using the ExternalSecrets operator to authenticate to vault --- the ExternalSecrets operator lets me embed an ldap.LDAPAuth into my CRD so that's why I am using this particular API https://external-secrets.io/latest/api/generator/vault/

**Expected behavior**
I would imagine the LDAPAuth type to accept an additional `namespace` arg  here https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/ldap/ldap.go#L17 

which, if nonempty, would get injected here https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/api/auth/ldap/ldap.go#L112 before the `auth` component.

**Environment:**
Using the VaultDynamicSecret CRD which is handled by the ExternalSecrets operator in k8s https://external-secrets.io/latest/api/generator/vault/. Once the API is added into this hashicorp vault repo, the ExternalSecrets operator will also need to be updated to consume the new type.

I'm happy to make a PR for this if a maintainer thinks this is a reasonable understanding of the issue and a reasonable solution.

title: Error 500 when trying to export missing certificate-chain from the transit engine
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->

**Describe the bug**
The [export-key](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/transit#export-key) endpoint returns a 500 error with the message "selected key version does not have a certificate chain imported" when attempting to export a missing (non-imported) certificate chain. While the message is informative, the error code is misleading—it should likely be a 404. This poses challenges for us, as the issue is automatically reported as a real error, even though this behavior is expected.

**To Reproduce**
Python script:

"""
This script is used to test the export of the certificate chain and verify the
Vault server's 500 error response.
"""

import hvac
from packaging.version import Version
import requests

BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8200"


class VaultAPIError(requests.exceptions.RequestException):
    """Vault API Error"""


def compare_versions(version1, version2):
    """Returns: -1, 0, 1"""
    return (Version(version1) > Version(version2)) - (
        Version(version1) < Version(version2)
    )


def export_certificate_chain(client):
    """Export Certificate Chain: not supported in hvac 2.3.0"""
    url = BASE_URL + "/v1/transit/export/certificate-chain/my-transit-key"
    response = requests.get(url, headers={"X-Vault-Token": client.token}, timeout=3)
    if response.status_code != 200:
        data = response.json()
        errors = data.get("errors", [])
        print(f"GET {url}: {response.status_code} - {errors}")

        assert response.status_code == 500, "500 error response expected"
        assert (
            "selected key version does not have a certificate chain imported"
            in errors[0]
        ), "expected error message"


def delete_key(client, key_name):
    """Delete key"""
    client.secrets.transit.update_key_configuration(
        name=key_name, deletion_allowed=True
    )
    client.secrets.transit.delete_key(name=key_name)


def main():
    """main"""
    client = hvac.Client(url=BASE_URL, token="vault-root-token")
    assert client.is_authenticated()

    url = BASE_URL + "/v1/sys/version-history"
    response = requests.request(
        "LIST",
        url,
        headers={
            "X-Vault-Token": "vault-root-token",
        },
        timeout=3, 
    )
    if response.status_code != 200:
        raise VaultAPIError(f"LIST {url}: {response.status_code} {response.text}")
    version = None
    data = response.json()
    for key in data["data"]["keys"]:
        if not version or list(map(int, key.split("."))) > list(
            map(int, version.split("."))
        ):
            version = key
    # https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/v1.15.x/secret/transit#export-key
    assert (
        compare_versions(version, "1.15.0") >= 0
    ), "export CertificateChain requires 1.15.x"

    if "transit/" not in client.sys.list_mounted_secrets_engines():
        client.sys.enable_secrets_engine(
            "transit", path="transit", mount_point="transit"
        )

    key_name = "my-transit-key"
    client.secrets.transit.create_key(
        name=key_name, exportable=True, key_type="rsa-2048"
    )

    try:
        export_certificate_chain(client)
    except Exception:
        delete_key(client, key_name)
        raise

    delete_key(client, key_name)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()


**Expected behavior**
While the message is informative, the error code 500 is misleading—it should likely be a 404.

title: 1.19.0 Breaking Bug: AWS STS 400 Error: {"errors":["number of regions does not match number of endpoints"]}
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
After updating to 1.19.0, when calling an aws sts endpoint, we now receive `{"errors":["number of regions does not match number of endpoints"]}`. These calls all used to work just fine. 

The new error was introduced in this PR https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/29051

The AWS backend is configured like:

```
resource "vault_aws_secret_backend" "aws-chia" {
  access_key = var.chia_aws_access_key_id
  secret_key = var.chia_aws_secret_access_key
  path       = "aws"
}
```

You will note that in this config, no sts endpoint is set at all since that is supposed to be an optional parameter, so it was previously using whatever the default was. If I'm following the flow correctly, `&endpoint` was likely nil at this point https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.18.5/builtin/logical/aws/client.go#L96 and AWS SDK probably had a fallback.

On the new PR / 1.19.0:

fallback region is specifically set to us-east-1 in the client.go file https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/c937b3e2546bb40606b4cba1d1a5a1a53bfc2840/builtin/logical/aws/client.go#L36 and then later, if no region(s) were otherwise set, this hardcoded default is added to the regions list https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/c937b3e2546bb40606b4cba1d1a5a1a53bfc2840/builtin/logical/aws/client.go#L96

No such logic exists for endpoints - if no endpoints are set in config at all (which is not documented as required), the endpoints will be an empty list.

The combination of these two factors results in this error always firing for very simple sts configurations, since endpoints will be 0 and regions will always be at least 1. (I have not tried editing the code and trying a new build, but this is the only explanation I see at first glance that explains the issue)

title: Repeated forced Raft snapshot restores in Vault 1.19.0 cause unexpected sealing cycles in DR cluster
body_text:
**Description:**
After upgrading from Vault OSS 1.18.5 to 1.19.0, our process to update our DR cluster every 6 hours using a forced Raft snapshot restore now results in repeated sealing/unsealing cycles. In our workflow, we routinely perform restore using our production snapshot. Although we tolerate a brief downtime during each restore, in 1.19.0 the node repeatedly re-seals itself after auto-unsealing. This behavior did not occur in previous release 1.18.5.

**Environment:**

Vault Version: 1.19.0
Storage: Raft
Seal Configuration: Azure Key Vault (with identical settings to production)
DR Setup: 5-node DR cluster
Restore Process: Every 6 hours, we perform the following steps:
    Perform prod backup.
    On DR cluster , run vault operator raft snapshot restore --force /path/to/snapshot.snap.
    Vault auto-unseals using Azure Key Vault on PROD and DR.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

On DR cluster : Execute a forced snapshot restore:

vault operator raft snapshot restore --force /path/to/snapshot.snap

Observe that after the restore, the node auto-unseals briefly but then quickly seals again, entering a cycle of sealing and unsealing.

**Expected Behavior:**

After restoring the snapshot, the node should load the production state and remain unsealed (aside from a brief, one-time downtime during the restore).

**Actual Behavior:**

Each forced snapshot restore triggers a full pre‑seal teardown followed by auto‑unseal. However, in 1.19.0 this process repeats itself—either due to internal key upgrade logic or cluster state reconciliation—resulting in repeated sealing/unsealing cycles, which impacts DR readiness.

**Additional Context:**

This restore process used to work correctly in Vault 1.18.5 regardless if source backup is from cluster with 1.18.5 or 1.19.0.
We perform this restore every 6 hours because our production data changes frequently, and we require near–real-time updates in DR.
Relevant log messages include lines such as:

[INFO] core: pre-seal teardown starting  
[INFO] core: Vault is sealed  
[INFO] core: failed to perform key upgrades, reloading using auto seal  
[INFO] core: vault is unsealed  

The 1.19.0 release notes mention improvements in forced snapshot restore and key upgrade flows, but we’re encountering this issue in 1.19.0.

Questions:

Is this repeated sealing/unsealing behavior in Vault OSS 1.19.0 the intended outcome when performing forced snapshot restores on an already initialized DR cluster?
Are there any recommended changes to the restore process to avoid repeated sealing in Vault OSS 1.19.0 while still performing full restores every 6 hours?

Any guidance or workarounds for avoiding the repeated seal/unseal cycle during our routine DR snapshot restores would be greatly appreciated.

title: Vault Healthcheck Reports OK Despite Critical Errors
body_text:
**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version : 1.18.4
* Deploy via Kubernetes
* Data Base with posgresql (not raft!)
* Audit log activated

**Problem**
During a mass import of secrets into Vault, the volume of logs generated saturated the disk mount on the /var/log/ partition. This made the API unusable due to the inability to write logs. The disk saturation also blocked the connection to the site, resulting in 500 errors.
However, despite these errors, the Vault healthcheck remains at a status of 200, as if everything is functioning normally. Consequently, there is no HA failover to our other nodes.

**Questions**
1. Is it normal for the Vault healthcheck to remain at a status of 200 despite these errors?
2. Is there another way to verify the status of the services to ensure everything is functioning correctly?
3. Is it possible to add a new verification method to the healthcheck to detect this type of issue?

Thank you in advance for your responses.
