title: vault agent ldap authentication support password from env
body_text:
**Describe the solution you'd like**

The ldap agent should be able to source the password from the environment variable VAULT_LDAP_PASSWORD which is supported by the cli `vault login...`


It would also be helpful to document the format of how the password file should look.
top_3_comments_text: heatherezell: Could you please provide more information about your configuration and which version of Vault you're using? If you can provide this via the issue templates, that'd help. Thanks! | nwsparks: @heatherezell thanks, it's a feature request not a question. this issue is present in all versions of the cli. with the vault CLI you can store the password in the environment via `VAULT_LDAP_PASSWORD` which `vault login -method=ldap` will read from. however attempting to use the vault agent via the cli, `vault agent -config ~/.vault-agent.hcl` it does not respect that environment variable and requires you to store the password in a file.

title: PKI sign not_after can exceed max_ttl
body_text:
**Description**

The `sign/pki/{role}` endpoint signs certificates that exceed the role's `max_ttl`. 

**To Reproduce**

1. Setup a PKI with CA cert with `not_after` in far future
2. Create role with `max_ttl` set
```
vault write pki/roles/tmp \
    key_bits=384 key_type=ec key_usage=DigitalSignature
    max_ttl=60d ttl=60d
```
 3. Request sign a CSR with `not_after` parameter:
```
vault write pki/sign/tmp csr=@example.pem common_name=example.com not_after=2040-01-01T10:10:10Z
```

**Expected behavior**
The issued certificate has `not_after = now() + 60d` and warning like *not_after is after the date permitted by maxTTL XXX, so maximum possible not_after ZZZ is being used*.

This warning will be issued if TTL is supplied explicitely, e.g.:
```
vault write pki/sign/tmp csr=@example.pem common_name=example.com ttl=90d
```

It seems that the check in the code is simply not present for the `not_after` branch in `builtin/logical/pki/issuing/issue_common.go` L990.

If this is somehow expected behavior, I think it needs to be documented what function does `max_ttl` on the role serve. I would expect it is there to restrict the validity of issued certificates.

**Environment:**
Server version: `Version         1.19.0`
OS: Suse Leap 15.6 x86

title: Fix problematic error returns
body_text:
In  https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/userpass/path_user_password.go#L86, err is returned, but err has already been checked at #L77, so it must be nil at this point. 




Considering the context, it should be changed to return intErr instead.

**Describe the bug** When enabling saving of logs to file with the `log_file` option in the config file, not all of the logs seen in stdout are present in the log file. It seems that not all components are having their logs written to disk. `_stdout` ``` 2025-03-17T13:49:58.777+1300 [INFO] core: post-unseal setup complete 2025-03-17T13:49:58.777+1300 [INFO] core: vault is unsealed 2025-03-17T13:50:25.217+1300 [INFO] expiration: revoked lease: lease_id=auth/token/create/h9b988de6c1b7866c94ad25727a2ac4a7415db180ab56a9284166b23f82472fbb ==> Vault shutdown triggered 2025-03-17T13:50:29.838+1300 [INFO] core: marked as sealed 2025-03-17T13:50:29.839+1300 [INFO] core: pre-seal teardown starting ``` `vault.log` ``` 2025-03-17T13:49:58.777+1300 [INFO] core: post-unseal setup complete 2025-03-17T13:49:58.777+1300 [INFO] core: vault is unsealed 2025-03-17T13:50:29.838+1300 [INFO] core: marked as sealed 2025-03-17T13:50:29.839+1300 [INFO] core: pre-seal teardown starting ``` I'm experiencing this both in containerised cloud deployments and local test deployments. The only time this seems to behave as expected is when running an in-memory dev server (`vault server --dev --config=minimal.hcl`). I've tried various permutations on the minimal config file below, including changing `log_format` to `"json"`, changing the `log_level`, using raft storage instead, disabling mlock, and enabling TLS. I've also tried passing in the log file path via CLI flag to no effect. To be clear, I'm not expecting to see the `==> Vault shutdown triggered` line in the log file, but the lease revocation line should be there. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start and unseal a cluster with the minimal config file below 2. Make a request such as `vault token create --ttl=5s` to create a token that will have its lease revoked very shortly 3. Compare the contents of stdout to those of the file. The log line about the expired lease is missing from the file **Expected behavior** From the description in the [docs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands/server#_log_file), I would expect that everything logged to stdout should also appear in the log file. > The absolute path where Vault should save log messages in addition to other, existing outputs like journald / stdout. title: [BUG] Error fetching multiple secrets
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->


**Environment:**
## vault-action version
v2.7.3
## Server Operating System/Architecture: ubuntu-latest


## Describe the bug
Trying to fetch Multiple Secrets with vault-action@v2.7.3 (github actions) using AppRole authentication is not working
Vault server configuration file(s):

```hcl
 - name: Get Secrets
        id: secrets
        uses: hashicorp/vault-action@v2.7.3
        with:
          roleId: ${{ secrets.VAULT_ROLE_ID }}
          secretId: ${{ secrets.VAULT_SECRET_ID }}
          url: ${{ secrets.VAULT_ADDR }}
          method: approle
          secrets: |
             github/secrets/secret_name * | MYAPP_ ;
```

## Expected behavior
Multiple Secrets should be fetched at once in json format:
```
{
MYAPP_key1 : secret1,
MYAPP_key2: secret2,
MYAPP_key3: secret3
}
```

## Log Output
|Test Case|Error|
| --- | --- |
|`github/secrets/secret_name * \| MYAPP_ ;`|Unable to retrieve result for data.data."**". No match data was found. Double check your Key or Selector.|
|`github/secrets/secret_name ** \| MYAPP_ ;`|Unable to retrieve result for data.data."*". No match data was found. Double check your Key or Selector.|

## Additional context
with vault cli, the below command is giving the output that I need in github action, using -format and -field flag. Is there any way to do the same here?
```
vault kv get -format=json -field=data github/secrets/secret_name
```
```
{
  "key1": "secret1",
  "key2": "secre2",
  "key3": "secret3"
}

```
 fetching a particular secret with the key name is working fine.
```
- name: Get Secrets
  id: secrets
  uses: hashicorp/vault-action@v2.7.3
  with:
    roleId: ${{ secrets.VAULT_ROLE_ID }}
    secretId: ${{ secrets.VAULT_SECRET_ID }}
    url: ${{ secrets.VAULT_ADDR }}
    method: approle
    secrets: |
      github/secrets/secret_name key1 | KEY1;
```


Thanks in advance!

title: Endpoints reported through discovery not spec conform
body_text:
The discovery spec requires that all url properties  MUST use the https scheme.

https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderMetadata

Vault uses ...

```
{
  "issuer": "/v1/identity/oidc/provider/default",
  "jwks_uri": "/v1/identity/oidc/provider/default/.well-known/keys",
  "authorization_endpoint": "/ui/vault/identity/oidc/provider/default/authorize",
  "token_endpoint": "/v1/identity/oidc/provider/default/token",
  "userinfo_endpoint": "/v1/identity/oidc/provider/default/userinfo",
  "request_parameter_supported": false,
  "request_uri_parameter_supported": false,
  "id_token_signing_alg_values_supported": [
    "RS256",
    "RS384",
    "RS512",
    "ES256",
    "ES384",
    "ES512",
    "EdDSA"
  ],
  ...
}
```

As a consequence coreos/go-oidc cannot be used with Vault without convoluted OIDC hacks.

CrossRef: https://github.com/coreos/go-oidc/issues/454

title: cleanupInternalCRLMapping double slash path delete trips up zookeeper backend
body_text:
the delete on the storage in _cleanupInternalCRLMapping in builtin/logical/pki/issuing/config_revocation.go  passes a path with two consecutive slashes to the backend, e.g. when baseCRLPath is "unified-crls/" in the !isLocal case

                if err := s.Delete(ctx, baseCRLPath+"/"+crl); err != nil {

While probably no issue for the default backends it trips up the zookeeper one in cleanupLogicalPath

adding filepath.Clean to the splitting in cleanupLogicalPath (`nodes := strings.Split(filepath.Clean(path), "/")`) or properly joining in _cleanupInternalCRLMapping fixes the problem

title: Identity Token role with template containing nested JSON objects results in "unbalanced templating characters" error
body_text:
**Describe the bug**

Writing to an OIDC role with a template containing nested JSON objects causes an error: `unbalanced templating characters`. Vault thinks the `}}` in the template is a malformed template variable.

```

Write to an oidc role with a json template that contains `}}` a part of a nested object:

title: `pki/generate/root/existing` reorders DN fields in Issuer, breaking strict DN matching
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
When using the `pki/generate/root/existing` endpoint in Vault to create a self-signed CA certificate with an existing private key, the resulting certificate's Issuer DN may have its attribute order changed compared to the input subject DN. This isn't an issue if the issuer was originally generated by Vault. However, if the issuer was imported from an external PEM bundle, the reordered DN can cause mismatches in environments that expect an exact DN match.

This behavior breaks use cases where strict byte-level or order-preserving DN matching is required — such as replacing or chaining with an existing CA certificate that expects an exact Issuer DN match (e.g., in downstream verification systems or tooling).

Example:

Imported Subject DN:
```
C=US, O=Example Corp, OU=Certificate Authority, L=Example City, ST=Example State
```

Resulting Issuer DN in the generated certificate If we passed the same values.
```
C=US, ST=Example State, L=Example City, O=Example Corp, OU=Certificate Authority
```

Even though the DNs are semantically equivalent, the field reordering changes the encoded ASN.1 structure, which breaks certain verification flows.

**Root cause**
This appears to be due to Vault's use of Go's crypto/x509/pkix.Name type, which reorders DN fields by default during encoding.

**Expected behavior**
Vault should preserve the exact input order of DN fields when generating a certificate, or at minimum, provide an option to disable reordering and preserve field order as provided. PKI plugin should probably have likely `pki/generate/root/existing` endpoint should have `issuer_ref` parameter to re-generate a exact matched CA with same key material but different validity date.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.19.0
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): Vault v1.19.0
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Debian Bookworm

Vault server configuration file(s):

```hcl
storage "file" {
  path = "/opt/vault/data"
}

listener "tcp" {
  address     = "0.0.0.0:8200"

body_text:

-->

**Describe the bug**
The token is refreshed for authentication methods that return `ExpiresIn`, but there are cases where `ExpiresOn` is returned instead.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run vault in Azure Container Apps
2. Enable System assigned identity
3. Wait 1d for authorization token expiration

**Expected behavior**
Authorization token update

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.19.1
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): 1.19.1
* Server Operating System/Architecture: docker linux/amd64

Vault server configuration file(s):

```json
{
    "backend": {
        "azure": {
            "accountName": "...",
            "container": "...",
            "use_msi": "true"
        }
    },
    "..."
}
```

**Additional context**
[Bug location](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a698cdee5e091e7e38fac582195b8e13fcf18c9c/physical/azure/azure.go#L140)

Here’s the fix that worked for me.

```go
expIn, err := authToken.Token().ExpiresIn.Int64()
if err != nil {
	logger.Error("couldn't retrieve jwt claim for 'expiresIn' from refreshed token", "error", err)
	return 0
}
```

to

```go
func getTokenExpiryInSeconds(token *adal.ServicePrincipalToken, logger log.Logger) (int64, error) {
	expIn, err := token.Token().ExpiresIn.Int64()
	if err == nil {
		logger.Debug("token expires in", "access_token_expiry", expIn)
		return expIn, nil
	}

	expOn, err := token.Token().ExpiresOn.Int64()
	if err == nil {
		logger.Debug("token expires on", "access_token_expiry", expOn)
		return expOn - time.Now().Unix(), nil
	}

	logger.Debug("unable to retrieve token expiry information from both ExpiresIn and ExpiresOn")
	return 0, errors.New("unable to determine token expiry")
}

...

expIn, err := getTokenExpiryInSeconds(authToken, logger)
if err != nil {
	logger.Error("couldn't get token expiry", "error", err)
	return 0
}

```

title: Vault re-enables Windows disk performance counters every time it is launched
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->

**Describe the bug**

Whenever vault.exe is launched — not even in server mode, simply to print a help message — it re-enables [Windows disk performance counters](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/diskperf).

Usually, these counters are always enabled on Windows systems, but **some users may choose to keep them disabled**. And vault.exe's behavior goes against the Principle of Least Astonishment.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Make sure Windows disk perf counters are disabled: `diskperf.exe -N` (Restart is not required)
2. Open Task Manager's "Performance" tab to make sure that disk counters are gone
3. Run `vault.exe --help`
4. Open Task Manager's "Performance" tab again to see that disk counters are back again

Expected behavior:

vault.exe should not be making unexpected system-wide changes to Windows OS.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version: `Vault v1.19.2 (2ee4ea013b31a770a2fc421bb1e4bc74a9669185), built 2025-04-17T16:41:30Z`
* Vault CLI Version: same as above
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Windows Server 2022 version 21H2 (`10.0.20348.3453`), x64 CPU

title: Allow to set a custom CA when retrieving CRL on Certificate Authenticaiton method
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have a CRL distribution point as HTTPS using a certificate from an internal CA.
When adding the CRL to the authenticaiton configuration, using curl:
```
$ curl --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" --request POST https://svc1215p-vault.${DOMAIN}/v1/auth/puppet/crls/test -d '{"url":"https://svc1215p-puppet.${DOMAIN}/puppet-ca/v1/certificate_revocation_list/ca"}'
```
I get the following error message:
```
{"errors":["1 error occurred:\n\t* Get \"https://svc1215p-puppet.${DOMAIN}/puppet-ca/v1/certificate_revocation_list/ca\": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority\n\n"]}
```

As I am running the vault server in Kubernetes, adding the custom CA to the image seem to be a big too much work.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Having a way to specify the CA certificate used by the server when getting the CRL from the distribution point.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

The distribution point cannot be configured as plain HTTP.

I analyzed the code to search for a way to configure Vault to use the CA but when I found the call chain:

https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/cert/path_crls.go#L279
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/credential/cert/backend.go#L157

I realized that there was no way to configure the CA for that specific call. So the only way left would be to change the system anchors. Sadly I am in Kubernetes, so changing the CA anchors would be a lot of work.


**Explain any additional use-cases**

This would allow users of the certificate authentication method to change their Root-CA without having to make changes to the infrastructure.

**Additional context**

The CA is Puppet-CA and we want to use the certificates generated by Puppet for securing the configuration, to make the puppet-agents access directly the secrets without going through the server. Managing the CRL is critical since Puppet does not support OCSP, and thus CRLs become the only way to tell if a certificate was revoked.

The two are completely different use-cases and codepaths. At no point in my use-case Vault is an issuer for a CA or needs to get a leaf certificate from a remote CA. Vault needs to open an HTTPS connection to a remote server to make an HTTP GET request for a CRL file served by a remote CA used to authenticate clients using the TLS Certificate Authentication method. This is the related documentation that I found: - https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/cert - https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/cert#create-crl There doesn't seem to be any related tutorials, or any other documentation, which is why I went and read the code of Vault and found out that there doesn't seem to be any way to set the CA except modifying the CA trust bundle of the OS (which is hard in Kubernetes when following the best practices of security: read-only root filesystem, no root user, etc). My workaround is to serve the CRL using HTTP by using a weird reverse-proxy setup. I have in my kubernetes cluster an Ingress that will serve as HTTP a remote URL in HTTPS and point Vault TLS Certificate Authentication method to download the CRL using the local HTTP URL instead of the remote HTTPS one. title: Limit PKI role to allow hostnames without domain part (shortname) as SAN
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
For a self signing PKI, I need to create a role to allow hostnames *only* as SAN while limiting to certain domains.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A certificate should be created with the following limitations:

Subject: CN = host.foobar.com
X509v3 extensions:
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
DNS: host.foobar.com,
DNS: host

A parameter to allow hostnames *only* as SAN (alt_names)

Automated certificate generation via ansible should be possible like so:

    - name: 'Request internal cert, key and signing CA cert from PKI'
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: "{{ hashicorp_vault_url }}"
        method: POST
        headers:
          X-Vault-Token: "{{ hashicorp_vault_token }}"
        body_format: json
        body:
          common_name: "{{ host.name }}.{{ host.domain}}"
          alt_names: "{{ host.name }}"
          ttl: "50d"

Where {{ host.name }} would be host and {{ host.name }}.{{ host.domain}} would be host.foobar.com in the above example.

Role limits should be 
allowed_domain: foobar.com
allow_subdomains: true
enforce_hostnames: true

All else should be denied.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Allow "any names" which would leave the PKI open to create anything outside our internal use case and is considered a risk.

title: [Feature Request] Allow Conditional Forwarding in Plugin Read Operations (ErrReadOnly without global forwarding flag)
body_text:
# [Feature Request] Vault plugins should be able to trigger conditional forwarding to leader from inside plugin logic

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

We are developing a custom secret engine plugin with a `ReadOperation` that conditionally performs credential rotation **only if expired**. Normally, it's a lightweight read; rotation happens maybe 1% of the time. The challenge arises in Vault HA mode.

Currently:
- Standby nodes silently **redirect or forward all requests** to the leader node, even if the plugin path is **read-only** and does **not** have `ForwardPerformanceSecondary` set.
- Even when forwarding is disabled (`X-Vault-No-Request-Forwarding: true`) and **inconsistent reads are explicitly allowed** (`X-Vault-Inconsistent: allow-standby`), Vault **still returns 307 redirects**.
- **The plugin handler is never invoked on the standby node**, even if no storage is accessed and the token was created after the node joined.

This prevents plugin authors from dynamically deciding whether a request actually needs to be forwarded based on runtime logic like:

```go
if credsExpired {
  return logical.ErrReadOnly // But Vault ignores this if the path wasn't marked forwardable
}
```

The Vault core decides to forward or redirect *before* the plugin is ever called, making it impossible to handle conditional mutations cleanly without sacrificing HA scalability.

---

### Describe the solution you'd like

We’d like a way for plugins to:

- Be **invoked normally** on standby/performance secondary nodes
- Inspect request details, and return something like `logical.ErrReadOnly` to **trigger forwarding**
- Without requiring the operation to be globally marked with `ForwardPerformanceSecondary: true`

**Two possible solutions:**
1. Allow `logical.ErrReadOnly` to trigger forwarding even without the flag, as long as Vault is in HA mode and the plugin opted in.
2. Introduce a method like `b.MaybeForwardToLeader(req)` or a plugin callback that lets the plugin signal forwarding dynamically based on logic like expiration.

This would preserve read scalability while still allowing safety when writes are needed.

---

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- **Setting `ForwardPerformanceSecondary: true`**: Causes all reads to be forwarded, even non-mutating ones. This overloads the leader and negates HA performance.
- **Splitting the plugin into `/read` and `/rotate` paths**: Viable, but requires client changes and breaks compatibility with existing APIs.
- **Wrapping `HandleRequest`**: Not officially supported, brittle, and bypasses Vault's internal routing and validation logic.

---

### Explain any additional use-cases

- Dynamic credentials that expire and require regeneration inside read paths
- Usage metering or TTL tracking based on token usage
- Lightweight refresh logic triggered during reads, which only occasionally mutates state
- General plugin optimization in high-traffic environments (100,000s of reads)

---

Thank you!

title: Make user_id optional in certificate requests
body_text:
I need to sign a CSR with a subject that includes a (empty) UID field. I have no control over the application which creates those CSR with the UID field.
However Vaults _/pki/sign/:rolename_ endpoint rejects the CSR with the error message "user_id is not allowed by this role". This happens regardless whether use_csr_common_name or use_csr_sans are set to true or false.

allowed_user_ids for the role is empty, as I do not want the issued certificates to contain any user_id.

It would be great if there was an option similar to _serial_number_source_, where you could control whether the UID from a CSR should be ignored.

title: UI permissions errors for Tokens generated in Chroot Namespace
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->

**Describe the bug**
if you have a chroot namespace set up like this:
```hcl
listener "tcp" {
  address = "127.0.0.1:8200"
  chroot_namespace = "prod"
}
```
tokens generated in that namespace will be unable to use the UI due to permisisons errors.
assuming the chroot namespace is `prod`, the UI thinks the token belongs to `prod/prod` instead of `prod` (which the UI should see as root ns)
This issue is present for OIDC tokens, 
but it's also present for userpass tokens, but only if you log in, copy the token, and then use the token to log in
I havent tried other types of tokens.


1. log in
2. UI makes get request to `auth/token/lookup-self`, with no namespace header. the response contains field `data.namespace_path` = `prod`
3. `localstorage->vault-token☃1` has field `userRootNamespace` = `prod`
4. all future requests use `localstorage->vault-token☃1.userRootNamespace` to add header `X-Vault-Namespace: prod` to all requests
5. because of the chroot namespace, vault server treats the requests as asking for namespace `prod/prod`, which fails
6. manually setting `localstorage->vault-token☃1.userRootNamespace` to empty makes vault behave correctly, requests are successful (because UI now tries to access root namespace, which vault transforms into `prod`)





**Expected behavior**
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

**Environment:**

* Vault Server Version: `1.19.3+ent`
* Server Operating System/Architecture: docker on ARM, kernel 6.13.6-200.fc41.aarch64

Vault server configuration file(s):

```hcl
storage "raft" {
  path    = "/data"
  node_id = "node1"
}
listener "tcp" {
  address                           = "0.0.0.0:8200" # vault_root.REMOVED
  tls_disable                       = "true"
  x_forwarded_for_authorized_addrs  = "172.20.0.3"

}
listener "tcp" {
  address                           = "0.0.0.0:8201" # vault_dev.REMOVED
  tls_disable                       = "true"
  chroot_namespace                  = "dev"
  x_forwarded_for_authorized_addrs  = "172.20.0.3"
}

listener "tcp" {
  address                           = "0.0.0.0:8202" # vault.REMOVED
  tls_disable                       = "true"
  chroot_namespace                  = "prod"
  x_forwarded_for_authorized_addrs  = "172.20.0.3"
}


plugin_directory = "/plugins"

api_addr = "https://vault_root.DOMAIN"
cluster_addr = "https://127.0.0.1:8201"
ui = true

sentinel {
  additional_enabled_modules = ["http"]
}
```

docker-compose.yml
```yml

  vault:
    restart: always

    environment:
      - VAULT_LICENSE=REMOVED

title: Issues using label_selector in auto_join field on new v1.19.1-ent install

### Bug Description
We discovered a bug nearly identical to the auto_join issue (https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/29874) that we experienced during the upgrade process. The upgrade process was fixed, but doing a clean install of the v1.19.1 vault cluster triggers the bug.

On a clean install (see reproduction steps), I have three vault nodes running v1.19.1-ent. I run 'vault operator init' on one to initialize it. The other two nodes are getting the following error.

```yaml

title: `skip_import_rotation` and `skip_static_role_import_rotation` not persisted in Vault 1.19
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
The parameters `skip_import_rotation` and `skip_static_role_import_rotation` are silently ignored or not persisted when creating MySQL connections and static roles in Vault 1.19, despite being valid and supported as per documentation.

This behavior occurs even when using both the CLI and the HTTP API.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Enable database secrets engine
```
$ vault secrets enable database
Success! Enabled the database secrets engine at: database/
```
2. Write the DB Connection Config
```
$ vault write database/config/my-mysql-db \
  plugin_name=mysql-database-plugin \
  connection_url="{{username}}:{{password}}@tcp(mysql:3306)/sample_db" \
  allowed_roles="my-static-role" \
  username="**********" \
  password="**********" \
  skip_static_role_import_rotation=true
Success! Data written to: database/config/my-mysql-db
```
3. Read the DB Connection Config
```
$ vault read database/config/my-mysql-db

---                                   -----

4. Create static role

  password=********** \
  rotation_period=24h \

Success! Data written to: database/static-roles/my-static-role
```
4. Read static role
```
$ vault read database/static-roles/my-static-role

5. Get static role credentials
```

**Expected behavior**
Vault should not ignore the values set for the parameters `skip_static_role_import_rotation` in the DB connection config and `skip_import_rotation` in the static role creation. Since `skip_static_role_import_rotation` and `skip_import_rotation` were explicitly set to `true`, the returned password should be the initial one, not a newly rotated one. When reading the DB config or static role, vault should return the values that were explicitly set.

title: FTR: allow snapshot restore without initializing the cluster first
body_text:
### **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When restoring a raft snapshot as per the SOP <https://docs.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/standard-procedures/sop-restore> to a cluster, it has to be initialized and unsealed first. However, as stated in the SOP and in <https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/performing-restore-from-snapshot-invalidates-existing-auto-unseal-recovery-keys/55326> , all content of that cluster (especially unseal/recovery keys) is removed/overwritten with the backup content.

Thus the requirement to have an initialized+unseald cluster introduces a new set of secrets and operation procedure to deal with them (and mental capacity to separate them from the actually needed stuff), without actually needing these.

### **Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow restoring into an empty cluster, which has not been initialized, and implicitly don't require unsealing in that case.

`vault status` tells me "Initialized: false", so the cluster knows if it has any content, and can distinguish that case from an initialized (possibly filled with content) but sealed cluster.

title: Allow Enabling Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) for DynamoDB Storage Backend
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When Vault automatically creates a [DynamoDB backend](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/storage/dynamodb), there's currently no way to enable [Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)](https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/pitr/). This is a critical data protection feature that many production environments require, especially for secure storage like HashiCorp Vault. Currently, users must either manually create the table with PITR enabled beforehand or modify the table after Vault creates it, adding complexity to deployment automation and potentially leaving data unprotected during the initial setup period.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a configuration option to the DynamoDB storage backend to enable PITR when Vault creates the table. This could be implemented as a simple boolean parameter in the storage configuration, such as:

```
hclstorage "dynamodb" {
  table = "vault-data"
  region = "us-west-2"
  recovery_enabled = true
  recovery_period_days = 35  # Optional, defaulting to 35
}
```

The dynamodb.go file in the physical/dynamodb directory would need to be modified to include the Point-in-Time Recovery specification in the `CreateTableInput` when the table is created during the `ensureTableExists` function.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Pre-creating the DynamoDB table with PITR enabled before deploying Vault
- Using AWS Lambda or other automation to modify the table after Vault creates it
- Using a different storage backend that supports native backup/restore
- Implementing an external scheduled backup solution

All of these alternatives add complexity to the deployment process and require additional resources or manual steps that could be avoided with native PITR support.

**Explain any additional use-cases**
- Disaster recovery - PITR provides the ability to restore the Vault database to any point in time within the recovery window, crucial for recovering from data corruption or accidental deletions.
- Compliance requirements - Many regulatory frameworks require point-in-time recovery capabilities for sensitive data storage.
- Audit capabilities - Being able to recover to specific points in time can help with security audits and investigations.

**Additional context**
Enabling DynamoDB PITR for Vault's storage would provide important benefits beyond Vault's existing disaster recovery mechanisms:
- It allows recovery from storage-level corruption or accidental data deletion, which Vault's built-in DR might not address
- PITR operates at the AWS infrastructure level, separate from Vault's application-level backup systems, providing defense-in-depth
- It's a zero-performance-impact backup solution that's completely managed by AWS

The implementation would be straightforward from a technical perspective - the AWS SDK for Go only requires adding a PointInTimeRecoverySpecification struct to the CreateTableInput when creating the DynamoDB table in the ensureTableExists function. This would be a minimal code change with significant security benefits for production deployments.

title: Vault issues expired certificates with leaf_not_after_behavior truncate
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
Vault issues expired certificates when the **leaf_not_after_behavior** is set to **truncate** and the **default issuer** in a **pki** has expired.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Setup a vault pki with a given default issuer
2. Let the default Issuer expire
3. Request a certificate from the default issuer

This bug can be easily replicated with the following setup:

`id=$(kubectl exec vault-0 -i -- vault list -format json pki/issuers | jq -r '.[0]')
kubectl exec vault-0 -i -- vault write pki/issuer/$id leaf_not_after_behavior=truncate`

With the err behavior, Vault errors because the cert's NotAfter goes beyond the issuer's. This prevents Vault from issuing when the CA has expired.

With truncate, Vault copies the NotAfter e.g.:

`min(cert's NotAfter, CA's NotAfter)`

Which leads to Vault issuing expired certificates.

**Expected behavior**
Vault should not issue expired certificates with the truncate leaf_not_after_behavior.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version: 1.17.2
* Vault CLI Version: 1.17.2
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Kubernetes

**Additional context**
This issue lead to a problem with cert-manager for us: https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/7741
But the original root cause seems to be in vault.

**Describe the bug**

The dependencies provided by `go version -m vault` indicate the wrong vault dependency version.

This causes tools, such as Trivy, to be unable to determine what version of Vault this binary is. SBOMs are generated with incorrect information, security scanners report false positives, and other such problems result from this issue.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

2. Extract `vault` from the zip file
3. Run: `go version -m vault`

title: openapi: Post request body does not show the request schema in custom plugins
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->

**Describe the bug**
If a custom plugin is added to Vault, OpenAPI Explorer does not show properly the Request body for the plugin's POST endpoints. It shows a `"string"` instead of filling out the parameters based on the path fields.

This is due to [github.com/mitchellh/mapstructure](https://github.com/mitchellh/mapstructure). When it goes through the OpenAPI map (as the specification is retrieved through a map), it tries to match the map key with a struct field with a simple case-insensitive match, `Ref` does not match with `$ref`, and the values are ignored.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Add a custom Vault plugin to Vault (such as [vault-auth-plugin-example](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-auth-plugin-example))
2. Log in to Vault and open API Explorer
3. Check a `POST` endpoint of the custom plugin
4. Request body shows "string" instead of a Schema.

**Expected behavior**
Request body shows a schema.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.19.4
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.19.4
* Server Operating System/Architecture: macOS 15.5 (24F74)

Vault server configuration file(s):

```hcl
plugin_directory = "<vault folder>/plugins"
```

title: Vault Agent supporting token helper similar to token file auto auth
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, Vault Agent's auto-auth methods do not support using Vault's token helper functionality to retrieve tokens. This limits integration with custom or external token storage mechanisms that are already supported by the Vault CLI via token helpers. Users who rely on token helpers for managing tokens (e.g., storing tokens in a secure location or using a custom retrieval mechanism) cannot leverage this in Vault Agent auto-auth workflows.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Introduce a new auto-auth method for Vault Agent that uses Vault's token helper functionality to retrieve a Vault token, similar to the existing token file method. This method would:
- Invoke the configured token helper to fetch the Vault token directly.
- Not attempt to auto-renew the token; it simply retrieves the token as provided by the token helper.
- Require configuration values for the Vault address and Vault namespace to ensure the correct context is used when invoking the token helper.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Using the existing token file auto-auth method, but this does not support the flexibility and security of token helpers (e.g., encrypted storage, hardware-backed helpers, etc.).
- Manually scripting token retrieval and writing to a file, but this is error-prone and less secure than using the built-in token helper interface.

**Explain any additional use-cases**
- We want to use vault agent on end user laptops to elimiate usage of secrets on disk in .env files

**Additional context**
- The new auto-auth method should closely mirror the behavior of the token file method, but use the token helper interface for token retrieval.
- This would improve consistency between Vault CLI and Vault Agent, and enable more flexible and secure token management strategies.
- Reference: [Vault Token Helper Documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands/token-helper)

title: Extend UsernameMetadata to Allow Custom Metadata for Auditing Use Cases
body_text:
**Use Case**:

We have a requirement from our auditing team to prove which developer accessed a production database and why. Developers authenticate via ADFS into Vault, which generates a temporary database username and password. Database logging is enabled, and we rely on the username for traceability.

The current setup works well, but we would like to allow developers to include a *ticket reference* (e.g., from JIRA, TOPdesk, or GitHub) when requesting credentials. This reference would be added to the generated username (within reasonable length constraints), so it can later be parsed and correlated with approved change requests.

This would provide a clear and auditable link between:

* The person who made a change,
* The exact change,
* And the business approval for it.

**Proposal**:

Extend `UsernameMetadata` and/or the relevant API to allow passing in additional metadata (such as a `TicketID` or other key-value fields). These would then be made available to the username template engine.

**Example**:

```go
type UsernameMetadata struct {
	DisplayName string
	RoleName    string
	Extra       map[string]string // e.g. {"ticket": "JIRA-1234"}
}
```

**Next Steps**:

I'm willing to contribute this feature and plan to begin development soon. However, if there are any existing plans, design considerations, or alternative approaches I should be aware of, please let me know as soon as possible to avoid duplication or misalignment.

Looking forward to your feedback.

title: Alicloud KMS Seal Does Not Refresh STS Credentials from ECS Metadata
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->

**Describe the bug**
We are using auto unseal with Alicloud KMS. 
We use RAM Role attached to the ECS that grants access to the KMS key on Alibaba
We do not want to use static accesskey/secretkey
Vault seal configuration:

```
seal "alicloudkms" {
  region     = "cn-xxx"
  domain     = "kms-vpc.cn-xxx.aliyuncs.com"
  kms_key_id = "xxx-xxx"
}
```
Vault starts up correctly and can use the KMS seal initially.
However, after ~6 hours, the STS credentials expire, and Vault does not refresh them. 
We start seeing this error in logs:

```
[WARN] core.autoseal: seal wrapper health check failed: seal_name=alicloudkms
err=failed to encrypt test value, seal wrapper may be unreachable: error encrypting data: SDK.ServerError
ErrorCode: InvalidAccessKeyId.NotFound
Message: The Access Key ID provided does not exist in our records.
```

The ECS metadata service still returns valid credentials with a new expiration (curl http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/role_name).

Vault does not re-read or refresh those credentials after startup.

If we restart Vault, it will unseal automatically but we got the errors after 6h again

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy Vault on ECS with a RAM Role that can access KMS.
2. Configure alicloudkms seal without static credentials.
seal "alicloudkms" {
  region     = "cn-xxx"
  domain     = "kms-vpc.cn-xxx.aliyuncs.com"
  kms_key_id = "xxx-xxx"
}
3. Start Vault – everything works.
4. wait for 6h (STS expiration)
5. Observe errors like InvalidAccessKeyId.NotFound in the logs.

**Expected behavior**
Vault should re-fetch STS credentials from the ECS metadata service when the current token expires.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): v1.17
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Linux Redhat8

title: agent: Support `once` in template config
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
`vault-agent` will unexpectedly refresh secrets and rerender template more frequently than configured.
This can causes issues resulting in loss of service availability in various scenarios. For example, unexpected rerendering and reissuing of a Nomad agents Consul ACL token will result in the agent losing connection with Consul ([documented](https://developer.hashicorp.com/nomad/docs/configuration/consul#token)).

Related:
- #29507
- #25904
- #11030
- #20006

**Describe the solution you'd like**
`consul-template` supports the [`once`](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul-template/blob/main/docs/configuration.md#once-mode) mode, which effectively treats any otherwise dynamic secrets in a template as static.

This seems like an applicable solution for some situation.


**Additional context**
- #31065 could be an alternative solution for some scenarios. The benefit of #31065 is template rendering can be decoupled from the vault agent process lifecycle.

title: failed to persist packed storage entry
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->

**Describe the bug**
Seeming randomly all k8s auth attempts started failing with the error `{"errors":["failed to persist packed storage entry: put failed due to value being too large, max value size for key logical/a26fa07c-1ec6-d453-8051-29622713f275/packer/buckets/49 is 1048576, got 1048669"]}`. The bucket was not consistent (seems like it was most or all of them), and the size varied by a few bytes, but otherwise it was the same message. Nothing should have changed as far as I know so this seemingly started happening out of nowhere. I suspect _something_ changed in the k8s auth identity itself and that's what triggered it. The only way to resolve it and unbreak the cluster was to bump `max_entry_size` in the raft storage config.

I traced the error to [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/7f64b68ec8eecb1935e2ca02950fb38d37e44c5b/physical/raft/raft.go#L2016) in raft and [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/7f64b68ec8eecb1935e2ca02950fb38d37e44c5b/helper/storagepacker/storagepacker.go#L266) in storagepacker. My suspicion is that [PutItem is calling upsert](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/7f64b68ec8eecb1935e2ca02950fb38d37e44c5b/helper/storagepacker/storagepacker.go#L354-L357) which blindly [overwrites the item](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/7f64b68ec8eecb1935e2ca02950fb38d37e44c5b/helper/storagepacker/storagepacker.go#L110) and ultimately results in this error.

**To Reproduce**
I'm honestly not sure why this happened. The change seems to have come out of nowhere.

**Expected behavior**
If the item's size has increased and it is beyond the capacity of the bucket then the item should be moved to a new bucket.

**Environment:**
* Vault Server Version (retrieve with `vault status`): 1.19.1
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): N/A
* Server Operating System/Architecture: Ubuntu 24.04 / arm64/Gravaton

Vault server configuration file(s):

```hcl
ui = true

listener "tcp" {
  address = "0.0.0.0:8443"

  tls_cert_file = "/opt/vault/tls/tls.crt"
  tls_key_file  = "/opt/vault/tls/tls.key"
}

listener "tcp" {
  address     = "0.0.0.0:8080"
  tls_disable = "true"

  http_read_timeout = "30m"
}

seal "awskms" {
  region     = "redacted"
  kms_key_id = "redacted"
}

storage "raft" {
  path = "/data/vault"
  retry_join = {
    auto_join        = "provider=aws tag_key=ClusterName tag_value=vault"
    auto_join_scheme = "http"
    auto_join_port   = 8080
  }
}

telemetry {
  dogstatsd_addr = "127.0.0.1:8125"
}

max_lease_ttl = "8765h"
api_addr      = "https://redacted.com"
cluster_addr  = "https://w.x.y.z:8444"
```

**Additional context**
This seems like the same issue as https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/23793, but that bug is nearly two years old and related to DynamoDB.

title: Allow Vault to directly integrate with kubeconfig / kubectl for dynamic token generation
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'd like to use Vault to generate Kubernetes tokens in a dynamic and fully integrated way, the same way [AWS describes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/create-kubeconfig.html) it.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The AWS mechanism internally uses the AWS CLI to dynamically generate a kubernetes token (see [update-kubeconfig](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/eks/update-kubeconfig.html)). To achieve this, the `kubeconfig` will contain an `exec` definition inside the `user` section where the `aws-cli` gets called.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This can be solved in different ways:
* The Vault CLI could provide a mode, where it will return a `ExecCredentials`, so it could be called be directly like the `aws` example.
* The token returned from Vault must be converted into the expected `ExecCredentials` format by an external script.

**Additional context**
If you have the AWS account credentials exposed via the defined mechanisms like environment variables (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KE`), and provide a `kubeconfig` file like the following, the token generation is done as a encapsulated from within the `kubectl` context. Therefore such mechanism is quiet user friendly.

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
preferences: {}
clusters:
- cluster:
    certificate-authority-data: ***
    server: https://***.eks.amazonaws.com
  name: cluster
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: cluster
    user: user
  name: context
current-context: context
users:
- name: user
  user:
    exec:
      apiVersion: client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1
      command: aws
      args:
      - --region
      - < AWS_REGION >
      - eks
      - get-token
      - --cluster-name
      - < my_cluster >
      - --output
      - json
```

Internally the mechanism used here is based on the `exec` or [ExecConfig](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/config-api/kubeconfig.v1/#ExecConfig) where the AWS-CLI returns the data as an [ExecCredentials](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/config-api/client-authentication.v1beta1/) format, including either a `token` or `certificate`.

```json
{
  "apiVersion": "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1",
  "status": {
    "token": "***"
  }
}
```

title: Feature Request: Support appending components to User-Agent via environment variable (ex: VAULT_APPEND_USER_AGENT)
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It can be useful to append additional context/information to the `User-Agent` header to more quickly track down the source of HTTP requests. For example, you can embed the Kubernetes pod namespace/name, or if the request originates from CI/CD the commit SHA and/or Pull Request URL.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Many tools support this pattern via a `_APPEND_USER_AGENT` environment variable, for example most Terraform providers support this via `TF_APPEND_USER_AGENT`. It would be great if vault could do the same, appending additional components to the default `User-Agent` when `VAULT_APPEND_USER_AGENT` is set/present.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This can be accomplished today via the `VAULT_HEADERS` environment variable which was added in #16663, ex:
```
VAULT_HEADERS='{"User-Agent": "hello-world"}' vault kv get foo/bar
``` 
However, this will _replace_ the default `User-Agent` which (after #31063 is fixed) can still contain useful information such as the Vault version. It would better to support an explicit _append_ operation, `User-Agent` already has special handling in other places (ex: auditing) in vault.

**Additional context**
Related issues: #31063 and #16663

title: agent: allow write-once templates
body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Sometimes we want secrets backed by a dynamic engine to still have a very long lease and be manually rotated. For example, consul tokens for nomad, or certain applications of PKI. Currently it does not seem possible to prevent the agent from reissuing and overwriting prematurely. 


**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a new configuration field (e.g.) `overwrite` (default: true) to `template` config. If set to false, the agent will not be leasing secrets or writing to the file if it already exists.

This means that after the initial rendering, updates to templates with `overwrite=false` becomes decoupled from the vault agent process lifecycle which becomes a lot more robust and predictable. While it does mean custom automation or manual intervention becomes required to actually rerender those files, sometimes that is precisely what we want or a good tradeoff.

**Explain any additional use-cases**
Could also be potentially useful for making reliable workarounds for issues such as these more straightforward for operators
- #29507
- #25904
- #11030
- #20006

**Additional context**
- This has some overlap with #30802

title: Vault UI Allows Database Static Role and Dynamic Role Overwrite Without Warning — Expected Behavior or Improvement Area?

Hi Team,

I noticed something while working with Vault's Database Secrets Engine and wanted to check if this is expected or worth flagging as an improvement:

When I create a static role and dynamic role under the Database Secrets Engine with a name that already exists, the Vault UI lets me save it without showing any error or warning. It basically overwrites the existing role silently — same as running vault write from the CLI.

In comparison, when creating folders in KV, Vault UI shows an error if I try to use a name that's already taken, which avoids confusion. But for static roles in the DB engine, there's no similar check or prompt.

Ideally, the UI should either block duplicate role names during creation or at least warn the user that saving will overwrite the existing role.

Keeps it consistent with how the KV secret engine handles duplicate folder names.

Helps prevent accidental config overwrites, especially when multiple admins are using the UI.

Makes it clear to the user what's happening, rather than silently replacing the role definition.

**Tested on:**

Vault OSS 1.19.0

Using Postgres with the Database Secrets Engine

Can you confirm if this silent overwrite via UI is intended? And is there any plan to introduce some kind of duplicate name check or warning for static roles in the future?

title: Vault documentation and code encourage passing unseal keys on the command line
body_text:
**Describe the bug**

A variety of places in the Vault documentation and code encourage operators to pass unseal keys on the command line, or don't appropriately discourage them.

Passing unseal keys on the command line is vulnerable not only to being stored in shell history, it's also visible to anybody on the same machine. i can pretty consistently see an unseal key passed on the command line with a command like:
```
$ vault operator unseal aeouaeouaoeu & ps -ocmd | grep [v]ault
[1] 1846022
vault operator unseal aeouaeouaoeu
```

Obviously winning this race is harder if `vault` and `ps` aren't being spawned from the same shell, but I expect that malware could easily continuously monitor commands on the machine to extract the key.

Locations that encourage passing unseal keys on the command line:
* Most prominently, `vault operator unseal` rejects passing unseal keys on stdin. According to `echo | vault operator unseal`, "You should run the unseal command from a terminal for maximum security. If this is not an option, the unseal key can be provided as the first argument to the unseal command. The raw error was:  file descriptor 0 is not a terminal". I am not aware of a realistic Linux security model in which passing a secret on stdin is less secure than passing it on the command line, so I'm unclear why `vault operator unseal` *blocks* the former and allows the latter.
* The [sealing best practices](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/configuration/seal/seal-best-practices#operator-overhead) suggest storing unseal keys in encrypted form, but there's no real guidance on how to decrypt unseal keys and feed them into Vault, and doing it safely is surprisingly tough -- the most natural approach, `gpg --decrypt unseal.gpg | vault operator unseal` won't work, and the (probably) next most obvious approach (`vault operator unseal $(gpg --decrypt unseal.gpg)`) can leak keys.
* The [operator unseal](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands/operator/unseal) docs calls out that a command like `vault operator unseal aoeuoaeu` will leave the key in the shell history, but `vault operator unseal $(gpg --decrypt unseal.gpg)` wouldn't be vulnerable to that so people reading the docs might think that's safe. The docs should also call out that the argument is visible to anybody else on the machine in appropriately-timed `ps` output, even if the key isn't literally typed on the command line.
* There's a tutorial to [Use PGP encrypted key shares](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/tutorials/archive/pgp-encrypted-key-shares#unseal-vault-with-encrypted-key-shares) (that concept seems great -- that seems like the right way for people who aren't doing auto-sealing to manage keys), but the tutorial simply says to unseal using `vault operator unseal $(gpg --decrypt /root/.gnupg/alice_unseal_key.dat)` -- there's no caveat about the confidentiality issues with that. There's also a version for "API call using cURL", which similarly appears to leak the key.

**To Reproduce**

i can pretty consistently see an unseal key passed on the command line with a command like:
```
$ vault operator unseal aeouaeouaoeu & ps -ocmd | grep [v]ault
[1] 1846022
vault operator unseal aeouaeouaoeu
```

**Expected behavior**

These four pieces of documentation (and potentially others) should provide or link to secure ways to unseal Vault. Given the current `vault operator unseal`, this probably looks like [a curl command using that assembles the right JSON](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/8416#issuecomment-981244340).

However, in my opinion, `gpg --decrypt unseal.gpg | vault operator unseal` should work. As previously described, I can't think of a reason that's less secure than `vault operator unseal foo`, which *is* supported. While I have some sympathy to an attitude of ["If the vault CLI exposes every possible way to interact with the underlying API it'll be a bad case of second system syndrome."](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/8416#issuecomment-592187362), extending a command that already accepts interactive entry of a key to also accept the key on stdin hardly seems excessive. Part of the argument against changing `vault operator unseal` was that there are other approaches available, but [one approach](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/8416#issuecomment-590671685) in the thread accidentally leaks keys as well and [the other I saw](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/issues/8416#issuecomment-981244340) is convoluted to actually implement. For one of the most sensitive secrets in a secret-management tool, I think there should be a *straightforward*, intuitive way to enter it automatically that doesn't risk minor tweaks leaking the key, and I don't think we have that right now. 

(Honestly, the fact that the recommended unseal approach is to type a key in interactively is wild to me. Echo is disabled on *entry*, but most people presumably don't memorize their unseal keys. That suggests that people are e.g. GPG-encrypting the unseal keys, and then presumably decrypting it to the screen and copy/pasting the keys back in, so I would guess most unseal keys show up on screen anyway. It's possible people are using a copy button in a password manager or something like `gpg --decrypt unseal.gpg | xclip`, but I'd guess that's less common -- and all of these mean the keys are on the clipboard, for any apps that monitor *that*. Something like `gpg --decrypt unseal.gpg | vault operator unseal` would mean the unseal keys are decrypted for a matter of milliseconds, never appearing on screen, disk, or clipboard.)

title: URGENT: 1.20.0 breaking changes must be clearly mentioned at the TOP of release logs
body_text:
As part of our security posture, we regularly update our production dependencies. This includes Vault. However, todays updates broke all our production sites for 12 minutes because of a BIG breaking change listed way down in the release notes, namely:

```
server: disable_mlock configuration option is now required for integrated storage and no longer has a default. If you are using the default value with integrated storage, you must now explicitly set disable_mlock to true or false or Vault server will fail to start. [https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/pull/29974]
```

About 2 minutes after the updates applied, we started getting alerts and other indications that Vault had not booted back up, including uptime monitors screaming. But the logs from Vault didn't mention anything as to why, it just wouldn't boot.

So we checked the most recent Vault release notes, but there was no clearly labeled major breakage changed noted mentioned between 1.19.0 and 1.20.0. This delayed a quick resolution. Eventually we found the breakage note (buried 1/2 way down the release notes), made the needed config change, and Vault came back online, followed shortly by our production servers.

A breaking change like this absolutely must be at the top of the release notes, clearly highlighted! I would also argue that such a breaking change should be reserved for a major release i.e. v2.0.0, not a minor release.

Vault UI shows "Renew token" button and warning even when renew-self is denied

should not show the Renew token button, or

title: Transient failures in `loadTrustedCerts` can wind up poisoning the cache
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->

**Describe the bug**
Transient failures can result in `loadTrustedCerts` caching only a partial set of certificates in the cache used for authentication.

Specifically, if the backend encounters a transient error in [the `Cert` constructor](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/740107f47e6cef72879dcf6ae3c94ebbf74536e3/builtin/credential/cert/path_login.go#L706) then the error is dropped on the floor and the loop continues. Any certificate that was successfully loaded gets put into the cache, and any certificate that failed to load for any reason is excluded.

We specifically had a case where a request timed out while the cache was being filled. Our Vault instance saw a spike of traffic after a restart and was consequently throttled. As a result of that, the request timed out while it was loading certificates, and the `Cert` constructor failed because the context was canceled. Despite the canceled context, the partial list of certificates was installed in the cache. From that point on, the clients could never successfully authenticate with the process.

I don't have a turnkey reproduction of this problem yet.

**Expected behavior**
I would expect that the process doesn't wind up with a poisoned cache, and eventually self-corrects.

title: docs: `sign-intermediate`'s behavior with notAfter beyond the signer's expiry doesn't match the docs
body_text:
**Describe the bug**

According to `sign-intermediate`'s [`ttl`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#ttl-2), "this can be after the expiration of the signing CA". However, even when [`leaf_not_after_behavior`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#leaf_not_after_behavior) is set to `permit`, a `notAfter` beyond the expiry of the signer will get truncated. While I suppose technically a too-long TTL *can* indeed be given, I don't think anybody reading that description would expect truncation.

Also, according to the [`sign-intermediate`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#sign-intermediate) docs, that endpoint does not accept the `enforce_leaf_not_after_behavior` option (per docs, only `sign-verbatim` does). However, in practice and based on [code examination](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/main/builtin/logical/pki/path_root.go#L396C38-L396C69), that option does seem to be accepted (and setting it to true and the [`leaf_not_after_behavior`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/v1.16.x/secret/pki#leaf_not_after_behavior) to `permit` seems to be the only way to get what appears to have been the 1.16 default behavior of allowing certs extending past the CA's validity -- neither option on their own seems to do it, which I find weird).

It's possible this is a code bug rather than a doc bug -- certainly I find `enforce_leaf_not_after_behavior` to be a bit odd, and also really wish I could make a single request with a "yes, I mean it, just sign this" flag -- but it looks like a deliberate choice where people just forgot to update the docs.

title: docs: create/update role allows days as a time suffix
body_text:
**Describe the bug**
According to https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#create-update-role, 

> [ttl](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#ttl-5) (string: "") - Specifies the Time To Live value to be used for the validity period of the requested certificate, provided as a string duration with time suffix. Hour is the largest suffix. The value specified is strictly used for future validity. If not set, uses the system default value or the value of max_ttl, whichever is shorter. See not_after as an alternative for setting an absolute end date (rather than a relative one).
> [max_ttl](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#max_ttl) (string: "") - Specifies the maximum Time To Live provided as a string duration with time suffix. Hour is the largest suffix. If not set, defaults to the system maximum lease TTL.

However, empirically `d` (days) seems to work (which is convenient, because cert lifetimes on the order of 90 days are pretty common).

**Expected behavior**

As with e.g. [`not_before_duration`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/pki#not_before_duration), say this accepts durations and link to https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/duration-format

Hi HashiCorp Support,

We’re experiencing an issue with our Vault setup that we hope you can help clarify.

**Problem Summary:**
We’re using the Vault Transit secrets engine alongside the KV v2 engine. When IP whitelisting is not enabled, both the KV and Transit APIs work correctly. However, once IP whitelisting is applied, the KV API still works, but all calls to the Transit encryption and decryption APIs start returning 403 permission denied, even though the Vault policies are unchanged.

**Vault Setup Details:**
Vault version: v1.15.5
Auth method: AppRole
Transit mount path: abc-platform-encryption/
Key name: apps_staging_abc_key
Vault deployment: self-hosted on VM
Sentinel: ❌ Not in use
nginx/proxies/firewall: ❌ Not in use

When IP whitelisting is not applied, the following works:
```
curl -H "X-Vault-Token: <token>" \
  https://vault.example.com/v1/abc-platform-encryption/encrypt/apps_staging_abc_key
```
And
`curl https://vault.example.com/v1/abc-platform/data/apps/staging/abc-sight/service`

**What Fails:**
Once IP whitelisting is applied (via Vault’s policy or any internal constraint — not via external firewalls), the exact same encrypt call returns:
```
{
  "errors": ["permission denied"]
}
```
The GET on the KV path continues to work from the same IP and with the same token.

**What We've Tried:**
- Verified that the token has the correct policies via vault token lookup
- Verified the encryption key exists via vault list

path "abc-platform-encryption/encrypt/*" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}
path "abc-platform-encryption/decrypt/*" {

```
- Tested with new tokens and re-authenticated with AppRole
- Not using Sentinel, firewall, nginx, or any reverse proxy
- IP whitelisting is being enforced somewhere in Vault — but we cannot determine where or why it’s path-specific

**Our Ask:**
Could you help us understand:
- Why Vault allows kv paths through IP whitelisting but blocks transit/encrypt calls?
- What Vault features or internal mechanisms could be enforcing IP restrictions per-path even when no Sentinel or firewall exists?
- How can we properly configure IP whitelisting in a way that doesn’t block the Transit engine?

title: Audit log timestamp as first field in log entry
body_text:
<!-- Please reserve GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests.

For questions, the best place to get answers is on our [discussion forum](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/c/vault), as they will get more visibility from experienced users than the issue tracker.

Please note: We take Vault's security and our users' trust very seriously. If you believe you have found a security issue in Vault, please responsibly disclose by contacting us at security@hashicorp.com. Our PGP key is available at [our security page](https://www.hashicorp.com/security/).

-->

**Describe the bug**
Audit logs have timestamp in json great!, but time field is pushed back in the record. Previously ( older vault version say 1.15.4 ) it used to be as the first field in log.

**Why it matters?**
Log forwarders slurp the audit file and forward to their servers.
1. Time stamp is generally searched within ~100 chars of each line
2. Uniqueness of each record to determine a file or record is already forwarded is generally based on first ~250 chars

In our case, we use Splunk. The Splunk UI shows that it is guessing time for each event ( not accurate ) and it is all returned as text blobs, previously it is all jsonsyntax highlighted.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

Create a audit logger device

1. Run `vault server --dev`
2. Run `VAULT_ADDR=http://localhost:8200 VAULT_TOKEN=[REDACTED_VAULT_TOKEN] vault audit enable file elide_list_responses=true file_path=stdout`
3. Audit log
```
{"auth":....,"request":....,"time":"2025-08-06T13:52:53.595695Z","type":"response"}
```

**Expected behavior**
Timestamp in audit log as first field
```
{"time":"2025-08-06T13:52:53.595695Z","auth":....,"request":....,"type":"response"}
```

**Environment:**
Vault version: v1.20.2
Previously working version: v.1.15.4 ( or above, I have not tested other above versions )

**Additional Context:**
Splunk [default timestamp processor](https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/9.4.2/Data/Tunetimestampextractionforbetterindexingperformance#Adjust_timestamp_lookahead) The default number of characters that the timestamp processor looks into an event is 128
Splunk [input.conf](https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/Admin/Inputsconf) By default, the input only performs CRC checks against the first 256 bytes of a file

I'm not convinced that Vault should update the ordering of its JSON fields just to appease a single vendor's observability tooling, especially when that tooling has knobs to turn to successfully read the timestamp field. My concerns are twofold. 1. Would such a change have a negative impact on Vault performance, specifically for high-volume Vault servers? I'm not familiar with how Vault marshals its audit logs to JSON, but ordering the fields would require some custom marshaller from what I understand. I _believe_ the default JSON marshaller in Go orders based on struct fields but I'm not sure. 2. The point of emitting valid JSON is that tooling can unmarshal that JSON and be told which field holds the timestamp. That's how popular tooling does it. I know Splunk doesn't do this but again I'm not sure changing the ordering to appease one tool is the best path forward.

title: bug: final build artifact under hashicorp/vault does not contain version metadata

**Describe the bug**
When I pull `hashicorp/vault:latest` from the published docker registry I expect the `module version` of `/bin/vault` to be populated in the go build settings. I also expect `version.VersionMetadata` to contain the correct version value.

I'm looking at the following artifact: `/bin/vault`
I see the following build settings for the binary located at `/bin/vault` for hashicorp/vault@edd642f4c72a:
```
        "goBuildSettings": [
          {
            "key": "-buildmode",
            "value": "exe"
          },

            "key": "-compiler",
            "value": "gc"
          },

            "key": "-ldflags",
            "value": " -X github.com/hashicorp/vault/version.GitCommit=824d12909d5b596ddd3f34d9c8f169b4f9701a0c -X github.com/hashicorp/vault/version.BuildDate=2025-08-05T19:05:39Z -X github.com/hashicorp/vault/version.VersionMetadata="
          },

            "value": "0"
          },
          {
            "key": "GOARCH",
            "value": "arm64"
          },
          {
            "key": "GOOS",
            "value": "linux"
          },
          {
            "key": "GOARM64",
            "value": "v8.0"
          }
        ],
```

Specifically, I'm looking to get the value for `github.com/hashicorp/vault/version.VersionMetadata=`

If this is not possible then Golang also provides an automatic mechanism for ways this value to be discovered in compiled programs
https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/debug@master#BuildInfo

From 1.24 build info [documentation](https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.24#go-command)
> The go build command now sets the [main module’s version](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/runtime/debug#BuildInfo.Main) in the compiled binary based on the version control system tag and/or commit. A +dirty suffix will be appended if there are uncommitted changes. Use the -buildvcs=false flag to omit version control information from the binary.

If the tag is available when the binary is built and the toolchain is `>go1.24` the module version should use the vcs tag.

**To Reproduce**
- Run an instance of the container: `docker run -it hashicorp/vault@sha256:5cd2003247e0a574a66c66aee1916b1e9e7f99640298f2e61271a8842d2d2a19 /bin/sh`
- Copy the binary from the container to a context that has the go tool chain: `docker cp <CONTAINER_ID>:/bin/vault ./vault`
- Get the version information
```
go version -m ./vault | grep Version
        build   -ldflags=" -X github.com/hashicorp/vault/version.GitCommit=824d12909d5b596ddd3f34d9c8f169b4f9701a0c -X github.com/hashicorp/vault/version.BuildDate=2025-08-05T19:05:39Z -X github.com/hashicorp/vault/version.VersionMetadata="
```
- Check the main module version:
```
 go version -m ./vault
./vault: go1.24.4
        path    github.com/hashicorp/vault
        mod     github.com/hashicorp/vault      (devel)
```

If the 1.24 build feature was working as intended `(devel)` would be populated by the vcs tag for the given commit.

It does seem like vault knows what version it is. I'm currently trying to track down a nice way of figuring out how that's injected without resorting to `strings` on the binary:
```
docker run -it hashicorp/vault@sha256:5cd2003247e0a574a66c66aee1916b1e9e7f99640298f2e61271a8842d2d2a19 /bin/sh
/ # /bin/vault version
Vault v1.20.2 (824d12909d5b596ddd3f34d9c8f169b4f9701a0c), built 2025-08-05T19:05:39Z
```

**Expected behavior**
I expect that the VCS information is complete for the distributed artifact.

If the binary knows the commit the tag associated with the commit should be injected at one of the suggested fields. `module.Main` or `github.com/hashicorp/vault/version.VersionMetadata="`

**Additional context**
I'm not familiar with where the tag is generated, but I think the docker build process should take into account an ENV variable that can be read and injected here:
https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/a18b4dfc9bfd09a7897ed105e4420a7821878c3e/Dockerfile#L194-L213

title: Missing release of `vault/sdk` package breaks compilation for project depending on Vault `1.20.2` or `1.20.3`
body_text:
**Describe the bug**

Vault 1.20.2 was released which uses the [Download](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.20.2/vault/plugincatalog/plugin_catalog.go#L876) field from the [PluginRunner](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.20.2/sdk/helper/pluginutil/runner.go#L79) struct.

Vault version `1.20.2` depends on `vault/sdk` version `0.18.0` (see [go.mod](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.20.2/go.mod#L169)).

The issue is that version `0.18.0` of the `vault/sdk` package doesn't have that field (see `PluginRunner` in version `0.18.0` [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/sdk/v0.18.0/sdk/helper/pluginutil/runner.go#L66)).

Local builds of Vault work because of [this replace rule](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault/blob/v1.20.2/go.mod#L23), but project pulling `github.com/hashicorp/vault v1.20.2` in their go.mod are left in a broken state with the following error:

```
# github.com/hashicorp/vault/vault/plugincatalog
../../../../pkg/mod/github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.20.2/vault/plugincatalog/plugin_catalog.go:876:13: plugin.Download undefined (type *pluginutil.PluginRunner has no field or method Download)
../../../../pkg/mod/github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.20.2/vault/plugincatalog/plugin_catalog.go:888:57: plugin.Download undefined (type *pluginutil.PluginRunner has no field or method Download)
../../../../pkg/mod/github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.20.2/vault/plugincatalog/plugin_catalog.go:1021:13: plugin.Download undefined (type pluginutil.SetPluginInput has no field or method Download)
../../../../pkg/mod/github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.20.2/vault/plugincatalog/plugin_catalog.go:1031:13: plugin.Download undefined (type pluginutil.SetPluginInput has no field or method Download)
../../../../pkg/mod/github.com/hashicorp/vault@v1.20.2/vault/plugincatalog/plugin_catalog.go:1102:3: unknown field Download in struct literal of type pluginutil.PluginRunner

```

Solution would be to:
1. Release a new version of `github.com/hashicorp/vault/sdk`
